text:
Spiced Pumpkin Lentil Soup

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 2 cups pumpkin puree (canned or roasted)
- 1 medium onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 carrot, grated
- 1 celery stalk, finely chopped
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- 1/4 tsp ground cinnamon
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves for garnish

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, and celery; sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
2. Stir in the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, and cinnamon; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add the rinsed red lentils, pumpkin puree, and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a boil.
4. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and the soup has thickened.
5. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. If the soup is too thick, thin with a little extra broth or water.
6. Using an immersion blender, blend the soup until smooth, leaving a few lentil pieces for texture if desired.
7. Ladle the soup into bowls and garnish with fresh cilantro leaves. Serve hot.
title: Spiced Pumpkin Lentil Soup

text:
Crispy Chickpea and Kale Stir‑Fry

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 cups kale, stems removed and torn into bite‑size pieces
- 1 red bell pepper, sliced thin
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp garlic powder
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds (optional)

Instructions:
1. Pat the chickpeas dry with a clean kitchen towel and toss them with smoked paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
2. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat; add the seasoned chickpeas and cook, stirring occasionally, until golden and crisp, about 6‑8 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
3. In the same skillet, add the sliced red bell pepper and stir‑fry for 2 minutes until just softened.
4. Add the kale and continue to stir‑fry until wilted, about 3 minutes.
5. Return the crispy chickpeas to the pan, drizzle with soy sauce, and toss everything together for another minute to combine flavors.
6. Serve hot, sprinkled with toasted sesame seeds if desired. Enjoy!
title: Crispy Chickpea and Kale Stir‑Fry

text:
Roasted Red Pepper and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 2 large red bell peppers, roasted, peeled, and diced
- 1/4 cup toasted pine nuts
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley
- 2 tablespoons extra‑virgin olive oil
- 1 tablespoon red wine vinegar
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a saucepan, combine the quinoa and water; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and transfer to a large bowl to cool.
2. While the quinoa cools, toss the diced roasted red peppers with the olive oil, red wine vinegar, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; set aside to marinate for 5 minutes.
3. Add the marinated red peppers, toasted pine nuts, and chopped parsley to the cooled quinoa; gently toss to combine.
4. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or vinegar if needed.
5. Serve at room temperature or chilled, garnished with a drizzle of olive oil if desired.
title: Roasted Red Pepper and Quinoa Salad

text:
Lemon‑Garlic Orzo with Roasted Cherry Tomatoes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup orzo pasta
- 2 cups water
- 1 pint cherry tomatoes, halved
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tbsp lemon juice
- ¼ cup fresh basil, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup grated Parmesan cheese (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the halved cherry tomatoes with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, salt, and pepper, then spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 15‑20 minutes, until they burst and caramelize.
2. While the tomatoes roast, bring water to a boil in a medium saucepan, add a pinch of salt, and cook the orzo according to package instructions (usually 8‑10 minutes) until al dente; drain and set aside.
3. In a large skillet over medium heat, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil and the minced garlic. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant, being careful not to burn the garlic.
4. Add the cooked orzo to the skillet, stirring to coat it with the garlic‑oil mixture. Cook for 2 minutes to let the flavors meld.
5. Remove the skillet from heat and stir in the lemon zest, lemon juice, and roasted cherry tomatoes. Toss gently to combine.
6. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste, then fold in the chopped basil.
7. Serve warm, sprinkled with grated Parmesan cheese if desired.
title: Lemon‑Garlic Orzo with Roasted Cherry Tomatoes

text:
Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Black Bean Tacos

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 2 teaspoons maple syrup
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- Salt and black pepper, to taste
- 1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed
- ½ cup corn kernels (fresh or frozen)
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- 8 small corn tortillas
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- Lime wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the diced sweet potatoes with olive oil, maple syrup, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the sweet potatoes in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway, until tender and caramelized.  
4. While the sweet potatoes roast, heat a skillet over medium heat and add the black beans and corn; cook, stirring occasionally, for 5‑7 minutes until warmed through.  
5. Remove the sweet potatoes from the oven and transfer them to the skillet with the beans and corn; stir gently to combine and adjust seasoning if needed.  
6. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet or microwave for 20 seconds, then keep them covered with a clean kitchen towel to stay soft.  
7. To assemble each taco, place a generous spoonful of the sweet potato‑bean mixture onto a tortilla, sprinkle with chopped cilantro and feta cheese if using, and finish with a squeeze of fresh lime juice.  
8. Serve the tacos immediately, accompanied by extra lime wedges on the side.
title: Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Black Bean Tacos

text:
Thai Coconut Basil Chicken Soup

Ingredients:
- 2 tbsp vegetable oil
- 1 lb boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite‑size pieces
- 1 medium onion, finely chopped
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 red Thai chili, sliced (optional)
- 4 cups chicken broth
- 1 can (13.5 oz) coconut milk
- 2 tbsp fish sauce
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 1 cup fresh Thai basil leaves
- 1 cup bean sprouts
- 1 carrot, julienned
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 3 minutes.
2. Stir in the garlic, ginger, and Thai chili; cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
3. Add the chicken pieces, season with salt and pepper, and brown them lightly, about 4 minutes.
4. Pour in the chicken broth and bring the mixture to a gentle boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
5. Stir in the coconut milk and fish sauce; let the soup simmer for another 5 minutes, adjusting seasoning with salt, pepper, and lime juice.
6. Add the carrot strips and bean sprouts; cook for 2 minutes until just tender.
7. Remove the pot from heat and fold in the Thai basil leaves, allowing them to wilt.
8. Ladle the soup into bowls and serve hot, garnished with extra basil or a drizzle of lime juice if desired.
title: Thai Coconut Basil Chicken Soup

text:
Herb‑Infused Farro with Roasted Butternut Squash and Toasted Pecans

Ingredients:
- 1 cup farro, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 small butternut squash, peeled and cubed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly cracked black pepper
- ¼ cup toasted pecan halves, roughly chopped
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 clove garlic, minced

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the cubed butternut squash with 1 tablespoon olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until tender and caramelized.
2. Meanwhile, bring the vegetable broth to a boil in a medium saucepan. Add the rinsed farro, reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 20‑25 minutes, or until the grains are al dente and the liquid is absorbed.
3. In a small skillet, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant, then stir in the toasted pecans for 1‑2 minutes to enhance their aroma.
4. Combine the cooked farro, roasted squash, garlic‑pecan mixture, chopped parsley, and lemon juice in a large bowl. Toss gently to distribute all ingredients evenly.
5. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed. Serve warm or at room temperature as a hearty side or a light main dish.
title: Herb‑Infused Farro with Roasted Butternut Squash and Toasted Pecans

text:
Saffron‑Infused Barley Risotto with Roasted Brussels Sprouts

Ingredients:
- 1 cup pearl barley
- 1/2 teaspoon saffron threads
- 3 cups low‑sodium vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 small onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 cup dry white wine
- 1 cup roasted Brussels sprouts, halved
- 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, soak the saffron threads in 2 tablespoons of warm water for 5 minutes.
2. Heat the vegetable broth in a saucepan and keep it at a gentle simmer.
3. In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 3–4 minutes.
4. Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another 30 seconds until fragrant.
5. Add the pearl barley to the skillet, stirring to coat the grains with oil and aromatics for 2 minutes.
6. Pour in the white wine, stirring constantly, until the liquid is mostly absorbed.
7. Add the saffron infusion (including the threads) to the barley, then begin adding the simmering broth one ladleful at a time, stirring frequently. Wait until each addition is mostly absorbed before adding the next.
8. Continue this process for 25–30 minutes, or until the barley is tender yet retains a slight bite and the mixture is creamy.
9. Gently fold in the roasted Brussels sprouts, allowing them to warm through for 2–3 minutes.
10. Remove the skillet from heat, stir in the grated Parmesan cheese, and season with salt and pepper to taste.
11. Serve hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley if desired.
title: Saffron‑Infused Barley Risotto with Roasted Brussels Sprouts

text:
Miso‑Glazed Eggplant with Sesame‑Ginger Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 2 medium eggplants, cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 3 tbsp white miso paste
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tsp sesame oil
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- 2 green onions, sliced
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 1 tbsp olive oil

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, whisk together miso paste, maple syrup, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, ginger, and garlic; set aside.  
3. Toss the eggplant cubes with olive oil, salt, and pepper, then spread them on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast the eggplant for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.  
5. While the eggplant roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed.  
6. Fluff the quinoa with a fork and stir in half of the miso‑glaze, mixing until evenly coated.  
7. Remove the roasted eggplant from the oven and drizzle the remaining miso‑glaze over it; toss gently to coat.  
8. Plate the quinoa, top with the glazed eggplant, and garnish with toasted sesame seeds and sliced green onions.  
9. Serve warm, optionally with a squeeze of lime for extra brightness.
title: Miso‑Glazed Eggplant with Sesame‑Ginger Quinoa

text:
Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Tabbouleh

Ingredients:
- 1 medium cauliflower head, cut into florets
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup fine‑bulgur wheat
- 1/2 cup fresh parsley, finely chopped
- 1/4 cup fresh mint leaves, finely chopped
- 1 small red onion, minced
- 1 large cucumber, diced
- 2 tomatoes, seeded and diced
- 3 tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil
- 2 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss cauliflower florets with 1 Tbsp olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.
2. While the cauliflower roasts, place bulgur in a heat‑proof bowl, cover with boiling water, and let sit for 10‑12 minutes until fluffy; drain any excess water and fluff with a fork.
3. In a large mixing bowl, combine roasted cauliflower, chickpeas, bulgur, parsley, mint, red onion, cucumber, and tomatoes.
4. In a small cup, whisk together the remaining 2 Tbsp olive oil, lemon juice, a pinch of salt, and a grind of black pepper; pour over the salad and toss gently to coat.
5. Adjust seasoning if needed, then serve at room temperature or chilled.
title: Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Tabbouleh

text:
Garlic‑Lime Shrimp with Coconut Rice

Ingredients:
- 1 cup jasmine rice
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup water
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- Zest and juice of 1 lime
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp red pepper flakes
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Rinse the jasmine rice under cold water until the water runs clear.  
2. In a medium saucepan combine the rice, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.  
3. While the rice cooks, pat the shrimp dry and season with salt, pepper, smoked paprika, and red pepper flakes.  
4. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the minced garlic and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.  
5. Add the seasoned shrimp to the skillet in a single layer and cook 2‑3 minutes per side, or until the shrimp turn pink and opaque.  
6. Stir in the lime zest and juice, tossing to coat the shrimp evenly. Cook for an additional 30 seconds to meld the flavors.  
7. Fluff the coconut rice with a fork and divide it among serving bowls. Top each bowl with the garlic‑lime shrimp.  
8. Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve immediately.
title: Garlic‑Lime Shrimp with Coconut Rice

text:
Cumin‑Roasted Carrot and Lentil Stew

Ingredients:
- 2 lb carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch pieces
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 1 large onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)
- Juice of ½ lemon

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the carrot pieces with 1 tbsp olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, until caramelized and tender.
2. While the carrots roast, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 5 minutes, until translucent.
3. Stir in the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more, until fragrant.
4. Add the rinsed lentils and vegetable broth to the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer and cook for 15‑20 minutes, until the lentils are just tender.
5. Transfer the roasted carrots to the pot, stirring to combine. Simmer the stew for an additional 5 minutes to let the flavors meld.
6. Season with additional salt, pepper, and the lemon juice. Adjust seasoning as needed.
7. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with chopped cilantro, and serve hot.
title: Cumin‑Roasted Carrot and Lentil Stew

text:
Charred Corn and Avocado Summer Chowder

Ingredients:
- 4 ears fresh corn, husks removed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 2 medium potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 3 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 1 ripe avocado, diced
- 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, chopped
- Juice of 1 lime

Instructions:
1. Preheat a grill pan over medium‑high heat. Brush the corn cobs with olive oil and grill, turning occasionally, until kernels are charred, about 8‑10 minutes. Remove from heat, let cool, then slice the kernels off the cob and set aside.  
2. In a large pot, heat the remaining olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, 4‑5 minutes.  
3. Stir in the minced garlic and red bell pepper; cook for another 2 minutes until fragrant.  
4. Add the cubed potatoes, smoked paprika, cumin, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Cook, stirring, for 1 minute to toast the spices.  
5. Pour in the vegetable broth and bring the mixture to a gentle boil. Reduce heat and simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 12‑15 minutes.  
6. Stir in the coconut milk and the charred corn kernels. Simmer for 3‑4 minutes to meld flavors; adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice as desired.  
7. Ladle the chowder into bowls and garnish each serving with diced avocado, chopped cilantro, and an extra squeeze of lime. Serve hot or warm.
title: Charred Corn and Avocado Summer Chowder

text:
Smokey Chipotle Sweet Potato and Black Bean Enchiladas

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed
- 1 red onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 cup corn kernels (fresh or frozen)
- 1 cup shredded Monterey Jack cheese
- 8 corn tortillas
- 1 cup enchilada sauce
- 1 tsp chipotle powder
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)
- Lime wedges (for serving)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the diced sweet potatoes with a drizzle of oil, chipotle powder, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, heat a skillet over medium heat and sauté the onion until translucent, about 4 minutes. Add the garlic and cook another minute.
3. Stir in the black beans and corn, cooking until heated through, then season with additional salt, pepper, and a pinch of chipotle powder if desired. Remove from heat.
4. In a large bowl, combine the roasted sweet potatoes, bean‑corn mixture, and half of the shredded cheese. Mix gently to distribute evenly.
5. Warm the corn tortillas briefly in the microwave (15 seconds) or on a dry skillet so they become pliable. Spoon about ¼ cup of the filling onto each tortilla, roll tightly, and place seam‑side down in a 9×13‑inch baking dish.
6. Pour the enchilada sauce evenly over the rolled tortillas, ensuring they are fully covered. Sprinkle the remaining cheese on top.
7. Bake for 15‑20 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbly.
8. Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve with lime wedges on the side. Enjoy!
title: Smokey Chipotle Sweet Potato and Black Bean Enchiladas

text:
Roasted Garlic and Herb Polenta with Sautéed Wild Mushrooms

Ingredients:
- 1 cup coarse cornmeal (polenta)
- 4 cups water
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- 1 tsp dried rosemary
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/4 tsp black pepper
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 8 oz mixed wild mushrooms, sliced
- 1 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese (optional)

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan bring water to a boil, add minced garlic, thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper.  
2. Gradually whisk in the cornmeal, reducing heat to low; cook, stirring frequently, for 25‑30 minutes until thick and creamy.  
3. Stir in butter and Parmesan (if using); keep warm.  
4. While polenta cooks, heat olive oil in a skillet over medium‑high heat.  
5. Add sliced mushrooms and sauté for 5‑7 minutes until golden and tender, seasoning with a pinch of salt.  
6. Spoon the creamy polenta onto plates, top with sautéed mushrooms, and garnish with fresh parsley.
title: Roasted Garlic and Herb Polenta with Sautéed Wild Mushrooms

text:
Honey‑Glazed Salmon with Sesame‑Ginger Bok Choy

Ingredients:
- 4 salmon fillets (6 oz each)
- 2 Tbsp honey
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 Tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 Tbsp sesame oil
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 4 cups baby bok choy, halved
- 1 Tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 1 lime, cut into wedges (optional)

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, whisk together honey, soy sauce, ginger, garlic, rice vinegar, and sesame oil to form a glaze.
2. Pat salmon fillets dry, season with salt and pepper, and place on a parchment‑lined baking sheet.
3. Brush each fillet generously with the glaze, reserving a little for later.
4. Preheat oven to 400 °F (200 °C) and bake salmon 10‑12 minutes, until it flakes easily.
5. Meanwhile, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add bok choy halves, cut side down, and sauté 3‑4 minutes until lightly browned.
6. Flip bok choy, add a splash of water, cover, and steam 2‑3 minutes until tender.
7. Drizzle the remaining glaze over the bok choy and toss to coat.
8. Remove salmon from oven, brush with any remaining glaze, and rest 2 minutes.
9. Serve each salmon fillet atop the sautéed bok choy, sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds, and garnish with lime wedges if desired.
title: Honey‑Glazed Salmon with Sesame‑Ginger Bok Choy

text:
Spicy Coconut Lime Chicken Thighs

Ingredients:
- 4 bone‑in, skin‑on chicken thighs
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tbsp fish sauce
- 1 tbsp honey
- 2 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp chili flakes
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)
- Lime wedges (for serving)

Instructions:
1. Pat the chicken thighs dry and season both sides with salt, pepper, smoked paprika, cumin, and chili flakes.  
2. In a bowl, whisk together coconut milk, lime juice, fish sauce, honey, minced garlic, and grated ginger.  
3. Heat a large skillet over medium‑high heat and add the chicken thighs, skin side down. Cook for 5‑6 minutes until the skin is golden and crisp.  
4. Flip the thighs, pour the coconut‑lime mixture over them, and reduce heat to medium. Cover and simmer for 15‑20 minutes, or until the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C) and the sauce thickens slightly.  
5. Remove the lid, increase the heat, and cook for an additional 2‑3 minutes to caramelize the sauce, stirring occasionally.  
6. Transfer the chicken to a serving platter, spoon the remaining sauce over the top, and garnish with chopped cilantro and lime wedges. Enjoy!
title: Spicy Coconut Lime Chicken Thighs

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Sweet Potato and Kale

Ingredients:
- 8 oz (225 g) tempeh, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp low‑sodium soy sauce
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and diced ½‑inch
- 4 cups kale leaves, stems removed and torn
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional garnish: toasted sesame seeds

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, minced garlic, smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt.  
3. Toss the diced sweet potato with ½ Tbsp olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and spread in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 12 minutes.  
4. While the sweet potatoes begin roasting, heat the remaining ½ Tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the tempeh cubes and sauté for 4‑5 minutes until lightly browned.  
5. Remove the sweet potatoes from the oven, stir them, then return to the oven for another 8‑10 minutes, or until tender and caramelized.  
6. When the tempeh is browned, pour the maple‑soy glaze over it, stirring to coat. Cook for an additional 2 minutes, allowing the glaze to thicken and cling to the tempeh.  
7. In a large bowl, combine the roasted sweet potatoes, glazed tempeh, and raw kale. Drizzle with a little extra soy sauce or a splash of lemon juice if desired, then toss gently until the kale is slightly wilted.  
8. Plate the mixture, garnish with toasted sesame seeds if using, and serve warm. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Sweet Potato and Kale

text:
Turmeric‑Infused Chickpea and Spinach Curry

Ingredients:
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 large onion, finely diced
- 3 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1 can (14 oz) diced tomatoes
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- 3 cups fresh baby spinach
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Juice of ½ lime
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Sprinkle the turmeric, cumin, and smoked paprika over the aromatics, stirring constantly for 30 seconds to toast the spices.
4. Pour in the diced tomatoes with their juices, chickpeas, and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.
5. Add the fresh spinach in batches, stirring until wilted, about 2 minutes. Season with salt, pepper, and lime juice, adjusting to taste.
6. Remove from heat, garnish with chopped cilantro, and serve hot over steamed basmati rice or warm naan bread.
title: Turmeric‑Infused Chickpea and Spinach Curry

text:
Roasted Tomato and Basil Polenta Cakes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quick‑cook polenta
- 2 cups water
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1 cup cherry tomatoes, halved
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 garlic clove, minced
- 1/4 cup fresh basil leaves, chopped
- 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese
- 1 egg, lightly beaten
- 1/4 cup all‑purpose flour
- Freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a saucepan, bring water and salt to a boil; whisk in the polenta and cook, stirring constantly, for 5 minutes until thickened. Remove from heat and let cool slightly.
2. While the polenta rests, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the cherry tomatoes with olive oil, minced garlic, and a pinch of black pepper on a baking sheet; roast for 12‑15 minutes until caramelized.
3. Fold the roasted tomatoes, chopped basil, Parmesan, and beaten egg into the warm polenta until evenly combined.
4. Sprinkle the flour over the mixture and gently stir to incorporate; the mixture should be thick enough to hold its shape.
5. Heat a thin layer of olive oil in a non‑stick skillet over medium heat. Scoop ¼‑cup portions of the polenta mixture and flatten into small cakes; cook 3‑4 minutes per side until golden brown and crisp.
6. Serve the polenta cakes hot, garnished with extra basil leaves and a drizzle of olive oil if desired.
title: Roasted Tomato and Basil Polenta Cakes

text:
Lemon‑Thyme Quinoa Stuffed Bell Peppers

Ingredients:
- 4 large red or yellow bell peppers, tops cut off and seeds removed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 small onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 cup cherry tomatoes, halved
- 1/2 cup corn kernels (fresh or frozen)
- 1/4 cup toasted pine nuts
- 1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tablespoons lemon juice
- 1 teaspoon dried thyme
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1/2 cup shredded mozzarella cheese (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Place the prepared bell peppers upright in a baking dish.
2. In a saucepan, combine quinoa and vegetable broth; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
3. While the quinoa cooks, heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 3‑4 minutes until translucent. Stir in garlic and cook for another 30 seconds.
4. Add cherry tomatoes and corn to the skillet; cook for 2‑3 minutes until the tomatoes begin to soften.
5. Transfer the cooked quinoa to the skillet and stir in pine nuts, parsley, lemon zest, lemon juice, dried thyme, salt, and pepper. Mix until evenly combined.
6. Spoon the quinoa mixture into each bell pepper cavity, packing gently. If using, sprinkle the tops with shredded mozzarella cheese.
7. Cover the baking dish with foil and bake for 25 minutes. Remove the foil and continue baking for an additional 10 minutes, or until the peppers are tender and the cheese is melted and golden.
8. Remove from the oven, let cool for 5 minutes, then serve warm, garnished with extra parsley and a drizzle of lemon juice if desired.
title: Lemon‑Thyme Quinoa Stuffed Bell Peppers

text:
Ginger‑Soy Glazed Tofu with Sesame‑Brown Rice

Ingredients:
- 1 block (14 oz) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 Tbsp soy sauce
- 1 Tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp freshly grated ginger
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 Tbsp toasted sesame oil
- 1 Tbsp cornstarch
- 1 cup brown rice
- 2 cups water
- 1 Tbsp sesame seeds
- 2 green onions, sliced
- 1 tsp toasted sesame oil (for drizzling)

Instructions:
1. Rinse the brown rice, then combine with 2 cups water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 40‑45 minutes until tender.
2. While the rice cooks, whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, maple syrup, ginger, garlic, and 1 Tbsp sesame oil in a bowl; stir in cornstarch until smooth.
3. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat and add a splash of oil; add the tofu cubes and sauté until golden on all sides, about 6‑8 minutes.
4. Pour the sauce over the tofu, stirring to coat; continue cooking for 2‑3 minutes until the glaze thickens and becomes glossy.
5. Fluff the cooked brown rice with a fork and stir in the toasted sesame seeds.
6. Serve the glazed tofu atop the sesame‑brown rice, garnish with sliced green onions and a drizzle of the remaining toasted sesame oil. Enjoy!
title: Ginger‑Soy Glazed Tofu with Sesame‑Brown Rice

text:
Roasted Garlic and Lemon Chickpea Tagine

Ingredients:
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large onion, finely chopped
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp ras el hanout
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup diced tomatoes (canned or fresh)
- ½ cup vegetable broth
- Zest of 1 lemon
- Juice of 1 lemon
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Cooked couscous or quinoa, for serving

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.  
2. Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.  
3. Sprinkle the cumin, coriander, smoked paprika, and ras el hanout over the aromatics; toast the spices for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.  
4. Add the chickpeas, diced tomatoes, and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then reduce the heat to low and let it cook for 15–20 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken.  
5. Stir in the lemon zest, lemon juice, and half of the chopped cilantro. Season with salt and pepper to taste.  
6. Spoon the tagine over a bed of fluffy couscous or quinoa, garnish with the remaining cilantro, and serve hot.
title: Roasted Garlic and Lemon Chickpea Tagine

text:
Crispy Pesto Zucchini Noodles with Sun‑Dried Tomato Pesto

Ingredients:
- 3 medium zucchini
- 1/4 cup sun‑dried tomatoes (packed in oil, drained)
- 1/4 cup fresh basil leaves
- 1 garlic clove
- 2 tbsp pine nuts
- 2 tbsp grated Parmesan cheese
- 2 tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 tbsp olive oil (for sautéing)

Instructions:
1. Using a spiralizer, turn the zucchini into noodles and set aside on a paper towel to release excess moisture.
2. In a food processor, combine sun‑dried tomatoes, basil, garlic, pine nuts, Parmesan, olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper; blend until smooth, adding a splash of water if needed to reach a sauce‑like consistency.
3. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the zucchini noodles and sauté for 2‑3 minutes, just until they begin to soften but still retain a slight crunch.
4. Remove the noodles from the skillet and toss them with the sun‑dried tomato pesto, ensuring each strand is evenly coated.
5. Return the coated noodles to the skillet and cook for an additional 1‑2 minutes, allowing the pesto to lightly caramelize and the noodles to become crisp‑tender.
6. Serve immediately, garnished with extra pine nuts and a sprinkle of Parmesan if desired. Enjoy!
title: Crispy Pesto Zucchini Noodles with Sun‑Dried Tomato Pesto

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Butternut Squash and Farro Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 cup farro, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 small butternut squash, peeled and cubed (about 3 cups)
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1/4 cup dried cranberries
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the cubed butternut squash with olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, cumin, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the squash in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until tender and caramelized.  
4. While the squash roasts, combine the rinsed farro and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the farro is tender and the liquid is absorbed.  
5. Remove the farro from heat and fluff with a fork. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.  
6. Transfer the cooked farro to a large mixing bowl; add the roasted squash, dried cranberries, and toasted pumpkin seeds. Toss gently to combine.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.  
8. Serve warm, garnished with chopped fresh parsley if desired. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Butternut Squash and Farro Pilaf

text:
Harissa‑Spiced Lentil and Sweet Potato Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon harissa paste
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 can (14 oz) diced tomatoes
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Juice of 1/2 lemon

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes.
2. Stir in the garlic, harissa paste, and smoked paprika; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add the diced sweet potatoes and toast them lightly for 2–3 minutes, stirring to coat with the spice mixture.
4. Pour in the vegetable broth and diced tomatoes, then bring the mixture to a gentle boil.
5. Add the rinsed red lentils, reduce the heat to a simmer, and cover the pot. Cook for 20–25 minutes, or until the lentils and sweet potatoes are tender.
6. Season with salt, pepper, and lemon juice. Adjust the harissa level if you prefer more heat.
7. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve hot.
title: Harissa‑Spiced Lentil and Sweet Potato Stew

text:
Coconut Lime Quinoa Salad with Toasted Almonds

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 1 cup canned coconut milk
- 1 tablespoon lime zest
- 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice
- 1/4 cup finely chopped red onion
- 1/2 cup diced mango
- 1/3 cup toasted sliced almonds
- 2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro
- 1 teaspoon honey
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa, water, and coconut milk; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed.
2. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork and transfer to a large bowl to cool slightly.
3. Stir in lime zest, lime juice, red onion, mango, cilantro, and honey; season with salt and pepper.
4. Gently fold in toasted almonds just before serving.
5. Serve chilled or at room temperature as a refreshing side or light main dish.
title: Coconut Lime Quinoa Salad with Toasted Almonds

text:
Spiced Carrot and Coconut Milk Soup

Ingredients:
- 1 lb carrots, peeled and sliced
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp ground coriander
- ¼ tsp ground cinnamon
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 can (13.5 oz) coconut milk
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)
- Lime wedges (for serving)

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes.
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add the sliced carrots, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, and cayenne pepper. Toss to coat the carrots with the spices and cook for 2 minutes.
4. Pour in the vegetable broth, bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until the carrots are very tender, about 15‑20 minutes.
5. Using an immersion blender (or transferring to a countertop blender in batches), puree the soup until smooth.
6. Stir in the coconut milk, and season with salt and black pepper. Heat gently for another 3‑5 minutes, but do not let the soup boil.
7. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with chopped cilantro, and serve with a lime wedge on the side for a bright finish.
title: Spiced Carrot and Coconut Milk Soup

text:
Sesame‑Crusted Tofu with Coconut Lime Rice

Ingredients:
- 1 block (14 oz) firm tofu, pressed and cut into ½‑inch slices
- 2  tbsp sesame seeds (mixed black and white)
- 1  tbsp soy sauce
- 1  tsp maple syrup
- 1  tsp rice vinegar
- 1  tbsp cornstarch
- 2  tbsp neutral oil (e.g., grapeseed)
- 1  cup jasmine rice
- 1  cup coconut milk
- 1  cup water
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2  tbsp fresh lime juice
- 2  tbsp chopped cilantro
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a shallow bowl, whisk together soy sauce, maple syrup, rice vinegar, and cornstarch until smooth. Add the tofu slices, turning to coat; let marinate for 10 minutes.  
2. Spread the sesame seeds on a plate. Press each tofu slice into the seeds, coating both sides.  
3. Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the tofu and cook 3‑4 minutes per side, until golden and crisp. Transfer to a paper‑towel‑lined plate.  
4. While the tofu cooks, rinse the jasmine rice under cold water until the water runs clear.  
5. In a saucepan, combine coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a gentle boil, then stir in the rice. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.  
6. Remove the rice from heat; fluff with a fork and stir in lime zest, lime juice, and chopped cilantro. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste.  
7. Serve the sesame‑crusted tofu atop the coconut lime rice, garnished with extra cilantro and a drizzle of soy sauce if desired. Enjoy warm!
title: Sesame‑Crusted Tofu with Coconut Lime Rice

text:
Lemon‑Basil Orzo with Grilled Zucchini and Feta

Ingredients:
- 1 cup orzo pasta
- 2 medium zucchini, sliced lengthwise
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 lemon, zest and juice
- 1/4 cup fresh basil leaves, chopped
- 1/2 cup crumbled feta cheese
- 1 garlic clove, minced
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Cook the orzo in salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente; drain and set aside.  
2. Meanwhile, preheat a grill pan over medium-high heat. Brush the zucchini slices with 1 tablespoon olive oil and season with salt and pepper.  
3. Grill the zucchini for 2‑3 minutes per side, until grill marks appear and the flesh is tender; remove from heat and let cool slightly, then cut into bite‑size pieces.  
4. In a large bowl, combine the cooked orzo, grilled zucchini, minced garlic, lemon zest, and lemon juice.  
5. Drizzle the remaining olive oil over the mixture, toss gently, then fold in the chopped basil.  
6. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste, then sprinkle the crumbled feta on top before serving.
title: Lemon‑Basil Orzo with Grilled Zucchini and Feta

text:
Maple‑Glazed Brussels Sprout and Chickpea Sheet Pan Dinner

Ingredients:
- 1 lb Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds (optional, for garnish)
- Fresh parsley, chopped (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a large bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper.
3. Add the Brussels sprout halves and chickpeas to the bowl; toss until everything is evenly coated with the glaze.
4. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet, ensuring the sprouts are cut‑side down for optimal caramelization.
5. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until the Brussels sprouts are golden‑brown and tender and the chickpeas are crisp.
6. Remove from the oven and transfer to a serving platter. Sprinkle with toasted pumpkin seeds and chopped parsley, if using, for added texture and freshness.
7. Serve warm as a hearty main dish or a side; it pairs well with quinoa, rice, or a simple green salad.
title: Maple‑Glazed Brussels Sprout and Chickpea Sheet Pan Dinner

text:
Roasted Coconut‑Lime Shrimp Tacos with Mango Slaw

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 2 Tbsp coconut oil, melted
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 Tbsp lime juice
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp sea salt
- 8 small corn tortillas
- 1 ripe mango, julienned
- ¼ red onion, thinly sliced
- 1 Tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 Tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tsp honey
- ¼ tsp chili flakes
- 1 avocado, sliced (optional)
- Lime wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, whisk together melted coconut oil, lime zest, lime juice, cumin, smoked paprika, and sea salt. Add the shrimp and toss to coat; let marinate for 10 minutes.
2. While the shrimp marinates, prepare the mango slaw: combine mango strips, red onion, cilantro, rice vinegar, honey, and chili flakes in a small bowl; toss gently and set aside.
3. Heat a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the shrimp and cook for 2‑3 minutes per side, until pink and opaque. Remove from heat.
4. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet or microwave until pliable, about 30 seconds.
5. To assemble each taco, place a handful of cooked shrimp on a tortilla, top with mango slaw, and add avocado slices if using.
6. Serve immediately with lime wedges on the side for squeezing over the tacos. Enjoy!
title: Roasted Coconut‑Lime Shrimp Tacos with Mango Slaw

text:
Lemon‑Thyme Farro with Roasted Eggplant and Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 1 cup farro
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 medium eggplant, cubed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 1 tbsp fresh thyme leaves
- 1/4 cup pomegranate seeds
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss eggplant cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until golden and tender.  
2. While the eggplant roasts, rinse farro under cold water. In a saucepan, combine farro and vegetable broth; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 20‑25 minutes until the grains are tender and the liquid is absorbed.  
3. Drain any excess liquid from the farro, then stir in the remaining olive oil, lemon zest, and fresh thyme. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste.  
4. Gently fold the roasted eggplant into the farro mixture.  
5. Transfer to serving bowls and garnish with pomegranate seeds for a burst of color and sweetness. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Thyme Farro with Roasted Eggplant and Pomegranate

text:
Cinnamon‑Spiced Apple and Chickpea Tagine

Ingredients:
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 large onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1/4 teaspoon ground ginger
- 2 medium apples, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- 1/2 cup dried apricots, chopped
- 1 tablespoon tomato paste
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Cooked couscous or quinoa, for serving

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy‑bottomed pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
2. Stir in the minced garlic, ground cinnamon, cumin, smoked paprika, and ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add the cubed apples and cook, stirring occasionally, for 3–4 minutes until they begin to soften.
4. Mix in the chickpeas, dried apricots, tomato paste, and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat to low.
5. Cover the pot and simmer for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the apples are tender and the sauce has thickened.
6. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste. Remove from heat.
7. Spoon the tagine over a bed of cooked couscous or quinoa, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve warm.
title: Cinnamon‑Spiced Apple and Chickpea Tagine

text:
Spicy Peanut Noodle Stir‑Fry with Crunchy Veggies

Ingredients:
- 8 oz rice noodles
- 2 tbsp peanut butter
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp sriracha
- 1 tbsp honey
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tsp sesame oil
- 1 cup shredded red cabbage
- 1 cup julienned carrots
- 1 cup sliced bell peppers (mixed colors)
- 1/2 cup edamame, shelled
- 2 green onions, sliced
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tsp grated ginger

Instructions:
1. Cook the rice noodles according to package directions, drain, and rinse under cold water; set aside.
2. In a small bowl, whisk together peanut butter, soy sauce, sriracha, honey, lime juice, sesame oil, garlic, and ginger until smooth; set the sauce aside.
3. Heat a large skillet or wok over medium‑high heat and add a splash of oil; stir‑fry the carrots, bell peppers, and cabbage for 3–4 minutes until crisp‑tender.
4. Add the edamame and continue to stir‑fry for another minute.
5. Reduce heat to medium, add the cooked noodles and the prepared sauce to the skillet; toss everything together until the noodles are evenly coated and heated through, about 2 minutes.
6. Remove from heat, garnish with sliced green onions, toasted sesame seeds, and fresh cilantro; serve immediately.
title: Spicy Peanut Noodle Stir‑Fry with Crunchy Veggies

text:
Roasted Paprika Chickpea and Sweet Potato Skillet

Ingredients:
- 1 large sweet potato, diced
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 red bell pepper, sliced
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
- 2 green onions, sliced
- Fresh cilantro leaves for garnish
- 1 tbsp lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a bowl, toss the diced sweet potato, chickpeas, and red bell pepper with olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, cayenne (if using), salt, and pepper until evenly coated.
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the sweet potatoes are tender and lightly caramelized.
4. Remove from the oven and transfer to a serving platter; drizzle with lemon juice and sprinkle with sliced green onions and fresh cilantro.
5. Serve hot as a main dish or alongside a simple green salad.
title: Roasted Paprika Chickpea and Sweet Potato Skillet

text:
Roasted Garlic‑Lemon Chickpea and Spinach Flatbread

Ingredients:
- 1 cup canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 cups fresh baby spinach
- 1 large garlic clove, minced
- 1 tablespoon lemon zest
- 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- ¼ teaspoon sea salt
- ¼ teaspoon black pepper
- 1 pre-made whole‑wheat flatbread (10‑inch)
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese
- 2 tablespoons toasted pine nuts
- Fresh parsley leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Place the flatbread on a baking sheet.
2. In a bowl, toss the chickpeas with olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.
3. Spread the seasoned chickpeas over the flatbread, then top with the fresh spinach.
4. Roast in the oven for 12‑15 minutes, until the chickpeas are golden and the spinach is wilted.
5. While the flatbread bakes, combine minced garlic, lemon zest, and lemon juice in a small bowl; set aside.
6. Remove the flatbread from the oven and immediately drizzle the lemon‑garlic mixture over the top.
7. Sprinkle crumbled feta, toasted pine nuts, and fresh parsley leaves across the flatbread.
8. Slice into wedges and serve warm. Enjoy!
title: Roasted Garlic‑Lemon Chickpea and Spinach Flatbread

text:
Crispy Coconut‑Lime Tilapia with Mango Avocado Salsa

Ingredients:
- 4 tilapia fillets (about 6 oz each)
- 1 cup unsweetened shredded coconut
- ½ cup panko breadcrumbs
- Zest of 1 lime
- 1 tablespoon lime juice
- 1 teaspoon sea salt
- ½ teaspoon black pepper
- 2 large eggs, beaten
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 ripe mango, diced
- 1 ripe avocado, diced
- ¼ cup red onion, finely chopped
- 1 small jalapeño, seeded and minced
- 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 tablespoon lime juice (extra for salsa)
- Pinch of cayenne pepper (optional)

Instructions:
1. In a shallow dish, combine the shredded coconut, panko breadcrumbs, lime zest, salt, and pepper.
2. Pat the tilapia fillets dry with paper towels. Brush each fillet with lime juice, then dip them into the beaten eggs, allowing excess to drip off.
3. Press each fillet into the coconut‑panko mixture, coating both sides evenly; set the coated fillets on a plate.
4. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. When the oil shimmers, add the fillets and cook 3‑4 minutes per side, or until the coating is golden brown and the fish flakes easily with a fork.
5. While the fish cooks, prepare the salsa: in a bowl, gently toss together the diced mango, avocado, red onion, jalapeño, cilantro, lime juice, and a pinch of cayenne if using. Season with a little salt to taste.
6. Transfer the cooked tilapia to a serving platter. Spoon the mango‑avocado salsa over each fillet or serve it on the side.
7. Garnish with additional cilantro leaves and a wedge of lime, then enjoy immediately.
title: Crispy Coconut‑Lime Tilapia with Mango Avocado Salsa

text:
Lemon‑Rosemary Quinoa Pilaf with Grilled Portobello Mushrooms

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 lemon, zest and juice
- 1 teaspoon fresh rosemary, finely chopped
- 1 garlic clove, minced
- 2 large Portobello mushroom caps, stems removed
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 tablespoons toasted pine nuts
- 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan, combine the quinoa and vegetable broth; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy.
2. While the quinoa cooks, whisk together olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, rosemary, garlic, salt, and pepper in a shallow dish; brush both sides of the Portobello caps with the mixture.
3. Preheat a grill or grill pan over medium‑high heat; grill the mushrooms for 4‑5 minutes per side, until tender and lightly charred. Slice the mushrooms into thick strips.
4. Fluff the cooked quinoa with a fork and stir in the remaining lemon‑rosemary dressing, adjusting seasoning if needed.
5. Transfer the quinoa to a serving platter, top with the grilled mushroom strips, and sprinkle with toasted pine nuts and chopped parsley. Serve warm.
title: Lemon‑Rosemary Quinoa Pilaf with Grilled Portobello Mushrooms

text:
Roasted Garlic and Herb Chickpea Stuffed Sweet Potatoes

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- 1 tsp dried rosemary
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- Fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. Scrub the sweet potatoes, pat dry, and prick each several times with a fork. Rub them with 1 tbsp olive oil and place on the prepared baking sheet.
3. Roast the sweet potatoes for 45‑50 minutes, or until tender when pierced with a knife.
4. While the potatoes roast, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
5. Add the chickpeas, thyme, rosemary, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5‑7 minutes until the chickpeas are lightly browned and the herbs are aromatic.
6. Remove the sweet potatoes from the oven and let them cool for 5 minutes. Slice each potato lengthwise, being careful not to cut all the way through.
7. Gently fluff the interior of each potato with a fork, then spoon the seasoned chickpea mixture into the openings, dividing it evenly.
8. Sprinkle crumbled feta over the stuffed potatoes, if using, and return to the oven for an additional 5 minutes to warm the cheese.
9. Remove from the oven, garnish with chopped parsley, and serve hot.
title: Roasted Garlic and Herb Chickpea Stuffed Sweet Potatoes

text:
Cinnamon‑Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup cooked quinoa
- 1 avocado, sliced
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tbsp tahini
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tsp maple syrup
- 2 tbsp water
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and half the cinnamon; spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
3. In another bowl, combine chickpeas with the remaining olive oil, smoked paprika, the remaining cinnamon, and a pinch of salt and pepper; spread them beside the sweet potatoes.  
4. Roast the vegetables for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway through, until sweet potatoes are tender and chickpeas are crisp.  
5. While the vegetables roast, prepare the dressing: whisk together tahini, lemon juice, maple syrup, and water until smooth; add salt to taste.  
6. Assemble the bowls: divide cooked quinoa among four serving bowls, top with roasted sweet potatoes, chickpeas, avocado slices, and toasted pumpkin seeds.  
7. Drizzle the tahini‑lemon dressing over each bowl and garnish with fresh cilantro leaves. Enjoy warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Buddha Bowl

text:
Lemon‑Thyme Chickpea and Quinoa Stuffed Portobello Caps

Ingredients:
- 4 large portobello mushroom caps, stems removed
- 1 cup cooked quinoa
- 1 cup canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1/2 cup cherry tomatoes, halved
- 1/4 cup crumbled feta cheese
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves
- 1 garlic clove, minced
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a bowl, combine cooked quinoa, chickpeas, cherry tomatoes, feta, lemon juice, olive oil, thyme, and minced garlic. Season with salt and pepper; toss gently to mix.
3. Place the portobello caps gill‑side up on the prepared baking sheet. Spoon the quinoa mixture evenly into each cap, pressing lightly to fill.
4. Bake for 18‑20 minutes, until the mushrooms are tender and the filling is heated through.
5. Remove from the oven, garnish with chopped parsley, and serve warm.
title: Lemon‑Thyme Chickpea and Quinoa Stuffed Portobello Caps

text:
Coconut‑Lime Baked Cod with Turmeric Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 4 cod fillets (about 6 oz each)
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups coconut milk
- 1 tablespoon lime zest
- 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 tablespoon coconut oil, melted
- 1 tablespoon soy sauce
- 1 tablespoon honey
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a small bowl, whisk together lime zest, lime juice, minced garlic, melted coconut oil, soy sauce, honey, salt, and pepper; set aside.
3. Place the cod fillets on the prepared baking sheet and brush each generously with the lime‑garlic mixture.
4. Bake the cod for 12‑15 minutes, or until the fish flakes easily with a fork.
5. While the cod bakes, combine quinoa, coconut milk, turmeric, and cumin in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.
6. Fluff the quinoa with a fork and stir in chopped cilantro; season with additional salt if needed.
7. Serve each cod fillet atop a mound of turmeric quinoa, drizzling any remaining pan juices over the top. Enjoy!
title: Coconut‑Lime Baked Cod with Turmeric Quinoa

text:
Maple‑Mustard Glazed Pork Tenderloin with Roasted Root Vegetables

Ingredients:
- 1 lb pork tenderloin
- 2 tbsp Dijon mustard
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp fresh rosemary, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper
- 2 carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch pieces
- 1 parsnip, peeled and cut into 1‑inch pieces
- 1 small sweet potato, cubed
- 2 tbsp olive oil

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together Dijon mustard, maple syrup, apple cider vinegar, minced garlic, rosemary, salt, and pepper.  
3. Pat the pork tenderloin dry with paper towels, then brush the glaze over the entire surface, reserving half for later.  
4. Toss the carrots, parsnip, and sweet potato with olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread them around the pork on the prepared baking sheet.  
5. Roast in the preheated oven for 20 minutes, then brush the pork with the remaining glaze.  
6. Continue roasting for another 15‑20 minutes, or until the pork reaches an internal temperature of 145°F (63°C) and the vegetables are tender and caramelized.  
7. Remove from the oven, let the pork rest for 5 minutes before slicing, and serve with the roasted root vegetables.
title: Maple‑Mustard Glazed Pork Tenderloin with Roasted Root Vegetables

text:
Zesty Orange Glazed Tempeh with Sesame Broccoli

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 2 tbsp orange marmalade
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp rice vinegar
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp sesame oil
- 2 cups broccoli florets
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- 2 green onions, sliced
- ½ cup cooked brown rice (optional, for serving)

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl whisk together orange marmalade, soy sauce, rice vinegar, ginger, and garlic to form the glaze.  
2. Heat ½ tbsp sesame oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat; add tempeh and sauté until golden, about 4‑5 minutes.  
3. Pour the orange glaze over the tempeh, stirring to coat; cook for another 2‑3 minutes until the sauce thickens and clings to the tempeh. Transfer tempeh to a plate.  
4. In the same skillet add the remaining ½ tbsp sesame oil and the broccoli florets; stir‑fry for 4‑5 minutes until crisp‑tender.  
5. Return the glazed tempeh to the skillet, toss with the broccoli, and heat through for 1 minute.  
6. Serve the tempeh‑broccoli mixture over cooked brown rice, if desired, and garnish with toasted sesame seeds and sliced green onions.
title: Zesty Orange Glazed Tempeh with Sesame Broccoli

text:
Harissa‑Roasted Eggplant and Chickpea Couscous

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 ½ cups couscous
- 1 ½ cups vegetable broth
- 2 Tbsp harissa paste
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup fresh parsley, chopped
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the eggplant cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, harissa paste, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the seasoned eggplant on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.  
4. While the eggplant roasts, bring the vegetable broth to a boil in a saucepan, stir in the couscous, cover, and remove from heat. Let sit for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.  
5. In a skillet over medium heat, add the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil and the chickpeas; sauté for 4‑5 minutes until lightly crisped and warmed through. Season with a pinch of salt.  
6. Combine the roasted eggplant, sautéed chickpeas, and couscous in a large serving bowl. Add chopped parsley, lemon zest, and lemon juice; toss gently to distribute flavors.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or harissa if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Harissa‑Roasted Eggplant and Chickpea Couscous

text:
Spicy Harissa Roasted Cauliflower with Chickpea Couscous

Ingredients:
- 1 large head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup couscous
- 2 tbsp harissa paste
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Zest and juice of 1 lemon
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 ½ cups vegetable broth (for couscous)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cauliflower florets with 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp harissa paste, cumin, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the cauliflower on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.  
4. While the cauliflower roasts, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the chickpeas and the remaining 1 tbsp harissa paste, stirring for 2‑3 minutes until fragrant.  
5. Add the vegetable broth and bring to a boil; then stir in the couscous, cover, and remove from heat. Let sit for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.  
6. Fold the roasted cauliflower into the couscous‑chickpea mixture. Add lemon zest, lemon juice, and chopped cilantro; toss gently to combine.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or harissa if desired.  
8. Serve warm, garnished with extra cilantro and a drizzle of olive oil if desired.
title: Spicy Harissa Roasted Cauliflower with Chickpea Couscous

text:
Maple‑Brown Butter Gnocchi with Roasted Pears and Sage

Ingredients:
- 1 lb (450 g) potato gnocchi
- 3 Tbsp unsalted butter
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 ripe pears, cored and sliced into ½‑inch wedges
- 1 Tbsp fresh sage leaves, chopped
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup grated Parmesan cheese (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the pear wedges with olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper, then spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet. Roast for 15‑20 minutes, until caramelized and tender.  
3. While the pears roast, melt the butter in a large skillet over medium‑low heat. Continue cooking, swirling the pan occasionally, until the butter turns a nutty brown color and gives off a fragrant aroma (about 4‑5 minutes).  
4. Stir the maple syrup into the browned butter, whisking to combine, then remove the pan from heat.  
5. Add the gnocchi to the skillet, tossing to coat them evenly with the maple‑brown butter sauce. Increase the heat to medium and sauté for 3‑4 minutes, allowing the gnocchi to develop a light golden crust.  
6. Gently fold in the roasted pear wedges and chopped sage, seasoning with additional salt and pepper to taste. Cook for another minute just to warm the pears through.  
7. Transfer the gnocchi mixture to serving plates, sprinkle with grated Parmesan if desired, and serve immediately.
title: Maple‑Brown Butter Gnocchi with Roasted Pears and Sage

text:
Curry‑Infused Coconut Lentil Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 tablespoon coconut oil
- 1 onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tablespoon red curry paste
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1 can (14 oz) coconut milk
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup diced sweet potato
- 1 red bell pepper, sliced
- 1 tablespoon lime juice
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves for garnish

Instructions:
1. Heat coconut oil in a large pot over medium heat; add onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes.  
2. Stir in garlic, ginger, red curry paste, and turmeric; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
3. Add the rinsed lentils, sweet potato, and bell pepper, stirring to coat with the spice mixture.  
4. Pour in coconut milk and vegetable broth; bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered for 20‑25 minutes, or until lentils and sweet potatoes are tender.  
5. Season with salt, pepper, and lime juice; adjust seasoning as needed.  
6. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro, and serve hot.
title: Curry‑Infused Coconut Lentil Stew

text:
Lemon‑Honey Glazed Chicken with Roasted Garlic Broccoli

Ingredients:
- 4 bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs
- 2 tbsp honey
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 head broccoli, cut into florets
- 2 tbsp grated Parmesan cheese
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together honey, lemon juice, soy sauce, minced garlic, grated ginger, and olive oil.  
3. Pat the chicken thighs dry, season with salt and pepper, and place them on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Brush the honey‑lemon glaze over the chicken, reserving a tablespoon for later.  
5. Toss the broccoli florets with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper, and spread them around the chicken on the sheet.  
6. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, until the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C) and the broccoli is tender and slightly caramelized.  
7. During the last 5 minutes of cooking, sprinkle the Parmesan over the broccoli and brush the remaining glaze on the chicken.  
8. Remove from the oven, let rest 5 minutes, then serve the chicken alongside the roasted garlic broccoli.
title: Lemon‑Honey Glazed Chicken with Roasted Garlic Broccoli

text:
Crispy Coconut‑Lime Chickpea Tacos with Pineapple Salsa

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp coconut oil, melted
- 1 Tbsp lime zest
- 1 Tbsp lime juice
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper
- Salt and black pepper, to taste
- 8 small corn tortillas
- ½ cup diced fresh pineapple
- ¼ cup finely chopped red onion
- 1 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- 1 tsp honey
- 1 tsp rice vinegar
- Optional: sliced avocado for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, combine the melted coconut oil, lime zest, lime juice, smoked paprika, cumin, cayenne, salt, and pepper. Add the chickpeas and toss to coat evenly.  
3. Spread the chickpeas in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until crisp and golden.  
4. While the chickpeas roast, prepare the pineapple salsa: in a small bowl, mix diced pineapple, red onion, cilantro, honey, and rice vinegar; set aside.  
5. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 30 seconds per side, or wrap them in foil and heat in the oven for 5 minutes.  
6. Assemble each taco by placing a generous spoonful of crispy chickpeas onto a tortilla, topping with pineapple salsa, and adding avocado slices if desired. Serve immediately.
title: Crispy Coconut‑Lime Chickpea Tacos with Pineapple Salsa

text:
Roasted Red Lentil and Sweet Corn Salad with Mint Yogurt Dressing

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 1 cup fresh or frozen sweet corn kernels
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1 small red onion, finely chopped
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh mint leaves
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley
- 1/3 cup plain Greek yogurt
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 tablespoon lemon juice
- 1 teaspoon honey
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a saucepan, combine the red lentils and water; bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 12‑15 minutes until tender but still holding shape. Drain any excess water and set the lentils aside to cool.
2. While the lentils cook, heat a skillet over medium heat and add the olive oil. Add the corn kernels and sauté for 4‑5 minutes until lightly charred. Remove from heat and let cool.
3. In a large bowl, combine the cooked lentils, sautéed corn, diced red bell pepper, and chopped red onion.
4. In a small mixing bowl, whisk together the Greek yogurt, lemon juice, honey, a pinch of salt, and a generous grind of black pepper to create the dressing.
5. Pour the yogurt dressing over the lentil mixture and toss gently to coat evenly.
6. Fold in the chopped mint and parsley, adjusting seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if desired.
7. Serve the salad at room temperature or chilled, garnished with a few extra mint leaves for color. Enjoy!
title: Roasted Red Lentil and Sweet Corn Salad with Mint Yogurt Dressing

text:
Maple‑Soy Glazed Tofu with Roasted Brussels Sprouts

Ingredients:
- 14 oz extra‑firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 2 cups Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes
- 2 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- 2 green onions, sliced
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and grated ginger.  
3. Toss the Brussels sprouts with olive oil, salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes; spread them on one half of the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Arrange the tofu cubes on the other half of the sheet and drizzle with half of the maple‑soy glaze, reserving the remaining glaze for later.  
5. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until the sprouts are caramelized and the tofu is golden and slightly crisp.  
6. While the vegetables roast, pour the reserved glaze into a small skillet over medium heat and simmer for 2 minutes, or until it thickens slightly.  
7. Remove the sheet from the oven, drizzle the reduced glaze over the tofu and Brussels sprouts, then sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds and sliced green onions.  
8. Serve immediately, paired with steamed rice or quinoa if desired.
title: Maple‑Soy Glazed Tofu with Roasted Brussels Sprouts

text:
Maple‑Balsamic Roasted Carrots with Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 lb carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch sticks
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tbsp balsamic vinegar
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 green onions, thinly sliced
- Optional: crumbled feta cheese for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together maple syrup, balsamic vinegar, olive oil, thyme, salt, and pepper. Add the carrot sticks and toss to coat evenly.  
3. Spread the carrots in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway through, until caramelized and tender.  
4. While the carrots roast, combine rinsed quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat, let sit 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.  
5. Transfer the quinoa to a serving bowl, top with roasted carrots, toasted pumpkin seeds, and sliced green onions.  
6. If desired, sprinkle crumbled feta over the top and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Maple‑Balsamic Roasted Carrots with Quinoa

text:
Smoky Paprika Shrimp and Coconut Rice Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup jasmine rice
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- 1 cup water
- 1 tbsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp garlic powder
- ½ tsp salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 red bell pepper, thinly sliced
- 1 small red onion, thinly sliced
- 1 cup fresh baby spinach
- 1 lime, cut into wedges
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- Optional: 1 tbsp toasted coconut flakes for garnish

Instructions:
1. Rinse the jasmine rice under cold water until the water runs clear. In a medium saucepan combine the rice, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.  
2. While the rice cooks, pat the shrimp dry with paper towels. In a small bowl, toss the shrimp with smoked paprika, cumin, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the seasoned shrimp and sauté for 2‑3 minutes per side, or until pink and opaque. Transfer the cooked shrimp to a plate and set aside.  
4. In the same skillet, add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil. Add the sliced red bell pepper and red onion, stirring frequently, and cook for 4‑5 minutes until softened and lightly caramelized.  
5. Add the baby spinach to the skillet and toss until wilted, about 1 minute. Return the shrimp to the pan and stir to combine all ingredients, heating through for another minute.  
6. To assemble the bowls, divide the coconut rice among four serving bowls. Top each with the shrimp‑vegetable mixture. Squeeze fresh lime juice over each bowl, sprinkle with chopped cilantro, and, if desired, garnish with toasted coconut flakes. Serve immediately.
title: Smoky Paprika Shrimp and Coconut Rice Bowl

text:
Maple‑Sriracha Glazed Chicken Wings with Roasted Sweet Potato Wedges

Ingredients:
- 2 lb chicken wings, separated at the joint
- 1 ½ cups sweet potatoes, cut into ½‑inch wedges
- ¼ cup pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp Sriracha sauce
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp garlic powder
- ½ tsp black pepper
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp cornstarch
- 1 Tbsp water
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Lime wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the sweet potato wedges with 1 Tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and black pepper; spread them in a single layer on half of the prepared baking sheet.  
3. Roast the sweet potatoes for 20 minutes, then flip and continue roasting another 15 minutes until golden and crisp.  
4. While the potatoes roast, combine maple syrup, Sriracha, soy sauce, and the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil in a small saucepan; heat over medium‑low heat, stirring, until the mixture thickens slightly, about 3 minutes.  
5. Place the chicken wings in a large zip‑top bag or shallow dish and pour half of the glaze over them, reserving the other half for finishing; toss to coat evenly.  
6. Arrange the glazed wings on the remaining half of the baking sheet, ensuring they are not touching. Roast for 25 minutes, then flip the wings, brush with more glaze, and roast an additional 15 minutes until the skin is crispy and the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C).  
7. In a small bowl, whisk together cornstarch and water; stir the mixture into the remaining glaze in the saucepan, cooking for 1‑2 minutes until glossy and slightly thickened.  
8. Drizzle the thickened glaze over the roasted wings, sprinkle fresh cilantro on top, and serve with the sweet potato wedges and lime wedges on the side.
title: Maple‑Sriracha Glazed Chicken Wings with Roasted Sweet Potato Wedges

text:
Maple‑Glazed Cauliflower Steaks with Walnut Pesto

Ingredients:
- 1 large cauliflower, sliced into 1‑inch thick steaks
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- ½ cup walnuts, lightly toasted
- 1 cup fresh basil leaves
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 2 Tbsp lemon juice
- 2 Tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil (for pesto)
- ¼ tsp salt (for pesto)
- 2 Tbsp grated Parmesan cheese (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, maple syrup, smoked paprika, sea salt, and black pepper. Brush both sides of each cauliflower steak generously with the glaze.  
3. Arrange the glazed steaks on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, flipping once, until tender and caramelized.  
4. While the cauliflower roasts, prepare the walnut pesto: combine toasted walnuts, basil, minced garlic, lemon juice, extra‑virgin olive oil, and ¼ tsp salt in a food processor. Pulse until coarse but well‑combined; stir in grated Parmesan if using.  
5. Remove the cauliflower steaks from the oven and let them rest for 2 minutes. Drizzle the walnut pesto over the steaks, allowing the warm glaze to melt into the pesto.  
6. Serve immediately, garnished with additional toasted walnut pieces and a sprinkle of fresh basil if desired.
title: Maple‑Glazed Cauliflower Steaks with Walnut Pesto

text:
Maple‑Glazed Carrot and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
