- 2 large carrots, peeled and sliced into thin ribbons
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 ½ cups cooked brown rice
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves for garnish
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper.  
3. Toss the carrot ribbons and chickpeas in the maple mixture until evenly coated.  
4. Spread the carrots and chickpeas in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
5. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the carrots are tender and the chickpeas are crisp.  
6. While the vegetables roast, divide the cooked brown rice among four serving bowls.  
7. Top each bowl of rice with the roasted carrots and chickpeas, then drizzle with lemon juice.  
8. Sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds and fresh cilantro over each bowl. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Maple‑Glazed Carrot and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

text:
Maple‑Glazed Eggplant and Quinoa Stuffed Peppers

Ingredients:
- 2 large red bell peppers, tops cut off and seeded
- 1 medium eggplant, diced
- 1 cup cooked quinoa
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Place the diced eggplant on a baking sheet, drizzle with olive oil, and toss with smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway, until golden and tender.
2. While the eggplant roasts, bring a pot of water to a boil, add the quinoa, reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes or until fluffy. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together the maple syrup and soy sauce. Add the minced garlic and stir to combine.
4. In a large mixing bowl, combine the roasted eggplant, cooked quinoa, and maple‑soy mixture. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed.
5. Stuff each prepared bell pepper with the quinoa‑eggplant mixture, pressing gently to fill them completely. Place the stuffed peppers upright in a baking dish.
6. Drizzle any remaining maple‑soy sauce over the tops of the peppers. Cover the dish with foil and bake for 15 minutes, then remove the foil and bake an additional 10 minutes until the peppers are tender and the filling is slightly caramelized.
7. Remove from the oven, sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds over each pepper, and garnish with fresh cilantro leaves before serving. Enjoy warm.
title: Maple‑Glazed Eggplant and Quinoa Stuffed Peppers

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu and Roasted Sweet Potato Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 block (14 oz) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp low‑sodium soy sauce
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 2 cups chopped kale, stems removed
- ¼ cup pumpkin seeds, toasted
- Zest and juice of 1 lime
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the diced sweet potatoes with ½ Tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and half the smoked paprika; spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until caramelized and tender.  
3. While the sweet potatoes roast, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, remaining olive oil, cumin, and the rest of the smoked paprika in a shallow dish. Add the tofu cubes, toss to coat, and let marinate for 5 minutes.  
4. After the sweet potatoes have roasted for 10 minutes, add the marinated tofu to the same baking sheet, spreading the pieces apart from the potatoes. Roast everything together for another 15‑20 minutes, until the tofu is golden and the edges are crisp.  
5. Meanwhile, combine quinoa and water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
6. In a large skillet over medium heat, add a splash of olive oil and sauté the kale for 3‑4 minutes, just until wilted. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper, then remove from heat.  
7. Assemble the bowls: start with a base of quinoa, top with roasted sweet potatoes, maple‑glazed tofu, sautéed kale, and toasted pumpkin seeds.  
8. Finish each bowl with a drizzle of lime juice, a sprinkle of lime zest, and an extra pinch of salt and pepper if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu and Roasted Sweet Potato Buddha Bowl

text:
Sesame‑Honey Glazed Tempeh with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp soy sauce
- 1 Tbsp sesame oil
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- ½ cup water
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 Tbsp lime juice
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 Tbsp olive oil (for roasting)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Toss the diced sweet potatoes with olive oil, salt, and pepper, spread them in a single layer, and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.  
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, whisk together maple syrup, soy sauce, sesame oil, garlic, and ginger in a bowl. Add the tempeh cubes, toss to coat, and let marinate for 5 minutes.  
3. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated tempeh and cook, stirring occasionally, for 6‑8 minutes until the pieces are caramelized and crisp on the edges. Remove from heat.  
4. In a medium saucepan, combine quinoa, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes.  
5. Fluff the quinoa with a fork and stir in lime zest, lime juice, and half of the chopped cilantro. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste.  
6. To assemble the bowl, divide the coconut‑lime quinoa among four serving bowls. Top each with a portion of roasted sweet potatoes and the sesame‑honey tempeh. Garnish with the remaining cilantro and, if desired, a drizzle of extra soy sauce or a squeeze of lime. Enjoy warm.
title: Sesame‑Honey Glazed Tempeh with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa

text:
Ginger‑Lime Shrimp with Coconut Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 12 large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup quinoa
- 1 ¾ cups coconut milk
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, grated
- Zest and juice of 1 lime
- 1 tablespoon soy sauce
- 1 teaspoon honey
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Rinse quinoa under cold water, then combine with coconut milk in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together lime zest, lime juice, soy sauce, honey, and a pinch of salt; set aside.  
3. Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium‑high heat. Add garlic and ginger, sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.  
4. Add shrimp to the skillet, season with pepper, and cook 2‑3 minutes per side until pink and opaque.  
5. Pour the lime‑soy mixture over the shrimp, stirring to coat; cook an additional minute until sauce thickens slightly.  
6. Serve the shrimp over the coconut quinoa, garnish with chopped cilantro and an extra squeeze of lime if desired.
title: Ginger‑Lime Shrimp with Coconut Quinoa

text:
Miso‑Sesame Glazed Salmon with Soba Noodle Salad

Ingredients:
- 4 salmon fillets (about 6 oz each)
- 3 Tbsp white miso paste
- 2 Tbsp soy sauce
- 1 Tbsp sesame oil
- 1 Tbsp honey
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 8 oz soba noodles
- 1 cup shredded red cabbage
- 1 cup julienned carrots
- ½ cup sliced cucumber
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- 2 Tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- 1 Tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tsp chili oil (optional)
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Lime wedges for serving

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, whisk together miso paste, soy sauce, sesame oil, honey, grated ginger, and minced garlic to form the glaze.
2. Pat the salmon fillets dry, season lightly with salt and pepper, and brush each side generously with the miso‑sesame glaze.
3. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Place the glazed salmon on a parchment‑lined baking sheet and bake for 10‑12 minutes, or until the fish flakes easily with a fork and the glaze is caramelized.
4. While the salmon cooks, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the soba noodles and cook according to package instructions (usually 4‑5 minutes). Drain, rinse under cold water, and set aside.
5. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked soba noodles, shredded red cabbage, julienned carrots, sliced cucumber, and chopped cilantro.
6. In a small dressing bowl, whisk together rice vinegar, a drizzle of sesame oil, chili oil (if using), and a pinch of salt. Pour the dressing over the noodle mixture and toss to coat evenly.
7. Divide the soba noodle salad among four serving plates. Top each with a glazed salmon fillet.
8. Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds over the salmon and salad, and serve with lime wedges on the side for squeezing. Enjoy warm or at room temperature.
title: Miso‑Sesame Glazed Salmon with Soba Noodle Salad

text:
Citrus‑Spiced Chickpea and Sweet Potato Skillet

Ingredients:
- 1 large sweet potato, diced
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 red bell pepper, sliced
- 1 small red onion, thinly sliced
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp orange zest
- 2 tbsp fresh orange juice
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- 1/4 tsp ground cinnamon
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- 1 tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat a large skillet over medium heat and add the olive oil.
2. Add the diced sweet potato and cook, stirring occasionally, for 8‑10 minutes until it begins to soften and turn golden.
3. Toss in the sliced red onion and bell pepper; sauté for another 4 minutes until the vegetables are tender-crisp.
4. Stir in the chickpeas, orange zest, cumin, smoked paprika, cinnamon, salt, and pepper; cook for 2 minutes to toast the spices.
5. Pour the orange juice over the mixture, scraping any browned bits from the pan, and let it simmer for 3‑4 minutes until the sweet potato is fully cooked and the sauce thickens.
6. Remove from heat, sprinkle with chopped cilantro and toasted pumpkin seeds if using, and serve warm.
title: Citrus‑Spiced Chickpea and Sweet Potato Skillet

text:
Spiced Orange Glazed Tempeh with Coconut Rice

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 1/4 cup freshly squeezed orange juice
- 2 Tbsp soy sauce (or tamari)
- 1 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 Tbsp lime juice
- 1 Tbsp neutral‑flavor oil (e.g., grapeseed)
- 1 cup jasmine rice
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup water
- Pinch of salt
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Lime wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Place the tempeh cubes in a shallow dish and set aside.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together orange juice, soy sauce, maple syrup, grated ginger, minced garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, and lime juice to create the glaze.  
3. Pour half of the glaze over the tempeh, toss to coat, and let marinate while you prepare the rice (about 10 minutes).  
4. Rinse the jasmine rice under cold water until the water runs clear. In a medium saucepan combine the rice, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.  
5. Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated tempeh and sauté for 4‑5 minutes, turning occasionally, until the pieces are golden brown on all sides.  
6. Pour the remaining glaze into the skillet with the tempeh, stirring to coat. Cook for an additional 2‑3 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken and cling to the tempeh.  
7. Serve the orange‑glazed tempeh over a bed of coconut jasmine rice, garnish with fresh cilantro and lime wedges. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Orange Glazed Tempeh with Coconut Rice

text:
Maple‑Glazed Lentil and Kale Stuffed Portobello Caps

Ingredients:
- 4 large portobello mushroom caps, stems removed
- 1 cup cooked green lentils
- 2 cups kale, stems removed and chopped
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- 1/4 tsp sea salt
- 1/4 tsp black pepper
- 2 tbsp toasted pine nuts (optional)
- 2 tbsp crumbled feta cheese (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat; add kale and sauté until wilted, about 3‑4 minutes.
3. Stir in cooked lentils, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper; cook for another 2 minutes, then drizzle in the maple syrup and mix until evenly coated.
4. Place the portobello caps gill‑side up on the prepared baking sheet; spoon the lentil‑kale mixture into each cap, pressing gently to fill.
5. Bake for 15‑18 minutes, until the mushrooms are tender and the filling is heated through.
6. Remove from the oven, sprinkle with toasted pine nuts and crumbled feta if using, and serve warm.
title: Maple‑Glazed Lentil and Kale Stuffed Portobello Caps

text:
Spiced Apricot Quinoa Salad with Toasted Pistachios

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 1/2 cup dried apricots, chopped
- 1/3 cup pistachios, shelled and toasted
- 1 small red onion, finely diced
- 1/2 cup fresh parsley, chopped
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp honey
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1/4 tsp ground cardamom
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Juice of 1 lemon

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan, combine quinoa and water; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes or until water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and transfer to a large bowl to cool.
2. While the quinoa cools, toast pistachios in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3‑4 minutes, stirring frequently, until fragrant and lightly browned. Set aside to cool.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, honey, lemon juice, cumin, cinnamon, cardamom, salt, and pepper to create the dressing.
4. Add the chopped apricots, diced red onion, and parsley to the cooled quinoa; toss gently to combine.
5. Pour the dressing over the quinoa mixture and stir until everything is evenly coated.
6. Fold in the toasted pistachios just before serving for a crunchy finish.
7. Serve the salad at room temperature or chilled, as a light main dish or side. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Apricot Quinoa Salad with Toasted Pistachios

text:
Garlic‑Rosemary Roasted Chickpea and Cauliflower Tacos

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 small head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 3 Tbsp olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 Tbsp fresh rosemary, finely chopped
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 8 small corn tortillas
- 1 lime, cut into wedges
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 avocado, sliced
- ¼ cup red onion, thinly sliced
- ½ cup salsa of choice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, combine the chickpeas, cauliflower florets, olive oil, minced garlic, rosemary, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; toss until everything is evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the cauliflower is golden and the chickpeas are crisp.  
4. While the vegetables roast, warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 30 seconds per side, or wrap them in foil and heat in the oven for the last 5 minutes of roasting.  
5. Assemble each taco by placing a generous spoonful of the roasted chickpea‑cauliflower mixture onto a tortilla, then top with red onion slices, avocado, cilantro, and a drizzle of salsa.  
6. Finish with a squeeze of fresh lime juice and serve immediately.
title: Garlic‑Rosemary Roasted Chickpea and Cauliflower Tacos

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Lentil Soup

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 tablespoon coconut oil
- 1 medium onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 teaspoon ground coriander
- 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper (optional)
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk
- Juice of 1 lime
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 cups fresh spinach leaves
- 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Heat the coconut oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes.
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add the cumin, coriander, smoked paprika, and cayenne pepper; toast the spices for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
4. Pour in the vegetable broth and bring the mixture to a gentle boil.
5. Add the rinsed red lentils, reduce heat to a simmer, and cook uncovered for 15‑20 minutes, or until the lentils are tender.
6. Stir in the coconut milk, lime juice, and lime zest; simmer for an additional 3 minutes to meld the flavors.
7. Season with salt and black pepper to taste, then fold in the fresh spinach leaves until wilted.
8. Ladle the soup into bowls and garnish each serving with chopped cilantro. Serve hot, optionally with a wedge of lime on the side.
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Lentil Soup

text:
Sesame‑Ginger Spicy Noodle Bowl with Roasted Veggies

Ingredients:
- 8 oz whole‑wheat spaghetti or rice noodles
- 1 cup broccoli florets
- 1 cup sliced carrots
- 1 red bell pepper, sliced into strips
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tbsp sesame oil
- 1 tbsp honey or maple syrup
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 garlic clove, minced
- 1 tsp sriracha or chili garlic sauce (adjust to taste)
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- 2 green onions, sliced
- Salt and pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss broccoli, carrots, and red bell pepper with olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 15‑20 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelized.
2. While the vegetables roast, cook the noodles according to package directions; drain and rinse under cold water to stop cooking.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, honey, grated ginger, minced garlic, and sriracha until smooth.
4. Transfer the cooked noodles to a large bowl, pour the sauce over them, and toss to coat evenly.
5. Add the roasted vegetables to the noodle bowl and gently mix to combine.
6. Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds and sliced green onions on top for garnish.
7. Serve warm or at room temperature, adjusting seasoning with extra soy sauce or sriracha if desired.
title: Sesame‑Ginger Spicy Noodle Bowl with Roasted Veggies

text:
Cinnamon‑Roasted Pumpkin and Lentil Curry

Ingredients:
- 1 small pumpkin, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1/2 tsp turmeric
- 1 can (14 oz) coconut milk
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tbsp tomato paste
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Cooked basmati rice, for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the pumpkin cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, cinnamon, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.
2. While the pumpkin roasts, heat the remaining olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
3. Stir in the garlic, ginger, cumin, smoked paprika, and turmeric; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Add the tomato paste and stir to combine, then pour in the vegetable broth and coconut milk. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil.
5. Add the rinsed red lentils, reduce heat to a simmer, and cook for 15‑20 minutes, or until the lentils are soft but not mushy.
6. Fold the roasted pumpkin into the curry, season with additional salt and pepper to taste, and let simmer for another 5 minutes to meld flavors.
7. Serve the curry over cooked basmati rice, garnished with fresh cilantro leaves. Enjoy warm!
title: Cinnamon‑Roasted Pumpkin and Lentil Curry

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa Bowls with Roasted Chickpeas

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- Salt and pepper, to taste
- 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
- 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger
- 1 tablespoon honey or maple syrup
- 2 cups mixed baby greens
- 1/2 cup shredded carrots
- 1/4 cup sliced almonds, toasted
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the chickpeas with olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking halfway, until crisp.
2. Meanwhile, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together lemon juice, grated ginger, and honey (or maple syrup); drizzle over the cooked quinoa and stir to combine.
4. Assemble each bowl: start with a base of quinoa, top with mixed greens, shredded carrots, roasted chickpeas, and toasted almonds.
5. Drizzle any remaining lemon‑ginger dressing over the bowl, garnish with cilantro leaves, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa Bowls with Roasted Chickpeas

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Salad

Ingredients:
- 3 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch sticks
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1/2 tsp sea salt
- 1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 4 cups mixed salad greens
- 1/4 cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped
- 1/4 cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the carrot sticks and chickpeas with maple syrup, cinnamon, olive oil, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the carrots are tender‑crisp and the chickpeas are golden and slightly crisp.  
5. While the vegetables roast, toast the walnuts in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2‑3 minutes, shaking the pan frequently; set aside to cool.  
6. In a large salad bowl, combine the mixed greens, roasted carrots, roasted chickpeas, toasted walnuts, and feta cheese if using.  
7. Drizzle the fresh lemon juice over the salad and toss gently to distribute.  
8. Serve warm or at room temperature, optionally with an extra drizzle of maple syrup for added sweetness.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Salad

text:
Maple‑Glazed Carrot and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 4 large carrots, peeled and sliced into thin ribbons
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 tbsp lime juice

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan, combine quinoa and water; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
2. While the quinoa cooks, preheat a large skillet over medium heat. Add olive oil, then toss in the carrot ribbons.
3. Drizzle the maple syrup over the carrots, sprinkle cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; stir to coat evenly.
4. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 6‑8 minutes until carrots are tender‑crisp and lightly caramelized.
5. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl; add the maple‑glazed carrots, toasted pumpkin seeds, and chopped cilantro.
6. Drizzle lime juice over the salad and toss gently to combine all flavors.
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired.
8. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with a few extra pumpkin seeds and cilantro leaves.
title: Maple‑Glazed Carrot and Quinoa Salad

text:
Maple‑Glazed Cauliflower Tacos with Avocado Crema

Ingredients:
- 1 small head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 8 small corn tortillas
- 1 ripe avocado
- 2 tbsp Greek yogurt
- 1 tsp lime juice
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- ¼ cup red cabbage, thinly sliced
- 1 jalapeño, thinly sliced (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together maple syrup, olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Toss the cauliflower florets in the mixture until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the cauliflower on the prepared baking sheet in a single layer and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway through, until caramelized and tender.  
4. While the cauliflower roasts, prepare the avocado crema: combine the avocado, Greek yogurt, lime juice, a pinch of salt, and blend until smooth. Set aside.  
5. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 30 seconds per side, or until pliable.  
6. Assemble each taco by placing a generous spoonful of roasted cauliflower onto a tortilla, then top with red cabbage, jalapeño slices (if using), and a drizzle of avocado crema.  
7. Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve immediately.
title: Maple‑Glazed Cauliflower Tacos with Avocado Crema

text:
Spiced Orange‑Glazed Chickpea and Quinoa Skillet

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 large orange, zest and juice
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp ground cinnamon
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1 small red onion, thinly sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- ½ cup frozen corn, thawed
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa and vegetable broth; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and fluff with a fork. Set aside.
2. While the quinoa cooks, whisk together orange zest, orange juice, maple syrup, soy sauce, smoked paprika, cumin, and cinnamon in a small bowl; set the glaze aside.
3. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the red onion and bell pepper; sauté 4‑5 minutes until softened.
4. Stir in garlic and cook for another 30 seconds until fragrant.
5. Add the chickpeas and corn to the skillet; pour half of the orange glaze over them. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5‑6 minutes until the chickpeas begin to caramelize.
6. Reduce heat to medium and stir in the cooked quinoa, mixing thoroughly. Drizzle the remaining orange glaze over the mixture and toss to coat evenly.
7. Season with salt and pepper to taste; continue cooking 2‑3 minutes to let flavors meld.
8. Remove from heat, garnish with chopped cilantro, and serve warm.
title: Spiced Orange‑Glazed Chickpea and Quinoa Skillet

text:
Spicy Sesame Ginger Shrimp with Coconut Lime Noodles

Ingredients:
- 12 oz rice noodles
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 2 tbsp sesame oil
- 3 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 red bell pepper, thinly sliced
- 1 cup snap peas
- 1/4 cup soy sauce
- 2 tbsp honey
- 1 tbsp sriracha
- Zest of 1 lime
- Juice of 2 limes
- 2 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- 3 green onions, sliced
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Cook the rice noodles according to package directions, drain, and rinse with cold water; set aside.  
2. In a small bowl whisk together soy sauce, honey, sriracha, lime zest, and lime juice; set the sauce aside.  
3. Heat sesame oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add garlic and ginger, sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.  
4. Add the shrimp and cook for 2‑3 minutes per side, until pink and opaque; remove shrimp and set aside.  
5. In the same skillet, add bell pepper and snap peas; stir‑fry for 3‑4 minutes until crisp‑tender.  
6. Return the shrimp to the skillet, pour the sauce over the mixture, and toss to coat; cook for another minute to heat through.  
7. Add the cooked noodles to the skillet, tossing everything together until the noodles are evenly coated with the sauce.  
8. Remove from heat, sprinkle toasted sesame seeds, sliced green onions, and cilantro over the top.  
9. Serve immediately, with extra lime wedges on the side if desired.
title: Spicy Sesame Ginger Shrimp with Coconut Lime Noodles

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Glazed Sweet Potato and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup cooked quinoa
- 2 cups baby spinach leaves
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese
- 1 Tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with ½ Tbsp olive oil, ½ tsp cinnamon, ½ tsp smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
3. In the same bowl, combine the chickpeas with the remaining olive oil, maple syrup, the other ½ tsp cinnamon, a pinch of salt, and pepper; toss to coat. Scatter the chickpeas around the sweet potatoes on the baking sheet.  
4. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning the vegetables halfway through, until the sweet potatoes are tender and caramelized and the chickpeas are crisp.  
5. While the vegetables roast, divide the cooked quinoa between two bowls, and top each with a handful of baby spinach.  
6. When the sweet potatoes and chickpeas are done, remove from the oven and let cool slightly. Spoon the roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas over the quinoa and spinach.  
7. Drizzle each bowl with lemon juice, sprinkle with crumbled feta, and garnish with toasted pumpkin seeds. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Glazed Sweet Potato and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

text:
Smoky Chipotle Lime Chickpea Tacos

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp chipotle chili powder
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp garlic powder
- Salt and black pepper, to taste
- Juice of 1 lime
- 8 small corn tortillas
- ½ cup red cabbage, thinly sliced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- 1 avocado, sliced
- Lime wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat a skillet over medium heat and add the olive oil.
2. Toss the chickpeas with smoked paprika, chipotle chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, salt, and pepper; spread them in the skillet.
3. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 6‑8 minutes until the chickpeas are crisp and fragrant.
4. Remove from heat and stir in the lime juice; set aside.
5. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry pan or microwave until pliable.
6. Assemble each taco by layering crispy chickpeas, red cabbage, cilantro, feta (if using), and avocado slices on a tortilla.
7. Serve with extra lime wedges and enjoy immediately.
title: Smoky Chipotle Lime Chickpea Tacos

text:
Lemon‑Cilantro Quinoa with Grilled Halloumi and Roasted Cherry Tomatoes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 cup cherry tomatoes, halved
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 8 oz halloumi cheese, sliced 1/2‑inch thick
- 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, chopped
- Zest of 1 lemon
- Juice of 1 lemon
- Freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the cherry tomatoes with olive oil, smoked paprika, and salt, then spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 15‑20 minutes, until blistered.
2. While the tomatoes roast, combine quinoa and water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
3. Heat a grill pan over medium‑high heat. Brush the halloumi slices lightly with olive oil and grill 2‑3 minutes per side, until golden brown and slightly melted.
4. In a large bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted tomatoes, grilled halloumi, chopped cilantro, lemon zest, and lemon juice. Toss gently to mix.
5. Season with freshly ground black pepper and additional salt if needed. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Cilantro Quinoa with Grilled Halloumi and Roasted Cherry Tomatoes

text:
Spicy Coconut Lime Shrimp Tacos with Pineapple Slaw

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 2 tbsp coconut oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp cayenne pepper
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- Zest of 1 lime
- Juice of 2 limes
- 2 tbsp coconut milk
- 8 small corn tortillas
- 1 cup fresh pineapple, finely diced
- ½ cup red cabbage, thinly sliced
- ¼ cup red onion, thinly sliced
- 2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 tbsp honey
- 1 tbsp rice vinegar
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, combine smoked paprika, cayenne, cumin, lime zest, lime juice, coconut milk, and a pinch of salt; whisk to create a marinade.
2. Add the shrimp to the marinade, toss to coat, and let sit for 10 minutes while you prepare the slaw.
3. In a separate bowl, mix diced pineapple, red cabbage, red onion, cilantro, honey, rice vinegar, and a pinch of salt; stir until well combined and set aside.
4. Heat coconut oil in a skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated shrimp in a single layer and cook 2‑3 minutes per side, until pink and slightly charred.
5. Warm the corn tortillas on a dry skillet or directly over a flame for 20‑30 seconds per side, keeping them pliable.
6. Assemble each taco by placing a few shrimp on a tortilla, topping with a generous spoonful of pineapple slaw, and finishing with an extra drizzle of lime juice if desired.
7. Serve immediately, garnished with additional cilantro and lime wedges.
title: Spicy Coconut Lime Shrimp Tacos with Pineapple Slaw

text:
Maple‑Glazed Carrot and Lentil Soup

Ingredients:
- 2 lb carrots, peeled and sliced
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 large onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
2. Stir in the minced garlic, cumin, and smoked paprika; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add the sliced carrots and drizzle the maple syrup over them, stirring to coat. Cook for 3 minutes, allowing the carrots to caramelize slightly.
4. Pour in the vegetable broth and bring the mixture to a gentle boil. Reduce heat to a simmer and add the rinsed red lentils.
5. Simmer uncovered for 20‑25 minutes, or until the carrots are tender and the lentils have broken down, stirring occasionally.
6. Using an immersion blender (or transferring to a countertop blender in batches), puree the soup until smooth. If the soup is too thick, add a splash more broth or water to reach desired consistency.
7. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Return to low heat to warm through.
8. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with chopped fresh parsley, and drizzle a tiny extra drizzle of maple syrup if desired. Serve hot.
title: Maple‑Glazed Carrot and Lentil Soup

text:
Lemon‑Dill Quinoa Salad with Grilled Asparagus and Feta

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 1 bunch asparagus, trimmed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 lemon, zest and juice
- 2 tbsp fresh dill, chopped
- 1/3 cup crumbled feta cheese
- 1/4 cup toasted pine nuts
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a saucepan, combine quinoa and water; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
2. While the quinoa cooks, preheat a grill or grill pan over medium-high heat. Toss the asparagus with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper, then grill 3‑4 minutes per side until tender‑crisp and lightly charred. Slice the asparagus into 1‑inch pieces.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, chopped dill, salt, and pepper to create the dressing.
4. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, grilled asparagus, feta cheese, and toasted pine nuts. Drizzle the lemon‑dill dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat evenly.
5. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with extra dill or a lemon wedge if desired.
title: Lemon‑Dill Quinoa Salad with Grilled Asparagus and Feta

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu and Roasted Beet Salad

Ingredients:
- 14 oz firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp low‑sodium soy sauce
- 1 Tbsp apple cider vinegar
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 2 medium beets, peeled and cut into wedges
- 4 cups arugula
- ¼ cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese
- 2 Tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, apple cider vinegar, smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt; toss the tofu cubes in the mixture and let them marinate for 10 minutes.  
3. Meanwhile, drizzle the beet wedges with 1 Tbsp olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and spread them on the prepared baking sheet. Roast the beets for 20 minutes.  
4. After the beets have roasted for 10 minutes, add the marinated tofu to the same sheet, arranging the pieces in a single layer. Roast both beets and tofu for an additional 15 minutes, turning the tofu once, until the tofu is golden and the beets are tender.  
5. While the vegetables finish cooking, whisk together the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, lemon juice, a pinch of salt, and black pepper to create the dressing.  
6. In a large salad bowl, combine the arugula, roasted beet wedges, and warm tofu cubes. Drizzle the dressing over the salad, toss gently to coat, then top with toasted walnuts and crumbled feta. Serve immediately.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu and Roasted Beet Salad

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Chickpea and Sweet Potato Curry

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 can (13.5 oz) coconut milk
- 1 ½ tbsp curry powder
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 inch piece fresh ginger, minced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 cups fresh spinach leaves
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and ginger, sautéing until fragrant, about 1 minute.  
2. Stir in the curry powder, ground cumin, and lime zest; cook for another 30 seconds to release the spices’ aromas.  
3. Add the diced sweet potatoes and chickpeas, tossing to coat them evenly with the spice mixture.  
4. Pour in the coconut milk and bring the mixture to a gentle simmer. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and cook until the sweet potatoes are tender, 12–15 minutes.  
5. Stir in the fresh lime juice, then season with salt and pepper to taste.  
6. Fold in the spinach leaves and cook just until wilted, about 2 minutes.  
7. Remove the pan from heat and garnish with chopped cilantro. Serve hot over steamed rice or quinoa.
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Chickpea and Sweet Potato Curry

text:
Maple‑Spiced Tempeh with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp low‑sodium soy sauce
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground black pepper
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup water
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 Tbsp lime juice
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Pinch of sea salt

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, whisk together maple syrup, soy sauce, garlic, ginger, smoked paprika, black pepper, and olive oil; add the tempeh cubes and toss to coat. Let marinate for 15 minutes.
2. While the tempeh marinates, combine quinoa, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes.
3. Fluff the quinoa with a fork and stir in lime zest, lime juice, and chopped cilantro; set aside.
4. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated tempeh in a single layer and cook, stirring occasionally, until golden and caramelized, about 6‑8 minutes.
5. Divide the coconut‑lime quinoa among serving bowls, top with the maple‑spiced tempeh, and garnish with extra cilantro or a drizzle of lime juice if desired. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Spiced Tempeh with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa

text:
Saffron‑Infused Coconut Lentil Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 cup green lentils, rinsed
- 1 cup basmati rice
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 small onion, finely diced
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/2 teaspoon ground coriander
- 1 pinch saffron threads, soaked in 2 tbsp warm water
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1/2 cup frozen peas
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)
- Toasted slivered almonds (optional)

Instructions:
1. Heat olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes.  
2. Stir in the minced garlic, cumin, and coriander; cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.  
3. Add the rinsed lentils and rice, stirring to coat them with the spices and oil.  
4. Pour in the soaked saffron with its liquid, coconut milk, and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils and rice are tender and the liquid is absorbed.  
5. During the last 5 minutes of cooking, fold in the frozen peas; they will heat through.  
6. Season the pilaf with salt and black pepper to taste. Remove from heat and let it sit, covered, for 5 minutes.  
7. Fluff the pilaf with a fork, then transfer to a serving bowl. Garnish with chopped cilantro and toasted slivered almonds, if desired. Serve warm.
title: Saffron‑Infused Coconut Lentil Pilaf

text:
Coconut‑Lime Baked Halibut with Herb Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 4 halibut fillets (about 6 oz each)
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 Tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tsp lime zest
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 Tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or low‑sodium vegetable broth
- 1 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- 1 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and cubed
- 2 cups chopped kale, stems removed
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a shallow dish, whisk together coconut milk, lime juice, lime zest, garlic, ginger, 1 Tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper. Place the halibut fillets in the mixture, turning to coat, and let marinate while you prepare the vegetables.  
3. Toss the sweet potato cubes with the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper, then spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 10 minutes.  
4. Remove the baking sheet, push the sweet potatoes to one side, and add the marinated halibut fillets (drain excess sauce). Return to the oven and bake for 12‑15 minutes, until the fish flakes easily with a fork and the sweet potatoes are tender.  
5. While the fish bakes, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork, then stir in parsley, cilantro, and a pinch of salt.  
6. In a large skillet over medium heat, add a splash of olive oil and sauté the chopped kale until wilted, about 3‑4 minutes; season with salt and pepper.  
7. To serve, spoon a bed of herb quinoa onto each plate, top with a portion of sautéed kale, place a baked halibut fillet beside the vegetables, and drizzle any remaining pan juices over the fish. Garnish with extra lime zest if desired.
title: Coconut‑Lime Baked Halibut with Herb Quinoa

text:
Herb‑Crusted Cod with Lemon‑Butter Orzo and Roasted Asparagus

Ingredients:
- 4 cod fillets (about 6 oz each)
- 1 cup orzo pasta
- 1 lb asparagus, trimmed and cut into 2‑inch pieces
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 3 Tbsp unsalted butter, divided
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- 1 Tbsp chopped fresh thyme
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- 1 tsp garlic powder
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the asparagus with 1 Tbsp olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and spread in a single layer on the prepared sheet. Roast for 12‑15 minutes, until tender‑crisp and lightly browned.  
3. While the asparagus roasts, combine parsley, thyme, oregano, garlic powder, salt, and pepper in a shallow dish. Pat the cod fillets dry, then press each side into the herb mixture to coat evenly.  
4. Heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the cod fillets and cook 3‑4 minutes per side, or until the fish is opaque and flakes easily with a fork. Remove from heat and keep warm.  
5. Meanwhile, bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add the orzo and cook according to package directions, usually 8‑10 minutes, until al dente. Drain, return to the pot, and stir in 2 Tbsp butter, lemon zest, and lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper to taste.  
6. To serve, divide the lemon‑butter orzo among plates, top with a cod fillet, and arrange the roasted asparagus alongside. Garnish with extra chopped parsley if desired. Enjoy immediately.
title: Herb‑Crusted Cod with Lemon‑Butter Orzo and Roasted Asparagus

text:
Spiced Orange‑Glazed Tempeh with Coconut Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 block (8 oz) firm tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- ¼ cup fresh orange juice
- 2 Tbsp soy sauce
- 1 Tbsp maple syrup
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- ½ cup water
- Zest of 1 orange
- Juice of ½ lime
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a shallow bowl, whisk together orange juice, soy sauce, maple syrup, smoked paprika, cumin, garlic, and orange zest; set aside.
2. Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add tempeh strips and sear 3‑4 minutes per side until golden brown.
3. Pour the orange‑glaze over the tempeh, reduce heat to low, and simmer 5‑7 minutes, turning once, until the sauce thickens and coats the tempeh; season with salt and pepper.
4. Meanwhile, combine quinoa, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and quinoa is fluffy.
5. Remove quinoa from heat and stir in lime juice and chopped cilantro; adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed.
6. Serve the spiced orange‑glazed tempeh atop a bed of coconut quinoa, garnished with extra cilantro and a drizzle of any remaining glaze. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Orange‑Glazed Tempeh with Coconut Quinoa

text:
Curry‑Spiced Sweet Potato and Black Bean Enchiladas

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 teaspoon curry powder
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 8 small corn tortillas
- 1 cup shredded Monterey Jack cheese
- ½ cup salsa verde
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)
- Lime wedges (for serving)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. Toss the diced sweet potatoes with olive oil, cumin, curry powder, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.
3. Roast the sweet potatoes for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.
4. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine the black beans with a pinch of salt and pepper in a bowl; set aside.
5. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet for 10‑15 seconds per side, just until pliable.
6. Assemble each enchilada: place a spoonful of roasted sweet potatoes and a spoonful of black beans onto a tortilla, drizzle a little salsa verde, and roll tightly.
7. Arrange the rolled enchiladas seam‑side down in a greased 9‑inch baking dish; sprinkle the shredded cheese evenly over the top.
8. Bake for 12‑15 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbly.
9. Remove from the oven, garnish with chopped cilantro, and serve with lime wedges on the side. Enjoy!
title: Curry‑Spiced Sweet Potato and Black Bean Enchiladas

text:
Harissa‑Roasted Sweet Potato and Lentil Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 ½ cups cooked green or brown lentils (or 1 cup dry lentils, cooked)
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 Tbsp harissa paste
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 cups baby spinach leaves
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- 2 Tbsp lemon juice
- 1 Tbsp tahini
- 1 tsp honey or maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp warm water (more if needed)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with olive oil, harissa paste, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the seasoned sweet potatoes in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning once, until tender and caramelized.  
4. While the sweet potatoes roast, prepare the dressing: whisk together lemon juice, tahini, honey (or maple syrup), and warm water in a small bowl until smooth; season with a pinch of salt.  
5. In a skillet over medium heat, briefly sauté the cooked lentils for 2‑3 minutes to warm them through and develop a light crust.  
6. To assemble each bowl, place a handful of baby spinach at the bottom, then add a scoop of warm lentils and a generous portion of harissa‑roasted sweet potatoes.  
7. Drizzle the tahini‑lemon dressing over the top, sprinkle with toasted pumpkin seeds, and add crumbled feta if using.  
8. Serve immediately, or let the bowls cool and store in airtight containers for up to 3 days. Enjoy!
title: Harissa‑Roasted Sweet Potato and Lentil Buddha Bowl

text:
Maple‑Glazed Cauliflower Steaks with Walnut‑Pomegranate Chimichurri

Ingredients:
- 1 large cauliflower head, sliced into 1‑inch thick steaks
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped
- ¼ cup pomegranate arils
- 2 Tbsp fresh parsley, finely chopped
- 1 Tbsp fresh mint, finely chopped
- 1 Tbsp red wine vinegar
- 1 tsp honey
- 1 small garlic clove, minced
- 2 Tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil (for chimichurri)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together maple syrup, 1 Tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper.  
3. Brush both sides of each cauliflower steak generously with the maple mixture and place on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, flipping halfway through, until the cauliflower is tender and caramelized at the edges.  
5. While the cauliflower roasts, prepare the walnut‑pomegranate chimichurri: combine toasted walnuts, pomegranate arils, parsley, mint, red wine vinegar, honey, minced garlic, and 2 Tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil in a bowl; stir gently to coat.  
6. Once the cauliflower steaks are done, transfer them to a serving platter. Spoon the walnut‑pomegranate chimichurri over the top, allowing some to drizzle onto the plate.  
7. Serve warm, garnished with additional pomegranate seeds and a drizzle of extra‑virgin olive oil if desired. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Cauliflower Steaks with Walnut‑Pomegranate Chimichurri

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Garlic Brussels Sprouts

Ingredients:
- 1 block (14 oz) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp garlic powder
- 1 lb Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional garnish: toasted sesame seeds and chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, smoked paprika, and garlic powder. Add the tofu cubes, toss to coat, and set aside.  
3. In a separate bowl, combine the Brussels sprouts, olive oil, minced garlic, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet, cut‑side down.  
4. Roast the Brussels sprouts for 12 minutes, then remove the sheet from the oven and give the sprouts a quick stir.  
5. Add the glazed tofu cubes to the same baking sheet, arranging them among the sprouts. Return the sheet to the oven and roast for an additional 15‑18 minutes, or until the tofu is caramelized and the Brussels sprouts are crisp‑tender and golden.  
6. Remove from the oven, transfer to a serving platter, and sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds and chopped parsley, if using. Serve warm as a main dish or over cooked grains.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Garlic Brussels Sprouts

text:
Harissa‑Roasted Eggplant and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 Tbsp harissa paste
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice
- 1 cucumber, diced
- 1 cup cherry tomatoes, halved
- ¼ cup fresh mint leaves, chopped
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the eggplant cubes with harissa paste, olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until tender and lightly charred.  
2. While the eggplant roasts, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and fluff with a fork.  
3. In a large bowl, whisk together lemon juice, a drizzle of olive oil, and a pinch of salt and pepper to make a quick dressing.  
4. Add the cooked quinoa, roasted eggplant, diced cucumber, cherry tomatoes, and chopped mint to the bowl; toss gently to combine and coat with the dressing.  
5. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if needed.  
6. Serve the salad at room temperature or chilled, topped with crumbled feta cheese if desired. Enjoy!
title: Harissa‑Roasted Eggplant and Quinoa Salad

text:
Roasted Garlic‑Lime Cauliflower Steaks with Quinoa Tabbouleh

Ingredients:
- 1 large cauliflower head, sliced into 1‑inch thick “steaks”
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- Zest and juice of 1 lime
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1/2 cup chopped fresh parsley
- 1/4 cup diced red onion
- 1/4 cup toasted pine nuts
- 2 tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil (for the tabbouleh)
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- Pinch of sea salt

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, combine olive oil, minced garlic, lime zest, lime juice, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Brush both sides of the cauliflower steaks generously with the mixture.  
3. Arrange the steaks on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, flipping halfway through, until golden‑brown and tender.  
4. While the cauliflower roasts, bring vegetable broth to a boil in a saucepan. Add the rinsed quinoa, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and fluff with a fork.  
5. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large bowl. Stir in chopped parsley, diced red onion, toasted pine nuts, extra‑virgin olive oil, lemon juice, and a pinch of sea salt. Mix gently to combine.  
6. To serve, place a cauliflower steak on each plate, spoon a generous mound of quinoa tabbouleh alongside, and drizzle any remaining pan juices over the top. Enjoy warm or at room temperature.
title: Roasted Garlic‑Lime Cauliflower Steaks with Quinoa Tabbouleh

text:
Roasted Garlic and Herb Sweet Potato Gnocchi with Sage Butter

Ingredients:
- 1 lb (450 g) store‑bought or homemade sweet potato gnocchi
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp dried rosemary
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 4 Tbsp unsalted butter
- 10 fresh sage leaves, roughly torn
- ¼ cup grated Parmesan cheese
- Optional: ¼ cup toasted walnut halves, roughly chopped

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the gnocchi with olive oil, minced garlic, rosemary, thyme, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread them in a single layer on a parchment‑lined baking sheet.  
2. Roast for 12‑15 minutes, turning once, until the gnocchi are golden‑brown and slightly crisp on the edges.  
3. While the gnocchi roast, melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the torn sage leaves and cook for 1‑2 minutes, allowing the butter to turn fragrant and lightly browned.  
4. Transfer the roasted gnocchi to the skillet, tossing gently to coat them in the sage‑brown butter. Cook for an additional minute to let the flavors meld.  
5. Remove from heat, sprinkle with grated Parmesan and, if using, toasted walnuts. Serve immediately, garnished with a few extra sage leaves if desired.
title: Roasted Garlic and Herb Sweet Potato Gnocchi with Sage Butter

text:
Cinnamon‑Roasted Apple and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 2 large apples, cored and sliced into ½‑inch wedges
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp honey
- ¼ cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley, finely chopped

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan, combine the rinsed quinoa and water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork and set aside to cool slightly.  
2. While the quinoa cooks, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).  
3. In a mixing bowl, toss the apple wedges with the olive oil, ground cinnamon, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of black pepper until evenly coated.  
4. Spread the apples in a single layer on a parchment‑lined baking sheet. Roast for 12‑15 minutes, turning once, until the apples are tender and lightly caramelized. Remove from the oven and let cool for a few minutes.  
5. In a large salad bowl, whisk together the lemon juice, honey, a drizzle of olive oil, and a generous pinch of salt and pepper to create the dressing.  
6. Add the cooked quinoa to the bowl with the dressing, tossing to combine.  
7. Gently fold in the roasted apple wedges, toasted walnuts, and crumbled feta cheese.  
8. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or honey if desired.  
9. Sprinkle the fresh parsley over the top and serve the salad warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Roasted Apple and Quinoa Salad

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa Bowl with Roasted Chickpeas

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp sea salt
- 1 lime, zest and juice
- 1 Tbsp coconut milk
- 1 small red onion, thinly sliced
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- ½ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- ¼ cup toasted coconut flakes
- Optional: 1 avocado, sliced for topping

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the chickpeas with olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, and sea salt until evenly coated. Spread them on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking halfway, until crisp and golden.  
3. While the chickpeas roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.  
4. In a small mixing bowl, whisk together lime zest, lime juice, coconut milk, and a pinch of salt to create the dressing.  
5. Assemble the bowl: start with a base of quinoa, then add roasted chickpeas, sliced red onion, diced red bell pepper, and avocado if using. Drizzle the coconut‑lime dressing over the top.  
6. Garnish with chopped cilantro and toasted coconut flakes. Serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa Bowl with Roasted Chickpeas

text:
Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Carrot and Lentil Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch rounds
- 1 cup cooked green lentils (or 1/2 cup dry lentils, cooked)
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 Tbsp fresh parsley, finely chopped
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice
- 2 Tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.  
3. Add the carrot rounds to the bowl and toss until evenly coated with the spice mixture.  
4. Spread the carrots in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and caramelized.  
5. While the carrots roast, place the cooked lentils in a mixing bowl. Add lemon juice, a pinch of salt, and half of the chopped parsley; toss gently.  
6. Once the carrots are done, let them cool slightly, then combine them with the seasoned lentils.  
7. Transfer the salad to a serving platter, sprinkle the remaining parsley and toasted pumpkin seeds on top, and drizzle any remaining pan juices over the dish.  
8. Serve warm or at room temperature as a hearty main or side.
title: Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Carrot and Lentil Salad

text:
Cinnamon‑Roasted Pear and Quinoa Salad with Walnut Vinaigrette

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 2 ripe pears, cored and sliced into wedges
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- 2 tablespoons olive oil, divided
- ½ cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped
- 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
- 1 teaspoon maple syrup
- ¼ teaspoon sea salt
- ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- 2 cups baby arugula

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the pear wedges with 1 tablespoon olive oil, ground cinnamon, and a pinch of salt; spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
3. Roast the pears for 15‑18 minutes, turning once, until they are caramelized and tender. Remove from the oven and set aside to cool slightly.  
4. While the pears roast, combine quinoa and water in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes or until the water is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, lemon juice, maple syrup, sea salt, and black pepper to create the vinaigrette.  
6. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted pear wedges, toasted walnuts, and baby arugula. Drizzle the walnut vinaigrette over the salad and toss gently to coat evenly.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Roasted Pear and Quinoa Salad with Walnut Vinaigrette

text:
Maple‑Saffron Roasted Cauliflower with Lentil Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 large head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup
- ½ teaspoon saffron threads
- 2 tablespoons warm water
- 3 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 medium onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- ½ teaspoon salt (plus more to taste)
- ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)
- Lemon wedges, for serving (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, combine the maple syrup, 1 tablespoon olive oil, and a pinch of salt; toss the cauliflower florets in this mixture until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the cauliflower on the prepared baking sheet in a single layer and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway through, until golden‑brown and tender.  
4. While the cauliflower roasts, place the saffron threads in the warm water and let steep for 5 minutes.  
5. In a medium saucepan, heat the remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 4‑5 minutes until translucent.  
6. Stir in the minced garlic and cumin; cook for another 30 seconds until fragrant.  
7. Add the rinsed lentils, vegetable broth, salt, and the saffron‑infused water (including the threads). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and the liquid is absorbed.  
8. Fluff the cooked lentils with a fork and adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.  
9. To serve, divide the lentil pilaf among plates, top with the maple‑roasted cauliflower, and sprinkle chopped parsley over the top. Add a lemon wedge on the side for a bright finish, if desired.
title: Maple‑Saffron Roasted Cauliflower with Lentil Pilaf

text:
Spiced Orange‑Maple Tempeh with Coconut Quinoa  

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- ¼ cup fresh orange juice
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp low‑sodium soy sauce
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 Tbsp coconut oil, divided
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and diced ½‑inch
- 2 cups kale leaves, stems removed and torn
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- ½ cup water
- Zest of 1 orange
- Juice of ½ lime
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a shallow bowl, whisk together orange juice, maple syrup, soy sauce, garlic, ginger, orange zest, and a pinch of salt. Add the tempeh cubes, toss to coat, and let marinate while you prepare the other components (about 10 minutes).  
2. Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Spread the diced sweet potato on a parchment‑lined baking sheet, drizzle with ½ Tbsp coconut oil, season with salt and pepper, and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender.  
3. In a medium saucepan, combine quinoa, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and stir in lime juice and cilantro.  
4. Heat the remaining ½ Tbsp coconut oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Remove tempeh from the marinade (reserve the liquid) and add to the skillet. Sear for 3‑4 minutes per side, until caramelized. Pour the reserved marinade into the pan, reduce heat to medium, and cook 2‑3 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the tempeh.  
5. Add the roasted sweet potato and kale to the skillet with the tempeh. Toss everything together and cook for another 2 minutes, just until the kale wilts. Adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired.  
6. Serve the spiced orange‑maple tempeh mixture over a bed of coconut quinoa, garnished with extra cilantro and a drizzle of maple syrup if you like extra sweetness. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Orange‑Maple Tempeh with Coconut Quinoa

text:
Spicy Harissa Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp harissa paste
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 cups baby spinach leaves
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice
- 2 Tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds
- Optional: fresh cilantro leaves for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes and chickpeas with harissa paste, olive oil, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway through, until the sweet potatoes are tender and lightly caramelized.  
4. While the vegetables roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the quinoa is fluffy and the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
5. In a large serving bowl, layer the cooked quinoa, roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas, and fresh baby spinach. Drizzle lemon juice over the top and toss gently to combine.  
6. Sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds and optional cilantro over each bowl for added crunch and freshness. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Spicy Harissa Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

text:
Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Chickpea Tacos

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 8 small corn tortillas
- 1 ripe avocado, sliced
- 1 lime, cut into wedges
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Optional: hot sauce or sliced jalapeño for heat

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the diced sweet potatoes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, ½ tsp cumin, ½ tsp smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
3. Roast the sweet potatoes for 20 minutes, stirring halfway through, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
4. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine the chickpeas, maple syrup, remaining ½ tsp cumin, ½ tsp smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt in a separate bowl.  
5. After the sweet potatoes have roasted 20 minutes, add the glazed chickpeas to the same baking sheet, stirring to coat. Roast for an additional 10‑12 minutes, until the chickpeas are slightly crisp and the glaze is sticky.  
6. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 30 seconds per side, or wrap them in foil and heat in the oven for 5 minutes.  
7. Assemble each taco by placing a generous spoonful of the roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas onto a tortilla, then top with avocado slices, a drizzle of any remaining maple glaze from the pan, cilantro, and a squeeze of lime juice. Add hot sauce or jalapeño if desired.  
8. Serve immediately and enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Chickpea Tacos

text:
Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Chickpea and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup sliced toasted almonds
- ¼ cup dried cranberries
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the chickpeas with 1 Tbsp olive oil, thyme, smoked paprika, lemon zest, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until crisp and golden.  
3. While the chickpeas roast, combine quinoa and water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.  
4. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl. Add the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, lemon juice, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Toss to combine.  
5. Once the chickpeas are cool enough to handle, add them to the quinoa along with toasted almonds, dried cranberries, and parsley if using. Gently mix everything together.  
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional lemon juice, salt, or pepper as desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Chickpea and Quinoa Salad

text:
Maple‑Glazed Eggplant and Lentil Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cubed
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- 1/4 tsp ground cinnamon
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 can (14 oz) diced tomatoes
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat a large pot over medium heat and add the olive oil. Sauté the onion until translucent, about 4 minutes, then add the garlic and cook for another minute.  
2. Stir in the smoked paprika, cumin, and cinnamon, letting the spices toast briefly to release their aroma.  
3. Add the cubed eggplant and drizzle the maple syrup over it; toss to coat and cook for 5‑7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the eggplant begins to soften and caramelize.  
4. Pour in the vegetable broth and diced tomatoes, then add the rinsed lentils. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to a gentle simmer.  
5. Cover and simmer for 25‑30 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and the stew has thickened. Stir occasionally and season with salt and pepper to taste.  
6. Serve hot, garnished with a sprinkle of fresh parsley. Enjoy the sweet‑smoky harmony of maple‑glazed eggplant and hearty lentils.
title: Maple‑Glazed Eggplant and Lentil Stew

text:
Spiced Cardamom Carrot and Lentil Soup

Ingredients:
- 2 lb carrots, peeled and diced
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch piece fresh ginger, grated
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 tsp ground cardamom
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp ground coriander
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.  
2. Stir in the garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
3. Add the diced carrots, ground cardamom, cumin, and coriander. Toss to coat the vegetables with the spices and cook for 2 minutes.  
4. Pour in the vegetable broth and bring the mixture to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes, or until the carrots are tender.  
5. Add the rinsed red lentils and continue to simmer, uncovered, for another 10‑12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are soft and the soup has thickened.  
6. Stir in the coconut milk, then season with salt and pepper to taste. Simmer for an additional 2 minutes to heat through.  
7. Using an immersion blender (or transferring to a countertop blender in batches), blend the soup until smooth and velvety.  
8. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve hot.
title: Spiced Cardamom Carrot and Lentil Soup

text:
Cinnamon‑Honey Roasted Parsnip and Lentil Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 large parsnips, peeled and cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 cup cooked green or brown lentils, rinsed and drained
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 2 cups fresh arugula
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese
- 2 Tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cubed parsnips with olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the seasoned parsnips in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway through, until golden and tender.  
4. While the parsnips roast, place the cooked lentils in a mixing bowl. Add the lemon juice and a pinch of salt; toss gently.  
5. Once the parsnips are done, let them cool slightly, then add them to the bowl with the lentils.  
6. Fold in the fresh arugula, crumbled feta, and toasted pumpkin seeds, mixing just enough to distribute the ingredients without wilting the greens.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a drizzle of lemon juice if desired.  
8. Serve the salad warm or at room temperature, garnished with an extra sprinkle of cinnamon or pumpkin seeds if you like.
title: Cinnamon‑Honey Roasted Parsnip and Lentil Salad

text:
Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Black Bean Burrito Bowl

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth or water
- 1 (15‑oz) can black beans, drained and rinsed
- 1 avocado, sliced
- 1 lime, cut into wedges
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- ¼ cup crumbled feta or cotija cheese (optional)
- Hot sauce or chipotle mayo, for serving (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
