2. In a large bowl, toss the cubed sweet potatoes with olive oil, maple syrup, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the sweet potatoes in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway through, until tender and caramelized.  
4. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.  
5. In a small saucepan, gently heat the black beans over medium heat until warmed through; season with a pinch of salt and pepper.  
6. To assemble each bowl, start with a base of quinoa, then add a generous scoop of roasted sweet potatoes and black beans. Top with avocado slices, a sprinkle of cilantro, and a wedge of lime.  
7. If desired, drizzle with hot sauce or chipotle mayo and sprinkle with feta or cotija cheese. Serve immediately and enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Black Bean Burrito Bowl

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Chickpea and Kale Stir‑Fry

Ingredients:
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 3 cups chopped kale, stems removed
- 1 medium red bell pepper, thinly sliced
- 1 small red onion, thinly sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tbsp coconut oil
- 2 tbsp coconut milk
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 tbsp toasted coconut flakes, for garnish
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Heat the coconut oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat until shimmering.  
2. Add the sliced red onion and bell pepper; sauté for 3–4 minutes until they begin to soften.  
3. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.  
4. Sprinkle the cumin, smoked paprika, and cayenne (if using) over the vegetables; stir to coat.  
5. Add the cooked chickpeas and kale to the skillet; toss everything together and cook for 4–5 minutes, allowing the kale to wilt.  
6. Pour in the coconut milk and lime juice, stirring to create a light sauce; simmer for 2 minutes until the mixture is glossy.  
7. Season with salt and black pepper to taste; adjust lime or spice levels if desired.  
8. Transfer the stir‑fry to serving bowls, garnish with toasted coconut flakes and chopped cilantro, and serve immediately.
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Chickpea and Kale Stir‑Fry

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Farro Salad with Roasted Chickpeas and Pomegranate  

Ingredients:
- 1 cup farro, rinsed
- 2 cups water or low‑sodium vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup pomegranate seeds
- ½ cup toasted sliced almonds
- ¼ cup fresh mint leaves, chopped
- ¼ cup fresh parsley, chopped
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tablespoons lemon juice
- 1 tablespoon grated fresh ginger
- 2 teaspoons honey or maple syrup
- 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Toss the chickpeas with olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper; spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking halfway, until crisp and golden.
2. While the chickpeas roast, combine farro and water (or broth) in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 20‑25 minutes until tender but still chewy. Drain any excess liquid and let cool slightly.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together lemon zest, lemon juice, grated ginger, honey (or maple syrup), Dijon mustard, and a pinch of salt to create the dressing.
4. Transfer the cooked farro to a large mixing bowl. Add the roasted chickpeas, pomegranate seeds, toasted almonds, mint, parsley, and drizzle the dressing over the top.
5. Toss gently to combine, adjusting seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if desired.
6. Serve the salad warm, at room temperature, or chilled, garnished with extra pomegranate seeds and a sprinkle of fresh herbs. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Ginger Farro Salad with Roasted Chickpeas and Pomegranate

text:
Coconut‑Lime Garlic Shrimp with Turmeric Rice

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch piece ginger, grated
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 cup basmati rice
- 1 ¾ cups water
- ½ tsp salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear; set aside.
2. In a medium saucepan, combine the rice, water, turmeric, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.
3. While the rice cooks, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger, sautéing for 30 seconds until fragrant.
4. Add the shrimp to the skillet, seasoning with black pepper. Cook for 2 minutes per side, or until the shrimp turn pink and opaque.
5. Pour the coconut milk and lime juice over the shrimp, stirring to combine. Simmer for 3‑4 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken slightly and coat the shrimp.
6. Taste the sauce and adjust seasoning with additional salt or lime juice if desired.
7. Serve the coconut‑lime garlic shrimp over the turmeric rice, garnished with chopped cilantro if using. Enjoy!
title: Coconut‑Lime Garlic Shrimp with Turmeric Rice

text:
Coconut‑Lime Glazed Seared Scallops with Quinoa Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 12 sea scallops, patted dry
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp coconut milk
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp butter
- 1 small red bell pepper, diced
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a saucepan, combine quinoa and vegetable broth; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and stir in coconut milk, lime zest, and a pinch of salt; set aside, keeping warm.
2. While the quinoa cooks, whisk together lime juice, maple syrup, grated ginger, and soy sauce in a small bowl to create the glaze.
3. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Season the scallops with salt and pepper, then add them to the pan, leaving space between each piece. Sear for 2‑3 minutes on one side until golden brown, then flip.
4. Drizzle the glaze over the scallops and add butter to the pan. Cook for another 1‑2 minutes, basting the scallops with the pan sauce until they are opaque in the center.
5. Remove the scallops from the skillet and set aside on a warm plate. Add the diced red bell pepper to the same skillet and sauté for 2 minutes until just softened.
6. Spoon the quinoa pilaf onto serving plates, top with the sautéed red bell pepper, and arrange the glazed scallops on top.
7. Garnish each plate with chopped cilantro and a final squeeze of lime juice. Serve immediately.
title: Coconut‑Lime Glazed Seared Scallops with Quinoa Pilaf

text:
Roasted Garlic and Lemon Kale Caesar Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 bunch kale, stems removed and leaves torn
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tablespoons freshly squeezed lemon juice
- 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard
- 1 teaspoon maple syrup
- ¼ cup grated Parmesan cheese
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the kale leaves with minced garlic, olive oil, salt, and pepper, then spread on a baking sheet.
2. Roast the kale for 8‑10 minutes, stirring halfway, until crisped but not burnt; let cool slightly.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together lemon zest, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, maple syrup, and a pinch of salt to create the dressing.
4. Transfer the roasted kale to a large bowl, drizzle with the lemon‑garlic dressing, and toss to coat evenly.
5. Add the grated Parmesan and toasted pumpkin seeds, giving the salad a final gentle toss.
6. Serve immediately, garnished with extra lemon zest if desired.
title: Roasted Garlic and Lemon Kale Caesar Salad

text:
Spiced Pomegranate Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Mint

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 ½ tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground coriander
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 ½ tbsp fresh lemon juice
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 tbsp fresh mint leaves, chopped
- 1 small red onion, finely diced (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the chickpeas with olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika, coriander, salt, and pepper until evenly coated. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until crisp and golden.  
3. While the chickpeas roast, combine quinoa and water in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the water is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
4. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl. Add the roasted chickpeas, diced red onion (if using), lemon juice, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Toss gently to combine.  
5. Fold in the chopped mint and pomegranate seeds just before serving to preserve their fresh flavor and texture.  
6. Serve warm or at room temperature as a hearty salad or side dish, garnished with extra pomegranate seeds and mint if desired.
title: Spiced Pomegranate Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Mint

text:
Spiced Apricot Glazed Tempeh with Quinoa and Roasted Brussels Sprouts

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- ¼ cup apricot preserves
- 2 tbsp low‑sodium soy sauce
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- 1 tbsp olive oil (for tempeh)
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups vegetable broth
- 12 oz Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 1 tbsp olive oil (for vegetables)
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- Zest of 1 lemon
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the Brussels sprouts with 1 tbsp olive oil, half the minced garlic, salt, and pepper; spread them cut‑side down on the sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway, until caramelized.  
3. While the sprouts roast, whisk together apricot preserves, soy sauce, smoked paprika, cumin, and a pinch of salt in a small bowl to form the glaze.  
4. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the tempeh strips and sear 3‑4 minutes per side until golden. Pour the apricot glaze over the tempeh, toss to coat, and cook an additional 2‑3 minutes until the glaze thickens and clings. Remove from heat.  
5. In a medium saucepan, combine rinsed quinoa and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Fluff with a fork and stir in lemon zest, the remaining garlic, and a drizzle of olive oil; season with salt and pepper.  
6. To serve, spoon a bed of quinoa onto each plate, top with roasted Brussels sprouts, and arrange the apricot‑glazed tempeh strips alongside. Garnish with an extra pinch of lemon zest or fresh herbs if desired. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Apricot Glazed Tempeh with Quinoa and Roasted Brussels Sprouts

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea Stew

Ingredients:
- 2 cans (15 oz each) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 can (13.5 oz) full‑fat coconut milk
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 cups fresh spinach, roughly chopped
- 2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped (plus extra for garnish)
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional: 1 small red chili, sliced for heat

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4‑5 minutes.  
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for another 30 seconds until fragrant.  
3. Sprinkle the ground turmeric and cumin over the aromatics, stirring constantly for 1 minute to toast the spices.  
4. Pour in the coconut milk and vegetable broth, scraping the bottom of the pot to release any browned bits.  
5. Add the chickpeas, lime zest, and lime juice. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to a simmer.  
6. Let the stew simmer uncovered for 15‑20 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the broth to thicken slightly. Season with salt and pepper to taste; add sliced red chili if desired.  
7. Stir in the chopped spinach and half of the cilantro; cook for 2‑3 minutes until the spinach wilts.  
8. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with the remaining cilantro and a drizzle of extra lime juice if you like extra brightness. Serve hot with crust
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea Stew

text:
Spiced Orange‑Glazed Chickpea and Farro Skillet

Ingredients:
- 1 cup farro, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- ¼ cup fresh orange juice
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro, for garnish
- Zest of 1 orange, for garnish

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine the farro and water (or broth). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the grains are tender and the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and set aside.
2. While the farro cooks, whisk together the orange juice, maple syrup, smoked paprika, cumin, minced garlic, and a pinch of salt and pepper in a small bowl; set the glaze aside.
3. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the chickpeas and sauté for 3‑4 minutes, allowing them to brown slightly.
4. Pour the orange‑maple glaze over the chickpeas, stirring to coat evenly. Cook for another 2‑3 minutes, letting the glaze thicken and cling to the chickpeas.
5. Add the cooked farro to the skillet, mixing gently to combine the grains with the glazed chickpeas. Cook for an additional minute to heat through, adjusting seasoning with more salt or pepper if needed.
6. Transfer the skillet mixture to serving plates, sprinkle with orange zest and chopped cilantro, and serve warm.
title: Spiced Orange‑Glazed Chickpea and Farro Skillet

text:
Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Beet and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 medium beets, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/4 teaspoon smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1/4 cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped
- 1/4 cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- 2 tablespoons fresh orange juice
- 1 tablespoon honey
- 1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar
- 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the beet cubes with olive oil, cinnamon, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, until tender and caramelized.
2. While the beets roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and let cool slightly.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together orange juice, honey, apple cider vinegar, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of olive oil to create the dressing.
4. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted beets, toasted walnuts, and chopped parsley. Drizzle the dressing over the mixture and toss gently to coat evenly.
5. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a splash of orange juice if needed. Sprinkle crumbled feta on top, if using, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Beet and Quinoa Salad

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Shrimp with Garlic Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1/2 tsp sea salt
- 1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan, combine the quinoa, vegetable broth, and half of the minced garlic; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and stir in the coconut milk, lime juice, salt, and pepper; keep warm.  
2. While the quinoa cooks, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the remaining garlic and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.  
3. Add the shrimp to the skillet, sprinkle with turmeric, and season with a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 3–4 minutes, or until the shrimp turn pink and are just cooked through.  
4. Remove the skillet from heat and drizzle an extra splash of lime juice over the shrimp for brightness.  
5. Spoon the creamy garlic quinoa onto serving plates, top with the turmeric‑spiced shrimp, and garnish with chopped cilantro if desired. Serve immediately.
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Shrimp with Garlic Quinoa

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu and Roasted Brussels Sprout Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 block (14 oz) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 cups Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 1 cup cooked brown rice
- 1 ½ tablespoons pure maple syrup
- 1 tablespoon soy sauce
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1 teaspoon toasted sesame oil
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- ½ cup shredded carrots
- ¼ cup sliced almonds, toasted
- 2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, smoked paprika, sesame oil, minced garlic, salt, and pepper.  
3. Toss the cubed tofu in half of the glaze mixture, then spread on one side of the prepared sheet.  
4. Toss the Brussels sprouts with the remaining glaze, arrange on the other side of the sheet, and drizzle with a little extra sesame oil.  
5. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway through, until the tofu is golden and the sprouts are crisp‑tender and caramelized.  
6. While the tofu and sprouts roast, warm the cooked brown rice in a microwave or skillet.  
7. Assemble the bowls: start with a base of brown rice, top with roasted tofu, Brussels sprouts, shredded carrots, toasted almonds, and fresh cilantro.  
8. Serve immediately, optionally drizzling any leftover pan juices over the bowl for extra flavor.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu and Roasted Brussels Sprout Buddha Bowl

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu and Roasted Sweet Potato Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 block (14 oz) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 cup cooked quinoa
- ½ cup shredded red cabbage
- ¼ cup sliced almonds, toasted
- 2 Tbsp tahini
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tsp grated ginger
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the sweet potato dice with 1 Tbsp olive oil, 1 Tbsp maple syrup, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast 20‑25 minutes until caramelized and tender.  
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, whisk together the remaining maple syrup, soy sauce, and a pinch of salt; toss the tofu cubes in this glaze.  
3. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium heat, add a drizzle of olive oil, and sear the glazed tofu for 3‑4 minutes per side until golden and crisp. Set aside.  
4. In a small bowl, whisk tahini, lemon juice, grated ginger, a splash of water, and a pinch of salt to create a drizzle sauce; adjust consistency with more water if needed.  
5. Assemble bowls: start with a base of cooked quinoa, top with roasted sweet potatoes, seared tofu, shredded red cabbage, and toasted almonds.  
6. Drizzle the tahini‑lemon sauce over each bowl, garnish with fresh cilantro, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu and Roasted Sweet Potato Buddha Bowl

text:
Spicy Ginger Lime Chickpea and Quinoa Stir‑Fry

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 tablespoon sesame oil
- 1 tablespoon grated fresh ginger
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 red bell pepper, thinly sliced
- 1 carrot, julienned
- 2 green onions, sliced
- 2 tablespoons soy sauce
- 1 tablespoon lime juice
- 1 teaspoon sriracha (or more to taste)
- 1 tablespoon honey or maple syrup
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan, combine the quinoa and water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the water is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and set aside.
2. While the quinoa cooks, whisk together the soy sauce, lime juice, sriracha, and honey in a small bowl; set the sauce aside.
3. Heat the sesame oil in a large skillet or wok over medium‑high heat. Add the grated ginger and minced garlic, stirring for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
4. Add the sliced red bell pepper and julienned carrot to the skillet. Stir‑fry for 3–4 minutes, until the vegetables are just tender but still crisp.
5. Toss the drained chickpeas into the skillet and cook for another 2 minutes, allowing them to heat through and absorb some of the aromatics.
6. Pour the prepared sauce over the vegetables and chickpeas, stirring to coat everything evenly. Cook for 1–2 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
7. Stir in the cooked quinoa, breaking up any clumps, and mix until the quinoa is fully incorporated and heated through.
8. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Remove from heat and garnish with sliced green onions and chopped cilantro.
9. Serve immediately, optionally with extra lime wedges or a drizzle of sriracha for added heat.
title: Spicy Ginger Lime Chickpea and Quinoa Stir‑Fry

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Soba Noodle Salad with Sesame‑Toasted Edamame  

Ingredients:
- 8 oz soba noodles  
- 1 cup shelled edamame, thawed if frozen  
- 1 tbsp sesame oil  
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds  
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated  
- 2 tbsp lemon juice  
- 1 tbsp soy sauce or tamari  
- 1 tbsp honey or maple syrup  
- 1 clove garlic, minced  
- 1 cup shredded red cabbage  
- 1 carrot, julienned  
- 2 green onions, sliced  
- Salt and pepper to taste  

Instructions:
1. Cook the soba noodles according to package directions, drain, and rinse under cold water to stop cooking.  
2. While the noodles cook, heat the sesame oil in a dry skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the edamame and toast, stirring frequently, until lightly browned and fragrant, about 3–4 minutes; remove from heat and set aside.  
3. In a small bowl, whisk together the grated ginger, lemon juice, soy sauce, honey, minced garlic, toasted sesame seeds, and a pinch of salt and pepper to create the dressing.  
4. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooled soba noodles, toasted edamame, shredded red cabbage, julienned carrot, and sliced green onions.  
5. Pour the dressing over the noodle mixture and toss gently until everything is evenly coated.  
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if desired.  
7. Serve the salad chilled or at room temperature, garnished with extra sesame seeds and a drizzle of sesame oil if desired.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Soba Noodle Salad with Sesame‑Toasted Edamame

text:
Maple‑Glazed Butternut Squash and Lentil Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 medium butternut squash, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp ground cinnamon
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 3 cups baby arugula
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tbsp crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar
- 1 tsp Dijon mustard

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cubed butternut squash with 1 tablespoon olive oil, maple syrup, smoked paprika, cumin, cinnamon, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the squash in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway through, until tender and caramelized.  
4. While the squash roasts, combine lentils and 3 cups water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 20‑25 minutes, or until lentils are tender but still hold their shape. Drain any excess liquid and season with a pinch of salt.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, and a pinch of salt and pepper to create the dressing.  
6. In a large serving bowl, combine the roasted squash, cooked lentils, and baby arugula. Drizzle the dressing over the mixture and toss gently to combine.  
7. Top the salad with toasted pumpkin seeds and, if desired, crumbled feta cheese. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Maple‑Glazed Butternut Squash and Lentil Salad

text:
Sage‑Infused Mushroom Barley Risotto

Ingredients:
- 1 cup pearl barley
- 2 cups mixed mushrooms, sliced
- 1 small onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 3 cups vegetable broth, warmed
- ½ cup dry white wine
- 2 teaspoons fresh sage, finely chopped
- 1 teaspoon fresh thyme leaves
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- ¼ cup grated Parmesan cheese
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Rinse the barley under cold water and set aside.
2. In a large saucepan, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 3 minutes.
3. Stir in the garlic and cook for another 30 seconds until fragrant.
4. Add the sliced mushrooms and sauté until they release their moisture and begin to brown, about 5‑6 minutes.
5. Pour in the white wine, stirring to deglaze the pan, and let it reduce by half, roughly 2 minutes.
6. Stir in the barley, coating it with the mushroom mixture, then add the fresh sage and thyme.
7. Begin adding the warmed vegetable broth, one ladleful at a time, stirring frequently. Wait until each addition is mostly absorbed before adding the next. Continue this process for 30‑35 minutes, or until the barley is tender but still has a slight bite.
8. Season the risotto with salt and pepper to taste.
9. Remove the pan from heat and stir in the grated Parmesan cheese until melted and creamy.
10. Serve hot, garnished with an extra sprinkle of fresh sage if desired.
title: Sage‑Infused Mushroom Barley Risotto

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch rounds
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 tsp olive oil
- 1/4 tsp sea salt
- 1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the carrot rounds with olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the carrots in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until tender and caramelized.  
4. While the carrots roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.  
5. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl. Add the roasted carrots, toasted pumpkin seeds, chopped parsley, and lemon juice. Toss gently to combine.  
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a drizzle of maple syrup if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad

text:
Coconut‑Lime Chickpea and Roasted Corn Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 ears fresh corn, husked
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- ½ cup cherry tomatoes, halved
- ¼ cup red onion, finely chopped
- 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, chopped
- 3 tablespoons coconut milk
- 2 tablespoons lime juice
- 1 teaspoon lime zest
- 1 teaspoon honey or maple syrup
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 tablespoon olive oil

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the corn kernels (cut from the cobs) with ½ tablespoon olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper; spread them on the sheet and roast for 12‑15 minutes, stirring halfway, until lightly charred.  
3. While the corn roasts, combine chickpeas, red bell pepper, cherry tomatoes, red onion, and cilantro in a large bowl.  
4. In a small bowl whisk together coconut milk, lime juice, lime zest, honey, cumin, the remaining ½ tablespoon olive oil, and a pinch of salt and pepper.  
5. When the corn is done, let it cool slightly, then add it to the chickpea mixture.  
6. Pour the coconut‑lime dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly.  
7. Adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired.  
8. Serve the salad at room temperature or chilled, garnished with extra cilantro or lime wedges.
title: Coconut‑Lime Chickpea and Roasted Corn Salad

text:
Maple‑Glazed Pumpkin and Chickpea Curry

Ingredients:
- 1 lb (450 g) pumpkin, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tbsp curry powder
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)
- Cooked basmati rice, for serving

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes.  
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
3. Sprinkle the curry powder, cumin, and smoked paprika over the aromatics, stirring constantly for 30 seconds to toast the spices.  
4. Add the cubed pumpkin to the pan, tossing to coat it with the spice mixture. Cook for 3–4 minutes, allowing the pumpkin to begin softening.  
5. Pour in the coconut milk and maple syrup, stirring to combine. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.  
6. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and let the curry simmer for 15–20 minutes, or until the pumpkin is fork‑tender.  
7. Add the chickpeas to the skillet, stirring them into the sauce. Simmer uncovered for an additional 5 minutes to heat the chickpeas through and thicken the sauce slightly.  
8. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Adjust sweetness with a drizzle of extra maple syrup if desired.  
9. Serve the maple‑glazed pumpkin and chickpea curry over cooked basmati rice, garnished with chopped fresh cilantro. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Pumpkin and Chickpea Curry

text:
Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Cauliflower Steaks with Herbed Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 large cauliflower head
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh mint
- 1 tbsp toasted pine nuts (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Slice the cauliflower into ¾‑inch thick “steaks” by cutting from top to bottom; you should get 2–3 usable steaks.  
3. In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, thyme, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.  
4. Brush both sides of each cauliflower steak with the lemon‑thyme mixture, placing them on the prepared baking sheet.  
5. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, flipping halfway through, until the edges are golden and the center is tender.  
6. While the cauliflower roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed.  
7. Remove the quinoa from heat and fluff with a fork; stir in chopped parsley, mint, and toasted pine nuts, then season with a pinch of salt and pepper.  
8. To serve, plate a cauliflower steak atop a generous scoop of herbed quinoa, drizzle any remaining lemon‑thyme glaze from the pan over the top, and garnish with extra herbs or pine nuts if desired.
title: Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Cauliflower Steaks with Herbed Quinoa

text:
Lemon‑Basil Farro with Roasted Chickpeas and Sun‑Dried Tomatoes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup farro, rinsed
- 2 ½ cups low‑sodium vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- ½ cup sun‑dried tomatoes, thinly sliced
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- ¼ cup fresh basil leaves, torn
- ¼ cup grated Parmesan cheese (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the chickpeas with 1 Tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking halfway, until crisp.
2. While the chickpeas roast, combine farro and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 20‑25 minutes, or until the farro is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
3. In a small skillet, heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil over medium heat. Add the sliced sun‑dried tomatoes and sauté for 2‑3 minutes to release their flavor.
4. Transfer the cooked farro to a large bowl. Stir in the lemon zest, lemon juice, sautéed sun‑dried tomatoes, and roasted chickpeas.
5. Toss gently with the torn basil leaves. Adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed.
6. Serve warm, sprinkled with grated Parmesan cheese if desired. Enjoy as a hearty main or a satisfying side dish.
title: Lemon‑Basil Farro with Roasted Chickpeas and Sun‑Dried Tomatoes

text:
Crispy Pomegranate‑Glazed Tofu with Sesame‑Lime Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 2 Tbsp pomegranate molasses
- 1 Tbsp low‑sodium soy sauce
- 1 tsp cornstarch
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 Tbsp sesame oil
- 2 Tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tsp lime zest
- 2 Tbsp chopped green onions
- 1 Tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium bowl, whisk together pomegranate molasses, soy sauce, and cornstarch until smooth. Add the tofu cubes and gently toss to coat; let marinate while you prepare the quinoa.
2. In a saucepan, combine rinsed quinoa and water (or broth). Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and stir in sesame oil, lime juice, lime zest, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Set aside.
3. Heat 1 Tbsp olive oil in a large non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated tofu in a single layer, reserving any excess sauce. Cook, turning occasionally, until all sides are golden and crisp, about 8‑10 minutes. Transfer tofu to a plate.
4. Reduce heat to medium and add the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil to the skillet. Pour the reserved sauce into the pan and cook, stirring, for 1‑2 minutes until it thickens and becomes a glossy glaze.
5. Return the crispy tofu to the skillet, tossing to coat evenly with the glaze. Cook an additional minute to heat through.
6. To serve, spoon a bed of sesame‑lime quinoa onto each plate, top with the pomegranate‑glazed tofu, and garnish with chopped green onions and toasted sesame seeds. Adjust seasoning with extra salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired. Enjoy!
title: Crispy Pomegranate‑Glazed Tofu with Sesame‑Lime Quinoa

text:
Maple‑Miso Glazed Eggplant with Sesame Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 2 medium eggplants, sliced into ½‑inch rounds
- 3 Tbsp maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp white miso paste
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp rice vinegar
- 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 Tbsp sesame seeds, toasted
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a small bowl, whisk together maple syrup, miso paste, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and minced garlic to form the glaze.
3. Brush both sides of the eggplant slices with the glaze, season lightly with salt and pepper, and arrange on the prepared baking sheet.
4. Roast the eggplant for 20‑25 minutes, flipping halfway through, until caramelized and tender.
5. While the eggplant roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes or until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and stir in toasted sesame seeds.
6. Serve the glazed eggplant over the sesame quinoa, garnish with chopped cilantro and an extra drizzle of glaze if desired. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Miso Glazed Eggplant with Sesame Quinoa

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Lentil and Spinach Soup

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 large onion, diced
- 2 carrots, peeled and diced
- 2 celery stalks, diced
- 3 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1 teaspoon lemon zest
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 2 cups water
- 2 cups fresh spinach, roughly chopped
- 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional garnish: chopped fresh parsley and a drizzle of olive oil

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots, and celery; sauté for 5‑7 minutes, until the vegetables are softened.
2. Stir in the garlic, ginger, cumin, smoked paprika, and lemon zest; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add the rinsed red lentils, vegetable broth, and water. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15‑20 minutes, or until the lentils are tender.
4. Stir in the chopped spinach and simmer for an additional 2‑3 minutes, just until the spinach wilts.
5. Remove the pot from heat and stir in the lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
6. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with fresh parsley and a drizzle of olive oil if desired, and serve hot.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Lentil and Spinach Soup

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Shrimp and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 2 tbsp coconut oil, divided
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 garlic clove, minced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 small red bell pepper, diced
- ½ cup shredded purple cabbage
- ¼ cup toasted coconut flakes
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a saucepan, combine quinoa and water; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and set aside to cool.
2. While the quinoa cooks, whisk together smoked paprika, cumin, cayenne (if using), lime zest, lime juice, maple syrup, minced garlic, and a pinch of salt in a small bowl to create the dressing.
3. Pat the shrimp dry with paper towels. Toss them with 1 tablespoon of coconut oil, half of the dressing, and a pinch of black pepper.
4. Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of coconut oil in a skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the shrimp in a single layer and cook 2‑3 minutes per side, until pink and opaque. Transfer to a plate and set aside.
5. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooled quinoa, diced red bell pepper, shredded cabbage, and chopped cilantro. Drizzle the remaining dressing over the mixture and toss gently to coat.
6. Top the quinoa salad with the cooked shrimp, toasted coconut flakes, and an extra squeeze of lime juice if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Shrimp and Quinoa Salad

text:
Citrus‑Infused Quinoa with Roasted Fennel and Pistachios

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 1 large fennel bulb, thinly sliced
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Zest of 1 orange
- Juice of 1 orange
- 1/4 cup toasted pistachios, roughly chopped
- 1/4 cup dried cranberries
- 1 tsp honey
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
- Fresh mint leaves for garnish (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the sliced fennel with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper, then spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until caramelized and tender.
2. While the fennel roasts, combine quinoa and water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the water is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes.
3. Fluff the cooked quinoa with a fork and transfer to a large bowl. Add orange zest, orange juice, honey, and the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil. Toss gently to coat the grains evenly.
4. Fold the roasted fennel, toasted pistachios, and dried cranberries into the quinoa mixture. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste.
5. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with fresh mint leaves if desired. Enjoy as a vibrant side dish or a light main course.
title: Citrus‑Infused Quinoa with Roasted Fennel and Pistachios

text:
Lemon‑Saffron Orzo with Roasted Asparagus and Toasted Almonds

Ingredients:
- 1 cup orzo pasta
- 1 bunch asparagus, trimmed and cut into 2‑inch pieces
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp saffron threads
- 1/4 cup hot water
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1/4 cup toasted sliced almonds
- 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the asparagus with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 12‑15 minutes, until tender and lightly browned.
2. While the asparagus roasts, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the orzo and cook according to package directions until al dente, about 8‑9 minutes. Drain, reserving 1/4 cup of the cooking water.
3. In a small bowl, combine the saffron threads with the hot water and let steep for 5 minutes to release color and flavor.
4. In the same pot used for the orzo, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil over medium heat. Add the saffron infusion (including the threads) and stir for 30 seconds. Add the cooked orzo, lemon zest, lemon juice, and the reserved cooking water. Toss to coat, heating through for 2 minutes.
5. Gently fold the roasted asparagus into the orzo mixture. Season with additional salt and pepper, if needed.
6. Transfer the orzo and asparagus to a serving bowl. Sprinkle with toasted almonds and grated Parmesan. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Saffron Orzo with Roasted Asparagus and Toasted Almonds

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Roasted Cauliflower & Lentil Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 cup green lentils, rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- 1 tbsp honey (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
2. In a bowl, whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, grated ginger, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.
3. Toss cauliflower florets in the seasoned oil mixture until evenly coated; spread on the prepared sheet.
4. Roast cauliflower for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender.
5. While cauliflower roasts, place lentils in a saucepan, cover with water, bring to boil, then simmer 15‑20 minutes until just tender; drain and set aside.
6. In a large salad bowl combine roasted cauliflower, cooked lentils, toasted pumpkin seeds, and chopped parsley.
7. Drizzle additional lemon‑ginger dressing (mix remaining oil mixture with honey if using) over the salad and toss gently to combine.
8. Serve warm or at room temperature, adjusting seasoning with extra salt or lemon juice as desired.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Roasted Cauliflower & Lentil Salad

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Sweet Potato and Kale Stir‑Fry

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tsp rice vinegar
- 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and cut into ½‑inch dice
- 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 4 cups kale leaves, stems removed and torn into bite‑size pieces
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds, for garnish
- 2 green onions, sliced, for garnish
- Cooked brown rice or quinoa, for serving (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Toss the sweet potato dice with 1 tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.  
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, whisk together maple syrup, soy sauce, rice vinegar, and toasted sesame oil in a shallow bowl. Add the tofu cubes and gently toss to coat; let marinate for 5 minutes.  
3. Heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet or wok over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated tofu (reserve any excess sauce) and stir‑fry for 4‑5 minutes, turning until all sides are caramelized. Remove tofu to a plate.  
4. In the same skillet, add the minced garlic and grated ginger; sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the kale and stir‑cook for 2‑3 minutes, until wilted but still bright green.  
5. Return the tofu to the skillet, pour in any reserved maple‑soy sauce, and toss everything together. Cook for another minute to let the flavors meld.  
6. Gently fold in the roasted sweet potato cubes, heating through for 1‑2 minutes. Adjust seasoning with additional salt or a splash of soy sauce if needed.  
7. Serve the stir‑fry over cooked brown rice or quinoa, if desired. Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds and sliced green onions on top for garnish. Enjoy while hot!
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Sweet Potato and Kale Stir‑Fry

text:
Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Chickpea and Farro Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup farro, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- Zest of 1 lemon
- Juice of 1 lemon
- 1 tsp dried thyme (or 1 Tbsp fresh thyme leaves)
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- ½ tsp salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 1 cup cherry tomatoes, halved
- ½ cup cucumber, diced
- ¼ cup feta cheese, crumbled
- 2 Tbsp fresh parsley, chopped

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the chickpeas with 1 Tbsp olive oil, garlic, thyme, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking halfway, until golden and crisp.  
3. While the chickpeas roast, combine farro and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook 20‑25 minutes until tender. Drain any excess liquid and let cool slightly.  
4. In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, a pinch of salt, and black pepper to create the dressing.  
5. Add the cooked farro, roasted chickpeas, cherry tomatoes, cucumber, and parsley to the bowl. Toss gently to coat everything evenly with the dressing.  
6. Sprinkle the crumbled feta over the top, give a final light toss, and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Chickpea and Farro Salad

text:
Spiced Orange‑Glazed Chickpea and Sweet Potato Skillet

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 red bell pepper, sliced
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp orange marmalade
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- Zest of 1 orange
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)
- 1 Tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat a large skillet over medium heat and add the olive oil.  
2. Add the diced sweet potatoes and sauté, stirring occasionally, for 8‑10 minutes until they begin to soften and turn golden.  
3. Stir in the sliced red bell pepper and cook an additional 3 minutes.  
4. In a small bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, orange marmalade, smoked paprika, cumin, cayenne, orange zest, salt, and pepper.  
5. Add the chickpeas to the skillet, then pour the glaze over the vegetables. Toss everything to coat evenly.  
6. Reduce the heat to low, cover the skillet, and let the mixture simmer for 5‑7 minutes, or until the sweet potatoes are tender and the glaze has thickened.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed; remove from heat.  
8. Serve hot, garnished with chopped cilantro and toasted pumpkin seeds, if desired.
title: Spiced Orange‑Glazed Chickpea and Sweet Potato Skillet

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa and Roasted Cauliflower Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 1 medium cauliflower head, cut into florets
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tbsp honey or maple syrup
- ¼ tsp salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- ¼ cup toasted sliced almonds
- 2 green onions, thinly sliced
- 1 handful fresh cilantro leaves, chopped

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. Toss the cauliflower florets with olive oil, salt, and pepper, then spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet; roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.
3. While the cauliflower roasts, combine quinoa and water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
4. In a small bowl, whisk together lemon zest, lemon juice, grated ginger, and honey (or maple syrup) to create the dressing.
5. In a large bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted cauliflower, toasted almonds, green onions, and cilantro; drizzle the lemon‑ginger dressing over the mixture and toss gently to coat evenly.
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if desired; serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa and Roasted Cauliflower Salad

text:
Maple‑Glazed Pear and Walnut Couscous

Ingredients:
- 1 cup couscous
- 1 ¼ cups water
- 2 ripe pears, cored and thinly sliced
- ¼ cup walnuts, toasted and roughly chopped
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp ground cinnamon
- ¼ tsp salt
- Fresh arugula leaves, for garnish
- Crumbled goat cheese (optional)

Instructions:
1. In a saucepan, bring water to a boil, add the salt, then stir in the couscous; remove from heat, cover, and let sit for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
2. While the couscous rests, heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the sliced pears, sprinkle with cinnamon, and sauté for 2‑3 minutes until they begin to soften.  
3. Drizzle the maple syrup over the pears, continue cooking for another 2 minutes, allowing the syrup to caramelize and coat the fruit. Remove from heat.  
4. In a large bowl, combine the fluffed couscous, caramelized pears, and toasted walnuts. Toss gently to distribute the ingredients evenly.  
5. Plate the couscous mixture, top with a handful of fresh arugula leaves, and sprinkle with crumbled goat cheese if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Maple‑Glazed Pear and Walnut Couscous

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Lentil and Kale Soup

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 tablespoon coconut oil
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper (optional)
- 1 can (14 oz) coconut milk
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon lime juice
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 cups kale, stems removed and torn into bite‑size pieces
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Lime wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Heat the coconut oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4–5 minutes.
2. Stir in the garlic, ginger, cumin, smoked paprika, and cayenne (if using); cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add the rinsed red lentils, coconut milk, and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer and cook, uncovered, for 15–20 minutes, or until the lentils are tender.
4. Mix in the lime juice, lime zest, and season with salt and pepper to taste.
5. Add the kale and simmer for an additional 3–4 minutes, just until the kale wilts but retains its bright green color.
6. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve with lime wedges on the side. Enjoy hot!
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Lentil and Kale Soup

text:
Spicy Orange‑Miso Glazed Salmon with Coconut Rice

Ingredients:
- 4 salmon fillets (about 6 oz each)
- 1/4 cup orange juice, freshly squeezed
- 2 tbsp white miso paste
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 cup jasmine rice
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup water
- Zest of 1 orange
- 1 lime, cut into wedges
- 2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 tbsp vegetable oil

Instructions:
1. Rinse the jasmine rice under cold water until the water runs clear. Combine the rice, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and keep warm.  
2. While the rice cooks, prepare the glaze: in a small bowl whisk together orange juice, miso paste, maple syrup, soy sauce, grated ginger, minced garlic, and orange zest until smooth.  
3. Pat the salmon fillets dry with paper towels, then season both sides lightly with salt and pepper.  
4. Heat the vegetable oil in a large non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the salmon, skin‑side down if it has skin, and sear for 3–4 minutes until the edges turn opaque. Flip the fillets and cook for another 2 minutes.  
5. Pour the orange‑miso glaze over the salmon, reduce the heat to medium, and spoon the sauce over the fish. Continue cooking for 2–3 minutes, basting frequently, until the salmon is cooked through (internal temperature 145 °F) and the glaze is glossy and slightly thickened.  
6. Transfer the salmon to serving plates. Spoon a generous portion of coconut rice beside each fillet. Drizzle any remaining glaze from the pan over the rice.  
7. Garnish with chopped cilantro, a squeeze of fresh lime juice, and serve immediately. Enjoy!
title: Spicy Orange‑Miso Glazed Salmon with Coconut Rice

text:
Spiced Orange‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Black Bean Skillet

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 (15‑oz) can black beans, drained and rinsed
- 1/4 cup fresh orange juice
- Zest of 1 orange
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- 1 Tbsp lime juice

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
2. Add the diced sweet potatoes, season with salt and pepper, and sauté for 8‑10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they begin to soften and turn golden.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together orange juice, orange zest, maple syrup, cumin, smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt.
4. Pour the orange‑maple mixture over the sweet potatoes, stirring to coat evenly. Continue cooking for 3‑4 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken.
5. Add the black beans to the skillet, stirring gently to combine. Cook for an additional 2‑3 minutes, just until the beans are heated through.
6. Remove the skillet from heat and drizzle with lime juice. Taste and adjust seasoning with more salt or pepper if needed.
7. Sprinkle chopped cilantro over the top and serve immediately, either on its own or over cooked rice or quinoa. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Orange‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Black Bean Skillet

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Chickpeas

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the chickpeas with 1 tbsp olive oil, minced garlic, cumin, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking the pan halfway, until golden and crisp.  
3. While the chickpeas roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.  
4. In a small skillet over medium heat, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil. Add the grated ginger and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Stir in lemon zest, lemon juice, and maple syrup; cook for another minute, then remove from heat.  
5. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large bowl. Pour the lemon‑ginger dressing over the quinoa and toss to combine.  
6. Gently fold in the roasted garlic chickpeas and chopped cilantro, if using. Adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice as desired.  
7. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with extra cilantro or a lemon wedge. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Chickpeas

text:
Sage‑Roasted Butternut Squash and Lentil Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 medium butternut squash, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp dried sage (or 1 tbsp fresh sage, chopped)
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tbsp dried cranberries
- 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 2 cups baby arugula
- Optional: crumbled feta cheese for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the cubed butternut squash with olive oil, sage, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and caramelized.  
2. While the squash roasts, combine lentils and 3 cups water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer 20‑25 minutes until lentils are tender but not mushy. Drain any excess water and set aside.  
3. In a small bowl, whisk together apple cider vinegar, maple syrup, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of olive oil to make a dressing.  
4. In a large bowl, combine roasted squash, cooked lentils, toasted pumpkin seeds, dried cranberries, and baby arugula. Drizzle the dressing over the mixture and toss gently to coat.  
5. Serve the salad warm or at room temperature, topped with crumbled feta if desired.
title: Sage‑Roasted Butternut Squash and Lentil Salad

text:
Spiced Orange‑Glazed Cauliflower and Chickpea Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 large head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- 1/2 cup orange juice (freshly squeezed)
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- 1/4 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)
- Toasted pumpkin seeds (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes.
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for another minute until fragrant.
3. Add the cauliflower florets and toss to coat with the aromatics; sauté for 3–4 minutes.
4. Sprinkle the smoked paprika, cumin, cinnamon, and cayenne pepper over the vegetables; stir well to distribute the spices.
5. Pour in the orange juice, maple syrup, and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to a simmer.
6. Add the chickpeas, season with salt and black pepper, and let the stew simmer uncovered for 15–20 minutes, or until the cauliflower is tender and the sauce has thickened slightly.
7. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed; if the stew is too thick, add a splash more broth or water.
8. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with chopped cilantro and toasted pumpkin seeds, and serve hot. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Orange‑Glazed Cauliflower and Chickpea Stew

text:
Spiced Orange‑Glazed Cauliflower and Lentil Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 large head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 cup dried green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 cup orange juice (freshly squeezed)
- Zest of 1 orange
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes.
2. Stir in the minced garlic, cumin, coriander, smoked paprika, and orange zest; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add the cauliflower florets and toss to coat with the spices, cooking for 2–3 minutes.
4. Pour in the orange juice, vegetable broth, and lentils. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to a gentle simmer.
5. Cover and simmer for 25–30 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and the cauliflower is soft.
6. Season with salt and pepper to taste. If the stew is too thick, add a splash more broth or water.
7. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with chopped cilantro, and serve hot.
title: Spiced Orange‑Glazed Cauliflower and Lentil Stew

text:
Spiced Cardamom Sweet Potato and Chickpea Curry

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp ground cardamom
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- 1 (14‑oz) can coconut milk
- 1 cup diced tomatoes (canned or fresh)
- 2 cups fresh spinach leaves
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)
- Cooked rice or quinoa, for serving

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4‑5 minutes.
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for another minute until fragrant.
3. Sprinkle in the ground cardamom, cumin, coriander, smoked paprika, and cayenne (if using). Toast the spices for 30 seconds, stirring constantly to release their aromas.
4. Add the cubed sweet potatoes and chickpeas to the pot, tossing to coat them with the spice mixture.
5. Pour in the diced tomatoes and coconut milk, stirring to combine. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer, uncovered, for 20‑25 minutes, or until the sweet potatoes are tender.
6. Season the curry with salt and black pepper to taste. Stir in the fresh spinach leaves and cook for 2‑3 minutes, just until wilted.
7. Serve the curry over cooked rice or quinoa, and garnish with chopped cilantro. Enjoy while hot!
title: Spiced Cardamom Sweet Potato and Chickpea Curry

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- Salt and black pepper, to taste
- 4 cups mixed baby greens
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- Dressing:
  - 3 Tbsp apple cider vinegar
  - 1 Tbsp Dijon mustard
  - 1 Tbsp honey
  - ¼ cup extra‑virgin olive oil
  - Pinch of salt

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Salad

text:
Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch rounds
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 1 tsp dried thyme (or 1 Tbsp fresh thyme leaves)
- 1/4 tsp sea salt, plus more to taste
- 1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 1/4 cup toasted sliced almonds
- 1/4 cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the carrot rounds with 1 Tbsp olive oil, thyme, salt, and pepper; spread them in a single layer on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until caramelized and tender.  
2. While the carrots roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.  
3. In a small bowl whisk together the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, lemon juice, lemon zest, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of pepper.  
4. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl; add the roasted carrots, toasted almonds, and the lemon‑thyme dressing. Toss gently to combine, adjusting seasoning if needed.  
5. Sprinkle crumbled feta and chopped parsley over the salad just before serving. Enjoy warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad

text:
Saffron‑Honey Glazed Carrots with Herbed Couscous

Ingredients:
- 1 lb carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch sticks
- 2 Tbsp honey
- ½ tsp saffron threads, steeped in 2 Tbsp warm water
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup couscous
- 1 ¼ cup vegetable broth
- 2 Tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- 1 Tbsp fresh mint, chopped
- Zest of 1 lemon

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the carrot sticks with olive oil, honey, the saffron infusion (including the threads), salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the carrots in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until tender and caramelized.  
4. While the carrots roast, bring the vegetable broth to a boil in a saucepan, then stir in the couscous. Remove from heat, cover, and let sit for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
5. Stir the chopped parsley, mint, and lemon zest into the couscous, then season with a pinch of salt and pepper.  
6. To serve, spoon a bed of herbed couscous onto plates, top with the saffron‑honey glazed carrots, and drizzle any pan juices over the top. Enjoy warm.
title: Saffron‑Honey Glazed Carrots with Herbed Couscous

text:
Spiced Orange‑Glazed Tofu with Coconut Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 14 oz firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- ½ cup water
- ¼ cup fresh orange juice
- Zest of 1 orange
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 Tbsp sesame oil
- 2 Tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- 2 Tbsp chopped green onions
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Salt and pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
2. While the quinoa cooks, whisk together orange juice, orange zest, maple syrup, soy sauce, cumin, smoked paprika, ginger, garlic, and sesame oil in a shallow bowl.  
3. Toss the tofu cubes in the orange‑glaze mixture, ensuring each piece is well‑coated. Let marinate for 5 minutes.  
4. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the tofu and glaze; cook 3‑4 minutes per side, turning gently, until the tofu is golden and the glaze thickens and caramelizes.  
5. To assemble, spoon a bed of coconut quinoa onto each plate, top with the orange‑glazed tofu, and drizzle any remaining pan sauce over the top.  
6. Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds, chopped green onions, and fresh cilantro over the dish. Season with additional salt and pepper if desired. Serve warm.
title: Spiced Orange‑Glazed Tofu with Coconut Quinoa

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Brussels Sprouts and Herbed Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 3 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp low‑sodium soy sauce
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 Tbsp apple cider vinegar
- 1 lb Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a shallow bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, minced garlic, and apple cider vinegar. Add the tempeh cubes, toss to coat, and let marinate while you prepare the vegetables (about 10 minutes).  
2. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
3. Toss the halved Brussels sprouts with 1 Tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread them cut‑side down on the prepared sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until caramelized and tender.  
4. While the sprouts roast, heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated tempeh (reserve any excess sauce) and sauté for 4‑5 minutes, turning until golden brown on all sides. Pour the reserved sauce into the pan and cook an additional 2 minutes, allowing it to glaze the tempeh. Remove from heat and set aside.  
5. Meanwhile, combine the rinsed quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes.  
6. Fluff the quinoa with a fork and stir in the chopped thyme, a pinch of salt, and a grind of black pepper.  
7. To serve, divide the herbed quinoa among plates, top with the roasted Brussels sprouts, and arrange the maple‑glazed tempeh on top. Garnish with an extra sprinkle of thyme if desired. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Brussels Sprouts and Herbed Quinoa

text:
Lemon‑Thyme Quinoa with Roasted Fennel and Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 large fennel bulb, thinly sliced
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/4 tsp black pepper
- 1/3 cup pomegranate arils
- 2 tbsp toasted pine nuts (optional)
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the sliced fennel with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper, then spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until caramelized and tender.
2. While the fennel roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy.
3. Remove the cooked quinoa from heat; fluff with a fork and stir in the remaining olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, dried thyme, and a pinch of salt and pepper.
4. Gently fold the roasted fennel into the quinoa mixture. Transfer to a serving bowl.
5. Top with pomegranate arils, toasted pine nuts (if using), and a sprinkle of fresh parsley.
6. Serve warm or at room temperature as a vibrant side dish or light main course. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Thyme Quinoa with Roasted Fennel and Pomegranate

text:
Citrus‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Lentil Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 large head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Zest of 1 orange
- Juice of 1 orange
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tsp honey
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup toasted sliced almonds
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss cauliflower florets with 1 tbsp olive oil, orange zest, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.  
2. While the cauliflower roasts, combine lentils with 2 cups water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer 20‑25 minutes until lentils are just tender but still hold their shape. Drain any excess water and set aside.  
3. In a small bowl whisk together orange juice, lemon juice, honey, and the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil; season with a pinch of salt and pepper.  
4. In a large mixing bowl combine the roasted cauliflower, cooked lentils, and the citrus dressing; toss gently to coat evenly.  
5. Transfer the salad to a serving platter, sprinkle with toasted sliced almonds and chopped parsley, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Citrus‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Lentil Salad

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Chickpea and Spinach Curry

Ingredients:
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 3 cups fresh spinach leaves
- 1 ½ tablespoons coconut oil
- 1 small onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch piece fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 teaspoon ground coriander
- ½ teaspoon turmeric
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon red‑pepper flakes (optional)
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tablespoons lime juice
- 1 cup coconut milk
- ½ cup vegetable broth
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Cooked basmati rice, for serving

Instructions:
1. Heat the coconut oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes.
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Sprinkle the cumin, coriander, turmeric, smoked paprika, and red‑pepper flakes over the aromatics; toast the spices for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
4. Add the chickpeas, coconut milk, and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer and let it cook for 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.
5. Fold in the lime zest, lime juice, and fresh spinach. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the spinach wilts and reduces in volume, about 2 minutes.
6. Season the curry with salt and black pepper to taste. Adjust the heat by adding more red‑pepper flakes or a splash of lime juice if desired.
7. Spoon the hot curry over bowls of cooked basmati rice and garnish with chopped cilantro leaves.
8. Serve immediately, accompanied by extra lime wedges if desired. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Chickpea and Spinach Curry

text:
Crispy Coconut Lime Chickpea Tacos with Mango Salsa

Ingredients:
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 ½ tbsp coconut oil, melted
- 1 tbsp lime zest
- 2 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 8 small corn tortillas
- 1 ripe mango, diced
- ¼ cup red onion, finely chopped
- 1 jalapeño, seeded and minced
- 2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 tbsp lime juice (for salsa)
- Pinch of sugar (optional, for salsa)

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, combine the chickpeas, melted coconut oil, lime zest, lime juice, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; toss until evenly coated.  
2. Heat a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the chickpea mixture and cook, stirring occasionally, for 6–8 minutes until the chickpeas are golden and crisp.  
3. While the chickpeas cook, prepare the mango salsa: in a small bowl, mix diced mango, red onion, jalapeño, cilantro, lime juice, and a pinch of sugar if desired; set aside.  
4. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet for about 30 seconds per side, or wrap in a damp paper towel and microwave for 20 seconds.  
5. To assemble each taco, place a generous spoonful of the crispy coconut‑lime chickpeas onto a tortilla, then top with mango salsa.  
6. Serve immediately, garnished with extra cilantro or lime wedges if desired.
title: Crispy Coconut Lime Chickpea Tacos with Mango Salsa

text:
Coconut‑Lime Spiced Quinoa Stuffed Bell Peppers

Ingredients:
- 4 large red or orange bell peppers, tops cut off and seeds removed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- 1 cup cooked chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup fresh spinach, roughly chopped
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, grated
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tablespoons lime juice
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon chili flakes (optional)
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Place the prepared bell peppers upright in a baking dish.
2. In a saucepan, combine the quinoa and coconut milk. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let stand for 5 minutes.
3. While the quinoa cooks, heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger, sauté for 1‑2 minutes until fragrant.
4. Stir in the chickpeas, cumin, chili flakes, lime zest, and lime juice. Cook for 3‑4 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. Season with salt and pepper.
5. Add the cooked quinoa and chopped spinach to the skillet. Toss everything together until the spinach wilts and the mixture is well combined. Adjust seasoning if needed.
6. Spoon the quinoa‑chickpea filling into each bell pepper cavity, packing it tightly. Sprinkle the tops with chopped cilantro.
7. Cover the baking dish with foil and bake for 25 minutes. Remove the foil and bake an additional 10‑12 minutes, or until the peppers are tender and the tops are lightly browned.
8. Remove from the oven and let cool for a few minutes before serving. Garnish with extra cilantro or a drizzle of lime juice if desired. Enjoy!
title: Coconut‑Lime Spiced Quinoa Stuffed Bell Peppers

text:
