Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa Stuffed Portobello Mushrooms

Ingredients:
- 4 large portobello mushroom caps, stems removed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, minced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tablespoons lemon juice
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
- 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, chopped
- 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Lightly brush the mushroom caps with olive oil and place them gill‑side up on a baking sheet.
2. In a saucepan, combine quinoa and vegetable broth; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
3. While the quinoa cooks, heat a skillet over medium heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. Sauté the minced ginger and garlic for 1‑2 minutes until fragrant.
4. Add the chickpeas to the skillet, stirring for 3‑4 minutes until they begin to brown slightly. Season with salt and pepper.
5. In a large bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, chickpea mixture, lemon juice, and chopped parsley. Mix well.
6. Spoon the quinoa‑chickpea filling evenly into each mushroom cap, pressing gently to pack the mixture.
7. Sprinkle grated Parmesan over the tops of the stuffed mushrooms, if using.
8. Bake for 18‑20 minutes, until the mushrooms are tender and the filling is heated through.
9. Remove from the oven, let cool for a couple of minutes, then serve warm, garnished with additional parsley if desired.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa Stuffed Portobello Mushrooms

text:
Maple‑Glazed Pumpkin and Lentil Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 lb (450 g) pumpkin, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 1 large onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat; add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
2. Stir in the garlic, cumin, and smoked paprika, cooking for another minute until fragrant.
3. Add the cubed pumpkin and lentils, then pour in the vegetable broth; bring the mixture to a boil.
4. Reduce the heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 20‑25 minutes, or until the pumpkin is tender and the lentils are soft.
5. Drizzle the maple syrup over the stew, stirring gently to combine; season with salt and pepper to taste.
6. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with chopped parsley, and serve hot.
title: Maple‑Glazed Pumpkin and Lentil Stew

text:
Maple‑Glazed Carrot and Chickpea Tagine

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch chunks
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 medium onion, thinly sliced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 in piece fresh ginger, grated
- 1 ½ cups diced tomatoes (canned or fresh)
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- ½ cup dried apricots, halved
- ¼ cup golden raisins
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- ½ tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the sliced onion and sauté for 4–5 minutes, until softened.
2. Stir in the garlic and ginger; cook for another minute until fragrant.
3. Add the carrot chunks, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, and smoked paprika. Toss to coat the carrots in the spices and cook for 2 minutes.
4. Pour in the diced tomatoes, vegetable broth, maple syrup, apricots, and raisins. Stir to combine, then bring the mixture to a gentle boil.
5. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20–25 minutes, or until the carrots are tender.
6. Stir in the chickpeas and continue to simmer uncovered for 5 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken slightly. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
7. Remove from heat and let the tagine rest for a couple of minutes. Garnish with fresh cilantro leaves before serving. Enjoy over couscous, quinoa, or warm flatbread.
title: Maple‑Glazed Carrot and Chickpea Tagine

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Brussels Sprouts and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 lb Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- ¼ cup sliced toasted almonds
- ¼ cup dried cranberries
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Add the halved Brussels sprouts and toss to coat evenly.  
3. Spread the Brussels sprouts in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until caramelized and tender.  
4. While the sprouts roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.  
5. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl. Add the roasted Brussels sprouts, toasted almonds, dried cranberries, and lemon juice. Toss gently to combine.  
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a drizzle of maple syrup if desired.  
7. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with extra almond slices or a sprinkle of cinnamon if desired.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Brussels Sprouts and Quinoa Salad

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa Stuffed Acorn Squash

Ingredients:
- 2 medium acorn squashes, halved and seeded
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- 1 tablespoon coconut oil
- 1 small red bell pepper, diced
- 1 cup cooked chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, grated
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tablespoons lime juice
- 1 tablespoon maple syrup
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- ¼ teaspoon smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Place the acorn squash halves cut‑side up on a baking sheet, brush lightly with coconut oil, and season with salt and pepper. Roast for 35‑40 minutes, until the flesh is tender and lightly caramelized.  
2. While the squash roasts, combine quinoa and coconut milk in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.  
3. In a large skillet over medium heat, add a drizzle of coconut oil. Sauté the garlic and ginger for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the diced red bell pepper and cook for 3‑4 minutes until softened.  
4. Stir in the cooked chickpeas, cumin, smoked paprika, lime zest, lime juice, and maple syrup. Cook for another 2 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. Season with salt and pepper to taste.  
5. Fold the quinoa into the skillet mixture, mixing until evenly combined. Adjust seasoning if needed.  
6. Remove the roasted acorn squash from the oven. Spoon the quinoa‑chickpea filling into each squash cavity, packing gently.  
7. Return the stuffed squashes to the oven and bake for an additional 10 minutes, allowing the tops to crisp slightly.  
8. Remove from the oven, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve warm. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa Stuffed Acorn Squash

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa & Roasted Veggie Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- 1 tablespoon coconut oil
- 1 tablespoon lime juice
- 1 tablespoon maple syrup
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1 sweet potato, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup broccoli florets
- 1 red bell pepper, sliced
- 1 cup cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Optional: lime wedges for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the sweet potato, broccoli, and red bell pepper with olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.
2. While the vegetables roast, heat coconut oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the rinsed quinoa and toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
3. Pour the coconut milk into the saucepan, bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.
4. In a small bowl, whisk together lime juice, maple syrup, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of olive oil to create a dressing.
5. In a large mixing bowl, combine the roasted vegetables, cooked chickpeas, and the lime‑maple dressing. Toss gently to coat.
6. To serve, divide the coconut quinoa among bowls, top with the dressed roasted veggie and chickpea mixture, and garnish with fresh cilantro and optional lime wedges. Enjoy warm or at room temperature.
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa & Roasted Veggie Bowl

text:
Ginger‑Lime Roasted Sweet Potato and Black Bean Bowl

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 Tbsp fresh ginger, minced
- 2 Tbsp lime juice
- 1 tsp lime zest
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 avocado, sliced
- 2 Tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cubed sweet potatoes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, minced ginger, lime juice, lime zest, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the seasoned sweet potatoes in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway through, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
4. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.  
5. In a small skillet over medium heat, add the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil and the rinsed black beans. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 3‑4 minutes until warmed through; season with a pinch of salt and pepper.  
6. To assemble each bowl, place a generous scoop of quinoa at the bottom, top with roasted sweet potatoes, black beans, sliced avocado, and a sprinkle of fresh cilantro. Drizzle any remaining pan juices over the bowl.  
7. Garnish with toasted pumpkin seeds, if using, and serve immediately with extra lime wedges on the side.
title: Ginger‑Lime Roasted Sweet Potato and Black Bean Bowl

text:
Spiced Pomegranate Quinoa with Roasted Cauliflower and Hazelnuts

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 small head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1 tablespoon maple syrup
- 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
- 1/2 cup pomegranate seeds
- 1/3 cup hazelnuts, roughly chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the cauliflower florets with 1 tablespoon olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
3. Roast the cauliflower for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden‑brown and tender.  
4. While the cauliflower roasts, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15‑18 minutes until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, maple syrup, lemon juice, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of pepper to make the dressing.  
6. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl; add the roasted cauliflower, pomegranate seeds, and chopped hazelnuts. Drizzle the dressing over the mixture and toss gently to combine.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if desired.  
8. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with fresh cilantro leaves. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Pomegranate Quinoa with Roasted Cauliflower and Hazelnuts

text:
Maple‑Glazed Seitan with Roasted Sweet Potato and Kale

Ingredients:
- 8 oz seitan, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp garlic powder
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 lb kale, stems removed and torn into bite‑size pieces
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 tsp lemon zest (optional, for finishing)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet. Roast for 20 minutes, stirring once.  
3. While the sweet potatoes roast, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil in a shallow dish.  
4. Add the seitan strips to the glaze, turning to coat evenly. Let sit for 5 minutes to absorb flavor.  
5. After the sweet potatoes have roasted 20 minutes, push them to one side of the pan and add the glazed seitan strips in a single layer. Roast for an additional 12‑15 minutes, turning the seitan halfway through, until the edges are caramelized and the sweet potatoes are tender.  
6. While the seitan and sweet potatoes finish cooking, heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add the kale and a splash of water; sauté for 3‑4 minutes until wilted but still bright green. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.  
7. Remove the pan from the oven. Transfer the roasted sweet potatoes and seitan to the skillet with the kale, tossing gently to combine. Adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a drizzle of maple syrup if desired.  
8. Serve hot, sprinkled with lemon zest for a fresh finish. Enjoy as a hearty main dish or over cooked grains like quinoa or brown rice.
title: Maple‑Glazed Seitan with Roasted Sweet Potato and Kale

text:
Garlic‑Infused Sweet Potato and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 1  tablespoon olive oil
- 2  cloves garlic, minced
- 1  teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½  teaspoon ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2  cups baby spinach leaves
- ½  cup cooked quinoa
- ¼  cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2  tablespoons tahini
- 1  tablespoon lemon juice
- 1  teaspoon maple syrup
- Water, as needed for dressing consistency

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the sweet potato cubes with olive oil, minced garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper; spread them in a single layer on a baking sheet.
2. Roast the sweet potatoes for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until tender and lightly caramelized.
3. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine the chickpeas with a drizzle of olive oil, a pinch of salt, and a sprinkle of smoked paprika; spread on a separate part of the baking sheet and roast for the last 12‑15 minutes until crisp.
4. In a small bowl, whisk together tahini, lemon juice, maple syrup, and enough water to achieve a drizzle‑able consistency; season with salt and pepper.
5. Assemble the bowls: start with a base of cooked quinoa, add a handful of baby spinach, then top with roasted sweet potatoes, crispy chickpeas, and toasted pumpkin seeds.
6. Drizzle the tahini‑lemon dressing over the assembled bowls and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Garlic‑Infused Sweet Potato and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

text:
Garlic‑Lime Grilled Halloumi with Minted Couscous

Ingredients:
- 8 oz Halloumi cheese, sliced ½‑inch thick
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 Tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tsp lime zest
- 1 cup couscous
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- ¼ cup fresh mint leaves, finely chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional: ½ cup halved cherry tomatoes for garnish

Instructions:
1. In a shallow bowl, whisk together 1 Tbsp olive oil, minced garlic, lime juice, lime zest, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Add the Halloumi slices, turning to coat; let marinate while you prepare the couscous (about 10 minutes).  
2. Meanwhile, bring the vegetable broth to a boil in a small saucepan. Stir in the couscous, cover, and remove from heat. Let stand 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.  
3. Stir the chopped mint into the couscous, drizzle with the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, and season with additional salt and pepper to taste. Set aside.  
4. Preheat a grill pan or outdoor grill over medium‑high heat. Lightly oil the grates. Grill the marinated Halloumi 2‑3 minutes per side, until golden brown grill marks appear and the cheese is warmed through.  
5. Transfer the grilled Halloumi to a serving platter. Spoon the minted couscous around the cheese, and scatter cherry tomato halves if using.  
6. Finish with an extra squeeze of lime juice and a sprinkle of fresh mint leaves. Serve immediately, warm or at room temperature.
title: Garlic‑Lime Grilled Halloumi with Minted Couscous

text:
Maple‑Sage Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Grain Bowl

Ingredients:
- 3 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch rounds
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp fresh sage leaves, finely chopped
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp sea salt
- ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice
- 2 Tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the carrot rounds and chickpeas with 1 Tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, chopped sage, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until carrots are tender and chickpeas are crisp‑golden.  
4. While the vegetables roast, bring 2 cups water to a boil in a saucepan. Add the quinoa, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed and quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.  
5. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large serving bowl. Top with the roasted carrots and chickpeas. Drizzle the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil and lemon juice over the bowl, then toss gently to combine.  
6. Sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds on top for crunch and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Sage Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Grain Bowl

text:
Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Carrot and Farro Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup farro, rinsed
- 3 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch rounds
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 teaspoon lemon zest
- 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
- 1 tablespoon fresh thyme leaves, chopped
- 1/4 cup toasted pine nuts
- 1/4 cup crumbled feta cheese
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional: 1 tablespoon honey for a touch of sweetness

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the carrot rounds with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread them in a single layer and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
3. While the carrots roast, bring 2 cups water to a boil in a saucepan, add the farro, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 20‑25 minutes until al dente; drain any excess water and set aside.  
4. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, chopped thyme, and honey (if using); season with salt and pepper.  
5. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked farro, roasted carrots, and dressing; toss gently to coat evenly.  
6. Transfer the salad to a serving platter, sprinkle with toasted pine nuts and crumbled feta, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Carrot and Farro Salad

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Lentil Soup

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1 carrot, diced
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk
- Juice of 1 lemon
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves for garnish (optional)

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 4–5 minutes, until translucent.
2. Stir in the minced garlic, grated ginger, and ground turmeric; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add the diced carrot and rinsed red lentils, stirring to coat them with the aromatics.
4. Pour in the vegetable broth, bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer. Cover and cook for 15–20 minutes, or until the lentils and carrots are tender.
5. Using an immersion blender, blend the soup until smooth (or blend in batches in a countertop blender). Return to the pot if needed.
6. Stir in the coconut milk and lemon juice, and season with salt and black pepper to taste. Heat gently for another 2–3 minutes, avoiding a rapid boil.
7. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves if desired, and serve hot.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Lentil Soup

text:
Lime‑Infused Coconut Chickpea & Sweet Potato Curry

Ingredients:
- 1 lb (450 g) sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 can (13.5 oz) full‑fat coconut milk
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- 1 large onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- zest of 1 lime
- 2 tbsp lime juice
- 2 tbsp red curry paste
- 1 tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 2 tbsp coconut oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Cooked jasmine rice, for serving

Instructions:
1. Heat the coconut oil in a large pot over medium heat; add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.  
2. Stir in the garlic, ginger, and red curry paste; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
3. Add the sweet potato cubes, chickpeas, coconut milk, vegetable broth, lime zest, lime juice, soy sauce, and maple syrup; stir to combine.  
4. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer until the sweet potatoes are tender, about 15–20 minutes.  
5. Taste and season with salt and pepper; adjust lime juice or maple syrup if a brighter or sweeter balance is desired.  
6. Remove the pot from heat and let the curry rest for 5 minutes to allow flavors to meld.  
7. Spoon the curry over bowls of cooked jasmine rice and garnish with fresh cilantro leaves.  
8. Serve immediately, offering extra lime wedges on the side for added brightness.
title: Lime‑Infused Coconut Chickpea & Sweet Potato Curry

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Roasted Eggplant and Lentil Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cubed
- 1 cup brown lentils, rinsed
- ½ cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 lemon, zest and juice
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, minced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 3 cups vegetable broth
- ¼ tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the cubed eggplant with 1 tablespoon olive oil, half the lemon zest, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender.
2. While the eggplant roasts, combine lentils, quinoa, vegetable broth, cumin, smoked paprika, minced ginger, and garlic in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until both lentils and quinoa are cooked and liquid is absorbed.
3. Remove the saucepan from heat and let it sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff the mixture with a fork and stir in the remaining lemon zest, lemon juice, and the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil. Adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.
4. Gently fold the roasted eggplant into the lentil‑quinoa mixture, ensuring even distribution.
5. Transfer the pilaf to a serving bowl, garnish with chopped fresh parsley, and serve warm. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Ginger Roasted Eggplant and Lentil Pilaf

text:
Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Eggplant and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp ground black pepper
- 1 tsp sea salt
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- ¼ cup dried cranberries
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp honey or maple syrup
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh mint
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the eggplant cubes with olive oil, cinnamon, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper; spread them on a baking sheet.
2. Roast the eggplant for 25‑30 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.
3. While the eggplant roasts, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and let cool slightly.
4. In a small bowl, whisk together lemon juice, honey (or maple syrup), and a pinch of salt to make the dressing.
5. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted eggplant, toasted pumpkin seeds, dried cranberries, mint, and parsley.
6. Drizzle the dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat evenly. Adjust seasoning with extra salt or lemon juice if desired.
7. Serve warm or at room temperature as a hearty main dish or side. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Eggplant and Quinoa Salad

text:
Sage‑Infused Roasted Butternut Squash and Barley Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 cup pearl barley, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 medium butternut squash, peeled and cubed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp fresh sage, finely chopped
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- 1/4 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tbsp dried cranberries
- 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the cubed butternut squash with olive oil, sage, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway, until tender and caramelized.
2. While the squash roasts, combine the rinsed barley and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30‑35 minutes, or until the barley is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
3. Transfer the cooked barley to a large mixing bowl. Add the roasted squash, toasted pumpkin seeds, dried cranberries, and fresh lemon juice. Toss gently to combine, adjusting seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed.
4. Serve warm or at room temperature as a hearty side dish or a light main course. Enjoy!
title: Sage‑Infused Roasted Butternut Squash and Barley Pilaf

text:
Maple‑Glazed Sweet Corn and Black Bean Salad

Ingredients:
- 3 cups fresh or frozen sweet corn kernels
- 1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- ½ red onion, finely chopped
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp lime juice
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional: 1 avocado, diced, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat a large skillet over medium‑high heat and add the corn kernels; cook, stirring occasionally, until the corn is lightly charred, about 5‑7 minutes. Transfer to a large mixing bowl.
2. In a small bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, lime juice, olive oil, ground cumin, salt, and pepper to create the dressing.
3. Add the black beans, diced red bell pepper, red onion, and cilantro to the bowl with the roasted corn; toss gently to combine.
4. Pour the maple‑lime dressing over the salad and toss again until everything is evenly coated.
5. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice if needed.
6. Serve the salad at room temperature or chilled, topped with diced avocado if desired. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Sweet Corn and Black Bean Salad

text:
Roasted Garlic and Chili Lime Quinoa with Pan‑Seared Cod

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon chili flakes
- Zest of 1 lime
- Juice of 1 lime
- 2 × 6‑oz cod fillets
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 tablespoon butter
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine the rinsed quinoa and water; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the water is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
2. While the quinoa cooks, heat the olive oil in a small skillet over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and chili flakes, sautéing for 1‑2 minutes until fragrant but not browned.
3. Stir the garlic‑chili mixture, lime zest, and lime juice into the cooked quinoa; season with salt and pepper to taste. Keep warm.
4. Pat the cod fillets dry with paper towels, then season both sides generously with salt and pepper.
5. In a non‑stick skillet, melt the butter over medium‑high heat. Add the cod fillets skin‑side down (if skin is present) and sear for 3‑4 minutes until the edges turn opaque.
6. Flip the fillets and cook an additional 2‑3 minutes, or until the fish flakes easily with a fork. Remove from the pan and let rest for a minute.
7. Plate a generous scoop of the lime‑garlic quinoa, top with a seared cod fillet, and garnish with chopped cilantro. Serve immediately.
title: Roasted Garlic and Chili Lime Quinoa with Pan‑Seared Cod

text:
Maple‑Glazed Cauliflower Steaks with Turmeric Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 large cauliflower head, sliced into 1‑inch thick steaks
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- ¼ cup toasted sliced almonds
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- Zest of 1 lemon

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Brush both sides of each cauliflower steak generously with the glaze.  
3. Arrange the steaks on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, flipping once, until golden brown and tender.  
4. While the cauliflower roasts, combine the rinsed quinoa, vegetable broth, and turmeric in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy.  
5. Fluff the quinoa with a fork and stir in the toasted almonds, parsley, and lemon zest. Season with a pinch of salt if needed.  
6. To serve, place a cauliflower steak on each plate, spoon a generous mound of turmeric quinoa alongside, and drizzle any remaining maple glaze from the pan over the top. Enjoy warm.
title: Maple‑Glazed Cauliflower Steaks with Turmeric Quinoa

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Shrimp and Mango Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups water
- 12 large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 tablespoon coconut oil
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon ground coriander
- Zest of 1 lime
- Juice of 2 limes
- 1 tablespoon honey
- 1 ripe mango, diced
- ¼ cup red bell pepper, finely diced
- ¼ cup red onion, thinly sliced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan, combine the quinoa and water; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and set aside to cool.
2. While the quinoa cooks, whisk together the lime zest, lime juice, honey, smoked paprika, cumin, coriander, salt, and pepper in a small bowl to create the dressing.
3. Heat the coconut oil in a skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the shrimp, season with a pinch of salt, and sauté for 2‑3 minutes per side until pink and opaque. Transfer the cooked shrimp to a plate and let cool slightly.
4. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooled quinoa, diced mango, red bell pepper, red onion, and cilantro.
5. Add the cooked shrimp to the bowl, then pour the lime‑coconut dressing over everything. Toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly.
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired. Serve the salad chilled or at room temperature, garnished with extra cilantro or lime wedges if desired.
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Shrimp and Mango Quinoa Salad

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Black Bean Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 (15‑oz) can black beans, drained and rinsed
- 1 red onion, thinly sliced
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 2 Tbsp fresh lime juice
- 4 cups mixed salad greens (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.  
3. Add the cubed sweet potatoes to the bowl and toss to coat evenly with the maple‑cinnamon mixture.  
4. Spread the sweet potatoes in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until tender and caramelized.  
5. While the sweet potatoes roast, place the sliced red onion on a separate half‑sheet and drizzle with a little olive oil; roast for the last 10 minutes of the sweet potato cooking time, until softened and slightly charred.  
6. In a large mixing bowl, combine the roasted sweet potatoes, roasted red onion, black beans, chopped cilantro, and lime juice. Toss gently to mix.  
7. If using, arrange mixed salad greens on a serving platter or individual plates and top with the warm sweet‑potato‑black‑bean mixture.  
8. Serve immediately, optionally drizzling any remaining pan juices over the salad for extra flavor.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Black Bean Salad

text:
Lemon‑Basil Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Sun‑Dried Tomatoes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1/3 cup sun‑dried tomatoes, chopped
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- ¼ cup fresh basil leaves, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss chickpeas with 1 Tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast 20‑25 minutes, shaking halfway, until crisp.
2. While chickpeas roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat, let sit 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together remaining olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt.
4. Transfer cooked quinoa to a large bowl; add roasted chickpeas, sun‑dried tomatoes, and chopped basil. Drizzle the lemon dressing over the mixture and toss gently to combine.
5. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if needed. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Basil Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Sun‑Dried Tomatoes

text:
Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad with Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch rounds
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- 1/2 tsp sea salt
- 1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 1/4 cup pomegranate seeds
- 1/4 cup crumbled feta cheese
- 2 Tbsp fresh mint leaves, chopped
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tsp honey

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the carrot rounds with olive oil, cinnamon, cumin, salt, and pepper until evenly coated. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
3. Roast the carrots for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until tender and lightly caramelized. Remove from the oven and let cool slightly.  
4. While the carrots roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside to cool.  
5. In a large mixing bowl, whisk together lemon juice, honey, and a pinch of salt. Add the cooled quinoa and toss to combine.  
6. Gently fold in the roasted carrots, pomegranate seeds, crumbled feta, and chopped mint. Adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if desired.  
7. Serve the salad at room temperature or chilled, garnished with a few extra pomegranate seeds and mint leaves. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad with Pomegranate

text:
Spiced Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Garlic Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 14 oz extra‑firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- 2 tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp fresh lime juice
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 2 green onions, sliced (for garnish)
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 400 °F (200 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, whisk together maple syrup, smoked paprika, cumin, cayenne, soy sauce, and lime juice. Add tofu cubes, toss to coat, and let marinate 10 minutes.  
3. Spread marinated tofu on the prepared baking sheet. Bake 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and slightly crisp.  
4. While tofu bakes, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes or until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit 5 minutes.  
5. In a skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add minced garlic
title: Spiced Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Garlic Quinoa

text:
Maple‑Ginger Glazed Eggplant with Quinoa Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 2 medium eggplants, sliced into ½‑inch rounds
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 3 Tbsp maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp soy sauce (or tamari)
- 1 Tbsp freshly grated ginger
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 Tbsp lime juice
- ½ tsp ground cinnamon
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, grated ginger, minced garlic, olive oil, lime juice, cinnamon, salt, and pepper.  
3. Brush both sides of each eggplant slice with the glaze, placing them on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast the eggplant for 20‑25 minutes, flipping halfway through, until tender and caramelized.  
5. While the eggplant roasts, combine the quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed.  
6. Remove the quinoa from heat and fluff with a fork; season with a pinch of salt and pepper.  
7. To serve, spoon a bed of quinoa onto each plate, top with the glazed eggplant rounds, and drizzle any remaining pan glaze over the top.  
8. Garnish with chopped cilantro, if desired, and enjoy warm.
title: Maple‑Ginger Glazed Eggplant with Quinoa Pilaf

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa and Roasted Eggplant Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 medium eggplant, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and diced ½‑inch
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)
- Lime wedges (for serving)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the eggplant and sweet potato cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, salt, pepper, and a pinch of smoked paprika. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
3. While the vegetables roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.  
4. In a small skillet over medium heat, add the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil. Add the chickpeas, cumin, coriander, cayenne (if using), and a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5‑7 minutes until the chickpeas are golden and fragrant.  
5. In a small saucepan, whisk together coconut milk, maple syrup, lime juice, and a pinch of salt. Heat gently until just simmering, then remove from heat.  
6. To assemble the bowl, divide the cooked quinoa among four serving bowls. Top each with a generous portion of roasted eggplant, sweet potato, and spiced chickpeas. Drizzle the coconut‑lime sauce over everything.  
7. Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve with lime wedges on the side for an extra burst of freshness. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa and Roasted Eggplant Bowl

text:
Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Grain Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 small head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup farro (or quinoa), cooked according to package instructions
- ¼ cup toasted sliced almonds
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- 1 Tbsp tahini
- 1 Tbsp warm water (more if needed)
- 1 tsp honey or maple syrup (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cauliflower florets and chickpeas with olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, thyme, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the cauliflower is golden‑brown and the chickpeas are crisp.  
4. While the vegetables roast, cook the farro (or quinoa) according to the package directions; fluff with a fork and set aside.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together tahini, warm water, and honey (if using) until smooth and drizzle‑able; add a pinch of salt to taste.  
6. To assemble the bowl, divide the cooked farro among serving bowls, top with the roasted cauliflower and chickpeas, sprinkle toasted almonds, chopped parsley, and a drizzle of the tahini sauce.  
7. Finish with an extra squeeze of lemon juice, if desired, and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Grain Bowl

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu and Roasted Beet Salad with Walnut Vinaigrette

Ingredients:
- 14 oz extra‑firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 3 medium beets, peeled and cut into ½‑inch wedges
- 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup
- 1 tablespoon soy sauce
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 3 cups mixed baby greens
- ½ cup toasted walnut halves
- ¼ cup crumbled goat cheese (optional)
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar
- 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Toss the beet wedges with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper, then spread them in a single layer and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and caramelized.  
2. While the beets roast, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, smoked paprika, and the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil in a bowl; add the tofu cubes and gently toss to coat.  
3. After the beets have roasted, increase the oven temperature to 425°F (220°C). Spread the glazed tofu on the same baking sheet (or a separate one) and bake for 15‑20 minutes, turning once, until the edges are golden and crisp.  
4. In a small jar, combine the apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of maple syrup; shake well to emulsify, then slowly whisk in 2 tablespoons of warm water to create a smooth vinaigrette.  
5. In a large salad bowl, place the mixed baby greens, roasted beets, and crispy tofu. Drizzle the walnut vinaigrette over the top and toss gently to combine.  
6. Sprinkle toasted walnut halves and crumbled goat cheese over the salad, season with additional salt and pepper if desired, and serve immediately.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu and Roasted Beet Salad with Walnut Vinaigrette

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Parsnip and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 large parsnips, peeled and cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- ¼ cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped
- ¼ cup dried cranberries
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- Optional: 2 Tbsp crumbled feta cheese for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, cinnamon, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Add the cubed parsnips and toss to coat evenly.  
3. Spread the coated parsnips in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning once halfway through, until golden‑brown and tender.  
4. While the parsnips roast, combine the rinsed quinoa and water (or broth) in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.  
5. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl. Add the roasted parsnips, toasted walnuts, dried cranberries, and lemon juice. Toss gently to combine.  
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a drizzle of maple syrup if desired.  
7. Serve warm or at room temperature, optionally topped with crumbled feta cheese. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Parsnip and Quinoa Salad

text:
Honey‑Sriracha Glazed Tempeh with Sesame Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 2 tbsp honey
- 1 tbsp sriracha sauce
- 1 tbsp low‑sodium soy sauce
- 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 1 cup broccoli florets
- 1 large carrot, sliced into thin matchsticks
- 2 tbsp sesame seeds, toasted
- 2 green onions, sliced
- Salt and pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, whisk together honey, sriracha, soy sauce, sesame oil, minced garlic, and lime juice to create the glaze.  
2. Place the tempeh cubes in a shallow dish and pour half of the glaze over them, tossing to coat evenly. Let marinate for 10 minutes.  
3. While the tempeh marinates, combine quinoa and water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until water is absorbed. Remove from heat and fluff with a fork.  
4. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated tempeh and the remaining glaze; cook, stirring occasionally, until the tempeh is golden brown and the glaze thickens, about 5‑7 minutes. Transfer to a plate.  
5. In the same skillet, add a splash of water and steam the broccoli and carrot matchsticks until just tender, about 3‑4 minutes. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.  
6. To assemble, divide the cooked quinoa among bowls. Top with glazed tempeh, steamed broccoli, and carrots. Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds and sliced green onions over each bowl.  
7. Drizzle any leftover glaze from the pan over the bowls, adjust seasoning if needed, and serve warm.
title: Honey‑Sriracha Glazed Tempeh with Sesame Quinoa

text:
Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Eggplant and Chickpea Couscous

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup couscous
- 1 ¼ cups vegetable broth or water
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 lemon (zest and juice)
- 2 tsp fresh thyme leaves (or 1 tsp dried thyme)
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- ½ tsp salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- ¼ cup toasted pine nuts (optional)
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the eggplant cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, half the minced garlic, salt, pepper, and half the lemon zest. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
3. Roast the eggplant for 20 minutes, then add the chickpeas (tossed with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, garlic, salt, and pepper) to the pan. Roast for an additional 15 minutes, or until the eggplant is golden and tender and the chickpeas are slightly crisp.  
4. While the vegetables roast, bring the vegetable broth (or water) to a boil in a medium saucepan. Stir in the couscous, cover, and remove from heat. Let sit for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.  
5. Transfer the fluffed couscous to a large mixing bowl. Add the roasted eggplant and chickpeas, lemon juice, lemon zest, and fresh thyme. Toss gently to combine, adjusting salt and pepper to taste.  
6. Serve the couscous mixture in bowls, sprinkled with toasted pine nuts and chopped parsley for color and crunch. Enjoy warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Eggplant and Chickpea Couscous

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea and Spinach Stew

Ingredients:
- 2 cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 4 cups fresh spinach leaves, roughly chopped
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 large onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch piece fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- ½ teaspoon sea salt (or to taste)
- ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish (optional)

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 4–5 minutes, until softened and translucent.  
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for another 1 minute, stirring constantly to avoid burning.  
3. Sprinkle the ground turmeric over the aromatics, stirring to coat the mixture; let it toast lightly for 30 seconds to release its flavor.  
4. Add the cooked chickpeas, coconut milk, and vegetable broth to the pot. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer.  
5. Simmer the stew for 10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the broth to thicken slightly.  
6. Stir in the chopped spinach and let it wilt, about 2 minutes.  
7. Add the fresh lemon juice, salt, and black pepper; taste and adjust seasoning as needed.  
8. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with cilantro leaves if desired, and serve hot with crusty bread or over cooked rice.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea and Spinach Stew

text:
Crispy Orange‑Glazed Tempeh with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- ¼ cup fresh orange juice
- 2 tbsp soy sauce (or tamari)
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp cornstarch
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- ½ cup water
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- ¼ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 2 green onions, thinly sliced (optional garnish)

Instructions:
1. In a medium bowl, whisk together orange juice, soy sauce, maple syrup, and cornstarch until smooth; set aside.
2. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the tempeh cubes and sauté for 4–5 minutes, turning until golden brown on all sides.
3. Pour the orange‑glaze mixture over the tempeh. Reduce heat to medium and cook, stirring frequently, until the sauce thickens and coats the tempeh, about 2 minutes. Remove from heat and keep warm.
4. While the tempeh cooks, combine quinoa, coconut milk, water, lime juice, salt, and pepper in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy.
5. Fluff the quinoa with a fork and transfer to a serving bowl. Top with the crispy orange‑glazed tempeh.
6. Garnish with sliced green onions, if desired, and serve immediately. Enjoy!
title: Crispy Orange‑Glazed Tempeh with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Garlic Sweet Potato Mash

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and sliced into ½‑inch slabs
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp ground ginger
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- ¼ cup unsweetened almond milk
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh chives, thinly sliced (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a shallow dish, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, smoked paprika, and ground ginger.  
3. Brush both sides of each tofu slab with the maple‑ginger glaze and place them on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast the tofu for 20‑25 minutes, flipping halfway through, until the edges are caramelized and the tofu is heated through.  
5. While the tofu roasts, toss the sweet potato cubes with minced garlic, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on a second baking sheet.  
6. Roast the sweet potatoes for 25‑30 minutes, stirring once, until they are tender and lightly browned.  
7. Transfer the roasted sweet potatoes to a large bowl; add almond milk and mash with a potato masher or fork until smooth. Adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.  
8. Plate a generous scoop of the sweet potato mash, top with the maple‑glazed tofu slabs, and drizzle any remaining pan juices over the dish.  
9. Garnish with sliced chives, if desired, and serve warm.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Garlic Sweet Potato Mash

text:
Crispy Coconut‑Lime Tempeh with Mango Avocado Salsa

Ingredients:
- 1 package (8 oz) tempeh, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- ¼ cup coconut milk
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 2 tbsp coconut oil, divided
- 1 ripe mango, diced
- 1 avocado, diced
- ¼ cup red onion, finely chopped
- 1 jalapeño, seeded and minced
- 2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 tbsp lime zest
- Optional: tortilla chips or rice for serving

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, whisk together coconut milk, lime juice, maple syrup, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Add the tempeh cubes and toss to coat; let marinate for 10 minutes.
2. Heat 1 tbsp coconut oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Remove tempeh from the marinade (reserve the liquid) and add to the skillet. Cook, turning occasionally, until golden and crispy, about 6‑8 minutes. Transfer tempeh to a plate.
3. Add the remaining 1 tbsp coconut oil to the skillet. Pour in the reserved marinade and simmer for 2‑3 minutes until slightly thickened, then return the tempeh to the pan and toss to coat. Remove from heat.
4. In a separate bowl, combine diced mango, avocado, red onion, jalapeño, cilantro, lime zest, and a pinch of salt. Gently stir to create the salsa.
5. Serve the crispy coconut‑lime tempeh topped with mango avocado salsa. Pair with tortilla chips or a bed of rice if desired. Enjoy!
title: Crispy Coconut‑Lime Tempeh with Mango Avocado Salsa

text:
Spiced Coconut‑Lime Chickpea and Tomato Stew

Ingredients:
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 large onion, diced
- 3 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1 can (14 oz) diced tomatoes
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- 1 lime, zest and juice
- ½ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.  
2. Stir in the garlic, ginger, cumin, smoked paprika, and turmeric; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
3. Pour in the diced tomatoes with their juices, chickpeas, coconut milk, and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to a simmer.  
4. Simmer the stew for 15‑20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the flavors meld and the sauce thickens slightly.  
5. Add the lime zest, lime juice, and season with salt and pepper. Stir to combine.  
6. Remove from heat and fold in the chopped cilantro. Adjust seasoning if needed.  
7. Serve hot over steamed rice, quinoa, or with warm flatbread. Garnish with extra cilantro and a lime wedge if desired.
title: Spiced Coconut‑Lime Chickpea and Tomato Stew

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Acorn Squash with Lentil Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 2 small acorn squash, halved and seeded
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 tsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 ½ cups vegetable broth
- 1 small onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp ground turmeric
- 2 Tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- Juice of ½ lemon

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, cinnamon, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Brush the mixture evenly over the cut sides of the acorn squash halves. Place them cut‑side down on the prepared sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, or until the flesh is tender and caramelized.  
3. While the squash roasts, combine the lentils and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender but still hold their shape. Drain any excess liquid if needed.  
4. In a skillet over medium heat, add a drizzle of olive oil and sauté the onion until translucent, about 4 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for another 30 seconds. Stir in the cumin, smoked paprika, and turmeric, cooking until fragrant, about 1 minute.  
5. Add the cooked lentils to the skillet, tossing to coat them with the spiced onion mixture. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste, then remove from heat.  
6. To serve, place a roasted acorn squash half on each plate. Spoon a generous portion of the spiced lentil pilaf into the cavity of the squash. Drizzle with lemon juice, then sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds and chopped parsley over the top.  
7. Enjoy the warm, sweet‑savory combination immediately.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Acorn Squash with Lentil Pilaf

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Farro with Roasted Broccoli and Almonds

Ingredients:
- 1 cup farro, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 large head broccoli, cut into florets
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp fresh ginger, minced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tbsp lemon juice
- ¼ cup sliced almonds, toasted
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the broccoli florets with 1 tablespoon olive oil, turmeric, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelized.
2. While the broccoli roasts, combine the farro and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25‑30 minutes, or until the farro is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
3. In a small skillet, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and ginger, sauté for 1‑2 minutes until fragrant.
4. Stir the lemon zest and lemon juice into the garlic‑ginger mixture, then pour it over the cooked farro. Toss to combine, seasoning with additional salt and pepper to taste.
5. Transfer the farro to a serving bowl, top with the roasted broccoli, and sprinkle toasted sliced almonds over the top.
6. Serve warm or at room temperature, optionally garnished with extra lemon zest.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Farro with Roasted Broccoli and Almonds

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Farro Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup farro, rinsed
- 3 medium beets, peeled and cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- ½ tsp ground cinnamon
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- ½ tsp sea salt, plus more to taste
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 2 cups arugula
- ¼ cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped
- ¼ cup crumbled goat cheese
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tsp Dijon mustard (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the beet cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, ½ tsp salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the beets in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring once, until tender and caramelized.  
4. While the beets roast, bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add the farro, reduce to a simmer, and cook 20‑25 minutes until al dente. Drain and rinse under cold water to stop cooking.  
5. In a small jar, whisk together the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, lemon juice, Dijon mustard (if using), and a pinch of salt and pepper to make the dressing.  
6. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked farro, roasted beets, arugula, and toasted walnuts. Drizzle with the dressing and toss gently to combine.  
7. Transfer the salad to a serving platter or individual plates, and top with crumbled goat cheese.  
8. Serve warm or at room temperature, adjusting seasoning with extra salt or pepper if needed. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Farro Salad

text:
Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Chickpea Tostadas

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 8 small corn tortillas
- 1 ripe avocado, sliced
- 1 lime, cut into wedges
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- ¼ cup red onion, thinly sliced
- Optional: hot sauce or chipotle mayo for drizzling

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the diced sweet potatoes with ½ Tbsp olive oil, ½ tsp cumin, ½ tsp smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
3. While the sweet potatoes roast, heat the remaining ½ Tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the chickpeas, the remaining cumin and smoked paprika, maple syrup, salt, and pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, for 5‑7 minutes until the chickpeas are glossy and slightly crisp.  
4. Warm the corn tortillas: stack them on a plate, cover with a damp paper towel, and microwave for 30‑45 seconds, or toast them individually in a dry skillet for 30 seconds per side.  
5. Assemble each tostada by spreading a generous spoonful of the maple‑glazed chickpeas onto a tortilla, followed by a mound of roasted sweet potatoes. Top with avocado slices, red onion, and a sprinkle of fresh cilantro.  
6. Finish with a squeeze of lime juice over each tostada and, if desired, drizzle with hot sauce or chipotle mayo. Serve immediately.
title: Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Chickpea Tostadas

text:
Spiced Orange‑Glazed Cauliflower and Chickpea Tacos

Ingredients:
- 1 small head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- Salt and black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup orange marmalade
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 8 small corn tortillas
- ½ cup red cabbage, thinly sliced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 lime, cut into wedges
- Optional garnish: sliced radishes, avocado slices

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cauliflower florets with 1 tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, cayenne, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
3. Roast the cauliflower for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.  
4. While the cauliflower roasts, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the chickpeas, season with a pinch of salt and pepper, and sauté for 5‑7 minutes until slightly crisp.  
5. In a small saucepan, combine orange marmalade, soy sauce, rice vinegar, and grated ginger. Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring until smooth, then remove from heat.  
6. Toss the roasted cauliflower and sautéed chickpeas together in a large bowl, then drizzle the orange glaze over them. Toss gently to coat evenly.  
7. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet or microwave for 30 seconds.  
8. Assemble each taco by placing a generous spoonful of the orange‑glazed cauliflower and chickpeas onto a tortilla, then top with red cabbage, cilantro, and a squeeze of lime juice. Add optional radish or avocado slices if desired.  
9. Serve immediately and enjoy!
title: Spiced Orange‑Glazed Cauliflower and Chickpea Tacos

text:
Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Cauliflower and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 medium head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- ¼ cup dried cranberries
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cauliflower florets with olive oil, cinnamon, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the seasoned cauliflower on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway through, until golden and tender.  
4. While the cauliflower roasts, combine quinoa and 2 cups water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes or until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside to cool slightly.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together lemon juice and a drizzle of olive oil; season with a pinch of salt and pepper to make the dressing.  
6. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted cauliflower, toasted pumpkin seeds, dried cranberries, and chopped parsley.  
7. Drizzle the lemon dressing over the salad and toss gently to combine all ingredients.  
8. Serve warm or at room temperature, adjusting seasoning with extra salt, pepper, or lemon juice if desired.
title: Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Cauliflower and Quinoa Salad

text:
Spiced Cardamom Carrot and Quinoa Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 large carrots, peeled and diced
- 1 small onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp ground cardamom
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- 1/4 tsp smoked paprika
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1/4 cup toasted almonds, sliced
- 2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Juice of 1/2 lemon

Instructions:
1. Rinse quinoa under cold water until the water runs clear; set aside.  
2. In a medium saucepan, heat 1 Tbsp olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced carrots and sauté for 5‑6 minutes until they begin to soften.  
3. Add the onion and garlic; cook another 2 minutes until fragrant.  
4. Stir in ground cardamom, cumin, smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt; toast the spices for about 30 seconds.  
5. Add the rinsed quinoa and vegetable broth; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15‑18 minutes, or until the quinoa is fluffy and the liquid is absorbed.  
6. While the quinoa cooks, heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil in a small skillet over medium heat. Toast the sliced almonds until golden, about 2‑3 minutes; set aside.  
7. Fluff the cooked quinoa with a fork, then stir in lemon juice, fresh cilantro, and the toasted almonds. Adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.  
8. Serve warm as a side dish or a light main, garnished with extra cilantro and a drizzle of olive oil if desired.
title: Spiced Cardamom Carrot and Quinoa Pilaf

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa and Roasted Broccoli Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 large head broccoli, cut into florets
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1/2 teaspoon ground coriander
- 1/2 teaspoon sea salt
- 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
- 1 lime, zest and juice
- 1 tablespoon coconut aminos or soy sauce
- 1 tablespoon maple syrup
- 1/4 cup toasted coconut flakes
- 2 green onions, thinly sliced
- Optional garnish: fresh cilantro leaves

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the broccoli florets with olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika, coriander, salt, and pepper. Spread evenly on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until crisp‑tender and lightly browned.  
3. While the broccoli roasts, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the grains are fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
4. In a small bowl, whisk together lime zest, lime juice, coconut aminos, and maple syrup. Adjust seasoning with a pinch more salt if desired.  
5. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl. Add the roasted broccoli, drizzle the lime‑coconut dressing over the top, and toss gently to combine.  
6. Divide the mixture between two serving bowls. Sprinkle each with toasted coconut flakes, sliced green onions, and fresh cilantro if using. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa and Roasted Broccoli Bowl

text:
Cinnamon‑Spiced Carrot and Lentil Soup

Ingredients:
- 2 lb carrots, peeled and diced
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- ½ tsp ground cinnamon
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.  
2. Stir in the garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
3. Add the diced carrots, cumin, coriander, and cinnamon. Toss to coat the vegetables with the spices and cook for 2 minutes.  
4. Pour in the vegetable broth and bring the mixture to a boil. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer until the carrots are very tender, about 15 minutes.  
5. Add the rinsed red lentils and continue to simmer, uncovered, for 10‑12 minutes, or until the lentils are soft and beginning to break down.  
6. Stir in the coconut milk, then season with salt and pepper to taste. Use an immersion blender (or transfer to a countertop blender in batches) to puree the soup until smooth and creamy.  
7. Return the soup to the pot, re‑heat gently if needed, and adjust seasoning if necessary.  
8. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with chopped cilantro, and serve hot. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Spiced Carrot and Lentil Soup

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa Stuffed Portobello Mushrooms

Ingredients:
- 4 large portobello mushroom caps, stems removed and gills scraped
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon coconut oil
- 1 small red onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 cup canned black beans, drained and rinsed
- ½ cup corn kernels (fresh or frozen)
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tablespoons lime juice
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Optional garnish: sliced avocado, toasted coconut flakes, lime wedges

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper and place the mushroom caps, gill side up, on the sheet.
2. In a saucepan, combine the quinoa and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
3. While the quinoa cooks, heat the coconut oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the diced red onion and sauté for 3‑4 minutes until softened. Stir in the garlic and cook another 30 seconds.
4. Add the black beans, corn, cumin, smoked paprika, lime zest, and lime juice to the skillet. Cook, stirring, for 2‑3 minutes until heated through. Season with salt and pepper.
5. Fold the cooked quinoa into the bean‑corn mixture. Stir in the chopped cilantro and adjust seasoning if needed.
6. Spoon the quinoa filling evenly into each mushroom cap, pressing gently to pack.
7. Bake the stuffed mushrooms for 15‑18 minutes, until the caps are tender and the filling is hot.
8. Remove from the oven, garnish with sliced avocado, toasted coconut flakes, and a wedge of lime if desired. Serve warm.
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa Stuffed Portobello Mushrooms

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Chickpea and Spinach Stir‑Fry

Ingredients:
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 3 cups fresh baby spinach
- 1 medium red bell pepper, thinly sliced
- 1 small red onion, thinly sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tbsp coconut oil
- 2 tbsp coconut milk
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp ground coriander
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro, for garnish
- Cooked jasmine rice or quinoa, for serving

Instructions:
1. Heat the coconut oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat until shimmering.  
2. Add the sliced red onion and bell pepper; sauté for 3–4 minutes until they begin to soften.  
3. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.  
4. Sprinkle the cumin, smoked paprika, coriander, and cayenne (if using) over the vegetables; stir to coat.  
5. Add the cooked chickpeas, coconut milk, and lime juice to the pan; toss everything together and let the mixture simmer for 2 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.  
6. Reduce the heat to medium and fold in the fresh spinach; cook, stirring, until the spinach wilts, about 1 minute.  
7. Season with salt and black pepper to taste; remove from heat.  
8. Serve the stir‑fry over warm jasmine rice or quinoa, and garnish with chopped cilantro. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Chickpea and Spinach Stir‑Fry

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Lentil Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 large head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- ½ teaspoon saffron threads
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 medium onion, finely diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- Zest of 1 lemon
- ¼ cup toasted sliced almonds
- 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the cauliflower florets with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper, then spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender.
2. While the cauliflower roasts, place the saffron threads in a small bowl with 2 tablespoons hot water; let steep for 5 minutes.
3. In a medium saucepan, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes. Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another minute.
4. Add the rinsed lentils to the saucepan, pour in the vegetable broth, and stir in the saffron infusion (including the threads). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender but not mushy. Add more broth or water if needed.
5. Once the lentils are cooked, fold in the roasted cauliflower, lemon zest, and half of the toasted almonds. Season with salt and pepper to taste; heat through for 2‑3 minutes, stirring gently.
6. Transfer the pilaf to a serving bowl, garnish with the remaining toasted almonds and chopped parsley. Serve warm as a hearty main or side dish.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Lentil Pilaf

text:
Cinnamon‑Lime Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Salad

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and sliced into thin rounds
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 Tbsp fresh lime juice
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- Optional: 1 Tbsp maple syrup for extra sweetness

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the carrot rounds and chickpeas with olive oil, cinnamon, lime zest, lime juice, salt, pepper, and maple syrup if using.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until carrots are tender and edges are caramelized.  
4. While the vegetables roast, combine quinoa and coconut milk in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.  
5. Transfer the roasted carrots and chickpeas to a large serving bowl; add the cooked quinoa and gently toss to combine.  
6. Sprinkle chopped cilantro over the salad, give a final light toss, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Lime Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Salad

text:
Maple‑Glazed Cauliflower and Chickpea Curry

Ingredients:
- 1 medium cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp curry powder
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 Tbsp fresh ginger, minced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 2 cups fresh spinach leaves
- 1 Tbsp lime juice
- 2 Tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 Tbsp vegetable oil

Instructions:
