1. Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes.  
2. Stir in the minced garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
3. Sprinkle the curry powder, turmeric, and cumin over the aromatics, stirring constantly for 30 seconds to toast the spices.  
4. Add the cauliflower florets to the pan and toss to coat with the spice mixture. Cook for 5‑6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the cauliflower begins to soften and develop a light golden color.  
5. Pour in the coconut milk and maple syrup, stirring to combine. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.  
6. Add the chickpeas, season with salt and pepper, and continue to simmer for 10‑12 minutes, or until the cauliflower is tender and the sauce has thickened slightly.  
7. Stir in the spinach leaves and cook for 2 minutes, just until wilted.
title: Maple‑Glazed Cauliflower and Chickpea Curry

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Parsnip and Chickpea Salad

Ingredients:
- 3 large parsnips, peeled and cut into ½‑inch sticks
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 4 cups mixed salad greens
- ¼ cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped
- 2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tsp Dijon mustard
- 1 Tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil (for dressing)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.  
3. Add the parsnip sticks and chickpeas to the bowl; toss until evenly coated.  
4. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
5. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until parsnips are tender and caramelized and chickpeas are crisp.  
6. While the vegetables roast, whisk together lemon juice, Dijon mustard, and extra‑virgin olive oil; season with a pinch of salt and pepper to make the dressing.  
7. In a large serving bowl, combine mixed greens, toasted walnuts, and the warm roasted parsnips and chickpeas.  
8. Drizzle the lemon‑mustard dressing over the salad and toss gently to combine.  
9. Serve immediately, optionally garnished with an extra drizzle of maple syrup or a sprinkle of fresh herbs.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Parsnip and Chickpea Salad

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Lentil Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup dried green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- ½ teaspoon sea salt
- ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- 4 cups fresh arugula
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, cinnamon, olive oil, salt, and pepper.  
3. Add the cubed sweet potatoes to the bowl and toss until evenly coated. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast the sweet potatoes for 25‑30 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.  
5. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine the lentils and 2 cups of water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook for 20‑25 minutes, or until lentils are tender but not mushy. Drain any excess liquid and set aside to cool slightly.  
6. In a large salad bowl, place the arugula, roasted sweet potatoes, and cooked lentils. Drizzle with lemon juice and toss gently to combine.  
7. Sprinkle the toasted pumpkin seeds over the top for crunch.  
8. Serve the salad warm or at room temperature, adjusting salt and pepper to taste. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Lentil Salad

text:
Citrus‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch dice
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon orange zest
- 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/2 teaspoon sea salt
- 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the diced carrots and chickpeas with 1 tablespoon olive oil, garlic, cumin, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until carrots are tender and lightly caramelized.  
4. While the vegetables roast, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy.  
5. Remove the quinoa from heat and stir in the orange zest, lemon juice, and the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil.  
6. Gently fold the roasted carrots and chickpeas into the seasoned quinoa, mixing just enough to distribute evenly.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if desired.  
8. Transfer the pilaf to a serving bowl, garnish with chopped fresh parsley, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Citrus‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Pilaf

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea and Kale Stir‑Fry

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 cups kale, stems removed and torn into bite‑size pieces
- 1 red bell pepper, sliced
- 1 small onion, thinly sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 2 tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- ¼ tsp red‑pepper flakes (optional)
- Salt and black pepper, to taste
- Cooked brown rice or quinoa, for serving

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl whisk together soy sauce, maple syrup, lemon juice, turmeric, ginger, garlic, and red‑pepper flakes; set aside.  
2. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add onion and bell pepper; sauté 3–4 minutes until they begin to soften.  
3. Add chickpeas and cook, stirring, for 2 minutes to heat through.  
4. Pour the sauce over the vegetables and chickpeas, stirring to coat. Cook 2 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.  
5. Add kale and toss until wilted, about 2–3 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste.  
6. Remove from heat and drizzle with a little extra lemon juice, if desired.  
7. Serve the stir‑fry over warm brown rice or quinoa, optionally garnished with toasted sesame seeds.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea and Kale Stir‑Fry

text:
Saffron‑Lemon Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Asparagus

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups water
- ½ teaspoon saffron threads
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
- 2 tablespoons olive oil, divided
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 pound asparagus, trimmed and cut into 2‑inch pieces
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, combine the chickpeas, 1 tablespoon olive oil, minced garlic, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until golden and crisp.  
3. Toss the asparagus with the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Add to the same baking sheet (or a second sheet) and roast for 12‑15 minutes, until tender‑crisp.  
4. While the vegetables roast, place the saffron threads in a small cup with 2 tablespoons hot water; let steep 5 minutes.  
5. In a medium saucepan, bring the 1 ¾ cups water to a boil. Stir in the rinsed quinoa, the saffron infusion (including the water), and a pinch of salt. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the quinoa is fluffy and the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes.  
6. Fluff the quinoa with a fork and stir in the lemon zest and lemon juice. Adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed.  
7. To serve, divide the saffron‑lemon quinoa among bowls, top with roasted chickpeas and asparagus, and sprinkle with chopped parsley if desired. Enjoy warm or at room temperature.
title: Saffron‑Lemon Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Asparagus

text:
Coconut‑Lime Braised Chickpea & Sweet Potato Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (14 oz) coconut milk
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tbsp coconut oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground turmeric
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Lime wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Heat the coconut oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger, sautéing until fragrant, about 1 minute.  
2. Stir in the cumin, smoked paprika, and turmeric; cook for another 30 seconds to toast the spices.  
3. Add the cubed sweet potatoes and chickpeas, tossing to coat them evenly with the spice mixture.  
4. Pour in the coconut milk and vegetable broth, bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the sweet potatoes are tender.  
5. Stir in the lime juice, season with salt and pepper to taste, and let the stew simmer uncovered for 5 minutes to thicken slightly.  
6. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro and a lime wedge on the side. Serve hot with crusty bread or steamed rice, if desired.
title: Coconut‑Lime Braised Chickpea & Sweet Potato Stew

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea and Kale Soup

Ingredients:
- 2 cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 4 cups chopped kale, stems removed
- 1 large carrot, diced
- 1 medium onion, finely chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- ½ teaspoon sea salt (or to taste)
- ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- Optional garnish: chopped fresh cilantro or parsley

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté for 4–5 minutes, until softened and translucent.  
2. Stir in the garlic, ginger, and turmeric; cook for 1 minute, allowing the aromatics to release their flavors.  
3. Add the diced carrot and cook for another 2 minutes, stirring occasionally.  
4. Pour in the vegetable broth and bring the mixture to a gentle boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes, or until the carrots are tender.  
5. Add the cooked chickpeas and chopped kale to the pot. Simmer for 5 minutes, until the kale wilts and the chickpeas are heated through.  
6. Season with salt, pepper, and lemon juice. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.  
7. Ladle the soup into bowls and garnish with fresh cilantro or parsley, if desired. Serve hot.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea and Kale Soup

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Chickpea Salad

Ingredients:
- 3 medium beets, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 4 cups arugula
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese
- ¼ cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, salt, and pepper.  
3. Add the cubed beets and chickpeas to the bowl, toss to coat evenly, and spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the beets are tender and caramelized and the chickpeas are crisp.  
5. While the vegetables roast, place arugula in a large serving bowl and drizzle with lemon juice; toss gently.  
6. Once roasted, let the beets and chickpeas cool slightly, then add them to the arugula.  
7. Sprinkle crumbled feta and toasted walnuts over the top.  
8. Toss the salad lightly to combine all ingredients, taste, and adjust seasoning with additional salt or lemon juice if desired.  
9. Serve warm or at room temperature as a hearty main or side dish.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Chickpea Salad

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Acorn Squash with Quinoa and Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 1 medium acorn squash, halved and seeded
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 Tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- Optional: 1 Tbsp lemon juice for a bright finish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, cinnamon, olive oil, salt, and pepper.  
3. Brush the mixture evenly over the cut sides of the acorn squash halves. Place them cut‑side down on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast for 35‑40 minutes, or until the flesh is fork‑tender and caramelized.  
5. While the squash roasts, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
6. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large bowl. Stir in the optional lemon juice, a pinch of salt, and half of the toasted pumpkin seeds.  
7. When the squash is done, flip the halves cut‑side up. Spoon a generous portion of the quinoa mixture into each cavity.  
8. Garnish each stuffed squash with pomegranate seeds, the remaining toasted pumpkin seeds, and chopped parsley. Serve warm.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Acorn Squash with Quinoa and Pomegranate

text:
Spiced Orange‑Maple Quinoa Stuffed Acorn Squash

Ingredients:
- 2 medium acorn squash, halved and seeded
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- Zest of 1 orange
- 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup
- ¼ cup dried cranberries
- 2 cups kale, stems removed and chopped
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Place the acorn squash halves cut‑side up on a baking sheet, brush with a little olive oil, and season with salt and pepper. Roast for 30‑35 minutes, until the flesh is tender and lightly caramelized.
2. While the squash roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
3. In a large skillet, heat 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add the cumin and smoked paprika, stirring for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the chickpeas and cook for 3‑4 minutes, allowing them to brown slightly.
4. Add the chopped kale to the skillet and sauté until wilted, about 2 minutes. Stir in the cooked quinoa, orange zest, maple syrup, and dried cranberries. Season with salt and pepper to taste, mixing until everything is evenly coated.
5. Remove the roasted acorn squash from the oven. Spoon the quinoa‑chickpea mixture into each squash cavity, packing it gently.
6. Return the stuffed squash to the oven and bake for an additional 10 minutes to meld flavors.
7. Remove from the oven, sprinkle each half with toasted pumpkin seeds, and serve warm. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Orange‑Maple Quinoa Stuffed Acorn Squash

text:
Saffron‑Infused Coconut Lentil Soup

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 medium onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, grated
- 1/2 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 pinch saffron threads
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk (full‑fat)
- 2 cups fresh spinach leaves
- 1 tablespoon lime juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, soak the saffron threads in 2 tablespoons of hot water for 5 minutes.
2. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes.
3. Stir in the garlic, ginger, turmeric, and cumin; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Add the rinsed red lentils, vegetable broth, and the saffron infusion (including the liquid). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer.
5. Cover and simmer for 15‑20 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and beginning to break down.
6. Stir in the coconut milk and continue to simmer uncovered for another 5 minutes, allowing the soup to thicken slightly.
7. Add the spinach leaves and cook for 2 minutes, just until wilted.
8. Remove the pot from heat; stir in the lime juice and season with salt and pepper to taste.
9. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve hot.
title: Saffron‑Infused Coconut Lentil Soup

text:
Saffron‑Infused Chickpea & Sweet Potato Tagine

Ingredients:
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 large onion, finely chopped
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 red bell pepper, sliced
- 1 tbsp tomato paste
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- ½ cup canned diced tomatoes
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp ground coriander
- ¼ tsp ground cinnamon
- ¼ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp saffron threads, steeped in 2 tbsp hot water
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Toasted slivered almonds, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy‑bottomed pot over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.  
2. Stir in the garlic and red bell pepper; cook for another 2 minutes until fragrant.  
3. Add the tomato paste, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, and smoked paprika. Cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute to toast the spices.  
4. Pour in the saffron‑infused water, vegetable broth, and diced tomatoes. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil.  
5. Add the cubed sweet potatoes and chickpeas. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the sweet potatoes are tender.  
6. Season the tagine with salt and pepper to taste. If the sauce is too thick, stir in a little more broth or water.  
7. Transfer the stew to serving bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves and toasted slivered almonds, and serve hot with couscous or crusty bread.
title: Saffron‑Infused Chickpea & Sweet Potato Tagine

text:
Saffron‑Honey Roasted Beet and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 3 medium beets, peeled and cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 Tbsp honey
- ¼ tsp saffron threads
- 1 Tbsp warm water (for saffron)
- ¼ cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- 2 Tbsp fresh mint leaves, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, combine the saffron threads with 1 Tbsp warm water; let steep for 5 minutes.  
3. Toss the beet cubes with olive oil, honey, the saffron infusion (including the threads), salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast the beets for 25‑30 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until tender and caramelized.  
5. While the beets roast, bring the quinoa and water (or broth) to a boil in a saucepan. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.  
6. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl. Add the roasted beets, toasted walnuts, mint, and lemon juice. Toss gently to combine.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a drizzle of honey if desired.  
8. Serve the salad warm or at room temperature, topped with crumbled feta if using. Enjoy!
title: Saffron‑Honey Roasted Beet and Quinoa Salad

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Parsnip and Lentil Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 large parsnips, peeled and cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 cup dried green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 2 Tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice
- 2 Tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Add the cubed parsnips and toss to coat evenly.  
3. Spread the seasoned parsnips in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.  
4. While the parsnips roast, place the rinsed lentils in a saucepan with 3 cups water. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook for 20‑25 minutes, or until lentils are tender but still hold their shape. Drain any excess liquid.  
5. In a large mixing bowl, combine the roasted parsnips, cooked lentils, chopped parsley, lemon juice, and toasted pumpkin seeds. Toss gently to distribute.  
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a drizzle of maple syrup if desired.  
7. Serve warm or at room temperature as a hearty salad or side dish. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Parsnip and Lentil Salad

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Chickpea and Kale Soup

Ingredients:
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 4 cups chopped kale, stems removed
- 1 large onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp red‑pepper flakes (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.  
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
3. Sprinkle the cumin and red‑pepper flakes (if using) over the aromatics, stirring to combine.  
4. Add the chickpeas and vegetable broth; bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.  
5. Stir in the chopped kale and continue to simmer for another 5‑7 minutes, until the kale is wilted but still bright green.  
6. Remove the pot from heat and stir in the fresh lemon juice. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.  
7. Ladle the soup into bowls and serve hot, optionally garnished with a drizzle of olive oil or a sprinkle of lemon zest.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Chickpea and Kale Soup

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Turnip and Lentil Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 large turnips, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup dried green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 3 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- ½ tsp sea salt, plus more to taste
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- ¼ cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped
- ¼ cup dried cranberries
- 2 Tbsp fresh parsley, finely chopped
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cubed turnip with 2 Tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the turnip mixture in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until golden and tender.  
4. While the turnip roasts, combine lentils and 3 cups water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook 20‑25 minutes, or until lentils are just tender but still hold their shape. Drain any excess water and set aside.  
5. In a small skillet over medium heat, toast the walnuts for 2‑3 minutes, shaking the pan frequently, until fragrant. Remove from heat.  
6. In a large mixing bowl, combine the roasted turnip, cooked lentils, toasted walnuts, dried cranberries, and fresh parsley. Drizzle with the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil and lemon juice, then toss gently to blend.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a drizzle of maple syrup if desired.  
8. Serve the salad warm or at room temperature, garnished with extra parsley if desired. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Turnip and Lentil Salad

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Shrimp with Coconut Lime Rice

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup jasmine rice
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup water
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp grated ginger
- 1 tbsp lime zest
- 2 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp honey
- Salt and pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Rinse the jasmine rice under cold water until the water runs clear.  
2. In a saucepan combine rice, coconut milk, water, lime zest, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until tender; fluff with a fork and set aside.  
3. In a small bowl whisk together lemon juice, ginger, lime juice, honey, and a pinch of salt to make the glaze.  
4. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add minced garlic and sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.  
5. Add the shrimp, season with salt and pepper, and cook 2‑3 minutes per side until pink and opaque.  
6. Pour the lemon‑ginger‑lime glaze over the shrimp, stirring to coat. Cook an additional minute until the sauce thickens slightly.  
7. Serve the glazed shrimp over the coconut lime rice, garnish with fresh cilantro, and enjoy immediately.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Shrimp with Coconut Lime Rice

text:
Spiced Orange‑Maple Glazed Tempeh with Quinoa and Roasted Broccoli

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- ¼ cup fresh orange juice
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp ground ginger
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 large head broccoli, cut into florets
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional garnish: chopped fresh cilantro or toasted sesame seeds

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a shallow bowl, whisk together orange juice, maple syrup, smoked paprika, cumin, ginger, a pinch of salt, and black pepper.  
3. Place the tempeh strips in the bowl, turning to coat evenly. Let marinate while you prepare the vegetables, about 5 minutes.  
4. Meanwhile, toss the broccoli florets with 1 Tbsp olive oil, minced garlic, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
5. Roast the broccoli for 12‑15 minutes, until tender‑crisp and lightly browned, stirring once halfway through.  
6. While the broccoli roasts, heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat and add the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil. Remove tempeh from the marinade (reserve the excess liquid) and sear the strips for 3‑4 minutes per side, until golden and caramelized.  
7. Reduce the heat to medium, pour the reserved marinade over the tempeh, and cook for an additional 2 minutes, allowing the glaze to thicken and coat the pieces. Remove from heat.  
8. In a medium saucepan, combine rinsed quinoa and water (or broth). Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Fluff with a fork and season with a pinch of salt.  
9. To serve, divide quinoa among plates, top with roasted broccoli and the orange‑maple glazed tempeh. Garnish with cilantro or toasted sesame seeds, if desired. Enjoy warm!
title: Spiced Orange‑Maple Glazed Tempeh with Quinoa and Roasted Broccoli

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Lentil Soup

Ingredients:
- 2 medium beets, peeled and diced
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 carrot, diced
- 1 celery stalk, diced
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh thyme leaves for garnish (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Toss the diced beets with 1 Tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast 25‑30 minutes, until tender and caramelized.  
2. While the beets roast, heat the remaining olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion, carrot, and celery; sauté 5‑7 minutes until softened.  
3. Stir in garlic and cumin; cook 1 minute until fragrant.  
4. Add the rinsed lentils and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer 15 minutes.  
5. Add the roasted beets (with any pan juices) to the pot. Simmer another 10‑12 minutes, until the lentils are tender.  
6. Using an immersion blender, blend the soup until smooth but still slightly chunky, or blend half and return to the pot for texture.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a drizzle of maple syrup if desired. Serve hot, garnished with fresh thyme leaves.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Lentil Soup

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Chickpea and Sweet Potato Tacos

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 ½ tbsp coconut oil, divided
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground coriander
- ½ tsp cayenne pepper (adjust to taste)
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tbsp lime juice
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 8 small corn tortillas
- ½ cup diced red cabbage
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- Lime wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the diced sweet potatoes with 1 tbsp coconut oil, cumin, smoked paprika, coriander, cayenne, and a pinch of salt. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until tender and caramelized.  
3. While the sweet potatoes roast, heat the remaining ½ tbsp coconut oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the chickpeas and sauté for 5‑6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they begin to crisp.  
4. Stir the lime zest, lime juice, and chopped cilantro into the chickpeas; cook another minute to combine flavors. Remove from heat.  
5. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet or directly over a low flame, about 30 seconds per side, until pliable.  
6. Assemble each taco: place a spoonful of roasted sweet potatoes, top with spiced chickpeas, then add red cabbage, feta (if using), and a drizzle of extra lime juice.  
7. Serve immediately with lime wedges on the side for extra brightness. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Chickpea and Sweet Potato Tacos

text:
Maple‑Glazed Seared Scallops with Citrus Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 12 sea scallops, patted dry
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp lime zest
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 small red bell pepper, diced
- 1 Tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Lime wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, grated ginger, and lime zest. Set aside.
2. Bring the water to a boil in a saucepan, add the quinoa, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the grains are tender and the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and keep warm.
3. While the quinoa cooks, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the minced garlic and diced red bell pepper; sauté for 2‑3 minutes until fragrant and slightly softened.
4. Pat the scallops dry, season lightly with salt and pepper, and place them in the hot skillet. Sear without moving for about 2 minutes per side, until a golden crust forms and the centers are opaque.
5. During the last minute of cooking, pour the maple‑soy glaze over the scallops. Spoon the glaze around the pan and let it reduce, coating the scallops glossy and caramelized.
6. Remove the scallops from the skillet and set aside on a warm plate. Toss the cooked quinoa with the sautéed garlic‑pepper mixture, cilantro, and a squeeze of fresh lime juice; season with salt and pepper to taste.
7. Plate a serving of citrus quinoa, top with three seared scallops, and drizzle any remaining glaze from the pan over the top. Garnish with extra cilantro and lime wedges. Serve immediately.
title: Maple‑Glazed Seared Scallops with Citrus Quinoa

text:
Spiced Orange‑Maple Glazed Seitan with Coconut Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 8 oz seitan, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- ¼ cup fresh orange juice
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp low‑sodium soy sauce
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 Tbsp olive oil (for seitan)

Instructions:
1. In a shallow bowl, whisk together orange juice, maple syrup, soy sauce, garlic, ginger, cumin, smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Add the seitan strips, toss to coat, and let marinate while you prepare the quinoa (about 10 minutes).
2. Meanwhile, combine quinoa, coconut milk, water, and lime zest in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and fluff with a fork; stir in cilantro and season with additional salt if needed.
3. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Remove seitan from the marinade (reserve the liquid) and sear the strips for 3‑4 minutes per side, until golden and slightly crisp.
4. Pour the reserved marinade into the skillet with the seitan. Reduce heat to medium and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and coats the seitan, about 3 minutes.
5. Serve the orange‑maple glazed seitan over a bed of coconut quinoa. Garnish with extra cilantro, a squeeze of lime juice, and a drizzle of any remaining glaze if desired. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Orange‑Maple Glazed Seitan with Coconut Quinoa

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Shrimp and Mango Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- 1 ripe mango, diced
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, minced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- Zest and juice of 1 lime
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon chili flakes (adjust to taste)
- 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, chopped
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine the quinoa and coconut milk; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is tender. Fluff with a fork and set aside to cool slightly.  
2. While the quinoa cooks, whisk together lime zest, lime juice, ginger, garlic, cumin, chili flakes, olive oil, salt, and pepper in a large bowl to create the dressing.  
3. Add the raw shrimp to the bowl with the dressing, tossing to coat evenly. Let marinate for 5 minutes while the quinoa finishes cooking.  
4. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the shrimp and cook for 2‑3 minutes per side, or until pink and opaque. Remove from heat and let cool for a minute.  
5. In the large bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, cooked shrimp, diced mango, and chopped cilantro. Drizzle any remaining dressing over the mixture and toss gently to combine.  
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired. Serve the salad warm, at room temperature, or chilled, garnished with extra cilantro or a sprinkle of chili flakes.
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Shrimp and Mango Quinoa Salad

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Garlic Brussels Sprouts and Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 block (14 oz) extra‑firm tofu, pressed and cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce (or tamari for gluten‑free)
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp garlic powder
- 1 lb Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth or water
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional garnish: toasted sesame seeds and chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, smoked paprika, and garlic powder. Add the tofu cubes, toss to coat, and let marinate while you prepare the vegetables.  
3. On the same baking sheet, spread the halved Brussels sprouts. Drizzle with olive oil, sprinkle the minced garlic, season with salt and pepper, and toss to combine.  
4. Roast the Brussels sprouts for 12 minutes, then remove the sheet from the oven, give the sprouts a quick stir, and add the marinated tofu cubes to the pan. Return to the oven and roast for an additional 15‑18 minutes, turning the tofu once, until the sprouts are caramelized and the tofu is golden and slightly crisp.  
5. While the vegetables roast, combine the rinsed quinoa and vegetable broth (or water) in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the quinoa is fluffy and the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.  
6. Taste the quinoa and season with a pinch of salt and pepper if needed.  
7. To serve, divide the quinoa among plates, top with the roasted garlic Brussels sprouts and maple‑glazed tofu. Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds and fresh parsley, if desired. Enjoy warm!
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Garlic Brussels Sprouts and Quinoa

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch sticks  
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed  
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup  
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon  
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided  
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed  
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth  
- 1 avocado, sliced  
- 2 cups fresh baby spinach  
- 2 Tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds  
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice  
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste  

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the carrot sticks and chickpeas with 1 Tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until carrots are tender and chickpeas are crisp‑golden.  
4. While the vegetables roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, lemon juice, a pinch of salt, and a dash of pepper to make a simple dressing.  
6. To assemble each
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

text:
Maple‑Glazed Carrot and Lentil Tacos

Ingredients:
- 8 small corn tortillas
- 1 cup dried brown or green lentils, rinsed
- 2 large carrots, peeled and grated
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1/4 teaspoon ground coriander
- 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper (optional)
- 1/2 cup red cabbage, thinly sliced
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 avocado, sliced
- 1 lime, cut into wedges
- Salt and black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan, combine the lentils with 2 cups water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer, uncovered, for 20‑25 minutes or until tender. Drain any excess water and set aside.
2. While the lentils cook, heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the grated carrots and sauté for 3‑4 minutes until they begin to soften.
3. Stir in the cooked lentils, maple syrup, cumin, smoked paprika, coriander, cayenne (if using), salt, and pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, for another 5‑6 minutes until the mixture is glossy and the flavors meld. Remove from heat.
4. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet or directly over a gas flame for about 30 seconds per side, keeping them pliable.
5. To assemble each taco, place a generous spoonful of the maple‑glazed carrot‑lentil mixture onto a tortilla. Top with sliced red cabbage, avocado, and a sprinkle of fresh cilantro.
6. Serve the tacos with lime wedges on the side for squeezing over the top. Enjoy warm!
title: Maple‑Glazed Carrot and Lentil Tacos

text:
Roasted Garlic & Herb Farro with Sautéed Spinach and Sun‑Dried Tomatoes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup farro, rinsed
- 2 ½ cups low‑sodium vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- 1 tsp dried rosemary
- ½ tsp dried oregano
- 4 cups fresh spinach, roughly chopped
- ½ cup sun‑dried tomatoes, thinly sliced (oil‑packed, drained)
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- Zest of 1 lemon

Instructions:
1. Heat 1 tbsp of olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat, add the rinsed farro, and toast for 2‑3 minutes until lightly golden.  
2. Pour in the vegetable broth, bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 20‑25 minutes, or until the farro is tender and the liquid is absorbed.  
3. While the farro cooks, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat and add the minced garlic; sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.  
4. Stir in the dried thyme, rosemary, and oregano, cooking for another 30 seconds to release their aromas.  
5. Add the chopped spinach to the skillet, tossing until wilted, about 2‑3 minutes.  
6. Mix in the sun‑dried tomatoes and season with salt and pepper, stirring for another minute to combine flavors.  
7. Fluff the cooked farro with a fork and transfer it to the skillet, mixing it thoroughly with the spinach‑tomato mixture.  
8. Remove from heat, sprinkle the lemon zest over the top, give a final gentle toss, and serve warm.
title: Roasted Garlic & Herb Farro with Sautéed Spinach and Sun‑Dried Tomatoes

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa & Roasted Brussels Sprout Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups coconut milk
- 1 tablespoon lime zest
- 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon sea salt
- 1 tablespoon maple syrup
- 2 cups Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- ½ teaspoon garlic powder
- ¼ teaspoon black pepper
- 1 cup canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 green onions, thinly sliced
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Optional: sliced avocado for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the Brussels sprouts with olive oil, garlic powder, black pepper, and a pinch of salt. Spread them cut‑side down on the sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until caramelized and tender.  
3. While the sprouts roast, combine quinoa and coconut milk in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy.  
4. Remove the quinoa from heat and stir in lime zest, lime juice, cumin, smoked paprika, maple syrup, and sea salt. Fluff with a fork.  
5. In the last 5 minutes of roasting, add the chickpeas to the baking sheet to warm through and develop a slight crisp.  
6. To assemble the bowl, place a generous scoop of lime‑infused quinoa in the bottom of each serving bowl. Top with roasted Brussels sprouts, warm chickpeas, toasted pumpkin seeds, and sliced green onions.  
7. Garnish with fresh cilantro leaves and, if desired, avocado slices. Serve immediately, drizzling any extra lime juice over the top.
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa & Roasted Brussels Sprout Bowl

text:
Spiced Cardamom Lentil and Roasted Tomato Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 2 cups cherry tomatoes, halved
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp ground cardamom
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the halved cherry tomatoes with 1 tablespoon olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 15‑20 minutes, until blistered and slightly caramelized.
2. While the tomatoes roast, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 4‑5 minutes, until translucent.
3. Stir in the minced garlic, ground cardamom, cumin, and smoked paprika; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Add the rinsed red lentils to the pot, stirring to coat them with the spices.
5. Pour in the vegetable broth, bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer. Cover and cook for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
6. Once the lentils are tender, fold in the roasted tomatoes and simmer for an additional 5 minutes to meld flavors.
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
8. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with chopped fresh cilantro, and serve hot. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Cardamom Lentil and Roasted Tomato Stew

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa & Roasted Eggplant Stack

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups coconut milk
- 1 tablespoon lime zest
- 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice
- 1 tablespoon maple syrup
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1 medium eggplant, sliced into ½‑inch rounds
- 2 tablespoons coconut oil, divided
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)
- Optional: ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together 1 tablespoon coconut oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Brush both sides of the eggplant slices with the mixture and place on the prepared sheet.  
3. Roast the eggplant for 20‑25 minutes, flipping halfway through, until golden and tender.  
4. While the eggplant roasts, combine quinoa and coconut milk in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and quinoa is fluffy.  
5. Remove the quinoa from heat and stir in lime zest, lime juice, maple syrup, and a pinch of salt. Fluff with a fork.  
6. To assemble, spoon a generous mound of the spiced coconut lime quinoa onto a plate, top with two roasted eggplant rounds, and repeat to create a stack.  
7. Garnish each stack with chopped cilantro and toasted pumpkin seeds, if using. Serve warm.
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa & Roasted Eggplant Stack

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea & Spinach Curry

Ingredients:
- 2 cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 4 cups fresh baby spinach, washed
- 1 ½ cups full‑fat coconut milk
- 1 large onion, finely diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch piece fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tbsp ground turmeric
- 1 tbsp lemon zest
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp red‑pepper flakes (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4‑5 minutes.  
2. Stir in the minced garlic, grated ginger, and red‑pepper flakes; cook for another 30 seconds until fragrant.  
3. Sprinkle the ground turmeric over the aromatics and stir to coat, letting the spices toast lightly for 1 minute.  
4. Pour in the coconut milk, lemon zest, and lemon juice. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, stirring occasionally.  
5. Add the cooked chickpeas to the pan, season with salt and pepper, and let the curry simmer for 8‑10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken slightly.  
6. Fold in the fresh spinach, stirring until it wilts completely, about 2‑3 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if desired.  
7. Remove the skillet from heat. Serve the curry over steamed basmati rice, quinoa, or cauliflower rice. Garnish generously with chopped cilantro.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea & Spinach Curry

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Sweet Corn and Avocado Salsa

Ingredients:
- 1 block (14 oz) extra‑firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 Tbsp olive oil (for tofu)
- 2 ears sweet corn, husked and kernels removed
- 1 Tbsp butter, melted
- 1 tsp chili powder
- 1 avocado, diced
- ½ red onion, finely chopped
- 1 small jalapeño, seeded and minced
- juice of 1 lime
- 2 Tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, whisk together maple syrup, soy sauce, smoked paprika, and cumin. Add the tofu cubes, toss to coat, and let marinate while you prepare the corn (about 5 minutes).  
3. Spread the corn kernels on the prepared sheet, drizzle with melted butter, sprinkle with chili powder, salt, and pepper. Roast for 12‑15 minutes, stirring halfway, until lightly charred.  
4. Meanwhile, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated tofu and sear, turning occasionally, until all sides are golden and caramelized, about 8‑10 minutes. Remove from heat.  
5. In a small bowl, combine diced avocado, red onion, jalapeño, lime juice, cilantro, and a pinch of salt. Gently toss to form the salsa.  
6. To serve, arrange a bed of roasted corn on a plate, top with the maple‑glazed tofu, and spoon the avocado salsa over the top. Finish with an extra drizzle of lime juice and a sprinkle of fresh cilantro if desired. Enjoy warm or at room temperature.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Sweet Corn and Avocado Salsa

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Sweet Potato and Kale Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 block (14 oz) extra‑firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp garlic powder
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 4 cups kale leaves, stems removed and torn
- 1 small red onion, thinly sliced
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp apple cider vinegar
- 1 Tbsp Dijon mustard

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, cumin, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.  
3. While the sweet potatoes roast, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil in a shallow dish. Add the tofu cubes, toss to coat, and let marinate for 5 minutes.  
4. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated tofu and cook, turning occasionally, until all sides are caramelized and crisp, about 8‑10 minutes. Remove from heat.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk the apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of olive oil to create a quick vinaigrette.  
6. Place the kale and red onion in a large salad bowl. Drizzle with the vinaigrette and massage the kale for 1‑2 minutes until it softens and darkens.  
7. Add the roasted sweet potatoes, caramelized tofu, and toasted pumpkin seeds to the kale mixture. Toss gently to combine.  
8. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a splash of maple syrup if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Sweet Potato and Kale Salad

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Roasted Cauliflower with Herbed Couscous

Ingredients:
- 1 large head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 3 Tbsp olive oil
- 2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 Tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 1 cup couscous
- 1 ¼ cup vegetable broth (or water)
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh mint
- Zest of 1 lemon

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, grated ginger, turmeric, minced garlic, salt, and pepper.  
3. Toss the cauliflower florets in the spiced mixture until evenly coated. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway through, until the cauliflower is golden‑brown and tender.  
5. While the cauliflower roasts, bring the vegetable broth to a boil in a medium saucepan. Stir in the couscous, cover, and remove from heat. Let sit for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.  
6. Stir the chopped parsley, mint, and lemon zest into the fluffed couscous. Adjust seasoning with a pinch of salt if needed.  
7. To serve, divide the herbed couscous among plates, top with the roasted cauliflower, and drizzle any pan‑drippings over the top. Garnish with an extra sprinkle of fresh herbs or lemon zest if desired. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Roasted Cauliflower with Herbed Couscous

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa and Roasted Brussels Sprout Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup water
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tsp lime zest
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp chili flakes
- 2 tbsp coconut oil, melted
- 1 lb Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the halved Brussels sprouts with olive oil, salt, pepper, maple syrup, and chili flakes until evenly coated. Spread them cut‑side down on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until caramelized and tender.  
3. While the sprouts roast, combine quinoa, coconut milk, and water in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes.  
4. Fluff the cooked quinoa with a fork and stir in the melted coconut oil, lime juice, lime zest, and a pinch of salt. Adjust seasoning to taste.  
5. Transfer the quinoa to a large serving bowl, add the roasted Brussels sprouts, and gently toss to combine.  
6. Sprinkle chopped cilantro over the top, if using, and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa and Roasted Brussels Sprout Salad

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu and Roasted Brussels Sprout Quinoa Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 block (14 oz) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp garlic powder
- 1 lb Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- ¼ cup toasted sliced almonds
- 2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional garnish: chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, smoked paprika, and garlic powder. Toss the tofu cubes in the glaze until fully coated, then spread them on half of the prepared baking sheet.  
3. On the other half of the sheet, toss the Brussels sprouts with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast the tofu and Brussels sprouts for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway through, until the tofu is caramelized and the sprouts are crisp‑tender and lightly browned.  
4. While the tofu and sprouts roast, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the quinoa is fluffy and the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together the lemon juice, a drizzle of olive oil, and a pinch of salt and pepper to make a quick dressing.  
6. Assemble the bowls: start with a base of quinoa, top with roasted Brussels sprouts and maple‑glazed tofu, drizzle the lemon dressing over everything, and sprinkle toasted almonds and fresh parsley (if using) on top. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu and Roasted Brussels Sprout Quinoa Bowl

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Sweet Potato and Kale Stir‑Fry

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp rice vinegar
- 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 3 cups kale leaves, stems removed and torn
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds, for garnish
- 2 green onions, sliced, for garnish
- Cooked brown rice or quinoa, for serving (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, whisk together maple syrup, soy sauce, rice vinegar, and toasted sesame oil in a shallow bowl. Add the tofu cubes and gently toss to coat; let marinate for 5 minutes.
3. Heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated tofu (reserve any excess sauce) and sear for 2‑3 minutes per side, until caramelized. Transfer tofu to a plate.
4. In the same skillet, add the minced garlic and grated ginger; sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the kale and stir‑fry for 2‑3 minutes, until wilted but still bright green.
5. Return the tofu to the skillet, pour in any reserved glaze, and toss everything together. Cook for another 1‑2 minutes, allowing the glaze to thicken and coat the vegetables.
6. Remove from heat and stir in the roasted sweet potato cubes, gently mixing to combine.
7. Serve the maple‑glazed tofu stir‑fry over cooked brown rice or quinoa, if desired. Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds and sliced green onions for garnish. Enjoy while hot!
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Sweet Potato and Kale Stir‑Fry

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Edamame

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 cup frozen edamame, thawed
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1 tablespoon lemon juice
- 1 tablespoon soy sauce or tamari
- 1/4 teaspoon sea salt
- 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
- 2 green onions, sliced (optional)
- 1 tablespoon toasted sesame seeds (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the edamame with ½ tablespoon olive oil, minced garlic, and a pinch of salt; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 12‑15 minutes, stirring once, until lightly browned.
2. While the edamame roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes.
3. Fluff the quinoa with a fork and stir in the grated ginger, ground turmeric, lemon juice, soy sauce, and the remaining ½ tablespoon olive oil. Season with sea salt and black pepper to taste.
4. Fold the roasted garlic edamame into the quinoa mixture until evenly distributed.
5. Transfer to a serving bowl, garnish with sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds if desired, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Edamame

text:
Spiced Orange‑Maple Quinoa Stuffed Bell Peppers

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 4 large red or orange bell peppers, tops cut off and seeds removed
- 1 medium sweet potato, peeled and diced
- 1 cup canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp orange zest
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground coriander
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 lime, cut into wedges (for serving)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Place the diced sweet potato on a baking sheet, drizzle with 1 tablespoon olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.
2. While the sweet potato roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
3. In a large bowl, mix the cooked quinoa, roasted sweet potato, chickpeas, maple syrup, orange zest, cumin, smoked paprika, coriander, cayenne (if using), and the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Stir in half of the chopped cilantro.
4. Spoon the quinoa mixture evenly into the hollowed bell peppers, packing gently. Place the stuffed peppers upright in a baking dish. If any liquid accumulates, drizzle a little extra broth or water into the dish to keep them moist.
5. Cover the dish with foil and bake for 20 minutes. Remove the foil and bake an additional 10‑12 minutes, until the peppers are tender and the filling is heated through.
6. Remove from the oven, garnish each pepper with the remaining cilantro, and serve with lime wedges on the side for a bright finish. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Orange‑Maple Quinoa Stuffed Bell Peppers

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Lentil Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and sliced into ¼‑inch rounds
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- ½ cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped
- 1 Tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, olive oil, cinnamon, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Add the carrot rounds and toss to coat evenly. Spread the carrots in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until caramelized and tender.  
3. While the carrots roast, combine lentils and 3 cups water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 20‑25 minutes until lentils are tender but not mushy. Drain any excess liquid and set aside.  
4. In a separate pot, bring 1 cup water to a boil, add quinoa, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the grains are fluffy and the water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
5. Assemble the Buddha bowls: divide the cooked quinoa among four bowls, top each with a scoop of lentils, then arrange the roasted carrots over the lentils. Sprinkle chopped cilantro and toasted pumpkin seeds, if using, over each bowl.  
6. Serve warm or at room temperature, drizzling any remaining maple‑cinnamon glaze from the pan over the bowls for extra flavor. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Lentil Buddha Bowl

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Shrimp and Avocado Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 12 oz large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 ripe avocado, diced
- 1 lemon (zest and juice)
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, minced
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 2 tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa and water; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and set aside to cool slightly.
2. While the quinoa cooks, whisk together olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, minced ginger, turmeric, salt, and pepper in a large bowl to create the dressing.
3. Pat the shrimp dry with paper towels. Add them to the bowl with the dressing, tossing to coat evenly. Let marinate for 5 minutes.
4. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the shrimp and sauté 2‑3 minutes per side, or until pink and opaque. Transfer the cooked shrimp to a plate and set aside.
5. In the same bowl used for the dressing, combine the cooked quinoa, diced avocado, and chopped cilantro. Drizzle any remaining dressing over the mixture and toss gently to combine.
6. Top the quinoa salad with the sautéed shrimp. Adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if desired.
7. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with extra cilantro or lemon wedges if desired. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Shrimp and Avocado Quinoa Salad

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Corn and Black Bean Salad

Ingredients:
- 3 cups fresh or frozen sweet corn kernels
- 1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- ½ red onion, thinly sliced
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- ½ tsp ground cinnamon
- Juice of 1 lime
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional: 1 avocado, cubed, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the corn kernels with 1 Tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, and a pinch of salt and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the corn in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 15‑20 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until the kernels are caramelized and lightly browned.  
4. While the corn roasts, combine the black beans, diced red bell pepper, and sliced red onion in a medium bowl.  
5. In a small jar, whisk together the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, lime juice, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of black pepper to make the dressing.  
6. When the corn is done, let it cool for 5 minutes, then add it to the bean‑vegetable mixture.  
7. Pour the lime‑olive oil dressing over the salad, add the chopped cilantro, and toss gently to combine.  
8. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice if needed.  
9. Serve the salad warm or at room temperature, topped with cubed avocado if desired. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Corn and Black Bean Salad

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Acorn Squash and Chickpea Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 medium acorn squash, halved and seeded
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- 2 Tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, cinnamon, smoked paprika, olive oil, salt, and pepper.  
3. Brush the cut sides of the acorn squash halves with the maple‑cinnamon mixture, then place them cut‑side down on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast the squash for 25‑30 minutes, until tender and caramelized.  
5. While the squash roasts, spread the chickpeas on a separate part of the baking sheet, drizzle with any remaining maple‑cinnamon mixture, and toss to coat. Roast for the last 15 minutes of the squash’s cooking time, stirring once, until the chickpeas are crisp.  
6. Remove both squash and chickpeas from the oven; let the squash cool slightly, then scoop the flesh into a large bowl, breaking it up with a fork.  
7. Add the roasted chickpeas, toasted pumpkin seeds, feta (if using), parsley, and lemon juice to the bowl. Toss gently to combine.  
8. Adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a drizzle of maple syrup if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Acorn Squash and Chickpea Salad

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Bowl

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/2‑inch sticks
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp sea salt
- ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 1 Tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 2 cups cooked quinoa
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- Optional: ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the carrot sticks and chickpeas with olive oil, turmeric, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until carrots are tender and lightly caramelized and chickpeas are crisp.  
4. While the vegetables roast, whisk together lemon juice, lemon zest, and grated ginger in a small bowl; set aside.  
5. Divide the cooked quinoa among four serving bowls. Top each with the roasted carrots and chickpeas.  
6. Drizzle the lemon‑ginger dressing over the bowls, then sprinkle with toasted pumpkin seeds, chopped parsley, and optional feta cheese.  
7. Serve warm or at room temperature, enjoying the bright, aromatic flavors.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Bowl

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Chickpeas and Kale

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp ground ginger
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tbsp lemon zest
- 2 cups kale, stems removed and torn into bite‑size pieces
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional garnish: toasted sesame seeds

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the chickpeas with olive oil, half the minced garlic, ground ginger, salt, and pepper; spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until crisp and golden.
2. While the chickpeas roast, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.
3. In a large skillet over medium heat, add a drizzle of olive oil and the remaining garlic; sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the kale and a splash of water, cooking until wilted, about 3‑4 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
4. Stir the roasted chickpeas, lemon juice, and lemon zest into the cooked quinoa; then gently fold in the sautéed kale.
5. Serve warm, sprinkled with toasted sesame seeds if desired. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Chickpeas and Kale

text:
Coconut Curry Lentil & Spinach Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 can (13.5 oz) coconut milk
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 2 tbsp curry powder
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp ground turmeric
- 2 cups fresh spinach leaves
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. In a large pot, heat a splash of oil over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Sprinkle the curry powder, cumin, and turmeric over the aromatics, stirring constantly for 30 seconds to toast the spices.
4. Add the rinsed red lentils, coconut milk, and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer.
5. Cover and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and the stew has thickened, stirring occasionally.
6. Season with salt, pepper, and lime juice. Adjust seasoning to taste.
7. Fold in the fresh spinach leaves and cook for 2‑3 minutes, just until wilted.
8. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with chopped cilantro, and serve hot.
title: Coconut Curry Lentil & Spinach Stew

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa & Roasted Broccoli Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup water
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tsp lime zest
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp red pepper flakes
- 2 tbsp coconut oil, melted
- 1 large head broccoli, cut into florets
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup toasted sliced almonds
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the broccoli florets with olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread them on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until crisp‑tender and lightly browned.  
3. While the broccoli roasts, combine quinoa, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt in a medium saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15‑18 minutes until liquid is absorbed and quinoa is fluffy.  
4. Remove the cooked quinoa from heat and stir in melted coconut oil, lime juice, lime zest, maple syrup, cumin, smoked paprika, and red pepper flakes; fluff with a fork and season with additional salt and pepper if needed.  
5. Transfer the quinoa to a large mixing bowl, add the roasted broccoli, and toss gently to combine.  
6. Sprinkle toasted sliced almonds and chopped cilantro over the salad; serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa & Roasted Broccoli Salad

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- ¼ cup dried cranberries
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- Juice of 1 lemon

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Add the cubed sweet potatoes and toss to coat evenly.  
3. Spread the sweet potatoes in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway through, until tender and caramelized.  
4. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.  
5. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl. Add the roasted sweet potatoes, toasted pumpkin seeds, dried cranberries, chopped parsley, and lemon juice. Toss gently to combine.  
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a drizzle of maple syrup if desired.  
7. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with extra parsley and pumpkin seeds if desired. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Quinoa Salad

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Sweet Potato and Lentil Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 1 cup green lentils, rinsed
- ½ cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 small red onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp saffron threads, steeped in 2 tbsp hot water
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)
- Lemon wedges (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine lentils, quinoa, and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15‑18 minutes, or until both lentils and quinoa are cooked and the liquid is absorbed.  
3. In a skillet, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté 3‑4 minutes until translucent. Stir in the minced garlic and cook another minute.  
4. Add the steeped saffron (including the liquid) to the skillet, stirring to combine and release its color and aroma.  
5. Fold the cooked lentil‑quinoa mixture into the skillet, mixing gently to coat with the saffron‑onion mixture. Season with additional salt and pepper if needed.  
6. Transfer the roasted sweet potatoes to the skillet and gently toss everything together until evenly distributed and warmed through, about 2‑3 minutes.  
7. Serve the pilaf hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley and a squeeze of lemon juice, if desired. Enjoy!
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Sweet Potato and Lentil Pilaf

text:
Spiced Orange‑Maple Quinoa & Roasted Butternut Squash Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 medium butternut squash, peeled and cubed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 Tbsp maple syrup
- Zest of 1 orange
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup pumpkin seeds, toasted
- ¼ cup dried cranberries
- 2 Tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- Juice of ½ orange (optional, for extra brightness)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the cubed butternut squash with 1 Tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, orange zest, cumin, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning once, until tender and caramelized.
2. While the squash roasts, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, orange zest, orange juice (if using), a pinch of salt, and a dash of pepper to create a dressing.
4. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl. Add the roasted butternut squash, toasted pumpkin seeds, dried cranberries, and chopped parsley.
5. Drizzle the orange‑maple dressing over the salad and toss gently to combine, ensuring everything is evenly coated.
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a splash of orange juice if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
