title: Spiced Orange‑Maple Quinoa & Roasted Butternut Squash Salad

text:
Citrus‑Infused Chickpea & Farro Salad with Toasted Almonds

Ingredients:
- 1 cup farro, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups water or low‑sodium vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 orange, zest and juice
- 1 lemon, zest and juice
- 2 tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil
- 1 small red onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 cups baby spinach, loosely packed
- ¼ cup toasted sliced almonds
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine the rinsed farro and water (or broth). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook 20–25 minutes until the farro is tender but still slightly chewy. Drain any excess liquid and set aside to cool slightly.  
2. While the farro cooks, heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the diced red onion and sauté 3–4 minutes until softened. Stir in the minced garlic and cook another 30 seconds until fragrant. Remove from heat.  
3. In a large mixing bowl whisk together the orange zest, lemon zest, orange juice, lemon juice, remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper to create the citrus dressing.  
4. Add the cooked farro, sautéed onion‑garlic mixture, chickpeas, and baby spinach to the bowl with the dressing. Toss gently until everything is evenly coated and the spinach begins to wilt.  
5. Transfer the salad to a serving platter or individual bowls. Sprinkle the toasted sliced almonds and chopped parsley over the top for crunch and freshness.  
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a splash of citrus juice if desired. Serve warm, at room temperature, or chilled. Enjoy!
title: Citrus‑Infused Chickpea & Farro Salad with Toasted Almonds

text:
Spiced Cardamom Pumpkin and Lentil Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 lb (450 g) dried green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 cups (500 ml) vegetable broth
- 2 cups (500 ml) water
- 1 lb (450 g) pumpkin, peeled and cubed
- 1 medium onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp ground cardamom
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Optional: a squeeze of lime juice

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4‑5 minutes.  
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for another minute until fragrant.  
3. Sprinkle the ground cardamom, cumin, and smoked paprika over the aromatics, stirring constantly for 30 seconds to toast the spices.  
4. Add the cubed pumpkin and rinsed lentils to the pot, mixing to coat them with the spiced onion mixture.  
5. Pour in the vegetable broth and water, bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to a gentle simmer.  
6. Cover the pot and let the stew cook for 25‑30 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and the pumpkin is soft. Stir occasionally and add a splash more water if the stew becomes too thick.  
7. Once the lentils and pumpkin are cooked, stir in the maple syrup, and season with salt and pepper to taste. Adjust seasoning with a squeeze of lime juice if desired.  
8. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve hot with crusty bread or over a bed of cooked quinoa for extra heartiness.
title: Spiced Cardamom Pumpkin and Lentil Stew

text:
Spiced Cardamom Lentil and Roasted Tomato Soup

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 4 large ripe tomatoes, quartered
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 carrot, peeled and diced
- 1 celery stalk, diced
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 teaspoon ground cardamom
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1 bay leaf
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 tablespoon lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Arrange the tomato quarters on a baking sheet, drizzle with 1 tablespoon olive oil, and season with salt and pepper. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, until the skins blister and the flesh softens.
2. While the tomatoes roast, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion, carrot, and celery; sauté for 5‑7 minutes, until the vegetables are softened.
3. Stir in the minced garlic, ground cardamom, cumin, and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute, allowing the spices to become fragrant.
4. Add the rinsed red lentils, roasted tomatoes (with any pan juices), vegetable broth, and bay leaf to the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a gentle simmer.
5. Cover and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and the soup has thickened. Stir occasionally.
6. Remove the bay leaf. Using an immersion blender (or transferring the soup in batches to a countertop blender), puree the soup until smooth but still slightly textured.
7. Season with salt, pepper, and lemon juice to taste. Adjust consistency with a splash of water or broth if needed.
8. Ladle the soup into bowls and garnish with chopped fresh cilantro. Serve hot with crusty bread or a side of rice.
title: Spiced Cardamom Lentil and Roasted Tomato Soup

text:
Cinnamon‑Spiced Sweet Potato and Black Bean Enchiladas

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed
- 1 small red onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 8 small corn tortillas
- ½ cup shredded Monterey Jack cheese
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 lime, cut into wedges
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the diced sweet potatoes with olive oil, cinnamon, smoked paprika, cumin, cayenne, salt, and pepper. Spread them on the prepared sheet and roast 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
3. While the sweet potatoes roast, heat a skillet over medium heat, add a drizzle of oil, and sauté the onion until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add the garlic and cook another 30 seconds.  
4. Add the black beans to the skillet, season with a pinch of salt and pepper, and heat through, about 2 minutes. Remove from heat.  
5. In a large bowl combine the roasted sweet potatoes, black‑bean mixture, and half of the cilantro; toss gently to mix.  
6. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet for ~20 seconds per side. Spoon the sweet‑
title: Cinnamon‑Spiced Sweet Potato and Black Bean Enchiladas

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Lentil and Spinach Soup

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 can (13.5 oz) coconut milk
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 large onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch piece fresh ginger, grated
- zest of 1 lime
- 2 Tbsp lime juice
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- ½ tsp chili flakes (optional)
- 4 cups fresh spinach leaves
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes.
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add the cumin, coriander, chili flakes, and lime zest; toast the spices for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
4. Pour in the rinsed lentils, coconut milk, and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to a gentle simmer.
5. Cover and simmer for 15‑20 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and the soup has thickened slightly.
6. Stir in the lime juice and season with salt and pepper to taste.
7. Add the fresh spinach leaves and cook for 2‑3 minutes, just until wilted.
8. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with cilantro leaves, and serve hot.
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Lentil and Spinach Soup

text:
Cinnamon‑Spiced Pear and Walnut Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 2 ripe pears, cored and diced
- ½ cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped
- ¼ cup dried cranberries
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp ground ginger
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh arugula leaves, for serving (optional)

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa and water; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and transfer to a large bowl to cool slightly.
2. While the quinoa cooks, heat 1 tbsp of olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the diced pears, sprinkle with cinnamon and ginger, and sauté for 4‑5 minutes until the pears are softened and lightly caramelized. Drizzle with maple syrup, stir to coat, and cook for an additional minute. Remove from heat.
3. Add the toasted walnuts, dried cranberries, and the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil to the bowl of quinoa. Gently fold in the warm spiced pears, ensuring an even distribution of ingredients.
4. Season the salad with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste. If desired, serve the quinoa mixture atop a bed of fresh arugula leaves for added peppery bite.
5. Serve warm or at room temperature, and enjoy the sweet‑spicy harmony of cinnamon‑spiced pears, crunchy walnuts, and fluffy quinoa.
title: Cinnamon‑Spiced Pear and Walnut Quinoa Salad

text:
Spicy Sesame‑Lime Tofu with Coconut Rice and Pickled Veggies

Ingredients:
- 1 block (14 oz) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 Tbsp sesame oil
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce
- 1 Tbsp lime juice
- 1 tsp sriracha or chili garlic sauce
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 cup jasmine rice
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup water
- ½ cup shredded carrots
- ½ cup thinly sliced red cabbage
- ¼ cup rice vinegar
- 1 Tbsp honey or maple syrup
- 1 tsp sesame seeds, toasted
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, whisk together sesame oil, soy sauce, lime juice, sriracha, and grated ginger; add the tofu cubes and toss to coat. Let marinate for 10 minutes.
2. While the tofu marinates, combine jasmine rice, coconut milk, and water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
3. Prepare the pickled veggies: in a small bowl, mix rice vinegar, honey, a pinch of salt, and a splash of lime juice; add shredded carrots and sliced red cabbage, stirring to coat. Let sit for at least 5 minutes.
4. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated tofu and cook, turning occasionally, until golden and crisp on all sides, about 6‑8 minutes. Season with a little salt and pepper.
5. To serve, spoon a bed of coconut rice onto each plate, top with the crispy tofu, and arrange pickled veggies alongside. Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds and chopped cilantro over the dish for garnish. Enjoy while warm.
title: Spicy Sesame‑Lime Tofu with Coconut Rice and Pickled Veggies

text:
Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Cauliflower Steaks with Chickpea‑Tahini Drizzle

Ingredients:
- 1 large cauliflower head, sliced into 1‑inch thick “steaks”
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 3 tbsp tahini
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp olive oil (plus extra for roasting)
- 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves (plus extra for garnish)
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh parsley (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Brush both sides of the cauliflower steaks with olive oil, then season with salt, pepper, and half of the thyme leaves. Arrange them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
3. Toss the chickpeas with a drizzle of olive oil, smoked paprika, minced garlic, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Spread the chickpeas around the cauliflower steaks on the same baking sheet.  
4. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, flipping the cauliflower steaks halfway through, until the edges are golden‑brown and the chickpeas are crisp.  
5. While the vegetables roast, whisk together the tahini, lemon juice, remaining thyme, and a splash of water (about 2 tbsp) until smooth and drizzle‑ready. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.  
6. Remove the cauliflower steaks and chickpeas from the oven. Transfer the steaks to a serving platter, scatter the roasted chickpeas on top, and drizzle generously with the lemon‑thyme tahini sauce.  
7. Garnish with chopped parsley and any remaining fresh thyme leaves. Serve warm as a main‑course or hearty side.
title: Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Cauliflower Steaks with Chickpea‑Tahini Drizzle

text:
Lemon‑Rosemary Barley Salad with Grilled Zucchini and Feta

Ingredients:
- 1 cup pearl barley
- 2 ½ cups low‑sodium vegetable broth
- 2 medium zucchini, sliced lengthwise into ¼‑inch strips
- 1 ½ cups crumbled feta cheese
- 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
- 1 teaspoon lemon zest
- 1 tablespoon fresh rosemary, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 3 tablespoons extra‑virgin olive oil, divided
- ¼ teaspoon sea salt
- ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Rinse the barley under cold water, then combine it with the vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30‑35 minutes, or until the barley is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.
2. While the barley cooks, preheat a grill pan or outdoor grill over medium‑high heat. Brush the zucchini strips with 1 tablespoon olive oil and season with a pinch of salt and pepper. Grill the zucchini 2‑3 minutes per side, until grill marks appear and the flesh is tender. Transfer to a cutting board and slice into bite‑size pieces.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil, lemon juice, lemon zest, minced garlic, chopped rosemary, salt, and pepper to create the dressing.
4. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked barley, grilled zucchini, and half of the feta cheese. Pour the lemon‑rosemary dressing over the mixture and toss gently to coat evenly.
5. Transfer the salad to a serving platter or individual bowls. Sprinkle the remaining feta cheese on top and garnish with chopped parsley, if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Rosemary Barley Salad with Grilled Zucchini and Feta

text:
Cinnamon‑Lime Chickpea & Sweet Potato Skillet

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and diced ½‑inch
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1 small onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan, combine the quinoa and water (or broth). Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
2. While the quinoa cooks, heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the diced sweet potato, season with a pinch of salt, and sauté 8‑10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender and lightly browned.  
3. Push the sweet potato to the side of the skillet. Add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, then the onion and red bell pepper. Cook, stirring, for 4‑5 minutes until softened.  
4. Stir in the garlic, cumin, cinnamon, and smoked paprika; cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.  
5. Add the chickpeas to the skillet and toss to coat with the spices. Cook 2‑3 minutes until the chickpeas are warmed through.  
6. Fold the cooked quinoa into the skillet, mixing everything evenly.  
7. Remove the skillet from heat. Sprinkle the lime zest, drizzle the lime juice, and season with salt and pepper to taste.  
8. Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve warm, optionally with a drizzle of extra‑virgin olive oil.
title: Cinnamon‑Lime Chickpea & Sweet Potato Skillet

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 cup cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1/2 cup dried apricots, chopped
- 1/4 cup slivered almonds, toasted
- 1 tsp saffron threads
- 1/4 cup warm water
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)
- Lemon wedges (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the cauliflower florets with 1 tbsp olive oil, ½ tsp cumin, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20–25 minutes, until golden and tender.
2. While the cauliflower roasts, place the saffron threads in ¼ cup warm water and let steep for 5 minutes.
3. Heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the chickpeas, the remaining ½ tsp cumin, smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt. Sauté for 3–4 minutes until lightly browned.
4. Add the rinsed quinoa to the saucepan, stir to coat, then pour in 2 cups water (or broth) and the saffron infusion (including the threads). Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the quinoa is fluffy. Fluff with a fork.
5. Stir the chopped apricots and toasted almonds into the cooked quinoa. Season with additional salt and pepper as needed.
6. To serve, spread the saffron‑infused quinoa on a platter, top with roasted cauliflower and sautéed chickpeas
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Pilaf

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Quinoa Bowl with Roasted Edamame

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice
- 1 cup frozen edamame, thawed and patted dry
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1 avocado, sliced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the edamame with a drizzle of olive oil, a pinch of salt, and half the turmeric; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 12‑15 minutes, stirring once, until slightly crisp.
2. Meanwhile, combine quinoa, coconut milk, remaining turmeric, lime zest, and a pinch of salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy.
3. Remove the quinoa from heat and stir in lime juice. Adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.
4. Divide the cooked quinoa among serving bowls. Top each bowl with roasted edamame, diced red bell pepper, avocado slices, and a generous sprinkle of chopped cilantro.
5. Drizzle any remaining olive oil over the bowls, serve immediately, and enjoy the bright, aromatic flavors.
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Quinoa Bowl with Roasted Edamame

text:
Saffron‑Infused Chickpea and Spinach Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 cup basmati rice, rinsed
- 1½ cups vegetable broth
- ½ teaspoon saffron threads
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 small onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (canned, drained and rinsed)
- 3 cups fresh spinach, roughly chopped
- Zest of 1 lemon
- ¼ cup toasted pine nuts
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, combine the vegetable broth with the saffron threads and let steep for 5 minutes.
2. Heat the olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 3–4 minutes.
3. Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another 30 seconds until fragrant.
4. Add the rinsed basmati rice to the saucepan, stirring to coat the grains with the oil and aromatics for 2 minutes.
5. Pour the saffron‑infused broth over the rice, bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
6. While the rice cooks, heat a skillet over medium heat and add a splash of olive oil. Toss in the chickpeas and sauté for 3–4 minutes until lightly browned.
7. Add the chopped spinach to the skillet with the chickpeas and cook, stirring, until the spinach wilts, about 2 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
8. Fluff the cooked rice with a fork and gently fold in the chickpea‑spinach mixture, lemon zest, and toasted pine nuts. Adjust seasoning if needed.
9. Transfer the pilaf to a serving bowl, drizzle with a little extra olive oil if desired, and serve warm. Enjoy!
title: Saffron‑Infused Chickpea and Spinach Pilaf

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Beet and Lentil Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 2 medium beets, peeled and diced
- 1 cup green lentils, rinsed
- ½ cup brown rice, rinsed
- 1 small onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 ½ cups vegetable broth
- ¼ teaspoon saffron threads
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, chopped

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the diced beets with 1 tablespoon olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, until tender and caramelized.
2. While the beets roast, place the saffron threads in a small bowl with 2 tablespoons hot vegetable broth; let steep for 5 minutes.
3. In a medium saucepan, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté for 3‑4 minutes until translucent.
4. Stir in the minced garlic and cumin; cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
5. Add the rinsed lentils and brown rice to the saucepan, stirring to coat with the aromatics.
6. Pour in the remaining vegetable broth, the saffron‑infused broth, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 35‑40 minutes, or until the lentils and rice are tender and the liquid is absorbed.
7. Remove the saucepan from heat; fluff the pilaf with a fork and gently fold in the roasted beets, lemon zest, and chopped parsley. Adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.
8. Serve warm as a hearty main dish or a vibrant side, garnished with extra parsley and a drizzle of olive oil if desired.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Beet and Lentil Pilaf

text:
Roasted Garlic & Lemon Chickpea & Quinoa Stuffed Sweet Potatoes

Ingredients:
- 4 medium sweet potatoes
- 1 cup cooked quinoa
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 lemon, zest and juice
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 Tbsp fresh parsley, chopped (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. Scrub the sweet potatoes, pat dry, and place them on the prepared sheet. Rub each potato with 1 Tbsp olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Bake for 45‑55 minutes, or until tender when pierced with a fork.
3. While the potatoes bake, heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
4. Stir in the chickpeas, cumin, smoked paprika, lemon zest, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5‑6 minutes until the chickpeas are lightly browned.
5. Add the cooked quinoa to the skillet, drizzle with lemon juice, and toss to combine. Adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice as desired. Remove from heat and stir in chopped parsley, if using.
6. When the sweet potatoes are done, let them cool slightly. Slice each potato lengthwise down the center, being careful not to cut all the way through, and gently fluff the interior with a fork.
7. Spoon the chickpea‑quinoa mixture evenly into the opened sweet potatoes, pressing lightly to fill.
8. Return the stuffed potatoes to the oven for 5‑7 minutes to warm the filling. Serve hot, garnished with extra parsley or a drizzle of tahini if desired.
title: Roasted Garlic & Lemon Chickpea & Quinoa Stuffed Sweet Potatoes

text:
Roasted Garlic and Herb Quinoa Stuffed Portobello Mushrooms

Ingredients:
- 4 large portobello mushroom caps, stems removed and gills scraped
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- 1 tsp dried rosemary
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ cup grated Parmesan cheese
- ¼ cup chopped fresh parsley
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Lightly grease a baking sheet with 1 tablespoon of olive oil.
2. In a saucepan, combine the quinoa and vegetable broth; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
3. While the quinoa cooks, place the mushroom caps gill‑side up on the prepared baking sheet. Brush each cap with the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil and season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
4. In a small skillet over medium heat, sauté the minced garlic for 1‑2 minutes until fragrant. Add the dried thyme, rosemary, and smoked paprika; stir for another 30 seconds.
5. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a mixing bowl. Add the sautéed garlic‑herb mixture, grated Parmesan, chopped parsley, and season with additional salt and pepper. Toss to combine.
6. Spoon the quinoa mixture evenly into the mushroom caps, pressing gently to pack the filling.
7. Bake for 18‑20 minutes, until the mushrooms are tender and the tops are golden brown.
8. Remove from the oven, let cool for a couple of minutes, then serve warm, garnished with extra parsley if desired.
title: Roasted Garlic and Herb Quinoa Stuffed Portobello Mushrooms

text:
Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad with Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch sticks
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- 1/4 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1/3 cup pomegranate seeds
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh mint
- 2 tbsp crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- Dressing:
  - 3 tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil
  - 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar
  - 1 tsp honey
  - 1 tsp Dijon mustard
  - Pinch of salt

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the carrot sticks with olive oil, cinnamon, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the carrots in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
4. While the carrots roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.  
5. In a small jar, whisk together the dressing ingredients: olive oil, apple cider vinegar, honey, Dijon mustard, and a pinch of salt. Set aside.  
6. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted carrots, pomegranate seeds, toasted pumpkin seeds, and chopped mint. Drizzle with the dressing and toss gently to coat.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed.  
8. Transfer the salad to a serving platter or individual bowls, and sprinkle crumbled feta on top, if using. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad with Pomegranate

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Bowl

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/2‑inch sticks
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- 1 cup cooked quinoa (optional, for serving)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, grated ginger, turmeric, minced garlic, salt, and pepper.  
3. Add the carrot sticks and chickpeas to the bowl; toss until evenly coated with the spice mixture.  
4. Spread the carrots and chickpeas in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
5. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until carrots are tender and lightly caramelized and chickpeas are crisp.  
6. While the vegetables roast, prepare quinoa according to package instructions, if using.  
7. Remove the roasted carrots and chickpeas from the oven; transfer to a serving bowl and sprinkle with chopped cilantro.  
8. Serve the roasted mixture over a bed of quinoa or on its own, drizzling any pan‑drippings over the top for extra flavor. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Bowl

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Lentil Soup

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 carrots, peeled and diced
- 2 celery stalks, diced
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves (or 1/2 tsp dried)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 tablespoon olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt. Spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway, until caramelized and tender.  
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots, and celery; sauté for 5‑7 minutes until softened.  
3. Stir in the garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.  
4. Add the rinsed red lentils and vegetable broth to the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes.  
5. Once the lentils are partially cooked, stir in the roasted sweet potatoes, coconut milk, and thyme. Simmer gently for an additional 10‑12 minutes, or until the lentils are fully tender and the soup is thickened.  
6. Season with salt and pepper to taste. If you prefer a smoother texture, blend the soup partially or fully with an immersion blender.  
7. Ladle the soup into bowls, drizzle a little extra coconut milk or maple syrup if desired, and garnish with a sprinkle of fresh thyme or a pinch of cinnamon. Enjoy warm!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Lentil Soup

text:
Spiced Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 8 oz (225 g) tempeh, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp low‑sodium soy sauce
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 Tbsp lime juice
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups vegetable broth
- ½ cup coconut milk
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 2 green onions, sliced thin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a shallow bowl, whisk together maple syrup, soy sauce, smoked paprika, cumin, garlic, ginger, and lime juice. Add the tempeh cubes, toss to coat, and let marinate for at least 15 minutes.
2. While the tempeh marinates, combine the rinsed quinoa, vegetable broth, and coconut milk in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork and season with salt and pepper.
3. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated tempeh (reserve any excess sauce) and sauté 5‑7 minutes, turning occasionally, until the pieces are golden‑brown and caramelized.
4. Pour the reserved sauce into the skillet with the tempeh and cook an additional 2 minutes, allowing the glaze to thicken and coat the tempeh evenly. Remove from heat.
5. Stir the chopped cilantro and sliced green onions into the cooked quinoa. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired.
6. To serve, spoon a bed of coconut‑lime quinoa onto plates, top with the spiced maple‑glazed tempeh, and garnish with extra cilantro or green onions if you like. Enjoy warm!
title: Spiced Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa Pilaf

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Black Bean Tacos

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 ½ cups cooked black beans (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 8 small corn tortillas
- 1 avocado, sliced
- ½ red onion, thinly sliced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped
- 1 lime, cut into wedges
- Optional: crumbled feta or cotija cheese for topping

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, cinnamon, cumin, smoked paprika, olive oil, salt, and pepper.  
3. Add the diced sweet potatoes to the bowl and toss until evenly coated with the maple‑spice mixture.  
4. Spread the sweet potatoes in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until tender and caramelized.  
5. While the sweet potatoes roast, warm the black beans in a small saucepan over low heat, adding a pinch of salt and a squeeze of lime juice if desired.  
6. Heat the corn tortillas on a dry skillet over medium heat for about 30 seconds per side, or until pliable. Keep warm by covering with a clean kitchen towel.  
7. To assemble each taco, place a generous spoonful of roasted sweet potatoes on a tortilla, top with black beans, sliced avocado, red onion, and a sprinkle of cilantro.  
8. Drizzle any remaining maple‑cinnamon glaze from the baking sheet over the tacos, and finish with a squeeze of fresh lime juice. Add crumbled feta or cotija cheese, if using.  
9. Serve immediately and enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Black Bean Tacos

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Edamame Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 ½ cups frozen edamame, thawed
- 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- ½ teaspoon sea salt
- ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
- 2 tablespoons toasted pumpkin seeds (optional)
- 2 cups mixed baby greens

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, cinnamon, olive oil, salt, and pepper.  
3. Add the cubed sweet potatoes to the bowl and toss until evenly coated. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast the sweet potatoes for 20 minutes, then stir and continue roasting for another 15‑20 minutes, or until tender and caramelized.  
5. While the sweet potatoes roast, place the thawed edamame in a small saucepan, cover with water, and simmer for 3‑4 minutes. Drain and set aside.  
6. In a large salad bowl, combine the roasted sweet potatoes, cooked edamame, mixed baby greens, and lemon juice. Toss gently to mix.  
7. Sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds over the top for added crunch, if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Edamame Salad

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Roasted Eggplant and Chickpea Bowl  

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cut into 1‑inch cubes  
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed  
- 2 Tbsp olive oil  
- 1 tsp ground turmeric  
- 1 tsp freshly grated ginger  
- 1 tsp lemon zest  
- 2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice  
- 2 cloves garlic, minced  
- ½ tsp smoked paprika  
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste  
- 1 cup cooked quinoa (cooled)  
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley  
- 1 Tbsp toasted pine nuts (optional)  

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the eggplant cubes and chickpeas with olive oil, turmeric, ginger, lemon zest, lemon juice, garlic, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the eggplant is golden‑brown and tender and the chickpeas are crisp.  
4. While the vegetables roast, prepare the quinoa if not already cooked: combine ½ cup quinoa with 1 cup water, bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook 15 minutes; fluff with a fork and let cool slightly.  
5. To assemble the bowl, divide the quinoa among serving bowls, top with the roasted eggplant‑chickpea mixture, and sprinkle with fresh parsley and toasted pine nuts.  
6. Finish with an extra squeeze of lemon juice and a drizzle of olive oil, if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Roasted Eggplant and Chickpea Bowl

text:
Maple‑Glazed Roasted Eggplant and Quinoa Salad with Pomegranate  

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cut into ½‑inch cubes  
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup  
- 1 Tbsp olive oil, plus extra for drizzling  
- 1 tsp smoked paprika  
- ½ tsp ground cumin  
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste  
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed  
- 2 cups vegetable broth or water  
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds  
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds  
- 2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice  
- 1 Tbsp chopped fresh mint  
- 1 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley  

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together maple syrup, olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Add the eggplant cubes and toss to coat evenly.  
3. Spread the glazed eggplant in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until the pieces are caramelized and tender.  
4. While the eggplant roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.  
5. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl. Add lemon juice, chopped mint, and parsley; toss to combine.  
6. Gently fold the roasted eggplant into the quinoa mixture.  
7. Portion the salad onto serving plates or a large platter. Sprinkle pomegranate seeds and toasted pumpkin seeds over the top for color and crunch.  
8. Drizzle a little extra olive oil, if desired, and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Roasted Eggplant and Quinoa Salad with Pomegranate

text:
Roasted Garlic and Herb Quinoa Stuffed Bell Peppers

Ingredients:
- 4 large red or yellow bell peppers, tops cut off and seeds removed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon dried oregano
- 1 teaspoon dried thyme
- 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1 cup cherry tomatoes, halved
- 1/2 cup canned black beans, drained and rinsed
- 1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1/2 cup shredded mozzarella cheese (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Place the prepared bell peppers upright in a baking dish.
2. In a saucepan, combine quinoa and vegetable broth; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes or until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
3. While the quinoa cooks, heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add minced garlic and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
4. Stir in oregano, thyme, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; cook another minute.
5. Add cherry tomatoes and black beans to the skillet; cook 3‑4 minutes until tomatoes soften.
6. Remove the skillet from heat and fold in the cooked quinoa, fresh parsley, and adjust seasoning if needed.
7. Spoon the quinoa mixture into each bell pepper cavity, packing gently. Top with shredded mozzarella if using.
8. Cover the baking dish with foil and bake for 25 minutes. Remove foil and bake an additional 10 minutes, or until peppers are tender and cheese is melted and golden.
9. Let the stuffed peppers rest for 5 minutes before serving. Enjoy!
title: Roasted Garlic and Herb Quinoa Stuffed Bell Peppers

text:
Cinnamon‑Lime Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch rounds
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 Tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tsp sea salt
- ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the carrot rounds with olive oil, cinnamon, lime zest, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the carrots in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
4. While the carrots roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.  
5. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl. Add the roasted carrots, lime juice, and gently toss to combine.  
6. Adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired.  
7. Sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds and chopped cilantro over the salad just before serving.  
8. Serve warm, at room temperature, or chilled as a hearty side or light main dish.
title: Cinnamon‑Lime Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad

text:
Spiced Maple‑Glazed Eggplant and Quinoa Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- ½ tsp sea salt, plus more to taste
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 2 cups chopped kale, stems removed
- 2 Tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, smoked paprika, cumin, 1 Tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper. Add the cubed eggplant and toss to coat evenly.  
3. Spread the glazed eggplant in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until the pieces are tender and caramelized.  
4. While the eggplant roasts, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
5. In a skillet, heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped kale and sauté 3‑4 minutes, until wilted but still bright green. Season with a pinch of salt.  
6. To assemble the bowl, divide the quinoa among serving bowls. Top each with roasted maple‑glazed eggplant, sautéed kale, a drizzle of fresh lemon juice, and a sprinkle of toasted pumpkin seeds.  
7. Serve warm, adjusting salt and pepper to taste. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Maple‑Glazed Eggplant and Quinoa Bowl

text:
Miso‑Glazed Tempeh with Sesame‑Ginger Broccoli

Ingredients:
- 8 oz (225 g) tempeh, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 2 Tbsp white miso paste
- 1 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp low‑sodium soy sauce
- 1 tsp rice‑vinegar
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 Tbsp sesame oil, divided
- 1 lb (450 g) broccoli florets
- 1 Tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- 1 tsp lime juice
- Pinch red‑pepper flakes (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl whisk together miso paste, maple syrup, soy sauce, rice‑vinegar, garlic, ginger, and ½ Tbsp sesame oil to form the glaze. Set aside.  
2. Heat the remaining ½ Tbsp sesame oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the tempeh cubes and sauté 4–5 minutes, turning once, until lightly browned on all sides.  
3. Pour the miso glaze over the tempeh, stirring to coat. Cook an additional 2 minutes, allowing the glaze to thicken and cling to the tempeh. Transfer the tempeh to a plate and keep warm.  
4. In the same skillet, add the broccoli florets. Sauté 5–6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the broccoli is crisp‑tender and begins to caramelize.  
5. Drizzle the remaining ½ tsp sesame oil over the broccoli, then add lime juice, red‑pepper flakes (if using), and season with salt and pepper. Toss to combine.  
6. Plate the sesame‑ginger broccoli and top with the miso‑glazed tempeh. Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds over the dish for garnish. Serve immediately.
title: Miso‑Glazed Tempeh with Sesame‑Ginger Broccoli

text:
Harissa‑Spiced Roasted Eggplant and Lentil Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cubed
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 tbsp harissa paste
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 red bell pepper, sliced
- 1 small red onion, thinly sliced
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 1 lemon, cut into wedges (for serving)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cubed eggplant, red bell pepper, and red onion with olive oil, harissa paste, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the vegetables in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until tender and slightly charred.  
4. While the vegetables roast, combine the rinsed lentils and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 20‑25 minutes, or until lentils are tender but not mushy. Drain any excess liquid and season with salt and pepper.  
5. To assemble the bowl, divide the cooked lentils among serving bowls. Top each with a generous portion of the harissa‑roasted vegetables.  
6. Sprinkle fresh cilantro over the top and add a lemon wedge on the side for squeezing.  
7. Serve warm, optionally drizzling a little extra olive oil or a dollop of plain yogurt for creaminess.
title: Harissa‑Spiced Roasted Eggplant and Lentil Bowl

text:
Garlic‑Lime Roasted Cauliflower Steaks with Herbed Couscous

Ingredients:
- 1 large cauliflower head
- 3 Tbsp olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 Tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tsp lime zest
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup couscous
- 1 ¼ cup vegetable broth (or water)
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- 1 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 1 Tbsp toasted pine nuts (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Trim the leaves and stem from the cauliflower, then slice it into ¾‑inch thick “steaks” (you should get 2–3 usable steaks; keep any loose florets for another use).  
3. In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, minced garlic, lime juice, lime zest, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.  
4. Brush both sides of each cauliflower steak generously with the garlic‑lime mixture and place them on the prepared baking sheet.  
5. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, flipping halfway through, until the edges are golden‑brown and the interior is tender.  
6. While the cauliflower roasts, bring the vegetable broth to a boil in a medium saucepan. Stir in the couscous, cover, and remove from heat. Let sit for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.  
7. Stir the chopped parsley, cilantro, lemon zest, and toasted pine nuts (if using) into the fluffed couscous. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.  
8. To serve, plate a cauliflower steak, spoon a generous mound of herbed couscous beside it, and drizzle any remaining pan juices over the top. Garnish with extra cilantro leaves and a wedge of lime if desired. Enjoy!
title: Garlic‑Lime Roasted Cauliflower Steaks with Herbed Couscous

text:
Harissa‑Glazed Eggplant and Quinoa Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 tablespoons harissa paste
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon lemon juice
- ¼ cup toasted pine nuts
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the eggplant cubes with 1 tablespoon olive oil, harissa paste, minced garlic, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the seasoned eggplant on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway through, until tender and lightly charred.  
4. While the eggplant roasts, combine the rinsed quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the quinoa is fluffy and the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes.  
5. Fluff the cooked quinoa with a fork and stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt and pepper.  
6. Transfer the quinoa to a serving bowl, gently fold in the roasted harissa‑glazed eggplant, and sprinkle toasted pine nuts over the top.  
7. Garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, if desired, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Harissa‑Glazed Eggplant and Quinoa Pilaf

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Shrimp with Garlic‑Herb Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups water
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- Optional: lime wedges for serving

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa, water, and coconut milk. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed and quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, 5 minutes.
2. While quinoa cooks, whisk together lime juice, turmeric, minced garlic, olive oil, salt, and pepper in a large bowl.
3. Add the shrimp to the bowl and toss to coat evenly. Let marinate for 5 minutes.
4. Heat a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the shrimp and cook 2‑3 minutes per side, until pink and opaque. Remove from heat and stir in chopped cilantro and parsley.
5. Fluff the cooked quinoa with a fork and transfer to a serving platter. Top with the turmeric‑lime shrimp.
6. Garnish with extra cilantro, parsley, and lime wedges if desired. Serve immediately.
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Shrimp with Garlic‑Herb Quinoa

text:
Sesame‑Crusted Salmon with Citrus Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 4 salmon fillets (6 oz each)
- 2 Tbsp black sesame seeds
- 2 Tbsp white sesame seeds
- 1 Tbsp olive oil (for searing)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or low‑sodium vegetable broth
- 1 orange, zest and juice
- 1 lime, zest and juice
- 2 Tbsp honey
- 1 Tbsp apple cider vinegar
- 2 Tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil (for dressing)
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- ¼ cup red onion, finely diced
- Pinch of red‑pepper flakes (optional)

Instructions:
1. Pat the salmon fillets dry with paper towels; season both sides with salt and pepper.
2. In a shallow dish, combine black and white sesame seeds. Press the top side of each fillet into the seeds to create an even crust.
3. Heat 1 Tbsp olive oil in a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the salmon, crust side down, and cook 4‑5 minutes until golden and crisp. Flip and cook another 3‑4 minutes, or until the fish reaches an internal temperature of 145 °F. Transfer to a plate and keep warm.
4. Meanwhile, bring 2 cups water or broth to a boil in a saucepan. Add the rinsed quinoa, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.
5. In a small bowl, whisk together orange zest, lime zest, orange juice, lime juice, honey, apple cider vinegar, extra‑virgin olive oil, and a pinch of salt to create the citrus dressing.
6. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl. Add the diced red onion, chopped cilantro, and half of the citrus dressing. Toss gently to combine.
7. Plate a generous scoop of the citrus quinoa salad on each serving plate. Top with a sesame‑crusted salmon fillet.
8. Drizzle the remaining citrus dressing over the salmon and garnish with additional cilantro, sesame seeds, and red‑pepper flakes if desired. Serve immediately.
title: Sesame‑Crusted Salmon with Citrus Quinoa Salad

text:
Coconut‑Lime Shrimp and Avocado Rice Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup jasmine rice
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 ripe avocado, sliced
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- ½ tsp red pepper flakes
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Rinse the jasmine rice under cold water until the water runs clear. In a medium saucepan combine the rice, coconut milk, and ½ cup water; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until tender. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
2. While the rice cooks, season the shrimp with salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes.  
3. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger, sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.  
4. Add the seasoned shrimp to the skillet and cook 2‑3 minutes per side, or until pink and opaque. Remove from heat and drizzle with fresh lime juice.  
5. Assemble the bowls: divide the coconut‑infused rice among four serving bowls, top with the cooked shrimp, sliced avocado, and a sprinkle of chopped cilantro.  
6. Serve immediately, optionally with extra lime wedges and a drizzle of soy sauce or hot sauce if desired.
title: Coconut‑Lime Shrimp and Avocado Rice Bowl

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Chickpea and Sweet Potato Tostadas

Ingredients:
- 8 corn tortillas
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and diced
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 tbsp coconut oil
- 1 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tsp lime zest
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp chili flakes (adjust to taste)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ½ cup red cabbage, thinly sliced
- 1 ripe avocado, sliced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the diced sweet potato with 1 tablespoon of coconut oil, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of smoked paprika; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of coconut oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger; sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
3. Stir in the chickpeas, cumin, coriander, chili flakes, and the remaining smoked paprika. Cook, stirring, for 3‑4 minutes until the chickpeas are lightly toasted.
4. Pour in the coconut milk, lime juice, and lime zest. Bring to a gentle simmer and let the mixture reduce for about 5 minutes, or until it thickens slightly. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
5. Once the sweet potatoes are done, fold them into the chickpea‑coconut sauce, mixing gently to combine. Keep warm on low heat.
6. Warm the corn tortillas: either toast them in a dry skillet for 30 seconds per side or microwave them covered with a damp paper towel for 20 seconds.
7. To assemble each tostada, place a warm tortilla on a plate, spoon a generous layer of the chickpea‑sweet potato mixture over it, then top with sliced red cabbage, avocado slices, and a sprinkle of fresh cilantro.
8. Finish with toasted pumpkin seeds, if using, and an extra squeeze of lime juice. Serve immediately. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Chickpea and Sweet Potato Tostadas

text:
Spicy Coconut Lime Tempeh Lettuce Wraps

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- ¼ cup coconut milk
- 2 Tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tsp lime zest
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 Tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 2 Tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp sriracha or chili garlic sauce (adjust to heat preference)
- 1 Tbsp sesame oil
- 1 Tbsp vegetable oil (for cooking)
- 8–10 large butter lettuce leaves, rinsed and dried
- ½ cup shredded carrots
- ½ cup cucumber, thinly sliced into matchsticks
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped
- 2 Tbsp roasted peanuts, roughly chopped (optional)
- Salt and pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, whisk together coconut milk, lime juice, lime zest, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, maple syrup, sriracha, and sesame oil. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.  
2. Add the tempeh cubes to the marinade, toss to coat, and let sit for at least 15 minutes (or up to 1 hour in the refrigerator for deeper flavor).  
3. Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Remove tempeh from the marinade (reserve the excess liquid) and add to the hot skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the tempeh is golden brown and crisp on the edges, about 6–8 minutes.  
4. Pour the reserved marinade into the skillet with the tempeh. Reduce heat to medium and simmer for 2–3 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken and coat the tempeh. Remove from heat.  
5. To assemble each wrap, place a lettuce leaf on a plate, spoon a generous portion of the coconut‑lime tempeh onto the center, then top with shredded carrots, cucumber matchsticks, and chopped cilantro.  
6. Sprinkle roasted peanuts over the filling, if using, and drizzle any remaining sauce from the pan. Serve immediately, letting diners fold the lettuce around the filling and enjoy.
title: Spicy Coconut Lime Tempeh Lettuce Wraps

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea & Sweet Potato Curry

Ingredients:
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 large onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tbsp coconut oil
- 1 tbsp red curry paste
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 cup coconut milk
- ½ cup vegetable broth
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Cooked jasmine rice or quinoa, for serving

Instructions:
1. Heat the coconut oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes.  
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for another minute until fragrant.  
3. Add the red curry paste, ground turmeric, and cumin. Cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute to toast the spices.  
4. Toss in the cubed sweet potatoes and chickpeas, coating them with the spice mixture.  
5. Pour in the coconut milk and vegetable broth, stirring to combine. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to a simmer.  
6. Cover the pot and let the curry simmer for 15‑20 minutes, or until the sweet potatoes are tender.  
7. Stir in the lime juice and maple syrup, then season with salt and pepper to taste. Adjust the seasoning if needed.  
8. Serve the curry over cooked jasmine rice or quinoa, and garnish with fresh cilantro leaves. Enjoy!
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea & Sweet Potato Curry

text:
Maple‑Sage Roasted Acorn Squash with Quinoa and Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 2 small acorn squashes, halved and seeded
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp fresh sage, finely chopped
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- ½ cup pomegranate seeds
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Place the squash halves cut‑side up on a baking sheet.
2. In a small bowl, whisk together maple syrup, chopped sage, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Brush the mixture generously over the flesh of each squash half.
3. Roast the squash for 35‑40 minutes, or until the flesh is tender and caramelized at the edges.
4. While the squash roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Fluff with a fork and season with a pinch of salt.
5. Remove the squash from the oven and let cool slightly. Using a spoon, gently scoop out some of the flesh, leaving a border to keep the shape, and mix the scooped squash into the cooked quinoa.
6. Spoon the quinoa‑squash mixture back into the roasted squash shells, dividing evenly.
7. Top each filled squash with pomegranate seeds and toasted pumpkin seeds for crunch and a burst of color.
8. Serve warm, drizzled with any remaining maple‑sage glaze from the baking sheet. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Sage Roasted Acorn Squash with Quinoa and Pomegranate

text:
Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Parsnip and Quinoa Bowl with Pomegranate  

Ingredients:
- 2 large parsnips, peeled and cut into ½‑inch cubes  
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed  
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth  
- 2 Tbsp olive oil  
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon  
- ½ tsp ground cumin  
- ½ tsp smoked paprika  
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste  
- ¼ cup toasted hazelnuts, roughly chopped  
- ½ cup fresh pomegranate seeds  
- 2 Tbsp fresh parsley, finely chopped  
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice  

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cubed parsnips with olive oil, cinnamon, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the seasoned parsnips on a parchment‑lined baking sheet in a single layer. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.  
4. While the parsnips roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.  
5. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large serving bowl. Add the roasted parsnips, toasted hazelnuts, pomegranate seeds, and chopped parsley.  
6. Drizzle lemon juice over the bowl, season with additional salt and pepper if needed, and toss gently to combine.  
7. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with a few extra pomegranate seeds and hazelnuts for crunch.
title: Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Parsnip and Quinoa Bowl with Pomegranate

text:
Spiced Cardamom Chickpea and Sweet Potato Skillet

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed  
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced  
- 1 small red onion, diced  
- 2 cloves garlic, minced  
- 1 tsp ground cardamom  
- 1 tsp ground cumin  
- ½ tsp smoked paprika  
- 2 tbsp olive oil  
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste  
- 2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped  
- Juice of 1 lime  

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté 3–4 minutes until softened.  
2. Stir in the minced garlic and cook another 30 seconds until fragrant.  
3. Add the sweet potato cubes, sprinkle with the ground cardamom, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat evenly.  
4. Cover the skillet and cook 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sweet potatoes are just tender.  
5. Add the chickpeas to the pan, stir, and continue cooking uncovered for 5 minutes, allowing the chickpeas to brown slightly and the flavors to meld.  
6. Remove from heat, drizzle the lime juice over the skillet, and sprinkle the chopped cilantro on top.  
7. Serve hot, either as a standalone main dish or over cooked quinoa, rice, or warm flatbread.
title: Spiced Cardamom Chickpea and Sweet Potato Skillet

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa‑Stuffed Eggplant Boats

Ingredients:
- 2 medium eggplants
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- 2 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tbsp coconut oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 2 cups fresh spinach, chopped
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- ½ tsp chili flakes
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Slice each eggplant in half lengthwise and scoop out a shallow cavity, leaving about ¼‑inch of flesh around the edges.
2. Place the eggplant halves on a baking sheet, brush the exposed flesh with 1 tbsp coconut oil, and season with salt and pepper. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, until tender.
3. While the eggplants roast, combine quinoa and coconut milk in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
4. In a skillet over medium heat, add the remaining 1 tbsp coconut oil. Sauté garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then add the diced red bell pepper. Cook 3‑4 minutes until softened.
5. Stir in the chopped spinach and cook until wilted, about 2 minutes. Remove from heat.
6. In a large bowl, mix the cooked quinoa, sautéed vegetables, lime juice, maple syrup, chili flakes, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Adjust seasoning to taste.
7. Spoon the quinoa mixture into the roasted eggplant cavities, dividing evenly among the halves.
8. Return the stuffed eggplants to the oven and bake for an additional 10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.
9. Remove from the oven, garnish with fresh cilantro, and serve hot. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa‑Stuffed Eggplant Boats

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Shrimp and Avocado Quinoa Bowl

Ingredients:
- 12 oz peeled and deveined shrimp
- 1 cup quinoa
- 2 cups water or low‑sodium broth
- 1 ripe avocado, diced
- 1 lemon (zest and juice)
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, minced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tsp honey or maple syrup
- 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes
- Salt and pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro, chopped (optional)

Instructions:
1. Rinse the quinoa under cold water. In a saucepan combine quinoa and water (or broth), bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
2. In a small bowl whisk together lemon juice, lemon zest, minced ginger, garlic, soy sauce, honey, red pepper flakes, and a pinch of salt.  
3. Pat the shrimp dry and season lightly with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the shrimp and cook 2‑3 minutes per side, until pink and opaque. Transfer shrimp to a plate.  
4. Reduce the skillet to medium heat, pour the lemon‑ginger sauce in, and simmer 1‑2 minutes until it thickens slightly.  
5. Return the shrimp to the skillet, tossing to coat them in the sauce. Remove from heat.  
6. To assemble, divide the cooked quinoa among bowls, top with the glazed shrimp, diced avocado, and a drizzle of any remaining sauce. Garnish with chopped cilantro and an extra squeeze of lemon if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Shrimp and Avocado Quinoa Bowl

text:
Spiced Orange‑Maple Quinoa & Roasted Beet Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 medium beets, peeled and cubed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon orange zest
- 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/4 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 cups baby arugula
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the cubed beets with olive oil, salt, and pepper, spread them on a baking sheet, and roast for 25‑30 minutes, until tender and caramelized.
2. While the beets roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together orange zest, maple syrup, cumin, smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt to create the dressing.
4. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl. Add the roasted beets, arugula, and toasted pumpkin seeds.
5. Drizzle the orange‑maple dressing over the salad and toss gently to combine, ensuring everything is evenly coated.
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a splash of maple syrup if desired.
7. Serve the salad warm or at room temperature, garnished with extra pumpkin seeds and a light drizzle of the remaining dressing if desired. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Orange‑Maple Quinoa & Roasted Beet Salad

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Power Bowl

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 cups kale, stems removed and torn
- 1 ripe avocado, sliced
- 2 Tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes and chickpeas with olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway through, until the sweet potatoes are tender and caramelized.  
4. While the vegetables roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.  
5. In a skillet over medium heat, add a splash of olive oil and sauté the kale for 3‑4 minutes until wilted; season with a pinch of salt.  
6. Assemble the bowls: divide the cooked quinoa among four serving bowls, top with roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas, sautéed kale, avocado slices, and a sprinkle of toasted pumpkin seeds.  
7. Drizzle each bowl with fresh lemon juice, adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if desired, and serve warm.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Power Bowl

text:
Sage‑Infused Sweet Potato and Chickpea Curry

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 can (13.5 oz) coconut milk
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 in piece fresh ginger, grated
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp ground cumin
- 1 tbsp ground coriander
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp dried sage (or 2 tbsp fresh sage, chopped)
- ½ tsp chili flakes (adjust to taste)
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4–5 minutes.  
2. Stir in the minced garlic, grated ginger, cumin, coriander, turmeric, dried sage, and chili flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
3. Add the cubed sweet potatoes to the pot, tossing to coat them with the spice mixture.  
4. Pour in the coconut milk and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15–20 minutes, or until the sweet potatoes are tender.  
5. Stir in the chickpeas and lime juice. Simmer for an additional 5 minutes to heat the chickpeas through and allow the flavors to meld.  
6. Taste and season with salt and pepper as needed.  
7. Ladle the curry into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve hot with rice, quinoa, or warm naan.
title: Sage‑Infused Sweet Potato and Chickpea Curry

text:
Honey‑Lime Roasted Cauliflower and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 large head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 2 tablespoons honey
- 1 lime, zest and juice
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- ¼ teaspoon sea salt
- ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together olive oil, honey, lime zest, lime juice, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper.  
3. Add the cauliflower florets to the bowl and toss until evenly coated. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast the cauliflower for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway through, until golden‑brown and tender.  
5. While the cauliflower roasts, combine quinoa and 2 cups water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside to cool slightly.  
6. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted cauliflower, chopped cilantro, and toasted pumpkin seeds.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with extra lime juice or a pinch more salt if needed.  
8. Serve warm or at room temperature, drizzled with any remaining pan juices for extra flavor. Enjoy!
title: Honey‑Lime Roasted Cauliflower and Quinoa Salad

text:
Saffron‑Infused Coconut Lentil and Spinach Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 medium onion, finely diced
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon ground coriander
- ¼ teaspoon saffron threads, steeped in 2 tbsp warm water
- 1 can (14 oz) full‑fat coconut milk
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 4 cups fresh baby spinach
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Juice of 1/2 lemon

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4–5 minutes.
2. Stir in the minced garlic, cumin, and coriander; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add the rinsed red lentils, coconut milk, vegetable broth, and the saffron infusion (including the threads). Bring to a gentle boil.
4. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15–20 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and the stew has thickened, stirring occasionally.
5. Season the stew with salt, pepper, and lemon juice. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
6. Add the fresh spinach in batches, stirring until wilted, about 2–3 minutes.
7. Remove from heat and let the stew rest for 2 minutes to meld flavors.
8. Serve hot, garnished with a drizzle of coconut milk or a sprinkle of toasted pumpkin seeds if desired.
title: Saffron‑Infused Coconut Lentil and Spinach Stew

text:
Maple‑Basil Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and sliced into 1/4‑inch rounds
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp fresh basil, finely chopped
- 1 tsp sea salt
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 1/4 tsp ground cumin
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp lemon juice
- 1 Tbsp apple cider vinegar
- 1 clove garlic, minced

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the carrot rounds with olive oil, maple syrup, salt, pepper, and cumin. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until caramelized and tender.  
3. While the carrots roast, combine the quinoa and 2 cups water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook 15 minutes or until the water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.  
4. In a small jar or bowl, whisk together lemon juice, apple cider vinegar, minced garlic, and a pinch of salt to create the dressing.  
5. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted carrots, chopped basil, and toasted pumpkin seeds. Drizzle the dressing over the mixture and toss gently to coat evenly.  
6. Serve the salad warm or at room temperature, garnished with extra basil leaves if desired.
title: Maple‑Basil Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea and Sweet Potato Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, minced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- Zest of 1 lemon
- Juice of 1 lemon
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 2 tbsp pumpkin seeds, toasted (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, turmeric, cumin, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.  
3. In a skillet over medium heat, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil. Add minced garlic and ginger; sauté 1‑2 minutes until fragrant. Add the chickpeas, lemon zest, and a pinch of salt; cook, stirring occasionally, for 5‑6 minutes until the chickpeas are warmed and slightly crisp.  
4. In a small bowl, whisk together lemon juice, 1 tbsp olive oil, and a dash of pepper to make a quick dressing.  
5. Assemble the bowls: start with a base of quinoa, top with roasted sweet potatoes, then the ginger‑garlic chickpeas. Drizzle the lemon dressing over everything.  
6. Garnish each bowl with chopped cilantro and toasted pumpkin seeds, if using. Serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea and Sweet Potato Bowl

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Sesame‑Brown Butter Broccoli

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 large head broccoli, cut into florets
- 2 tbsp sesame oil
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tbsp low‑sodium soy sauce
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tsp lemon juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds (optional, for garnish)
- 2 green onions, sliced (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa and water (or broth); bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
2. While the quinoa cooks, heat 1 tbsp sesame oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the tofu cubes and sauté 6‑8 minutes, turning once, until golden brown on all sides. Remove tofu and set aside.  
3. In the same skillet, add the remaining 1 tbsp sesame oil and the broccoli florets. Stir‑fry 4‑5 minutes until bright green and just tender.  
4. Reduce heat to medium and add the butter. Once melted, stir in the minced garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
