5. Whisk together maple syrup, soy sauce, and lemon juice; pour over the broccoli‑butter mixture. Toss to coat and cook 1‑2 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.  
6. Return the tofu to the skillet, mixing gently to combine with the glazed broccoli. Season with salt and pepper to taste; heat for another minute to re‑warm the tofu.  
7. Serve the maple‑glazed tofu and sesame‑brown butter broccoli over the cooked quinoa. Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds and sliced green onions, if desired. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Sesame‑Brown Butter Broccoli

text:
Saffron‑Infused Coconut Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup water
- 1/4 teaspoon saffron threads
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, combine the saffron threads with the coconut milk and let steep for 5 minutes to release color and flavor.  
2. While the saffron infuses, heat a saucepan over medium heat, add the quinoa, and toast for 2
title: Saffron‑Infused Coconut Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Lentil Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 1/2 teaspoon saffron threads
- 2 tablespoons hot water
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 small onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 ½ cups vegetable broth
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, chopped
- ¼ cup toasted sliced almonds (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the carrot cubes with 1 tablespoon olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway, until caramelized and tender.  
2. While the carrots roast, place the saffron threads in a small bowl, add the hot water, and let steep for 5 minutes.  
3. In a medium saucepan, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté 4‑5 minutes until translucent. Stir in the minced garlic and cumin; cook 1 minute more.  
4. Add the rinsed lentils to the saucepan, stirring to coat them with the aromatics. Pour in the vegetable broth and the saffron infusion (including the threads). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and most liquid is absorbed.  
5. Remove the saucepan from heat. Gently fold the roasted carrots into the lentil mixture. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste.  
6. Transfer the pilaf to a serving bowl, sprinkle with chopped parsley and toasted sliced almonds if using, and serve warm.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Lentil Pilaf

text:
Miso‑Brown Butter Ramen with Crispy Tofu and Bok Choy

Ingredients:
- 200 g fresh ramen noodles
- 1 block (300 g) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 cups bok choy, stems sliced thin, leaves separated
- 2 tablespoons white miso paste
- 2 tablespoons unsalted butter
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger
- 2 tablespoons soy sauce
- 1 tablespoon sesame oil
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 teaspoon chili flakes (optional)
- 2 green onions, sliced
- 1 soft‑boiled egg, halved (optional)
- 1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons water (slurry)

Instructions:
1. In a skillet over medium heat, add 1 tablespoon butter and the cubed tofu; fry until golden and crispy on all sides, about 6‑8 minutes. Transfer to a plate and set aside.
2. In the same skillet, add the remaining butter, minced garlic, and grated ginger; sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
3. Stir in the miso paste, soy sauce, and sesame oil, cooking for another minute to combine.
4. Pour in the vegetable broth and bring to a gentle boil; add the chili flakes if using.
5. Add the ramen noodles and cook according to package instructions, usually 3‑4 minutes, until just tender.
6. While the noodles cook, stir in the cornstarch slurry to thicken the broth slightly; simmer for 1 minute.
7. Add the bok choy stems first, cook 1 minute, then add the leaves and cook until wilted, about 1‑2 minutes.
8. Divide the ramen and broth into bowls; top each with crispy tofu, sliced green onions, and the soft‑boiled egg if desired.
9. Serve immediately, enjoying the rich miso‑brown butter broth with the crisp tofu and fresh bok choy.
title: Miso‑Brown Butter Ramen with Crispy Tofu and Bok Choy

text:
Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Black Bean Chili

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 2 (15‑oz) cans black beans, drained and rinsed
- 1 onion, finely chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp chili powder
- 1 Tbsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 (14‑oz) can diced tomatoes
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 lime, juiced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 Tbsp olive oil

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes.
2. Stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin, and smoked paprika; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add the diced sweet potatoes and maple syrup, tossing to coat the potatoes evenly with the spices and syrup.
4. Pour in the diced tomatoes and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer.
5. Cover and let the chili simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the sweet potatoes are tender.
6. Stir in the black beans and lime juice; continue to simmer for another 5 minutes to heat the beans through.
7. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Adjust the heat with additional chili powder if desired.
8. Ladle the chili into bowls and garnish with fresh cilantro. Serve with optional toppings such as avocado slices, sour cream, or extra drizzle of maple syrup.
title: Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Black Bean Chili

text:
Citrus‑Glazed Tempeh with Herbed Quinoa and Roasted Carrots

Ingredients:
- 8 oz (225 g) tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 2 tbsp orange juice
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp olive oil (for tempeh)
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth or water
- 1 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- 1 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- Zest of 1 orange
- 3 medium carrots, peeled and cut into ¼‑inch sticks
- 1 tbsp olive oil (for carrots)
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a small bowl, whisk together orange juice, lime juice, maple syrup, soy sauce, grated ginger, and minced garlic. Set aside.
3. Toss the carrot sticks with 1 tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.
4. While the carrots roast, heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the tempeh strips and sear for 2‑3 minutes per side, until golden brown.
5. Pour the citrus glaze over the tempeh, reduce heat to medium, and cook, stirring occasionally, for another 3‑4 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the tempeh. Remove from heat and set aside.
6. Meanwhile, combine rinsed quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes.
7. Fluff the quinoa with a fork and stir in chopped parsley, cilantro, orange zest, and a pinch of salt and pepper.
8. To serve, divide the herbed quinoa among plates, top with the citrus‑glazed tempeh, and arrange the roasted carrots on the side. Garnish with extra fresh herbs or a drizzle of the remaining glaze if desired. Enjoy!
title: Citrus‑Glazed Tempeh with Herbed Quinoa and Roasted Carrots

text:
Cinnamon‑Lime Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Salad

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch sticks
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 Tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 Tbsp maple syrup
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 2 cups mixed baby greens
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- Optional: crumbled feta cheese for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the carrot sticks and chickpeas with olive oil, cinnamon, lime zest, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the carrots are tender and lightly caramelized and the chickpeas are crisp.  
5. While the vegetables roast, whisk together lime juice and maple syrup in a small bowl to create the dressing.  
6. In a serving platter, arrange the mixed baby greens. Top with the warm roasted carrots and chickpeas.  
7. Drizzle the lime‑maple dressing over the salad, then sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds and, if desired, crumbled feta cheese.  
8. Serve immediately, while the carrots are still warm, for a delightful contrast of sweet, spicy, and tangy flavors.
title: Cinnamon‑Lime Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Salad

text:
Orange‑Ginger Quinoa with Charred Broccoli and Toasted Almonds

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 large head broccoli, cut into florets
- 1 tablespoon olive oil (for broccoli)
- 1 tablespoon olive oil (for quinoa)
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- Zest of 1 orange
- 2 tablespoons fresh orange juice
- 1/4 cup sliced toasted almonds
- 2 tablespoons dried cranberries (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss broccoli florets with 1 Tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper, then spread on a baking sheet and roast for 15‑20 minutes, turning halfway, until charred at the edges.
2. While the broccoli roasts, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes.
3. Fluff the cooked quinoa with a fork and stir in the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, minced ginger, orange zest, and orange juice. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
4. Transfer the quinoa to a serving bowl. Top with the charred broccoli, toasted almonds, and dried cranberries if using.
5. Serve warm or at room temperature, optionally drizzling a little extra orange juice for brightness. Enjoy!
title: Orange‑Ginger Quinoa with Charred Broccoli and Toasted Almonds

text:
Cinnamon‑Orange Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and cubed
- 1 (15 oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 tsp orange zest
- 1 Tbsp fresh orange juice
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup quinoa
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- Optional: drizzle of tahini for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, combine the sweet potato cubes, chickpeas, olive oil, cinnamon, orange zest, orange juice, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; toss until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 25–30 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until the sweet potatoes are tender and the chickpeas are crisp.  
4. While the vegetables roast, rinse the quinoa under cold water. In a medium saucepan, bring the quinoa and vegetable broth to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the broth is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.  
5. Divide the cooked quinoa among serving bowls. Top each with the roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas.  
6. Sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds and chopped parsley over the bowls. If desired, drizzle with a little tahini before serving. Enjoy warm!
title: Cinnamon‑Orange Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Bowl

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea & Spinach Stir‑Fry

Ingredients:
- 1 cup cooked chickpeas
- 2 cups fresh spinach leaves
- 1 red bell pepper, thinly sliced
- 1 small yellow onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tablespoon maple syrup
- 1 tablespoon soy sauce or tamari
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon chili flakes (optional)
- 2 tablespoons coconut oil
- 1 cup cooked quinoa
- Juice of 1 lemon
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Heat the coconut oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat until shimmering.  
2. Add the diced onion and sauté for 2–3 minutes, until it begins to soften.  
3. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for another 30 seconds, being careful not to burn.  
4. Sprinkle the turmeric, cumin, and chili flakes over the aromatics; stir to coat and release the spices’ fragrance, about 1 minute.  
5. Add the sliced red bell pepper and cook, stirring occasionally, for 3–4 minutes until just tender but still crisp.  
6. Toss in the cooked chickpeas, maple syrup, and soy sauce. Stir well and let the mixture heat through, about 2 minutes, allowing the sauce to glaze the chickpeas.  
7. Fold in the fresh spinach leaves; cook, stirring, until wilted, roughly 1–2 minutes.  
8. Add the cooked quinoa, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Mix everything together until the quinoa is evenly heated and coated with the flavorful sauce.  
9. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a drizzle of maple syrup if desired.  
10. Serve hot, garnished with extra chili flakes or a squeeze of lemon if you like extra brightness. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea & Spinach Stir‑Fry

text:
Sesame‑Miso Glazed Tempeh with Coconut‑Lime Rice  

Ingredients:
- 8 oz (225 g) tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips  
- 2 Tbsp white miso paste  
- 1 Tbsp sesame oil  
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce or tamari  
- 1 Tbsp maple syrup  
- 1 tsp freshly grated ginger  
- 1 clove garlic, minced  
- 1 cup jasmine rice  
- 1 cup coconut milk  
- 1 cup water  
- Zest of 1 lime  
- Juice of 1 lime  
- 2 Tbsp toasted sesame seeds  
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro (optional)  

Instructions:
1. Rinse the jasmine rice under cold water until the water runs clear.  
2. In a medium saucepan combine the rice, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until tender. Remove from heat and stir in lime zest and juice; keep covered.  
3. While the rice cooks, whisk together miso, sesame oil, soy sauce, maple syrup, ginger, and garlic in a shallow bowl to form the glaze.  
4. Place the tempeh strips in the glaze, tossing to coat evenly. Let marinate for 5 minutes.  
5. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the glazed tempeh and cook 3‑4 minutes per side, or until golden and caramelized. Transfer to a plate.  
6. Fluff the coconut‑lime rice with a fork and divide it among serving bowls.  
7. Top each bowl of rice with the sesame‑miso tempeh strips. Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds over the top.  
8. Garnish with chopped cilantro, if desired, and serve immediately.
title: Sesame‑Miso Glazed Tempeh with Coconut‑Lime Rice

text:
Miso‑Glazed Sea Bass with Sesame‑Ginger Bok Choy

Ingredients:
- 4 sea bass fillets (about 6 oz each)
- 2 Tbsp white miso paste
- 1 Tbsp honey
- 1 Tbsp low‑sodium soy sauce
- 1 tsp rice vinegar
- 1 tsp freshly grated ginger
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 Tbsp sesame oil, divided
- 4 cups baby bok choy, halved lengthwise
- 1 Tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- 2 green onions, thinly sliced
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- Freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, whisk together miso paste, honey, soy sauce, rice vinegar, grated ginger, minced garlic, and ½ Tbsp sesame oil to form the glaze.  
2. Pat the sea bass fillets dry with paper towels, season lightly with black pepper, and brush each fillet generously with the miso glaze on both sides.  
3. Heat olive oil in a large non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. When shimmering, add the sea bass fillets skin‑side down and cook 3–4 minutes until the skin is crisp. Flip carefully, brush with any remaining glaze, and cook another 2–3 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily. Transfer to a plate and keep warm.  
4. While the fish cooks, add the remaining ½ Tbsp sesame oil to the same skillet. Add the bok choy halves, cut side down, and sauté for 2 minutes. Flip, add a splash of water (about 2 Tbsp), cover, and steam for another 2 minutes until the leaves are tender but still bright green.  
5. Remove the bok choy from the pan, drizzle with a little soy sauce if desired, and arrange on serving plates. Place a glazed sea bass fillet on top of each bok choy nest.  
6. Garnish each serving with toasted sesame seeds, sliced green onions, and an extra drizzle of sesame oil if you like. Serve immediately.
title: Miso‑Glazed Sea Bass with Sesame‑Ginger Bok Choy

text:
Spiced Cardamom Sweet Potato and Quinoa Skillet

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1 small red onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp ground cardamom
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Juice of 1 lime

Instructions:
1. Heat 1 Tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the diced sweet potatoes, season with a pinch of salt, and sauté for 8‑10 minutes until they begin to soften and develop a light golden crust.
2. Add the chopped onion and garlic to the skillet; cook, stirring frequently, for another 3 minutes until the onion becomes translucent.
3. Stir in the ground cardamom, smoked paprika, and cayenne (if using); toast the spices for 30 seconds to release their aroma.
4. Add the quinoa, diced red bell pepper, and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the quinoa is fluffy and the liquid is absorbed.
5. Once cooked, remove the skillet from heat. Fluff the quinoa‑sweet‑potato mixture with a fork, then stir in the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, lime juice, and chopped cilantro. Adjust seasoning with salt and black pepper to taste.
6. Serve hot, garnished with extra cilantro or a drizzle of lime juice if desired. Enjoy as a hearty main dish or a satisfying side.
title: Spiced Cardamom Sweet Potato and Quinoa Skillet

text:
Garlic‑Rosemary Roasted Eggplant and Lentil Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 1 cup green lentils, rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp fresh rosemary, finely chopped
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup quinoa
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1/4 cup pine nuts, toasted
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the eggplant cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, minced garlic, rosemary, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the seasoned eggplant in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway through, until golden and tender.  
4. While the eggplant roasts, combine lentils and 2 cups vegetable broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer, uncovered, for 20‑25 minutes or until lentils are tender but not mushy. Drain any excess liquid and set aside.  
5. Rinse quinoa under cold water. In a separate pot, bring quinoa and 2 cups water (or broth) to a boil, then cover and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.  
6. In a small skillet over medium heat, toast pine nuts with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, stirring frequently, until lightly browned and fragrant, about 3 minutes. Remove from heat.  
7. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted eggplant, lentils, toasted pine nuts, lemon juice, and chopped parsley. Toss gently to mix; adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if desired.  
8. Serve the bowl warm or at room temperature, garnished with extra parsley or a drizzle of olive oil if desired. Enjoy!
title: Garlic‑Rosemary Roasted Eggplant and Lentil Bowl

text:
Spiced Apricot Glazed Salmon with Herb Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 4 salmon fillets (6 oz each)
- 1/2 cup apricot preserves
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp Dijon mustard
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups low‑sodium vegetable broth
- 1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped
- 2 tbsp fresh mint, chopped
- Zest of 1 lemon
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, whisk together apricot preserves, soy sauce, Dijon mustard, smoked paprika, cumin, cayenne (if using), and 1 tablespoon olive oil to form the glaze.  
2. Pat salmon fillets dry, season with salt and pepper, and place them on a parchment‑lined baking sheet.  
3. Brush the apricot glaze generously over the salmon, reserving a tablespoon for finishing.  
4. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and bake the salmon for 12‑15 minutes, or until the flesh flakes easily with a fork.  
5. While the salmon cooks, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the rinsed quinoa and toast for 2 minutes, stirring frequently.  
6. Add vegetable broth, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy.  
7. Remove the quinoa from heat, stir in chopped parsley, mint, lemon zest, and season with salt and pepper to taste.  
8. Drizzle the reserved apricot glaze over the baked salmon, serve each fillet atop a bed of herb quinoa, and garnish with extra fresh herbs if desired.
title: Spiced Apricot Glazed Salmon with Herb Quinoa

text:
Cinnamon‑Spiced Apple and Quinoa Breakfast Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 1 large apple, diced
- 1 tablespoon coconut oil
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- 2 tablespoons maple syrup
- 1/4 cup chopped walnuts
- 2 tablespoons dried cranberries
- pinch of salt
- 1/4 cup Greek yogurt (optional, for serving)

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan, combine quinoa and water with a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until water is absorbed and quinoa is fluffy.  
2. While quinoa cooks, heat coconut oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add diced apple, sprinkle with cinnamon, and sauté for 5‑6 minutes until softened and lightly caramelized.  
3. Stir maple syrup into the apples and cook another minute, allowing the syrup to glaze the fruit.  
4. Once quinoa is done, fluff with a fork and divide it into two serving bowls.  
5. Top each bowl of quinoa with the cinnamon‑apple mixture, then sprinkle chopped walnuts and dried cranberries over the top.  
6. Add a dollop of Greek yogurt if desired, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Spiced Apple and Quinoa Breakfast Bowl

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Soup

Ingredients:
- 1 lb carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch pieces
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the carrots with 1 tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, cumin, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway, until caramelized and tender.  
2. While the carrots roast, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté for 5 minutes until translucent. Add the garlic and cook another minute.  
3. Add the roasted carrots, chickpeas, and vegetable broth to the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes to let the flavors meld.  
4. Using an immersion blender (or transferring to a countertop blender in batches), puree the soup until smooth but still slightly textured.  
5. Return the soup to the pot, taste, and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a drizzle of maple syrup if desired. Warm through for 2‑3 minutes.  
6. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with chopped fresh parsley, and serve hot. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Soup

text:
Roasted Garlic & Herb Farro with Lemon‑Tahini Dressing

Ingredients:
- 1 cup farro, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 head garlic, cloves separated but unpeeled
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- 1/4 cup tahini
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the garlic cloves with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper, and spread them on a baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes until soft and caramelized.  
2. While the garlic roasts, combine farro and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 20‑25 minutes until the farro is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.  
3. In a small skillet, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add dried oregano and thyme, stirring for 30 seconds until fragrant.  
4. Transfer the cooked farro to a large bowl. Add the toasted herbs, roasted garlic (squeezed out of their skins), and chopped parsley. Toss to combine.  
5. In a separate bowl, whisk together tahini, lemon juice, maple syrup, a pinch of salt, and 2‑3 tablespoons warm water until the dressing is smooth and pourable.  
6. Drizzle the lemon‑tahini dressing over the farro mixture. Toss gently to coat evenly. Adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if needed.  
7. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with extra parsley and a drizzle of olive oil if desired.
title: Roasted Garlic & Herb Farro with Lemon‑Tahini Dressing

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa & Roasted Eggplant Stack

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa
- 2 cups vegetable broth or water
- 1 medium eggplant, sliced into ½‑inch rounds
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp sea salt
- 1 cup canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp coconut aminos (or soy sauce)
- 1 tsp lime zest
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tbsp coconut oil
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- 1 small red onion, thinly sliced
- ½ cup diced red bell pepper
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds (optional)

Instructions:
1. Rinse the quinoa, then combine it with the broth (or water) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until the grains are tender. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
2. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the eggplant rounds with olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, and sea salt. Spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 20 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and soft.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, coconut aminos, lime zest, lime juice, and coconut oil to create a glaze.
4. Heat a skillet over medium heat, add a drizzle of oil, and sauté the chickpeas until lightly crisp, about 5 minutes. Stir in half of the glaze and cook another minute. Transfer to a bowl.
5. In the same skillet, add the sliced red onion and diced bell pepper. Sauté until softened, about 4 minutes. Drizzle with the remaining glaze and toss to coat.
6. To assemble, divide the cooked quinoa among serving bowls. Layer roasted eggplant rounds on top, followed by glazed chickpeas and the sautéed vegetables. Sprinkle with chopped cilantro and toasted pumpkin seeds.
7. Serve warm with extra lime wedges on the side, if desired.
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa & Roasted Eggplant Stack

text:
Spiced Orange‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Soup

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and sliced into 1‑inch pieces
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated
- Zest of 1 orange
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup full‑fat coconut milk
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the carrot pieces with 1 tbsp olive oil, orange zest, 1 tbsp maple syrup, cumin, coriander, smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt. Spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway, until caramelized and tender.  
2. While the carrots roast, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté 5 minutes until translucent.  
3. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook 1 minute until fragrant.  
4. Add the roasted carrots (with any pan juices) and the chickpeas to the pot. Pour in the vegetable broth and bring to a gentle boil. Reduce heat and simmer 10 minutes to let the flavors meld.  
5. Using an immersion blender (or transferring to a countertop blender in batches), puree the soup until smooth but still slightly textured. Return to the pot if needed.  
6. Stir in the coconut milk and the remaining 1 tbsp maple syrup. Warm the soup over low heat; adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste.  
7. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with chopped cilantro, and serve hot. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Orange‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Soup

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 medium beets, peeled and cubed
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
- ½ tsp sea salt, plus more to taste
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- ¼ cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped
- 2 cups arugula
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- ¼ cup crumbled goat cheese (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the beet cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
3. Roast the beets for 25‑30 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until tender and caramelized.  
4. While the beets roast, combine quinoa and 2 cups water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook 15 minutes or until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside to cool slightly.  
5. In a small jar, whisk together the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, lemon juice, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of pepper to make the dressing.  
6. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted beets, arugula, and toasted walnuts. Drizzle with the lemon‑olive dressing and toss gently to coat.  
7. Transfer the salad to serving plates, sprinkle with crumbled goat cheese if using, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Quinoa Salad

text:
Cinnamon‑Infused Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 red onion, thinly sliced
- 3 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 2 Tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes, chickpeas, and red onion with 2 Tbsp olive oil, cinnamon, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the sweet potatoes are tender and lightly caramelized.  
4. Remove from the oven and let cool slightly (about 5 minutes).  
5. Transfer the roasted vegetables and chickpeas to a serving bowl. Drizzle with the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil and lemon juice, then toss gently.  
6. Sprinkle chopped parsley over the top and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Infused Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Salad

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Baked Cod with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 4 cod fillets (about 6 oz each)
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp grated ginger
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp honey
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- ½ cup water
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- 1 tbsp toasted coconut flakes (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together lemon juice, grated ginger, olive oil, honey, salt, and pepper.  
3. Place the cod fillets on the prepared baking sheet and brush each piece generously with the lemon‑ginger mixture.  
4. Bake the cod for 12‑15 minutes, or until the fish flakes easily with a fork.  
5. While the cod cooks, combine quinoa, coconut milk, water, and lime zest in a medium saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is tender.  
6. Remove the quinoa from heat and fluff with a fork; stir in chopped cilantro.  
7. Plate each cod fillet atop a mound of coconut‑lime quinoa.  
8. If desired, sprinkle toasted coconut flakes over the top for extra texture and a hint of tropical flavor.  
9. Serve immediately, garnished with additional cilantro or a wedge of lemon.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Baked Cod with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Tacos

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled into thin ribbons
- 1 (15 oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 8 small corn tortillas
- 1 avocado, sliced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 lime, cut into wedges
- Salt and black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, combine the carrot ribbons, chickpeas, olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, cumin, cayenne (if using), salt, and pepper. Toss until everything is evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20–25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the carrots are tender and the chickpeas are crisp‑golden.  
4. While the vegetables roast, warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 30 seconds per side, or microwave them covered with a damp paper towel for 20 seconds.  
5. To assemble each taco, place a generous spoonful of the roasted carrots and chickpeas onto a tortilla, then top with avocado slices and a sprinkle of chopped cilantro.  
6. Serve the tacos with lime wedges on the side and drizzle extra maple syrup over the top if desired. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Tacos

text:
Spiced Orange‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Soup

Ingredients:
- 2 lb carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch pieces
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 large onion, diced
- 3 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp orange zest
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp ground cinnamon
- ¼ tsp ground cardamom
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Orange wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the carrot pieces with 1 tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, orange zest, cumin, smoked paprika, cinnamon, cardamom, and a pinch of salt. Spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway, until caramelized and tender.  
2. While the carrots roast, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 5 minutes until translucent.  
3. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly to avoid burning.  
4. Add the roasted carrots and chickpeas to the pot, then pour in the vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes to let the flavors meld.  
5. Using an immersion blender (or transferring in batches to a countertop blender), puree the soup until smooth but still slightly textured. Return to the pot if needed.  
6. Stir in the coconut milk and the remaining 1 tbsp maple syrup. Heat gently for 3‑4 minutes; do not let it boil. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste.  
7. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve with an orange wedge on the side for an extra burst of citrus. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Orange‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Soup

text:
Sesame‑Lime Glazed Tempeh with Turmeric Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 2 tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp sesame oil
- 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups water or vegetable broth
- ½ tsp ground turmeric
- ¼ tsp ground cumin
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 cup frozen peas, thawed
- ½ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Optional: sliced green onions for garnish

Instructions:
1. In a shallow bowl, whisk together soy sauce, lime juice, maple syrup, sesame oil, grated ginger, and minced garlic to create the glaze.  
2. Add the tempeh strips, toss to coat, and let marinate for 10‑15 minutes while you prepare the quinoa.  
3. In a medium saucepan, combine rinsed quinoa, water (or broth), turmeric, and cumin. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed.  
4. Remove the quinoa from heat, fluff with a fork, stir in olive oil, peas, and season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.  
5. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Remove tempeh from the glaze (reserve the glaze) and sear the strips 3‑4 minutes per side, until golden brown.  
6. Pour the reserved glaze
title: Sesame‑Lime Glazed Tempeh with Turmeric Quinoa

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Garlic Broccoli and Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 cups broccoli florets
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 tbsp low‑sodium soy sauce
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, olive oil, minced garlic, lemon juice, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.  
3. Add the cubed tofu to the bowl and toss gently to coat; let it marinate while you prepare the broccoli.  
4. Spread the broccoli florets on the prepared baking sheet, drizzle with a little olive oil, and season with salt and pepper.  
5. Place the marinated tofu cubes on the same sheet, arranging them in a single layer.  
6. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning the tofu and broccoli halfway through, until the broccoli is tender‑crisp and the tofu is golden and caramelized.  
7. While the tofu and broccoli roast, bring 2 cups water to a boil in a medium saucepan. Add the rinsed quinoa, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the water is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.  
8. Transfer the roasted tofu and broccoli to a serving bowl, add the cooked quinoa, and gently toss to combine.  
9. Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds over the top, if using, and serve warm.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Garlic Broccoli and Quinoa

text:
Maple‑Glazed Roasted Brussels Sprouts with Quinoa and Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 1 lb Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 Tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together olive oil, maple syrup, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper.  
3. Add the halved Brussels sprouts to the bowl and toss until evenly coated. Spread them cut‑side down on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until the sprouts are caramelized and tender.  
5. While the sprouts roast, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.  
6. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl. Add lemon juice, a pinch of salt, and the chopped parsley; toss to combine.  
7. Once the Brussels sprouts are done, transfer them to the bowl with quinoa. Gently fold in the pomegranate seeds and toasted pumpkin seeds.  
8. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if desired.  
9. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with extra pomegranate seeds and parsley if desired.
title: Maple‑Glazed Roasted Brussels Sprouts with Quinoa and Pomegranate

text:
Citrus‑Infused Quinoa with Charred Broccolini and Toasted Almonds

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups low‑sodium vegetable broth
- 1 bunch broccolini, trimmed into 2‑inch pieces
- 2 tablespoons olive oil, divided
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
- ¼ cup sliced almonds, toasted
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine the rinsed quinoa and vegetable broth; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and stir in the lemon zest, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Set aside.  
2. While the quinoa cooks, preheat a grill pan or large skillet over medium‑high heat. Toss the broccolini with 1  tablespoon of olive oil, the minced garlic, and a generous pinch of salt and pepper.  
3. Place the broccolini on the hot grill pan, cut side down, and cook for 3‑4 minutes until charred and tender‑crisp, turning once. Transfer to a serving bowl.  
4. In the same pan, add the remaining 1  tablespoon of olive oil and toast the sliced almonds over medium heat, stirring frequently, until golden and fragrant, about 2 minutes. Remove from heat.  
5. To assemble, spoon the citrus‑infused quinoa onto plates, top with the charred broccolini, and sprinkle the toasted almonds over the top. Adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if desired. Serve warm.
title: Citrus‑Infused Quinoa with Charred Broccolini and Toasted Almonds

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea & Spinach Pasta

Ingredients:
- 12 oz whole‑wheat spaghetti
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 4 cups fresh baby spinach
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tbsp lemon juice
- ½ cup low‑sodium vegetable broth
- ¼ tsp red‑pepper flakes (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Grated Parmesan cheese, for serving (optional)

Instructions:
1. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti according to package directions until al dente; reserve ½ cup of the cooking water, then drain the pasta.  
2. While the pasta cooks, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger, sautéing for 30 seconds until fragrant.  
3. Stir in the ground turmeric and red‑pepper flakes, cooking for another 20 seconds to toast the spices.  
4. Add the chickpeas to the skillet and toss to coat with the aromatics; cook for 2‑3 minutes until the chickpeas are warmed through.  
5. Pour in the vegetable broth, lemon zest, and lemon juice, stirring to combine. Let the mixture simmer for 2 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken slightly.  
6. Add the fresh spinach and cook, stirring, until wilted, about 1‑2 minutes. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.  
7. Transfer the cooked spaghetti to the skillet, adding the reserved pasta water a little at a time to achieve a silky coating. Toss everything together until the pasta is evenly coated with the lemon‑ginger turmeric sauce.  
8. Remove from heat, plate the pasta, and sprinkle with grated Parmesan cheese if desired. Serve immediately, garnished with an extra pinch of lemon zest.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea & Spinach Pasta

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Shrimp and Pineapple Quinoa Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- 1 ½ cups water
- 1 cup fresh pineapple, diced
- 1 red bell pepper, thinly sliced
- 2  tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1  tbsp lime zest
- 2  tsp coconut oil
- 2  garlic cloves, minced
- 1  tsp fresh ginger, grated
- ½  tsp chili flakes
- ¼  tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼  cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1  tbsp toasted coconut flakes (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine the quinoa, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
2. While the quinoa cooks, heat the coconut oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger; sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.  
3. Add the shrimp to the skillet, sprinkle with chili flakes, cumin, salt, and pepper. Cook for 2‑3 minutes per side, or until the shrimp turn pink and opaque. Remove the shrimp and set aside.  
4. In the same skillet, add the sliced red bell pepper and cook for 2 minutes, stirring occasionally, until just softened.  
5. Return the shrimp to the pan, stir in the lime juice, lime zest, and diced pineapple. Cook for an additional minute to heat the pineapple through and allow the flavors to meld.  
6. Assemble the bowls: divide the coconut‑cooked quinoa among four serving bowls, top with the shrimp‑pineapple mixture, and scatter chopped cilantro over each. If desired, garnish with toasted coconut flakes for extra crunch.  
7. Serve immediately, adjusting seasoning with extra lime juice or salt if needed. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Shrimp and Pineapple Quinoa Bowl

text:
Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Eggplant and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- ¼ cup dried cranberries
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). In a large bowl, toss the eggplant cubes with olive oil, cinnamon, smoked paprika, cumin, maple syrup, salt, and pepper until evenly coated. Spread the eggplant on a parchment‑lined baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.  
2. While the eggplant roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the quinoa is fluffy and the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.  
3. In a large mixing bowl, combine the roasted eggplant, cooked quinoa, toasted pumpkin seeds, and dried cranberries. Drizzle with fresh lemon juice and toss gently to distribute the flavors.  
4. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice as desired.  
5. Serve the salad warm or at room temperature, garnished with chopped fresh parsley if desired. Enjoy as a hearty main dish or a vibrant side.
title: Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Eggplant and Quinoa Salad

text:
Garlic‑Lime Roasted Broccoli Quinoa Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 large head broccoli, cut into florets
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the broccoli florets with olive oil, minced garlic, lime zest, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the broccoli on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until crisp‑tender and lightly browned.  
4. While the broccoli roasts, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.  
5. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl. Add the roasted broccoli, lime juice, and toasted pumpkin seeds. Toss gently to combine.  
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired.  
7. Serve warm, garnished with chopped cilantro if using. Enjoy as a hearty main dish or a satisfying side.
title: Garlic‑Lime Roasted Broccoli Quinoa Bowl

text:
Herb‑Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Grain Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup farro, rinsed
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1 teaspoon dried thyme
- ½ teaspoon garlic powder
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 cups baby spinach
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tablespoons lemon‑tahini dressing (store‑bought or homemade)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the sweet potato cubes and chickpeas with olive oil, smoked paprika, dried thyme, garlic powder, salt, and pepper; spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
3. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the sweet potatoes are tender and the chickpeas are crisp and golden.  
4. Meanwhile, cook the farro in a pot of salted boiling water according to package directions (usually 20‑25 minutes), then drain and set aside.  
5. In a large bowl combine the cooked farro, roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas, fresh baby spinach, and toasted pumpkin seeds; toss gently.  
6. Drizzle the lemon‑tahini dressing over the bowl, give a final toss, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Herb‑Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Grain Bowl

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa with Roasted Chickpea and Kale Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 3 cups kale leaves, stems removed and torn
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, finely grated
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Toss the chickpeas with 1 tbsp olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking halfway, until crisp and golden.
2. While the chickpeas roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
3. In a large bowl, whisk together the remaining olive oil, grated ginger, lemon zest, lemon juice, minced garlic, and a pinch of salt and pepper to make the dressing.
4. Add the warm quinoa to the bowl, toss with the dressing, then fold in the kale leaves. Let the mixture sit for 2‑3 minutes so the kale wilts slightly.
5. Top the quinoa‑kale salad with the roasted chickpeas and sprinkle toasted sesame seeds, if using. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa with Roasted Chickpea and Kale Salad

text:
Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 Tbsp fresh thyme leaves (or 1 tsp dried)
- Zest of 1 lemon
- Juice of 1 lemon
- 1 avocado, sliced
- ½ red onion, thinly sliced
- 2 Tbsp tahini
- 1 Tbsp maple syrup
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Toss the sweet potato cubes and chickpeas with 1 Tbsp olive oil, thyme, lemon zest, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet.
2. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until sweet potatoes are tender and chickpeas are crisp.
3. Meanwhile, cook the quinoa: combine quinoa and 2 cups water in a saucepan, bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
4. In a small bowl, whisk together tahini, maple syrup, lemon juice, remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and enough water (about 2 Tbsp) to reach a drizzling consistency.
5. Assemble the bowls: divide quinoa among four serving bowls, top with roasted chickpeas and sweet potatoes, sliced avocado, and red onion.
6. Drizzle the lemon‑tahini dressing over each bowl, garnish with extra thyme leaves if desired, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Buddha Bowl

text:
Maple‑Glazed Eggplant and Lentil Tacos

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 ½ cups cooked green or brown lentils (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp ground black pepper
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 8 small corn or flour tortillas
- ½ cup diced red onion
- ½ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- 1 avocado, sliced
- 1 lime, cut into wedges
- Optional: hot sauce or sliced jalapeños for heat

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cubed eggplant with 1 Tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, and black pepper until evenly coated. Spread the eggplant in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender.  
3. While the eggplant roasts, combine the maple syrup, soy sauce, and the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil in a small bowl.  
4. In a skillet over medium heat, add the cooked lentils and the maple‑soy mixture. Stir and cook for 3‑4 minutes, allowing the lentils to absorb the glaze and become slightly caramelized.  
5. When the eggplant is done, transfer it to the skillet with the glazed lentils. Toss gently to combine and heat through, about 2 minutes.  
6. Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet or microwave for 30 seconds.  
7. To assemble each taco, place a generous spoonful of the maple‑glazed eggplant‑lentil mixture onto a tortilla. Top with diced red onion, cilantro, avocado slices, and a squeeze of lime juice. Add hot sauce or jalapeños if desired.  
8. Serve immediately and enjoy the sweet‑savory flavor of the maple‑glazed eggplant paired with hearty lentils.
title: Maple‑Glazed Eggplant and Lentil Tacos

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Tagine

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch chunks
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 ½ × 15‑oz cans, drained and rinsed)
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- ½ teaspoon saffron threads, steeped in 2 Tbsp hot water
- 1 ½ cups vegetable broth
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- ½ tsp ground cinnamon
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- ¼ cup dried apricots, chopped
- 2 Tbsp toasted almond slices
- 2 Tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the carrot chunks with 1 Tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
2. While the carrots roast, heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 4‑5 minutes, until translucent.  
3. Stir in the minced garlic, cumin, coriander, and cinnamon; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
4. Add the cooked chickpeas, roasted carrots, chopped apricots, and the saffron infusion (including the threads). Mix well to combine.  
5. Pour in the vegetable broth, bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, and let it cook uncovered for 10‑12 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken slightly.  
6. Season with salt, pepper, and lemon juice; adjust seasoning to taste.  
7. Transfer the tagine to a serving dish, garnish with toasted almond slices and fresh cilantro. Serve hot with couscous, quinoa, or crusty bread.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Tagine

text:
Spiced Ginger Pumpkin and Black Bean Chili

Ingredients:
- 1 lb (450 g) ground turkey or plant‑based crumble
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cinnamon
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (adjust to taste)
- 1 can (15 oz) pumpkin puree
- 2 cans (15 oz each) black beans, drained and rinsed
- 1 can (14.5 oz) diced tomatoes
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Lime wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add the ground turkey (or plant‑based crumble) and brown, breaking it up with a spoon, about 6‑8 minutes.
4. Sprinkle in the cumin, smoked paprika, cinnamon, and cayenne; stir to coat the meat and aromatics, cooking for another minute.
5. Mix in the pumpkin puree, diced tomatoes, black beans, vegetable broth, and maple syrup. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil.
6. Reduce heat to low and simmer, uncovered, for 25‑30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chili thickens and flavors meld.
7. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Adjust heat with additional cayenne or a splash of lime juice if desired.
8. Ladle the chili into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro, and serve with lime wedges on the side. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Ginger Pumpkin and Black Bean Chili

text:
Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Cauliflower and Lentil Salad with Pomegranate Vinaigrette

Ingredients:
- 1 large head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves (plus extra for garnish)
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1/2 red onion, thinly sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/4 cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil (for dressing)
- 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar
- 1 tsp Dijon mustard
- 1 tsp honey
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss cauliflower florets with 2 tbsp olive oil, thyme, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet.
2. Roast cauliflower for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden‑brown and tender. Remove from oven and let cool slightly.
3. While the cauliflower roasts, place lentils in a saucepan, cover with water, bring to a boil, then simmer 20‑25 minutes until al dente. Drain and set aside.
4. In a small skillet, heat a drizzle of olive oil over medium heat. Sauté red onion and garlic for 3‑4 minutes until softened. Transfer to a large mixing bowl.
5. Add the roasted cauliflower, cooked lentils, and sautéed onion‑garlic mixture to the bowl. Toss gently to combine.
6. In a separate jar, whisk together the dressing: 2 tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil, apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, honey, lemon zest, and lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
7. Pour the vinaigrette over the salad and toss until everything is evenly coated.
8. Transfer the salad to a serving platter, sprinkle pomegranate seeds and extra thyme leaves on top for color and crunch. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Cauliflower and Lentil Salad with Pomegranate Vinaigrette

text:
Spiced Cardamom Sweet Potato and Chickpea Curry

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp ground cardamom
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- ½ tsp turmeric
- 1 cup coconut milk
- ½ cup vegetable broth
- 2 cups fresh spinach leaves
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4–5 minutes.  
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for another minute until fragrant.  
3. Sprinkle the ground cardamom, cumin, coriander, and turmeric over the aromatics, stirring constantly for 30 seconds to toast the spices.  
4. Add the cubed sweet potatoes to the pot, tossing to coat them in the spice mixture.  
5. Pour in the coconut milk and vegetable broth, stirring to combine. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to a simmer.  
6. Cover the pot and let the curry simmer for 15–20 minutes, or until the sweet potatoes are tender when pierced with a fork.  
7. Add the chickpeas and spinach leaves, stirring until the spinach wilts and the chickpeas are heated through, about 3–4 minutes.  
8. Season the curry with salt, pepper, and lime juice. Adjust seasoning to taste.  
9. Remove from heat and ladle the curry into bowls. Garnish each serving with chopped cilantro and an extra squeeze of lime if desired. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Cardamom Sweet Potato and Chickpea Curry

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Chickpea and Spinach Pasta

Ingredients:
- 12 oz whole‑wheat spaghetti
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 4 cups fresh baby spinach
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tbsp lime zest
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch piece ginger, grated
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp red‑pepper flakes (optional)
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti according to package directions until al dente. Reserve ½ cup of the pasta cooking water, then drain the pasta.
2. While the pasta cooks, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger; sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
3. Stir in the cumin and red‑pepper flakes, cooking for another 20 seconds to toast the spices.
4. Add the chickpeas to the skillet and toss to coat with the aromatics. Cook for 3–4 minutes, allowing them to brown slightly.
5. Pour in the coconut milk, lime juice, and lime zest. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, stirring occasionally, and let it reduce by about one‑third, roughly 5 minutes.
6. Add the fresh spinach to the skillet and stir until wilted, about 2 minutes. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
7. Combine the cooked spaghetti with the sauce, adding the reserved pasta water a little at a time to achieve a silky coating. Toss everything together until the pasta is evenly coated.
8. Transfer the pasta to serving bowls, garnish with chopped cilantro, and serve immediately. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Chickpea and Spinach Pasta

text:
Maple‑Glazed Chickpea and Sweet Potato Sheet Pan Dinner

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp garlic powder
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 1 Tbsp fresh thyme leaves, chopped
- Optional: a squeeze of fresh lemon juice for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a large bowl, combine the sweet potato cubes, chickpeas, olive oil, maple syrup, smoked paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Toss until everything is evenly coated.
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet, ensuring the sweet potatoes are not overcrowded.
4. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the sweet potatoes are tender and caramelized and the chickpeas are crisp.
5. Remove from the oven and immediately sprinkle the chopped fresh thyme over the hot vegetables; toss gently to distribute.
6. Transfer to a serving platter, drizzle with a little extra maple syrup if desired, and finish with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice for brightness. Serve warm.
title: Maple‑Glazed Chickpea and Sweet Potato Sheet Pan Dinner

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Shrimp and Avocado Quinoa Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 1 avocado, diced
- 1 red bell pepper, thinly sliced
- 1 small red onion, thinly sliced
- 2 tbsp coconut oil
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tbsp coconut milk
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground coriander
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Lime wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa and water; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until the quinoa is tender and the water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
2. While the quinoa cooks, whisk together lime juice, coconut milk, cumin, smoked paprika, coriander, cayenne, salt, and pepper in a large bowl to create the dressing.
3. Heat coconut oil in a skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the shrimp, season with a pinch of salt, and sauté 2‑3 minutes per side until pink and opaque. Transfer the cooked shrimp to the bowl with the dressing and toss to coat.
4. Add the cooked quinoa, sliced red bell pepper, red onion, and diced avocado to the bowl. Gently toss everything together, ensuring the dressing evenly coats the ingredients.
5. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired.
6. Divide the mixture among serving bowls, garnish each with fresh cilantro leaves and a lime wedge, and serve immediately. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Shrimp and Avocado Quinoa Bowl

text:
Crispy Coconut‑Lime Tempeh with Mango‑Avocado Salsa

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- ¼ cup coconut milk
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp cornstarch
- 2 tbsp neutral oil (e.g., canola)
- 1 ripe mango, diced
title: Crispy Coconut‑Lime Tempeh with Mango‑Avocado Salsa

text:
Citrus‑Ginger Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Avocado

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 orange, juiced (about ¼ cup)
- 1 lemon, juiced (about 2 Tbsp)
- 1 inch piece fresh ginger, grated
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 Tbsp honey or maple syrup
- ½ teaspoon red‑pepper flakes (optional)
- 1 ripe avocado, sliced
- 2 Tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Toss the chickpeas with olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper; spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until crisp and golden.
2. While the chickpeas roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together orange juice, lemon juice, grated ginger, minced garlic, honey, red‑pepper flakes, and a pinch of salt and pepper to create the citrus‑ginger dressing.
4. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl, add the roasted chickpeas, and pour the dressing over the top. Toss gently to combine, adjusting seasoning if needed.
5. Divide the quinoa mixture among serving bowls, top each with sliced avocado and a sprinkle of fresh cilantro. Serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Citrus‑Ginger Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Avocado

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Roasted Carrot and Lentil Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and sliced into thin rounds
- 1 cup cooked green lentils (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp sea salt
- ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 1 Tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tsp lime zest
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 1 Tbsp honey or maple syrup (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the carrot rounds with olive oil, turmeric, cumin, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the carrots in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
4. While the carrots roast, place the cooked lentils in a mixing bowl. Add lime juice, lime zest, and a drizzle of olive oil; toss to combine.  
5. When the carrots are done, let them cool slightly, then add them to the lentil bowl.  
6. Gently fold in the chopped cilantro, toasted pumpkin seeds, and honey or maple syrup if using, adjusting seasoning with extra salt or lime juice to taste.  
7. Serve the salad warm or at room temperature, garnished with a few extra cilantro leaves and pumpkin seeds. Enjoy!
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Roasted Carrot and Lentil Salad

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea & Sweet Potato Skillet

Ingredients:
- 1 lb (450 g) sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, minced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the diced sweet potatoes and sauté for 5‑7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they begin to soften and develop a light golden crust.  
2. Add the minced ginger and garlic to the pan; cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly to avoid burning.  
3. Sprinkle the turmeric, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper over the vegetables. Stir well to coat the sweet potatoes evenly with the spices.  
4. Add the chickpeas to the skillet, mixing them into the spiced sweet potatoes. Cook for 3‑4 minutes, allowing the chickpeas to heat through and absorb the flavors.  
5. Remove the skillet from heat. Stir in the lemon zest, lemon juice, and chopped cilantro. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if desired.  
6. Serve the skillet hot, garnished with extra cilantro or a drizzle of olive oil if you like. It pairs well with steamed rice, quinoa, or a simple green salad.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea & Sweet Potato Skillet

text:
Cinnamon‑Lime Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 2 cups cooked quinoa
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- 2 tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread them in a single layer on the sheet.  
3. In the same bowl, combine chickpeas with the remaining olive oil, cinnamon, lime zest, lime juice, and a pinch of salt; toss to coat.  
4. Add the seasoned chickpeas to the baking sheet, arranging them beside the sweet potatoes.  
5. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the sweet potatoes are tender and the chickpeas are crisp.  
6. While the vegetables roast, prepare the quinoa according to package instructions; fluff with a fork.  
7. Divide the cooked quinoa among serving bowls, top with the roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas, and sprinkle with cilantro and toasted pumpkin seeds.  
8. Serve warm, optionally drizzling extra lime juice over the top for added brightness.
title: Cinnamon‑Lime Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Bowl

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Salad with Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 4 cups mixed baby greens
- ½ cup pomegranate seeds
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, cinnamon, olive oil, salt, and pepper.  
3. Add the cubed sweet potatoes and chickpeas to the bowl; toss until evenly coated.  
4. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
5. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the sweet potatoes are tender and caramelized and the chickpeas are crisp.  
6. While the vegetables roast, place the mixed greens in a large salad bowl and drizzle with lemon juice; toss gently.  
7. Once roasted, let the sweet potatoes and chickpeas cool slightly, then add them to the greens.  
8. Sprinkle the pomegranate seeds and toasted pumpkin seeds over the top.  
9. Toss the salad lightly to combine all ingredients and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Salad with Pomegranate

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Brussels Sprouts and Quinoa Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp garlic powder
- 1 lb (450 g) Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1/4 cup toasted sliced almonds
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, smoked paprika, and garlic powder. Add the tofu cubes, toss to coat, and set aside.  
3. On the same bowl, drizzle the Brussels sprouts with olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and spread them cut‑side‑down on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 15 minutes.  
4. While the sprouts roast, place the coated tofu on a separate portion of the baking sheet. Roast the tofu alongside the sprouts for another 15‑20 minutes, turning once, until golden and caramelized.  
5. Meanwhile, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and fluff with a fork.  
6. Once the Brussels sprouts are tender and slightly crisp, remove from the oven. Transfer the roasted sprouts and tofu to a large serving bowl. Add the cooked quinoa, toasted almonds, and gently toss everything together.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a drizzle of maple syrup if desired. Garnish with chopped parsley before serving. Enjoy warm or at room temperature.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Brussels Sprouts and Quinoa Pilaf

text:
Spiced Orange‑Glazed Cauliflower Steak with Quinoa Tabbouleh

Ingredients:
- 1 large cauliflower head
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1/2 tsp ground coriander
- 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- Zest of 1 orange
- 2 tbsp fresh orange juice
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh mint
- 1/4 cup diced cucumber
- 1/4 cup diced red bell pepper
- 2 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Trim the leaves and stem from the cauliflower, then slice it into 1‑inch‑thick “steaks” (you’ll get 2–3 usable pieces).  
3. In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, coriander, cayenne, orange zest, orange juice, maple syrup, salt, and pepper.  
4. Brush both sides of each cauliflower steak generously with the orange‑spice glaze. Place on the prepared baking sheet.  
5. Roast the cauliflower steaks for 20‑25 minutes, flipping once, until tender and caramelized at the edges.  
6. While the cauliflower roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and let cool slightly.  
7. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large bowl. Add parsley, mint, cucumber, red bell pepper, lemon juice, and olive oil. Toss gently to combine; season with salt and pepper to taste.  
8. To serve, place a quinoa tabbouleh mound on each plate, top with a glazed cauliflower steak, and drizzle any remaining orange glaze from the pan over the top. Enjoy warm.
title: Spiced Orange‑Glazed Cauliflower Steak with Quinoa Tabbouleh

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Sweet Pepper and Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2  tbsp maple syrup
- 1  tbsp soy sauce
- 1  tsp smoked paprika
- 1  tbsp olive oil
- 2  red bell peppers, sliced
- 1  yellow bell pepper, sliced
- 1  tbsp balsamic vinegar
- 1  cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2  cups vegetable broth
- 1/4  cup chopped fresh cilantro
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the sliced bell peppers with olive oil, balsamic vinegar, salt, and pepper; spread them on the prepared sheet and roast for 15‑20 minutes, until caramelized.
