3. While the peppers roast, whisk together maple syrup, soy sauce, and smoked paprika in a bowl. Add the tofu cubes, toss to coat, and let marinate for 5 minutes.  
4. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium heat. Add the tofu and sear for 3‑4 minutes per side until golden and glossy; set aside.  
5. In a saucepan, combine quinoa and vegetable broth; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.  
6. To assemble, divide the cooked quinoa among serving bowls, top with roasted peppers, add the maple‑glazed tofu, and sprinkle with fresh cilantro.  
7. Serve warm or at room temperature, adjusting salt and pepper to taste.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Sweet Pepper and Quinoa

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa with Roasted Beet and Feta

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 medium beets, peeled and cubed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp sea salt
- 1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1/4 cup crumbled feta cheese
- 2 tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds
- 1 handful fresh arugula (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the beet cubes with olive oil, salt, and pepper, then spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, until tender and caramelized.
2. While the beets roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together lemon juice, lemon zest, and grated ginger. Drizzle this dressing over the cooked quinoa and stir to combine.
4. Gently fold the roasted beets into the quinoa mixture. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt or lemon juice if desired.
5. Transfer the quinoa‑beet mixture to serving bowls. Top each with crumbled feta, toasted pumpkin seeds, and a handful of arugula if using.
6. Serve warm or at room temperature, and enjoy the bright, earthy flavors.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa with Roasted Beet and Feta

text:
Spiced Orange‑Maple Glazed Tempeh with Quinoa and Roasted Broccoli

Ingredients:
- 8 oz (225 g) tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 large head broccoli, cut into florets
- 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tbsp orange zest
- 2 tbsp freshly‑squeezed orange juice
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp ground cinnamon
- Salt and freshly cracked black pepper, to taste
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds (optional, for garnish)
- Fresh cilantro leaves, torn (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a small bowl, whisk together 1 tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, orange zest, orange juice, cumin, smoked paprika, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Set the glaze aside.
3. Toss the broccoli florets with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 15‑20 minutes, turning once, until tender‑crisp and lightly caramelized.
title: Spiced Orange‑Maple Glazed Tempeh with Quinoa and Roasted Broccoli

text:
Spiced Orange‑Glazed Tofu with Coconut Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 14 oz firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 1/4 cup fresh orange juice
- 2 Tbsp soy sauce
- 1 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 Tbsp cornstarch
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- 1 Tbsp lime juice
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, whisk together orange juice, soy sauce, maple syrup, ginger, and garlic; set aside.
2. Toss the tofu cubes with cornstarch until lightly coated, then spread on a parchment‑lined baking sheet.
3. Bake the tofu at 400°F (200°C) for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
4. While the tofu bakes, combine quinoa and coconut milk in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and season with salt and pepper.
5. Transfer the baked tofu to a shallow dish and pour the orange‑soy glaze over it; toss gently to coat and let sit 5 minutes.
6. In a large bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, lime juice, and cilantro; adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
7. Serve the glazed tofu atop the coconut quinoa salad, drizzling any remaining glaze over the top. Enjoy warm or at room temperature.
title: Spiced Orange‑Glazed Tofu with Coconut Quinoa Salad

text:
Spiced Orange‑Glazed Cauliflower and Chickpea Tacos

Ingredients:
- 1 small head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp orange marmalade
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- 8 small corn tortillas
- ½ cup red cabbage, thinly sliced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 lime, cut into wedges
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together orange marmalade, soy sauce, smoked paprika, cumin, cayenne, olive oil, salt, and pepper.  
3. Add the cauliflower florets and chickpeas to the bowl, tossing to coat evenly with the glaze.  
4. Spread the coated cauliflower and chickpeas in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
5. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway through, until the cauliflower is tender and lightly caramelized.  
6. While the vegetables roast, warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 30 seconds per side.  
7. Assemble each taco by placing a generous spoonful of the roasted cauliflower and chickpeas onto a tortilla, then top with sliced red cabbage and chopped cilantro.  
8. Finish with a squeeze of fresh lime juice and serve immediately.
title: Spiced Orange‑Glazed Cauliflower and Chickpea Tacos

text:
Lemon‑Basil Quinoa with Roasted Eggplant and Pomegranate  

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 large eggplant, cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1/4 cup fresh basil leaves, chopped
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tbsp lemon juice
- 1/3 cup pomegranate arils
- 1/4 cup toasted pine nuts
- 1 clove garlic, minced

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the eggplant cubes with olive oil, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.
2. While the eggplant roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together lemon zest, lemon juice, minced garlic, and a pinch of salt to create the dressing.
4. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl. Add the chopped basil, drizzle the lemon‑garlic dressing over the quinoa, and toss gently to combine.
5. Fold in the roasted eggplant, pomegranate arils, and toasted pine nuts, mixing just enough to distribute evenly.
6. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with extra basil leaves and a drizzle of olive oil if desired. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Basil Quinoa with Roasted Eggplant and Pomegranate

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Shrimp and Mango Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups water
- 1 ripe mango, peeled and diced
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 2 tbsp coconut oil
- 2 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tbsp honey
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa and water; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until the water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Shrimp and Mango Quinoa Salad

text:
Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Pumpkin and Quinoa Bowl with Sage Pesto  

Ingredients:
- 1 small sugar pumpkin (about 2 lb), peeled, seeded, and cubed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup fresh sage leaves
- ¼ cup toasted walnuts
- 2 tbsp grated Parmesan cheese
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- ¼ cup extra‑virgin olive oil (for pesto)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the pumpkin cubes with olive oil, cinnamon, cumin, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning once, until caramelized and tender.  
2. While the pumpkin roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
3. Prepare the sage pesto: in a food processor blend sage, toasted walnuts, Parmesan, garlic, lemon juice, and the ¼ cup olive oil until smooth. Season with salt and pepper to taste.  
4. In a large bowl, combine the cooked quinoa and roasted pumpkin. Drizzle with the sage pesto and toss gently to coat evenly.  
5. Serve warm, garnished with extra toasted walnuts, a sprinkle of Parmesan, and a few fresh sage leaves if desired. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Pumpkin and Quinoa Bowl with Sage Pesto

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Brussels Sprouts and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 lb (450 g) Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp sea salt
- ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- ¼ cup toasted sliced almonds
- ¼ cup dried cranberries
- Zest of 1 orange
- 2 Tbsp freshly squeezed orange juice
- 1 Tbsp apple cider vinegar

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, ground cinnamon, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Add the Brussels sprouts and toss to coat evenly.  
3. Spread the coated sprouts in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until they are caramelized and tender.  
4. While the sprouts roast, combine the rinsed quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together the orange zest, orange juice, and apple cider vinegar to create a bright dressing.  
6. In a large serving bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted Brussels sprouts, toasted almonds, and dried cranberries. Drizzle the orange‑cider dressing over the mixture and toss gently to distribute.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature as a hearty side or a light main dish. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Brussels Sprouts and Quinoa Salad

text:
Citrus‑Honey Glazed Carrot and Lentil Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and sliced into thin ribbons
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 2 tbsp honey
- 1 tbsp fresh orange juice
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1/4 cup toasted almond slivers
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. In a saucepan, combine lentils with 3 cups water, bring to a boil, then simmer 20‑25 minutes until tender but still firm; drain and set aside.
2. While lentils cook, heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add carrot ribbons and sauté 5‑7 minutes until just softened.
3. In a small bowl whisk together honey, orange juice, lemon zest, cumin, salt, and pepper.
4. Pour the glaze over the carrots, tossing to coat; cook another 2 minutes until the glaze thickens and clings to the carrots.
5. In a large bowl combine cooked lentils, glazed carrots, toasted almonds, and parsley; toss gently.
6. Adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a splash of orange juice if needed. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Citrus‑Honey Glazed Carrot and Lentil Salad

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Chickpea Salad

Ingredients:
- 3 medium beets, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp sea salt
- ½ tsp black pepper
- ¼ cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped
- 2 Tbsp crumbled feta cheese
- 2 Tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- 1 Tbsp apple cider vinegar

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together maple syrup, ground cinnamon, olive oil, sea salt, and black pepper.  
3. Add the cubed beets and chickpeas to the bowl, toss to coat evenly, and spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the beets are tender and caramelized and the chickpeas are crisp.  
5. Transfer the roasted beets and chickpeas to a serving bowl; drizzle with apple cider vinegar and toss gently.  
6. Sprinkle toasted walnuts, crumbled feta, and chopped parsley over the top.  
7. Serve warm or at room temperature as a hearty salad or side dish.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Chickpea Salad

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chicken with Quinoa Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 4 boneless, skinless chicken thighs
- 1 ½ cups quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups low‑sodium chicken broth
- 1 ½ tbsp coconut oil
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch piece fresh ginger, grated
- ½ cup unsalted roasted peanuts, roughly chopped
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, combine turmeric, cumin, smoked paprika, lime zest, lime juice, minced garlic, grated ginger, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of olive oil to form a paste.
2. Pat the chicken thighs dry with paper towels, then rub the spice paste evenly over both sides of each piece. Let them rest for 10 minutes while you prepare the quinoa.
3. Heat 1 tbsp coconut oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the chicken thighs, skin‑side down, and sear for 4‑5 minutes until golden brown. Flip and cook an additional 3‑4 minutes; remove chicken and set aside.
4. In the same skillet, add the remaining ½ tbsp coconut oil and toast the quinoa for 1‑2 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
5. Pour the chicken broth into the skillet, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the quinoa is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
6. While the quinoa cooks, return the chicken to the skillet, cover, and let it finish cooking over low heat for another 5‑7 minutes, ensuring the interior reaches 165 °F (74 °C).
7. Fluff the quinoa with a fork, then stir in the chopped peanuts and half of the cilantro. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired.
8. Plate the quinoa pilaf, top each portion with a chicken thigh, and garnish with the remaining cilantro. Serve immediately, optionally with extra lime wedges on the side.
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chicken with Quinoa Pilaf

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Glazed Seared Scallops with Coconut Lime Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 12 oz sea scallops, patted dry
- 1 cup quinoa
- 1 ¾ cups coconut water
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp ground ginger
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Rinse the quinoa, then combine it with coconut water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed; fluff with a fork and set aside.
2. In a small bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, ground cinnamon, ground ginger, lime juice, and a pinch of salt and pepper.
3. Pat the scallops dry and season lightly with salt and pepper. Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium‑high heat.
4. Add the scallops in a single layer and sear for about 2 minutes per side, until a golden crust forms and the interior is just opaque. Transfer to a plate.
5. Pour the maple‑cinnamon glaze over the scallops in the skillet and cook for an additional 30 seconds, allowing the glaze to caramelize slightly.
6. Serve the glazed scallops atop the coconut‑lime quinoa, garnish with chopped cilantro, and finish with an extra drizzle of lime juice if desired.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Glazed Seared Scallops with Coconut Lime Quinoa

text:
Maple‑Basil Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp fresh basil, finely chopped
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, half the maple syrup, smoked paprika, thyme, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
3. Roast the sweet potatoes for 20 minutes, then remove the sheet, flip the cubes, and add the chickpeas tossed with the remaining olive oil and maple syrup. Return to the oven and roast for an additional 15 minutes, or until the sweet potatoes are tender and the chickpeas are crisp.  
4. Transfer the roasted vegetables to a serving bowl. While still warm, drizzle with the fresh basil, toasted pumpkin seeds, and lemon juice. Toss gently to combine.  
5. If using, sprinkle crumbled feta cheese over the top and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy as a hearty side or a light main dish.
title: Maple‑Basil Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Salad

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Lentil Soup

Ingredients:
- 1 lb carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch pieces
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 large onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch piece fresh ginger, grated
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the carrot pieces with 1 Tbsp olive oil, cinnamon, and a pinch of salt; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until caramelized and tender.
2. While the carrots roast, heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 5 minutes, until translucent.
3. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Add the rinsed red lentils, roasted carrots, vegetable broth, maple syrup, and cumin to the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 15‑20 minutes, or until the lentils are soft.
5. Using an immersion blender (or transferring to a countertop blender in batches), puree the soup until smooth and creamy. Return to the pot if needed.
6. Stir in the coconut milk and heat through gently; do not boil. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
7. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve hot.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Lentil Soup

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Garlic Sweet Potato Mash  

Ingredients:
- 1 block (14 oz) extra‑firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp ground ginger
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- ¼ cup unsweetened almond milk (or any plant‑based milk)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh chives, chopped (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, minced garlic, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet; roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning once, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, whisk together maple syrup, soy sauce, smoked paprika, ground ginger, and the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil in a shallow bowl. Add the tofu cubes and toss to coat evenly.  
3. Spread the glazed tofu on a separate parchment‑lined baking sheet. Bake for 20‑25 minutes, flipping halfway through, until the edges are golden and crisp.  
4. Transfer the roasted sweet potatoes to a large bowl; add almond milk and mash with a potato masher or fork until smooth. Adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a drizzle of maple syrup if desired.  
5. Plate a generous scoop of the sweet potato mash, top with the maple‑glazed tofu, and sprinkle chopped chives over the dish for a fresh finish. Serve warm.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Garlic Sweet Potato Mash

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Edamame and Kale  

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, grated
- 1 cup frozen edamame, shelled
- 2 cups kale, stems removed and torn into bite‑size pieces
- 1 tablespoon lemon juice
- 1 teaspoon lemon zest
- 1/2 teaspoon sea salt
- 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- 1 tablespoon toasted sesame seeds (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the edamame with half the olive oil, half the minced garlic, and a pinch of salt; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 12‑15 minutes, stirring once, until lightly browned.  
2. While the edamame roasts, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.  
3. In a large skillet, heat the remaining olive oil over medium heat. Add the remaining garlic and grated ginger; sauté 1‑2 minutes until fragrant. Add the kale and sauté 3‑4 minutes, until wilted but still bright green.  
4. Stir the roasted edamame into the skillet with the kale, then add the cooked quinoa. Toss everything together, seasoning with lemon juice, lemon zest, salt, and pepper. Cook 2 minutes more to let flavors meld.  
5. Transfer to serving bowls and sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds, if using. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Edamame and Kale

text:
Spiced Cardamom Carrot and Lentil Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 large carrots, peeled and diced
- 1 small onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon ground cardamom
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- ¼ teaspoon smoked paprika
- 3 cups low‑sodium vegetable broth
- ½ cup basmati rice, rinsed
- ¼ cup toasted slivered almonds
- 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Juice of ½ lemon

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 3‑4 minutes.
2. Stir in the garlic, ground cardamom, cumin, and smoked paprika; cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
3. Add the diced carrots and rice, stirring to coat them with the spices for 1‑2 minutes.
4. Pour in the rinsed lentils and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils and rice are tender and the liquid is absorbed.
5. Remove the pan from heat and let it sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff the pilaf with a fork.
6. Stir in the lemon juice, season with salt and pepper to taste, and fold in the toasted almonds and chopped cilantro.
7. Serve warm as a hearty main dish or a side, garnished with extra cilantro if desired.
title: Spiced Cardamom Carrot and Lentil Pilaf

text:
Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Soup

Ingredients:
- 1 lb carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch pieces
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp ground cinnamon
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the carrot pieces with 1 tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and the ground cinnamon. Spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
2. While the carrots roast, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 4‑5 minutes, until translucent. Stir in the minced garlic and cumin; cook for another minute until fragrant.  
3. Add the roasted carrots, chickpeas, and vegetable broth to the pot. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.  
4. Using an immersion blender (or transferring to a countertop blender in batches), puree the soup until smooth, leaving a few carrot pieces for texture if desired.  
5. Season the soup with salt and pepper to taste. If the soup is too thick, thin it with a little extra broth or water.  
6. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with chopped cilantro, and serve hot. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Soup

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Garlic Brussels Sprouts and Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 1 lb (450 g) Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 3 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 cup (185 g) uncooked quinoa
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice
- Optional garnish: chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the Brussels sprouts with 1 Tbsp olive oil, half the minced garlic, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Spread them cut‑side down on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring once, until caramelized and tender.  
3. While the sprouts roast, rinse the quinoa under cold water. Combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and fluff with a fork; stir in lemon juice, a drizzle of olive oil, and a pinch of salt.  
4. Meanwhile, heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil in a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the cubed tofu and sear for 3‑4 minutes per side, until golden brown.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together the maple syrup and the remaining minced garlic. Pour the glaze over the tofu, tossing to coat. Cook an additional 2 minutes, allowing the glaze to thicken and cling to the tofu.  
6. To serve, divide the quinoa among plates, top with roasted Brussels sprouts, and arrange the maple‑glazed tofu on top. Sprinkle with fresh parsley if desired and enjoy immediately.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Garlic Brussels Sprouts and Quinoa

text:
Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Cauliflower and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 large head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp ground black pepper
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- ¼ cup dried cranberries
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp honey
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss cauliflower florets with 1 tbsp olive oil, cinnamon, smoked paprika, cumin, black pepper, and salt; spread on a baking sheet.
2. Roast cauliflower for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden‑brown and tender.
3. While the cauliflower roasts, combine quinoa and 2 cups water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside to cool slightly.
4. In a small bowl, whisk together lemon juice, honey, and the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil; season with a pinch of salt if desired.
5. In a large mixing bowl, combine the roasted cauliflower, cooked quinoa, toasted pumpkin seeds, and dried cranberries. Drizzle the lemon‑honey dressing over the mixture and toss gently to coat.
6. Sprinkle chopped parsley on top and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy as a hearty main or a vibrant side dish.
title: Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Cauliflower and Quinoa Salad

text:
Sage‑Infused Roasted Pumpkin and Barley Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup pearl barley, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 small pumpkin (about 2 lb), peeled and cubed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp dried sage (or 1 Tbsp fresh sage, chopped)
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp dried cranberries
- 2 Tbsp crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- 1 Tbsp apple cider vinegar
- 1 tsp honey
- 1 tsp Dijon mustard

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the pumpkin cubes with olive oil, sage, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning once, until tender and caramelized.  
2. While the pumpkin roasts, bring the barley and water (or broth) to a boil in a saucepan, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook 30‑35 minutes until the grains are tender and the liquid is absorbed. Drain any excess liquid and fluff with a fork.  
3. In a small bowl, whisk together the apple cider vinegar, honey, Dijon mustard, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of olive oil to create a tangy dressing.  
4. In a large mixing bowl combine the cooked barley, roasted pumpkin, toasted pumpkin seeds, dried cranberries, and the dressing. Toss gently to coat everything evenly.  
5. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a splash of vinegar if needed.  
6. Transfer the salad to a serving platter, sprinkle crumbled feta over the top (if using), and garnish with a few extra sage leaves. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Sage‑Infused Roasted Pumpkin and Barley Salad

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Shrimp with Coconut‑Lime Rice

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined  
- 1 cup jasmine rice, rinsed  
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk  
- ½ cup water  
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, minced  
- 1 tsp ground turmeric  
- Zest of 1 lime  
- 2 tbsp lime juice  
- 2 cloves garlic, minced  
- 2 tbsp olive oil  
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped  
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste  

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine the rinsed rice, coconut milk, water, lime zest, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Remove from heat and let it sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and stir in lime juice and half of the cilantro; set aside.  
2. While the rice cooks, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Shrimp with Coconut‑Lime Rice

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Chickpea and Spinach Tacos

Ingredients:
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 cups fresh baby spinach
- 8 small corn tortillas
- ¼ cup coconut milk
- 2 Tbsp fresh lime juice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 Tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp ground coriander
- ¼ tsp red‑pepper flakes (optional)
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- ½ red onion, thinly sliced
- 1 avocado, sliced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium bowl, whisk together coconut milk, lime juice, garlic, ginger, cumin, smoked paprika, coriander, red‑pepper flakes, salt, and pepper. Set aside.  
2. Heat 1 Tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the sliced red onion and sauté 3–4 minutes until softened. Transfer to a plate.  
3. Add the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil to the same skillet. Toss in the chickpeas and cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes until they begin to brown.  
4. Pour the coconut‑lime sauce over the chickpeas, stirring to coat. Cook 2 minutes more, allowing the sauce to thicken and cling to the beans.  
5. Add the fresh spinach to the skillet and toss until wilted, about 1 minute. Return the sautéed onions to the pan and mix everything together. Adjust seasoning with extra salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired.  
6. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet or microwave for 20 seconds, keeping them pliable.  
7. To assemble each taco, spoon a generous portion of the spiced chickpea‑spinach mixture onto a tortilla. Top with avocado slices, a sprinkle of chopped cilantro, and any additional lime wedges.  
8. Serve immediately, enjoying the bright, aromatic flavors of coconut, lime, and warm spices.
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Chickpea and Spinach Tacos

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Sesame‑Brown Butter Broccoli

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 cups broccoli florets
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp sesame oil
- 2 Tbsp unsalted butter
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 Tbsp low‑sodium soy sauce
- ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds (optional)
- 1 Tbsp rice vinegar (optional, for a bright finish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the tofu cubes with 1 Tbsp sesame oil, 1 Tbsp maple syrup, soy sauce, and black pepper; spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and bake for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.  
3. While the tofu bakes, melt the butter in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger, sautéing for 30 seconds until fragrant.  
4. Add the broccoli florets to the skillet, stirring to coat them in the butter mixture. Cook for 4‑5 minutes, then drizzle the remaining 1 Tbsp maple syrup over the broccoli and continue to sauté until the broccoli is tender‑crisp and the sauce has thickened, about 2‑3 minutes more.  
5. Remove the skillet from heat; stir in the toasted sesame seeds and, if using, a splash of rice vinegar for brightness.  
6. Transfer the roasted tofu to a serving platter, top with the sesame‑brown butter broccoli, and serve immediately over steamed rice or quinoa. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Sesame‑Brown Butter Broccoli

text:
Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Carrot and Lentil Salad with Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch rounds
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1/4 cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tsp honey (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the carrot rounds with 1 tbsp olive oil, cinnamon, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until caramelized and tender.  
2. While the carrots roast, place the lentils in a saucepan, cover with water, bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook 20‑25 minutes until al dente. Drain and set aside to cool slightly.  
3. In a large bowl combine the roasted carrots, cooked lentils, remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, lemon juice, and honey (if using). Toss gently to coat.  
4. Fold in the chopped parsley and pomegranate seeds, then season with additional salt and pepper to taste.  
5. Serve the salad warm or at room temperature, garnished with extra pomegranate seeds and parsley if desired.
title: Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Carrot and Lentil Salad with Pomegranate

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Garlic Sweet Potato and Kale

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 4 cups kale leaves, stems removed and torn
- 3 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, half the minced garlic, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20 minutes, stirring once halfway through.  
3. While the sweet potatoes roast, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, remaining garlic, and the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a shallow dish. Add the tempeh strips, turning to coat evenly; let marinate for 5 minutes.  
4. After the sweet potatoes have roasted 20 minutes, remove the sheet, push the potatoes to one side, and arrange the marinated tempeh strips on the empty side. Return to the oven and roast for an additional 15‑18 minutes, or until the tempeh is golden and the sweet potatoes are tender and caramelized.  
5. While the tempeh and sweet potatoes finish cooking, heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add a splash of olive oil, then add the kale. Sauté, stirring frequently, until wilted and bright green, about 3‑4 minutes. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.  
6. Transfer the roasted sweet potatoes and tempeh to the skillet with the kale. Toss everything together gently to combine and let the flavors meld for another 2 minutes.  
7. Serve hot, sprinkled with toasted sesame seeds if desired. Enjoy as a hearty main dish or a satisfying bowl over cooked quinoa or brown rice.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Garlic Sweet Potato and Kale

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Garlic Broccoli and Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 block (14 oz) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 cups broccoli florets
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup
- 2 tablespoons low‑sodium soy sauce
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tablespoons olive oil, divided
- 1 teaspoon toasted sesame seeds
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 tablespoon lemon juice (optional, for finishing)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the broccoli florets with 1 tablespoon olive oil, half the minced garlic, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of maple syrup; spread evenly on the prepared sheet.  
3. Roast the broccoli for 15‑20 minutes, stirring halfway, until tender‑crisp and lightly caramelized.  
4. While the broccoli roasts, combine the cubed tofu, remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, soy sauce, maple syrup, smoked paprika, the remaining minced garlic, and a pinch of pepper in a separate bowl. Toss gently to coat.  
5. Transfer the tofu to a second parchment‑lined baking sheet and bake alongside the broccoli for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden and slightly crisp on the edges.  
6. Meanwhile, bring 2 cups water to a boil in a saucepan, add the rinsed quinoa, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes or until the water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and season with a pinch of salt.  
7. Once both tofu and broccoli are done, combine them in a large serving bowl with the cooked quinoa. Drizzle any pan juices over the top.  
8. Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds and, if desired, a splash of lemon juice for brightness. Toss gently to distribute.  
9. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or maple syrup if needed. Serve warm.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Garlic Broccoli and Quinoa

text:
Saffron‑Infused Quinoa with Roasted Garlic and Kale

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 bunch kale, stems removed, leaves chopped
- 1/2 teaspoon saffron threads
- 1/4 cup warm water (for saffron)
- 1/2 cup toasted pine nuts
- 1/4 cup dried cranberries
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Juice of 1 lemon

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, combine saffron threads with warm water; let steep for 5 minutes.
2. Heat olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat; add minced garlic and sauté until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
3. Add the rinsed quinoa and toast, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes.
4. Pour in the vegetable broth and the saffron infusion (including the threads); bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes or until the quinoa is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
5. While the quinoa cooks, heat a drizzle of olive oil in a skillet over medium heat; add the chopped kale and sauté until wilted, about 4 minutes; season with salt and pepper.
6. Fluff the cooked quinoa with a fork; stir in the lemon juice, and season with additional salt and pepper to taste.
7. Transfer the quinoa to a serving bowl; top with the sautéed kale, toasted pine nuts, and dried cranberries.
8. Serve warm or at room temperature, optionally drizzling a little extra lemon juice over the top.
title: Saffron‑Infused Quinoa with Roasted Garlic and Kale

text:
Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Lentil Shepherd’s Pie

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup diced carrots
- 1 cup frozen peas
- 1 small onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tablespoons maple syrup
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Place the sweet potato cubes on a baking sheet, drizzle with 1 tablespoon olive oil, and toss with a pinch of salt; roast for 20‑25 minutes until tender and lightly caramelized.  
2. While the potatoes roast, combine lentils and vegetable broth in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until lentils are tender and most liquid is absorbed.  
3. In a large skillet, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add the onion and garlic, sautéing until translucent, about 3‑4 minutes.  
4. Stir in the diced carrots, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper; cook for another 5 minutes, until the carrots begin to soften.  
5. Add the cooked lentils, frozen peas, and maple syrup to the skillet; mix well and cook for 2‑3 minutes to heat through and allow the flavors to meld.  
6. Transfer the lentil‑vegetable mixture to a 9‑inch baking dish, spreading it into an even layer.  
7. Mash the roasted sweet potatoes with a fork or potato masher, adding a pinch of salt and a drizzle of maple syrup if desired; spread the mash over the lentil layer, smoothing the top.  
8. Bake the assembled pie for 15‑20 minutes, until the top is golden and the filling is bubbling.  
9. Remove from the oven, let cool slightly, garnish with chopped fresh parsley, and serve warm.
title: Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Lentil Shepherd’s Pie

text:
Spiced Cardamom Sweet Potato and Chickpea Soup

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp ground cardamom
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat; add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.  
2. Stir in the minced garlic, ground cardamom, and smoked paprika; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
3. Add the cubed sweet potatoes and chickpeas, then pour in the vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until the sweet potatoes are tender, about 15–20 minutes.  
4. Using an immersion blender (or transferring to a countertop blender), puree the soup until smooth but still slightly chunky.  
5. Return the soup to the pot, stir in the coconut milk, and season with salt and black pepper to taste; heat through for another 3–4 minutes.  
6. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with chopped cilantro, and serve hot.
title: Spiced Cardamom Sweet Potato and Chickpea Soup

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Power Salad

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch sticks
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- 1/2 tsp sea salt
- 1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 4 cups mixed baby greens
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- 2 Tbsp lemon‑juice vinaigrette (store‑bought or homemade)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the carrot sticks and chickpeas with olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until carrots are tender‑crisp and chickpeas are golden and slightly crisp.  
4. While the vegetables roast, place the mixed baby greens in a large serving bowl.  
5. When the carrots and chickpeas are done, let them cool for 5 minutes, then add them to the greens.  
6. Drizzle the lemon‑juice vinaigrette over the salad and toss gently to combine.  
7. Sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds and crumbled feta (if using) on top for extra texture and flavor.  
8. Serve immediately, or refrigerate the roasted components separately and assemble just before eating for a make‑ahead lunch.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Power Salad

text:
Spiced Orange‑Maple Quinoa Stuffed Sweet Potatoes  

Ingredients:
- 4 medium sweet potatoes
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup canned black beans, drained and rinsed
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1/2 red onion, finely chopped
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- Zest of 1 orange
- 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 tablespoon lime juice  

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Scrub the sweet potatoes, pierce each several times with a fork, and place them on the prepared sheet. Roast for 45‑55 minutes, or until tender when pressed.  
3. While the potatoes roast, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
4. In a large skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add the red onion and bell pepper; sauté 5‑6 minutes until softened. Stir in cumin, smoked paprika, orange zest, and maple syrup; cook 1 minute more.  
5. Add the cooked quinoa and black beans to the skillet. Toss to combine, then season with salt, pepper, and lime juice. Remove from heat and fold in chopped cilantro.  
6. When the sweet potatoes are done, let them cool slightly, then slice each lengthwise open, being careful not to cut all the way through. Gently fluff the interior with a fork.  
7. Spoon the orange‑maple quinoa mixture generously into each sweet potato cavity. Drizzle any remaining skillet juices over the top.  
8. Serve warm, garnished with extra cilantro or a squeeze of lime if desired.
title: Spiced Orange‑Maple Quinoa Stuffed Sweet Potatoes

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Chickpeas and Kale

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp ground ginger
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1/2 tsp sea salt
- 1/4 tsp black pepper
- 3 cups kale, stems removed and torn into bite‑size pieces
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the chickpeas with 1 tbsp olive oil, minced garlic, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until crisp and golden.  
3. While the chickpeas roast, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
4. In a large skillet, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil over medium heat. Add the ginger and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the kale and a pinch of salt; cook, stirring frequently, until wilted, about 3‑4 minutes.  
5. Stir the roasted chickpeas into the skillet with the kale, then add the cooked quinoa. Toss everything together, allowing the flavors to meld for another minute.  
6. Remove from heat and drizzle with lemon juice and lemon zest. Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds on top, if using. Serve warm.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Chickpeas and Kale

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Kale Quinoa Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and cubed
- 2 cups chopped kale, stems removed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- ½ teaspoon sea salt
- ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 tablespoon olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the sweet potatoes in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and caramelized.  
4. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine quinoa and 2 cups water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes or until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.  
5. In a skillet, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add the kale and sauté 3‑4 minutes until wilted; season with a pinch of salt.  
6. In a large bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted sweet potatoes, and sautéed kale. Drizzle with lemon juice and toss gently to mix.  
7. Divide the mixture into serving bowls and sprinkle each with toasted pumpkin seeds for crunch. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Kale Quinoa Bowl

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Parsnip and Quinoa Salad with Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 2 large parsnips, peeled and cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- ½ teaspoon sea salt
- ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- ¼ cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped
- ½ cup pomegranate arils
- 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
- 1 tablespoon chopped fresh parsley (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, cinnamon, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Add the cubed parsnips and toss to coat evenly.  
3. Spread the coated parsnips in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning once halfway through, until golden‑brown and tender.  
4. While the parsnips roast, combine the rinsed quinoa and water (or broth) in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.  
5. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl. Add the roasted parsnips, toasted walnuts, pomegranate arils, lemon juice, and parsley if using. Gently toss to combine all ingredients.  
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a drizzle of maple syrup if desired.  
7. Serve the salad warm or at room temperature, garnished with a few extra pomegranate seeds and walnut pieces for texture. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Parsnip and Quinoa Salad with Pomegranate

text:
Ginger‑Lime Quinoa with Roasted Cauliflower and Pistachios

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 medium cauliflower head, cut into florets
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp fresh ginger, minced
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tbsp lime juice
- ¼ cup pistachios, roughly chopped
- 2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss cauliflower florets with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender.
2. While the cauliflower roasts, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.
3. In a small skillet over medium heat, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil. Add minced ginger and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Stir in lime zest and lime juice, cooking another minute. Remove from heat.
4. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large bowl. Pour the ginger‑lime dressing over the quinoa and toss to combine.
5. Fold the roasted cauliflower into the quinoa mixture. Add chopped pistachios and cilantro, then season with additional salt and pepper to taste.
6. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with a sprinkle of extra pistachios and a lime wedge if desired. Enjoy!
title: Ginger‑Lime Quinoa with Roasted Cauliflower and Pistachios

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa and Roasted Brussels Sprouts

Ingredients:
- 8 oz (225 g) tempeh, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp low‑sodium soy sauce
- 1 Tbsp olive oil (for tempeh)
- 1 Tbsp coconut oil (for vegetables)
- 1 lb (450 g) Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 1 cup (185 g) uncooked quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups (360 ml) coconut milk
- ½ cup (120 ml) water
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 Tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, and 1 Tbsp olive oil. Add the tempeh cubes, toss to coat, and let marinate while you prepare the vegetables.  
3. Toss the halved Brussels sprouts with 1 Tbsp coconut oil, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway through, until caramelized and tender.  
4. While the sprouts roast, combine the quinoa, coconut milk, water, lime zest, and a pinch of salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
5. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated tempeh (including any excess sauce) and cook, stirring occasionally, for 5‑7 minutes until the tempeh is golden and the glaze has thickened. Remove from heat.  
6. In a small bowl, whisk together the lime juice, minced garlic, grated ginger, a drizzle of olive oil, and a pinch of salt and pepper to make a quick dressing.  
7. To assemble, divide the coconut‑lime quinoa among serving bowls. Top with roasted Brussels sprouts, maple‑glazed tempeh, and drizzle the lime‑garlic dressing over everything. Garnish with chopped cilantro if desired. Serve warm.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa and Roasted Brussels Sprouts

text:
Herb‑Roasted Quinoa Stuffed Acorn Squash with Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 2 medium acorn squash, halved and seeded
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 small onion, finely diced
- 1 cup canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1/4 cup dried cranberries, chopped
- 1/4 cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, chopped
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Place the acorn squash halves cut‑side up on a baking sheet, brush with half the olive oil, and season with salt and pepper. Roast for 30‑35 minutes, until the flesh is tender and lightly caramelized.  
2. While the squash roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
3. In a skillet over medium heat, add the remaining olive oil. Sauté the onion for 3‑4 minutes until translucent, then add the garlic and cook another 30 seconds.  
4. Stir in the chickpeas, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Cook for 2‑3 minutes, allowing the spices to toast lightly.  
5. Add the cooked quinoa, dried cranberries, and fresh parsley to the skillet. Toss everything together and adjust seasoning if needed.  
6. Remove the roasted squash from the oven. Spoon the quinoa‑chickpea mixture into each squash cavity, packing it gently.  
7. Return the stuffed squash to the oven and bake for an additional 10 minutes to meld flavors.  
8. Remove from the oven, sprinkle pomegranate seeds over the top for a burst of freshness, and serve warm.
title: Herb‑Roasted Quinoa Stuffed Acorn Squash with Pomegranate

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Sweet Potato and Kale Salad

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and cubed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 4 cups kale, stems removed and torn
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp apple cider vinegar
- 1 tsp Dijon mustard
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, smoked paprika, and cumin. Toss the tempeh strips in the mixture until fully coated.  
3. Place the cubed sweet potato on the prepared baking sheet, drizzle with 1 Tbsp olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and toss to coat. Roast for 20 minutes, turning halfway through.  
4. While the sweet potato roasts, heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the glazed tempeh and cook 3‑4 minutes per side, until golden and caramelized. Transfer to a plate.  
5. In a large bowl, combine the kale, apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of olive oil. Massage the kale for 1‑2 minutes until it softens and darkens.  
6. When the sweet potatoes are tender and lightly browned, remove them from the oven. Add the roasted sweet potatoes to the kale, along with the cooked tempeh. Toss gently to combine.  
7. Divide the salad among serving bowls, sprinkle each with toasted pumpkin seeds, and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Sweet Potato and Kale Salad

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Tagine

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch chunks
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 medium onion, thinly sliced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 in piece fresh ginger, grated
- ½ tsp saffron threads, steeped in 2 Tbsp hot water
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- ½ cup dried apricots, halved
- ¼ cup sliced almonds, toasted
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- ½ tsp ground cinnamon
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Cooked couscous or quinoa, for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the carrot chunks with 1 Tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and half the cumin; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
2. While the carrots roast, heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil in a large, oven‑safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the sliced onion and sauté 5 minutes, until softened.  
3. Stir in the garlic and ginger; cook 1 minute until fragrant.  
4. Add the chickpeas, roasted carrots, ground coriander, ground cinnamon, and the remaining cumin; stir to combine.  
5. Pour in the vegetable broth, the saffron‑infused water, and the apricot halves. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then season with salt and pepper.  
6. Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven and bake, uncovered, for 15‑20 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken slightly.  
7. Remove from the oven; taste and adjust seasoning if needed.  
8. Serve the tagine over a bed of fluffy couscous or quinoa, sprinkle with toasted almond slices, and garnish with fresh cilantro leaves. Enjoy!
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Tagine

text:
Saffron‑Infused Coconut Lentil and Spinach Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 large onion, finely diced
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- ½ tsp saffron threads, steeped in 2 tbsp hot water
- 2 cups fresh spinach leaves, packed
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Juice of ½ lemon

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat; add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes.  
2. Stir in the garlic and ginger, cooking for another minute until fragrant.  
3. Add the turmeric, rinsed lentils, coconut milk, vegetable broth, and the saffron infusion; bring to a gentle boil.  
4. Reduce heat to low and simmer, uncovered, for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and the stew has thickened, stirring occasionally.  
5. Fold in the spinach leaves and cook for 2‑3 minutes, just until wilted. Season with salt, pepper, and lemon juice.  
6. Serve hot, garnished with a drizzle of coconut cream or a sprinkle of toasted pumpkin seeds if desired.
title: Saffron‑Infused Coconut Lentil and Spinach Stew

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into matchsticks
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional: a squeeze of fresh lemon juice for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a shallow bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, smoked paprika, and cumin.  
3. Toss the tempeh strips in the glaze, ensuring each piece is well‑coated. Arrange them on one side of the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Toss the carrot matchsticks with olive oil, salt, and pepper, and spread them on the other side of the sheet.  
5. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning the tempeh and carrots halfway through, until the tempeh is golden and the carrots are tender‑crisp.  
6. While the tempeh and carrots roast, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and season with salt and pepper.  
7. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large bowl; add the roasted carrots, toasted pumpkin seeds, and chopped parsley. Toss gently to combine.  
8. Slice the roasted tempeh into bite‑size pieces and arrange on top of the quinoa‑carrot salad. Drizzle any remaining pan glaze over the tempeh, and finish with a squeeze of lemon juice if desired.  
9. Serve warm or at room temperature, enjoying the sweet‑smoky tempeh alongside the crunchy carrot‑quinoa salad.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad

text:
Cinnamon‑Lime Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- 1 teaspoon lime zest
- 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice
- 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1/4 teaspoon sea salt
- 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
- 2 cups cooked quinoa
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro
- Optional: 1 avocado, sliced

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with half the olive oil, cinnamon, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
3. Roast the sweet potatoes for 20 minutes, then add the chickpeas tossed with the remaining olive oil, lime zest, lime juice, and a pinch of salt. Roast for another 15‑18 minutes, stirring halfway, until sweet potatoes are tender and chickpeas are crisp.  
4. While the vegetables roast, cook quinoa according to package instructions; fluff with a fork and set aside.  
5. Assemble the bowls: divide quinoa among serving bowls, top with the roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas, then add avocado slices if using.  
6. Garnish each bowl with chopped cilantro and an extra squeeze of lime juice. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Lime Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Bowl

text:
Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Carrot and Lentil Salad with Pomegranate  

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch sticks  
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed  
- 2 tablespoons olive oil  
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon  
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin  
- ¼ teaspoon smoked paprika  
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste  
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds  
- 2 tablespoons toasted pumpkin seeds  
- 2 cups mixed baby greens  
- 2 tablespoons lemon‑juice vinaigrette (lemon juice, olive oil, honey, Dijon mustard)  

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the carrot sticks with olive oil, cinnamon, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the carrots in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
4. While the carrots roast, combine the lentils with 2 cups water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, and cook uncovered for 20‑25 minutes, or until tender but still holding shape. Drain any excess water and season with a pinch of salt.  
5. In a large serving bowl, layer the mixed baby greens, cooked lentils, and roasted carrots. Drizzle the lemon‑juice vinaigrette over the top and toss gently to combine.  
6. Garnish the salad with pomegranate seeds and toasted pumpkin seeds for a burst of color and crunch. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Carrot and Lentil Salad with Pomegranate

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Shrimp and Pineapple Fried Rice

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 2 cups cooked jasmine rice, chilled
- 1 cup fresh pineapple chunks
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1 small carrot, finely diced
- 3 green onions, sliced (white and green parts separated)
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 2 tbsp coconut oil
- 2 tbsp soy sauce (or tamari for gluten‑free)
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tsp toasted coconut flakes
- ½ tsp red‑pepper flakes (optional for heat)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Pat the shrimp dry with paper towels and season lightly with salt and pepper.  
2. Heat 1 tbsp coconut oil in a large skillet or wok over medium‑high heat. Add the shrimp and sauté 2–3 minutes per side, until pink and opaque. Remove shrimp and set aside.  
3. Add the remaining 1 tbsp coconut oil to the pan. Toss in the garlic, ginger, and the white parts of the green onions; stir‑fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.  
4. Add the diced carrot and red bell pepper; cook 2 minutes, stirring frequently, until just tender.  
5. Stir in the chilled jasmine rice, breaking up any clumps. Drizzle the soy sauce and lime juice over the rice, mixing thoroughly to coat.  
6. Fold in the pineapple chunks and the cooked shrimp; continue to stir‑fry for another 2 minutes, allowing the pineapple to caramelize slightly.  
7. Sprinkle the red‑pepper flakes (if using), toasted coconut flakes, and the green parts of the green onions. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste.  
8. Transfer the fried rice to a serving platter, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve immediately. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Shrimp and Pineapple Fried Rice

text:
Saffron‑Infused Quinoa with Roasted Fennel and Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups vegetable broth
- ½ teaspoon saffron threads
- 1 large fennel bulb, thinly sliced
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds
- ¼ cup toasted hazelnuts, roughly chopped
- 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
- 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, chopped

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the sliced fennel with 1 tablespoon olive oil, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until caramelized and tender.
2. While the fennel roasts, place the saffron threads in a small bowl with 2 tablespoons hot water; let steep for 5 minutes.
3. In a medium saucepan, combine the rinsed quinoa, vegetable broth, and the saffron infusion (including the water). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy.
4. Remove the quinoa from heat and fluff with a fork. Stir in the lemon juice, and season with additional salt and pepper if needed.
5. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large serving bowl. Add the roasted fennel, pomegranate seeds, and toasted hazelnuts; gently toss to combine.
6. Sprinkle the chopped parsley over the top and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Saffron‑Infused Quinoa with Roasted Fennel and Pomegranate

text:
Saffron‑Infused Coconut Lentil and Kale Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 medium onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, grated
- 1 carrot, diced
- 1 celery stalk, diced
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon ground coriander
- ¼ teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon saffron threads, steeped in 2 tbsp hot water
- 1 can (14 oz) coconut milk
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 2 cups chopped kale, stems removed
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Juice of 1/2 lemon
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish (optional)

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes.
2. Stir in the garlic, ginger, carrot, and celery; cook for another 2‑3 minutes until the vegetables begin to soften.
3. Sprinkle the cumin, coriander, and smoked paprika over the vegetables; toast the spices
title: Saffron‑Infused Coconut Lentil and Kale Stew

text:
Harissa‑Spiced Roasted Eggplant and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cubed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 tbsp harissa paste
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1/4 cup toasted pine nuts
- 1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped
- 2 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
2. Toss the eggplant cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, harissa paste, cumin, salt, and pepper; spread on the sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway
title: Harissa‑Spiced Roasted Eggplant and Quinoa Salad

text:
Maple‑Glazed Roasted Beet and Chickpea Salad

Ingredients:
- 3 medium beets, peeled and cubed
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 4 cups mixed baby greens
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- 1 Tbsp apple cider vinegar
- 1 tsp Dijon mustard

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cubed beets with olive oil, maple syrup, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the beets on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, or until tender and caramelized, stirring once halfway through.  
4. While the beets roast, whisk together the apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of olive oil to make the dressing.  
5. In a separate skillet over medium heat, add the chickpeas and toast for 5‑7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lightly crisped.  
6. In a large serving bowl, combine the mixed baby greens, roasted beets, toasted chickpeas, and pumpkin seeds.  
7. Drizzle the dressing over the salad and toss gently to combine.  
8. Top with crumbled feta, if using, and serve immediately.
title: Maple‑Glazed Roasted Beet and Chickpea Salad

text:
Ginger‑Lime Baked Cod with Herb Quinoa Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 4 cod fillets (about 6 oz each)
- 2 tbsp fresh ginger, finely grated
- 2 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp lime zest
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups low‑sodium vegetable broth
- 1 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- 1 tbsp fresh dill, chopped
- 1 tbsp chives, sliced
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tbsp olive oil (for quinoa)
- 1 small garlic clove, minced

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together grated ginger, lime juice, lime zest, olive oil, salt, and pepper.  
3. Pat the cod fillets dry with paper towels, then brush both sides with the ginger‑lime mixture; place them on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Bake the cod for 12‑15 minutes, or until the flesh flakes easily with a fork.  
5. While the fish cooks, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed.  
6. Remove the quinoa from heat and let it sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
7. Stir olive oil, minced garlic, lemon juice, parsley, dill, and chives into the cooked quinoa; season with a pinch of salt and pepper to taste.  
8. Serve each cod fillet atop a generous scoop of herb quinoa pilaf, drizzling any pan juices over the top. Enjoy!
title: Ginger‑Lime Baked Cod with Herb Quinoa Pilaf

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Garlic Quinoa and Sautéed Kale

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp low‑sodium soy sauce
- 2 cloves garlic, minced (plus 1 whole clove for roasting)
- 1 Tbsp olive oil (divided)
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 4 cups kale, stems removed and torn into bite‑size pieces
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the whole garlic clove with a drizzle of olive oil, a pinch of salt, and spread it on a small baking sheet. Roast for 15 minutes, until soft and fragrant; set aside to cool, then squeeze the roasted garlic into a bowl.
2. In a shallow dish, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, minced garlic, and the roasted garlic puree. Add the tempeh strips, turning to coat evenly. Let marinate while you prepare the quinoa, about 5 minutes.
3. Meanwhile, combine the rinsed quinoa, vegetable broth, and the remaining ½ Tbsp olive oil in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.
4. Spread the cooked quinoa on a parchment‑lined baking sheet, drizzle with a little extra olive oil, and roast in the oven for 10‑12 minutes, stirring once, until the edges are lightly crisped. This adds a nutty, roasted flavor.
5. While the quinoa roasts, heat a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add a splash of olive oil, then add the marinated tempeh strips in a single layer. Cook for 3‑4 minutes per side, until golden brown and caramelized. Transfer to a plate and keep warm.
6. In the same skillet, add the kale and a pinch of salt. Sauté for 2‑3 minutes, until wilted but still bright green. Finish with lemon juice, pepper, and a drizzle of the pan‑drippings from the tempeh for extra flavor.
7. To serve, divide the roasted garlic quinoa among bowls, top with the maple‑glazed tempeh, and pile on the sautéed kale. Garnish with an extra squeeze of lemon or a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds if desired. Enjoy warm!
title: Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Garlic Quinoa and Sautéed Kale

text:
Cinnamon‑Roasted Pumpkin and Quinoa Salad with Pomegranate Vinaigrette

Ingredients:
- 2 cups cubed pumpkin (about 1/2‑inch pieces)
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1/4 cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 tablespoons toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 cups baby arugula
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the pumpkin cubes with olive oil, cinnamon, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway, until tender and caramelized.  
2. While the pumpkin roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes or until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside to cool slightly.  
3. In a small bowl, whisk together 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 tablespoon pomegranate molasses, 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard, a pinch of salt, and a squeeze of fresh lemon juice to create the vinaigrette.  
4. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted pumpkin, and baby arugula. Drizzle with the pomegranate vinaigrette and toss gently to coat evenly.  
5. Sprinkle the salad with toasted pumpkin seeds and pomegranate seeds for crunch and burst of flavor. Adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.  
6. Serve the salad warm or at room temperature as a hearty main or side dish. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Roasted Pumpkin and Quinoa Salad with Pomegranate Vinaigrette

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Eggplant and Barley Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 1 cup pearl barley, rinsed
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 teaspoon saffron threads
- ¼ cup hot water
- 1 medium onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- ½ cup golden raisins
- ¼ cup toasted slivered almonds
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
