1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the eggplant cubes with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender.  
2. While the eggplant roasts, place the saffron threads in the ¼ cup hot water and let steep for 5 minutes.  
3. In a medium saucepan, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 3‑4 minutes until translucent.  
4. Stir in the minced garlic and red bell pepper; cook for another 2 minutes.  
5. Add the rinsed barley to the saucepan, stirring to coat with the aromatics for 1‑2 minutes.  
6. Pour in the vegetable broth, the saffron‑infused water (including the threads), and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30‑35 minutes, or until the barley is tender and the liquid is absorbed.  
7. Once the barley is cooked, fold in the roasted eggplant, golden raisins, and toasted almonds. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste.  
8. Transfer the pilaf to a serving bowl, garnish with chopped fresh parsley, and serve warm.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Eggplant and Barley Pilaf

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 medium cauliflower head, cut into florets
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp saffron threads
- 2 Tbsp hot water
- 1 small yellow onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp ground coriander
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup toasted slivered almonds
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the cauliflower florets with 1 Tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender.  
2. While the cauliflower roasts, combine the saffron threads and hot water in a small bowl; let steep for 5 minutes.  
3. In a medium saucepan, bring 2 cups water to a boil. Add the rinsed quinoa, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.  
4. Heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté 3‑4 minutes until translucent. Stir in the garlic, cumin, and coriander; cook 1 minute more until fragrant.  
5. Add the drained chickpeas to the skillet and stir to coat with the spices; cook 2‑3 minutes until heated through.  
6. Pour the saffron‑infused water into the skillet, stirring to combine. Cook for another minute, allowing the saffron flavor to meld with the chickpeas.  
7. Gently fold the roasted cauliflower and cooked quinoa into the skillet, mixing until evenly distributed. Season with salt, pepper, and lemon juice; adjust seasoning as needed.  
8. Transfer the pilaf to a serving platter, sprinkle toasted slivered almonds over the top, and garnish with fresh cilantro leaves. Serve warm.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Pilaf

text:
Saffron‑Infused Coconut Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Lime

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup water
- ½ teaspoon saffron threads
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- Zest of 1 lime
- Juice of 1 lime
- 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, combine the saffron threads with 2 tablespoons of hot water; let steep for 5 minutes.
2. In a medium saucepan, combine the rinsed quinoa, coconut milk, water, and the saffron infusion (including the liquid). Bring to a boil over medium‑high heat.
3. Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is tender. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
4. While the quinoa cooks, preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
5. In a mixing bowl, toss the chickpeas with olive oil, smoked paprika, ground cumin, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.
6. Spread the seasoned chickpeas in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until the chickpeas are golden and crisp.
7. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large bowl. Add lime zest, lime juice, and half of the chopped cilantro; toss gently to combine. Adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.
8. Divide the saffron‑infused quinoa among serving bowls. Top each bowl with a generous handful of roasted chickpeas and sprinkle with the remaining cilantro.
9. Serve warm or at room temperature, optionally with extra lime wedges on the side. Enjoy!
title: Saffron‑Infused Coconut Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Lime

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Lentil Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 medium beets, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup cooked green lentils
- 1/4 cup maple syrup
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- 2 cups mixed baby greens
- 1/4 cup toasted walnuts, chopped
- 2 tablespoons crumbled feta cheese
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, olive oil, cinnamon, salt, and pepper; toss the beet cubes in the mixture until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the beets on the prepared sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning once, until tender and caramelized.  
4. In a large salad bowl combine the roasted beets, cooked lentils, baby greens, and toasted walnuts; toss gently.  
5. Sprinkle the crumbled feta over the top and serve the salad warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Lentil Salad

text:
Maple‑Miso Glazed Eggplant with Coconut Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 2 medium eggplants, sliced into ½‑inch rounds
- 3 Tbsp maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp white miso paste
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
- 1 cup coconut quinoa (cooked according to package instructions)
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- 1 lime, cut into wedges
- 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a small bowl whisk together the maple syrup, miso paste, soy sauce, and sesame oil until smooth.
3. Brush both sides of each eggplant slice with the glaze, then place them on the prepared baking sheet. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
4. Roast the eggplant for 20‑25 minutes, flipping halfway through, until the edges are caramelized and the flesh is tender.
5. While the eggplant roasts, prepare the coconut quinoa: combine ½ cup quinoa with 1 cup coconut milk and a pinch of salt in a saucepan, bring to a boil, then simmer covered for 15 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
6. To serve, spoon a bed of coconut quinoa onto each plate, top with the glazed eggplant slices, sprinkle with cilantro, toasted sesame seeds, and a squeeze of lime juice. Enjoy warm.
title: Maple‑Miso Glazed Eggplant with Coconut Quinoa

text:
Coconut‑Lime Spiced Carrot and Chickpea Tagine  

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into ½‑inch rounds  
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed  
- 1 small onion, finely diced  
- 2 cloves garlic, minced  
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated  
- 1 tbsp coconut oil  
- 1 tbsp tomato paste  
- 1 cup vegetable broth  
- ½ cup coconut milk  
- 1 tsp ground cumin  
- 1 tsp ground coriander  
- ½ tsp ground cinnamon  
- ½ tsp smoked paprika  
- Zest of 1 lime  
- Juice of 1 lime  
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste  
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish  
- Cooked couscous or quinoa, for serving  

Instructions:
1. Heat the coconut oil in a heavy‑bottomed pot over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes.  
2. Stir in the garlic and ginger; cook for another 30 seconds until fragrant.  
3. Add the tomato paste, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, and smoked paprika. Cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute to toast the spices.  
4. Toss in the carrot rounds and chickpeas, coating them evenly with the spice mixture.  
5. Pour in the vegetable broth and bring the mixture to a gentle boil. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 12‑15 minutes, or until the carrots are tender.  
6. Stir in the coconut milk, lime zest, and lime juice. Simmer uncovered for 3‑4 minutes to thicken the sauce slightly.  
7. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Adjust lime juice if a brighter acidity is desired.  
8. Spoon the tagine over a bed of cooked couscous or quinoa. Garnish generously with fresh cilantro leaves and serve hot.
title: Coconut‑Lime Spiced Carrot and Chickpea Tagine

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Lentil Tacos

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 ½ cups cooked green or brown lentils (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 8 small corn tortillas
- ½ cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- 1 avocado, sliced
- 1 lime, cut into wedges
- ¼ cup diced red onion
- 2 Tbsp Greek yogurt or vegan sour cream (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a large bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, cinnamon, smoked paprika, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Add the diced sweet potatoes and toss to coat evenly.
3. Spread the sweet potatoes in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until tender and caramelized.
4. While the sweet potatoes roast, place the cooked lentils in a small saucepan over low heat. Add a pinch of salt and pepper and warm through, stirring occasionally.
5. Warm the corn tortillas: wrap them in a damp paper towel and microwave for 30‑45 seconds, or heat them directly on a dry skillet for 30 seconds per side.
6. Assemble each taco: place a spoonful of lentils on the tortilla, top with roasted sweet potatoes, a few slices of avocado, a sprinkle of red onion, and crumbled feta if using.
7. Drizzle a dollop of Greek yogurt or vegan sour cream over the filling, then garnish with fresh cilantro and a squeeze of lime juice.
8. Serve immediately, with extra lime wedges on the side. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Lentil Tacos

text:
Maple‑Glazed Eggplant and Quinoa Stuffed Portobello Caps

Ingredients:
- 4 large portobello mushroom caps, stems removed and gills scraped
- 1 medium eggplant, diced into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 small red onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 cups fresh spinach, roughly chopped
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- ½ tsp dried thyme
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the diced eggplant with 1 Tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, thyme, salt, and pepper. Spread the eggplant on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until caramelized and tender.  
3. While the eggplant roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
4. Heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Sauté the onion until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add the garlic and cook another 30 seconds. Stir in the roasted eggplant, cooked quinoa, and spinach; cook until the spinach wilts, about 2 minutes. Season with additional salt, pepper, and lemon juice.  
5. Place the portobello caps gill‑side up on a clean baking sheet. Spoon the quinoa‑eggplant mixture evenly into each cap, pressing gently to fill. Sprinkle crumbled feta over the tops.  
6. Bake the stuffed caps for 12‑15 minutes, until the mushrooms are tender and the feta is lightly golden.  
7. Remove from the oven, let cool for a couple of minutes, then serve warm, garnished with a drizzle of extra maple syrup if desired.
title: Maple‑Glazed Eggplant and Quinoa Stuffed Portobello Caps

text:
Spiced Maple‑Glazed Eggplant and Quinoa Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- 1/2 tsp ground coriander
- 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 small red onion, finely diced
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1/2 cup dried cranberries
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together maple syrup, soy sauce, smoked paprika, cumin, coriander, cayenne, and a pinch of salt; add the eggplant cubes and toss to coat evenly.  
3. Spread the glazed eggplant on the prepared baking sheet and drizzle with 1 tablespoon olive oil; roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and caramelized.  
4. While the eggplant roasts, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the diced red onion and sauté for 3‑4 minutes until translucent.  
5. Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another 30 seconds until fragrant.  
6. Add the rinsed quinoa to the saucepan, toast lightly for 2 minutes, then pour in the vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low,
title: Spiced Maple‑Glazed Eggplant and Quinoa Pilaf

text:
Cinnamon‑Orange Roasted Carrot and Lentil Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch rounds
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- Zest of 1 orange
- 2 tbsp freshly squeezed orange juice
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1/2 tsp sea salt
- 1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 2 cups mixed baby greens
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tbsp crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- Fresh mint leaves for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the carrot rounds with 1 tbsp olive oil, cinnamon, orange zest, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the carrots in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
4. While the carrots roast, combine the lentils with 2 cups water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, and cook uncovered for 20‑25 minutes, or until lentils are tender but still hold their shape. Drain any excess water.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, orange juice, maple syrup, and a pinch of salt to create the dressing.  
6. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked lentils, roasted carrots, and mixed baby greens. Drizzle the orange‑cinnamon dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat.  
7. Transfer the salad to serving plates, sprinkle with toasted pumpkin seeds, crumbled feta (if using), and garnish with fresh mint leaves.  
8. Serve warm or at room temperature, enjoying the sweet‑spicy harmony of cinnamon, orange, and earthy lentils.
title: Cinnamon‑Orange Roasted Carrot and Lentil Salad

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Acorn Squash and Chickpea Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 medium acorn squash, halved and seeded
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 tsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 1 cup long‑grain brown rice, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 small red onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- Juice of ½ lemon

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Place the acorn squash halves cut‑side up on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, cinnamon, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Brush the mixture generously over the flesh of the squash.  
3. Roast the squash for 25‑30 minutes, or until the flesh is tender and caramelized. Remove from the oven and set aside to cool slightly.  
4. While the squash roasts, heat a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add a drizzle of olive oil and sauté the red onion until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for another 30 seconds.  
5. Stir in the brown rice, cumin, smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt. Toast the rice for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.  
6. Pour in the vegetable broth, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40‑45 minutes, or until the rice is cooked and the liquid is absorbed.  
7. In the last 5 minutes of the rice cooking, fold the chickpeas into the pot to warm through.  
8. When the squash is cool enough to handle, scoop out the roasted flesh and mash it lightly with a fork; season with a little extra salt if needed.  
9. Fluff the rice‑chickpea mixture with a fork and gently fold in the mashed squash, lemon juice, and toasted pumpkin seeds.  
10. Transfer the pilaf to a serving bowl, garnish with chopped parsley, and serve warm. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Acorn Squash and Chickpea Pilaf

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp saffron threads, steeped in 2 Tbsp hot water
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup toasted slivered almonds
- 2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 Tbsp honey or maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cauliflower florets and chickpeas with olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika, the saffron infusion (including the liquid), salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the cauliflower is golden‑brown and tender and the chickpeas are crisp.  
4. While the vegetables roast, whisk together lemon juice, honey (or maple syrup), and a pinch of salt to make the dressing.  
5. Transfer the roasted cauliflower and chickpeas to a serving bowl. Drizzle the dressing over the hot vegetables and toss gently to combine.  
6. Sprinkle toasted slivered almonds and chopped parsley on top for crunch and freshness. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Salad

text:
Cinnamon‑Lime Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 medium sweet potatoes
title: Cinnamon‑Lime Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Buddha Bowl

text:
Spiced Cardamom Roasted Cauliflower and Quinoa Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 medium cauliflower head, cut into florets
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cardamom
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- 1/4 tsp sea salt
- 1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 1/4 cup toasted almond slivers
- 1/4 cup dried cranberries
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cauliflower florets with olive oil, ground cardamom, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the seasoned cauliflower on the prepared baking sheet in a single layer. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway through, until golden‑brown and tender.  
4. While the cauliflower roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together lemon juice and maple syrup to create a light dressing.  
6. Assemble the bowl: start with a base of cooked quinoa, top with roasted cauliflower, sprinkle toasted almond slivers and dried cranberries over the top, and drizzle the lemon‑maple dressing evenly.  
7. Garnish with chopped fresh cilantro if desired, serve warm or at room temperature, and enjoy!
title: Spiced Cardamom Roasted Cauliflower and Quinoa Bowl

text:
Ginger‑Lime Roasted Cauliflower Steaks with Turmeric Quinoa  

Ingredients:
- 1 large cauliflower head, sliced into 1‑inch “steaks”
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 Tbsp fresh ginger, minced
- 2 Tbsp lime juice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups vegetable broth
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- ¼ tsp cumin
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, minced ginger, lime juice, garlic, salt, and pepper.  
3. Brush both sides of the cauliflower steaks generously with the ginger‑lime mixture and place them on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast the cauliflower for 20‑25 minutes, flipping halfway through, until golden‑brown and tender.  
5. While the cauliflower roasts, combine quinoa, vegetable broth, turmeric, and cumin in a medium saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy.  
6. Remove the quinoa from heat and let it sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.  
7. To serve, plate a cauliflower steak, spoon a generous mound of turmeric quinoa beside it, and drizzle any remaining pan juices over the top.  
8. Garnish with chopped cilantro, if desired, and enjoy immediately.
title: Ginger‑Lime Roasted Cauliflower Steaks with Turmeric Quinoa

text:
Sage‑Infused Wild Rice and Roasted Butternut Squash Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup wild rice, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 small butternut squash, peeled and cubed (about 3 cups)
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp dried sage
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup dried cranberries
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- 2 tbsp apple cider vinaigrette
- 1 tbsp maple syrup

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the cubed butternut squash with olive oil, dried sage, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread evenly on the prepared sheet.  
3. Roast the squash for 25‑30 minutes, turning once, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
4. While the squash roasts, combine the wild rice and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 45‑50 minutes, or until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside to cool slightly.  
5. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked wild rice, roasted squash, dried cranberries, toasted pumpkin seeds, and chopped parsley.  
6. Drizzle the apple cider vinaigrette and maple syrup over the salad; toss gently to coat everything evenly.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.  
8. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with an extra sprinkle of pumpkin seeds and a few parsley leaves. Enjoy!
title: Sage‑Infused Wild Rice and Roasted Butternut Squash Salad

text:
Saffron‑Infused Coconut Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Lime  

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- ½ cup water
- ¼ teaspoon saffron threads
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1 lime, zest and juice
- ½ teaspoon sea salt
- ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, chopped (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, toss the chickpeas with 1 tablespoon olive oil, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread them on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking halfway, until crisp and golden.  
3. While the chickpeas roast, place the saffron threads in a tablespoon of hot water and let steep for 5 minutes.  
4. In a medium saucepan, combine the quinoa, coconut milk, water, and the saffron infusion (including the threads). Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is tender. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
5. Stir the lime zest, lime juice, and remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil into the cooked quinoa; season with additional salt and pepper to taste.  
6. Transfer the quinoa to a serving bowl, top with the roasted chickpeas, and garnish with chopped cilantro if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Saffron‑Infused Coconut Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Lime

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tbsp olive oil, divided
- 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into matchsticks
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 small red onion, thinly sliced
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Juice of ½ lime

Instructions:
1. In a shallow bowl, whisk together maple syrup, soy sauce, smoked paprika, cumin, and ½ tbsp olive oil. Add the tempeh strips, toss to coat, and let marinate while you prepare the vegetables (about 10 minutes).  
2. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Spread the carrot matchsticks on the sheet, drizzle with the remaining ½ tbsp olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and roast for 15‑18 minutes, turning once, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
3. While the carrots roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.  
4. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated tempeh strips in a single layer and cook 3‑4 minutes per side, until golden brown and caramelized. Transfer to a plate.  
5. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted carrots, sliced red onion, toasted pumpkin seeds, and chopped cilantro. Drizzle with lime juice, season with salt and pepper, and toss gently to combine.  
6. Divide the quinoa salad among serving bowls or plates. Top each portion with the maple‑glazed tempeh strips. Garnish with extra cilantro or pumpkin seeds if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad

text:
Spiced Cardamom Sweet Potato and Chickpea Tacos

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon ground cardamom
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- ¼ teaspoon ground cumin
- ¼ teaspoon cayenne pepper (optional)
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 8 small corn tortillas
- ½ cup red cabbage, thinly sliced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 2 tablespoons lime juice
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- 2 tablespoons plain Greek yogurt or vegan yogurt
- 1 teaspoon honey or maple syrup (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the diced sweet potatoes with olive oil, ground cardamom, smoked paprika, cumin, cayenne, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the seasoned sweet potatoes on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
4. While the sweet potatoes roast, heat a skillet over medium heat. Add the chickpeas and a drizzle of olive oil; sauté for 5‑7 minutes until slightly crisp, then season with a pinch of salt and pepper.  
5. In a small bowl, combine lime juice, yogurt, and honey or maple syrup; stir to create a quick lime‑yogurt drizzle.  
6. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet or microwave for 30 seconds, keeping them covered to stay pliable.  
7. Assemble each taco: place a spoonful of roasted sweet potatoes, followed by sautéed chickpeas, red cabbage, and a sprinkle of cilantro. Drizzle with the lime‑yogurt sauce and top with feta, if using.  
8. Serve immediately with extra lime wedges on the side. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Cardamom Sweet Potato and Chickpea Tacos

text:
Cinnamon‑Saffron Roasted Cauliflower and Quinoa Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 small head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp saffron threads, steeped in 2 tbsp warm water
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 2 green onions, thinly sliced
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cauliflower florets with olive oil, cinnamon, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the seasoned cauliflower on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden‑brown and tender.  
4. While the cauliflower roasts, combine quinoa and 2 cups water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes or until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together the saffron‑infused water, lemon juice, maple syrup, and a pinch of salt to create the dressing.  
6. In a large serving bowl, layer the cooked quinoa, roasted cauliflower, toasted pumpkin seeds, green onions, and cilantro.  
7. Drizzle the saffron‑cinnamon dressing over the bowl and toss gently to combine.  
8. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with extra cilantro if desired.
title: Cinnamon‑Saffron Roasted Cauliflower and Quinoa Bowl

text:
Spiced Cardamom Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch sticks
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cardamom
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 1/4 cup dried cranberries
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp honey or maple syrup
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the carrot sticks with olive oil, ground cardamom, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the carrots in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
4. While the carrots roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together lemon juice, honey (or maple syrup), a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of olive oil to create the dressing.  
6. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted carrots, toasted pumpkin seeds, dried cranberries, and chopped parsley.  
7. Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly.  
8. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if desired.  
9. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with extra parsley or pumpkin seeds if desired.
title: Spiced Cardamom Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Sweet Corn and Avocado Salsa

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 cups fresh or frozen sweet corn kernels
- 1 ripe avocado, diced
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp olive oil (plus extra for roasting)
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- 1 lime, juiced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- ¼ cup red onion, finely diced
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the corn kernels with 1 Tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of pepper; spread them in a single layer on the sheet and roast for 15‑18 minutes, stirring halfway, until lightly caramelized.  
3. While the corn roasts, whisk together the maple syrup, cumin, smoked paprika, lime juice, and a pinch of salt in a shallow bowl.  
4. Add the cubed tofu to the bowl and gently toss to coat evenly with the glaze. Let it sit for 5 minutes.  
5. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. Add the glazed tofu and cook, turning occasionally, until all sides are golden and the glaze thickens, about 6‑8 minutes.  
6. In a small mixing bowl, combine the diced avocado, roasted corn, red onion, cilantro, a squeeze of lime juice, and a drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper to taste; gently toss.  
7. To serve, arrange the maple‑glazed tofu on plates, top with the avocado‑corn salsa, and garnish with extra cilantro or lime wedges if desired. Enjoy warm or at room temperature.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Sweet Corn and Avocado Salsa

text:
Sage‑Infused Pumpkin and Lentil Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 cup dried green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 cups pumpkin puree (fresh or canned)
- 1 large onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 carrot, diced
- 1 celery stalk, diced
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground sage
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh sage leaves, for garnish (optional)

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, and celery; sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
2. Stir in the garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
3. Add the rinsed lentils, pumpkin puree, vegetable broth, and coconut milk. Mix well.
4. Sprinkle in the ground sage, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil.
5. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25‑30 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and the stew has thickened.
6. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. If the stew is too thick, add a splash of broth or water.
7. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with fresh sage leaves, and serve hot.
title: Sage‑Infused Pumpkin and Lentil Stew

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Lentil and Spinach Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 carrot, diced
- 2 cups fresh spinach, roughly chopped
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Juice of 1 lemon

Instructions:
1. Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes.  
2. Stir in the garlic, ginger, turmeric, cumin, and smoked paprika; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
3. Add the diced carrot and rinsed lentils, then pour in the vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer.  
4. Cover and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and the mixture has thickened.  
5. Stir in the chopped spinach and cook for 2‑3 minutes until wilted.  
6. Season with salt, pepper, and lemon juice. Adjust seasoning as needed.  
7. Serve hot, garnished with a drizzle of olive oil or fresh herbs if desired.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Lentil and Spinach Stew

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa Stuffed Sweet Potatoes

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups coconut milk
- 1 tablespoon lime zest
- 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ cup canned black beans, drained and rinsed
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Optional garnish: sliced avocado and toasted coconut flakes

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Scrub the sweet potatoes, pierce each several times with a fork, and place them on a baking sheet.
2. Roast the sweet potatoes for 45‑55 minutes, or until tender when pierced with a knife.
3. While the potatoes roast, combine quinoa and coconut milk in a medium saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy.
4. Remove the quinoa from heat and stir in lime zest, lime juice, cumin, smoked paprika, black beans, and cilantro. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
5. When the sweet potatoes are done, let them cool slightly, then slice each lengthwise down the center, being careful not to cut all the way through.
6. Fluff the quinoa mixture and spoon it generously into the openings of each sweet potato, allowing the filling to mound on top.
7. Garnish with sliced avocado and toasted coconut flakes, if desired, and serve warm. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa Stuffed Sweet Potatoes

text:
Crispy Pomegranate‑Balsamic Tofu with Herbed Couscous

Ingredients:
- 1 block (14 oz) extra‑firm tofu, pressed and cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 2 Tbsp pomegranate molasses
- 1 Tbsp balsamic vinegar
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp garlic powder
- 2 Tbsp cornstarch
- 3 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 cup couscous
- 1 ¼ cup vegetable broth
- ¼ cup fresh parsley, finely chopped
- 2 Tbsp fresh mint, chopped
- Zest of 1 lemon
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional garnish: pomegranate seeds and lemon wedges

Instructions:
1. In a shallow bowl, whisk together pomegranate molasses, balsamic vinegar, soy sauce, smoked paprika, and garlic powder. Add the tofu cubes and toss gently to coat; let marinate for 10 minutes.  
2. Sprinkle the cornstarch over the marinated tofu and toss until each piece is lightly coated.  
3. Heat 2 Tbsp olive oil in a large non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the tofu and cook, turning occasionally, until all sides are golden and crisp, about 6‑8 minutes. Transfer tofu to a plate and drizzle with the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil.  
4. Meanwhile, bring the vegetable broth to a boil in a medium saucepan. Stir in the couscous, cover, and remove from heat. Let stand for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.  
5. Stir the chopped parsley, mint, lemon zest, and a pinch of salt and pepper into the couscous. Adjust seasoning to taste.  
6. To serve, spoon a bed of herbed couscous onto each plate, top with the crispy pomegranate‑balsamic tofu, and garnish with extra pomegranate seeds and a lemon wedge if desired. Enjoy while hot!
title: Crispy Pomegranate‑Balsamic Tofu with Herbed Couscous

text:
Spiced Maple‑Glazed Eggplant and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup
- 1 tablespoon soy sauce or tamari
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- 2 tablespoons olive oil, divided
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 green onions, sliced
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Juice of 1 lime

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, smoked paprika, cumin, 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper. Add the eggplant cubes, toss to coat, and spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until caramelized and tender.  
3. While the eggplant roasts, cook the quinoa: combine quinoa and 2 cups water in a saucepan, bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside to cool slightly.  
4. In a small skillet over medium heat, toast the pumpkin seeds with a pinch of salt for 2‑3 minutes, stirring frequently, until fragrant. Remove from heat.  
5. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted eggplant, diced red bell pepper, toasted pumpkin seeds, and sliced green onions. Drizzle with the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil and lime juice, then toss gently to distribute. Adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice as desired.  
6. Serve the salad warm or at room temperature, garnished with extra pumpkin seeds or a drizzle of maple syrup if you like a sweeter finish. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Maple‑Glazed Eggplant and Quinoa Salad

text:
Spiced Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa and Roasted Broccoli

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- 1 Tbsp lime juice
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- 1 large head broccoli, cut into florets
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a shallow bowl, whisk together maple syrup, soy sauce, smoked paprika, cumin, ginger, and garlic. Toss the tempeh strips in the mixture until fully coated, then spread them on the prepared baking sheet.  
3. In a separate bowl, toss broccoli florets with 1 Tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper. Arrange the broccoli on the same baking sheet, keeping a space between the tempeh.  
4. Roast the tempeh and broccoli for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway through, until the tempeh is caramelized and the broccoli is tender and lightly charred.  
5. While the tempeh and broccoli roast, combine quinoa and coconut milk in a medium saucepan. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes.  
6. Fluff the quinoa with a fork, then stir in lime juice, lime zest, and chopped cilantro. Season with salt and pepper to taste.  
7. To serve, divide the coconut‑lime quinoa among plates, top with the maple‑glazed tempeh strips, and arrange the roasted broccoli alongside. Garnish with extra cilantro or a drizzle of maple syrup if desired. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa and Roasted Broccoli

text:
Spiced Cardamom Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch sticks
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cardamom
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 1/4 cup dried cranberries
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp honey or maple syrup
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the carrot sticks with olive oil, ground cardamom, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the carrots in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
4. While the carrots roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together lemon juice, honey (or maple syrup), a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of olive oil to create the dressing.  
6. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted carrots, toasted pumpkin seeds, dried cranberries, and chopped parsley.  
7. Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly.  
8. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if needed.  
9. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with extra parsley or pumpkin seeds if desired. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Cardamom Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad

text:
Saffron‑Infused Lentil and Spinach Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup long‑grain basmati rice, rinsed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 small onion, finely diced
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- ¼ teaspoon ground coriander
- ½ teaspoon saffron threads, steeped in 2 tablespoons hot water
- 3 cups fresh spinach, roughly chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Juice of ½ lemon
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish (optional)

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan, combine the lentils and vegetable broth; bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer, uncovered, for about 15 minutes until the lentils are just tender.
2. While the lentils cook, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 3–4 minutes until translucent.
3. Stir in the minced garlic, cumin, and coriander; cook for another 30 seconds until fragrant.
4. Add the rinsed rice to the skillet, stirring to coat each grain with the aromatics. Cook for 2 minutes, then pour in the saffron‑infused water and stir to combine.
5. Transfer the partially cooked rice mixture to the saucepan with the lentils. Add a pinch of salt and bring the combined mixture back to a gentle boil, then cover and simmer for 12–15 minutes, or until both the rice and lentils are fully cooked and the liquid is absorbed.
6. Remove the pot from heat and gently fold in the chopped spinach; cover for 2 minutes to allow the spinach to wilt.
7. Finish with a squeeze of lemon juice, adjust seasoning with salt and pepper, and fluff the pilaf with a fork.
8. Serve hot, garnished with fresh cilantro leaves if desired. Enjoy!
title: Saffron‑Infused Lentil and Spinach Pilaf

text:
Spiced Maple‑Glazed Pumpkin and Quinoa Salad with Pomegranate Vinaigrette

Ingredients:
- 2 cups cubed pumpkin (about 1 lb)
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- ¼ teaspoon ground cinnamon
- ¼ teaspoon sea salt
- 2 tablespoons olive oil, divided
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 cups mixed baby greens
- 2 tablespoons pomegranate molasses
- 1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar
- 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard
- Freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the pumpkin cubes with 1 tablespoon olive oil, maple syrup, cumin, smoked paprika, cinnamon, and sea salt until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the seasoned pumpkin on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and caramelized.  
4. While the pumpkin roasts, combine the rinsed quinoa with 2 cups water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside to cool slightly.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together pomegranate molasses, apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, and a pinch of black pepper to create the vinaigrette.  
6. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted pumpkin, mixed baby greens, pomegranate seeds, and toasted pumpkin seeds.  
7. Drizzle the vinaigrette over the salad and toss gently to distribute the dressing evenly.  
8. Serve immediately, garnished with an extra sprinkle of pomegranate seeds and pumpkin seeds if desired. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Maple‑Glazed Pumpkin and Quinoa Salad with Pomegranate Vinaigrette

text:
Spiced Orange‑Maple Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Brussels Sprouts  

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed  
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth  
- 1 lb Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved  
- 2 cloves garlic, minced  
- 1 tbsp olive oil  
- 1 tbsp pure maple syrup  
- Zest of 1 orange  
- ½ tsp smoked paprika  
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste  

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).  
2. In a bowl, toss the Brussels sprouts with olive oil, minced garlic, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread them cut‑side down on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until caramelized and tender.  
3. While the sprouts roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.  
4. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl. Stir in the orange zest and maple syrup, mixing until evenly coated. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.  
5. Add the roasted Brussels sprouts to the quinoa, gently tossing to combine.  
6. Serve warm, garnished with an extra drizzle of maple syrup or a sprinkle of orange zest if desired.
title: Spiced Orange‑Maple Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Brussels Sprouts

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 medium head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp freshly grated ginger
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- ¼ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 2 cups mixed baby greens
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- Optional: 2 Tbsp crumbled feta cheese

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cauliflower florets and chickpeas with olive oil, turmeric, ginger, lemon zest, garlic, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway, until the cauliflower is golden‑brown and the chickpeas are crisp.  
4. While the vegetables roast, whisk together the lemon juice and a drizzle of olive oil to make a simple dressing.  
5. In a serving bowl, combine the mixed greens, roasted cauliflower‑chickpea mixture, toasted pumpkin seeds, and feta (if using). Drizzle with the lemon dressing and toss gently to combine.  
6. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with extra lemon zest if desired.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Salad

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- ½ teaspoon saffron threads
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 small onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- Zest of 1 lemon
- ¼ cup toasted sliced almonds
- 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the carrot cubes with 1  tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.
2. While the carrots roast, place the saffron threads in a small bowl, cover with 2 tablespoons hot water, and let steep for 5 minutes.
3. In a medium saucepan, heat the remaining 1  tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 3‑4 minutes until translucent. Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another 30 seconds.
4. Add the rinsed quinoa to the saucepan, stirring to coat with the onion‑garlic mixture. Pour in the vegetable broth, saffron‑infused water (including the threads), and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the quinoa is fluffy and the liquid is absorbed.
5. Once the quinoa is cooked, gently fold in the roasted carrots, chickpeas, lemon zest, and toasted almonds. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
6. Transfer the pilaf to a serving bowl, garnish with chopped fresh parsley, and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Pilaf

text:
Roasted Garlic & Herb Farro with Lemon‑Parmesan Kale

Ingredients:
- 1 cup farro, rinsed
- 2 ½ cups low‑sodium vegetable broth
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon dried thyme
- 1 teaspoon dried oregano
- ½ teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes (optional)
- 4 cups kale, stems removed and torn into bite‑size pieces
- zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
- ¼ cup grated Parmesan cheese
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan, combine the rinsed farro and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the farro is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.
2. While the farro cooks, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and sauté for 30 seconds, until fragrant but not browned.
3. Stir in the dried thyme, oregano, and red pepper flakes; cook for another 30 seconds to release the herbs’ aromas.
4. Add the kale to the skillet, tossing to coat it in the garlic‑herb oil. Cook, stirring frequently, for 4‑5 minutes, until the kale is wilted but still bright green. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
5. Transfer the cooked farro to the skillet with the kale. Add the lemon zest, lemon juice, and grated Parmesan. Toss everything together until well combined and the cheese melts slightly, creating a light sauce.
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if desired. Serve warm, garnished with extra Parmesan or a drizzle of olive oil if you like. Enjoy!
title: Roasted Garlic & Herb Farro with Lemon‑Parmesan Kale

text:
Spiced Cardamom Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cardamom
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp sea salt
- 2 cups mixed baby greens
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tbsp honey
- 1 tbsp Dijon mustard

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes and chickpeas with olive oil, ground cardamom, smoked paprika, and sea salt until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the sweet potatoes are tender and lightly caramelized.  
4. While the vegetables roast, whisk together lemon juice, honey, and Dijon mustard in a small bowl to create the dressing.  
5. In a serving platter, arrange the mixed baby greens. Top with the roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas, then drizzle the lemon‑honey dressing over the salad.  
6. Sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds on top for crunch and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Spiced Cardamom Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Salad

text:
Citrus‑Glazed Seared Scallops with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 12 sea scallops, patted dry
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups coconut milk
- 1 tablespoon lime zest
- 2 tablespoons lime juice
- 2 tablespoons orange marmalade
- 1 tablespoon soy sauce
- 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 2 teaspoons olive oil
- 1 tablespoon butter
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Lime wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine the quinoa and coconut milk; bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is tender. Remove from heat, fluff with a fork, stir in lime zest and lime juice, and set aside.  
2. While the quinoa cooks, whisk together orange marmalade, soy sauce, grated ginger, minced garlic, and a pinch of salt in a small bowl to create the citrus glaze.  
3. Heat 1 tsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Pat the scallops with a little salt and pepper, then add them to the hot pan, leaving space between each piece. Sear for 2‑3 minutes without moving, until a golden crust forms. Flip and sear the other side for another 1‑2 minutes, until just opaque in the center.  
4. Reduce the heat to medium and pour the citrus glaze over the scallops. Cook, gently spooning the glaze over the scallops, for 1‑2 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the scallops. Remove the pan from heat and stir in the butter for a glossy finish.  
5. Divide the coconut‑lime quinoa among serving plates. Top each mound with three seared scallops, drizzle any remaining glaze from the pan over the top, and garnish with fresh cilantro leaves and lime wedges. Serve immediately.
title: Citrus‑Glazed Seared Scallops with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa

text:
Cinnamon‑Saffron Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 3 large carrots, peeled and sliced into sticks
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp ground cinnamon
- ¼ tsp saffron threads, dissolved in 1 tbsp warm water
- 1 cup cooked quinoa
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tbsp plain Greek yogurt
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the carrot sticks and chickpeas with olive oil, ground cinnamon, the saffron‑water mixture, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the seasoned carrots and chickpeas in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway through, until the carrots are tender and caramelized and the chickpeas are crisp.  
4. While the vegetables roast, prepare the quinoa according to package instructions; fluff with a fork and set aside.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together the Greek yogurt, lemon juice, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of olive oil to create a creamy dressing.  
6. To assemble the Buddha bowl, divide the cooked quinoa among two serving bowls. Top each with the roasted carrots, crispy chickpeas, toasted pumpkin seeds, and a dollop of the yogurt‑lemon dressing.  
7. Garnish with fresh cilantro leaves and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Saffron Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

text:
Citrus‑Ginger Chickpea and Quinoa Power Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups water
- 1 (15 oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tsp orange zest
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- 1 cup baby spinach
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Combine quinoa and water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
2. Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add grated ginger and sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.  
3. Add chickpeas, cumin, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring, 5‑6 minutes until chickpeas are lightly browned.  
4. Stir in diced red bell pepper and cook another 2 minutes, keeping the pepper crisp.  
5. Remove from heat; toss in baby spinach, lime juice, orange zest, and chopped cilantro; let the residual heat wilt the spinach.  
6. Divide quinoa into bowls, top with the chickpea‑vegetable mixture, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Citrus‑Ginger Chickpea and Quinoa Power Bowl

text:
Spiced Cardamom Roasted Beet and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 3 medium beets, peeled and cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cardamom
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp honey or maple syrup
- 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh mint
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the beet cubes with olive oil, ground cardamom, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread them on a baking sheet in a single layer.
2. Roast the beets for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until tender and caramelized. Remove from the oven and let cool slightly.
3. While the beets roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside to cool.
4. In a small bowl, whisk together lemon juice, honey (or maple syrup), apple cider vinegar, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of olive oil to create the dressing.
5. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted beets, toasted pumpkin seeds, chopped mint, and parsley. Drizzle the dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat evenly.
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if needed. Sprinkle crumbled feta on top, if using, and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Cardamom Roasted Beet and Quinoa Salad

text:
Spiced Maple‑Glazed Cauliflower and Chickpea Tacos

Ingredients:
- 1 small head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp ground coriander
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 8 small corn tortillas
- ½ cup red cabbage, thinly sliced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 avocado, sliced
- 2 Tbsp lime juice
- 1 Tbsp vegan sour cream (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together maple syrup, olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, coriander, cayenne, salt, and pepper.  
3. Add the cauliflower florets and chickpeas to the bowl, tossing to coat evenly with the spiced maple glaze.  
4. Spread the coated cauliflower and chickpeas in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
5. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the cauliflower is tender and caramelized and the chickpeas are crisp.  
6. While the vegetables roast, warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 30 seconds per side, then keep them covered to stay soft.  
7. In a small bowl, combine sliced avocado with lime juice, a pinch of salt, and gently toss.  
8. Assemble each taco: place a generous spoonful of roasted cauliflower and chickpeas on a tortilla, top with red cabbage, avocado slices, cilantro, and a drizzle of vegan sour cream if using.  
9. Serve immediately, enjoying the sweet‑spicy maple glaze with fresh toppings.
title: Spiced Maple‑Glazed Cauliflower and Chickpea Tacos

text:
Cinnamon‑Lime Roasted Carrot and Lentil Salad with Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch sticks
- 1 cup cooked green or brown lentils, rinsed and drained
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 Tbsp fresh lime juice
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the carrot sticks with olive oil, cinnamon, lime zest, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the carrots in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
4. While the carrots roast, combine the cooked lentils, lime juice, and cilantro in a mixing bowl; season with a pinch of salt and pepper.  
5. Once the carrots are done, let them cool slightly (about 5 minutes), then add them to the lentil mixture and toss gently to combine.  
6. Transfer the salad to a serving platter, sprinkle pomegranate seeds over the top for a burst of color and sweetness, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Lime Roasted Carrot and Lentil Salad with Pomegranate

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Lentil and Spinach Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 tablespoon coconut oil
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper (optional)
- 1 can (14 oz) coconut milk
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup water
- 1 tablespoon lime juice
- Zest of 1 lime
- 3 cups fresh spinach, roughly chopped
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Heat the coconut oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4–5 minutes.  
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for another minute until fragrant.  
3. Sprinkle in the turmeric, cumin, and cayenne (if using); toast the spices for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.  
4. Add the rinsed red lentils, coconut milk, vegetable broth, and water. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to a gentle simmer.  
5. Cover and let the stew simmer for 20–25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and the broth has thickened, stirring occasionally.  
6. Stir in the lime juice, lime zest, and chopped spinach. Cook for 2–3 minutes, just until the spinach wilts.  
7. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Adjust lime acidity if desired.  
8. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve hot with crusty bread or steamed rice.
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Lentil and Spinach Stew

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Roasted Carrot and Lentil Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch rounds
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp freshly grated ginger
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tsp honey or maple syrup
- 1/2 tsp sea salt
- 1/4 tsp black pepper
- 2 cups mixed baby greens
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the carrot rounds with 1 tbsp olive oil, turmeric, grated ginger, lemon zest, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the carrots in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
4. While the carrots roast, combine lentils with 2 cups water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, and cook 20‑25 minutes until tender but not mushy. Drain any excess water.  
5. In a small bowl whisk together remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, lemon juice, honey (or maple syrup), and a pinch of salt to make the dressing.  
6. In a large mixing bowl combine the cooked lentils, roasted carrots, baby greens, and dressing; toss gently to coat.  
7. Transfer the salad to serving plates, sprinkle with toasted pumpkin seeds and chopped parsley, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Roasted Carrot and Lentil Salad

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup basmati rice, rinsed
- 1/2 teaspoon saffron threads
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 small onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1/4 cup golden raisins
- 1/4 cup sliced toasted almonds
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss sweet potato cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast 20‑25 minutes until tender and caramelized.  
2. While sweet potatoes roast, place saffron threads in 2 Tbsp hot water; let steep 5 minutes.  
3. In a medium saucepan, heat remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil over medium heat. Add onion and sauté 3‑4 minutes until translucent; add garlic and cook 30 seconds more.  
4. Stir in
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Pilaf

text:
Crispy Sesame Tofu with Mango‑Chili Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 block firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 tbsp sesame oil
- 3 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp chili garlic sauce
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups water
- 1 ripe mango, diced
- 2 green onions, sliced
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Rinse the quinoa under cold water, then combine it with the water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until the water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, maple syrup, chili garlic sauce, and a pinch of salt.  
3. Heat the sesame oil in a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the tofu cubes and sauté until golden and crispy, about 6–8 minutes, turning occasionally.  
4. Pour the sauce over the tofu, toss to coat, and cook an additional 2 minutes until the glaze thickens.  
5. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, diced mango, sliced green onions, and toasted sesame seeds. Gently fold in the glazed tofu.  
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with extra salt, pepper, or chili sauce if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with a sprinkle of additional sesame seeds.
title: Crispy Sesame Tofu with Mango‑Chili Quinoa

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Shrimp and Avocado Quinoa Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups water
- 12 oz large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 tbsp coconut oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp lime zest
- 2 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tsp maple syrup
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 1 ripe avocado, diced
- ½ cup red cabbage, thinly sliced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds (optional)

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan, combine quinoa and water; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
2. While the quinoa cooks, whisk together lime zest, lime juice, maple syrup, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper in a small bowl to create the glaze.
3. Heat coconut oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add garlic and ginger, sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.
4. Add the shrimp to the skillet, pour the glaze over them, and cook 2‑3 minutes per side, or until shrimp turn pink and opaque. Remove from heat.
5. Assemble the bowls: divide the cooked quinoa among four serving bowls.
6. Top each quinoa base with equal portions of shrimp, diced avocado, red cabbage, and a sprinkle of cilantro.
7. Drizzle any remaining glaze from the pan over the bowls, and garnish with toasted sesame seeds if desired. Serve immediately.
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Shrimp and Avocado Quinoa Bowl

text:
Cinnamon‑Lime Roasted Chickpea and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice
- 1 tablespoon maple syrup
- ½ teaspoon sea salt
- ¼ teaspoon black pepper
- 1 small red bell pepper, diced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 2 green onions, thinly sliced
- Optional: ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds for garnish

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan, combine quinoa and water; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and set aside to cool.
2. While the quinoa cooks, preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
3. In a bowl, toss the chickpeas with olive oil, cinnamon, lime zest, salt, and pepper until evenly coated. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.
4. Roast the chickpeas for 20‑25 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until they are golden and crisp. Remove from oven and let cool slightly.
5. In a small mixing bowl, whisk together lime juice, maple syrup, and a pinch of salt to create the dressing.
6. In a large salad bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted chickpeas, diced red bell pepper, cilantro, and green onions. Drizzle the lime‑maple dressing over the mixture and toss gently to combine.
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired. Sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds on top for extra crunch, if using.
8. Serve the salad at room temperature or chilled; it pairs well with grilled fish or tofu for a complete meal. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Lime Roasted Chickpea and Quinoa Salad

text:
Turmeric‑Honey Glazed Cauliflower Steaks with Lemon‑Garlic Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 large cauliflower head
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 2 Tbsp honey
- 1 Tbsp turmeric powder
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 lemon, zest and juice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 Tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- 1 Tbsp toasted pine nuts (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Slice the cauliflower into ¾‑inch thick “steaks” by cutting from top to bottom; you should get 2‑3 usable steaks.  
3. In a small bowl whisk together olive oil, honey, turmeric, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper.  
4. Brush both sides of each cauliflower steak generously with the turmeric‑honey mixture and place on the prepared baking sheet.  
5. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, flipping halfway through, until the edges are caramelized and the center is tender.  
6. While the cauliflower roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed.  
7. Remove the quinoa from heat; fluff with a fork and stir in lemon zest, lemon juice, minced garlic, and a drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper to taste.  
8. Transfer the roasted cauliflower steaks to a serving platter. Spoon the lemon‑garlic quinoa around the steaks.  
9. Garnish with chopped parsley and toasted pine nuts, if using. Serve warm.
title: Turmeric‑Honey Glazed Cauliflower Steaks with Lemon‑Garlic Quinoa

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Shrimp and Mango Avocado Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 2 tbsp coconut oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- Zest of 1 lime
- Juice of 2 limes
- 1 tbsp honey
- 1 ripe mango, diced
- 1 avocado, diced
- ¼ cup red onion, finely chopped
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 2 tbsp toasted coconut flakes
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, whisk together lime zest, lime juice, honey, cumin, smoked paprika, cayenne (if using), and a pinch of salt and pepper.  
2. Toss the shrimp in the marinade and let sit for 10 minutes.  
3. Heat coconut oil in a skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the shrimp and cook 2‑3 minutes per side, until pink and opaque. Remove from heat and let cool slightly.  
4. In a large mixing bowl combine diced mango, avocado, red onion, cilantro, and toasted coconut flakes.  
5. Add the cooked shrimp to the bowl and gently toss everything together, drizzling any remaining pan juices over the salad.  
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional lime juice, salt, or pepper if needed.  
7. Serve immediately on a bed of mixed greens or with crisp lettuce cups. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Shrimp and Mango Avocado Salad

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 large head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 1 onion, diced
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp saffron threads, steeped in 2 tbsp hot water
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup canned diced tomatoes
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Lemon wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the cauliflower florets with olive oil, salt, pepper, cumin, and smoked paprika; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until golden and tender.  
2. While the cauliflower roasts, heat a large pot over medium heat. Add a splash of olive oil, then sauté the diced onion until translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another 30 seconds.  
3. Add the steeped saffron with its liquid, the diced tomatoes, and vegetable broth to the pot. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to a simmer.  
4. Stir in the roasted cauliflower and chickpeas. Simmer the stew for 10‑12 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld; season with additional salt and pepper to taste.  
5. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro, and serve with lemon wedges on the side for a bright finish.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Stew

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Quinoa Salad with Orange Vinaigrette

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 medium beets, peeled and cubed
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1/4 cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped
- 1/4 cup crumbled feta cheese
- 2 cups mixed baby greens
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the cubed beets with 1 tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway, until tender and caramelized.
2. While the beets roast, bring 2 cups water to a boil, add the quinoa, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes or until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside to cool slightly.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, 2 tbsp fresh orange juice, 1 tsp honey, a pinch of salt, and a dash of black pepper to create the orange vinaigrette.
4. In a large mixing bowl combine the cooked quinoa, roasted beets, toasted walnuts, and mixed greens. Drizzle with the orange vinaigrette and toss gently to coat.
5. Transfer the salad to serving plates, sprinkle crumbled feta over the top, and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Quinoa Salad with Orange Vinaigrette

text:
Maple‑Glazed Roasted Eggplant and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- ¼ cup dried cranberries
- 2 green onions, thinly sliced
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar
- 2 tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil
- 1 handful fresh mint leaves, torn

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together maple syrup, soy sauce, olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Add the eggplant cubes and toss to coat evenly.
