3. Spread the glazed eggplant on the prepared sheet in a single layer. Roast 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway through, until golden and tender.  
4. While the eggplant roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes or until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat, let stand 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together lemon juice, apple cider vinegar, extra‑virgin olive oil, and a pinch of salt to make the dressing.  
6. In a large serving bowl, combine cooked quinoa, roasted eggplant, toasted pumpkin seeds, dried cranberries, and green onions. Drizzle the dressing over the mixture and toss gently to combine.  
7. Taste and
title: Maple‑Glazed Roasted Eggplant and Quinoa Salad

text:
Saffron‑Infused Chickpea and Roasted Butternut Squash Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 cup long‑grain basmati rice
- 1½ cups water
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 small onion, finely diced
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon ground coriander
- ¼ teaspoon ground cinnamon
- ½ teaspoon saffron threads, steeped in 2 tbsp hot water
- 2 cups butternut squash, peeled and cubed
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- ¼ cup golden raisins
- ¼ cup toasted slivered almonds
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Lemon wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the cubed butternut squash with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized. Set aside.  
2. Rinse the basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear. In a medium saucepan combine the rice, water, a pinch of salt, and the saffron infusion (including the threads). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 12‑15 minutes, or until the rice is fluffy and the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
3. While the rice cooks, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté 3‑4 minutes until translucent. Stir in the minced garlic, cumin, coriander, and cinnamon; cook another minute until fragrant.  
4. Add the roasted butternut squash, chickpeas, and golden raisins to the skillet. Toss gently to combine and heat through, about 3 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste.  
5. Fold the cooked saffron‑infused rice into the skillet, mixing until the rice is evenly coated with the spiced vegetables and chickpeas. Adjust seasoning if needed.  
6. Transfer the pilaf to a serving platter. Sprinkle toasted slivered almonds over the top and garnish with fresh cilantro leaves. Serve with lemon wedges on the side for a bright finish.
title: Saffron‑Infused Chickpea and Roasted Butternut Squash Pilaf

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Sweet Potato and Kale Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and cubed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 3 cups kale, stems removed and torn
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Juice of ½ lemon

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, smoked paprika, and cumin. Toss the tempeh strips in half of the glaze, reserving the other half for later.  
3. Place the cubed sweet potato on the prepared sheet, drizzle with 1 Tbsp olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and roast for 20 minutes.  
4. While the sweet potato roasts, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
5. After the sweet potato has roasted 20 minutes, remove the sheet, push the potatoes to one side, and spread the glazed tempeh on the other side. Roast an additional 12‑15 minutes, turning tempeh halfway through, until golden and slightly crisp.  
6. In a large bowl, massage the kale with the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt for 2‑3 minutes until it softens.  
7. Add the cooked quinoa, roasted sweet potato, and tempeh (with any remaining glaze) to the bowl with kale. Toss
title: Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Sweet Potato and Kale Quinoa Salad

text:
Spiced Cardamom Coconut Rice with Roasted Veggies

Ingredients:
- 1 cup basmati rice
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup water
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cardamom
- 1/2 teaspoon sea salt
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 red bell pepper, sliced
- 1 small zucchini, sliced into half‑moons
- 1 cup cauliflower florets
- 1 tablespoon maple syrup
- 1 tablespoon lime juice
- 2 green onions, thinly sliced
- 2 tablespoons toasted coconut flakes (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the red bell pepper, zucchini, and cauliflower with olive oil, maple syrup, lime juice, and a pinch of salt. Spread evenly on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway, until caramelized and tender.  
3. While the vegetables roast, rinse the basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear.  
4. In a medium saucepan, combine the coconut milk, water, ground cardamom, and sea salt. Bring to a gentle boil, then stir in the rice. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is fluffy.  
5. Remove the rice from heat and let it sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
6. Transfer the cooked rice to a serving bowl, gently fold in the roasted vegetables, and sprinkle with sliced green onions and toasted coconut flakes, if using.  
7. Serve warm as a hearty main or side dish. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Cardamom Coconut Rice with Roasted Veggies

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Salad

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch sticks
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp sea salt
- ½ tsp black pepper
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 1 Tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp crumbled feta cheese (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the carrot sticks and chickpeas with olive oil, turmeric, cumin, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until carrots are tender and lightly caramelized and chickpeas are crisp.  
4. While the vegetables roast, whisk together lemon juice, lemon zest, and grated ginger in a small bowl to create the dressing.  
5. Transfer the roasted carrots and chickpeas to a serving platter. Drizzle the lemon‑ginger dressing over the hot vegetables and toss gently to combine.  
6. Sprinkle chopped parsley, toasted pumpkin seeds, and crumbled feta (if using) on top. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Salad

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Shrimp and Mango Avocado Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 2 tbsp coconut oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- Zest of 1 lime
- Juice of 2 limes
- 1 tbsp honey
- 1 ripe mango, peeled and diced
- 1 avocado, diced
- ¼ cup red onion, finely chopped
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, whisk together lime zest, lime juice, honey, cumin, smoked paprika, cayenne (if using), salt, and pepper.
2. Toss the shrimp in the marinade and let sit for 10 minutes.
3. Heat coconut oil in a skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the shrimp and cook 2‑3 minutes per side, until pink and opaque. Remove from heat and let cool slightly.
4. In a large mixing bowl, combine diced mango, avocado, red onion, and cilantro.
5. Add the cooked shrimp to the fruit mixture and gently toss to coat with any remaining pan juices.
6. Drizzle the remaining lime‑honey dressing over the salad, give a final gentle toss, and serve immediately, optionally over a bed of mixed greens.
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Shrimp and Mango Avocado Salad

text:
Saffron‑Infused Lentil and Roasted Tomato Soup

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 2 cups cherry tomatoes, halved
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 carrot, diced
- 1 celery stalk, diced
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 teaspoon ground saffron threads (or a pinch of saffron threads steeped in 2 tbsp warm water)
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Lemon wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the halved cherry tomatoes with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper, then spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until caramelized.
2. While the tomatoes roast, heat the remaining olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion, carrot, and celery; sauté for 5‑7 minutes until softened.
3. Stir in the minced garlic and smoked paprika; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Add the rinsed red lentils, vegetable broth, and the saffron infusion (or steeped threads). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer.
5. Simmer the soup for 15‑20 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and beginning to break down.
6. Once the tomatoes are roasted, add them (with any pan juices) to the pot. Use an immersion blender to blend the soup partially, leaving some texture, or blend half the soup in a countertop blender and return it to the pot.
7. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Let the soup simmer an additional 5 minutes to meld flavors.
8. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve with lemon wedges on the side for a bright finish.
title: Saffron‑Infused Lentil and Roasted Tomato Soup

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Garlic Sweet Potato and Kale

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and cubed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 4 cups kale, stems removed and torn
- Salt and pepper, to taste
- 1 Tbsp toasted sesame seeds (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, whisk together maple syrup, soy sauce, smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt. Toss the tempeh strips in the glaze and set aside.  
3. In another bowl, combine sweet potato cubes, half the olive oil, minced garlic, salt, and pepper. Spread them on the prepared sheet and roast for 20 minutes, stirring halfway through.  
4. After 20 minutes, push the sweet potatoes to one side of the sheet. Add the glazed tempeh strips to
title: Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Garlic Sweet Potato and Kale

text:
Cinnamon‑Lime Roasted Cauliflower and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 medium cauliflower head, cut into florets
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tsp maple syrup
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 green onions, thinly sliced
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss cauliflower florets with olive oil, cinnamon, lime zest, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the cauliflower on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender.  
4. While the cauliflower roasts, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together lime juice, maple syrup, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of olive oil to create the dressing.  
6. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted cauliflower, toasted pumpkin seeds, green onions, and cilantro.  
7. Pour the lime‑cinnamon dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat all ingredients.  
8. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Lime Roasted Cauliflower and Quinoa Salad

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Sweet Potato and Kale Quinoa Bowl

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 2 cups chopped kale, stems removed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 3 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 tbsp low‑sodium soy sauce
- 1 tbsp olive oil (plus extra for roasting)
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the diced sweet potatoes with a drizzle of olive oil, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine maple syrup, soy sauce, minced garlic, grated ginger, and lime juice in a shallow bowl. Add the tempeh cubes and toss to coat; let marinate for 5‑10 minutes.  
3. Meanwhile, cook the quinoa: bring 2 cups water to a boil, add the rinsed quinoa, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes or until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
4. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Remove tempeh from the marinade (reserve the excess sauce) and sear the cubes for 3‑4 minutes per side, until golden brown and slightly crisp. Pour the reserved sauce into the pan and cook an additional 2 minutes, allowing it to glaze the tempeh.  
5. In the same skillet, add the chopped kale and a splash of water; sauté for 2‑3 minutes until wilted but still bright green. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.  
6. Assemble the bowl: start with a base of cooked quinoa, top with roasted sweet potatoes, maple‑glazed tempeh, and sautéed kale. Drizzle any remaining glaze from the pan over the top and finish with an extra squeeze of lime juice if desired. Serve warm.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Sweet Potato and Kale Quinoa Bowl

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Beet and Quinoa Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 2 medium beets, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- Salt and pepper, to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Toss beet cubes with 1 tsp olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast 25‑30 minutes, until tender.
2. While the beets roast, whisk together maple syrup, soy sauce, smoked paprika, and the remaining olive oil in a shallow bowl. Add tempeh strips, coat, and let marinate 10 minutes.
3. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium heat. Add the marinated tempeh and cook 3‑4 minutes per side, until caramelized and golden. Transfer to a plate.
4. In a saucepan, combine quinoa and vegetable broth; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
5. Stir the roasted beets into the cooked quinoa, season with salt and pepper, and fold in toasted pumpkin seeds.
6. Serve the quinoa‑beet pilaf topped with the maple‑glazed tempeh. Garnish with chopped parsley, if desired.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Beet and Quinoa Pilaf

text:
Spiced Cardamom Sweet Potato and Quinoa Skillet

Ingredients:
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and diced
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 small onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon ground cardamom
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- ¼ teaspoon ground cumin
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- ½ cup frozen peas
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Lemon wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 3‑4 minutes.
2. Stir in the garlic, cardamom, smoked paprika, and cumin; cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
3. Add the diced sweet potato and toast for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it begins to soften.
4. Pour in the quinoa and vegetable broth, bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the quinoa is cooked and the sweet potato is tender.
5. Stir in the frozen peas and cook for an additional 2 minutes, just until heated through.
6. Season the skillet with salt and pepper to taste. Remove from heat and sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds over the top.
7. Garnish with fresh cilantro leaves and serve with lemon wedges on the side for a bright finish. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Cardamom Sweet Potato and Quinoa Skillet

text:
Maple‑Glazed Carrot and Lentil Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 large carrots, peeled and diced
- 1 small onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 2 ½ cups vegetable broth
- ½ tsp dried thyme
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 Tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds (optional, for garnish)
- Fresh parsley, chopped (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan, combine the lentils and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15‑20 minutes, or until the lentils are just tender but still hold their shape. Drain any excess liquid if needed and set the lentils aside.  
2. While the lentils cook, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté for 3‑4 minutes, until translucent.  
3. Stir in the minced garlic and diced carrots; cook, stirring occasionally, for about 5‑7 minutes, until the carrots begin to soften.  
4. Drizzle the maple syrup over the vegetables, sprinkle the dried thyme, and season with salt and pepper. Continue to sauté for another 2‑3 minutes, allowing the maple to caramelize and coat the carrots.  
5. Add the cooked lentils to the skillet, mixing gently to combine everything evenly. Cook for an additional 2 minutes to let the flavors meld.  
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with more salt, pepper, or a splash of maple syrup if desired.  
7. Transfer the pilaf to a serving bowl, garnish with toasted pumpkin seeds and chopped fresh parsley, if using. Serve warm as a hearty main or side dish.
title: Maple‑Glazed Carrot and Lentil Pilaf

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Tostadas

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- Salt and black pepper, to taste
- 8 small corn tortillas
- 1 avocado, sliced
- ½ cup crumbled feta cheese
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Lime wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the diced sweet potatoes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, smoked paprika, cayenne (if using), salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the sweet potatoes in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and caramelized.  
4. While the sweet potatoes roast, heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the chickpeas, season with a pinch of salt and pepper, and sauté for 5‑7 minutes until lightly crisped.  
5. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet or directly over a gas flame for about 30 seconds per side, keeping them pliable.  
6. To assemble each tostada, layer a spoonful of roasted sweet potatoes, followed by sautéed chickpeas, avocado slices, and a sprinkle of feta cheese.  
7. Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve with lime wedges on the side for squeezing over the top. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Tostadas

text:
Spiced Harissa Carrot and Lentil Soup

Ingredients:
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 large onion, diced
- 3 carrots, peeled and sliced into 1/4‑inch rounds
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon harissa paste
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup canned diced tomatoes (with juice)
- 1 bay leaf
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- A squeeze of lemon juice (optional)

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.  
2. Stir in the sliced carrots and minced garlic; cook for another 2 minutes, allowing the garlic to become fragrant.  
3. Add the harissa paste, cumin, and smoked paprika. Cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute to toast the spices.  
4. Pour in the rinsed red lentils, vegetable broth, diced tomatoes, and bay leaf. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to a gentle simmer.  
5. Cover the pot and let the soup simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the carrots are tender and the lentils have broken down, creating a thick texture.  
6. Remove the bay leaf. Using an immersion blender, blend the soup until smooth, or blend in batches in a countertop blender—be careful with the hot liquid.  
7. Return the soup to the pot, season with salt, pepper, and a squeeze of lemon juice if desired. Warm through for another 2 minutes.  
8. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve hot. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Harissa Carrot and Lentil Soup

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea and Kale Soup

Ingredients:
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 large onion, diced
- 3 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 2 cups chopped kale, stems removed
- 1 large carrot, sliced thin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Juice of 1 lemon

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.  
2. Stir in the garlic, ginger, turmeric, and cumin; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
3. Add the sliced carrot and chickpeas, then pour in the vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook for 15 minutes, or until the carrot is tender.  
4. Stir in the chopped kale and simmer for an additional 5 minutes, until the kale wilts.  
5. Season with salt, pepper, and lemon juice. Adjust seasoning as needed, then ladle the soup into bowls and serve hot.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea and Kale Soup

text:
Saffron‑Infused Coconut Chickpea and Spinach Stew

Ingredients:
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 large onion, diced
- 3 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon ground coriander
- ¼ teaspoon saffron threads, steeped in 2 tablespoons hot water
- 1 can (14 oz) coconut milk, full‑fat
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- 2 cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 4 cups fresh baby spinach
- 1 medium sweet potato, peeled and cubed
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Juice of 1 lime
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.  
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
3. Sprinkle in the cumin, smoked paprika, coriander, and the saffron infusion (including the threads). Cook, stirring constantly, for 30 seconds to toast the spices.  
4. Add the cubed sweet potato, coconut milk, and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to a simmer. Cover and cook for 12‑15 minutes, or until the sweet potato is tender.  
5. Stir in the cooked chickpeas and let the stew simmer uncovered for another 5 minutes to meld flavors.  
6. Add the fresh spinach in batches, allowing each handful to wilt before adding more. Cook for 2‑3 minutes until the spinach is fully incorporated.  
7. Season the stew with salt, pepper, and lime juice. Adjust seasoning to taste.  
8. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with chopped cilantro, and serve hot with crusty bread or steamed rice.
title: Saffron‑Infused Coconut Chickpea and Spinach Stew

text:
Roasted Turmeric Cauliflower with Lemon Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 large head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 lemon, zest and juice
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- 1 clove garlic, minced

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cauliflower florets with olive oil, turmeric, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the seasoned cauliflower in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway through, until golden‑brown and tender.  
4. While the cauliflower roasts, combine the rinsed quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy.  
5. Remove the quinoa from heat; stir in the minced garlic, lemon zest, lemon juice, and chopped parsley. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste.  
6. To serve, divide the lemon‑quinoa among plates, top with the roasted turmeric cauliflower, and garnish with extra parsley or a drizzle of olive oil if desired. Enjoy warm!
title: Roasted Turmeric Cauliflower with Lemon Quinoa

text:
Lemon‑Basil Quinoa with Roasted Sweet Potato and Feta

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and cubed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- ¼ cup fresh basil leaves, chopped
- ½ cup crumbled feta cheese
- Optional: 1 Tbsp toasted pine nuts for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the sweet‑potato cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.  
3. In a small skillet, heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and sauté 30 seconds until fragrant; stir in the lemon zest and juice, then remove from heat.  
4. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl. Pour the garlic‑lemon dressing over the quinoa and toss to combine.  
5. Gently fold in the roasted sweet‑potato cubes, chopped basil, and crumbled feta. Adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.  
6. Serve warm or at room temperature, sprinkled with toasted pine nuts if desired. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Basil Quinoa with Roasted Sweet Potato and Feta

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Lentil Soup

Ingredients:
- 1 lb carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch pieces
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch piece fresh ginger, grated
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ¼ tsp ground nutmeg
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the carrot pieces with 1 tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, nutmeg, and a pinch of salt. Spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway, until caramelized and tender.  
2. While the carrots roast, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 5 minutes until translucent.  
3. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
4. Add the rinsed red lentils and vegetable broth to the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes.  
5. Add the roasted carrots (including any pan juices) to the pot. Simmer for another 5 minutes to let the flavors meld.  
6. Using an immersion blender (or transferring to a countertop blender in batches), puree the soup until smooth and creamy.  
7. Stir in the coconut milk, season with salt and pepper, and heat through for 2‑3 minutes. Adjust seasoning if needed.  
8. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve hot.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Lentil Soup

text:
Sage‑Infused Mushroom and Barley Soup

Ingredients:
- 1 cup pearl barley, rinsed
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 8 ounces cremini mushrooms, sliced
- 1 teaspoon dried sage
- ½ teaspoon dried thyme
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 2 cups water
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
- Optional garnish: chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. In a large pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 4–5 minutes, until translucent.
2. Stir in the minced garlic and sliced mushrooms, cooking for another 5 minutes until the mushrooms release their moisture and begin to brown.
3. Sprinkle the dried sage and thyme over the vegetables, stirring to coat evenly; cook for 1 minute to release the aromatics.
4. Add the rinsed barley, vegetable broth, and water to the pot. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 35–40 minutes, or until the barley is tender.
5. Season the soup with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste. Stir in the lemon juice for a bright finish.
6. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with chopped fresh parsley if desired, and serve hot.
title: Sage‑Infused Mushroom and Barley Soup

text:
Cinnamon‑Orange Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch rounds  
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed  
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth  
- 2 tbsp olive oil  
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon  
- Zest of 1 orange  
- 2 tbsp freshly squeezed orange juice  
- 1 tbsp maple syrup  
- 1/4 tsp sea salt, plus more to taste  
- 1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper  
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds  
- 2 green onions, thinly sliced  
- Optional: 1/4 cup crumbled feta or goat cheese  

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).  
2. In a large bowl, toss the carrot rounds with olive oil, ground cinnamon, orange zest, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the carrots in a single layer on a parchment‑lined baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
4. While the carrots roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together orange juice, maple syrup, and a pinch of salt to create the dressing.  
6. In a large serving bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted carrots, toasted pumpkin seeds, and sliced green onions. Drizzle the orange‑maple dressing over the mixture and toss gently to coat.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed.  
8. If using, sprinkle crumbled feta or goat cheese on top just before serving. Enjoy warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Orange Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 3 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch sticks
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 1 cup cooked quinoa
- ½ cup sliced cucumber
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp lemon juice
- 1 Tbsp tahini
- 1 tsp maple syrup
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the carrot sticks and chickpeas with olive oil, turmeric, grated ginger, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until carrots are tender and chickpeas are crisp.  
4. While the vegetables roast, whisk together lemon juice, tahini, maple syrup, and a pinch of salt to make a smooth dressing; add a splash of water if needed to reach drizzling consistency.  
5. Divide cooked quinoa between two serving bowls. Top each with the roasted carrots and chickpeas, sliced cucumber, and toasted pumpkin seeds.  
6. Drizzle the lemon‑ginger tahini dressing over the bowls, then garnish with fresh cilantro leaves.  
7. Serve warm or at room temperature, enjoying a bright, protein‑packed Buddha bowl.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

text:
Spiced Cardamom Coconut Rice with Roasted Veggie Medley

Ingredients:
- 1 cup basmati rice
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- ½ cup water
- 4 green cardamom pods, lightly crushed
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1 yellow bell pepper, diced
- 1 medium zucchini, sliced into half‑moons
- 2 carrots, peeled and cut into ¼‑inch coins
- ½ red onion, cut into wedges
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 Tbsp lime juice
- 2 Tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the diced bell peppers, zucchini, carrots, red onion, and minced garlic with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread evenly on the prepared sheet.  
3. Roast the vegetables for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
4. While the veggies roast, rinse the basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear.  
5. In a medium saucepan, combine coconut milk, water, crushed cardamom pods, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a gentle boil over medium heat.  
6. Add the rinsed rice, stir once, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is fluffy.  
7. Remove the saucepan from heat; discard the cardamom pods, fluff the rice with a fork, and stir in lime juice and chopped cilantro.  
8. Transfer the cooked rice to a serving platter, top with the roasted vegetable medley, and garnish with additional cilantro if desired. Serve warm.
title: Spiced Cardamom Coconut Rice with Roasted Veggie Medley

text:
Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Cauliflower and Lentil Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 medium cauliflower head, cut into florets
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large onion, finely chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 2 tsp fresh thyme leaves (or 1 tsp dried thyme)
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup toasted pine nuts (optional, for garnish)
- Fresh parsley, chopped (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Toss the cauliflower florets with 1 tbsp olive oil, thyme, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender.  
2. While the cauliflower roasts, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté 4‑5 minutes until translucent. Stir in the garlic and cook another minute.  
3. Add the rinsed lentils to the saucepan, pour in the vegetable broth, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and the liquid is absorbed.  
4. Once the lentils are cooked, stir in the lemon zest, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Adjust seasoning to taste.  
5. Transfer the cooked lentils to a large serving bowl. Fold in the roasted cauliflower, mixing gently to combine.  
6. Garnish with toasted pine nuts and chopped parsley, if desired. Serve warm as a hearty main dish or a side. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Cauliflower and Lentil Pilaf

text:
Cinnamon‑Orange Roasted Carrot and Lentil Soup

Ingredients:
- 1 lb carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch pieces  
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed  
- 1 medium onion, diced  
- 3 cloves garlic, minced  
- 4 cups vegetable broth  
- 1 cup freshly squeezed orange juice  
- Zest of 1 orange  
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon  
- ½ tsp ground cumin  
- 2 tbsp olive oil  
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste  
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)  

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the carrot pieces with 1 tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and half the cinnamon. Spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, or until caramelized and tender.  
2. While the carrots roast, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 5 minutes, until translucent. Stir in the garlic and cumin; cook another minute until fragrant.  
3. Add the roasted carrots, red lentils, vegetable broth, orange juice, and orange zest to the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer. Cover and cook for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils are soft.  
4. Using an immersion blender (or transferring to a countertop blender in batches), puree the soup until smooth. If the soup is too thick, stir in a little extra broth or water to reach desired consistency.  
5. Season with salt, pepper, and the remaining cinnamon. Simmer for an additional 5 minutes to let the flavors meld.  
6. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with chopped cilantro, and serve hot. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Orange Roasted Carrot and Lentil Soup

text:
Maple‑Glazed Eggplant and Barley Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 1 cup pearl barley, rinsed
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 small onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 ½ cups vegetable broth
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped (optional)
- Fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the eggplant cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway, until caramelized and tender.  
3. While the eggplant roasts, heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 3‑4 minutes until translucent. Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another 30 seconds.  
4. Add the rinsed barley to the saucepan, stirring to coat the grains with the aromatics for 1‑2 minutes.  
5. Pour in the vegetable broth, add dried thyme, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30‑35 minutes, or until the barley is tender and the liquid is absorbed.  
6. Fluff the cooked barley with a fork and season with additional salt and pepper if needed.  
7. Gently fold the roasted maple‑glazed eggplant into the barley pilaf, mixing just enough to distribute the eggplant without breaking it apart.  
8. Transfer the pilaf to a serving bowl, sprinkle with toasted walnuts and fresh parsley, and serve warm. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Eggplant and Barley Pilaf

text:
Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Sweet Potato and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- ¼ teaspoon smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- ¼ cup dried cranberries
- 2 green onions, thinly sliced
- 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
- 1 tablespoon maple syrup
- 1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar
- 2 tablespoons extra‑virgin olive oil

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). In a large bowl toss the sweet potato cubes with olive oil, cinnamon, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning once, until tender and caramelized.  
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.  
3. In a small jar, whisk together lemon juice, maple syrup, apple cider vinegar, extra‑virgin olive oil, a pinch of salt, and a dash of pepper to create the dressing.  
4. In a large mixing bowl combine the cooked quinoa, roasted sweet potatoes, toasted pumpkin seeds, dried cranberries, and sliced green onions.  
5. Drizzle the dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly. Adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed.  
6. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with an extra sprinkle of pumpkin seeds and a wedge of lemon on the side. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Sweet Potato and Quinoa Salad

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Quinoa Bowl with Pomegranate  

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- ½ cup pomegranate seeds
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh mint leaves, for garnish  

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together maple syrup, cinnamon, smoked paprika, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Add the cubed sweet potatoes and toss to coat evenly.  
3. Spread the sweet potatoes in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway through, until tender and caramelized.  
4. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine quinoa and 2 cups water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
5. In a serving bowl, layer a generous scoop of quinoa, then top with the roasted sweet potatoes.  
6. Sprinkle pomegranate seeds, toasted pumpkin seeds, and crumbled feta over the top.  
7. Garnish with fresh mint leaves and a final drizzle of olive oil or a squeeze of lemon juice, if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Quinoa Bowl with Pomegranate

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch sticks
- 1 ½ cups cooked quinoa
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 Tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 1 ripe avocado, sliced
- 2 Tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, grated ginger, turmeric, minced garlic, salt, and pepper.  
3. Add the carrot sticks and chickpeas to the bowl; toss until evenly coated with the spice mixture.  
4. Spread the carrots and chickpeas in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until carrots are tender and lightly caramelized and chickpeas are crisp.  
5. While the vegetables roast, divide the cooked quinoa among two serving bowls.  
6. Top each bowl of quinoa with the roasted carrots and chickpeas, then arrange avocado slices on the side.  
7. Sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds and chopped cilantro over each bowl for added crunch and freshness.  
8. Serve warm or at room temperature, drizzling any remaining pan juices over the top if desired. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu and Roasted Garlic Sweet Potato Hash

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and diced into ½‑inch cubes
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped (optional garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the diced sweet potatoes with 1 tbsp olive oil, half the minced garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.  
3. While the sweet potatoes roast, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, remaining garlic, and a pinch of salt in a shallow dish. Add the tofu cubes and gently toss to coat; let sit for 5 minutes.  
4. Heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated tofu and sear for 3‑4 minutes per side, until caramelized and crisp.  
5. When the sweet potatoes are done, remove them from the oven and add them to the skillet with the tofu. Stir‑fry together for 2‑3 minutes to combine flavors, adjusting seasoning with extra salt or a drizzle of maple syrup if desired.  
6. Transfer the hash to serving plates, sprinkle with chopped parsley, and serve hot as a hearty breakfast or brunch dish.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu and Roasted Garlic Sweet Potato Hash

text:
Cinnamon‑Sage Roasted Butternut Squash and Barley Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 small butternut squash, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup pearl barley
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 tsp dried sage (or 2 tsp fresh sage, chopped)
- ½ tsp salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- ¼ cup dried cranberries
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp maple syrup (optional, for a hint of sweetness)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the cubed butternut squash with 1 tbsp olive oil, cinnamon, sage, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning once, until tender and caramelized.
2. While the squash roasts, rinse the barley and place it in a saucepan with 2 cups water. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 30‑35 minutes, or until the grains are tender and the water is absorbed. Drain any excess liquid and set aside to cool slightly.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, lemon juice, and maple syrup (if using); season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
4. In a large mixing bowl, combine the roasted squash, cooked barley, toasted pumpkin seeds, and dried cranberries. Drizzle the lemon‑maple dressing over the mixture and toss gently to coat evenly.
5. Serve the salad warm or at room temperature, garnished with an extra sprinkle of sage or cinnamon if desired. Enjoy as a hearty side or a light main dish.
title: Cinnamon‑Sage Roasted Butternut Squash and Barley Salad

text:
Spiced Ginger‑Pear Quinoa Salad with Toasted Hazelnuts

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 1 ripe pear, cored and diced
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, finely grated
- 1/3 cup hazelnuts, roughly chopped
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 tablespoon lemon juice
- 1 teaspoon pure maple syrup
- 1/4 teaspoon sea salt
- 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, chopped

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa and water; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and transfer to a large bowl to cool slightly.  
2. While the quinoa cooks, preheat a dry skillet over medium heat. Add the hazelnuts and toast, stirring frequently, until golden and fragrant, about 3‑4 minutes. Remove from heat and set aside.  
3. In a small bowl whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, maple syrup, grated ginger, salt, and pepper to form the dressing.  
4. Add the diced pear, toasted hazelnuts, and chopped parsley to the quinoa. Drizzle the ginger‑lemon dressing over the mixture and toss gently to combine, ensuring the pear pieces are evenly coated.  
5. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if desired. Serve the salad at room temperature or chilled, as a light main dish or side.
title: Spiced Ginger‑Pear Quinoa Salad with Toasted Hazelnuts

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Garlic Quinoa and Sautéed Kale

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp low‑sodium soy sauce
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 Tbsp olive oil (for tempeh)
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 Tbsp olive oil (for quinoa)
- 2 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
- 4 cups kale, stems removed and torn into bite‑size pieces
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a shallow bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, and 1 clove minced garlic. Add the tempeh cubes, toss to coat, and let marinate while you prepare the quinoa (about 10 minutes).  
2. Meanwhile, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes.  
3. Heat 2 Tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the sliced garlic and sauté 30 seconds until fragrant. Stir in the cooked quinoa, season with salt and pepper, and keep warm.  
4. While the quinoa rests, heat 1 Tbsp olive oil in a separate large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated tempeh in a single layer and cook, turning occasionally, until golden and caramelized, about 6‑8 minutes. Transfer to a plate.  
5. In the same skillet, add a splash more olive oil if needed and toss in the kale. Sauté, stirring frequently, until wilted but still bright green, about 3‑4 minutes. Drizzle with lemon juice and season with salt and pepper.  
6. To serve, spoon a bed of garlic‑quinoa onto each plate, top with sautéed kale, and arrange the maple‑glazed tempeh on top. Garnish with an extra drizzle of maple syrup or a squeeze of lemon if desired. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Garlic Quinoa and Sautéed Kale

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 ½ cans, drained and rinsed)
- 1 cup pearl couscous (or orzo)
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- ¼ teaspoon saffron threads
- 2 cups low‑sodium vegetable broth
- ¼ cup toasted slivered almonds
- 2 green onions, thinly sliced
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with 1  tablespoon of olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, or until tender and lightly caramelized, stirring halfway through.  
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, place the saffron threads in a small bowl and cover with 2 tablespoons of hot vegetable broth; let steep for 5 minutes to release color and flavor.  
3. In a medium saucepan, bring the remaining 1 ½ cups of vegetable broth to a boil. Stir in the pearl couscous, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 8‑10 minutes, or until the grains are tender and the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and fluff with a fork.  
4. In a large skillet, heat the remaining 1  tablespoon of olive oil over medium heat. Add the cooked chickpeas and sauté for 3‑4 minutes, allowing them to brown slightly.  
5. Add the roasted sweet potatoes, saffron‑infused broth, and the cooked couscous to the skillet with the chickpeas. Toss gently to combine, and cook for another 2‑3 minutes until everything is heated through and the saffron has evenly colored the pilaf.  
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.  
7. Transfer the pilaf to a serving bowl, sprinkle with toasted slivered almonds, sliced green onions, and chopped parsley if desired. Serve warm as a hearty main or side dish.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Pilaf

text:
Cinnamon‑Roasted Pumpkin and Quinoa Salad with Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 1 small sugar pumpkin, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 1/4 cup pomegranate seeds
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tbsp crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tsp honey

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss pumpkin cubes with olive oil, cinnamon, cumin, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet.  
2. Roast pumpkin for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway, until tender and caramelized. Set aside to cool slightly.  
3. Meanwhile, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and let cool.  
4. In a small bowl, whisk together lemon juice, honey, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of olive oil to make the dressing.  
5. In a large mixing bowl, combine roasted pumpkin, cooked quinoa, pomegranate seeds, toasted pumpkin seeds, parsley, and feta if using.  
6. Drizzle the dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat evenly.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if needed.  
8. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with extra pomegranate seeds and pumpkin seeds.
title: Cinnamon‑Roasted Pumpkin and Quinoa Salad with Pomegranate

text:
Crispy Coconut Lime Tempeh with Pineapple Salsa

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 1 cup fresh pineapple, diced
- ½ cup red bell pepper, finely chopped
- ¼ cup red onion, minced
- 1  tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1  tbsp lime juice
- 1  tsp lime zest
- 2  tbsp coconut oil, divided
- ½  cup panko breadcrumbs
- 2  tbsp unsweetened shredded coconut, toasted
- 1  tsp ground cumin
- ½  tsp sea salt
- ¼  tsp black pepper
- 1  tbsp maple syrup (optional, for extra glaze)

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, combine the diced pineapple, red bell pepper, red onion, cilantro, lime juice, and lime zest. Toss gently and set the salsa aside to let the flavors meld.  
2. In a shallow dish, mix the panko breadcrumbs, toasted shredded coconut, ground cumin, salt, and black pepper.  
3. Pat the tempeh strips dry with paper towels. Heat 1  tablespoon of coconut oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat.  
4. Dredge each tempeh strip in the breadcrumb‑coconut mixture, pressing lightly to adhere. Place the coated strips in the hot skillet and cook for 3‑4 minutes per side, or until golden and crispy. Add the remaining 1  tablespoon of coconut oil as needed to prevent sticking.  
5. If using, drizzle the maple syrup over the tempeh during the last minute of cooking and give the strips a quick flip to glaze.  
6. Transfer the crispy tempeh to a serving plate. Spoon the fresh pineapple salsa over the top or serve on the side for a bright, tangy contrast.  
7. Garnish with extra cilantro or a squeeze of lime, if desired, and enjoy warm.
title: Crispy Coconut Lime Tempeh with Pineapple Salsa

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Eggplant and Quinoa Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 1 red bell pepper, sliced
- 1 small red onion, thinly sliced
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together maple syrup, cinnamon, smoked paprika, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Add the cubed eggplant and toss to coat evenly.  
3. Spread the seasoned eggplant on the prepared baking sheet in a single layer. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway through, until golden and tender.  
4. While the eggplant roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
5. In the last 10 minutes of the eggplant’s roasting time, add the sliced red bell pepper and red onion to the same sheet, tossing lightly with a drizzle of olive oil and a pinch of salt. Roast until softened and slightly charred.  
6. To assemble the bowl, divide the cooked quinoa among four serving bowls. Top each with roasted eggplant, bell pepper, and onion. Sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds and chopped cilantro over the top.  
7. Drizzle each bowl with lemon juice and, if desired, an extra splash of maple syrup for added sweetness. Serve warm.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Eggplant and Quinoa Bowl

text:
Cinnamon‑Lime Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad with Pomegranate  

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into matchsticks
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice
- 1/4 cup pomegranate seeds
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional: 2 tablespoons chopped fresh mint  

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).  
2. In a bowl, toss the carrot matchsticks with olive oil, ground cinnamon, lime zest, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on a baking sheet.  
3. Roast the carrots for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway, until they are tender and lightly caramelized.  
4. While the carrots roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together lime juice, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of olive oil to make a dressing.  
6. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted carrots, pomegranate seeds, toasted pumpkin seeds, and optional mint.  
7. Pour the lime dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat everything evenly. Adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired.  
8. Serve the salad warm or at room temperature, garnished with extra pomegranate seeds and pumpkin seeds for crunch. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Lime Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad with Pomegranate

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Quinoa with Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpeas

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 small head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp fresh ginger, minced
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- Zest of 1 lemon
- Juice of 1 lemon
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional garnish: chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss cauliflower florets and chickpeas with 1 tbsp olive oil, turmeric, half the minced ginger, garlic, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet.
2. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until cauliflower is golden and chickpeas are crisp.
3. While the vegetables roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and fluff with a fork.
4. In a small bowl, whisk together remaining olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, the remaining minced ginger, and a pinch of salt and pepper.
5. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large bowl, add the roasted cauliflower and chickpeas, and drizzle the lemon‑ginger dressing over everything. Toss gently to combine.
6. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed; garnish with chopped parsley and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Quinoa with Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpeas

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Chickpea and Spinach Stuffed Sweet Potatoes  

Ingredients:
- 4 medium sweet potatoes, scrubbed
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 cups fresh spinach, roughly chopped
- 1/2 cup coconut milk
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tbsp coconut oil, melted
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish  

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Place the sweet potatoes on a baking sheet, brush lightly with coconut oil, and roast for 45‑50 minutes, or until tender when pierced with a fork.  
2. While the potatoes bake, heat a skillet over medium heat. Add the remaining coconut oil, then sauté the garlic and ginger for 1‑2 minutes until fragrant.  
3. Stir in the chickpeas, cumin, coriander, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes until the chickpeas are warmed through and begin to brown slightly.  
4. Add the chopped spinach and coconut milk to the skillet. Cook, stirring, until the spinach wilts and the mixture becomes a creamy sauce, about 3‑4 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in the lime juice.  
5. When the sweet potatoes are done, let them cool for 5 minutes. Slice each potato lengthwise, being careful not to cut all the way through, and gently fluff the interior with a fork.  
6. Spoon the chickpea‑spinach mixture evenly into each sweet potato cavity, pressing lightly to fill. Return the stuffed potatoes to the oven and bake for an additional 10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.  
7. Remove from the oven, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve warm.
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Chickpea and Spinach Stuffed Sweet Potatoes

text:
Harissa‑Spiced Chickpea and Sweet Potato Skillet

Ingredients:
- 1 lb (450 g) sweet potatoes, peeled and diced into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 2 Tbsp harissa paste
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 small red onion, thinly sliced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 cups fresh baby spinach
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the sliced red onion and sauté for 3‑4 minutes, until softened.
2. Stir in the minced garlic and smoked paprika; cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
3. Add the diced sweet potatoes to the skillet, spreading them in an even layer. Cook, stirring occasionally, for about 8‑10 minutes, until the potatoes begin to brown and are just tender.
4. Mix in the harissa paste, coating the sweet potatoes evenly. Cook for 1‑2 minutes to let the flavors meld.
5. Add the chickpeas and continue to stir, cooking for another 4‑5 minutes until the chickpeas are heated through and the sweet potatoes are fully tender.
6. Fold in the baby spinach and lemon juice; cook just until the spinach wilts, about 1 minute. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
7. Remove from heat, garnish with chopped cilantro, and serve hot as a main dish or over cooked quinoa or couscous.
title: Harissa‑Spiced Chickpea and Sweet Potato Skillet

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 ½ cups cooked quinoa
- 1 cup canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp saffron threads
- ¼ cup warm water
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup toasted slivered almonds
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, combine the saffron threads with warm water; let steep for 5 minutes.  
3. Toss the cauliflower florets with 1 tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Spread them on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.  
4. While the cauliflower roasts, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the chickpeas and sauté for 4‑5 minutes until lightly crisped; season with a pinch of salt.  
5. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted cauliflower, sautéed chickpeas, and the saffron‑infused water (including the threads). Toss gently to distribute the saffron color evenly.  
6. Drizzle the lemon juice over the salad, add the toasted almonds, and sprinkle with chopped parsley. Adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.  
7. Serve warm or at room temperature as a vibrant main‑course salad or side dish. Enjoy!
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Quinoa Salad

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Shrimp and Avocado Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 12 oz large shrimp, peeled and deveined  
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed  
- 2 cups water or low‑sodium vegetable broth  
- 1 ripe avocado, diced  
- 1 ½ tbsp fresh ginger, minced  
- 1 tsp ground turmeric  
- 2 tbsp olive oil  
- 1 tbsp lime juice  
- 1 tbsp honey or maple syrup  
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped  
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste  

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa and water (or broth); bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and set aside to cool slightly.  
2. While the quinoa cooks, whisk together olive oil, lime juice, honey, minced ginger, turmeric, salt, and pepper in a large bowl to create the dressing.  
3. Add the raw shrimp to the dressing, tossing to coat evenly. Let marinate for 5 minutes.  
4. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the shrimp and cook 2‑3 minutes per side, until pink and opaque. Transfer to the bowl with the dressing and toss to coat.  
5. Add the cooked quinoa, diced avocado, and chopped cilantro to the bowl. Gently stir everything together, adjusting seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired.  
6. Serve the salad warm or at room temperature, garnished with an extra sprinkle of cilantro and a drizzle of any remaining dressing. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Shrimp and Avocado Quinoa Salad

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Quinoa with Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpeas

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 small head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2  tbsp olive oil
- 1  tsp ground turmeric
- 1  tsp freshly grated ginger
- 1  tbsp lemon zest
- 2  tbsp fresh lemon juice
- ½  tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 2  tbsp chopped fresh parsley (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Toss cauliflower florets and chickpeas with olive oil, turmeric, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet.
2. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until cauliflower is golden‑brown and chickpeas are crisp.
3. Meanwhile, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
4. Stir the lemon zest, lemon juice, and grated ginger into the cooked quinoa; season with additional salt and pepper if needed.
5. Transfer the quinoa to a serving bowl, top with the roasted cauliflower and chickpeas, and garnish with chopped parsley. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Quinoa with Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpeas

text:
Saffron‑Infused Lentil and Kale Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 cup green lentils, rinsed
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 carrot, diced
- 1 celery stalk, diced
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1/4 teaspoon saffron threads, soaked in 2 Tbsp warm water
- 2 cups chopped kale, stems removed
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh lemon wedges for serving (optional)

Instructions:
1. In a large pot, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add onion, carrot, and celery; sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.  
2. Stir in garlic, cumin, and smoked paprika; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
3. Add the rinsed lentils, vegetable broth, and the saffron infusion (including threads). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until lentils are tender.  
4. Stir in the chopped kale and continue cooking for another 5 minutes, until kale is wilted.  
5. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Ladle into bowls and serve with a squeeze of fresh lemon if desired.
title: Saffron‑Infused Lentil and Kale Stew

text:
Lemon‑Basil Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh basil
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- 2 cups baby spinach leaves

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20 minutes.  
3. While the sweet potatoes roast, toss the chickpeas with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, lemon zest, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Add them to the baking sheet and continue roasting for another 15 minutes, stirring halfway, until both the potatoes and chickpeas are golden and crisp.  
4. Remove the tray from the oven and let the vegetables cool slightly. Transfer them to a large mixing bowl and drizzle with lemon juice. Add the chopped basil and gently toss to combine.  
5. To assemble the bowls, divide the baby spinach between two serving bowls. Top each with the roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas, then sprinkle with toasted pumpkin seeds and crumbled feta, if using.  
6. Serve warm or at room temperature, enjoying the bright lemon‑basil flavor with the sweet, smoky vegetables.
title: Lemon‑Basil Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Bowl

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Shrimp with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- ½ cup water
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- ¼ tsp salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed and quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let stand 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
2. While the quinoa cooks, whisk together lemon juice, lime juice, grated ginger, turmeric, minced garlic, olive oil, salt, and pepper in a large bowl.
3. Add the shrimp to the bowl and toss to coat evenly with the marinade. Let sit for 5 minutes.
4. Heat a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the shrimp and cook 2‑3 minutes per side, or until pink and opaque. Remove from heat.
5. To serve, spoon a bed of coconut‑lime quinoa onto each plate, top with the cooked shrimp, and drizzle any remaining pan juices over the top.
6. Garnish with chopped cilantro, if desired, and enjoy immediately.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Shrimp with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa

text:
Spiced Orange‑Glazed Tofu with Sesame‑Brown Rice and Steamed Broccoli

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 1 cup brown rice
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 cup broccoli florets
- 2 tbsp orange marmalade
- 1 tbsp soy sauce (or tamari for gluten‑free)
- 1 tsp sriracha or chili paste (adjust to taste)
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame oil
- 1 tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- 2 tbsp neutral oil (e.g., canola) for frying
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Optional garnish: sliced green onions, lime wedges

Instructions:
1. Rinse the brown rice, combine with water or broth in a saucepan, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 40‑45 minutes until tender. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.  
2. While the rice cooks, whisk together orange marmalade, soy sauce, sriracha, grated ginger, minced garlic, rice vinegar, and 1 tbsp sesame oil in a small bowl to create the glaze. Set aside.  
3. Heat the neutral oil in a large non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the tofu cubes in a single layer; season lightly with salt and pepper. Cook, turning occasionally, until all sides are golden brown and crisp, about 6‑8 minutes.  
4. Reduce the heat to medium and pour the orange glaze over the browned tofu. Toss gently to coat; cook for another 2‑3 minutes until the glaze thickens and becomes sticky. Remove from heat and sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds.  
5. Meanwhile, steam the broccoli florets until just tender but still bright green, about 4‑5 minutes.  
6. To assemble, divide the cooked brown rice among serving bowls. Top each with a portion of the orange‑glazed tofu and a handful of steamed broccoli. Drizzle any remaining glaze from the pan over the bowls.  
7. Garnish with extra sesame seeds, sliced green onions, and a squeeze of lime if desired. Serve warm.
title: Spiced Orange‑Glazed Tofu with Sesame‑Brown Rice and Steamed Broccoli

text:
Honey‑Sage Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch sticks
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 Tbsp honey
- 1 Tbsp fresh sage leaves, finely chopped
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice
- 1/4 cup toasted sliced almonds
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the carrot sticks with olive oil, honey, chopped sage, salt, and pepper; spread them in a single layer on a baking sheet.
2. Roast the carrots for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until they are caramelized and tender.
3. While the carrots roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside to cool slightly.
4. In a large bowl, whisk together lemon juice, a drizzle of olive oil, and a pinch of salt and pepper to make a dressing.
5. Add the cooked quinoa, roasted carrots, and toasted almonds to the bowl; toss gently to coat everything with the dressing.
6. Adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if needed. Serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Honey‑Sage Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Lentil Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp saffron threads
- 1/4 cup warm water
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1/4 cup toasted sliced almonds
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp honey
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss cauliflower florets with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper, then spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender.
2. While the cauliflower roasts, combine lentils with 3 cups water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer 20‑25 minutes until lentils are just tender but still hold their shape. Drain and set aside.
3. In a small bowl, dissolve saffron threads in warm water for 5 minutes. Stir in remaining olive oil, lemon juice, honey, and a pinch of salt to create the dressing.
4. In a large mixing bowl, combine roasted cauliflower, cooked lentils, diced red bell pepper, and toasted almonds. Drizzle the saffron‑lemon dressing over the mixture and toss gently to coat evenly.
5. Adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed. Transfer the salad to a serving platter, garnish with chopped parsley, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Lentil Salad

text:
Spiced Cardamom Pumpkin and Chickpea Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 lb (450 g) pumpkin, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 large onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp ground cardamom
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)
- Toasted pumpkin seeds (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.  
2. Stir in the garlic, ginger, ground cardamom, smoked paprika, cumin, and cayenne pepper; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
3. Add the cubed pumpkin and chickpeas, tossing to coat them with the spice mixture.  
4. Pour in the vegetable broth, bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer. Cover and cook for 15‑20 minutes, or until the pumpkin is tender.  
5. Stir in the coconut milk, season with salt and black pepper, and let the stew heat through for another 3‑5 minutes.  
6. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with chopped cilantro and toasted pumpkin seeds, and serve hot with crusty bread or rice.
title: Spiced Cardamom Pumpkin and Chickpea Stew

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Lentil Salad with Citrus Vinaigrette

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch rounds
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp saffron threads
- 2 tbsp hot water
- 1 tbsp honey
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tsp orange zest
- 1 tsp Dijon mustard
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
