2. Toss the bell pepper, zucchini, and cauliflower with olive oil, maple syrup, and a pinch of salt; spread them on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway, until caramelized and tender.
3. While the vegetables roast, rinse the basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear.
4. In a medium saucepan combine coconut milk, water, ground cardamom, and sea salt; bring to a gentle boil.
5. Add the rinsed rice, stir once, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is fluffy.
6. Fluff the cooked rice with a fork and gently fold in half of the roasted vegetables, reserving the rest for topping.
7. Serve the spiced coconut rice in bowls, top with the remaining roasted veggies, and garnish with fresh cilantro. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Cardamom Coconut Rice with Roasted Veggies

text:
Citrus‑Infused Tempeh with Herb Quinoa and Roasted Sweet Potatoes

Ingredients:
- 8 oz (225 g) tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into 1‑inch cubes
- ¼ cup freshly squeezed orange juice
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp dried thyme (or 1 tbsp fresh thyme leaves)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional garnish: chopped fresh parsley or cilantro

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper; spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.  
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and fluff with a fork; stir in the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, garlic, thyme, and a squeeze of orange juice. Season with salt and pepper.  
3. In a shallow bowl, whisk together orange juice, lemon zest, maple syrup, and a pinch of salt. Add the tempeh strips and let marinate for 5‑10 minutes, turning once.  
4. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated tempeh (reserve any excess sauce) and sear 3‑4 minutes per side, until caramelized and crisp. Drizzle the reserved sauce over the tempeh in the last minute of cooking.  
5. To serve, spoon a bed of herb‑quinoa onto each plate, top with roasted sweet potatoes, and arrange the citrus‑glazed tempeh on top. Garnish with fresh parsley or cilantro if desired. Enjoy warm!
title: Citrus‑Infused Tempeh with Herb Quinoa and Roasted Sweet Potatoes

text:
Maple‑Glazed Chickpea and Sweet Potato Skillet with Roasted Garlic  

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed  
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced  
- 3 cloves garlic, minced  
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup  
- 1 Tbsp olive oil  
- 1 tsp smoked paprika  
- ½ tsp ground cumin  
- Salt and pepper, to taste  
- Fresh parsley, chopped (optional)  

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Toss the diced sweet potatoes with ½ Tbsp olive oil, half the minced garlic, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until tender and caramelized.  
2. Meanwhile, heat the remaining ½ Tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the remaining minced garlic and sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.  
3. Add the chickpeas, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, 5‑7 minutes until the chickpeas are lightly browned.  
4. Stir in the maple syrup and cook 2 minutes, allowing it to coat the chickpeas.  
5. Transfer the roasted sweet potatoes to the skillet, toss everything together, and cook an additional 2‑3 minutes so the flavors meld.  
6. Remove from heat, garnish with chopped parsley if desired, and serve warm.
title: Maple‑Glazed Chickpea and Sweet Potato Skillet with Roasted Garlic

text:
Cinnamon‑Rosemary Roasted Carrot and Lentil Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 cup green lentils, rinsed
- 2 large carrots, peeled and diced
- 1 small onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 tsp fresh rosemary, chopped
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh parsley for garnish (optional)

Instructions:
1. In a medium pot, heat 1 tbsp olive oil over medium heat. Add the onion and garlic, sauté until translucent, about 3 minutes.  
2. Stir in the diced carrots, cinnamon, and rosemary; cook for another 2 minutes to release aromas.  
3. Add the lentils and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until lentils and carrots are tender.  
4. While the pilaf cooks, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a small skillet over medium‑high heat. Add a pinch of salt and pepper, then toast the cooked lentils and carrots for 2‑3 minutes to develop a light crust.  
5. Remove from heat, fluff with a fork, and adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.  
6. Serve warm, garnished with fresh parsley if desired.
title: Cinnamon‑Rosemary Roasted Carrot and Lentil Pilaf

text:
Sage‑Infused Roasted Sweet Potato and Lentil Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp dried sage
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, dried sage, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper; spread them in a single layer on a baking sheet.
2. Roast the sweet potatoes for 25‑30 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.
3. While the potatoes roast, combine lentils with 2 cups water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook for 20‑25 minutes, or until lentils are just tender but still hold their shape. Drain any excess water and set aside.
4. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, lemon juice, maple syrup, and a pinch of salt to create the dressing.
5. In a large mixing bowl, combine the roasted sweet potatoes, cooked lentils, toasted pumpkin seeds, and chopped parsley. Drizzle the dressing over the mixture and toss gently to coat evenly.
6. Adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed. Serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Sage‑Infused Roasted Sweet Potato and Lentil Salad

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Shrimp and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch piece fresh ginger, grated
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- ¼ tsp red‑pepper flakes (optional)

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa and coconut milk; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and set aside to cool slightly.  
2. While the quinoa cooks, whisk together lime juice, olive oil, garlic, ginger, salt, pepper, and red‑pepper flakes in a large bowl to form a dressing.  
3. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the shrimp and sauté 2‑3 minutes per side, or until pink and opaque. Transfer shrimp to the bowl with the dressing and toss to coat.  
4. Add the cooked quinoa, diced red bell pepper, and chopped cilantro to the bowl. Drizzle any remaining dressing over the mixture and gently toss everything together until evenly combined.  
5. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with extra cilantro and a sprinkle of red‑pepper flakes.
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Shrimp and Quinoa Salad

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Beet and Chickpea Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 3 medium beets, peeled and diced
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 ½ cups canned, drained and rinsed)
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 ½ cups vegetable broth
- ½ teaspoon saffron threads
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 small onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)
- Juice of ½ lemon

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the diced beets with 1  tablespoon olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, or until tender and caramelized.  
2. While the beets roast, place the saffron threads in a small bowl with 2  tablespoons hot vegetable broth; let steep for 5 minutes.  
3. In a medium saucepan, heat the remaining 1  tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté for 3‑4 minutes until translucent. Stir in the minced garlic and cumin; cook another 30 seconds.  
4. Add the rinsed quinoa to the saucepan, stirring to coat with the aromatics. Pour in the saffron‑infused broth plus the remaining vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the quinoa is fluffy and the liquid is absorbed.  
5. Remove the saucepan from heat; fluff the quinoa with a fork. Gently fold in the roasted beets, chickpeas, and lemon juice. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste.  
6. Transfer the pilaf to a serving bowl, garnish with chopped fresh parsley, and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Beet and Chickpea Pilaf

text:
Honey‑Glazed Tofu with Sesame‑Ginger Bok Choy and Brown Rice

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 Tbsp honey
- 2 Tbsp low‑sodium soy sauce
- 1 Tbsp sesame oil
- 1 tsp freshly grated ginger
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 Tbsp rice‑vinegar
- 1 lb (450 g) baby bok choy, stems sliced thin, leaves separated
- 1 cup (200 g) brown rice
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 tsp toasted sesame seeds
- 2 green onions, sliced
- 1 tsp lime zest (optional)
- pinch of red‑pepper flakes (optional)

Instructions:
1. Rinse the brown rice, combine with water (or broth) in a saucepan, bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 40‑45 minutes until tender; fluff and set aside.  
2. In a small bowl whisk together honey, soy sauce, sesame oil, grated ginger, minced garlic, rice‑vinegar, and red‑pepper flakes if using.  
3. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat; add the tofu cubes and sear 3‑4 minutes per side until golden brown.  
4. Pour the honey‑soy mixture over the tofu, toss to coat, and cook another 2‑3 minutes until the glaze thickens and clings to the tofu. Remove tofu from the pan and set aside.  
5. In the same skillet, add a splash of water (or extra oil) and stir‑fry the bok choy stems for 2 minutes, then add the leaves and cook until just wilted, about 1‑2 minutes.  
6. Return the glazed tofu to the skillet, mixing gently with the bok choy to combine and heat through.  
7. Divide the cooked brown rice among serving bowls, top with the honey‑glazed tofu and bok choy mixture.  
8. Garnish each bowl with toasted sesame seeds, sliced green onions, lime zest, and an extra drizzle of soy sauce if desired. Enjoy!
title: Honey‑Glazed Tofu with Sesame‑Ginger Bok Choy and Brown Rice

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Lentil Salad with Orange Vinaigrette

Ingredients:
- 2 medium beets, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup cooked green or brown lentils, rinsed and drained
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1/4 cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped
- 1/4 cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- 1 orange, segmented
- 1 tbsp fresh orange juice
- 1 tsp Dijon mustard
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh thyme leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the beet cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway, until tender and caramelized.  
2. While the beets roast, whisk together orange juice, Dijon mustard, the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and a dash of pepper to create the vinaigrette.  
3. In a large bowl combine the roasted beets, cooked lentils, orange segments, and toasted walnuts. Drizzle the orange vinaigrette over the mixture and toss gently to coat.  
4. Transfer the salad to a serving platter, sprinkle with crumbled feta (if using) and fresh thyme leaves, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Lentil Salad with Orange Vinaigrette

text:
Spiced Cardamom Sweet Potato and Quinoa Skillet

Ingredients:
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and diced
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 small onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon ground cardamom
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- ¼ teaspoon ground cumin
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- ½ cup frozen peas
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Lemon wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 3‑4 minutes.
2. Stir in the garlic, ground cardamom, smoked paprika, and cumin; cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
3. Add the diced sweet potato to the skillet, tossing to coat with the spices. Cook for 5‑6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sweet potato begins to soften.
4. Sprinkle the rinsed quinoa over the vegetables and stir to combine.
5. Pour in the vegetable broth, bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the quinoa is fluffy and the sweet potato is tender. If the liquid is absorbed before the quinoa is cooked, add a splash more broth or water.
6. Fold in the frozen peas and cook for an additional 2 minutes, just until heated through.
7. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Remove from heat and let the skillet rest, covered, for 2 minutes.
8. Transfer the skillet to a serving platter, sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds and fresh cilantro over the top, and serve with lemon wedges on the side. Enjoy warm!
title: Spiced Cardamom Sweet Potato and Quinoa Skillet

text:
Coconut Lime Shrimp with Mango Quinoa Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- 1 ½ cups water
- 1 ripe mango, diced
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tbsp lime zest
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- ½ tsp salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- Pinch of red‑pepper flakes (optional)

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa, coconut milk, water, lime zest, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed and quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let stand 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
2. While the quinoa cooks, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add garlic and ginger, sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.
3. Add the shrimp to the skillet, season with black pepper and red‑pepper flakes if using. Cook 2‑3 minutes per side, or until shrimp turn pink and opaque. Remove shrimp and set aside.
4. Stir lime juice into the cooked quinoa, then fold in the diced mango and chopped cilantro. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt or lime juice if desired.
5. Return the shrimp to the skillet just to re‑warm, then serve over the mango quinoa pilaf. Garnish with extra cilantro and a drizzle of olive oil if desired. Enjoy!
title: Coconut Lime Shrimp with Mango Quinoa Pilaf

text:
Saffron‑Infused Coconut Shrimp and Wild Rice Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup wild rice, rinsed
- 2 cups coconut milk
- 1 ½ cups water
- ½ teaspoon saffron threads
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 small onion, finely chopped
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1 cup frozen peas, thawed
- 1 lime, zest and juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, combine the saffron threads with 2 tablespoons of hot water; let steep for 5 minutes.
2. In a saucepan, bring the coconut milk, water, and saffron infusion to a gentle boil. Add the wild rice, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40‑45 minutes, or until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 10 minutes; fluff with a fork.
3. While the rice cooks, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 3 minutes.
4. Stir in the garlic and red bell pepper; cook for another 2 minutes until fragrant.
5. Add the shrimp to the skillet, season with salt and pepper, and cook, stirring occasionally, until the shrimp turn pink and opaque, about 4‑5 minutes.
6. Mix in the peas, lime zest, and lime juice; cook for 1 minute to heat through.
7. Gently fold the cooked wild rice into the shrimp mixture, adjusting seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice as desired.
8. Transfer to serving bowls, garnish with chopped cilantro, and enjoy immediately.
title: Saffron‑Infused Coconut Shrimp and Wild Rice Pilaf

text:
Roasted Garlic and Herb Chickpea & Sweet Potato Grain Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- 1 tsp dried rosemary
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 cups baby spinach
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp lemon‑tahini dressing (tahini, lemon juice, water, salt)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, half the minced garlic, smoked paprika, thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20 minutes, turning once.  
3. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine the chickpeas with the remaining olive oil, garlic, a pinch of salt, and pepper; spread on the same sheet (or a second sheet) and roast for 15 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through.  
4. Meanwhile, cook the quinoa: bring 2 cups water to a boil, add the quinoa, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until fluffy. Fluff with a fork.  
5. In a large bowl, toss the cooked quinoa with the baby spinach until the leaves wilt slightly.  
6. Assemble the bowls: start with a base of quinoa‑spinach mixture, top with roasted sweet potatoes, chickpeas, and a sprinkle of toasted pumpkin seeds. Drizzle the lemon‑tahini dressing over everything.  
7. Serve warm or at room temperature; enjoy!
title: Roasted Garlic and Herb Chickpea & Sweet Potato Grain Bowl

text:
Spiced Orange‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1/2 cup fresh orange juice
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 avocado, sliced
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- 1 lime, cut into wedges
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, ½ tsp salt, ¼ tsp pepper, and half of the smoked paprika; spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet. Roast for 20 minutes.  
3. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine the chickpeas with the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, cumin, the other half of the smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Add them to the baking sheet and roast together for another 15‑20 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until both vegetables are tender and lightly caramelized.  
4. Meanwhile, rinse the quinoa and cook it in a saucepan with 2 cups water. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.  
5. In a small saucepan over medium heat, whisk together orange juice, maple syrup, and a splash of water. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat and simmer 3‑4 minutes until the glaze thickens slightly. Remove from heat.  
6. Transfer the roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas to a large mixing bowl; drizzle the orange‑maple glaze over them and toss gently to coat evenly.  
7. To assemble each bowl, place a scoop of quinoa at the bottom, top with the glazed sweet potatoes and chickpeas, add avocado slices, and sprinkle with chopped cilantro. Serve with lime wedges on the side for squeezing over the top.
title: Spiced Orange‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

text:
Maple‑Glazed Seared Scallops with Citrus Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 12 sea scallops, patted dry
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp Dijon mustard
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups water
- Zest of 1 orange
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tbsp fresh orange juice
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- ¼ cup chopped fresh parsley
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, whisk together maple syrup, soy sauce, Dijon mustard, and a pinch of pepper.  
2. Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium‑high heat. When shimmering, add the scallops in a single layer; sear 2‑3 minutes per side until golden brown and just opaque in the center. Transfer scallops to a plate.  
3. Brush the maple‑soy mixture over the cooked scallops and let them sit for 1 minute to glaze.  
4. Meanwhile, combine quinoa and water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed.  
5. Remove the quinoa from heat; fluff with a fork and stir in orange zest, lemon zest, orange juice, lemon juice, and parsley. Season with salt and pepper to taste.  
6. Divide the citrus quinoa among serving plates, top with the glazed scallops, and drizzle any remaining glaze from the skillet over the dish. Serve immediately.
title: Maple‑Glazed Seared Scallops with Citrus Quinoa

text:
Maple‑Glazed Portobello Mushroom and Quinoa Stack

Ingredients:
- 4 large portobello mushroom caps, stems removed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves (or ½ tsp dried)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 cups baby spinach (optional, for serving)

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan, combine quinoa and vegetable broth; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
2. While the quinoa cooks, preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together maple syrup, olive oil, minced garlic, thyme, salt, and pepper.
4. Brush both sides of each mushroom cap generously with the maple‑garlic mixture and place them on the prepared baking sheet.
5. Roast the mushrooms for 12‑15 minutes, flipping once, until tender and caramelized.
6. To assemble, place a spoonful of quinoa on a plate, top with a roasted mushroom cap, and add a handful of baby spinach if desired. Drizzle any remaining maple glaze over the stack.
7. Serve warm as a hearty main dish or a satisfying plant‑based entrée.
title: Maple‑Glazed Portobello Mushroom and Quinoa Stack

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Chickpea and Butternut Squash Couscous

Ingredients:
- 1 cup couscous
- 1 ¼ cups vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 cups cubed butternut squash
- ½ teaspoon saffron threads
- 2 tablespoons hot water
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon lemon juice
- ¼ cup fresh parsley, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the cubed butternut squash and chickpeas with 1 tablespoon olive oil, minced garlic, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until the squash is tender and the chickpeas are crisp.
2. While the vegetables roast, place the saffron threads in 2 tablespoons hot water and let steep for 5 minutes.
3. Bring the vegetable broth to a boil, stir in the saffron infusion, then remove from heat. Add the couscous, cover, and let sit for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.
4. Transfer the roasted squash and chickpeas to a large bowl. Add the fluffed couscous, drizzle with the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil and lemon juice, and toss gently to combine.
5. Season with additional salt and pepper if needed, sprinkle with chopped parsley, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Chickpea and Butternut Squash Couscous

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Eggplant and Barley Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 1 cup pearl barley, rinsed
- 2 ½ cups vegetable broth
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 small red onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together the olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Add the eggplant cubes and toss to coat evenly.  
3. Spread the seasoned eggplant on the prepared baking sheet in a single layer. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning once halfway through, until golden and tender.  
4. While the eggplant roasts, bring the vegetable broth to a boil in a medium saucepan. Add the rinsed barley, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30‑35 minutes, or until the barley is tender and the liquid is absorbed.  
5. In a skillet over medium heat, add a drizzle of olive oil and sauté the diced red onion until translucent, about 4 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another 30 seconds.  
6. Stir the cooked barley into the skillet with the onions and garlic, mixing well. Season with additional salt and pepper if needed.  
7. Gently fold the roasted eggplant into the barley mixture, then sprinkle the toasted pumpkin seeds and chopped parsley over the top.  
8. Serve warm as a hearty main dish or a satisfying side, drizzled with a little extra maple syrup if desired.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Eggplant and Barley Pilaf

text:
Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Couscous

Ingredients:
- 1 medium cauliflower head, cut into florets
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup couscous
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup fresh parsley, chopped
- 2 tbsp toasted pine nuts (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cauliflower florets with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, dried thyme, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
3. Roast the cauliflower for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden‑brown and tender.  
4. While the cauliflower roasts, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the chickpeas and sauté for 5‑7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they begin to crisp and turn lightly golden. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper, then remove from heat.  
5. In a small saucepan, bring the vegetable broth to a boil. Stir in the couscous, cover, and remove from heat. Let stand for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.  
6. Combine the roasted cauliflower, sautéed chickpeas, and couscous in a large mixing bowl. Add lemon juice, lemon zest, and chopped parsley; toss gently to distribute flavors evenly.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if desired.  
8. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with toasted pine nuts for extra crunch, if using.
title: Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Couscous

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Beet and Walnut Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 2 medium beets, peeled and diced into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- ½ cup walnuts, roughly chopped
- 3 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 tsp garlic powder
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the diced beets with 1 Tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and half the smoked paprika. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until tender and caramelized.  
3. While the beets roast, combine the quinoa with 2 cups water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the grains are fluffy and the water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.  
4. In a large bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, garlic powder, the remaining smoked paprika, and a generous pinch of salt and pepper. Add the tofu cubes and toss to coat evenly.  
5. Transfer the glazed tofu to a separate baking sheet (or the same sheet after the beets are removed) and bake for 15‑18 minutes, turning halfway, until the tofu is golden and slightly crisp.  
6. In a skillet over medium heat, toast the chopped walnuts for 2‑3 minutes, stirring frequently, until fragrant. Remove from heat.  
7. In a large serving bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted beets, and toasted walnuts. Gently fold in the maple‑glazed tofu. Sprinkle fresh thyme leaves, if using, and adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper as desired.  
8. Serve warm or at room temperature, drizzled with any remaining maple‑glaze from the baking sheet. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Beet and Walnut Quinoa

text:
Citrus‑Infused Lentil and Kale Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 carrot, peeled and diced
- 1 celery stalk, diced
- zest of 1 orange
- juice of 1 orange
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- ¼ teaspoon red‑pepper flakes (optional)
- 2 cups chopped kale, stems removed
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, and celery; sauté until softened, about 5‑7 minutes.
2. Stir in the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, and red‑pepper flakes; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add the lentils, vegetable broth, orange zest, and orange juice. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer and cover. Cook for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender.
4. Season the stew with salt and pepper. Stir in the chopped kale and simmer for an additional 5 minutes, until the kale is wilted but still bright green.
5. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve hot. Enjoy!
title: Citrus‑Infused Lentil and Kale Stew

text:
Spiced Orange‑Maple Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Kale

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp sea salt, plus more to taste
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 2 cups kale, stems removed and torn into bite‑size pieces
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- Zest of 1 orange
- 2 Tbsp fresh orange juice
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp apple cider vinegar

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Toss the chickpeas with 1 Tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, ½ tsp salt, and black pepper. Spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until crisp and golden.
2. While the chickpeas roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.
3. In a large skillet, heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and sauté 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the kale and a pinch of salt; cook, stirring frequently, until wilted but still bright green, about 3‑4 minutes. Remove from heat.
4. In a small bowl, whisk together orange zest, orange juice, maple syrup, and apple cider vinegar to create the glaze.
5. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl. Add the sautéed kale, half of the roasted chickpeas, and the orange‑maple glaze. Toss gently to combine, adjusting seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed.
6. Serve the quinoa mixture in bowls, topping each with the remaining crispy chickpeas for extra crunch. Enjoy warm or at room temperature.
title: Spiced Orange‑Maple Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Kale

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Chickpea and Spinach Curry

Ingredients:
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 4 cups fresh spinach leaves
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- 1 large onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch piece fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tbsp lemon zest
- 2 tsp curry powder
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Cooked basmati rice or quinoa, for serving
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish (optional)

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4‑5 minutes.  
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for another 1 minute until fragrant.  
3. Sprinkle the curry powder, cumin, and smoked paprika over the aromatics; toast the spices for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.  
4. Add the chickpeas and coconut milk to the pan, stirring to combine. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer and let it cook for 5‑7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken slightly.  
5. Fold in the fresh spinach leaves, letting them wilt into the curry, about 2 minutes.  
6. Season with lemon juice, lemon zest, salt, and pepper. Adjust seasoning to taste, adding more lemon juice for brightness if desired.  
7. Serve the curry hot over basmati rice or quinoa, and garnish with fresh cilantro leaves if using. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Ginger Chickpea and Spinach Curry

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Kale Tabbouleh

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups kale, stems removed and torn into bite‑size pieces
- 1/2 red onion, finely diced
- 1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped
- 1/4 cup pumpkin seeds, toasted
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, plus extra for drizzling
- 3 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1/2 tsp sea salt
- 1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet‑potato cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the sweet potatoes in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender.  
4. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine quinoa and 2 cups water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook 15 minutes or until water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.  
5. In a large mixing bowl, massage the kale with the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt for 2‑3 minutes until it softens and darkens.  
6. Add the cooked quinoa, roasted sweet potatoes, diced red onion, and chopped parsley to the bowl with the kale. Toss gently to combine.  
7. Drizzle the lemon juice over the mixture, season with additional salt and pepper to taste, and give it one final toss.  
8. Transfer the tabbouleh to a serving platter, sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds on top, and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Kale Tabbouleh

text:
Citrus‑Infused Coconut Shrimp and Farro Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup farro, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- ½ cup water
- Zest of 1 lime
- ¼ cup fresh orange juice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine the farro, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the grains are tender and the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.  
2. While the farro cooks, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the garlic and ginger, sautéing for 30 seconds until fragrant.  
3. Add the shrimp to the skillet, season with salt and pepper, and cook for 2‑3 minutes per side, or until pink and opaque. Remove the shrimp and set aside.  
4. Reduce the skillet heat to medium and stir in the lime zest, orange juice, and a splash of water (about 2 tbsp) to deglaze the pan, scraping up any browned bits.  
5. Return the cooked farro to the skillet, tossing to coat it in the citrus‑coconut sauce. Cook for 2 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.  
6. Gently fold the shrimp back into the farro mixture, heat through for another minute, then remove from heat.  
7. Sprinkle the chopped cilantro over the dish, adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed, and serve warm.
title: Citrus‑Infused Coconut Shrimp and Farro Pilaf

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 8 oz (225 g) tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 3 large carrots, peeled and cut into matchsticks
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl whisk together maple syrup, soy sauce, smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt; toss the tempeh strips in the mixture until coated.  
3. Spread the tempeh on one side of the prepared sheet and arrange the carrot matchsticks on the other side; drizzle carrots with olive oil and season with salt and pepper.  
4. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning the tempeh halfway through, until the tempeh is golden and the carrots are tender‑crisp.  
5. While the tempeh and carrots roast, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.  
6. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large bowl, fold in the roasted carrots, and drizzle any remaining glaze from the pan over the mixture.  
7. Top the salad with the roasted tempeh strips, toasted pumpkin seeds, and chopped parsley; season with additional salt and pepper if needed.  
8. Serve warm or at room temperature as a hearty main‑course.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Carrot and Quinoa Salad

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Shrimp and Quinoa Stuffed Bell Peppers

Ingredients:
- 4 large red bell peppers, tops cut off and seeds removed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups vegetable broth
- 12 oz (340 g) large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 2 tbsp coconut oil
- 1 tbsp lime zest
- 3 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground coriander
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- ½ cup diced red onion
- 1 cup cherry tomatoes, halved
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 375 °F (190 °C). Place the prepared bell peppers upright in a baking dish.
2. In a saucepan, combine quinoa and vegetable broth; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
3. While the quinoa cooks, heat 1 tbsp coconut oil in a skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the shrimp, lime zest, cumin, smoked paprika, coriander, cayenne (if using), salt, and pepper. Cook 2‑3 minutes per side until pink and opaque. Remove shrimp and set aside.
4. In the same skillet, add the remaining 1 tbsp coconut oil and sauté red onion until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add cherry tomatoes and cook another 2 minutes.
5. Return the shrimp to the skillet, add lime juice, and toss to combine. Cook 1 minute to meld flavors, then remove from heat.
6. In a large bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, shrimp‑tomato mixture, and chopped cilantro. Adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired.
7. Spoon the quinoa‑shrimp filling into each bell pepper cavity, pressing gently to pack the mixture.
8. Cover the baking dish with foil and bake for 25 minutes. Remove foil and bake an additional 10 minutes, or until the peppers are tender and the tops are lightly browned.
9. Serve hot, garnished with extra cilantro and a wedge of lime on the side. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Shrimp and Quinoa Stuffed Bell Peppers

text:
Spiced Coconut‑Lime Chickpea and Roasted Tomato Pasta

Ingredients:
- 12 oz whole‑wheat spaghetti
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 cups cherry tomatoes, halved
- 1 ½ tbsp coconut oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tbsp lime zest
- 3 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp red‑pepper flakes (optional)
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the halved cherry tomatoes with 1 tbsp coconut oil, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of black pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 15‑20 minutes, until blistered and slightly caramelized.
2. While the tomatoes roast, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the spaghetti according to package directions until al dente; reserve ½ cup of pasta water, then drain.
3. In a large skillet over medium heat, melt the remaining ½ tbsp coconut oil. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger; sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
4. Stir in the chickpeas, cumin, smoked paprika, and red‑pepper flakes. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 3‑4 minutes until the chickpeas are warmed through and begin to brown slightly.
5. Add the roasted tomatoes, lime zest, lime juice, and maple syrup to the skillet. Toss everything together, letting the mixture simmer for 2‑3 minutes; if it looks dry, add a splash of the reserved pasta water.
6. Add the cooked spaghetti to the skillet, tossing to coat the noodles evenly with the sauce. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste, and drizzle a little more pasta water if needed for a silky texture.
7. Remove from heat and stir in the chopped cilantro. Serve immediately, garnished with extra cilantro or a wedge of lime if desired.
title: Spiced Coconut‑Lime Chickpea and Roasted Tomato Pasta

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Black Bean Tostada

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 ½ cups cooked black beans (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 1 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp sea salt
- Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 4 small corn tortillas
- 1 ripe avocado, sliced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped
- Juice of 1 lime
- Optional: crumbled feta or cotija cheese for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Toss the diced sweet potatoes with olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper; spread them in a single layer on a baking sheet.
2. Roast the sweet potatoes for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway, until tender and caramelized at the edges.
3. While the sweet potatoes roast, warm the black beans in a small saucepan over low heat, adding a splash of water and a pinch of salt; keep them hot.
4. Heat a dry skillet over medium‑high heat. Lightly toast each corn tortilla for about 30 seconds per side until pliable but not crispy; set aside.
5. Assemble each tostada: place a toasted tortilla on a plate, top with a generous scoop of roasted sweet potatoes, then add black beans.
6. Drizzle a little extra lime juice over the filling, then arrange avocado slices on top.
7. Sprinkle chopped cilantro (and optional cheese) over the assembled tostada. Serve immediately with extra lime wedges on the side.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Black Bean Tostada

text:
Ginger‑Lime Baked Tofu with Coconut Rice and Roasted Snap Peas

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 Tbsp soy sauce
- 1 Tbsp lime juice
- 1 Tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp sesame oil
- 1 cup jasmine rice
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- ½ cup water
- 1 lb (450 g) snap peas, trimmed
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves for garnish
- Lime wedges for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, whisk together soy sauce, lime juice, grated ginger, and sesame oil. Add the tofu cubes, toss to coat, and let marinate for 10 minutes.  
3. Spread the marinated tofu on the prepared baking sheet and bake for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and slightly crisp.  
4. While the tofu bakes, combine jasmine rice, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Fluff with a fork.  
5. On a separate baking sheet, toss snap peas with olive oil, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Roast in the same oven for 8‑10 minutes, until bright green and just tender.  
6. To serve, spoon coconut rice onto plates, top with baked tofu and roasted snap peas. Garnish with fresh cilantro and a squeeze of lime juice. Enjoy!
title: Ginger‑Lime Baked Tofu with Coconut Rice and Roasted Snap Peas

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea and Spinach Stew

Ingredients:
- 2 tablespoons coconut oil
- 1 large onion, diced
- 3 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1 can (14 oz) coconut milk
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 cups fresh baby spinach
- 1 lime, zest and juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro, chopped (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Heat the coconut oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Sprinkle the turmeric, cumin, and smoked paprika over the aromatics. Toast the spices for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
4. Pour in the coconut milk and vegetable broth, scraping the bottom of the pot to release any browned bits.
5. Add the chickpeas, bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
6. Stir in the fresh spinach and cook until wilted, about 2 minutes.
7. Add the lime zest and juice, then season with salt and pepper to taste. Adjust seasoning if needed.
8. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with chopped cilantro if desired, and serve hot with steamed rice or crusty bread.
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea and Spinach Stew

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Shrimp and Coconut Rice Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup jasmine rice
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- 1 cup water
- 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear. In a saucepan combine the rice, coconut milk, water, a pinch of salt, and half of the grated ginger. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Remove from heat and let it sit, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
2. While the rice cooks, whisk together the lemon juice, remaining ginger, turmeric, garlic, olive oil, salt, and pepper in a large bowl to create a marinating sauce.
3. Add the shrimp to the bowl, tossing to coat evenly. Let the shrimp marinate for 5 minutes while the rice finishes cooking.
4. Heat a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the shrimp and cook for 2‑3 minutes per side, until pink and opaque. Remove from heat.
5. In a serving bowl, combine the cooked coconut rice, cooked shrimp, and chopped cilantro. Drizzle any remaining sauce over the top and gently toss to combine.
6. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with an extra squeeze of lemon if desired. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Shrimp and Coconut Rice Salad

text:
Crispy Orange‑Glazed Tofu with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 block (14 oz) firm tofu, pressed and cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 2  tbsp cornstarch
- 2  tbsp neutral oil (e.g., canola)
- 1/4  cup fresh orange juice
- 2  tbsp soy sauce
- 1  tbsp maple syrup
- 1  tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1  clove garlic, minced
- 1  tsp rice‑vinegar
- Zest of 1 lime
- 1  tbsp lime juice
- 1  cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1  ½ cups coconut milk
- 1  cup water
- 1  cup snap peas, trimmed
- 1  cup shredded carrots
- 1  tbsp toasted sesame seeds (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. In a shallow bowl, toss the tofu cubes
title: Crispy Orange‑Glazed Tofu with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa

text:
Maple‑Glazed Chickpea and Sweet Potato Curry with Coconut Rice

Ingredients:
- 1 cup dried chickpeas (or 2 cups cooked)
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 large onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- 2 tbsp curry powder
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 can (13.5 oz) coconut milk
- 1 cup jasmine rice
- 1 cup coconut milk (for rice)
- 2 tbsp lime juice
- 2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- 2 tbsp vegetable oil
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. If using dried chickpeas, soak them overnight, then drain and boil until tender (about 1 hour). If using canned, rinse and set aside.  
2. In a medium saucepan, combine the jasmine rice with 1 cup coconut milk and 1 cup water; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until fluffy. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.  
3. While the rice cooks, heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes.  
4. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
5. Add the curry powder and maple syrup, stirring to coat the aromatics; cook 30 seconds to release the spices.  
6. Add the cubed sweet potatoes and cooked chickpeas to the skillet; pour in the can of coconut milk, bring to a gentle simmer, and season with salt and pepper.  
7. Cover and simmer 15‑20 minutes, or until the sweet potatoes are tender and the sauce has thickened slightly.  
8. Remove from heat and stir in the lime juice and chopped cilantro. Adjust seasoning if needed.  
9. Serve the maple‑glazed chickpea and sweet potato curry over a bed of coconut rice, garnished with extra cilantro and a drizzle of maple syrup if desired.
title: Maple‑Glazed Chickpea and Sweet Potato Curry with Coconut Rice

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Quinoa Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 ½ cups cooked quinoa
- 1 cup canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp saffron threads
- ¼ cup warm water
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 tbsp toasted sliced almonds
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)
- Lemon wedges (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, combine the saffron threads with warm water; let steep for 5 minutes.  
3. Toss the cauliflower florets with 1 tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast the cauliflower for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden‑brown and tender.  
5. While the cauliflower roasts, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the chickpeas and sauté for 5‑7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lightly crisp. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.  
6. In a large bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted cauliflower, and sautéed chickpeas. Drizzle the saffron‑infused water over the mixture and toss gently to distribute the color and flavor evenly.  
7. Adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed.  
8. Divide the bowl into serving plates, sprinkle with toasted sliced almonds and chopped parsley, and serve with lemon wedges on the side for a bright finish.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Quinoa Bowl

text:
Spiced Orange‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Chickpea Sheet Pan Dinner

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 Tbsp orange marmalade
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp ground cinnamon
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 Tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- Zest of 1 orange
- 1 Tbsp toasted sesame seeds (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a large bowl, whisk together olive oil, orange marmalade, smoked paprika, cumin, cinnamon, cayenne, salt, and pepper until smooth.
3. Add the cubed sweet potatoes and chickpeas to the bowl, tossing to coat evenly with the spiced orange glaze.
4. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet, ensuring the sweet potatoes are not overcrowded.
5. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until the sweet potatoes are tender and caramelized at the edges and the chickpeas are crisp.
6. Remove from the oven and immediately sprinkle with orange zest, chopped cilantro, and toasted sesame seeds, if using.
7. Serve hot as a main dish or over a bed of quinoa or rice for a complete meal. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Orange‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Chickpea Sheet Pan Dinner

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Garlic Brussels Sprouts and Farro

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 1 cup farro, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth (for cooking farro)
- 1 lb (450 g) Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Toss the Brussels sprouts with 1 tbsp olive oil, half the minced garlic, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway, until crisp‑tender and caramelized.  
2. While the sprouts roast, combine the farro and vegetable broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook 20‑25 minutes until the grains are tender and the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork, stir in lemon juice, thyme, and a pinch of salt; set aside.  
3. In a large bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, the remaining minced garlic, and a dash of salt and pepper. Add the cubed tofu and toss to coat evenly.  
4. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the glazed tofu and sear for 3‑4 minutes per side, until golden brown and caramelized. Transfer the tofu to a plate.  
5. To assemble, divide the farro among serving bowls, top with roasted Brussels sprouts, and arrange the maple‑glazed tofu on top. Drizzle any pan juices over the dish and garnish with extra thyme leaves if desired. Serve warm.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Garlic Brussels Sprouts and Farro

text:
Saffron‑Infused Coconut Lentil and Spinach Curry

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 large onion, finely diced
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tbsp saffron threads, steeped in 2 Tbsp hot water
- 1 tbsp curry powder
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tbsp tomato paste
- 4 cups fresh spinach, roughly chopped
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Cooked basmati rice or naan, for serving

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4‑5 minutes.  
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for another minute until fragrant.  
3. Add the curry powder, ground cumin, smoked paprika, and tomato paste. Cook, stirring constantly, for 1‑2 minutes to toast the spices.  
4. Pour in the steeped saffron mixture, coconut milk, and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil.  
5. Add the rinsed red lentils, reduce the heat to a simmer, and cover. Cook for 15‑20 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and the sauce has thickened, stirring occasionally.  
6. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Fold in the chopped spinach and cook for 2‑3 minutes, just until the spinach wilts.  
7. Remove the pan from heat. Ladle the curry over cooked basmati rice or serve with warm naan. Garnish with fresh cilantro leaves. Enjoy!
title: Saffron‑Infused Coconut Lentil and Spinach Curry

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Glazed Tempeh with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa and Roasted Brussels Sprouts

Ingredients:
- 1 block (8 oz) tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 Tbsp olive oil (for glaze)
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- Zest and juice of 1 lime
- 2 cups Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 1 Tbsp coconut oil (for roasting)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional garnish: chopped fresh cilantro or toasted sesame seeds

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the Brussels sprouts with coconut oil, salt, and pepper; spread them cut‑side down on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until caramelized and tender.  
3. While the sprouts roast, whisk together maple syrup, ground cinnamon, soy sauce, and olive oil in a shallow bowl.  
4. Pat the tempeh strips dry with paper towels, then dip each strip into the maple‑cinnamon glaze, ensuring both sides are coated. Arrange the glazed tempeh on a separate baking sheet.  
5. Bake the tempeh in the same oven for 12‑15 minutes, flipping halfway through, until the glaze is glossy and the edges are lightly crisp.  
6. Meanwhile, combine quinoa, coconut milk, lime zest, and a pinch of salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and stir in lime juice.  
7. To serve, spoon a bed of coconut‑lime quinoa onto plates, top with roasted Brussels sprouts, and arrange the cinnamon‑maple tempeh strips alongside. Garnish with cilantro or toasted sesame seeds if desired. Enjoy warm!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Glazed Tempeh with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa and Roasted Brussels Sprouts

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Brussels Sprouts and Quinoa Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 8 oz (225 g) tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 lb (450 g) Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 small red onion, finely diced
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- ¼ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a shallow bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, ground cinnamon, soy sauce, and ½ tbsp olive oil. Add the tempeh strips, toss to coat, and let marinate while you prepare the vegetables.
3. Toss the Brussels sprouts with the remaining ½ tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until crisp‑tender and caramelized.
4. While the sprouts roast, heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated tempeh strips in a single layer and sear for 3‑4 minutes per side, until golden and the glaze is sticky. Transfer the cooked tempeh to a plate.
5. In a medium saucepan, combine the rinsed quinoa and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes.
6. Fluff the quinoa with a fork and stir in the diced red onion, minced garlic, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Keep warm.
7. To serve, divide the quinoa pilaf among plates, top with roasted Brussels sprouts, and arrange the cinnamon‑maple glazed tempeh strips on top. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley if desired. Enjoy while hot!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Brussels Sprouts and Quinoa Pilaf

text:
Citrus‑Ginger Chickpea and Sweet Potato Skillet

Ingredients:
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and diced
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 1 red bell pepper, sliced
- 1 small red onion, thinly sliced
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, minced
- zest of 1 orange
- juice of 1 orange
- 1 tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tsp honey or maple syrup
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- pinch of red‑pepper flakes
- salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat a large skillet over medium heat and add the olive oil.
2. When the oil shimmers, add the diced sweet potato and sauté for 5‑7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it begins to soften and turn golden.
3. Add the sliced red onion and bell pepper to the skillet; continue cooking for another 3‑4 minutes until the vegetables are tender-crisp.
4. Stir in the minced ginger and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
5. In a small bowl, whisk together the orange zest, orange juice, soy sauce, honey, cumin, and red‑pepper flakes.
6. Add the chickpeas to the skillet, then pour the orange‑ginger sauce over everything. Toss to coat evenly and cook for 2‑3 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken and the sweet potato to finish cooking.
7. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Remove the skillet from heat and sprinkle the chopped cilantro and toasted sesame seeds over the top.
8. Serve hot, either on its own or over a bed of steamed rice or quinoa for a heartier meal. Enjoy!
title: Citrus‑Ginger Chickpea and Sweet Potato Skillet

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Chickpea and Butternut Squash Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 cups butternut squash, peeled and cubed
- ½ teaspoon saffron threads
- 2 tablespoons hot water (for saffron)
- 2 tablespoons olive oil, divided
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
- 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). In a small bowl, combine the saffron threads with 2 tablespoons hot water; let steep while you prepare the vegetables.  
2. Toss the cubed butternut squash and chickpeas with 1 tablespoon olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until the squash is tender and the chickpeas are crisp.  
3. Meanwhile, bring the quinoa and water (or broth) to a boil in a saucepan. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.  
4. In a large bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted squash, and chickpeas. Add the saffron infusion (including the threads) and the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil. Toss gently to coat everything evenly.  
5. Season with additional salt and pepper if needed, then drizzle with lemon juice and sprinkle with chopped parsley. Serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Chickpea and Butternut Squash Quinoa Salad

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Tacos with Avocado Crema

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and sliced into thin strips
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- Salt and black pepper, to taste
- 8 small corn tortillas
- 1 ripe avocado
- 1 Tbsp lime juice
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 2 Tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the carrot strips and chickpeas with maple syrup, cinnamon, smoked paprika, cayenne (if using), olive oil, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the carrots are tender and lightly caramelized and the chickpeas are crisp.  
4. While the vegetables roast, prepare the avocado crema: combine the avocado, lime juice, minced garlic, a pinch of salt, and a splash of water in a food processor or blender; blend until smooth and creamy. Adjust seasoning to taste.  
5. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 30 seconds per side, or wrap them in foil and heat in the oven for the last 5 minutes of roasting.  
6. Assemble each taco by placing a generous spoonful of the roasted carrot‑chickpea mixture onto a tortilla, drizzling with avocado crema, sprinkling with chopped cilantro, and topping with crumbled feta if desired.  
7. Serve immediately, enjoying the sweet‑spicy flavor contrast and fresh herb garnish.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Tacos with Avocado Crema

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Power Bowl

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup cooked quinoa
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- 1 avocado, sliced
- 2 Tbsp lemon‑tahini dressing (tahini, lemon juice, water, salt)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp cinnamon, ½ tsp smoked paprika, a pinch of salt, and half of the maple syrup. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
3. In the same bowl, toss the chickpeas with the remaining olive oil, the rest of the maple syrup, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Add the chickpeas to the baking sheet, arranging them around the sweet potatoes.  
4. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning the vegetables halfway through, until the sweet potatoes are tender and caramelized and the chickpeas are crisp.  
5. While the vegetables roast, prepare the quinoa according to package instructions; fluff with a fork and keep warm.  
6. Assemble each bowl: start with a base of quinoa, top with roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas, add sliced avocado, toasted pumpkin seeds, and chopped parsley.  
7. Drizzle the lemon‑tahini dressing over the bowl and serve immediately.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Power Bowl

text:
Maple‑Glazed Roasted Brussels Sprouts with Pomegranate Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 lb Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the Brussels sprouts with olive oil, maple syrup, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the sprouts cut‑side down on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway, until caramelized and tender.  
4. While the sprouts roast, combine quinoa and water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes or until water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.  
5. Stir lemon juice into the cooked quinoa, then gently fold in the roasted Brussels sprouts, pomegranate seeds, and chopped parsley.  
6. Serve warm or at room temperature, drizzling any remaining maple glaze from the pan over the top if desired.
title: Maple‑Glazed Roasted Brussels Sprouts with Pomegranate Quinoa

text:
Citrus‑Honey Glazed Tempeh with Quinoa and Roasted Brussels Sprouts

Ingredients:
- 8 oz (225 g) tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 lb (450 g) Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 2 tbsp honey
- 2 tbsp fresh orange juice
- 1 tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp sesame oil
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds (optional, for garnish)
- 2 green onions, thinly sliced (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Toss the Brussels sprouts with olive oil, salt, and pepper, then spread them on a baking sheet in a single layer. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until crisp‑tender and caramelized.  
2. While the sprouts roast, combine honey, orange juice, soy sauce, grated ginger, and sesame oil in a shallow bowl. Add the tempeh strips and toss to coat; let marinate for 5‑10 minutes.  
3. Bring the quinoa and water (or broth) to a boil in a saucepan, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the grains are fluffy. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
4. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated tempeh strips in a single layer and cook 3‑4 minutes per side, or until golden and caramelized, brushing with any remaining glaze during the last minute of cooking.  
5. To assemble, divide the cooked quinoa among serving bowls, top with roasted Brussels sprouts and glazed tempeh. Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds and sliced green onions, if using. Serve immediately.
title: Citrus‑Honey Glazed Tempeh with Quinoa and Roasted Brussels Sprouts

text:
Cinnamon‑Orange Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- Zest of 1 orange
- 2 Tbsp fresh orange juice
- 1 Tbsp maple syrup
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- ¼ tsp smoked paprika
- 2 cups baby spinach leaves
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp crumbled feta cheese (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, cinnamon, orange zest, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20 minutes.  
3. While the sweet potatoes roast, whisk together the remaining olive oil, orange juice, maple syrup, smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt in a small bowl to make the dressing.  
4. After the sweet potatoes have roasted for 20 minutes, add the chickpeas to the pan, drizzle with half of the dressing, and toss to combine. Roast for an additional 10‑12 minutes, until the sweet potatoes are tender and the chickpeas are lightly crisp.  
5. Transfer the roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas to a large serving bowl. Add the baby spinach, drizzle with the remaining orange‑maple dressing, and toss gently to coat.  
6. Sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds and crumbled feta over the top, if using. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Orange Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Salad

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu and Roasted Garlic Sweet Potato Curry

Ingredients:
- 1 block (14 oz) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 3  tbsp maple syrup
- 2  tbsp soy sauce
- 1  tbsp olive oil
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1  tsp ground cumin
- 1  tsp smoked paprika
- 1  tsp ground ginger
- 1  cup coconut milk
- 1  cup vegetable broth
- 1  tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2  tbsp water
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves for garnish
- Cooked brown rice, for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the diced sweet potatoes with 1  tbsp olive oil, half the minced garlic, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, until tender and caramelized.
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, whisk together maple syrup, soy sauce, cumin, smoked paprika, ground ginger, and the remaining garlic in a bowl.
3. Heat the remaining 1  tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the tofu cubes and sauté for 5‑7 minutes, turning until all sides are golden brown.
4. Pour the maple‑soy mixture over the tofu, stirring to coat. Cook for 2 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
5. Add the roasted sweet potatoes, coconut milk, and vegetable broth to the skillet. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook 5‑7 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
6. Stir in the cornstarch slurry and continue cooking for 1‑2 minutes, until the curry reaches a creamy consistency. Adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed.
7. Serve the maple‑glazed tofu and sweet potato curry over warm brown rice, garnished with fresh cilantro leaves. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu and Roasted Garlic Sweet Potato Curry

text:
Citrus‑Honey Glazed Carrot and Lentil Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and sliced into thin ribbons
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp honey
- 1 tbsp orange juice
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- 1 cup baby spinach leaves
- ¼ cup toasted almond slivers
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional: a drizzle of tahini sauce for serving

Instructions:
1. In a saucepan, combine the lentils, vegetable broth, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until lentils are tender but still hold their shape. Drain any excess liquid and set aside.  
2. While the lentils cook, whisk together honey, orange juice, lemon zest, cumin, smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt in a small bowl.  
3. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the carrot ribbons and sauté for 3‑4 minutes until they begin to soften.  
4. Pour the citrus‑honey glaze over the carrots, stirring to coat evenly. Continue cooking for another 2‑3 minutes, allowing the glaze to thicken and the carrots to caramelize.  
5. To assemble the bowl, place a handful of baby spinach at the bottom of each serving dish. Top with a scoop of cooked lentils, then arrange the glazed carrots on top.  
6. Sprinkle toasted almond slivers over the bowl, and season with additional salt and pepper if desired.  
7. If using, drizzle a spoonful of tahini sauce around the edge for extra richness. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Citrus‑Honey Glazed Carrot and Lentil Buddha Bowl

text:
Sage‑Infused Roasted Tomato and Lentil Soup

Ingredients:
- 1 lb (450 g) ripe tomatoes, quartered
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 large carrot, peeled and diced
- 1 celery stalk, diced
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 teaspoon dried sage (or 1 tablespoon fresh sage, chopped)
- 1 bay leaf
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional garnish: a drizzle of extra‑virgin olive oil and fresh sage leaves

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the quartered tomatoes with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper, then spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until caramelized.
2. While the tomatoes roast, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, and celery; sauté for 5‑7 minutes until softened.
3. Stir in the minced garlic and dried sage; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Add the rinsed red lentils, roasted tomatoes (with any pan juices), vegetable broth, and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer.
5. Cover and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and the soup has thickened. Remove the bay leaf.
6. Using an immersion blender (or a countertop blender in batches), puree the soup until smooth but still slightly chunky. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot, garnished with a drizzle of olive oil and fresh sage leaves if desired.
title: Sage‑Infused Roasted Tomato and Lentil Soup

text:
Crispy Coconut‑Lime Shrimp with Mango Avocado Salsa

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- ½ cup coconut flakes, unsweetened
- ¼ cup panko breadcrumbs
- 1 tsp lime zest
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 1 egg, lightly beaten
- 1 ripe mango, diced
- 1 avocado, diced
- ¼ cup red onion, finely chopped
- 1 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Olive oil for frying

Instructions:
1. In a shallow bowl, combine coconut flakes, panko, lime zest, salt, and pepper.
2. In another bowl, whisk together the egg and lime juice.
3. Pat the shrimp dry, then dip each piece first into the egg mixture, then coat thoroughly with the coconut‑panko mixture.
4. Heat a thin layer of olive oil in a skillet over medium‑high heat. Fry the shrimp for 2‑3 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through. Transfer to a paper‑towel‑lined plate to drain.
5. While the shrimp cooks, prepare the salsa: gently toss mango, avocado, red onion, and cilantro in a small bowl; season with a pinch of salt and a drizzle of lime juice.
6. Serve the crispy shrimp on a platter topped with generous spoonfuls of mango‑avocado salsa. Enjoy warm.
title: Crispy Coconut‑Lime Shrimp with Mango Avocado Salsa

text:
Lemon‑Basil Quinoa with Roasted Cauliflower and Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and black pepper, to taste
- 1/4 cup fresh basil leaves, chopped
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tbsp lemon juice
- 1/3 cup pomegranate seeds
- 1/4 cup toasted pine nuts (optional)

Instructions:
