1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss cauliflower florets with olive oil, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until golden and tender.
2. While the cauliflower roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
3. In a large bowl, whisk together lemon juice, lemon zest, and chopped basil; season lightly with salt and pepper.
4. Add the cooked quinoa to the bowl and toss to coat with the lemon‑basil dressing.
5. Gently fold in the roasted cauliflower, pomegranate seeds, and toasted pine nuts (if using).
6. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with extra basil leaves and a drizzle of olive oil if desired.
title: Lemon‑Basil Quinoa with Roasted Cauliflower and Pomegranate

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 ½  teaspoons saffron threads
- 2  tablespoons hot water
- 2  tablespoons olive oil
- 1  teaspoon ground cumin
- ½  teaspoon smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1  tablespoon lemon juice
- ¼  cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1  cup cooked quinoa or brown rice (optional, for serving)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, combine the saffron threads with hot water; let steep for 5 minutes.  
3. In a large mixing bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with 1  tablespoon olive oil, half the cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast the sweet potatoes for 20 minutes, then remove the sheet, flip the cubes, and add the chickpeas tossed with the remaining olive oil, cumin, salt, and pepper. Return to the oven and roast for an additional 15 minutes, or until the sweet potatoes are tender and the chickpeas are crisp.  
5. Transfer the roasted vegetables to a serving bowl; drizzle with the saffron‑infused water, lemon juice, and sprinkle with chopped cilantro. Toss gently to coat.  
6. Serve the saffron‑infused chickpea and sweet potato mixture over cooked quinoa or brown rice, if desired, and enjoy a vibrant, aromatic Buddha bowl.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Buddha Bowl

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Garlic Sweet Potato and Kale Stir‑Fry

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 2 tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp ground ginger
- 4 cups kale, stems removed and torn
- ½ cup water or vegetable broth
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional garnish: toasted sesame seeds and sliced green onions

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Toss the diced sweet potatoes with ½ tbsp olive oil, half the minced garlic, a pinch of salt, and smoked paprika; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until caramelized and tender.
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, whisk together maple syrup, soy sauce, rice vinegar, ground ginger, the remaining olive oil, and the rest of the minced garlic in a shallow bowl.
3. Pat the tofu cubes dry, then add them to the glaze, tossing gently to coat. Let them sit for 5 minutes to absorb flavor.
4. Heat a large non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the glazed tofu and sear for 3‑4 minutes per side, until golden and slightly crisp. Transfer the tofu to a plate.
5. In the same skillet, add the roasted sweet potatoes, kale, and ½ cup water or broth. Stir‑fry for 3‑4 minutes, covering the pan briefly to steam the kale until wilted but still bright green.
6. Return the tofu to the skillet, toss everything together, and cook for an additional minute to re‑heat the tofu and allow the flavors to meld. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
7. Serve hot, sprinkled with toasted sesame seeds and sliced green onions if desired. Enjoy the sweet‑savory glaze, creamy sweet potatoes, and crisp kale in each bite.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Garlic Sweet Potato and Kale Stir‑Fry

text:
Spiced Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Quinoa Bowl with Roasted Garlic Shrimp  

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed  
- 1 ¾ cups water or vegetable broth  
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined  
- 2 tbsp olive oil, divided  
- 1 tsp ground turmeric  
- ½ tsp smoked paprika  
- 1 tsp coconut‑lime glaze (mix 2 tbsp coconut milk, 1 tbsp lime juice, 1 tsp honey)  
- 3 cloves garlic, minced  
- 1 cup frozen corn, thawed  
- 1 cup cherry tomatoes, halved  
- ½ cup fresh cilantro, chopped  
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste  
- Lime wedges, for serving  

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa and water (or broth); bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
2. While quinoa cooks, preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Toss the shrimp with 1 tbsp olive oil, turmeric, smoked paprika, minced garlic, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet and roast 8‑10 minutes, until pink and opaque.  
3. In a small skillet over medium heat, add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and the coconut‑lime glaze. Warm for 1‑2 minutes, then stir in the corn and cherry tomatoes; cook until just heated through, about 3 minutes. Season with a pinch of salt.  
4. Assemble the bowl: place a bed of quinoa, top with the glazed corn‑tomato mixture, then arrange the roasted shrimp on top. Sprinkle chopped cilantro over everything.  
5. Serve immediately with lime wedges for squeezing over the bowl. Enjoy the bright, spiced flavors!
title: Spiced Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Quinoa Bowl with Roasted Garlic Shrimp

text:
Lemon‑Thyme Quinoa with Roasted Butternut Squash and Pomegranate  

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 small butternut squash, peeled and cubed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves (or ½ tsp dried thyme)
- Zest of 1 lemon
- Juice of 1 lemon
- ¼ tsp salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the cubed butternut squash with 1 tbsp olive oil, thyme, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
2. While the squash roasts, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
3. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt.  
4. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl; add the roasted butternut squash, drizzle with the lemon‑thyme dressing, and toss gently to combine.  
5. Sprinkle pomegranate seeds and toasted pumpkin seeds over the top for color and crunch. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Thyme Quinoa with Roasted Butternut Squash and Pomegranate

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Chickpea and Spinach Stuffed Portobello Mushrooms

Ingredients:
- 4 large portobello mushroom caps, stems removed
- 1 cup cooked chickpeas, rinsed and drained
- 2 cups fresh spinach leaves, roughly chopped
- 1/2 cup coconut milk
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tbsp coconut oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1/4 tsp red‑chili flakes (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a skillet over medium heat, melt the coconut oil. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger; sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
3. Stir in the chickpeas, cumin, and chili flakes. Cook for 2‑3 minutes, allowing the spices to toast lightly.
4. Add the chopped spinach and cook until wilted, about 1 minute. Pour in the coconut milk and lime juice, stirring to combine. Season with salt and pepper, then remove from heat.
5. Place the mushroom caps gill‑side up on the prepared baking sheet. Spoon the chickpea‑spinach mixture evenly into each cap, pressing gently to fill.
6. Bake for 15‑18 minutes, until the mushrooms are tender and the filling is heated through.
7. Remove from the oven and let cool for a couple of minutes. Serve warm, garnished with an extra squeeze of lime or a sprinkle of fresh cilantro if desired.
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Chickpea and Spinach Stuffed Portobello Mushrooms

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Shrimp and Coconut Rice

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup jasmine rice
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- 1 ½ cups water
- 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear. In a medium saucepan combine the rice, coconut milk, water, a pinch of salt, and half of the turmeric. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
2. While the rice cooks, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger, sautéing for 30 seconds until fragrant.  
3. Add the shrimp to the skillet, sprinkle with the remaining turmeric, salt, and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 2‑3 minutes, or until the shrimp turn pink and opaque.  
4. Stir in the lemon juice and continue cooking for another 30 seconds to combine the flavors. Remove the skillet from heat.  
5. Serve the shrimp over a bed of coconut rice, drizzling any pan juices over the top. Garnish with chopped cilantro and an extra squeeze of lemon if desired. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Shrimp and Coconut Rice

text:
Maple‑Glazed Roasted Eggplant and Farro Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 1 cup farro, rinsed
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 3 tbsp olive oil, divided
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds (optional garnish)
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the eggplant cubes with 2 tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, minced garlic, thyme, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the eggplant on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until caramelized and tender.  
4. While the eggplant roasts, bring 2 cups water to a boil, add the farro, reduce to a simmer, and cook 20‑25 minutes until al dente. Drain any excess water and let cool slightly.  
5. In a large mixing bowl combine the cooked farro, roasted eggplant, lemon juice, remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, and adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.  
6. Toss in chopped parsley and toasted pumpkin seeds just before serving.  
7. Serve warm or at room temperature as a hearty side or light main dish.
title: Maple‑Glazed Roasted Eggplant and Farro Salad

text:
Lemon‑Basil Quinoa with Roasted Eggplant and Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 large eggplant, cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp salt
- ½ tsp black pepper
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- Zest of 1 lemon
- Juice of 1 lemon
- ¼ cup fresh basil leaves, chopped
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds
- Optional: 1 tbsp toasted pine nuts for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the eggplant cubes with olive oil, salt, pepper, and half the minced garlic; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.
2. While the eggplant roasts, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together lemon zest, lemon juice, the remaining minced garlic, and a drizzle of olive oil; season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
4. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl; add the roasted eggplant, chopped basil, and the lemon‑garlic dressing. Toss gently to combine.
5. Serve the quinoa mixture in bowls, topped with pomegranate seeds and optional toasted pine nuts for extra crunch. Enjoy warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Basil Quinoa with Roasted Eggplant and Pomegranate

text:
Spiced Cardamom Sweet Potato and Quinoa Patties

Ingredients:
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup cooked quinoa
- 1/2 cup chickpeas, mashed
- 1 small red onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp ground cardamom
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- 1/4 tsp ground cumin
- 1/4 tsp sea salt
- 1/4 tsp black pepper
- 1 egg, lightly beaten (or flax egg for vegan)
- 2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- 2 tbsp oat flour (or all‑purpose flour)
- 2 tbsp olive oil, for pan‑frying
- Optional garnish: yogurt or tahini drizzle, lime wedges

Instructions:
1. Place the cubed sweet potato in a pot of salted water, bring to a boil, and cook until tender, about 10‑12 minutes. Drain and mash until smooth; set aside to cool slightly.  
2. In a large bowl combine the mashed sweet potato, cooked quinoa, mashed chickpeas, diced red onion, and minced garlic.  
3. Sprinkle the ground cardamom, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper over the mixture; stir to distribute the spices evenly.  
4. Add the beaten egg (or flax egg), chopped cilantro, and oat flour. Mix until the mixture holds together but is not overly wet. Adjust with a little more flour if needed.  
5. Using your hands, form the mixture into 8‑10 equal patties, about 1/2‑inch thick.  
6. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Once shimmering, add the patties in a single layer (work in batches if necessary).  
7. Cook each side for 4‑5 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Transfer cooked patties to a paper‑towel‑lined plate to absorb excess oil.  
8. Serve the patties warm, drizzled with yogurt or tahini and a squeeze of lime, alongside a fresh salad or grain bowl if desired.
title: Spiced Cardamom Sweet Potato and Quinoa Patties

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Couscous

Ingredients:
- 1 cup couscous
- 1 ¼ cups vegetable broth
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and diced (about 2 cups)
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 ½ teaspoons saffron threads
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- ¼ teaspoon ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup toasted sliced almonds
- 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, chopped
- Juice of ½ lemon

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the diced sweet potato and chickpeas with olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper; spread them in a single layer on a baking sheet.
2. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway, until the sweet potatoes are tender and the chickpeas are crisp.
3. While the vegetables roast, place the saffron threads in a small bowl, cover with 2 tablespoons of hot vegetable broth, and let steep for 5 minutes.
4. Bring the remaining broth to a boil in a saucepan, then stir in the saffron infusion. Remove from heat, add the couscous, cover, and let sit for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
5. Transfer the couscous to a large bowl; fold in the roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas, toasted almonds, and chopped parsley.
6. Drizzle the lemon juice over the mixture, season with additional salt and pepper if needed, and toss gently to combine.
7. Serve warm or at room temperature as a hearty side or light main dish. Enjoy!
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Couscous

text:
Miso‑Glazed Eggplant with Coconut‑Lime Barley Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 2 medium eggplants, sliced into ½‑inch rounds
- 3 Tbsp white miso paste
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp sesame oil
- 1 cup pearl barley
- 2 cups coconut milk
- 1 cup water
- Zest of 1 lime
- Juice of 1 lime
- 1 Tbsp toasted coconut flakes
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 1 Tbsp olive oil (for roasting)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together miso paste, maple syrup, rice vinegar, grated ginger, and sesame oil to form the glaze.  
3. Brush both sides of the eggplant slices with olive oil, season lightly with salt, and place on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast the eggplant for 20‑25 minutes, flipping halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
5. While the eggplant roasts, rinse the barley under cold water. Combine barley, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cover and cook for 30‑35 minutes, or until the grains are tender and the liquid is absorbed.  
6. Remove the barley from heat; stir in lime zest, lime juice, toasted coconut flakes, and chopped cilantro. Adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed.  
7. When the eggplant is done, brush each slice generously with the remaining miso glaze and return to the oven for an additional 5 minutes to set the glaze.  
8. To serve, spoon a mound of coconut‑lime barley pilaf onto each plate, top with 2‑3 glazed eggplant rounds, and garnish with extra cilantro and a drizzle of lime juice if desired. Enjoy!
title: Miso‑Glazed Eggplant with Coconut‑Lime Barley Pilaf

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Quinoa Salad with Orange Vinaigrette

Ingredients:
- 2 medium beets, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 tbsp olive oil (plus extra for drizzling)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 large orange, segmented and juiced
- 1 tbsp orange zest
- 2 tbsp apple cider vinegar
- 1 tsp Dijon mustard
- 2 cups baby arugula
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the cubed beets with 1 tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway, until tender and caramelized.
2. While the beets roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside to cool slightly.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together orange juice, orange zest, apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, a pinch of salt, and 1 tbsp olive oil to create the vinaigrette.
4. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted beets, arugula, and orange segments. Drizzle with the orange vinaigrette and toss gently to coat evenly.
5. Transfer the salad to a serving platter or bowls. Sprinkle crumbled feta (if using) and toasted pumpkin seeds on top for added texture and flavor.
6. Serve warm or at room temperature, and enjoy the sweet‑spicy harmony of cinnamon‑maple beets with bright orange dressing.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Quinoa Salad with Orange Vinaigrette

text:
Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Chickpea Pizza

Ingredients:
- 1 large sweet potato, thinly sliced
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 pre‑made pizza crust (or flatbread)
- ½ cup shredded mozzarella cheese
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese
- 2 tbsp fresh arugula
- 1 tbsp balsamic glaze (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the sweet‑potato slices with ½ tbsp olive oil, ½ tsp smoked paprika, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 15‑20 minutes, turning once, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
3. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine the chickpeas, maple syrup, remaining ½ tbsp olive oil, cumin, and a pinch of salt in a separate bowl. Spread the chickpeas on the same baking sheet (or a second sheet) and roast for 12‑15 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until they are golden and slightly crisp.  
4. Remove both trays from the oven. Place the pizza crust on a clean baking sheet. Evenly distribute the roasted sweet‑potato slices over the crust, followed by the maple‑glazed chickpeas.  
5. Sprinkle the shredded mozzarella and crumbled feta evenly over the toppings. Return the pizza to the oven and bake for 8‑10 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and bubbly.  
6. Remove the pizza, let it rest for 2 minutes, then top with fresh arugula. Drizzle with balsamic glaze, if using, and serve immediately.
title: Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Chickpea Pizza

text:
Harissa‑Glazed Eggplant and Barley Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 1 cup pearl barley
- 2 tbsp harissa paste
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 small red onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- 1 cup water
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- Optional: toasted pine nuts for garnish

Instructions:
1. Rinse the barley under cold water, then combine it with the vegetable broth and water in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 30‑35 minutes, or until the grains are tender and the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and set aside.
2. While the barley cooks, place the cubed eggplant in a large bowl. Add the harissa paste, 1 tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat evenly; let it marinate for 5 minutes.
3. Heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 3‑4 minutes until translucent.
4. Add the minced garlic and red bell pepper to the skillet; cook for another 2 minutes, stirring frequently.
5. Add the harissa‑coated eggplant to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 8‑10 minutes, or until the eggplant is softened and lightly caramelized. Adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed.
6. Stir the cooked barley into the skillet with the vegetables, mixing thoroughly to combine. Cook for 2‑3 minutes to let the flavors meld.
7. Remove from heat; drizzle the lemon juice over the pilaf and sprinkle with chopped parsley. Toss gently.
8. Serve warm, garnished with toasted pine nuts if desired. Enjoy!
title: Harissa‑Glazed Eggplant and Barley Pilaf

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea & Sweet Potato Skillet

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 2 cups fresh spinach leaves
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the diced sweet potatoes and sauté for 6‑8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they begin to soften and develop a light golden crust.  
2. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger to the skillet; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
3. Sprinkle the turmeric and cumin over the vegetables, stirring to coat evenly. Cook for another minute to toast the spices.  
4. Stir in the chickpeas, coconut milk, and lime juice. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then reduce the heat to low. Cover and let it cook for 10‑12 minutes, or until the sweet potatoes are tender.  
5. Uncover the skillet, season with salt and pepper to taste, and fold in the fresh spinach. Cook for 2‑3 minutes, just until the spinach wilts.  
6. Remove from heat, garnish with chopped cilantro, and serve hot. This skillet pairs well with steamed rice, quinoa, or warm flatbread.
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea & Sweet Potato Skillet

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Pumpkin and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 2 cups pumpkin, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 cups kale, stems removed and torn
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice
- 1 Tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the pumpkin cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, 1 Tbsp maple syrup, cinnamon, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
3. In the same bowl, combine the chickpeas with the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, the other 1 Tbsp maple syrup, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Add them to the baking sheet, arranging around the pumpkin.  
4. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway through, until the pumpkin is tender and caramelized and the chickpeas are crisp.  
5. While the vegetables roast, bring the quinoa and water (or broth) to a boil in a saucepan. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.  
6. In a skillet over medium heat, add a splash of olive oil and sauté the minced garlic for 30 seconds. Add the kale and a pinch of salt; cook, stirring, until wilted, about 3‑4 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in the lemon juice.  
7. To assemble the bowl, place a bed of quinoa in each serving dish, top with roasted pumpkin, crispy chickpeas, and sautéed kale. Sprinkle with toasted pumpkin seeds if using.  
8. Serve warm, drizzling any remaining maple‑cinnamon glaze from the pan over the top for extra flavor. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Pumpkin and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

text:
Cinnamon‑Sage Roasted Acorn Squash and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 medium acorn squash, halved and seeded
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 tsp dried sage
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the squash halves with 1 tbsp olive oil, cinnamon, sage, salt, pepper, and maple syrup; place cut‑side down on a baking sheet and roast for 35‑40 minutes until tender and caramelized.  
2. Meanwhile, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
3. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, apple cider vinegar, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of maple syrup to make a dressing.  
4. Scoop the roasted squash flesh from the skin and mash lightly with a fork. Fold the mashed squash into the cooked quinoa, then drizzle with the dressing and toss to combine.  
5. Transfer the salad to a serving bowl, sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds on top, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Sage Roasted Acorn Squash and Quinoa Salad

text:
Miso‑Glazed Eggplant with Sesame‑Ginger Barley Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 2 medium eggplants, sliced into ½‑inch rounds
- 3 Tbsp white miso paste
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce
- 1 Tbsp sesame oil
- 1 tsp freshly grated ginger
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 cup pearl barley
- 2 ½ cups vegetable broth
- 1 carrot, diced
- ½ cup frozen peas, thawed
- 2 Tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- 1 Tbsp lime juice
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Olive oil for brushing

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a small bowl, whisk together miso paste, maple syrup, soy sauce, sesame oil, grated ginger, and minced garlic until smooth.
3. Brush both sides of the eggplant slices with a thin layer of olive oil, then spread the miso glaze evenly over the top side of each slice.
4. Arrange the glazed eggplant slices, glaze‑side up, on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, flipping halfway through, until the eggplant is tender and the glaze is caramelized.
5. While the eggplant roasts, rinse the barley under cold water. In a medium saucepan, combine barley and vegetable broth; bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 30‑35 minutes until the grains are tender and the liquid is absorbed.
6. In the last 5 minutes of cooking, stir in the diced carrot and peas; season with salt and pepper.
7. Remove the barley from heat and fluff with a fork. Stir in lime juice, toasted sesame seeds, and half of the chopped cilantro.
8. To serve, place a generous scoop of sesame‑ginger barley pilaf on each plate, top with a few miso‑glazed eggplant rounds, and garnish with the remaining cilantro and an extra drizzle of sesame oil if desired. Enjoy warm.
title: Miso‑Glazed Eggplant with Sesame‑Ginger Barley Pilaf

text:
Turmeric‑Honey Roasted Cauliflower with Lemon‑Garlic Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 2 Tbsp honey
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- Salt and pepper, to taste
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 lemon (zest and juice)
- 2 Tbsp fresh parsley, chopped

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl whisk together honey, turmeric, smoked paprika, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Toss the cauliflower florets in the mixture until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the cauliflower in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning once, until golden‑brown and tender.  
4. While the cauliflower roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes or until the broth is absorbed.  
5. Remove the quinoa from heat; stir in minced garlic, lemon zest, lemon juice, and a drizzle of olive oil. Fluff with a fork.  
6. To serve, place a bed of lemon‑garlic quinoa on each plate, top with the turmeric‑honey roasted cauliflower, and garnish with chopped parsley and an extra squeeze of lemon if desired.
title: Turmeric‑Honey Roasted Cauliflower with Lemon‑Garlic Quinoa

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Garlic Broccoli and Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 3 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp low‑sodium soy sauce
- 1 Tbsp rice‑vinegar
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 2 cloves garlic, minced (for glaze)
- 1 large head broccoli, cut into florets
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, thinly sliced (for roasting)
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional: 1 Tbsp toasted sesame seeds for garnish
- Optional: chopped fresh cilantro or parsley for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a medium bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, rice‑vinegar, smoked paprika, and 2 minced garlic cloves. Add the tofu cubes, toss to coat, and let marinate while you prepare the broccoli.  
3. Spread the broccoli florets on the prepared baking sheet. Drizzle with 1 Tbsp olive oil, sprinkle the sliced garlic, and season with salt and pepper. Toss to combine.  
4. Place the marinated tofu on the same sheet, arranging the pieces in a single layer separate from the broccoli.  
5. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning the tofu and broccoli halfway through, until the broccoli is crisp‑tender and the tofu is golden and caramelized.  
6. While the tofu and broccoli roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and stir in lemon juice, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of olive oil.  
7. Transfer the roasted broccoli and tofu to a serving bowl. Drizzle any pan juices over the tofu for extra glaze.  
8. Serve the maple‑glazed tofu and garlic‑roasted broccoli over the fluffy quinoa. Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and fresh herbs, if desired. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Garlic Broccoli and Quinoa

text:
Roasted Garlic & Herb Millet with Lemon‑Tahini Dressing

Ingredients:
- 1 cup millet
- 2 cups vegetable broth or water
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- 1 tsp dried rosemary
- 1/2 tsp sea salt, plus more to taste
- 1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 3 tbsp lemon juice
- 2 tbsp tahini
- 1 tbsp warm water (to thin dressing)
- 2 tbsp toasted pine nuts (optional)
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Rinse the millet under cold water until the water runs clear; drain well.  
2. In a medium saucepan, heat 1 tbsp olive oil over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.  
3. Add the rinsed millet, thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper to the saucepan. Stir to coat the grains with the garlic‑oil mixture.  
4. Pour in the vegetable broth (or water), bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15‑20 minutes, or until the millet is tender and the liquid is absorbed.  
5. Remove the saucepan from heat and let it sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff the millet with a fork and drizzle the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil over it; stir gently.  
6. While the millet rests, whisk together lemon juice, tahini, warm water, a pinch of salt, and black pepper in a small bowl until smooth and pourable. Adjust thickness with extra water if needed.  
7. Transfer the fluffed millet to a serving bowl. Drizzle the lemon‑tahini dressing over the top and toss lightly to combine.  
8. Garnish with toasted pine nuts and chopped fresh parsley. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Roasted Garlic & Herb Millet with Lemon‑Tahini Dressing

text:
Herb‑Crusted Halibut with Lemon‑Garlic Quinoa and Roasted Asparagus

Ingredients:
- halibut fillet (4 oz per serving)
- quinoa (1 cup)
- asparagus spears (1 bunch)
- olive oil (2 Tbsp)
- lemon zest (1 tsp)
- garlic cloves, minced (2)
title: Herb‑Crusted Halibut with Lemon‑Garlic Quinoa and Roasted Asparagus

text:
Roasted Garlic & Herb Farro with Lemon‑Tahini Kale

Ingredients:
- 1 cup farro, rinsed
- 2 ½ cups low‑sodium vegetable broth
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon dried thyme
- ½ teaspoon dried rosemary
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- 4 cups kale, stems removed and torn into bite‑size pieces
- 2 tablespoons tahini
- 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
- 1 teaspoon maple syrup
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 tablespoons toasted pumpkin seeds (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
2. Stir in the farro, dried thyme, rosemary, and smoked paprika, coating the grains with the aromatics for about 1 minute.
3. Pour in the vegetable broth, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the farro is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.
4. While the farro cooks, place the kale in a large bowl. In a small bowl, whisk together the tahini, lemon juice, maple syrup, a pinch of salt, and 2‑3 tablespoons of warm water until smooth and pourable. Toss the dressing into the kale, massaging the leaves until they soften, about 2 minutes.
5. Combine the cooked farro with the dressed kale, mixing gently to distribute the flavors. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste.
6. Transfer the mixture to serving bowls, sprinkle with toasted pumpkin seeds if desired, and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Roasted Garlic & Herb Farro with Lemon‑Tahini Kale

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Lentil Soup with Coconut Milk

Ingredients:
- 1 lb carrots, peeled and sliced
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp coconut oil
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp smoked paprika
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk (full‑fat)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Toasted pumpkin seeds, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the carrot slices with coconut oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, cumin, smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway, until caramelized and tender.  
2. While the carrots roast, heat a large pot over medium heat. Add a splash of coconut oil and sauté the onion until translucent, about 5 minutes; add the garlic and cook another minute.  
3. Add the rinsed red lentils and vegetable broth to the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes.  
4. Transfer the roasted carrots to the pot. Using an immersion blender (or a countertop blender in batches), blend the soup until smooth and creamy.  
5. Stir in the coconut milk and season with salt and pepper. Simmer gently for 5 minutes to meld flavors.  
6. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves and toasted pumpkin seeds, and serve hot.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Lentil Soup with Coconut Milk

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Chickpea and Quinoa Stuffed Bell Peppers

Ingredients:
- 4 large red bell peppers, tops cut off and seeds removed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- ¼ teaspoon saffron threads, soaked in 2 tbsp warm water
- ½ cup dried apricots, finely chopped
- ¼ cup toasted pine nuts
- 2 green onions, sliced thin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Lemon wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Place the prepared bell peppers upright in a baking dish.
2. In a saucepan, combine quinoa and vegetable broth; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
3. While the quinoa cooks, heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the chickpeas, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; sauté for 4‑5 minutes until lightly browned.
4. Stir the soaked saffron (including the liquid) into the chickpeas, then add the chopped apricots and toasted pine nuts. Cook for another 2 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.
5. In a large bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, saffron‑chickpea mixture, and sliced green onions. Adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.
6. Spoon the filling evenly into each bell pepper cavity, pressing gently to pack the mixture.
7. Cover the baking dish with foil and bake for 25 minutes. Remove the foil and bake an additional 10 minutes, or until the peppers are tender and the tops are lightly golden.
8. Remove from the oven, let cool for a couple of minutes, then garnish with fresh cilantro and serve with lemon wedges on the side. Enjoy!
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Chickpea and Quinoa Stuffed Bell Peppers

text:
Turmeric‑Honey Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch sticks
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp honey
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 2 cups baby spinach leaves
- ¼ cup toasted sliced almonds
- 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the carrot sticks and chickpeas with olive oil, honey, turmeric, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway through, until carrots are tender‑crisp and chickpeas are golden.  
4. While the vegetables roast, combine quinoa and water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
5. In a serving bowl, layer the cooked quinoa, roasted carrots and chickpeas, fresh spinach, and toasted almonds.  
6. Drizzle the lemon juice over the top, season with an extra pinch of salt if desired, and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Turmeric‑Honey Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Quinoa with Roasted Broccoli and Almonds

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon coconut oil
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 head broccoli, cut into florets
- 2 tablespoons sliced almonds, toasted
- 1 tablespoon lime juice
- 1 teaspoon lime zest
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss broccoli florets with a drizzle of coconut oil, salt, and pepper, then spread on a baking sheet and roast for 15‑20 minutes, until crisp‑tender and lightly browned.
2. While the broccoli roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed.
3. In a small skillet over medium heat, melt the remaining coconut oil. Add garlic, ginger, and turmeric; sauté for 1‑2 minutes until fragrant.
4. Fluff the cooked quinoa with a fork and stir in the turmeric‑ginger mixture, lime juice, and lime zest. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
5. Transfer the quinoa to a serving bowl, top with roasted broccoli, and sprinkle toasted almonds over the top.
6. Serve warm, optionally garnished with extra lime zest or a drizzle of coconut milk for added richness.
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Quinoa with Roasted Broccoli and Almonds

text:
Spiced Harissa Sweet Potato and Black Bean Skillet

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and diced 1‑½ in pieces
- 1 (15‑oz) can black beans, drained and rinsed
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1 small yellow onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2
title: Spiced Harissa Sweet Potato and Black Bean Skillet

text:
Turmeric‑Honey Roasted Carrot and Lentil Salad with Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch sticks
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1 tablespoon honey
- 1/2 teaspoon sea salt
- 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- 1 cup cooked green lentils (about 1/2 cup dry)
- 1/4 cup red onion, finely diced
- 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, chopped
- 1/3 cup pomegranate seeds
- 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
- Optional: 1/4 cup crumbled feta cheese

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together olive oil, turmeric, honey, salt, and pepper. Add the carrot sticks and toss to coat evenly.  
3. Spread the carrots in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until tender and
title: Turmeric‑Honey Roasted Carrot and Lentil Salad with Pomegranate

text:
Maple‑Glazed Roasted Brussels Sprouts with Pomegranate Quinoa Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 lb Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 Tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds
- 1 Tbsp chopped fresh mint
- Zest of 1 lemon

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the Brussels sprouts with maple syrup, olive oil, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the sprouts cut‑side down on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until caramelized and tender.  
4. While the sprouts roast, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed.  
5. Remove the quinoa from heat and fluff with a fork; stir in lemon zest, pomegranate seeds, toasted pumpkin seeds, and chopped mint.  
6. Taste the quinoa pilaf and adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed.  
7. Transfer the roasted Brussels sprouts to a serving platter, top with the pomegranate quinoa pilaf, and drizzle any pan‑drippings over the top.  
8. Serve warm, garnished with extra pomegranate seeds and a sprinkle of fresh mint if desired.
title: Maple‑Glazed Roasted Brussels Sprouts with Pomegranate Quinoa Pilaf

text:
Cinnamon‑Lime Roasted Cauliflower and Lentil Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 large head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 cup dried green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cauliflower florets with 1 tbsp olive oil, cinnamon, lime zest, lime juice, minced garlic, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the seasoned cauliflower in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway through, until golden‑brown and tender.  
4. While the cauliflower roasts, combine the rinsed lentils with 2 cups water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 20‑25 minutes, or until lentils are tender but still hold their shape. Drain any excess liquid.  
5. In a serving bowl, layer the cooked lentils as the base, then top with the roasted cauliflower. Drizzle any remaining pan juices over the bowl.  
6. Garnish with chopped cilantro, an extra squeeze of lime juice if desired, and serve warm. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Lime Roasted Cauliflower and Lentil Bowl

text:
Maple‑Glazed Chickpea and Kale Sheet Pan Dinner

Ingredients:
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 4 cups chopped kale, stems removed
- 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup
- 2 tablespoons extra‑virgin olive oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon sea salt
- ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
- 2 tablespoons toasted sliced almonds (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a medium bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, olive oil, minced garlic, smoked paprika, salt, pepper, and lemon juice.  
3. Add the chickpeas to the bowl and toss until they are evenly coated with the glaze. Spread the chickpeas in a single layer on half of the prepared baking sheet.  
4. On the other half of the sheet, spread the chopped kale in an even layer, leaving a little space between leaves. Drizzle any remaining glaze over the kale and toss gently to coat.  
5. Roast in the preheated oven for 12‑15 minutes, stirring the chickpeas once halfway through, until the chickpeas are golden‑brown and slightly crisp and the kale is wilted and edges are crisp.  
6. Remove from the oven and transfer the chickpeas and kale to a serving platter. Sprinkle toasted sliced almonds over the top, if using, for extra crunch.  
7. Serve immediately as a hearty main dish or a vibrant side, paired with quinoa, rice, or crusty bread.
title: Maple‑Glazed Chickpea and Kale Sheet Pan Dinner

text:
Spiced Cardamom Sweet Potato and Chickpea Tacos

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 ½ tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cardamom
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 8 small corn tortillas
- ½ cup red cabbage, thinly sliced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 2 tbsp lime juice
- 1 avocado, sliced
- 2 tbsp crumbled feta (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the diced sweet potatoes with 1 tbsp olive oil, cardamom, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the sweet potatoes on the prepared sheet and roast for 20 minutes, stirring halfway through.  
4. While the sweet potatoes roast, heat the remaining ½ tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the chickpeas and sauté for 5‑6 minutes until lightly browned; season with a pinch of salt and pepper.  
5. In a small bowl, combine the lime juice and chopped cilantro; set aside as a quick cilantro‑lime dressing.  
6. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet for 30 seconds per side or wrap in foil and heat in the oven for the last 5 minutes of roasting.  
7. Assemble each taco: place a spoonful of roasted sweet potatoes, a handful of sautéed chickpeas, a pinch of red cabbage, avocado slices, and a drizzle of cilantro‑lime dressing.  
8. Top with crumbled feta if using, serve immediately, and enjoy!
title: Spiced Cardamom Sweet Potato and Chickpea Tacos

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 1 tbsp saffron threads, steeped in 2 tbsp warm water
- 1 cup cooked quinoa
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp honey or maple syrup
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, toss the chickpeas with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Spread on a separate baking sheet and roast for 15‑18 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until crisp.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together the saffron‑infused water, lemon juice, and honey (or maple syrup) to create a bright dressing.
4. Assemble the bowl: start with a base of cooked quinoa, top with roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas, drizzle the saffron‑lemon dressing over everything, and sprinkle with toasted pumpkin seeds and chopped cilantro.
5. Serve warm or at room temperature, enjoying the fragrant saffron notes paired with sweet, smoky vegetables.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Buddha Bowl

text:
Maple‑Glazed Chickpea and Roasted Butternut Squash Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 medium butternut squash, peeled and cubed (about 3 cups)
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp olive oil (plus extra for roasting)
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 cups kale, stems removed and torn
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice
- 2 Tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds
- Optional: a pinch of red‑pepper flakes for heat

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cubed butternut squash with 1 Tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and half the smoked paprika. Spread in a single layer and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
3. While the squash roasts, combine the chickpeas, maple syrup, remaining smoked paprika, cumin, a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper in another bowl. Spread the chickpeas on the same baking sheet (or a second sheet) and roast for 15‑18 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until they are crisp and glossy.  
4. Meanwhile, bring the quinoa and water (or broth) to a boil in a saucepan. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 12‑15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
5. In a skillet over medium heat, add a splash of olive oil and sauté the kale with lemon juice, salt, and pepper for 3‑4 minutes, just until wilted but still bright green.  
6. To assemble the bowl, divide the cooked quinoa among serving bowls. Top with roasted butternut squash, maple‑glazed chickpeas, sautéed kale, and a sprinkle of toasted pumpkin seeds. Add red‑pepper flakes if desired for extra heat.  
7. Serve warm, drizzling any remaining pan juices over the top for extra flavor. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Chickpea and Roasted Butternut Squash Bowl

text:
Sesame‑Lime Glazed Tempeh with Coconut‑Basil Rice

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 2 Tbsp sesame oil
- 3 Tbsp fresh lime juice
- 2 Tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 cup jasmine rice
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- ¼ cup water
- ¼ tsp salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- ¼ cup fresh basil leaves, torn
- 1 Tbsp toasted sesame seeds (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Rinse the jasmine rice under cold water until the water runs clear. Combine rice, coconut milk, water, and salt in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 12‑15 minutes until tender. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and stir in torn basil leaves.
2. While the rice cooks, prepare the glaze: in a small bowl whisk together lime juice, soy sauce, maple syrup, minced garlic, and grated ginger.
3. Heat sesame oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the tempeh cubes and sauté 4‑5 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown on all sides.
4. Pour the glaze over the tempeh, stirring to coat. Continue cooking 2‑3 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken and cling to the tempeh.
5. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired.
6. Serve the glazed tempeh over the coconut‑basil rice. Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds on top for extra crunch, if using. Enjoy!
title: Sesame‑Lime Glazed Tempeh with Coconut‑Basil Rice

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Lentil Soup with Sage

Ingredients:
- 3 medium beets, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 large carrot, diced
- 2 celery stalks, diced
- 1 onion, chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ¼ tsp ground nutmeg
- 2 tsp fresh sage leaves, finely chopped (plus extra for garnish)
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional garnish: a drizzle of crème fraîche or toasted walnut halves

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the beet cubes with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, a pinch of salt, and half the maple syrup on a baking sheet; roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring once, until tender and caramelized.
2. While the beets roast, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, and celery; sauté 5‑7 minutes until softened.
3. Stir in the garlic, cinnamon, nutmeg, and chopped sage; cook 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Add the rinsed red lentils, roasted beets (with any pan juices), vegetable broth, and the remaining maple syrup. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer.
5. Cook, uncovered, for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and the soup has thickened. Stir occasionally.
6. Season with salt, pepper, and lemon juice. Adjust sweetness or acidity by adding a little more maple syrup or lemon juice, if desired.
7. Using an immersion blender, puree the soup until smooth, leaving a few beet pieces for texture if you like. Alternatively, blend in batches in a countertop blender, then return to the pot.
8. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with a drizzle of crème fraîche (or a spoonful of plain yogurt), toasted walnut halves, and a sprinkle of fresh sage leaves. Serve hot.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Lentil Soup with Sage

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Barley Pilaf with Roasted Cauliflower

Ingredients:
- 1 cup pearl barley, rinsed
- 1 medium cauliflower head, cut into florets
- 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 lemon (zest and juice)
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, minced
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 3 cups vegetable broth
- ½ tsp salt (or to taste)
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss cauliflower florets with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender.  
2. While the cauliflower roasts, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the minced garlic, ginger, and turmeric; sauté for 1‑2 minutes until fragrant.  
3. Stir in the rinsed barley, coating it with the aromatics, and toast for 2‑3 minutes.  
4. Add the vegetable broth, lemon zest, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30‑35 minutes, or until the barley is tender and the liquid is absorbed.  
5. Remove the barley from heat; stir in the lemon juice and adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed.  
6. Transfer the pilaf to a serving bowl, top with the roasted cauliflower, and sprinkle chopped parsley over the top. Serve warm.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Barley Pilaf with Roasted Cauliflower

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa & Roasted Sweet Pepper Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups water
- ½ cup coconut milk
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tsp lime zest
- 1 tbsp coconut oil, melted
- 2 large red bell peppers, sliced into strips
- 1 large yellow bell pepper, sliced into strips
- ½ red onion, thinly sliced
- 1 small jalapeño, seeded and minced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the bell pepper strips, red onion, and jalapeño with 1 tablespoon of the melted coconut oil, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 15‑20 minutes, stirring halfway, until tender and slightly charred. Remove and let cool.
2. While the vegetables roast, combine quinoa and water in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 12‑15 minutes, or until water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes.
3. Fluff the cooked quinoa with a fork and stir in the coconut milk, lime juice, lime zest, and a pinch of salt. Adjust seasoning with additional salt or lime juice if desired.
4. Transfer the quinoa to a large mixing bowl. Add the roasted peppers and onion, chopped cilantro, and toasted pumpkin seeds. Toss gently to combine, ensuring the vegetables are evenly distributed.
5. Taste and adjust seasoning with more salt, pepper, or lime juice as needed. Serve the salad warm, at room temperature, or chilled, as a vibrant side dish or light main course. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa & Roasted Sweet Pepper Salad

text:
Spiced Orange‑Maple Roasted Acorn Squash and Lentil Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 medium acorn squash, halved and seeded
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- Salt and black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 small onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- 1 tablespoon maple syrup
- 1 tablespoon orange zest
- 2 tablespoons fresh orange juice
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds (optional garnish)
- Fresh parsley, chopped (optional garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Place the acorn squash halves cut‑side up on a baking sheet, brush with olive oil, and season with salt and pepper. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, until the flesh is tender and lightly caramelized.
2. While the squash roasts, heat a saucepan over medium heat, add a drizzle of olive oil, and sauté the diced onion until translucent, about 5 minutes.
3. Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more, then stir in the cumin and cinnamon, cooking until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
4. Add the rinsed lentils and vegetable broth to the saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender but still hold their shape. Add more broth if needed.
5. In a small bowl, whisk together the maple
title: Spiced Orange‑Maple Roasted Acorn Squash and Lentil Pilaf

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Lentil Tacos with Avocado Crema

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 cup dried green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 8 small corn tortillas
- 1 ripe avocado
- 2 tbsp plain Greek yogurt or vegan yogurt
- 1 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- Optional toppings: diced red onion, sliced jalapeño, crumbled feta or vegan cheese

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the diced sweet potatoes with olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper until evenly coated. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning once, until tender and caramelized.  
3. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine the rinsed lentils with 2 cups water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until lentils are tender but not mushy. Drain any excess water and set aside.  
4. Prepare the avocado crema: in a small bowl, mash the avocado with Greek yogurt, lime juice, a pinch of salt, and half of the chopped cilantro until smooth. Adjust seasoning to taste and set aside.  
5. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 30 seconds per side, or wrap them in foil and heat in the oven for the last 5 minutes of the sweet potatoes’ roasting time.  
6. Assemble each taco: place a spoonful of roasted sweet potatoes and a spoonful of cooked lentils onto a tortilla, drizzle with avocado crema, and sprinkle with the remaining cilantro. Add optional toppings such as red onion, jalapeño, or feta if desired.  
7. Serve immediately, enjoying the sweet‑spicy contrast of the cinnamon‑maple sweet potatoes, earthy lentils, and cool avocado crema.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Lentil Tacos with Avocado Crema

text:
Saffron‑Infused Wild Rice and Roasted Brussels Sprouts with Lemon Vinaigrette

Ingredients:
- 1 cup wild rice, rinsed
- 2 ½ cups vegetable broth
- 1 ½ teaspoons saffron threads
- 1 lb (450 g) Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup toasted sliced almonds
- 2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 Tbsp lemon zest
- 1 Tbsp honey or maple syrup
- ¼ cup extra‑virgin olive oil (for vinaigrette)
- 1 small garlic clove, minced
- Fresh parsley, chopped (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, toss the halved Brussels sprouts with 2 Tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread them cut‑side down on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until caramelized and tender.  
3. While the sprouts roast, place the saffron threads in a shallow cup and cover with 2 Tbsp hot water; let steep for 5 minutes.  
4. In a medium saucepan, combine the rinsed wild rice, vegetable broth, and the saffron infusion (including the threads). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 45‑50 minutes, or until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.  
5. Prepare the lemon vinaigrette: whisk together lemon juice, lemon zest, honey (or maple syrup), minced garlic, and ¼ cup extra‑virgin olive oil. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.  
6. Transfer the cooked wild rice to a large mixing bowl. Add the roasted Brussels sprouts, toasted almonds, and drizzle with the lemon vinaigrette. Toss gently to combine, adjusting seasoning if needed.  
7. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with chopped fresh parsley if desired. Enjoy as a hearty side or a light main dish.
title: Saffron‑Infused Wild Rice and Roasted Brussels Sprouts with Lemon Vinaigrette

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Farro with Roasted Broccoli and Almonds

Ingredients:
- 1 cup farro
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 head broccoli, cut into florets
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp turmeric powder
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 lemon, zest and juice
- 1/4 cup sliced almonds, toasted
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss broccoli florets with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast 15‑20 minutes until crisp‑tender and slightly charred.
2. While broccoli roasts, rinse farro under cold water. In a medium saucepan combine farro and vegetable broth; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 20‑25 minutes until
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Farro with Roasted Broccoli and Almonds

text:
Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Chickpea Breakfast Hash

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 4 large eggs
- 2 green onions, thinly sliced
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the diced sweet potatoes with olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper until evenly coated. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20 minutes.  
3. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine the chickpeas and maple syrup in a separate bowl; season lightly with salt and pepper.  
4. After the sweet potatoes have roasted, remove the sheet, stir the chickpeas into the sweet potatoes, and return to the oven for another 10 minutes, or until the sweet potatoes are tender and the chickpeas are lightly caramelized.  
5. Meanwhile, heat a non‑stick skillet over medium heat. Crack the eggs into the skillet and cook to your preferred doneness (sunny‑side‑up or over‑easy work well).  
6. Divide the sweet potato‑chickpea mixture among four plates, top each serving with a cooked egg, and sprinkle with sliced green onions and cilantro, if using. Serve immediately.
title: Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Chickpea Breakfast Hash

text:
Lemon‑Thyme Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Artichokes and Sun‑Dried Tomatoes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 cup marinated artichoke hearts, drained and halved
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 cup sun‑dried tomatoes, sliced
- 1 teaspoon fresh thyme leaves (or ½ tsp dried thyme)
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 tablespoons toasted pine nuts (optional, for garnish)
- Fresh parsley, chopped (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the artichoke halves with ½ tablespoon olive oil, half the minced garlic, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet and roast for 15‑18 minutes, until golden and fragrant.  
2. While the artichokes roast, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes.  
3. In a small skillet, heat the remaining ½ tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add the remaining garlic and sauté for 30 seconds until aromatic. Add the sun‑dried tomatoes and thyme; cook 2‑3 minutes, stirring occasionally.  
4. Fluff the cooked quinoa with a fork and transfer to a large mixing bowl. Stir in the sautéed garlic‑tomato mixture, roasted artichokes, lemon zest, and lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper to taste.  
5. Divide the quinoa among serving bowls. Top each bowl with toasted pine nuts and a sprinkle of fresh parsley, if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Thyme Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Artichokes and Sun‑Dried Tomatoes

text:
Saffron‑Infused Lentil and Roasted Tomato Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 can (14 oz) fire‑roasted diced tomatoes
- 1 large onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon saffron threads
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, combine the saffron threads with 2 tablespoons of hot water; let steep for 5 minutes.  
2. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes.  
3. Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another 30 seconds until fragrant.  
4. Add the cumin and smoked paprika; toast the spices for 1 minute, stirring constantly.  
5. Pour in the fire‑roasted tomatoes (with their juices) and the saffron infusion; stir to combine.  
6. Add the rinsed red lentils and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to a gentle simmer.  
7. Cover and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and the stew has thickened. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.  
8. Season with salt and pepper to taste. If the stew is too thick, add a splash more broth or water.  
9. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with chopped fresh cilantro, and serve hot with crusty bread or steamed rice.
title: Saffron‑Infused Lentil and Roasted Tomato Stew

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 large head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- ½ teaspoon saffron threads
- 2 tablespoons hot water
- 3 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 tablespoon lemon juice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup fresh parsley, chopped

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, combine the saffron threads with hot water; let steep for 5 minutes.  
3. In a large mixing bowl, toss the cauliflower florets and chickpeas with olive oil, minced garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.  
4. Drizzle the saffron infusion over the vegetables and chickpeas, tossing again to coat evenly.  
5. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway through, until the cauliflower is golden‑brown and tender.  
6. Remove from the oven and let cool slightly. Transfer to a serving bowl, add lemon juice, and sprinkle with fresh parsley.  
7. Toss gently to combine and serve warm or at room temperature as a hearty salad or side dish.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Salad

text:
Turmeric‑Honey Glazed Carrot and Chickpea Salad

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and sliced into thin ribbons
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp honey
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. In a large bowl, whisk together honey, turmeric, olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper to form a glaze.
2. Add the carrot ribbons to the bowl and toss until evenly coated with the glaze.
3. Spread the glazed carrots on a baking sheet in a single layer and roast in a preheated oven at 400°F (200°C) for 15‑20 minutes, or until tender and lightly caramelized, stirring halfway through.
4. While the carrots roast, place the chickpeas in a separate bowl and drizzle with a little of the remaining glaze; toss to coat.
5. Once the carrots are done, transfer them to a serving platter, add the glazed chickpeas, and sprinkle with chopped parsley.
6. Serve warm or at room temperature as a vibrant side dish or light main course.
title: Turmeric‑Honey Glazed Carrot and Chickpea Salad

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Quinoa‑Stuffed Acorn Squash

Ingredients:
- 2 medium acorn squash, halved and seeded
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice
- 1 cup canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 cups fresh spinach, roughly chopped
- ½ teaspoon sea salt
- ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- 2 tablespoons toasted pumpkin seeds (optional, for garnish)
- Fresh cilantro leaves, torn (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Place the acorn squash halves cut‑side up on a baking sheet, brush lightly with olive oil, and season with a pinch of salt and pepper. Roast for 35‑40 minutes, or until the flesh is tender and easily pierced with a fork.  
2. While the squash roasts, combine the quinoa and coconut milk in a medium saucepan. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.  
3. In a large skillet over medium heat, add a drizzle of olive oil and sauté the minced garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant. Stir in the turmeric, lime zest, and lime juice, cooking for another minute.  
4. Add the cooked quinoa, chickpeas, and chopped spinach to the skillet. Toss everything together and cook for 3‑4 minutes, until the spinach wilts. Season with salt and pepper to taste.  
5. Remove the roasted acorn squash from the oven. Using a spoon, gently fluff the interior of each half, then fill each cavity with the coconut‑lime quinoa mixture, packing it lightly.  
6. Return the stuffed squash to the oven and bake for an additional 10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.  
7. Remove from the oven, drizzle any remaining pan juices over the tops, and garnish with toasted pumpkin seeds and fresh cilantro, if desired. Serve warm.
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Quinoa‑Stuffed Acorn Squash

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea & Spinach Stew with Brown Rice  

Ingredients:
- 1 cup brown rice
- 1 ½ cups water
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 large onion, diced
- 3 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1 teaspoon
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea & Spinach Stew with Brown Rice

text:
Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Chickpea Breakfast Burrito  

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 4 large flour tortillas
- 1 ripe avocado, sliced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Juice of 1 lime
- Hot sauce (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the diced sweet potatoes with ½ Tbsp olive oil, ½ tsp cumin, ½ tsp smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
3. While the sweet potatoes roast, heat the remaining ½ Tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the chickpeas, the remaining cumin and smoked paprika, and sauté for 5‑6 minutes until the chickpeas are golden. Drizzle the maple syrup over the chickpeas, stir to coat, and cook an additional 2 minutes. Remove from heat.  
4. In a small bowl, combine the lime juice with a pinch of salt; set aside for the avocado garnish.  
5. Once the sweet potatoes are done, transfer them to the skillet with the maple‑glazed chickpeas. Gently toss to combine and warm through, about 2 minutes.  
6. Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet or microwave for 20 seconds until pliable.  
7. To assemble each burrito, place a generous scoop of the sweet potato‑chickpea mixture in the center of a tortilla. Top with avocado slices, a sprinkle of chopped cilantro, a drizzle of the lime‑juice mixture, and hot sauce if desired.  
8. Fold the sides of the tortilla over the filling, then roll tightly from the bottom up.  
9. Serve immediately, or wrap in foil and keep warm for up to 30 minutes. Enjoy your maple‑glazed sweet potato and chickpea breakfast burrito!
title: Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Chickpea Breakfast Burrito

text:
Roasted Garlic & Herb Chickpea and Sweet Potato Sheet Pan Dinner

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp dried rosemary
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- Optional garnish: chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, combine the sweet potato cubes, chickpeas, minced garlic, olive oil, rosemary, thyme, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Toss until everything is evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet, ensuring the sweet potatoes are not overcrowded.  
4. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the sweet potatoes are tender and lightly caramelized and the chickpeas are crisp.  
5. Remove from the oven and immediately drizzle with fresh lemon juice; toss gently to coat.  
6. Transfer to a serving platter, garnish with chopped parsley if desired, and serve hot.
title: Roasted Garlic & Herb Chickpea and Sweet Potato Sheet Pan Dinner

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Tostada with Avocado Crema

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp salt
- 4 corn tortillas
- 1 ripe avocado
- 1 Tbsp lime juice
- 2 Tbsp Greek yogurt or plant‑based yogurt
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the diced sweet potatoes with 1 Tbsp maple syrup, cinnamon, smoked paprika, and salt; spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
3. Roast the sweet potatoes for 20 minutes, then add the chickpeas tossed with the remaining 1 Tbsp maple syrup and a pinch of salt; continue roasting for another 15 minutes, or until the potatoes are tender and the chickpeas are crisp.  
4. While the vegetables roast, warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 30 seconds per side, then keep them wrapped in a clean kitchen towel to stay soft.  
5. Prepare the avocado crema by blending the avocado, lime juice, and yogurt until smooth; season with a pinch of salt.
