6. To assemble, spread a generous spoonful of the roasted sweet potato and chickpea mixture onto each tortilla, drizzle with avocado crema, and sprinkle with chopped cilantro. Serve immediately.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Tostada with Avocado Crema

text:
Lemon‑Basil Orzo with Grilled Eggplant and Pine Nuts

Ingredients:
- 1 cup orzo pasta
- 1 large eggplant, sliced into ½‑inch rounds
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- ¼ cup fresh basil leaves, chopped
- ¼ cup pine nuts, toasted
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional: grated Parmesan cheese for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat a grill or grill pan over medium‑high heat. Brush the eggplant slices with 1 Tbsp olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Grill 3‑4 minutes per side, until tender and lightly charred. Remove and set aside.
2. Meanwhile, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the orzo and cook according to package directions, about 8‑10 minutes, until al dente. Drain, reserving ¼ cup of the cooking liquid.
3. In a small skillet, heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and toast for 30 seconds until fragrant. Stir in the lemon zest, lemon juice, and the reserved cooking liquid; simmer for 1‑2 minutes.
4. Transfer the cooked orzo to a large bowl. Pour the lemon‑garlic sauce over the pasta and toss to combine. Fold in the chopped basil and season with additional salt and pepper to taste.
5. Arrange the grilled eggplant slices on top of the orzo. Sprinkle the toasted pine nuts over the dish and, if desired, finish with a drizzle of extra‑virgin olive oil and a sprinkle of grated Parmesan.
6. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with a few extra basil leaves. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Basil Orzo with Grilled Eggplant and Pine Nuts

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Beet and Quinoa Salad with Citrus Vinaigrette

Ingredients:
- 2 medium beets, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 ½ teaspoons saffron threads
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 orange, segmented
- 1 ½ tablespoons fresh lemon juice
- 1 ½ teaspoons honey or agave
- ¼ cup chopped fresh mint
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the beet cubes with 1 tablespoon olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, until tender and caramelized.
2. While the beets roast, combine the saffron threads with 2 tablespoons hot water; let steep for 5 minutes.
3. In a medium saucepan, bring the quinoa and broth (or water) to a boil. Add the saffron infusion, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside to cool slightly.
4. Prepare the citrus vinaigrette: whisk together lemon juice, honey, the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
5. In a large mixing bowl, combine the roasted beets, saffron‑infused quinoa, orange segments, and chopped mint. Drizzle the vinaigrette over the salad and toss gently to coat evenly.
6. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Sprinkle crumbled feta on top, if using, and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Beet and Quinoa Salad with Citrus Vinaigrette

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Power Bowl with Avocado Lime Dressing

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 cups cooked quinoa
- 1 ripe avocado
- Juice of 1 lime
- 1 Tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 Tbsp water (optional, for dressing consistency)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp cinnamon, ½ tsp smoked paprika, a pinch of salt, and half of the maple syrup. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20 minutes.  
3. While the sweet potatoes roast, toss the chickpeas with the remaining olive oil, the other 1 Tbsp maple syrup, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Add them to the baking sheet and roast for an additional 15 minutes, stirring halfway, until the chickpeas are crisp and the sweet potatoes are tender and caramelized.  
4. While the vegetables finish cooking, prepare the avocado lime dressing: combine the avocado flesh, lime juice, minced garlic, chopped cilantro, and a splash of water in a blender or food processor. Blend until smooth, adding more water if needed to reach a drizzle‑able consistency. Season with salt and pepper to taste.  
5. Divide the cooked quinoa among four bowls. Top each with a generous portion of the roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas. Drizzle the avocado lime dressing over the bowls and garnish with extra cilantro leaves if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Power Bowl with Avocado Lime Dressing

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Lentil and Kale Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes (optional)
- 2 carrots, sliced into thin rounds
- 1 celery stalk, diced
- 1 cup chopped kale, stems removed
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Juice of 1/2 lemon
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish (optional)

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4‑5 minutes.
2. Stir in the minced garlic, grated ginger, turmeric, cumin, and red pepper flakes; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add the sliced carrots and diced celery, stirring to coat them with the spices. Cook for another 2 minutes.
4. Pour in the rinsed lentils and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to a gentle simmer.
5. Cover and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender but still hold their shape.
6. Stir in the chopped kale and continue to simmer for 5‑7 minutes, until the kale wilts and becomes tender.
7. Season the stew with salt, pepper, and the fresh lemon juice. Adjust seasoning to taste.
8. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with cilantro leaves if desired, and serve hot. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Lentil and Kale Stew

text:
Saffron‑Infused Coconut Chickpea and Quinoa Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup water
- 1 ½ teaspoons saffron threads
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 small onion, finely diced
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 cup canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- ½ cup frozen peas
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Toasted slivered almonds, for garnish

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, combine the saffron threads with 2 tablespoons of hot water; let steep for 5 minutes.
2. In a medium saucepan, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 3 minutes; stir in the garlic and cumin and cook for another 30 seconds.
3. Add the quinoa, coconut milk, water, and the saffron infusion (including the threads) to the saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed.
4. While the quinoa cooks, heat a non‑stick skillet over medium heat. Add the chickpeas and peas, season with salt and pepper, and sauté for 4‑5 minutes until lightly browned.
5. Fluff the cooked quinoa with a fork and gently fold in the sautéed chickpeas and peas. Adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.
6. Transfer the pilaf to serving bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro and toasted slivered almonds, and serve warm.
title: Saffron‑Infused Coconut Chickpea and Quinoa Pilaf

text:
Sage‑Infused Wild Rice with Roasted Butternut Squash and Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 1 cup wild rice, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 teaspoons fresh sage, finely chopped
- 1 medium butternut squash, peeled and cubed
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1/2 teaspoon sea salt
- 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- 1/3 cup pomegranate seeds
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 1 tablespoon maple syrup
- 1 tablespoon balsamic vinegar
- 1 small red onion, thinly sliced
- 1 clove garlic, minced

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the cubed butternut squash with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, pepper, and maple syrup; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning once, until caramelized and tender.
2. While the squash roasts, combine the wild rice and vegetable broth in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 45‑50 minutes, or until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
3. In a small skillet, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add the sliced red onion and minced garlic; sauté for 3‑4 minutes until softened and fragrant. Remove from heat.
4. Once the rice is cooked, stir in the chopped sage, allowing the heat to release its aroma.
5. Transfer the cooked wild rice to a large serving bowl. Gently fold in the roasted butternut squash, sautéed onions, pomegranate seeds, and toasted pumpkin seeds.
6. Drizzle the balsamic vinegar over the top, give a final gentle toss, and
title: Sage‑Infused Wild Rice with Roasted Butternut Squash and Pomegranate

text:
Sesame‑Ginger Coconut Noodle Bowl with Roasted Tofu

Ingredients:
- 8 oz rice noodles
- 1 block firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 tbsp sesame oil
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 1 cup shredded red cabbage
- 1 cup julienned carrots
- ½ cup sliced cucumber
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- 2 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the tofu cubes with 1 tbsp sesame oil, soy sauce, maple syrup, ginger, and garlic; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.
2. Meanwhile, cook the rice noodles according to package directions, drain, and rinse with cold water; set aside.
3. In a small saucepan, combine coconut milk, rice vinegar, lime juice, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of sesame oil; heat gently until just simmering, then remove from heat.
4. In a large bowl, toss the cooked noodles with the coconut‑ginger sauce until evenly coated.
5. Divide the noodles among four bowls; top each with equal portions of roasted tofu, red cabbage, carrots, cucumber, and cilantro.
6. Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds over each bowl and finish with a splash of extra soy sauce or lime juice if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Sesame‑Ginger Coconut Noodle Bowl with Roasted Tofu

text:
Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Grain Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup quinoa
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 Tbsp fresh thyme leaves
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss cauliflower florets and chickpeas with olive oil, smoked paprika, thyme, salt, and pepper; spread in a single layer on the sheet.  
3. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until cauliflower is golden and chickpeas are crisp.  
4. Meanwhile, rinse quinoa under cold water, then combine with 2 cups water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until water is absorbed; fluff with a fork.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together lemon zest, lemon juice, a drizzle of olive oil, and a pinch of salt.  
6. Assemble bowls by dividing quinoa, then topping with roasted cauliflower, chickpeas, toasted pumpkin seeds, and parsley; drizzle with lemon‑thyme dressing and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Grain Bowl

text:
Saffron‑Infused Coconut Shrimp with Lime Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined  
- 1 cup coconut milk  
- ½ tsp saffron threads  
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice  
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed  
- 2 cups water  
- 2 cloves garlic, minced  
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated  
- 2 tbsp olive oil  
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste  
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. In a small saucepan, combine the coconut milk, saffron threads, and a pinch of salt. Heat over low heat until just simmering, then remove from heat and let steep for 5 minutes.  
2. While the saffron infuses, bring the quinoa and water to a boil in a medium pot. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the quinoa is fluffy and the water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and stir in the lime juice; set aside.  
3. Pat the shrimp dry and season with salt and pepper.  
4. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger, sautéing for 30 seconds until fragrant.  
5. Add the shrimp to the skillet in a single layer. Cook for 2 minutes per side, or until the shrimp turn pink and opaque.  
6. Pour the saffron‑coconut mixture over the shrimp, stirring to coat. Cook for an additional 2 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken slightly.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with more salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired.  
8. Serve the saffron‑infused coconut shrimp over a bed of lime‑quinoa, garnished with chopped cilantro. Enjoy while hot!
title: Saffron‑Infused Coconut Shrimp with Lime Quinoa

text:
Citrus‑Basil Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Grilled Zucchini

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 zucchini, sliced lengthwise
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- Zest of 1 lemon
- Juice of 1 lemon
- 2 tablespoons fresh basil, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the chickpeas with ½ tablespoon olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking halfway, until crisp.
2. Meanwhile, combine quinoa and water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
3. Heat the remaining ½ tablespoon olive oil in a grill pan over medium‑high heat. Grill the zucchini slices 2‑3 minutes per side until tender and lightly charred; season with salt and pepper.
4. In a large bowl, whisk together lemon zest, lemon juice, chopped basil, and a pinch of salt. Add the cooked quinoa, roasted chickpeas, and grilled zucchini; toss gently to combine.
5. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if needed. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with extra basil leaves.
title: Citrus‑Basil Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Grilled Zucchini

text:
Spiced Orange‑Maple Tofu with Roasted Cauliflower and Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 1 large head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 tablespoons maple syrup
- 1 teaspoon orange zest
- 1 tablespoon orange juice
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- ¼ teaspoon ground cinnamon
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 green onions, sliced (for garnish)
- 1 tablespoon toasted sesame seeds (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a large bowl, whisk together maple syrup, orange zest, orange juice, smoked paprika, cumin, cinnamon, 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper. Add the tofu cubes, toss to coat, and set aside.
3. Toss the cauliflower florets with the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.
4. Roast the cauliflower for 20 minutes, turning halfway through, until golden‑brown and tender.
5. While the cauliflower roasts, heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the coated tofu and sear for 3‑4 minutes per side, until caramelized and crisp. Remove from heat.
6. Meanwhile, bring 2 cups water to a boil, add the quinoa, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes or until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
7. In a serving bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted cauliflower, and seared tofu. Drizzle any remaining pan juices over the top.
8. Garnish with sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds, if using. Serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Orange‑Maple Tofu with Roasted Cauliflower and Quinoa

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Garlic Broccoli and Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 3 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp low‑sodium soy sauce
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 Tbsp olive oil (for tempeh)
- 1 lb broccoli florets
- 1 Tbsp olive oil (for broccoli)
- 1 ½ cups quinoa, rinsed
- 3 cups vegetable broth
- ½ tsp salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice
- Optional garnish: sliced green onions or toasted sesame seeds

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, whisk together maple syrup, soy sauce, and minced garlic. Add the tempeh cubes, toss to coat, and let marinate while you prepare the rest (about 10 minutes).
2. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Spread the broccoli florets on a baking sheet, drizzle with 1 Tbsp olive oil, sprinkle with a pinch of salt and pepper, and toss to coat.
3. Roast the broccoli for 15‑18 minutes, stirring halfway, until tender‑crisp and lightly browned.
4. While the broccoli roasts, heat 1 Tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated tempeh (including any excess sauce) and sauté for 6‑8 minutes, turning occasionally, until the tempeh is golden and the glaze thickens.
5. Meanwhile, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the quinoa is fluffy and the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes.
6. Fluff the quinoa with a fork, stir in lemon juice, and season with additional salt and pepper to taste.
7. To serve, divide the quinoa among bowls, top with roasted garlic broccoli and maple‑glazed tempeh. Garnish with sliced green onions or toasted sesame seeds if desired. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Garlic Broccoli and Quinoa

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Farro with Roasted Brussels Sprouts and Pomegranate  

Ingredients:
- 1 cup farro, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 ½ cups Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, grated
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- ½ teaspoon sea salt
- ¼ teaspoon black pepper
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 tablespoons toasted almond slivers
- 1 tablespoon lemon juice
- 1 teaspoon lemon zest

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the Brussels sprouts with olive oil, turmeric, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway, until caramelized and crisp‑tender.  
2. While the sprouts roast, combine the farro and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 20‑25 minutes until the grains are tender and the liquid is absorbed.  
3. In a small skillet over medium heat, add a drizzle of olive oil and sauté the garlic and grated ginger for 1‑2 minutes until fragrant.  
4. Fluff the cooked farro with a fork and stir in the garlic‑ginger mixture, lemon juice, and lemon zest; season with additional salt and pepper to taste.  
5. Transfer the farro to a serving bowl, top with the roasted Brussels sprouts, sprinkle pomegranate seeds and toasted almond slivers over the top.  
6. Serve warm or at room temperature, enjoying the bright citrus notes against the earthy turmeric and sweet‑tart pomegranate.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Farro with Roasted Brussels Sprouts and Pomegranate

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea & Spinach Stew with Brown Rice

Ingredients:
- 1 cup brown rice
- 2 cups water (for rice)
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 large onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 can (14 oz) coconut milk
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 4 cups fresh spinach, roughly chopped
- Juice of 1 lime
- Zest of 1 lime
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Optional: red‑pepper flakes for heat

Instructions:
1. Rinse the brown rice under cold water. In a medium saucepan combine rice and 2 cups water; bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 35‑40 minutes until tender. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
2. While the rice cooks, heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté 4‑5 minutes until translucent.  
3. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook 1‑2 minutes until fragrant.  
4. Sprinkle turmeric, cumin, and smoked paprika over the aromatics; stir constantly for 30 seconds to toast the spices.  
5. Add the chickpeas, coconut milk, and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce to a simmer.  
6. Let the stew simmer uncovered for 15‑20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens slightly.  
7. Fold in the chopped spinach and simmer 2‑3 minutes until wilted.  
8. Remove the pot from heat; stir in lime juice, lime zest, and season with salt, pepper, and optional red‑pepper flakes to taste.  
9. Spoon a generous portion of brown rice into each serving bowl, ladle the chickpea‑spinach stew over the rice, and garnish with fresh cilantro leaves. Enjoy warm!
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea & Spinach Stew with Brown Rice

text:
Maple‑Glazed Chickpea and Roasted Corn Salad with Lime Vinaigrette

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 ears fresh corn, kernels removed
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- Juice of 1 lime
- 2 Tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil (for dressing)
- 1 tsp honey
- ¼ tsp lime zest

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the chickpeas and corn kernels with 1 Tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the chickpeas are crisp and the corn is lightly charred.  
4. While the chickpeas and corn roast, whisk together lime juice, lime zest, honey, and 2 Tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil in a small jar; season with a pinch of salt and pepper to create the vinaigrette.  
5. Transfer the roasted chickpeas and corn to a large mixing bowl, add the chopped cilantro, and drizzle with the lime vinaigrette. Toss gently to combine.  
6. Taste and adjust seasoning, adding more salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired.  
7. Serve the salad warm or at room temperature, garnished with an extra sprinkle of cilantro or a drizzle of maple syrup if you like a touch more sweetness.
title: Maple‑Glazed Chickpea and Roasted Corn Salad with Lime Vinaigrette

text:
Citrus‑Infused Quinoa with Charred Brussels Sprouts and Toasted Hazelnuts

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- zest of 1 orange
- juice of 1 orange
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 pound Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 1/3 cup toasted hazelnuts, roughly chopped
- 1/4 cup dried cranberries
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1/2 teaspoon black pepper
- 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, chopped

Instructions:
1. In a saucepan combine quinoa and water (or broth). Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat, fluff with a fork, and stir in orange zest and juice. Set aside.  
2. While quinoa cooks, preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss Brussels sprouts with olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until caramelized and crisp on the edges.  
3. In a small skillet over medium heat, toast hazelnuts for 3‑4 minutes, stirring frequently, until fragrant and lightly browned. Transfer to a bowl.  
4. Combine the cooked quinoa, roasted Brussels sprouts, toasted hazelnuts, dried cranberries, and chopped parsley in a large serving bowl. Toss gently to distribute evenly.  
5. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or orange juice if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Citrus‑Infused Quinoa with Charred Brussels Sprouts and Toasted Hazelnuts

text:
Roasted Garlic and Lemon‑Basil Farro Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup farro, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 head garlic, cloves separated and peeled
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 cup cherry tomatoes, halved
- 1/4 cup fresh basil leaves, torn
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tbsp lemon juice
- 1/4 cup toasted pine nuts
- 1/4 cup crumbled feta cheese
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the garlic cloves with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, a pinch of salt, and spread them on a small baking sheet. Roast for 15‑20 minutes, until golden and fragrant; set aside to cool.
2. In a medium saucepan, combine the rinsed farro and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the farro is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.
3. While the farro cooks, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the cherry tomatoes and sauté for 3‑4 minutes, just until they begin to soften and release their juices. Remove from heat.
4. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked farro, roasted garlic (squeezed out of its skins), sautéed tomatoes, torn basil, lemon zest, and lemon juice. Toss gently to distribute the flavors evenly.
5. Season the salad with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste. Sprinkle the toasted pine nuts and crumbled feta over the top just before serving.
6. Serve warm or at room temperature as a hearty side dish or a light main course. Enjoy!
title: Roasted Garlic and Lemon‑Basil Farro Salad

text:
Roasted Garlic and Herb Chickpea & Sweet Potato Tacos

Ingredients:
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and diced into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp dried oregano
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 8 small corn tortillas
- ½ cup red cabbage, thinly sliced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped
- 1 avocado, sliced
- 2 Tbsp lime juice
- Optional: hot sauce or chipotle mayo for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the diced sweet potato with 1 Tbsp olive oil, half the minced garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
3. Roast the sweet potatoes for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
4. While the sweet potatoes roast, heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the remaining garlic and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the chickpeas, season with a pinch of salt and pepper, and cook, stirring occasionally, for 5‑7 minutes until the chickpeas are golden and slightly crisp.  
5. In a small bowl, combine the lime juice with a pinch of salt; drizzle over the roasted sweet potatoes as soon as they exit the oven and toss gently.  
6. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet or directly over a low flame for about 30 seconds per side, keeping them pliable.  
7. Assemble each taco: place a spoonful of roasted sweet potatoes, followed by a handful of crispy chickpeas, then top with red cabbage, avocado slices, and chopped cilantro.  
8. Drizzle with hot sauce or chipotle mayo if desired, serve immediately, and enjoy!
title: Roasted Garlic and Herb Chickpea & Sweet Potato Tacos

text:
Citrus‑Honey Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Carrot & Farro

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into matchsticks
- 1 cup farro, rinsed
- 3 Tbsp honey
- 2 Tbsp fresh orange juice
- 2 Tbsp soy sauce (or tamari)
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together honey, orange juice, soy sauce, garlic, ginger, 1 Tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper.  
3. Toss the carrot matchsticks with the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, spread them on the prepared sheet, and roast for 15 minutes, turning once.  
4. While the carrots roast, place the tempeh strips in a shallow dish and pour half of the glaze over them, reserving the other half for later. Marinate for 5 minutes, then arrange the tempeh on the same baking sheet beside the carrots. Roast for an additional 12‑15 minutes, brushing with the reserved glaze halfway through.  
5. Meanwhile, bring 2 ½ cups water to a boil, add the farro, reduce to a simmer, and cook until tender and chewy, about 20‑25 minutes. Drain any excess water and fluff with a fork.  
6. In a large bowl combine the cooked farro, roasted carrots, and glazed tempeh. Toss gently to distribute the flavors, garnish with chopped cilantro, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Citrus‑Honey Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Carrot & Farro

text:
Turmeric‑Honey Glazed Carrot and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into sticks
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp honey
- 1 tbsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup cooked quinoa
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- 1 avocado, sliced (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together olive oil, honey, turmeric, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.  
3. Add the carrot sticks and chickpeas to the bowl, tossing until evenly coated with the glaze.  
4. Spread the carrots and chickpeas in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
5. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until carrots are tender and lightly caramelized and chickpeas are crisp.  
6. While the vegetables roast, divide cooked quinoa among four serving bowls.  
7. Top each quinoa bowl with the roasted carrots and chickpeas.  
8. Drizzle lemon juice over the top, sprinkle with chopped cilantro, and add avocado slices if desired.  
9. Serve warm or at room temperature, enjoying the sweet‑spicy harmony of the turmeric‑honey glaze.
title: Turmeric‑Honey Glazed Carrot and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa with Roasted Sweet Potato and Kale

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 3 cups kale, stems removed and torn
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, grated
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- Zest of 1 lemon
- Juice of 1 lemon
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper, spread them on a baking sheet, and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine the quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
3. In a large skillet, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger, sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the kale and a pinch of salt; cook, stirring frequently, until the kale wilts,
title: Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa with Roasted Sweet Potato and Kale

text:
Sage‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Lentil Soup with Coconut Milk

Ingredients:
- 2 lb carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 large onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh sage, finely chopped
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh sage leaves for garnish (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the carrot chunks with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper, then spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, until caramelized.
2. While the carrots roast, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 5 minutes until translucent.
3. Stir in the minced garlic, chopped sage, cumin, and smoked paprika; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Add the rinsed red lentils and vegetable broth to the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes.
5. Transfer the roasted carrots to the pot. Simmer the mixture for another 10 minutes, or until the lentils are tender.
6. Using an immersion blender (or a countertop blender in batches), puree the soup until smooth and creamy.
7. Stir in the coconut milk, adjust seasoning with salt and pepper, and heat through for 2‑3 minutes without boiling.
8. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with fresh sage leaves if desired, and serve hot.
title: Sage‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Lentil Soup with Coconut Milk

text:
Maple‑Glazed Carrot and Lentil Soup with Coconut Cream

Ingredients:
- 2 lb carrots, peeled and sliced
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 large onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup full‑fat coconut milk
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp ground coriander
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add the sliced carrots, cumin, coriander, and a pinch of salt. Toss to coat the vegetables with the spices.
4. Pour in the vegetable broth and bring the mixture to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes, or until the carrots begin to soften.
5. Add the rinsed red lentils and maple syrup. Continue to simmer, uncovered, for 15‑20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils and carrots are completely tender.
6. Using an immersion blender (or transferring in batches to a countertop blender), puree the soup until smooth and velvety.
7. Stir in the coconut milk, and season with additional salt and pepper to taste. Heat gently for 2‑3 minutes—do not boil.
8. Ladle the soup into bowls, drizzle a swirl of extra coconut milk on top, and garnish with fresh cilantro leaves. Serve hot.
title: Maple‑Glazed Carrot and Lentil Soup with Coconut Cream

text:
Harissa‑Spiced Sweet Potato and Chickpea Flatbread

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp harissa paste
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 small red onion, thinly sliced
- 2 cups fresh baby spinach
- 4 oz crumbled feta cheese
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 4 large flatbreads or naan rounds
- Optional garnish: chopped fresh cilantro

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the diced sweet potatoes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the sliced red onion and sauté for 3‑4 minutes until softened.
3. Stir in the chickpeas and harissa paste, cooking for another 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
4. When the sweet potatoes are done, add them to the skillet with the chickpea mixture. Toss gently to combine, then fold in the baby spinach and cook until wilted, about 2 minutes. Remove from heat and drizzle with lemon juice.
5. Arrange the flatbreads on a baking sheet and warm them in the oven for 3‑4 minutes, just until lightly crisped.
6. Spoon the harissa‑spiced sweet potato and chickpea mixture evenly over each flatbread. Sprinkle crumbled feta over the top and garnish with chopped cilantro, if using.
7. Serve immediately while warm, with extra lemon wedges on the side for a bright finish. Enjoy!
title: Harissa‑Spiced Sweet Potato and Chickpea Flatbread

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Lentil Pilaf with Citrus Vinaigrette

Ingredients:
- 1 cup green lentils, rinsed
- 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into ½‑inch dice
- 1 small red onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon saffron threads
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup water
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- ¼ teaspoon smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
- 1 tablespoon orange zest
- 2 tablespoons extra‑virgin olive oil (for vinaigrette)
- 1 teaspoon honey or maple syrup
- 1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, combine the saffron threads with 2 tablespoons hot water; let steep for 5 minutes.  
2. Heat olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 3 minutes. Stir in the garlic and cook 30 seconds more.  
3. Add the diced carrots, cumin, and smoked paprika; stir and cook for 2 minutes to toast the spices.  
4. Pour in the lentils, vegetable broth, water, and the saffron infusion (including the threads). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 20‑25 minutes, or
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Lentil Pilaf with Citrus Vinaigrette

text:
Saffron‑Infused Coconut Lime Chickpea and Spinach Stew

Ingredients:
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 large onion, diced
- 3 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- ¼ teaspoon saffron threads, soaked in 2 tablespoons warm water
- 1 can (14 oz) coconut milk
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- 1 lime, zest and juice
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 4 cups fresh baby spinach
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat; add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
2. Stir in the minced garlic, grated ginger, cumin, and smoked paprika; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add the soaked saffron (including its liquid) to the pot, stirring to combine.
4. Pour in the coconut milk and vegetable broth, then bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.
5. Add the lime zest, lime juice, and chickpeas; let the stew simmer for 10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.
6. Fold in the fresh spinach and cook until wilted, about 2 minutes; season with salt and pepper to taste.
7. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with chopped cilantro, and serve hot.
title: Saffron‑Infused Coconut Lime Chickpea and Spinach Stew

text:
Lemon‑Sage Quinoa with Roasted Brussels Sprouts and Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 12 ounces Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 1 teaspoon fresh sage, finely chopped (plus extra leaves for garnish)
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
- 1/2 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
- 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- 1/3 cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 tablespoons toasted pine nuts (optional)
- 1/4 cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the Brussels sprouts with olive oil, half the salt, and pepper, then spread them cut‑side down on a baking sheet.
2. Roast the sprouts for 20‑25 minutes, stirring once, until caramelized and crisp on the edges. Remove from the oven and let cool slightly.
3. While the sprouts roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy.
4. Fluff the cooked quinoa with a fork and stir in lemon zest, lemon juice, chopped sage, and the remaining salt. Adjust seasoning to taste.
5. Transfer the quinoa to a large serving bowl. Add the roasted Brussels sprouts, pomegranate seeds, toasted pine nuts, and crumbled feta if using. Toss gently to combine.
6. Garnish with extra sage leaves and a drizzle of lemon juice. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Sage Quinoa with Roasted Brussels Sprouts and Pomegranate

text:
Rosemary‑Lemon Quinoa with Pan‑Seared Cod and Charred Asparagus

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups low‑sodium vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 lemon, zest and juice
- 1 tsp fresh rosemary, finely chopped
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 lb cod fillets, skinless
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 bunch asparagus, trimmed
- 1 tbsp butter
- Optional garnish: chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa and vegetable broth; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and fluff with a fork. Stir in 1 tbsp olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, rosemary, and minced garlic; season with salt and pepper. Set aside, keeping it warm.
2. While the quinoa cooks, preheat a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add 1 tbsp olive oil and the butter; once melted and shimmering, place the cod fillets in the pan. Cook 3‑4 minutes per side, or until the fish flakes easily with a fork and is golden brown. Season the cod with a pinch of salt and pepper. Transfer to a plate and keep warm.
3. Meanwhile, heat a grill pan or the same skillet over medium heat. Add a drizzle of olive oil and the asparagus spears. Cook, turning occasionally, until tender‑crisp and lightly charred, about 5‑6 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
4. To serve, spoon a bed of rosemary‑lemon quinoa onto each plate, top with a cod fillet, and arrange charred asparagus alongside. Garnish with chopped parsley if desired and enjoy immediately.
title: Rosemary‑Lemon Quinoa with Pan‑Seared Cod and Charred Asparagus

text:
Saffron‑Infused Coconut Lime Shrimp and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or low‑sodium vegetable broth
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp saffron threads
- 1 cup coconut milk (full‑fat)
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 small red bell pepper, thinly sliced
- 1 small cucumber, diced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 tbsp honey or agave syrup
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- Optional: ¼ tsp red‑pepper flakes for heat

Instructions:
1. In a small heat‑proof bowl, combine the saffron threads with 2 tbsp hot water; let steep for 5 minutes to release color and flavor.  
2. While the saffron infuses, bring the quinoa and broth to a boil in a saucepan; reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.  
3. In a skillet over medium‑high heat, add olive oil and the shrimp. Cook 2‑3 minutes per side, until pink and opaque. Remove shrimp and set aside.  
4. Reduce the skillet to medium, pour in the coconut milk, saffron infusion (including the water), lime zest, lime juice, honey, salt, and pepper. Stir and simmer 3‑4 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.  
5. Return the cooked shrimp to the skillet, tossing to coat them in the saffron‑coconut glaze. Cook an additional minute to re‑heat the shrimp.  
6. In a large bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, sliced red bell pepper, diced cucumber, and chopped cilantro.  
7. Drizzle the warm saffron‑coconut shrimp mixture over the quinoa salad, tossing gently to distribute the sauce evenly.  
8. Taste and adjust seasoning with extra lime juice, salt, or red‑pepper flakes if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Saffron‑Infused Coconut Lime Shrimp and Quinoa Salad

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup long‑grain basmati rice
- 2 ½ cups vegetable broth
- ½ teaspoon saffron threads
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 small red onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- ¼ teaspoon smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup toasted slivered almonds
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, a pinch of salt, and half the cumin. Spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning once, until tender and lightly caramelized.
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, place the saffron threads in a small bowl with 2 tablespoons of hot vegetable broth; let steep for 5 minutes to release color and flavor.
3. In a medium saucepan, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced red onion and sauté for 3‑4 minutes until translucent. Stir in the minced garlic and the remaining cumin and smoked paprika; cook for another minute until fragrant.
4. Add the basmati rice to the saucepan, stirring to coat the grains with the aromatics for 2 minutes. Pour in the saffron‑infused broth plus the remaining vegetable broth, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
5. When the rice is done, gently fold in the roasted sweet potatoes, chickpeas, and toasted almonds. Season with salt and pepper to taste, and heat through for 2‑3 minutes, stirring carefully to avoid breaking the sweet potatoes.
6. Transfer the pilaf to a serving dish, garnish with chopped fresh parsley, and serve warm. Enjoy!
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Pilaf

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 cup cooked quinoa
- 1 medium sweet potato, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp saffron threads, soaked in 2 tbsp warm water
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and pepper, to taste
- 2 cups baby spinach
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tbsp tahini

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). In a bowl, combine the sweet potato cubes, chickpeas, olive oil, saffron water, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper; toss to coat evenly.
2. Spread the mixture on a baking sheet in a single layer and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until the sweet potatoes are tender and the chickpeas are crisp.
3. While the vegetables roast, cook the quinoa according to package directions; fluff with a fork and set aside.
4. In a small bowl, whisk together the lemon juice, tahini, a pinch of salt, and enough water to achieve a drizzling consistency.
5. Assemble the bowl: start with a base of quinoa, add the roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas, then top with fresh baby spinach.
6. Drizzle the tahini‑lemon sauce over the bowl and sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds on top. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Buddha Bowl

text:
Roasted Garlic & Herb Chickpea and Sweet Potato Skillet

Ingredients:
- 1 large sweet potato, diced ½‑inch cubes
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon fresh rosemary, finely chopped
- 1 tablespoon fresh thyme leaves
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup vegetable broth
- 2 cups baby spinach
- 1 tablespoon lemon juice
- Optional garnish: crumbled feta cheese or toasted pumpkin seeds

Instructions:
1. Preheat a large cast‑iron skillet over medium heat and add the olive oil.
2. Once the oil shimmers, add the diced sweet potato; season with salt, pepper, and smoked paprika. Cook, stirring occasionally, for about 8‑10 minutes until the sweet potato begins to soften and develop a golden crust.
3. Add the minced garlic, rosemary, and thyme to the skillet. Stir and cook for 1‑2 minutes until fragrant.
4. Incorporate the chickpeas and pour in the vegetable broth. Continue to sauté for another 5 minutes, allowing the broth to reduce and the chickpeas to heat through.
5. Fold in the baby spinach and cook until wilted, about 1 minute. Remove the skillet from heat.
6. Drizzle the lemon juice over the mixture, give a final toss, and adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed.
7. Serve hot, topped with optional crumbled feta or toasted pumpkin seeds for extra texture and flavor.
title: Roasted Garlic & Herb Chickpea and Sweet Potato Skillet

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Tempeh with Coconut Quinoa and Roasted Carrots

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, cubed
- 1 cup quinoa
- 1 ¾ cups coconut milk
- 2 carrots, sliced into sticks
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Toss carrot sticks with ½ tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast 20‑25 minutes until caramelized.
2. While carrots roast, rinse quinoa and combine with coconut milk in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed; fluff with a fork.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, lemon juice, grated ginger, turmeric, maple syrup, and a pinch of salt.
4. Heat remaining ½ tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add tempeh cubes and sauté 5‑7 minutes until golden. Pour the sauce over the tempeh, stir, and cook an additional 2 minutes to coat.
5. Plate the coconut quinoa, top with the glazed tempeh and roasted carrots, and garnish with chopped cilantro. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Tempeh with Coconut Quinoa and Roasted Carrots

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Chickpea Power Salad

Ingredients:
- 3 medium beets, peeled and cubed
- 1 ½ cups cooked quinoa
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- 2 tablespoons olive oil, divided
- 1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar
- 2 cups baby arugula
- ¼ cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). On a baking sheet, toss the beet cubes with 1  tablespoon of olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway, until tender and caramelized.  
2. While the beets roast, spread the chickpeas on a separate baking sheet, drizzle with the remaining 1  tablespoon of olive oil, and season with salt and pepper. Roast for 15‑20 minutes, shaking the pan once, until slightly crisp.  
3. Cook quinoa according to package instructions; fluff with a fork and let cool slightly.  
4. In a large bowl, combine the roasted beets, roasted chickpeas, cooked quinoa, and baby arugula.  
5. Whisk together apple cider vinegar, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of olive oil; pour over the salad and toss gently to coat.  
6. Top the salad with toasted walnuts and crumbled feta. Adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a splash of vinegar if desired.  
7. Serve warm or at room temperature as a hearty main‑course salad. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Chickpea Power Salad

text:
Coconut‑Lime Baked Tofu with Turmeric Quinoa and Roasted Broccoli

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 Tbsp coconut oil, divided
- 1 Tbsp lime juice
- 1 tsp lime zest
- 1 tsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups water
- ½ tsp ground turmeric
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 1 lb (450 g) broccoli florets
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- Salt to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (optional garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, whisk together 1 Tbsp coconut oil, lime juice, lime zest, soy sauce, maple syrup, smoked paprika, and cumin. Add the tofu cubes, toss to coat, and spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
3. Toss the broccoli florets with olive oil, a pinch of salt, and the remaining 1 Tbsp coconut oil; place them on the same sheet beside the tofu.  
4. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning the tofu and broccoli halfway through, until the tofu is golden and the broccoli is crisp‑tender.  
5. While the tofu and broccoli roast, combine quinoa, water, turmeric, and black pepper in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the quinoa is fluffy and the liquid is absorbed.  
6. Fluff the quinoa with a fork and season with additional salt if needed.  
7. To serve, divide the turmeric quinoa among plates, top with roasted tofu and broccoli, and sprinkle with chopped cilantro if desired. Enjoy warm.
title: Coconut‑Lime Baked Tofu with Turmeric Quinoa and Roasted Broccoli

text:
Lemon‑Basil Grilled Portobello with Quinoa‑Pine Nut Salad

Ingredients:
- 4 large portobello mushroom caps, stems removed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- ¼ cup pine nuts
- 2 tablespoons fresh basil, finely chopped
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tablespoons lemon juice
- 2 tablespoons extra‑virgin olive oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat a grill or grill pan over medium‑high heat. Brush each mushroom cap with 1  tablespoon of olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
2. Grill the mushrooms, gill side down first, for 4–5 minutes per side, until tender and lightly charred. Remove from heat and set aside to cool slightly.
3. While the mushrooms grill, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and let cool for 5 minutes.
4. In a small skillet over low heat, toast pine nuts, stirring frequently, until golden and fragrant, about 2 minutes. Transfer to a bowl.
5. In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the remaining olive oil, lemon juice, lemon zest, minced garlic, chopped basil, salt, and pepper. Add the cooked quinoa and toasted pine nuts, tossing to combine.
6. Slice the grilled portobello caps into thick strips. Arrange the quinoa‑pine nut salad on plates, top with mushroom strips, and garnish with extra basil leaves if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Basil Grilled Portobello with Quinoa‑Pine Nut Salad

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Glazed Carrot and Lentil Tacos with Avocado Crema

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into thin matchsticks
- 1 cup cooked green or brown lentils
- 1 tablespoon maple syrup
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/4 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 8 small corn or flour tortillas
- 1 ripe avocado
- 1 tablespoon lime juice
- 1 tablespoon plain Greek yogurt or vegan yogurt
- 2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro
- 1/4 cup finely diced red onion
- Optional: hot sauce or sliced jalapeño for heat

Instructions:
1. In a large skillet over medium heat, warm the olive oil. Add the carrot matchsticks and sauté for 3‑4 minutes until they begin to soften.
2. Sprinkle the cinnamon, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper over the carrots. Stir to coat evenly.
3. Drizzle the maple syrup over the spiced carrots and continue cooking for another 2‑3 minutes, allowing the carrots to caramelize and become tender. Remove from heat.
4. Add the cooked lentils to the skillet, mixing gently to combine with the glazed carrots. Heat for 1‑2 minutes just to warm the lentils through; adjust seasoning if needed.
5. While the filling cooks, prepare the avocado crema: in a small bowl, mash the avocado with lime juice, yogurt, a pinch of salt, and a splash of water (if needed) until smooth and creamy.
6. Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet or microwave for about 30 seconds until pliable.
7. To assemble each taco, spoon a generous portion of the carrot‑lentil mixture onto the center of a tortilla. Top with a drizzle of avocado crema, a sprinkle of diced red onion, and fresh cilantro. Add hot sauce or jalapeño if desired.
8. Serve the tacos immediately, accompanied by any extra avocado crema on the side. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Glazed Carrot and Lentil Tacos with Avocado Crema

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Acorn Squash and Lentil Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 medium acorn squash, halved and seeded, cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 1 small onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 2 1/2 cups vegetable broth
- 1/4 tsp salt (or to taste)
- 1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 2 tbsp fresh thyme leaves, chopped (plus extra for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the cubed acorn squash with 1 tablespoon olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, cumin, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway, until tender and caramelized.  
2. While the squash roasts, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 4‑5 minutes until translucent.  
3. Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another 30 seconds until fragrant.  
4. Add the rinsed lentils to the saucepan, pour in the vegetable broth, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender but still hold their shape.  
5. Once the lentils are cooked, remove the lid and let any excess liquid evaporate, stirring occasionally.  
6. Gently fold the roasted acorn squash cubes into the cooked lentils. Sprinkle the chopped fresh thyme over the mixture and stir to combine.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed.  
8. Transfer the pilaf to a serving bowl, garnish with a few extra thyme leaves, and serve warm. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Acorn Squash and Lentil Pilaf

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Parsnip and Chickpea Salad with Pomegranate Vinaigrette

Ingredients:
- 2 large parsnips, peeled and cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 cups mixed baby greens
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 Tbsp toasted walnuts, roughly chopped
- 1 Tbsp apple cider vinegar
- 1 tsp Dijon mustard
- 1 Tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil (for dressing)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cubed parsnips with 1 Tbsp olive oil, ground cinnamon, maple syrup, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the seasoned parsnips on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20 minutes, turning halfway through.  
4. While the parsnips roast, toss the chickpeas with the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper; spread on a separate part of the sheet and roast for the last 12‑15 minutes, until lightly crisp.  
5. In a small jar or bowl, whisk together apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, extra‑virgin olive oil, a pinch of salt, and a dash of pepper to create the vinaigrette.  
6. In a large serving bowl, combine the mixed baby greens, roasted parsnips, roasted chickpeas, pomegranate seeds, and toasted walnuts.  
7. Drizzle the vinaigrette over the salad and toss gently to coat all ingredients.  
8. Serve immediately, garnished with a few extra pomegranate seeds if desired.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Parsnip and Chickpea Salad with Pomegranate Vinaigrette

text:
Saffron‑Infused Coconut Lime Chickpea and Spinach Soup

Ingredients:
- 1 cup dried chickpeas (or 2 ½ cups cooked/chickpeas, drained and rinsed)
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup full‑fat coconut milk
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon saffron threads
- 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice
- 4 cups fresh spinach leaves, roughly chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. If using dried chickpeas, soak them overnight, then drain and rinse. Cook them in a pot of boiling water until tender, about 45 minutes, then set aside. (If using canned chickpeas, skip this step and rinse them well.)  
2. In a large saucepan, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.  
3. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
4. Sprinkle the cumin, smoked paprika, and saffron threads over the aromatics; toast gently for 30 seconds, stirring constantly to release their flavors.  
5. Pour in the vegetable broth and bring the mixture to a gentle boil. Reduce heat and let simmer for 5 minutes.  
6. Add the cooked chickpeas and coconut milk to the pot; stir to combine and return to a low simmer.  
7. Season with salt and pepper, then add the lime juice. Simmer for another 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.  
8. Just before serving, fold in the chopped spinach and cook for 1–2 minutes, until the leaves wilt but remain bright green.  
9. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired.  
10. Ladle the soup into bowls and serve hot, optionally garnished with a drizzle of coconut milk, a few extra saffron threads, or fresh cilantro.
title: Saffron‑Infused Coconut Lime Chickpea and Spinach Soup

text:
Sesame‑Lime Glazed Tempeh with Coconut‑Basil Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 2 Tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 Tbsp sesame oil
- 1 Tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp grated ginger
- 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- 1 cup water
- ¼ cup fresh basil leaves, chopped
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a shallow bowl, whisk together soy sauce, sesame oil, lime juice, maple syrup, and grated ginger. Add the tempeh strips, toss to coat, and let marinate for 15 minutes.
2. While the tempeh marinates, combine quinoa, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed and quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and stir in chopped basil; set aside.
3. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add olive oil, then place the marinated tempeh strips in a single layer. Cook 3‑4 minutes per side, or until golden and caramelized, brushing the pan with any remaining glaze.
4. Transfer the cooked tempeh to a plate and sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds.
5. Serve the sesame‑lime tempeh over the coconut‑basil quinoa, drizzling any pan juices over the top. Adjust seasoning with extra lime juice, salt, or pepper if desired. Enjoy!
title: Sesame‑Lime Glazed Tempeh with Coconut‑Basil Quinoa

text:
Citrus‑Infused Chickpea and Farro Salad with Toasted Pistachios

Ingredients:
- 1 cup farro, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 orange, zest and juice
- 1 lemon, zest and juice
- 1/4 cup pistachios, shelled and roughly chopped
- 2 tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil
- 1 small red onion, finely diced
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- 1 tsp honey or maple syrup
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan, combine the farro and water (or broth). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook 20‑25 minutes until tender but still slightly chewy. Drain any excess liquid and set aside to cool.
2. While the farro cooks, preheat a small skillet over medium heat. Add the pistachios and toast, stirring frequently, for 3‑4 minutes until fragrant and lightly golden. Transfer to a bowl and let cool.
3. In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the olive oil, orange juice, lemon juice, orange zest, lemon zest, honey, salt, and pepper to create the citrus dressing.
4. Add the cooked farro, chickpeas, diced red onion, and chopped parsley to the bowl with the dressing. Toss gently to combine, ensuring everything is evenly coated.
5. Fold in the toasted pistachios just before serving to retain their crunch.
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a drizzle of honey if desired. Serve the salad at room temperature or chilled. Enjoy!
title: Citrus‑Infused Chickpea and Farro Salad with Toasted Pistachios

text:
Sage‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Lentil Salad with Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and sliced into thin rounds
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 teaspoon dried sage
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- ¼ teaspoon sea salt
- ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 cups mixed baby greens
- 2 tablespoons toasted pumpkin seeds
- 1 tablespoon lemon juice
- 1 tablespoon maple syrup
- 1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the carrot rounds with 1 tablespoon olive oil, dried sage, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread them in a single layer and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until caramelized and tender.  
3. While the carrots roast, combine lentils with 2 cups water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, and cook for 20‑25 minutes until tender but firm. Drain any excess water.  
4. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining olive oil, lemon juice, maple syrup, and apple cider vinegar to make the dressing.  
5. In a large mixing bowl, combine the roasted carrots, cooked lentils, mixed baby greens, and toasted pumpkin seeds; drizzle with the dressing and toss gently to coat.  
6. Transfer the salad to serving plates, garnish with fresh pomegranate seeds, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Sage‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Lentil Salad with Pomegranate

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Tostada with Avocado Crema  

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 8 small corn tortillas
- 1/2 red onion, thinly sliced
- 1 avocado
- 1 Tbsp lime juice
- 2 Tbsp Greek yogurt or vegan plain yogurt
- 2 Tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- Optional: crumbled feta or vegan feta, for topping

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the diced sweet potatoes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper until evenly coated. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
3. Roast the sweet potatoes for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until tender and caramelized.  
4. While the sweet potatoes roast, toss the chickpeas with the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, pepper, and a drizzle of maple syrup. Add them to the baking sheet during the last 10 minutes of roasting to heat through and crisp slightly.  
5. Warm the corn tortillas: place them on a separate baking sheet and bake for 3‑4 minutes, or heat them individually in a dry skillet over medium heat until pliable.  
6. Prepare the avocado crema: in a small blender or food processor, combine the avocado, lime juice, yogurt, a pinch of salt, and a splash of water (if needed) until smooth and creamy. Adjust seasoning to taste.  
7. Assemble each tostada: spread a spoonful of avocado crema on a tortilla, top with a generous mound of roasted sweet potatoes, chickpeas, and sliced red onion. Sprinkle with fresh cilantro and optional feta.  
8. Serve immediately, with extra lime wedges on the side for squeezing. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Tostada with Avocado Crema

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Chickpeas and Spinach

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 cloves garlic, minced

2. While the chickpeas roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.

4. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl. Add the roasted garlic chickpeas and pour the lemon‑ginger
title: Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Chickpeas and Spinach

text:

title: Sage‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Lentil Soup with Coconut Milk

Ingredients:

text:
Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Broccoli and Chickpea Couscous

Ingredients:
- 1 cup couscous
- 1 ¼ cups vegetable broth
- 2 cups broccoli florets
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 lemon, zest and juice
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 tbsp toasted pine nuts (optional)
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the broccoli and chickpeas with olive oil, thyme, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread in a single layer on the sheet and roast 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway, until broccoli is tender‑crisp and chickpeas are lightly crisp.  
3. While the vegetables roast, bring the vegetable broth to a boil in a medium saucepan, stir in the couscous, cover, and remove from heat. Let stand 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.  
4. Transfer the couscous to a large bowl; add the roasted broccoli and chickpeas, lemon zest, lemon juice, and a drizzle of olive oil. Toss gently to combine.  
5. Adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice as needed. Sprinkle toasted pine nuts and chopped parsley on top.  
6. Serve warm or at room temperature as a hearty side or light main dish.
title: Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Broccoli and Chickpea Couscous

text:
Sesame‑Ginger Glazed Tempeh with Turmeric Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 8 oz (225 g) tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tbsp sesame oil
- 1 tsp freshly grated ginger
- 1 tsp grated garlic
- ½ tsp ground turmeric
- ¼ tsp red‑pepper flakes (optional)
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 1 tbsp olive oil (for cooking tempeh)

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, maple syrup, sesame oil, ginger, garlic, turmeric, red‑pepper flakes, and lime juice to create the glaze.
2. Place the tempeh strips in a shallow dish and pour half of the glaze over them, turning to coat evenly. Let marinate for 10 minutes while you prepare the quinoa.
3. Combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and fluff with a fork; season with salt and pepper.
4. Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated tempeh strips in a single layer and cook 3‑4 minutes per side, until golden and crisp. Transfer to a plate.
5. Add the remaining glaze to the skillet and simmer for 1‑2 minutes, allowing it to thicken slightly. Return the tempeh to the pan, tossing to coat in the glossy glaze.
6. Divide the turmeric‑infused quinoa among serving bowls, top with the glazed tempeh, and sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds and chopped cilantro.
7. Serve warm, optionally with extra lime wedges for a bright finish. Enjoy!
title: Sesame‑Ginger Glazed Tempeh with Turmeric Quinoa

text:
Roasted Garlic and Chili Lime Tempeh with Coconut Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 cup jasmine or basmati rice – coconut milk
- 1 ½ cups water
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp chili flakes (adjust to taste)
- Zest of 1 lime
- Juice of 1 lime
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)
- Optional: toasted coconut flakes for topping

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine the coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, add the rice, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes or until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.  
2. While the rice cooks, preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
3. In a large bowl whisk together olive oil, minced garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, chili flakes, lime zest, lime juice, maple syrup, and a generous pinch of salt and pepper. Add the tempeh cubes and toss to coat evenly.  
4. Spread the seasoned tempeh in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once halfway through, until the tempeh is golden‑brown and slightly crisp on the edges.  
5. To serve, spoon a bed of coconut‑infused quinoa onto each plate, top with the roasted tempeh, and garnish with chopped cilantro and toasted coconut flakes, if using. Enjoy warm!
title: Roasted Garlic and Chili Lime Tempeh with Coconut Quinoa

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Quinoa Power Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 medium beets, peeled and cubed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 2 teaspoons maple syrup
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- 1/2 teaspoon sea salt
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 1/4 cup crumbled feta cheese
- 2 cups baby arugula
- 2 tablespoons lemon‑juice vinaigrette (lemon juice, olive oil, Dijon mustard, salt, pepper)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the beet cubes with olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, and sea salt; spread them in a single layer and roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway, until tender and caramelized.  
3. While the beets roast, combine quinoa and 2 cups water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
4. In a large bowl, combine cooked quinoa, roasted beets, baby arugula, and toasted pumpkin seeds; drizzle with the lemon‑juice vinaigrette and toss gently.  
5. Top the bowl with crumbled feta cheese and an extra drizzle of maple syrup if desired.  
6. Serve warm or at room temperature, enjoying the sweet‑spicy beet flavor paired with nutty quinoa and fresh greens.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Quinoa Power Bowl

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Tagine with Apricot  

Ingredients:
- 1 lb carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch pieces  
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed  
- ½ cup dried apricot halves, roughly chopped  
- 1 small onion, finely diced  
- 2 cloves garlic, minced  
- 1 tbsp olive oil  
- 1 tsp ground cumin  
- ½ tsp ground cinnamon  
- ¼ tsp ground ginger  
- ½ tsp saffron threads, steeped in 2 Tbsp hot water  
- 1 cup vegetable broth  
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste  
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish  

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the carrot pieces with olive oil, cumin, cinnamon, ginger, salt, and pepper; spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
2. While the carrots roast, heat a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add a splash of olive oil and sauté the onion until translucent, about 3 minutes. Stir in the garlic and cook for another minute.  
3. Add the chickpeas, roasted carrots, and chopped apricots to the skillet. Pour in the saffron‑infused water and vegetable broth, stirring to combine.  
4. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low. Cover and let it cook for 10‑12 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken slightly.  
5. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed. If the tagine is too thick, add a splash more broth or water.  
6. Serve the tagine hot, garnished with fresh cilantro leaves. It pairs beautifully with couscous, quinoa, or warm flatbread.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Tagine with Apricot

text:
Herb‑Crusted Salmon with Lemon‑Garlic Quinoa and Roasted Asparagus

Ingredients:
- 4 salmon fillets (about 6 oz each)
- 1 cup panko breadcrumbs
- 2  tbsp fresh chopped parsley
- 2  tbsp fresh chopped dill
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 1  tsp lemon pepper seasoning
- 2  garlic cloves, minced
- 2  tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1  cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2  cups low‑sodium chicken broth
- 2  tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1  tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil
- 1  lb asparagus, trimmed
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a shallow bowl, combine panko, parsley, dill, lemon zest, lemon pepper, and minced garlic. Drizzle 1  tbsp olive oil into the mixture and stir until evenly coated.
3. Pat the salmon fillets dry with paper towels, season lightly with salt and pepper, then press each fillet into the herb‑breadcrumb mixture, coating both sides.
4. Place the crusted salmon on the prepared baking sheet. Bake for 12‑15 minutes, or until the crust is golden and the salmon flakes easily with a fork.
5. While the salmon cooks, toss the asparagus with 1  tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a separate baking sheet and roast in the same oven for 10‑12 minutes, until tender‑crisp.
6. In a medium saucepan, bring the chicken broth to a boil. Add the quinoa, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and quinoa is fluffy.
7. Remove the quinoa from heat; fluff with a fork and stir in lemon juice, extra‑virgin olive oil, and a pinch of salt. Adjust seasoning to taste.
