8. To serve, divide the lemon‑garlic quinoa among plates, top with a salmon fillet, and arrange roasted asparagus alongside. Garnish with additional fresh herbs or a lemon wedge if desired.
title: Herb‑Crusted Salmon with Lemon‑Garlic Quinoa and Roasted Asparagus

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Beet and Chickpea Quinoa Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 medium beets, peeled and cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- ½ teaspoon sea salt
- ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- ¼ teaspoon saffron threads, steeped in 2 tablespoons hot water
- 2 tablespoons toasted almond slivers
- 2 tablespoons crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- Fresh arugula leaves, for garnish
- Lemon wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the beet cubes with olive oil, salt, and pepper, then spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning once, until tender and caramelized.
2. While the beets roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
3. In a small bowl, mix the chickpeas with smoked paprika, cumin, and a pinch of salt. Spread the seasoned chickpeas on a separate baking sheet and roast alongside the beets for the last 15 minutes, until slightly crisp.
4. Stir the saffron infusion into the cooked quinoa, mixing gently to distribute the golden hue and flavor evenly.
5. Assemble the bowl: start with a base of saffron‑infused quinoa, top with roasted beets, roasted chickpeas, a handful of arugula, toasted almond slivers, and crumbled feta if using.
6. Finish with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice and serve immediately. Enjoy warm or at room temperature.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Beet and Chickpea Quinoa Bowl

text:
Maple‑Saffron Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Carrot Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 8 oz (225 g) tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp saffron threads, steeped in 2 tbsp warm water
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into matchsticks
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- 1 tsp lime zest

Instructions:
1. In a shallow bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, saffron water, soy sauce, smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt.  
2. Add the tempeh strips to the marinade, toss to coat, and let sit for 10 minutes.  
3. While the tempeh marinates, heat ½ tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the carrot matchsticks, season with salt and pepper, and sauté 5‑6 minutes until tender‑cr
title: Maple‑Saffron Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Carrot Quinoa

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Lentil Soup with Coconut Milk

Ingredients:
- 1 lb carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch pieces
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 large onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp ground coriander
- ¼ tsp saffron threads, steeped in 2 Tbsp hot water
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- A squeeze of lemon juice (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the carrot pieces with olive oil, salt, and pepper, then spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until caramelized and tender.
2. While the carrots roast, heat a large pot over medium heat. Add a drizzle of olive oil, then sauté the diced onion until translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in the minced garlic, cumin, and coriander; cook for another minute until fragrant.
3. Add the roasted carrots, rinsed lentils, vegetable broth, and the saffron infusion (including the threads) to the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 15‑20 minutes, or until the lentils are soft.
4. Remove the pot from heat and use an immersion blender to puree the soup until smooth (or blend in batches in a countertop blender). Return the soup to the pot and stir in the coconut milk.
5. Warm the soup gently over low heat; season with additional salt, pepper, and a splash of lemon juice if desired. Serve hot, garnished with fresh cilantro leaves.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Lentil Soup with Coconut Milk

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Shrimp & Mango Quinoa Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 12 oz large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1 teaspoon lime zest
- 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice
- 1/2 teaspoon sea salt
- 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 ripe mango, diced
- 1/2 red bell pepper, finely diced
- 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 small red onion, minced
- 1 teaspoon honey (optional)

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa and water; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
2. While quinoa cooks, whisk together olive oil, turmeric, lime zest, lime juice, salt, and pepper in a bowl; add shrimp and toss to coat. Let marinate 10 minutes.
3. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the shrimp and cook 2‑3 minutes per side, until pink and opaque. Transfer to a plate.
4. In a small bowl combine coconut milk, diced mango, red bell pepper, red onion, cilantro, and honey (if using); stir gently to create a mango‑coconut sauce.
5. Divide the cooked quinoa among serving bowls, top with the sautéed shrimp, and spoon the mango‑coconut sauce over everything. Garnish with extra cilantro and a lime wedge if desired. Enjoy!
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Shrimp & Mango Quinoa Bowl

text:
Saffron‑Infused Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Chickpeas and Kale

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- ½ tsp saffron threads
- 2 cups kale, stems removed and torn into bite‑size pieces
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the chickpeas with 1 tbsp olive oil, half the minced garlic, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking halfway, until crisp.
2. While the chickpeas roast, combine the saffron threads with 2 tbsp hot water; let steep for 5 minutes.
3. In a medium saucepan, bring the quinoa and broth (or water) to a boil. Add the saffron infusion, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
4. In a large skillet, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil over medium heat. Add the remaining garlic and sauté for 30 seconds, then add the kale. Cook, stirring, until wilted, about 3‑4 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
5. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large bowl; fold in the sautéed kale, roasted chickpeas, and lemon juice. Adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if desired.
6. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with a drizzle of extra‑virgin olive oil if desired.
title: Saffron‑Infused Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Chickpeas and Kale

text:
Roasted Garlic‑Lime Chickpea and Sweet Potato Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tbsp lime zest
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 2 cups baby spinach
- ½ cup cooked quinoa
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Optional garnish: chopped fresh cilantro and toasted pumpkin seeds

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper; spread them in a single layer on the sheet and roast for 20 minutes.  
3. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine chickpeas, minced garlic, lime juice, lime zest, the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, and a pinch of salt in another bowl; add to the baking sheet with the sweet potatoes and roast together for an additional 15 minutes, stirring halfway.  
4. Meanwhile, heat a skillet over medium heat, add the baby spinach, and sauté until just wilted, about 2 minutes.  
5. Assemble the bowls: start with a base of cooked quinoa, top with roasted sweet potatoes, chickpeas, and wilted spinach.  
6. Finish with a drizzle of extra lime juice if desired, and garnish with cilantro and toasted pumpkin seeds. Enjoy warm or at room temperature.
title: Roasted Garlic‑Lime Chickpea and Sweet Potato Buddha Bowl

text:
Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Carrot and Lentil Soup with Coconut Milk

Ingredients:
- 1 lb carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch pieces
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp ground coriander
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk (full‑fat)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- 1 tbsp lime juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the carrot pieces with olive oil, half the cinnamon, and a pinch of salt; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until caramelized and tender.  
2. While the carrots roast, heat a large pot over medium heat. Add a drizzle of olive oil and sauté the onion until translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic, ginger, remaining cinnamon, cumin, and coriander; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
3. Add the rinsed lentils and vegetable broth to the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes.  
4. Transfer the roasted carrots to the pot. Using an immersion blender (or working in batches with a countertop blender), puree the soup until smooth.  
5. Stir in the coconut milk and lime juice, and season with salt and pepper to taste. Simmer gently for another 5 minutes to allow flavors to meld.  
6. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve hot. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Carrot and Lentil Soup with Coconut Milk

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea & Spinach Tacos

Ingredients:
- 8 small corn tortillas
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 ½ cans, drained and rinsed)
- 3 cups fresh baby spinach
- ½ cup coconut milk
- 2 Tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 small red onion, thinly sliced
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- 1 ripe avocado, sliced
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Heat 1 Tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the sliced red onion and sauté until softened, about 3 minutes.  
2. Stir in the minced garlic, turmeric, and cumin; cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.  
3. Add the chickpeas and coconut milk, stirring to coat. Simmer for 4‑5 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken slightly. Season with salt, pepper, and lime juice.  
4. Toss the fresh spinach into the skillet and cook just until wilted, about 1 minute. Remove from heat and stir in the chopped cilantro.  
5. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet or microwave for 20‑30 seconds until pliable.  
6. Spoon the chickpea‑spinach mixture evenly onto each tortilla. Top with avocado slices and an extra sprinkle of cilantro if desired.  
7. Serve immediately, optionally with lime wedges and a drizzle of hot sauce. Enjoy!
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea & Spinach Tacos

text:
Ginger‑Lime Baked Tofu with Coconut‑Basil Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 2 Tbsp soy sauce
- 1 Tbsp lime juice
- 1 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp sesame oil
- 1 cup jasmine rice
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup water
- ½ cup fresh basil leaves, chopped
- 1 Tbsp toasted coconut flakes
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 1 Tbsp olive oil for baking

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, whisk together soy sauce, lime juice, maple syrup, grated ginger, and sesame oil. Add the tofu cubes, toss to coat, and let marinate for 10 minutes.  
3. Spread the marinated tofu in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet, drizzle with olive oil, and bake for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.  
4. While the tofu bakes, combine jasmine rice, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.  
5. Remove the rice from heat and fluff with a fork. Stir in the chopped basil and toasted coconut flakes; season with additional salt and pepper if needed.  
6. To serve, spoon a generous portion of coconut‑basil quinoa onto each plate, top with baked ginger‑lime tofu, and garnish with extra basil leaves or a drizzle of lime juice if desired. Enjoy warm!
title: Ginger‑Lime Baked Tofu with Coconut‑Basil Quinoa

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Shrimp with Garlic‑Herb Couscous

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined  
- 1 cup coconut milk  
- 2 Tbsp fresh lime juice  
- 1 tsp ground turmeric  
- 3 cloves garlic, minced  
- 2 Tbsp olive oil  
- 1 cup couscous  
- 1 ½ cups water or low‑sodium vegetable broth  
- 2 Tbsp fresh parsley, chopped  
- ½ tsp sea salt, plus more to taste  
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper  

Instructions:
1. In a medium bowl, whisk together coconut milk, lime juice, turmeric, minced garlic, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Add the shrimp and toss to coat; let marinate for 10 minutes.  
2. While the shrimp marinates, bring the water or broth to a boil in a saucepan. Stir in the couscous, cover, and remove from heat. Let stand 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and stir in the chopped parsley.  
3. Heat a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the shrimp and any remaining marinade, spreading them in a single layer. Cook 2‑3 minutes per side, or until the shrimp turn pink and are just cooked through.  
4. Taste the sauce and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired.  
5. Spoon the garlic‑herb couscous onto serving plates, top with the turmeric‑lime shrimp, and drizzle any pan juices over the top.  
6. Garnish with extra parsley and a wedge of lime, if desired. Serve immediately.
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Shrimp with Garlic‑Herb Couscous

text:
Cinnamon‑Rosemary Roasted Carrot and Lentil Soup with Coconut Milk

Ingredients:
- 1 lb carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch pieces
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch piece fresh ginger, grated
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 tsp dried rosemary (or 1 tbsp fresh, chopped)
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk (full‑fat)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Juice of ½ lime (optional, for serving)
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the carrot pieces with 1 tbsp olive oil, half the cinnamon, half the rosemary, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring once, until caramelized and tender.  
2. While the carrots roast, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 4‑5 minutes, until translucent.  
3. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
4. Add the rinsed red lentils, roasted carrots (with any pan juices), the remaining cinnamon and rosemary, and the vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer.  
5. Cover and simmer for 15‑20 minutes, or until the lentils are soft and beginning to break down.  
6. Remove the pot from heat. Using an immersion blender, blend the soup until smooth and creamy; alternatively, transfer in batches to a countertop blender.  
7. Return the soup to low heat and stir in the coconut milk. Warm through for 3‑4 minutes; do not boil.  
8. Season with salt, pepper, and lime juice (if using). Adjust thickness with extra broth or water if needed.  
9. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves and a drizzle of coconut milk, if desired. Serve hot.
title: Cinnamon‑Rosemary Roasted Carrot and Lentil Soup with Coconut Milk

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Lentil and Spinach Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 tablespoon coconut oil
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 can (13.5 oz) coconut milk
- 3 cups vegetable broth
- 2 cups fresh spinach leaves, roughly chopped
- Juice of 1 lime
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Heat the coconut oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4–5 minutes.  
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for another minute until fragrant.  
3. Sprinkle the turmeric and cumin over the aromatics, stirring constantly for 30 seconds to toast the spices.  
4. Add the rinsed red lentils, coconut milk, and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to a gentle simmer.  
5. Cover and let the stew simmer for 15–20 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and have broken down, stirring occasionally.  
6. Stir in the chopped spinach and cook for 2–3 minutes, just until the leaves wilt.  
7. Remove the pot from heat and stir in the lime juice. Season with salt and pepper to taste.  
8. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve hot. Enjoy!
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Lentil and Spinach Stew

text:
Lemon‑Basil Quinoa with Roasted Sweet Potato and Feta

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 1 cup cherry tomatoes, halved
- ½ cup crumbled feta cheese
- ¼ cup fresh basil leaves, torn
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tsp lemon zest

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the sweet potato cubes with olive oil, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and caramelized.
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes or until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
3. In a large bowl, mix the roasted sweet potatoes, cherry tomatoes, lemon juice, lemon zest, and half of the torn basil; toss gently.
4. Add the cooked quinoa to the bowl and stir until everything is evenly combined.
5. Transfer the mixture to serving plates, sprinkle crumbled feta over the top, and garnish with the remaining fresh basil.
6. Serve warm or at room temperature, optionally drizzling a little extra olive oil or a squeeze of lemon for added brightness.
title: Lemon‑Basil Quinoa with Roasted Sweet Potato and Feta

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Quinoa with Roasted Broccolini and Toasted Almonds

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- ½ teaspoon ground turmeric
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice
- 1 bunch broccolini, trimmed into 2‑inch pieces
- 2 tablespoons sliced almonds
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the broccolini with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread in a single layer on the prepared sheet. Roast for 12‑15 minutes, until tender‑crisp and lightly browned.  
3. While the broccolini roasts, combine quinoa, coconut milk, turmeric, and a pinch of salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy.  
4. Remove the quinoa from heat and stir in lime zest and lime juice. Adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed.  
5. In a small skillet over medium heat, add the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil and the sliced almonds. Toast, stirring frequently, until golden and fragrant, about 3 minutes; set aside.  
6. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large bowl, fold in the roasted broccolini, and sprinkle with toasted almonds.  
7. Garnish with chopped cilantro, if desired, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Quinoa with Roasted Broccolini and Toasted Almonds

text:
Garlic‑Lime Roasted Cauliflower Steaks with Quinoa‑Pomegranate Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 large cauliflower head
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 Tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tsp lime zest
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups low‑sodium vegetable broth or water
- 1/4 cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- 1 Tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Slice the cauliflower into 3/4‑inch thick “steaks” by cutting from top to bottom; you should get 2–3 usable steaks.  
3. In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, minced garlic, lime juice, lime zest, salt, and pepper.  
4. Brush both sides of each cauliflower steak with the garlic‑lime mixture and place them on the prepared baking sheet.  
5. Roast for 20–25 minutes, flipping halfway through, until the edges are golden and the stems are tender.  
6. While the cauliflower ro
title: Garlic‑Lime Roasted Cauliflower Steaks with Quinoa‑Pomegranate Salad

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Power Bowl with Avocado Lime Dressing

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 cup cooked quinoa
- 1 avocado, sliced
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, cinnamon, smoked paprika, 1 tbsp maple syrup
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Power Bowl with Avocado Lime Dressing

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Quinoa with Roasted Cauliflower and Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth or water
- 1 medium cauliflower head, cut into florets
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 lemon (zest and juice)
- 1 garlic clove, minced
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 tbsp toasted almond slivers (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss cauliflower florets with 1 tbsp olive oil, half the turmeric, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender.
2. While the cauliflower roasts, combine quinoa and broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, grated ginger, lemon zest, lemon juice, minced garlic, the remaining turmeric, and a pinch of salt to create the dressing.
4. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl. Add the roasted cauliflower, drizzle the lemon‑ginger‑turmeric dressing over, and toss gently to combine.
5. Fold in the pomegranate seeds and toasted almond slivers, if using, for extra crunch and color.
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice as desired. Serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Quinoa with Roasted Cauliflower and Pomegranate

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea and Sweet Potato Skillet

Ingredients:
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and diced
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp freshly grated ginger
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 1 cup fresh spinach leaves
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro (optional)

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
2. Add the diced sweet potato and sauté for 8‑10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it begins to soften and turn golden.
3. Stir in the minced garlic, grated ginger, and ground turmeric; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Add the chickpeas, lemon zest, salt, and pepper; toss to coat and continue cooking for another 5 minutes, allowing the chickpeas to heat through and the sweet potatoes to become tender.
5. Pour in the lemon juice, stir, and let the mixture simmer for 2 minutes so the flavors meld.
6. Fold in the fresh spinach and cook until wilted, about 1 minute.
7. Remove from heat, sprinkle with chopped cilantro if using, and serve hot.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea and Sweet Potato Skillet

text:
Spiced Apricot Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 cup dried apricots, chopped
- 1/2 cup roasted chickpeas
- 1/4 cup toasted almonds, sliced
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro, chopped (optional garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the chickpeas with 1 tablespoon olive oil, a pinch of salt, and half the cumin; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking halfway, until crisp.  
2. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa and water (or broth); bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.  
3. While the quinoa cooks, heat the remaining olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the chopped apricots, maple syrup, cinnamon, and the remaining cumin; sauté 3‑4 minutes until the apricots are glossy and slightly caramelized.  
4. Stir the roasted chickpeas, toasted almonds, and a pinch of salt and pepper into the cooked quinoa; fold in the apricot mixture until evenly distributed.  
5. Transfer the quinoa mixture to a serving bowl, drizzle with a little extra olive oil if desired, and garnish with fresh cilantro.  
6. Serve warm or at room temperature as a hearty main or side dish.
title: Spiced Apricot Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Parsnip and Lentil Soup with Coconut Milk

Ingredients:
- 2 large parsnips, peeled and diced
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 can (13.5 oz) coconut milk
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 in piece fresh ginger, grated
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- ½ tsp ground cinnamon
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Optional: a squeeze of lime juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Toss the diced parsnips with 1 tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of maple syrup; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway, until caramelized and tender.  
2. While the parsnips roast, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté for 4‑5 minutes until translucent.  
3. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
4. Add the cumin, coriander, and ground cinnamon; toast the spices for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.  
5. Pour in the vegetable broth and coconut milk, scraping any bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil.  
6. Add the rinsed red lentils and the roasted parsnips (including any pan juices) to the pot. Reduce heat to a simmer and cook, uncovered, for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils are soft and the soup has thickened.  
7. Season with salt, pepper, and the remaining maple syrup to balance acidity; adjust seasoning as needed. If you like a smoother texture, blend half of the soup with an immersion blender, then stir it back into the pot.  
8. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and optionally finish with a squeeze of lime juice for brightness. Enjoy hot!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Parsnip and Lentil Soup with Coconut Milk

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Lentil Power Bowl

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and sliced into 1/4‑inch rounds
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 1/2 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/2 teaspoon ground coriander
- 2 cups fresh baby spinach
- 2 tablespoons toasted pumpkin seeds
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, olive oil, cinnamon, cumin, coriander, salt, and pepper. Add the carrot rounds and toss to coat evenly.  
3. Spread the carrots in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and caramelized.  
4. While the carrots roast, combine lentils and 2 cups water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 20‑25 minutes until lentils are tender but not mushy. Drain any excess liquid.  
5. In a separate pot, bring 1 cup water to a boil, add quinoa, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed and quinoa is fluffy. Fluff with a fork.  
6. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked lentils, quinoa, and fresh spinach. Drizzle with lemon juice and toss gently to wilt the spinach slightly.  
7. Divide the spinach‑lentil‑quinoa mixture into serving bowls. Top each bowl with the roasted carrots, sprinkle with toasted pumpkin seeds, and finish with an extra pinch of salt and pepper if desired.  
8. Serve warm or at room temperature, enjoying the sweet‑spicy flavor and hearty texture.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Lentil Power Bowl

text:
Spiced Cardamom Coconut Rice with Roasted Veggies

Ingredients:
- 1 cup basmati rice
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- ½ cup water
- 1 teaspoon ground cardamom
- ½ teaspoon sea salt
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 red bell pepper, sliced
- 1 small zucchini, diced
- 1 cup cauliflower florets
- 2 green onions, sliced
- 1 tablespoon toasted coconut flakes (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the red bell pepper, zucchini, and cauliflower with olive oil and a pinch of salt; spread them on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
3. While the vegetables roast, rinse the basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear.  
4. In a medium saucepan, combine the coconut milk, water, ground cardamom, and sea salt; bring to a gentle boil.  
5. Add the rinsed rice, stir once, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is fluffy.  
6. Remove the rice from heat and let it sit, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.  
7. Gently fold the roasted vegetables into the spiced coconut rice, mixing until evenly distributed.  
8. Transfer the rice and vegetable mixture to a serving bowl, garnish with sliced green onions and toasted coconut flakes if desired.  
9. Serve warm as a hearty main dish or a flavorful side. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Cardamom Coconut Rice with Roasted Veggies

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa with Roasted Beet and Feta

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 medium beets, peeled and cubed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tbsp lemon juice
- ½ cup crumbled feta cheese
- 1 cup arugula or baby spinach
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the cubed beets with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, salt, and pepper, then spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, or until tender and slightly caramelized. Set aside to cool slightly.  
2. While the beets roast, combine the quinoa and water (or broth) in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
3. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, grated ginger, lemon zest, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt and pepper to create the dressing.  
4. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl. Add the roasted beets, arugula (or spinach), and the lemon‑ginger dressing. Toss gently to combine, ensuring the beets are evenly distributed.  
5. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if desired.  
6. Divide the quinoa mixture among serving bowls and sprinkle each with crumbled feta cheese. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa with Roasted Beet and Feta

text:
Saffron‑Honey Roasted Carrot and Lentil Salad with Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch sticks
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- ½ teaspoon saffron threads
- 2 tablespoons honey
- 3 tablespoons olive oil, divided
- ½ teaspoon sea salt, plus more to taste
- ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 tablespoons sliced toasted almonds
- 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, chopped
- 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, combine the saffron threads with 1 tablespoon of hot water; let steep for 5 minutes.  
3. In a large mixing bowl, toss the carrot sticks with 2 tablespoons of olive oil, honey, the saffron infusion, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
4. Spread the carrots in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
5. While the carrots roast, place the lentils in a saucepan with 2 cups of water. Bring to a boil
title: Saffron‑Honey Roasted Carrot and Lentil Salad with Pomegranate

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Chickpea and Quinoa Power Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 tablespoon coconut oil
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1 tablespoon lime juice
- 1 teaspoon lime zest
- ½ cup coconut milk
- 1 cup shredded red cabbage, thinly sliced
- 1 medium carrot, julienned
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa and water (or broth); bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and fluff with a fork.
2. While quinoa cooks, heat coconut oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add chickpeas, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; sauté 5‑7 minutes until lightly browned.
3. Stir in lime juice, lime zest, and coconut milk; cook another 2 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken and coat the chickpeas. Adjust seasoning as needed.
4. Assemble the bowl: place a bed of cooked quinoa, top with spiced chickpeas, shredded cabbage, carrot ribbons, and a sprinkle of fresh cilantro.
5. Drizzle any remaining sauce from the pan over the bowl, add an extra squeeze of lime if desired, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Chickpea and Quinoa Power Bowl

text:
Maple‑Glazed Chickpea and Sweet Potato Tostada with Avocado Crema  

Ingredients:
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and diced
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- 4 small corn tortillas
- 1 ripe avocado
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 2 tbsp plain Greek yogurt or vegan yogurt
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the diced sweet potato with 1 tbsp maple syrup, smoked paprika, cumin, cayenne, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until tender and caramelized.
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine the chickpeas with the remaining 1 tbsp maple syrup, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of olive oil; spread on a second baking sheet and roast for 15‑18 minutes, stirring halfway, until crisp.
3. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 30 seconds per side, or until pliable.
4. Assemble the avocado crema: mash the avocado with lime juice, yogurt, a pinch of salt, and a splash of water to reach a drizzle‑able consistency.
5. To build each tostada, layer roasted sweet potatoes and crispy chickpeas on a tortilla, drizzle generously with avocado crema, and sprinkle with chopped cilantro.
6. Serve immediately, adding extra lime wedges or hot sauce if desired. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Chickpea and Sweet Potato Tostada with Avocado Crema

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Power Bowl with Lime Yogurt Drizzle

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 cup cooked quinoa
- 1 avocado, sliced
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- ½ cup plain Greek yogurt
- 1 Tbsp lime juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp cinnamon, ½ tsp smoked paprika, 1 Tbsp maple syrup, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
3. In the same bowl, toss the chickpeas with the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, the remaining ½ tsp smoked paprika, 1 Tbsp maple syrup, and a pinch of salt. Add them to the baking sheet beside the sweet potatoes.  
4. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway through, until the sweet potatoes are tender and caramelized and the chickpeas are crisp.  
5. While the vegetables roast, prepare the lime yogurt drizzle: whisk together the Greek yogurt, lime juice, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of maple syrup if desired. Set aside.  
6. Assemble the bowls: start with a base of cooked quinoa, top with roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas, add avocado slices, and sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds.  
7. Drizzle the lime yogurt sauce over the bowl, garnish with fresh cilantro, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Power Bowl with Lime Yogurt Drizzle

text:
Ginger‑Lime Coconut Shrimp with Quinoa Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 tbsp coconut oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tbsp lime juice
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1 small carrot, peeled and diced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Optional: crushed red pepper flakes for heat

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa, water, and a pinch of salt; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and fluff with a fork. Stir in ½ cup coconut milk, cover, and let sit 5 minutes.
2. While quinoa cooks, heat coconut oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add garlic and ginger; sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
3. Add the shrimp to the skillet, season with salt, pepper, and optional red pepper flakes. Cook 2‑3 minutes per side until pink and opaque. Remove shrimp and set aside.
4. In the same skillet, add the diced red bell pepper and carrot; sauté 4‑5 minutes until just tender.
5. Return the shrimp to the pan, pour in lime zest, lime juice, and the remaining ½ cup coconut milk. Stir to combine and simmer 2‑3 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken slightly.
6. Serve the shrimp and vegetable mixture over the coconut‑infused quinoa, garnish with fresh cilantro, and enjoy immediately.
title: Ginger‑Lime Coconut Shrimp with Quinoa Pilaf

text:
Spiced Orange‑Maple Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Broccoli

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 large head broccoli, cut into florets
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- Zest of 1 orange
- 1 tbsp fresh orange juice
- 1 cup cooked chickpeas (canned, drained and rinsed)
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 2 tbsp toasted sliced almonds (optional)
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the broccoli florets with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, half the minced garlic, a pinch of salt, and pepper; spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
3. Roast the broccoli for 18‑20 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until tender‑crisp and lightly caramelized.  
4. While the broccoli roasts, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the grains are fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining olive oil, maple syrup, orange zest, orange juice, the remaining minced garlic, and a pinch of salt.  
6. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl; add the roasted broccoli, chickpeas, and the maple‑orange dressing. Toss gently to combine, adjusting seasoning with extra salt or pepper if needed.  
7. Divide the quinoa mixture among serving bowls, sprinkle with toasted almonds and chopped parsley, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Spiced Orange‑Maple Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Broccoli

text:
Roasted Garlic and Lime Quinoa with Pan‑Seared Miso Tofu

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tbsp lime juice
- 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
- 14 oz firm tofu, pressed and cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 tbsp white miso paste
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 2 green onions, thinly sliced (white and green parts separated)
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine the rinsed quinoa and water; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until the water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
2. While the quinoa cooks, heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the minced garlic and the white parts of the green onions; sauté 1‑2 minutes until fragrant but not browned.  
3. Stir the lime zest, lime juice, and a pinch of salt into the cooked quinoa; fold in the sautéed garlic mixture. Keep warm on low heat.  
4. In a small bowl whisk together miso paste, soy sauce, grated ginger, and the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil to form a glaze.  
5. Pat the tofu cubes dry with paper towels. Add them to the same skillet (or a clean non‑stick pan) over medium‑high heat. Cook 3‑4 minutes per side until golden and crisp.  
6. Pour the miso‑soy glaze over the tofu, tossing gently to coat. Cook an additional 1‑2 minutes until the glaze thickens and clings to the tofu.  
7. To serve, spoon a bed of the roasted garlic‑lime quinoa onto plates, top with the pan‑seared miso tofu, and garnish with the green parts of the sliced green onions and chopped cilantro. Season with extra salt and pepper if desired. Enjoy!
title: Roasted Garlic and Lime Quinoa with Pan‑Seared Miso Tofu

text:
Maple‑Glazed Cauliflower and Chickpea Tacos with Avocado Crema

Ingredients:
- 1 small head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 8 small corn tortillas
- 1 ripe avocado
- 1 Tbsp lime juice
- 1 tsp honey
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- Lime wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, cayenne, salt, and pepper.  
3. Add the cauliflower florets and chickpeas to the bowl, toss to coat evenly, and spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway through, until the cauliflower is golden‑brown and tender and the chickpeas are crisp.  
5. While the vegetables roast, prepare the avocado crema: combine the avocado, lime juice, honey, a pinch of salt, and a splash of water in a blender; blend until smooth and creamy. Adjust seasoning as needed.  
6. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 30 seconds per side, or wrap them in foil and heat in the oven for the last 5 minutes of roasting.  
7. To assemble each taco, place a generous spoonful of the roasted cauliflower and chickpeas onto a tortilla, drizzle with avocado crema, sprinkle with chopped cilantro and feta (if using), and finish with a squeeze of fresh lime juice.  
8. Serve immediately with extra lime wedges on the side. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Cauliflower and Chickpea Tacos with Avocado Crema

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Roasted Cauliflower and Lentil Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 large head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 lemon, zest and juice
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, minced
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- ¼ cup toasted slivered almonds
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a large bowl, toss the cauliflower florets with 1 tbsp olive oil, minced ginger, garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.
3. Spread the cauliflower on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden‑brown and tender.
4. While the cauliflower roasts, combine the rinsed lentils, vegetable broth, lemon zest, and a pinch of salt in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils are cooked through and the liquid is absorbed.
5. Remove the roasted cauliflower from the oven and drizzle with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, lemon juice, and a sprinkle of additional salt and pepper; toss gently to combine.
6. Fold the roasted cauliflower into the cooked lentils, mixing gently to distribute evenly.
7. Transfer the pilaf to a serving bowl, top with toasted slivered almonds and fresh cilantro leaves, and serve warm.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Roasted Cauliflower and Lentil Pilaf

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Sesame Noodles with Roasted Tofu

Ingredients:
- 8 oz (225 g) rice noodles or spaghetti
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 Tbsp sesame oil
- 2 Tbsp soy sauce (or tamari for gluten‑free)
- 1 Tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 Tbsp honey or maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp freshly grated ginger
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp chili flakes (optional)
- 3 Tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- 2 green onions, thinly sliced
- 1 cup shredded carrots
- 1 cup snap peas, trimmed
- 1 Tbsp vegetable oil
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Lime wedges for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Toss the tofu cubes with 1 Tbsp sesame oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper, then spread them on a parchment‑lined baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
2. While the tofu roasts, cook the noodles according to package directions until al dente. Drain, rinse under cold water, and set aside.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey, grated ginger, minced garlic, chili flakes (if using), and the remaining 1 Tbsp sesame oil to create the dressing.
4. Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the shredded carrots and snap peas, sautéing for 3‑4 minutes until just tender but still crisp.
5. Add the cooked noodles to the skillet, pour the dressing over them, and toss everything together for 1‑2 minutes, allowing the noodles to absorb the sauce.
6. Gently fold in the roasted tofu cubes, toasted sesame seeds, and sliced green onions. Taste and adjust seasoning with extra soy sauce or a squeeze of lime if desired.
7. Serve the noodles in bowls, garnished with additional sesame seeds, green onions, and lime wedges on the side for extra brightness. Enjoy warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Sesame Noodles with Roasted Tofu

text:
Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 1 cup cooked quinoa
- ½ cup diced cucumber
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 tbsp tahini
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- Fresh mint leaves for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cauliflower florets and chickpeas with olive oil, cinnamon, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway through, until the cauliflower is golden and the chickpeas are crisp.  
4. While the vegetables roast, prepare the dressing by whisking together tahini, lemon juice, maple syrup, a pinch of salt, and enough water to reach a drizzle‑able consistency.  
5. Assemble the bowls: start with a base of cooked quinoa, top with roasted cauliflower and chickpeas, then add cucumber dice and pomegranate seeds.  
6. Drizzle the tahini‑lemon dressing over each bowl and garnish with fresh mint leaves. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

text:
Spiced Cardamom Sweet Potato and Chickpea Stew

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp ground cardamom
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- 1 can (14 oz) coconut milk
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Juice of 1 lime
- Fresh cilantro leaves for garnish

Instructions:
1. Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.  
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
3. Sprinkle in the ground cardamom, cumin, and smoked paprika; toast the spices for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.  
4. Add the cubed sweet potatoes and chickpeas, tossing to coat them evenly with the spice mixture.  
5. Pour in the coconut milk and vegetable broth, bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer.  
6. Cover the pot and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the sweet potatoes are tender.  
7. Season the stew with salt, pepper, and the juice of one lime; adjust seasoning to taste.  
8. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve hot.
title: Spiced Cardamom Sweet Potato and Chickpea Stew

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Shrimp with Herbed Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch piece fresh ginger, grated
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa, vegetable broth, and coconut milk; bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is tender. Remove from heat and fluff with a fork; stir in half of the chopped cilantro and season with salt and pepper. Set aside, keeping it warm.
2. While the quinoa cooks, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger, sautéing for 30 seconds until fragrant.
3. Sprinkle the turmeric over the shrimp, then add the shrimp to the skillet in a single layer. Cook for 2‑3 minutes per side, or until the shrimp turn pink and opaque.
4. Pour the lime juice over the cooked shrimp, toss to coat, and remove the skillet from heat.
5. To serve, spoon a bed of herbed quinoa onto each plate, top with the turmeric‑lime shrimp, and garnish with the remaining cilantro. Adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired. Enjoy!
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Shrimp with Herbed Quinoa

text:
Spiced Cardamom Coconut Lentil and Kale Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 tablespoon coconut oil
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground cardamom
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper (optional)
- 1 large carrot, diced
- 1 cup chopped kale, stems removed
- 1 can (14 oz) coconut milk
- 3 cups vegetable broth
- Salt and black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Lime wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Rinse the lentils under cold water and set aside.  
2. Heat the coconut oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for about 5 minutes, until translucent.  
3. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
4. Sprinkle in the ground cardamom, cumin, turmeric, and cayenne pepper; toast the spices for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.  
5. Add the diced carrot and rinsed lentils, stirring to coat them with the spiced onion mixture.  
6. Pour in the vegetable broth and coconut milk, bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to a gentle simmer.  
7. Simmer uncovered for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are tender and the stew has thickened slightly.  
8. Add the chopped kale and cook for an additional 5 minutes, or until the kale is wilted but still bright green.  
9. Season the stew with salt and black pepper to taste.  
10. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro, and serve with lime wedges on the side for a bright finish.
title: Spiced Cardamom Coconut Lentil and Kale Stew

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea and Quinoa Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup coconut milk (full‑fat)
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 small onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional: 2 tablespoons toasted sliced almonds for garnish

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea and Quinoa Pilaf

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Pumpkin and Quinoa Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 small pumpkin, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp saffron threads, steeped in 2 tbsp warm water
- 1 small onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss pumpkin cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast 20‑25 minutes until tender and caramelized.  
2. While pumpkin roasts, heat remaining olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in garlic, cumin, and smoked paprika; cook 1 minute until fragrant.  
3. Add quinoa to the saucepan, stirring to coat with spices. Pour in vegetable broth and the saffron infusion; bring to a boil.  
4. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until quinoa is fluffy and liquid absorbed.  
5. Fluff quinoa with a fork and gently fold in the roasted pumpkin. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.  
6. Serve warm, garnished with chopped parsley.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Pumpkin and Quinoa Pilaf

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Soup

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch pieces
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch piece fresh ginger, grated
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- ½ tsp ground cinnamon
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the carrot pieces with 1 tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, and a pinch of salt; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, until caramelized and tender.  
2. While the carrots roast, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 5 minutes, until translucent.  
3. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1‑2 minutes until fragrant.  
4. Add the roasted carrots and chickpeas to the pot, then pour in the vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes to meld flavors.  
5. Using an immersion blender (or transferring to a countertop blender in batches), puree the soup until smooth and creamy.  
6. Return the soup to the pot if needed, stir in the coconut milk, and season with salt and pepper to taste. Heat gently for another 2‑3 minutes, avoiding a rapid boil.  
7. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve hot. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Soup

text:
Crispy Coconut‑Lime Tofu with Pineapple Salsa

Ingredients:
- 1 block (14 oz) firm tofu, pressed and cut into ½‑inch cubes
- ½ cup unsweetened shredded coconut
- 2 tbsp lime zest
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tbsp cornstarch
- ¼ cup all‑purpose flour
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 1 cup fresh pineapple, diced
- ¼ cup red bell pepper, finely diced
- 2 tbsp red onion, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 tbsp honey or agave syrup
- 1 tsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp sesame oil
- 2 tbsp vegetable oil (for frying)

Instructions:
1. In a large bowl, combine the shredded coconut, lime zest, flour, cornstarch, salt, and pepper.
2. Toss the tofu cubes in the mixture, ensuring each piece is evenly coated; set aside.
3. Heat the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the coated tofu and fry for 3‑4 minutes per side, or until golden and crisp. Transfer to a paper‑towel‑lined plate to drain excess oil.
4. While the tofu cooks, prepare the pineapple salsa: in a separate bowl, combine diced pineapple, red bell pepper, red onion, cilantro, honey, soy sauce, lime juice, and sesame oil. Mix gently until well incorporated.
5. Let the salsa sit for 5 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
6. To serve, arrange the crispy tofu on a plate, spoon the pineapple salsa over the top, and garnish with an extra sprinkle of lime zest if desired. Enjoy warm or at room temperature.
title: Crispy Coconut‑Lime Tofu with Pineapple Salsa

text:
Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Curry

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tbsp coconut oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- 1 can (14 oz) coconut milk
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- 1 tbsp tomato paste
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)
- Cooked basmati rice or quinoa, for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 tbsp coconut oil, ½ tsp cinnamon, ½ tsp cumin, and a pinch of salt; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add the remaining ½ tbsp coconut oil and sauté the onion until translucent, about 5 minutes.
3. Stir in the garlic, ginger, remaining cinnamon, cumin, smoked paprika, and cayenne (if using); cook for 1‑2 minutes until fragrant.
4. Add the tomato paste, stirring to combine, then pour in the coconut milk and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.
5. Add the roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas to the skillet. Stir to coat everything evenly with the sauce.
6. Simmer the curry for 10‑12 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken slightly. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
7. Serve the curry over cooked basmati rice or quinoa, and garnish with fresh cilantro. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Curry

text:
Saffron‑Infused Coconut Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Lime  

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups coconut milk (full‑fat)
- ½ teaspoon saffron threads
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Zest of 1 lime
- Juice of 1 lime
- 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, chopped
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds (optional)

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, combine the saffron threads with 2 tablespoons of hot water; let steep for 5 minutes.  
2. In a medium saucepan, bring the coconut milk to a gentle simmer. Stir in the soaked saffron (including the liquid) and the rinsed quinoa. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15‑18 minutes, or until the quinoa is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
3. While the quinoa cooks, preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the chickpeas with olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on a baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until the chickpeas are golden and crisp.  
4. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl. Add the lime zest, lime juice, and half of the chopped cilantro; toss gently to combine.  
5. Fold the roasted chickpeas into the quinoa mixture. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired.  
6. Serve the saffron‑infused quinoa in bowls, garnished with the remaining cilantro, toasted pumpkin seeds, and an extra drizzle of lime juice if you like extra brightness. Enjoy warm or at room temperature.
title: Saffron‑Infused Coconut Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Lime

text:
Spiced Cardamom Pumpkin and Chickpea Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 lb (450 g) canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 cups (500 g) diced pumpkin or butternut squash
- 1 large onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp ground cardamom
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- 4 cups (1 L) vegetable broth
- 1 can (14 oz/400 ml) coconut milk
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- 1 tbsp lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
2. Stir in the garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Sprinkle the ground cardamom, cumin, smoked paprika, and cayenne (if using) over the aromatics. Toast the spices for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
4. Add the diced pumpkin and chickpeas to the pot, mixing to coat them with the spice blend.
5. Pour in the vegetable broth and bring the mixture to a gentle boil. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15‑20 minutes, or until the pumpkin is tender.
6. Stir in the coconut milk and lemon juice, then season with salt and pepper to taste. Simmer for an additional 5 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
7. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve hot.
title: Spiced Cardamom Pumpkin and Chickpea Stew

text:
Spiced Cardamom Coconut Chickpea and Sweet Potato Curry

Ingredients:
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 can (13.5 oz) coconut milk
- 1 large onion, finely chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch piece fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp ground cardamom
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 cup diced tomatoes (canned or fresh)
- 2 cups fresh spinach leaves
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Cooked basmati rice or quinoa, for serving

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until translucent, about 4‑5 minutes.  
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for another 1 minute until fragrant.  
3. Sprinkle the ground cardamom, cumin, and smoked paprika over the aromatics; toast the spices for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.  
4. Add the diced sweet potatoes and diced tomatoes to the pan, mixing to coat them with the spice blend.  
5. Pour in the coconut milk and bring the mixture to a gentle simmer. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and cook for 15‑20 minutes, or until the sweet potatoes are tender.  
6. Stir in the cooked chickpeas and let them heat through, about 3‑4 minutes.  
7. Fold in the fresh spinach leaves and cook until wilted, roughly 2 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste.  
8. Serve the curry over cooked basmati rice or quinoa, and garnish each bowl with a sprinkle of fresh cilantro leaves. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Cardamom Coconut Chickpea and Sweet Potato Curry

text:
Cinnamon‑Saffron Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Tagine

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch chunks
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 medium onion, finely diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 in piece fresh ginger, grated
- 1 ½ cups vegetable broth
- 1 (14‑oz) can diced tomatoes
- ½ tsp ground cinnamon
- ¼ tsp saffron threads, soaked in 2 tbsp warm water
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp ground coriander
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)
- 2 tbsp toasted slivered almonds (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the carrot chunks with 1 tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.
2. While the carrots roast, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large oven‑safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 4‑5 minutes, until translucent.
3. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for another minute until fragrant.
4. Add the ground cinnamon, cumin, coriander, and the soaked saffron with its liquid. Stir to coat the aromatics and toast the spices for 30 seconds.
5. Pour in the diced tomatoes (with their juices) and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then add the roasted carrots and chickpeas.
6. Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven and bake, uncovered, for 15‑20 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken slightly.
7. Remove from the oven, taste, and adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.
8. Serve the tagine hot, garnished with chopped cilantro and toasted slivered almonds for crunch. Enjoy with couscous, quinoa, or warm flatbread.
title: Cinnamon‑Saffron Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Tagine

text:
Rosemary‑Lemon Quinoa with Roasted Cauliflower and Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 medium head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 tsp fresh rosemary, finely chopped
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- ½ cup pomegranate seeds
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the cauliflower florets with 1 tbsp olive oil, rosemary, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender.
2. While the cauliflower roasts, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of pepper.
4. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl, drizzle with the lemon‑olive oil dressing, and toss to combine.
5. Gently fold the roasted cauliflower and pomegranate seeds into the quinoa mixture. Adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.
6. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with an extra sprinkle of fresh rosemary if desired.
title: Rosemary‑Lemon Quinoa with Roasted Cauliflower and Pomegranate

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Chickpea Power Salad with Orange Vinaigrette

Ingredients:
- 3 medium beets, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- 2 tablespoons olive oil, divided
- 4 cups mixed baby greens
- ½ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese
- 1 orange, zest and juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cubed beets with 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1 tablespoon maple syrup, ground cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning once, until tender and caramelized.  
3. While the beets roast, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the chickpeas and drizzle with the remaining 1 tablespoon maple syrup; sauté for 5‑7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chickpeas are golden and slightly crisp. Season with a pinch of salt.  
4. In a small bowl, whisk together the orange zest, orange juice, 1 tablespoon olive oil, and a pinch of salt and pepper to create the vinaigrette. Adjust seasoning to taste.  
5. In a large salad bowl, combine the mixed baby greens, roasted beets, maple‑glazed chickpeas, toasted pumpkin seeds, and crumbled feta.  
6. Drizzle the orange vinaigrette over the salad and toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly.  
7. Serve immediately, garnished with an extra sprinkle of pumpkin seeds or a few orange zest curls if desired.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Chickpea Power Salad with Orange Vinaigrette

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Coconut Chickpea Curry with Brown Rice

Ingredients:
- 1 cup brown rice
- 1 ½ cups water (for rice)
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 can (13.5 oz) coconut milk
- 1 large carrot, sliced thin
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1 small onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- ½ tsp turmeric
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves for garnish
- Lemon zest for garnish

Instructions:
1. Rinse the brown rice under cold water, then combine with 1 ½ cups water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 35‑40 minutes until tender; fluff with a fork and set aside.
2. While the rice cooks, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté for 3‑4 minutes until translucent.
3. Stir in the garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Add the carrot and red bell pepper; sauté for 4‑5 minutes until they begin to soften.
5. Sprinkle the cumin, coriander, turmeric, and cayenne (if using) over the vegetables; stir to coat evenly and toast the spices for 30 seconds.
6. Pour in the coconut milk and bring the mixture to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low and let it cook for 5 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken slightly.
7. Add the chickpeas, lemon juice, and lemon zest; stir well and simmer for another 3‑4 minutes until the chickpeas are heated through. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
8. Spoon the coconut chickpea curry over a bed of brown rice, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves and an extra drizzle of lemon juice if desired. Serve hot.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Coconut Chickpea Curry with Brown Rice

text:
Roasted Garlic‑Lime Chickpea & Sweet Potato Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- Zest and juice of 1 lime
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 2 cups cooked quinoa
- 1 avocado, sliced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 2 tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, half the minced garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper; spread them in a single layer on the baking sheet.  
3. Roast the sweet potatoes for 20 minutes, then flip them over.  
4. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine the chickpeas with the remaining olive oil, garlic, lime zest, lime juice, and a pinch of salt; add them to the baking sheet and roast for another 15 minutes, stirring once halfway through.  
5. Remove both vegetables from the oven; let them cool slightly.  
6. Assemble the bowls: start with a base of cooked quinoa, then top with roasted sweet potatoes, chickpeas, avocado slices, and a sprinkle of cilantro.  
7. Drizzle any remaining lime‑garlic sauce from the pan over the bowl and garnish with toasted pumpkin seeds.  
8. Serve warm or at room temperature, enjoying the bright, smoky flavors in every bite.
title: Roasted Garlic‑Lime Chickpea & Sweet Potato Buddha Bowl

text:
Saffron‑Infused Chickpea and Roasted Butternut Squash Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups vegetable broth
- 1 medium butternut squash, peeled and cubed (about 2 cups)
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp ground coriander
- ¼ tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp saffron threads, steeped in 2 tbsp hot water
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Juice of ½ lemon

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the cubed butternut squash with 1 tbsp olive oil, cumin, coriander, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
2. While the squash roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.  
3. In a skillet over medium heat, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil. Add the chickpeas and sauté 5‑6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they develop a golden crust. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.  
4. Stir the steeped saffron (including the liquid) into the cooked quinoa, mixing until the grains are evenly colored.  
5. Gently fold the roasted butternut squash, sautéed chickpeas, toasted pumpkin seeds, and chopped parsley into the saffron‑infused quinoa. Adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, and lemon juice to taste.  
6. Serve warm or at room temperature as a hearty side dish or a light main course. Enjoy!
title: Saffron‑Infused Chickpea and Roasted Butternut Squash Pilaf

text:
Maple‑Miso Glazed Eggplant with Turmeric Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 2 medium eggplants, sliced into ½‑inch rounds
- 3 Tbsp maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp white miso paste
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- ½ tsp salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, miso paste, olive oil, minced garlic, grated ginger, and ground turmeric until smooth.  
3. Brush both sides of each eggplant slice with the maple‑miso glaze, placing them on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast the eggplant for 20‑25 minutes, flipping halfway through, until the slices are tender and caramelized.  
5. While the eggplant roasts, combine the rinsed quinoa, vegetable broth, salt, and pepper in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy.  
6. Remove the quinoa from heat and stir in 1 tsp of the remaining glaze (if any) for extra flavor; fluff with a fork.  
7. To serve, arrange a bed of turmeric quinoa on each plate, top with the roasted eggplant slices, and drizzle any pan‑collected juices over the top.  
8. Garnish with chopped cilantro, if desired, and enjoy warm.
title: Maple‑Miso Glazed Eggplant with Turmeric Quinoa

text:
Maple‑Glazed Shrimp and Coconut Lime Quinoa Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup water
- 12 large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 red bell pepper, thinly sliced
- 1 cup snap peas, trimmed
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
2. While the quinoa cooks, whisk together maple syrup, lime juice, grated ginger, and minced garlic in a small bowl; set aside.
3. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the shrimp, season with salt and pepper, and sauté for 2 minutes per side, or until pink and opaque. Remove shrimp from the pan and set aside.
4. In the same skillet, add the sliced red bell pepper and snap peas. Stir‑fry for 3‑4 minutes until crisp‑tender. Return the shrimp to the pan, pour the maple‑lime glaze over everything, and toss to coat. Cook for an additional minute to heat through and allow the glaze to thicken slightly.
5. Fluff the cooked quinoa with a fork and divide it among four serving bowls. Top each bowl with the glazed shrimp and vegetable mixture.
