6. Garnish each bowl with chopped cilantro and an extra drizzle of lime juice, if desired. Serve warm.
title: Maple‑Glazed Shrimp and Coconut Lime Quinoa Bowl

text:
Spiced Orange‑Lime Chickpea and Farro Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup farro
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 orange, zest and juice
- 1 lime, zest and juice
- 2 tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Rinse the farro under cold water, then place it in a saucepan with 2 cups water; bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook until tender, about 25 minutes. Drain any excess liquid and let cool slightly.  
2. While the farro cooks, combine the chickpeas, orange zest, lime zest, and chopped cilantro in a large mixing bowl.  
3. In a small bowl, whisk together the orange juice, lime juice, olive oil, ground cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until emulsified.  
4. Add the cooked farro to the chickpea mixture, pour the dressing over everything, and toss gently to coat evenly.  
5. Sprinkle the toasted pumpkin seeds on top, give a final light toss, and serve the salad at room temperature or chilled.
title: Spiced Orange‑Lime Chickpea and Farro Salad

text:
Garlic‑Rosemary Roasted Eggplant and Lentil Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cubed
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp fresh rosemary, finely chopped
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 1/4 cup toasted pine nuts
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- Zest of 1 lemon

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the eggplant cubes with olive oil, minced garlic, rosemary, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
3. Roast the eggplant for 25‑30 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.  
4. While the eggplant roasts, combine lentils and vegetable broth in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer 20‑25 minutes, or until lentils are cooked but still hold their shape. Drain any excess liquid.  
5. Stir the roasted eggplant into the cooked lentils, mixing gently to combine.  
6. Transfer the pilaf to a serving bowl, sprinkle with toasted pine nuts, fresh parsley, and lemon zest.  
7. Adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed, then serve warm.
title: Garlic‑Rosemary Roasted Eggplant and Lentil Pilaf

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Chickpeas and Spinach

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 2 tbsp lemon juice
- 4 cups fresh baby spinach
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional garnish: toasted sesame seeds

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the chickpeas with 1 tbsp olive oil, half the minced garlic, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking halfway, until crisp.
2. Meanwhile, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
3. In a large skillet, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil over medium heat. Add the remaining garlic and grated ginger; sauté
title: Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Chickpeas and Spinach

text:
Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Grain Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup cooked farro or quinoa
- ¼ cup toasted sliced almonds
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- Optional: drizzle of tahini‑lemon sauce

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cauliflower florets and chickpeas with olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, thyme, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway through, until the cauliflower is golden‑brown and the chickpeas are crisp.  
4. While the vegetables roast, prepare the grain: cook farro or quinoa according to package instructions; fluff with a fork and keep warm.  
5. Assemble the bowl: place a generous scoop of cooked grain at the bottom, top with roasted cauliflower and chickpeas, then sprinkle toasted almonds, fresh parsley, and an extra drizzle of lemon juice if desired.  
6. Serve warm or at room temperature, optionally drizzled with tahini‑lemon sauce for added creaminess. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Grain Bowl

text:
Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Beet and Quinoa Salad with Orange Vinaigrette

Ingredients:
- 2 medium beets, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- ½ teaspoon sea salt
- ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- ¼ cup orange juice (freshly squeezed)
- 1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar
- 1 teaspoon honey or maple syrup
- 2 tablespoons toasted almond slivers
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- Fresh mint leaves for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the beet cubes with olive oil, cinnamon, salt, and pepper; spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, until tender and caramelized.  
2. While the beets roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside to cool slightly.  
3. In a small bowl, whisk together orange juice, apple cider vinegar, and honey (or maple syrup) to create the orange vinaigrette. Adjust seasoning with a pinch of salt if needed.  
4. In a large mixing bowl, combine the roasted beets, cooked quinoa, and toasted almond slivers. Drizzle the orange vinaigrette over the mixture and toss gently to coat evenly.  
5. Transfer the salad to serving plates, sprinkle crumbled feta cheese on top (if using), and garnish with fresh mint leaves. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Beet and Quinoa Salad with Orange Vinaigrette

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Quinoa Salad with Pomegranate Vinaigrette

Ingredients:
- 2 medium beets, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1/4 cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 2 tbsp apple cider vinegar
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1/4 cup toasted walnuts, chopped (optional)
- Fresh mint leaves, torn (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the cubed beets with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, a pinch of salt, and half the ground cinnamon. Spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, or until tender and caramelized. Let cool slightly.
2. While the beets roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside to cool.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining olive oil, maple syrup, apple cider vinegar, the remaining cinnamon, salt, and pepper to create the pomegranate vinaigrette.
4. In a large mixing bowl, combine the roasted beets, cooked quinoa, and pomegranate seeds. Drizzle the vinaigrette over the mixture and toss gently to coat evenly.
5. Transfer the salad to a serving platter, sprinkle with toasted walnuts and fresh mint leaves if using, and serve at room temperature or chilled.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Quinoa Salad with Pomegranate Vinaigrette

text:
Spiced Orange‑Maple Glazed Seitan with Coconut Quinoa  

Ingredients:
- 8 oz seitan, sliced into ½‑inch strips  
- 2 Tbsp orange marmalade  
- 1 Tbsp pure maple syrup  
- 1 tsp smoked paprika  
- ½ tsp ground cumin  
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)  
- 1 Tbsp olive oil  
- 1 cup coconut milk (full‑fat)  
- ½ cup quinoa, rinsed  
- 1 cup water  
- ¼ tsp salt  
- 2 Tbsp toasted coconut flakes (for garnish)  
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)  

Instructions:
1. In a shallow bowl combine orange marmalade, maple syrup, smoked paprika, cumin, and cayenne; stir to form a glaze.  
2. Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the seitan strips and sauté for 2‑3 minutes per side until lightly browned.  
3. Pour the orange‑maple glaze over the seitan, tossing to coat evenly. Cook for an additional 2 minutes, allowing the glaze to caramelize and cling to the seitan. Remove from heat and set aside.  
4. While the seitan cooks, bring coconut milk, water, quinoa, and salt to a boil in a saucepan. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy.  
5. Fluff the coconut quinoa with a fork and transfer to a serving bowl. Top with the glazed seitan strips.  
6. Sprinkle toasted coconut flakes and chopped cilantro over the dish for texture and freshness. Serve warm.
title: Spiced Orange‑Maple Glazed Seitan with Coconut Quinoa

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup long‑grain basmati rice
- 2 ½ cups vegetable broth
- 1 ½ teaspoons saffron threads
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 small red onion, finely diced
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)
- Toasted slivered almonds (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the sweet potato cubes with 1  tablespoon of olive oil, a pinch of salt, and half the cumin; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning once, until caramelized and tender.  
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, place the saffron threads in a small bowl with 2  tablespoons of hot vegetable broth; let steep for 5 minutes to release color and flavor.  
3. In a saucepan, heat the remaining 1  tablespoon of olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced red onion and sauté until translucent, about 3 minutes; add the minced garlic and cook another minute.  
4. Stir in the basmati rice, coating it with the aromatics, then add the saffron‑infused broth, the remaining vegetable broth, and the remaining cumin. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.  
5. When the rice is nearly done, fold in the roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas, gently mixing to combine. Cover and let sit off the heat for 5 minutes to allow flavors to meld.  
6. Fluff the pilaf with a fork, season with additional salt and pepper if needed, and transfer to a serving platter. Garnish with chopped cilantro and toasted slivered almonds, if desired. Enjoy warm as a hearty main or side dish.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Pilaf

text:
Crispy Chili‑Lime Tempeh with Turmeric Quinoa and Charred Broccoli

Ingredients:
- 8 oz (225 g) tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 1 ½ cups quinoa, rinsed
- 3 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 ½ tsp ground turmeric
- 1 ½ tsp smoked paprika
- 1 ½ tsp chili powder
- 1 ½ tbsp lime juice
- 2 tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 large head broccoli, cut into florets
- 1 garlic clove, minced
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish (optional)

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa, water (or broth), turmeric, and a pinch of salt; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
2. While the quinoa cooks, whisk together soy sauce, lime juice, maple syrup, chili powder, smoked paprika, and minced garlic in a shallow bowl.
3. Pat the tempeh strips dry with paper towels, then toss them in the sauce mixture, ensuring each piece is well‑coated. Let marinate for 5 minutes.
4. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated tempeh in a single layer and cook 3‑4 minutes per side, until golden and crispy. Transfer to a plate and keep warm.
5. In the same skillet, add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and the broccoli florets. Sauté 5‑6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the broccoli is tender‑crisp and has charred edges. Season with salt and pepper.
6. To assemble, divide the turmeric‑infused quinoa among serving bowls, top with charred broccoli and crispy tempeh strips. Drizzle any remaining pan juices over the dish.
7. Garnish with fresh cilantro leaves if desired and serve immediately.
title: Crispy Chili‑Lime Tempeh with Turmeric Quinoa and Charred Broccoli

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Shrimp with Garlic‑Brown Rice

Ingredients:
- 1 lb (450 g) large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup brown rice
- 2 cups water or low‑sodium chicken broth
- 2 tbsp coconut oil
- 1 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tsp turmeric powder
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tbsp honey or maple syrup
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional garnish: lime wedges and toasted coconut flakes

Instructions:
1. Rinse the brown rice under cold water, then combine it with water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40‑45 minutes, or until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let it sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
2. While the rice cooks, pat the shrimp dry with paper towels and place them in a bowl. Add turmeric, smoked paprika, lime juice, honey, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Toss to coat evenly and set aside to marinate for 10 minutes.  
3. Heat 1 tbsp of coconut oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger, sautéing for 30 seconds until fragrant.  
4. Add the marinated shrimp to the skillet in a single layer. Cook for 2‑3 minutes on each side, or until the shrimp turn pink and opaque. Transfer the cooked shrimp to a plate and keep warm.  
5. In the same skillet, add the remaining 1 tbsp coconut oil. Stir in the cooked brown rice, breaking up any clumps. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste, and cook for 2‑3 minutes, allowing the rice to absorb the garlic‑ginger flavors.  
6. Return the shrimp to the skillet, mixing gently with the rice to combine. Cook for an additional minute to re‑heat the shrimp.  
7. Remove from heat, sprinkle chopped cilantro over the dish, and drizzle with any remaining lime juice from the bowl.  
8. Serve hot, garnished with lime wedges and toasted coconut flakes if desired. Enjoy the bright, aromatic blend of coconut, lime, and turmeric with succulent shrimp and nutty brown rice.
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Shrimp with Garlic‑Brown Rice

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Chickpea Power Bowl

Ingredients:
- 2 medium beets, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 cup cooked quinoa
- 2 cups baby kale, stems removed
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 2 Tbsp lemon‑juice dressing (lemon juice mixed with a dash of olive oil and honey)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the beet cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp cinnamon, ½ Tbsp maple syrup, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
3. In the same bowl, combine the chickpeas with the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, ½ Tbsp maple syrup, a pinch of cinnamon, and a sprinkle of salt; spread the chickpeas on the same baking sheet beside the beets.  
4. Roast the beets and chickpeas for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway through, until the beets are tender and caramelized and the chickpeas are crisp.  
5. While the vegetables roast, cook quinoa according to package instructions and set aside.  
6. In a large serving bowl, layer the cooked quinoa, roasted beets, roasted chickpeas, and fresh baby kale.  
7. Drizzle the lemon‑juice dressing over the bowl, toss gently to combine, and top with toasted pumpkin seeds for crunch.  
8. Serve warm or at room temperature; enjoy the sweet‑spicy harmony of cinnamon‑maple beets, crunchy chickpeas, and vibrant kale.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Beet and Chickpea Power Bowl

text:
Spiced Orange‑Maple Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Kale

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- 1 tbsp pure maple syrup
- Zest of 1 orange
- 2 cups kale, stems removed and torn into bite‑size pieces
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 tbsp toasted sliced almonds (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the chickpeas with 1 tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, cayenne, and a pinch of salt. Spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until crisp and golden.
2. While the chickpeas roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, orange zest, minced garlic, lemon juice, and a generous pinch of salt and pepper.
4. In a large skillet over medium heat, add the kale and sauté for 2‑3 minutes, just until it begins to wilt. Drizzle the maple‑orange dressing over the kale, tossing to coat evenly; cook an additional minute, then remove from heat.
5. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a serving bowl, fold in the sautéed kale, and top with the roasted chickpeas. Sprinkle toasted almonds over the dish, if using, and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Orange‑Maple Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Kale

text:
Rosemary‑Lemon Chickpea and Sweet Potato Sheet Pan Dinner

Ingredients:
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and diced into ½‑inch cubes
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 teaspoon fresh rosemary, finely chopped (or ½ tsp dried)
- Zest of 1 lemon
- Juice of 1 lemon
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional garnish: chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, combine the diced sweet potatoes, chickpeas, olive oil, rosemary, lemon zest, minced garlic, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Toss until everything is evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet, ensuring the sweet potato pieces are not overcrowded.  
4. Roast for 20 minutes, then stir the vegetables with a spatula to promote even browning.  
5. Continue roasting for an additional 15‑20 minutes, or until the sweet potatoes are tender and lightly caramelized at the edges.  
6. Remove the sheet pan from the oven and immediately drizzle the fresh lemon juice over the roasted vegetables. Toss gently to combine.  
7. Transfer to a serving platter, garnish with chopped parsley if desired, and serve hot as a main‑course or hearty side.
title: Rosemary‑Lemon Chickpea and Sweet Potato Sheet Pan Dinner

text:
Maple‑Glazed Chickpea and Roasted Butternut Squash Curry

Ingredients:
- 1 cup canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 cups cubed butternut squash
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tbsp curry powder
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp smoked paprika
- 1 can (14 oz) coconut milk
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)
- Cooked basmati rice, for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the cubed butternut squash with 1 tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and half the curry powder; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.
2. While the squash roasts, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 4‑5 minutes until translucent.
3. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Add the chickpeas, maple syrup, remaining curry powder, cumin, and smoked paprika. Toss to coat and cook for 2‑3 minutes, allowing the spices to toast lightly.
5. Pour in the coconut milk and vegetable broth, stirring to combine. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.
6. Add the roasted butternut squash to the saucepan. Reduce heat to low and let the curry simmer for 10‑12 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
7. Serve the curry over hot basmati rice, garnish with chopped cilantro, and enjoy.
title: Maple‑Glazed Chickpea and Roasted Butternut Squash Curry

text:
Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Chickpea Curry with Coconut Rice

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 (15 oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup jasmine rice
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk (plus extra ½ cup for the curry)
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp curry powder
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 in piece fresh ginger, grated
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 2 cups fresh spinach leaves
- Juice of 1 lime
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Rinse the jasmine rice under cold water until the water runs clear. Combine the rice and 1 ½ cups coconut milk in a saucepan, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
2. While the rice cooks, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté 4–5 minutes until softened and translucent.  
3. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
4. Sprinkle the curry powder, cumin, and smoked paprika over the aromatics. Stir constantly for 30 seconds to toast the spices.  
5. Add the cubed sweet potatoes to the skillet, tossing to coat them evenly with the spice mixture. Cook for 3 minutes, then pour in the remaining ½ cup coconut milk. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and let cook 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sweet potatoes are just tender.  
6. Add the chickpeas and maple syrup to the pan. Stir to combine, then continue simmering uncovered for another 5 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken and the flavors to meld.  
7. Fold in the fresh spinach leaves and cook for 1–2 minutes until wilted. Season the curry with lime juice, salt, and pepper to taste.  
8. Serve the maple‑glazed sweet potato and chickpea curry over a bed of coconut rice. Garnish each serving with chopped fresh cilantro and an extra squeeze of lime if desired. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Chickpea Curry with Coconut Rice

text:
Maple‑Glazed Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Salad with Citrus Vinaigrette

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch sticks
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 ½ × 15‑oz cans, drained and rinsed)
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 4 cups mixed baby greens (arugula, spinach, and kale)
- ¼ cup toasted sliced almonds
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro (optional)

Citrus Vinaigrette:
- 3 Tbsp freshly squeezed orange juice
- 1 Tbsp freshly squeezed lemon juice
title: Maple‑Glazed Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Salad with Citrus Vinaigrette

text:
Saffron‑Infused Coconut Lime Chickpea and Quinoa Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 can (14 oz) full‑fat coconut milk
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 large carrot, diced
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1 small onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- ½ tsp saffron threads, steeped in 2 tbsp hot water
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 3‑4 minutes.  
2. Stir in the garlic and ginger; cook for another 30 seconds until fragrant.  
3. Add the diced carrot and red bell pepper; sauté for 4‑5 minutes until they begin to soften.  
4. Sprinkle the turmeric and the saffron‑infused water (including the threads) over the vegetables; stir to coat evenly.  
5. Pour in the coconut milk and vegetable broth, bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce to a simmer.  
6. Add the rinsed quinoa and chickpeas. Cover and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the quinoa is cooked and the vegetables are tender.  
7. Stir in the lime zest and lime juice; season with salt and pepper to taste.  
8. Remove from heat and let the stew rest for 2‑3 minutes to allow flavors to meld.  
9. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve hot.
title: Saffron‑Infused Coconut Lime Chickpea and Quinoa Stew

text:
Spiced Cardamom Coconut Lentil & Sweet Potato Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 can (13.5 oz) full‑fat coconut milk
- 3 cups vegetable broth
- 1 large onion, finely chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp ground cardamom
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 2 cups fresh spinach leaves
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté for 4–5 minutes, until translucent.  
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for another minute until fragrant.  
3. Sprinkle the ground cardamom, cumin, and turmeric over the aromatics, stirring constantly for 30 seconds to toast the spices.  
4. Add the diced sweet potatoes and rinsed red lentils to the pot, mixing to coat them with the spiced onion mixture.  
5. Pour in the coconut milk and vegetable broth, stirring to combine. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20–25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and the sweet potatoes are soft.  
6. Season the stew with salt and pepper to taste. If the stew is too thick, add a splash of extra broth or water to reach your desired consistency.  
7. Stir in the fresh spinach leaves and cook for 2–3 minutes, just until wilted.  
8. Remove the pot from heat and finish with a tablespoon of lime juice, adjusting seasoning if needed.  
9. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with chopped cilantro, and serve hot with crusty bread or steamed rice, if desired.
title: Spiced Cardamom Coconut Lentil & Sweet Potato Stew

text:
Coconut-Lime Turmeric Chickpea & Spinach Stir-Fry

Ingredients:
- 1 cup canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 cups fresh baby spinach
- 1 medium red bell pepper, sliced thin
- 1 small onion, thinly sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tbsp coconut oil
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tsp turmeric powder
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp red‑pepper flakes (optional)
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro (for garnish)
- Cooked brown rice or quinoa, for serving

Instructions:
1. Heat the coconut oil in a large skillet over medium heat until shimmering.  
2. Add the sliced onion and sauté for 2‑3 minutes until it begins to soften.  
3. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for another 30 seconds until fragrant.  
4. Sprinkle the turmeric, cumin, and red‑pepper flakes over the aromatics, stirring to coat evenly.  
5. Add the sliced red bell pepper and cook for 2 minutes, allowing it to retain a slight crunch.  
6. Toss in the chickpeas and stir‑fry for 3‑4 minutes, letting them absorb the spices.  
7. Reduce the heat to low, add the baby spinach, and drizzle with lime juice; cook, stirring, until the spinach wilts, about 1‑2 minutes.  
8. Season with salt and black pepper to taste, then remove from heat.  
9. Serve the stir‑fry over warm brown rice or quinoa, garnished with chopped cilantro.
title: Coconut-Lime Turmeric Chickpea & Spinach Stir-Fry

text:
Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Black Bean Enchilada Bake

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 ½ cups black beans, cooked and drained
- 1 cup corn kernels (fresh or frozen)
- 1 ½ cups shredded Monterey Jack cheese
- ½ cup red onion, finely chopped
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp chili powder
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 8 small corn tortillas
- 1 cup enchilada sauce (store‑bought or homemade)
- Fresh cilantro, chopped (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and lightly grease a 9×13‑inch baking dish.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the diced sweet potatoes with olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, chili powder, salt, and pepper. Spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
3. While the sweet potatoes roast, heat a skillet over medium heat and sauté the red onion until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add the black beans, corn, and half of the maple syrup; cook for another 2 minutes, stirring to combine.  
4. Remove the sweet potatoes from the oven and let cool slightly. In a large mixing bowl, combine the roasted sweet potatoes, bean‑corn mixture, and half of the shredded cheese. Mix gently.  
5. Warm the corn tortillas in the microwave for 20 seconds to make them pliable. Spoon a generous amount of the sweet‑potato mixture onto each tortilla, roll tightly, and place seam‑side down in the prepared baking dish.  
6. Pour the enchilada sauce evenly over the rolled tortillas, then drizzle the remaining maple syrup over the top. Sprinkle the remaining cheese over the sauce.  
7. Bake uncovered for 15‑20 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbly.  
8. Remove from the oven, let rest for 5 minutes, then garnish with fresh cilantro if desired. Serve warm.
title: Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Black Bean Enchilada Bake

text:
Rosemary‑Lemon Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 large head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 3 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 2 tsp fresh rosemary, finely chopped
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 2 Tbsp lemon juice
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 2 Tbsp toasted pine nuts
- 2 Tbsp fresh parsley, chopped

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, combine cauliflower florets, chickpeas, 2 Tbsp olive oil, rosemary, lemon zest, garlic, salt, and pepper. Toss until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until cauliflower is golden‑brown and chickpeas are crisp.  
4. While the vegetables roast, bring 2 cups water to a boil in a saucepan. Add quinoa, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil and lemon juice.  
6. Divide the cooked quinoa among serving bowls. Top each with the roasted cauliflower‑chickpea mixture. Drizzle the lemon‑olive oil dressing over the top.  
7. Garnish with toasted pine nuts and chopped parsley. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Rosemary‑Lemon Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Bowl

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Shrimp with Garlic‑Herb Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1/2 tsp sea salt
- 1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper
- Optional: pinch of red‑pepper flakes for heat

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa, water, coconut milk, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed and quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and stir in half the cilantro, lime zest, and a drizzle of olive oil; set aside.  
2. While the quinoa cooks, pat the shrimp dry with paper towels and season with turmeric, salt, and pepper.  
3. Heat the remaining olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the minced garlic and sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.  
4. Add the seasoned shrimp to the skillet in a single layer. Cook 2‑3 minutes per side, or until the shrimp turn pink and opaque.  
5. Stir in the lime juice and red‑pepper flakes (if using); cook an additional 30 seconds to combine flavors.  
6. Plate the garlic‑herb quinoa, top with the turmeric shrimp, and garnish with the remaining cilantro and an extra squeeze of lime if desired. Serve immediately.
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Shrimp with Garlic‑Herb Quinoa

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea & Spinach Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups water
- 1 cup canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 cups fresh spinach, roughly chopped
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 tablespoon lime juice
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- ½ teaspoon salt
- ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- ¼ cup toasted coconut flakes (optional)
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine the rinsed quinoa and water; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 12‑15 minutes until the water is absorbed and the quinoa is tender. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
2. While the quinoa cooks, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the turmeric and cumin, stirring for 30 seconds until fragrant.
3. Add the chickpeas to the skillet and sauté for 3‑4 minutes, allowing them to brown slightly.
4. Pour in the coconut milk, lime juice, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine and bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.
5. Add the chopped spinach to the skillet and cook, stirring occasionally, until wilted, about 2 minutes.
6. Fold the cooked quinoa into the skillet, mixing thoroughly so the flavors meld. Cook for an additional minute to heat through.
7. Remove from heat and transfer to serving bowls. Sprinkle toasted coconut flakes on top, if using, and garnish with fresh cilantro leaves. Serve warm.
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea & Spinach Pilaf

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Quinoa Stuffed Portobello Mushrooms

Ingredients:
- 4 large portobello mushroom caps, stems removed and gills scraped
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon coconut oil
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup canned black beans, drained and rinsed
- ½ cup corn kernels (fresh or frozen)
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- 2 tablespoons lime juice
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Place the mushroom caps gill‑side up on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
2. In a saucepan, combine quinoa and vegetable broth; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
3. While the quinoa cooks, heat coconut oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add grated ginger and turmeric, sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.
4. Stir in coconut milk, black beans, and corn; bring to a gentle simmer and cook 3‑4 minutes until slightly thickened. Season with salt and pepper.
5. Fold the cooked quinoa into the skillet mixture, then stir in chopped cilantro and lime juice. Adjust seasoning as needed.
6. Spoon the quinoa‑bean mixture evenly into each portobello cap, pressing gently to fill.
7. Bake the stuffed mushrooms for 15‑18 minutes, until the caps are tender and the filling is heated through.
8. Remove from oven, let cool 2 minutes, then garnish with extra cilantro or a drizzle of lime juice before serving. Enjoy!
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Quinoa Stuffed Portobello Mushrooms

text:
Sage‑Infused Wild Rice with Roasted Butternut Squash and Pomegranate  

Ingredients:
- 1 cup wild rice, rinsed
- 2 cups low‑sodium vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 small butternut squash, peeled and cubed (about 3 cups)
- 1 tsp dried sage
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds
- 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh parsley  

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the cubed butternut squash with 1 tbsp olive oil, dried sage, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway, until tender and caramelized.  
2. While the squash roasts, combine the wild rice and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 45‑50 minutes, or until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes.  
3. Fluff the cooked wild rice with a fork and stir in the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt and pepper.  
4. Gently fold the roasted butternut squash into the wild rice mixture, being careful not to mash the squash.  
5. Transfer the rice and squash to a serving bowl; sprinkle pomegranate seeds, toasted pumpkin seeds, and chopped parsley over the top for color and crunch.  
6. Serve warm or at room temperature as a hearty side dish or a light main course.
title: Sage‑Infused Wild Rice with Roasted Butternut Squash and Pomegranate

text:
Maple‑Glazed Carrot and Lentil Soup with Coconut Milk

Ingredients:
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 large onion, diced
- 3 carrots, peeled and sliced into rounds
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk (full‑fat)
- 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon ground coriander
- ¼ teaspoon smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Lime wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 4–5 minutes, until translucent.
2. Stir in the garlic and ginger; cook for another minute until fragrant.
3. Add the sliced carrots, cumin, coriander, and smoked paprika. Toss to coat the vegetables with the spices and cook for 2 minutes.
4. Pour in the vegetable broth and bring the mixture to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 10 minutes.
5. Add the rinsed red lentils and continue to simmer, uncovered, for 15–20 minutes, or until the carrots and lentils are tender.
6. Stir in the coconut milk and maple syrup. Season with salt and pepper, then simmer for an additional 5 minutes to meld the flavors.
7. Using an immersion blender, puree the soup until smooth and creamy. (Alternatively, blend in batches in a countertop blender, returning the soup to the pot.)
8. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro, and serve with lime wedges on the side. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Carrot and Lentil Soup with Coconut Milk

text:
Spiced Coconut‑Lime Chickpea & Sweet Potato Tagine

Ingredients:
- 1 lb (450 g) sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 large onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- 1 red bell pepper, sliced
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- 1 cup canned coconut milk
- 2 tbsp coconut oil
- 1 tbsp tomato paste
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- ½ tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp turmeric
- 1 tbsp fresh lime juice
- Zest of 1 lime
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Toasted slivered almonds, for garnish (optional)

Instructions:
1. Heat the coconut oil in a large, heavy‑bottomed pot over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes.
2. Stir in the garlic, ginger, and tomato paste; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add the cumin, coriander, cinnamon, smoked paprika, and turmeric; toast the spices for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
4. Toss in the sweet potato cubes and red bell pepper; stir to coat them with the spice mixture.
5. Pour in the vegetable broth and coconut milk, scraping any browned bits from the bottom
title: Spiced Coconut‑Lime Chickpea & Sweet Potato Tagine

text:
Saffron‑Infused Coconut Chickpea & Sweet Potato Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 large onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp ground coriander
- ¼ tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp saffron threads, steeped in 2 tbsp hot water
- 1 can (14 oz) full‑fat coconut milk
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Lime wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.  
2. Stir in the garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
3. Sprinkle the cumin, coriander, and cinnamon over the aromatics, stirring to coat evenly.  
4. Add the cubed sweet potatoes and chickpeas, then pour in the vegetable broth and the saffron infusion (including the threads). Bring to a boil.  
5. Reduce the heat to a simmer and cook, uncovered, for 15‑20 minutes, or until the sweet potatoes are tender.  
6. Stir in the coconut milk, season with salt and pepper, and let the stew simmer gently for another 5 minutes to meld flavors.  
7. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro, and serve with lime wedges on the side for a bright finish.  
8. Enjoy the warm, aromatic stew with crusty bread or over a bed of steamed rice, if desired.
title: Saffron‑Infused Coconut Chickpea & Sweet Potato Stew

text:
Spiced Cardamom Quinoa and Roasted Beet Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth or water
- 2 medium beets, roasted, peeled, and diced
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cardamom
- 1/4 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/4 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 2 tablespoons toasted walnuts, chopped
- 2 green onions, thinly sliced
- 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
- 1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar
- 1 teaspoon honey or maple syrup
- Salt and black pepper, to taste
- Fresh mint leaves, for garnish (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Wrap the beets in foil and roast for 45–60 minutes, until tender. Let cool, then peel and dice them.
2. While the beets roast, combine the rinsed quinoa and broth (or water) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside to cool slightly.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, ground cardamom, cumin, smoked paprika, lemon juice, apple cider vinegar, honey, salt, and pepper.
4. Place the cooked quinoa and diced roasted beets in a large mixing bowl. Pour the dressing over them and toss gently to combine.
5. Add the toasted walnuts and sliced green onions, tossing again to distribute evenly.
6. Transfer the salad to serving plates, garnish with fresh mint leaves if desired, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Spiced Cardamom Quinoa and Roasted Beet Salad

text:
Garlic‑Lime Roasted Cauliflower Steaks with Herbed Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 large head cauliflower, sliced into 1‑inch thick steaks
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- Zest and juice of 1 lime
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, chopped
- 1 tablespoon fresh mint, chopped
- 1 tablespoon toasted pumpkin seeds (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, minced garlic, lime zest, lime juice, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.  
3. Brush both sides of each cauliflower steak generously with the garlic‑lime mixture and place on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast the cauliflower steaks for 20‑25 minutes, flipping halfway through, until golden brown and tender.  
5. While the cauliflower roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed.  
6. Remove the quinoa from heat and fluff with a fork; stir in chopped parsley, mint, and a drizzle of any remaining lime juice from the pan.  
7. To serve, plate a cauliflower steak atop a mound of herbed quinoa, sprinkle with toasted pumpkin seeds, and finish with an extra squeeze of lime if desired. Enjoy warm!
title: Garlic‑Lime Roasted Cauliflower Steaks with Herbed Quinoa

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Quinoa Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 medium head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 ½ cups vegetable broth
- 1 ½ teaspoons saffron threads
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon lemon juice
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup toasted sliced almonds (optional, for garnish)
- Fresh parsley, chopped (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, combine the saffron threads with 2 tablespoons hot water; let steep for 5 minutes.  
3. Toss the cauliflower florets and chickpeas with olive oil, minced garlic, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway through, until the cauliflower is golden‑brown and the chickpeas are crisp.  
5. While the vegetables roast, bring the vegetable broth and saffron infusion to a boil in a saucepan. Add the quinoa, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy.  
6. Fluff the quinoa with a fork and stir in the lemon juice.  
7. Transfer the roasted cauliflower and chickpeas to the pot with the quinoa; gently toss to combine, adjusting seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.  
8. Serve warm, garnished with toasted almonds and chopped parsley, if desired. Enjoy!
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Quinoa Pilaf

text:
Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Carrot and Lentil Soup with Coconut Milk

Ingredients:
- 1 lb carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch pieces
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 large onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- ½ tsp ground cinnamon
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup full‑fat coconut milk
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the carrot pieces with 1 tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and the ground cinnamon; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway, until caramelized and tender.  
2. While the carrots roast, heat a large pot over medium heat. Add a drizzle of olive oil, then sauté the diced onion until translucent, about 5 minutes.  
3. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
4. Stir in the cumin, coriander, and cayenne pepper; toast the spices for 30 seconds.  
5. Add the roasted carrots, rinsed red lentils, and vegetable broth to the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 15‑20 minutes, or until the lentils are soft.  
6. Remove the pot from heat and blend the soup with an immersion blender (or transfer to a countertop blender in batches) until smooth and creamy.  
7. Return the soup to low heat and stir in the coconut milk. Season with salt and black pepper to taste; heat gently—do not boil.  
8. Finish with lime juice, adjusting seasoning if needed.  
9. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve hot.
title: Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Carrot and Lentil Soup with Coconut Milk

text: Rosemary‑Lemon Grilled Port
title: Rosemary‑Lemon Grilled Port

text:
Lemon‑Basil Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 large head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh basil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup cooked quinoa
- ¼ cup toasted sliced almonds
- 2 Tbsp crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- 1 Tbsp tahini for drizzling (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cauliflower florets and chickpeas with olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, lemon zest, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway through, until the cauliflower is golden‑brown and the chickpeas are crisp.  
4. While the vegetables roast, combine the cooked quinoa with lemon juice, chopped basil, and a pinch of salt; fluff with a fork.  
5. To assemble the bowl, place a generous scoop of herbed quinoa at the bottom, top with the roasted cauliflower and chickpeas, then sprinkle toasted almonds and feta (if using).  
6. Drizzle with tahini, if desired, and finish with an extra sprinkle of fresh basil and a squeeze of lemon juice. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Basil Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

text:
Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Chickpea and Butternut Squash Curry

Ingredients:
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 2 cups cubed butternut squash
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch piece fresh ginger, grated
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- ½ cup vegetable broth
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp ground coriander
- ¼ tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Juice of 1 lime

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the cubed butternut squash with ½ tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and half the cinnamon. Spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
2. While the squash roasts, heat the remaining ½ tbsp olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 4‑5 minutes, until translucent.  
3. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for another minute until fragrant.  
4. Sprinkle the cumin, coriander, turmeric, and the remaining cinnamon over the aromatics. Toast the spices for 30 seconds, stirring constantly to prevent burning.  
5. Add the cooked chickpeas, roasted butternut squash, coconut milk, and vegetable broth to the saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low and let it cook for 10‑12 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.  
6. Season the curry with salt and pepper to taste. Stir in the lime juice just before serving.  
7. Serve hot, garnished with fresh cilantro leaves, alongside steamed rice or warm naan bread.
title: Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Chickpea and Butternut Squash Curry

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tofu and Roasted Garlic Sweet Potato Skillet

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and diced ½‑inch
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce (or tamari for gluten‑free)
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp fresh thyme leaves
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional garnish: chopped fresh parsley or toasted pumpkin seeds

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the diced sweet potatoes with ½ Tbsp olive oil, half the minced garlic, a pinch of salt, pepper, and the thyme leaves; spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
3. Roast the sweet potatoes for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden‑brown and tender.  
4. While the potatoes roast, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, smoked paprika, remaining garlic, and the other ½ Tbsp olive oil in a shallow dish.  
5. Add the cubed tofu to the glaze, gently toss to coat, and let it sit for 5 minutes to absorb flavor.  
6. Heat a large skillet over medium‑high heat; add the glazed tofu in a single layer and sear for 3‑4 minutes per side, until caramelized and crisp.  
7. When the sweet potatoes are done, transfer them to the skillet with the tofu; stir‑combine and cook together for 2 minutes to let the flavors meld.  
8. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a drizzle more maple syrup if desired.  
9. Serve hot, garnished with chopped parsley or toasted pumpkin seeds for extra crunch.
title: Maple‑Glazed Tofu and Roasted Garlic Sweet Potato Skillet

text:
Spiced Coconut‑Lime Lentil and Kale Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper (optional)
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon lime juice
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 cups kale, stems removed and torn into bite‑size pieces
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Lime wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4–5 minutes.
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add the cumin, smoked paprika, and cayenne pepper; toast the spices for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
4. Pour in the rinsed lentils, coconut milk, and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to a gentle simmer.
5. Cover the pot and let the stew cook for 20–25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender.
6. Stir in the lime juice, lime zest, and kale. Simmer for an additional 5 minutes, allowing the kale to wilt but retain its bright green color.
7. Season the stew with salt and black pepper to taste. Adjust the lime intensity if desired.
8. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve with lime wedges on the side. Enjoy warm!
title: Spiced Coconut‑Lime Lentil and Kale Stew

text:
Sage‑Infused Pumpkin and Barley Soup

Ingredients:
- 2 cups diced pumpkin (about 1 lb)
- ½ cup pearl barley, rinsed
- 1 large onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup water
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 teaspoon dried sage (or 1 tablespoon fresh sage, chopped)
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup coconut cream (optional, for garnish)
- Fresh sage leaves, for garnish (optional)

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until translucent, about 4‑5 minutes.
2. Stir in the minced garlic and ground cumin; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add the diced pumpkin and toasted barley to the pot, stirring to coat them with the aromatics.
4. Pour in the vegetable broth and water, then sprinkle the dried sage over the mixture. Bring to a gentle boil.
5. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30‑35 minutes, or until the pumpkin is tender and the barley is cooked through.
6. Using an immersion blender, blend the soup until smooth and creamy, leaving a few small pieces of pumpkin for texture if desired. (Alternatively, transfer half of the soup to a blender, puree, and return to the pot.)
7. Season with salt and pepper to taste. If using, swirl in the coconut cream for extra richness.
8. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with fresh sage leaves and an extra drizzle of coconut cream if desired. Serve hot.
title: Sage‑Infused Pumpkin and Barley Soup

text:
Sesame‑Ginger Lime Tofu with Coconut Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 block (14 oz) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- ½ cup water
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp sesame oil
- 1 tbsp freshly grated ginger
- 2 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- 2 green onions, sliced
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a saucepan combine quinoa, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed; fluff with a fork.  
2. While the quinoa cooks, whisk together soy sauce, sesame oil, ginger, lime juice, maple syrup, and garlic in a bowl to make the glaze.  
3. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the tofu cubes and sear 3‑4 minutes per side until golden brown.  
4. Pour the glaze over the tofu, stirring to coat. Cook an additional 2 minutes until the sauce thickens and clings to the tofu.  
5. Season the tofu with salt and pepper, then remove from heat.  
6. Serve the glazed tofu over the coconut quinoa, sprinkling toasted sesame seeds and sliced green onions on top.  
7. Optional: garnish with extra lime wedges for added brightness.
title: Sesame‑Ginger Lime Tofu with Coconut Quinoa

text:
Spiced Cardamom Chickpea and Roasted Tomato Pasta

Ingredients:
- 12 oz (340 g) whole‑wheat penne pasta
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 cups cherry tomatoes, halved
- 1 large red onion, thinly sliced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cardamom
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp red‑pepper flakes (optional)
- ½ cup vegetable broth
- ¼ cup unsweetened almond milk
- 2 tbsp fresh basil, chopped
- 2 tbsp grated Parmesan or nutritional yeast (for vegans)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the cherry tomatoes, red onion, and a drizzle of olive oil with salt and pepper on a baking sheet; roast for 15‑20 minutes, stirring halfway, until caramelized.
2. While the vegetables roast, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the penne according to package directions until al dente; reserve ½ cup of the pasta water, then drain.
3. In a large skillet over medium heat, add the remaining olive oil and sauté the minced garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant.
4. Stir in the chickpeas, ground cardamom, smoked paprika, and red‑pepper flakes; cook, stirring, for 2‑3 minutes to toast the spices.
5. Add the roasted tomato‑onion mixture to the skillet, followed by the vegetable broth and almond milk. Simmer for 3‑4 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken slightly.
6. Toss the cooked penne into the skillet, adding reserved pasta water as needed to achieve a silky coating. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
7. Remove from heat, stir in fresh basil and grated Parmesan (or nutritional yeast). Serve immediately, garnished with extra basil if desired.
title: Spiced Cardamom Chickpea and Roasted Tomato Pasta

text:
Roasted Garlic‑Lime Tempeh with Coconut‑Basil Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 block (14 oz) tempeh, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tsp lime zest
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth or water
- 1 tbsp coconut oil
- ½ cup fresh basil leaves, chopped
- ¼ cup toasted coconut flakes
- ¼ cup sliced almonds, toasted
- ½ cup diced red bell pepper (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the tempeh cubes with olive oil, minced garlic, lime juice, lime zest, cumin, smoked paprika, cayenne (if using), salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the seasoned tempeh in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway through, until golden and slightly crisp.  
4. While the tempeh roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes.  
5. In a small skillet, melt coconut oil over medium heat. Add the toasted coconut flakes and sliced almonds, stirring constantly for 2‑3 minutes until fragrant and lightly browned. Remove from heat.  
6. Fluff the cooked quinoa with a fork and stir in the chopped basil, toasted coconut‑almond mixture, and a pinch of salt. Adjust seasoning with additional lime juice if desired.  
7. To serve, spoon a bed of coconut‑basil quinoa onto plates, top with the roasted garlic‑lime tempeh, and sprinkle diced red bell pepper for color and crunch.  
8. Enjoy warm
title: Roasted Garlic‑Lime Tempeh with Coconut‑Basil Quinoa

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Edamame

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth or water
- 1 cup frozen edamame, shelled
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon coconut oil
- 1 tablespoon fresh lime juice
- 1 teaspoon lime zest
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- ½ teaspoon sea salt
- ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- 2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro
- Optional: sliced avocado for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the edamame with half the coconut oil, minced garlic, salt, and pepper; spread in a single layer on the sheet.  
3. Roast for 12‑15 minutes, stirring once, until the edamame is lightly browned and fragrant.  
4. While the edamame roasts, combine quinoa and broth in a medium saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes or until liquid is absorbed.  
5. Remove the quinoa from heat and let it sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
6. Stir the remaining coconut oil, turmeric, lime juice, lime zest, and a pinch of salt into the warm quinoa until evenly coated.  
7. Transfer the quinoa to a serving bowl, top with the roasted garlic edamame, and sprinkle with fresh cilantro.  
8. Add avocado slices, if desired, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Edamame

text:
Sesame‑Crusted Salmon with Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 4 salmon fillets (about 6 oz each), skin removed
- 2  tbsp white sesame seeds
- 2  tbsp black sesame seeds
- 1  tbsp olive oil
- 1  tsp sea salt
- ½  tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2  cups low‑sodium vegetable broth
- 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp honey
- 1 tbsp soy sauce (or tamari for gluten‑free)
- 1 small garlic clove, minced
- 2  tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- 1  tbsp toasted sliced almonds (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Pat the salmon fillets dry with paper towels. Drizzle each with olive oil and season with salt and pepper.  
3. In a shallow dish, combine white and black sesame seeds. Press each salmon fillet into the seeds, coating both sides evenly. Place the coated fillets on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast the salmon for 12‑15 minutes, or until the flesh flakes easily with a fork and the sesame crust is golden.  
5. While the salmon cooks, bring the vegetable broth to a boil in a medium saucepan. Add the rinsed quinoa, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
6. In a small bowl, whisk together grated ginger, lemon zest, lemon juice, honey, soy sauce, and minced garlic.  
7. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large bowl, pour the lemon‑ginger dressing over it, and toss to combine. Stir in chopped cilantro and toasted almonds, if using.  
8. To serve, place a generous scoop of lemon‑ginger quinoa on each plate and top with a sesame‑crusted salmon fillet. Garnish with extra cilantro or lemon wedges if desired. Enjoy!
title: Sesame‑Crusted Salmon with Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea & Sweet Potato Tagine

Ingredients:
- 1 lb (450 g) sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 1 medium onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tbsp coconut oil
- 1 tbsp tomato paste
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp ground cinnamon
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- ½ cup coconut milk
- Zest of 1 lime
- Juice of 1 lime
- 2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Heat the coconut oil in a large, heavy‑bottomed pot over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes.  
2. Stir in the garlic and ginger; cook for another minute until fragrant.  
3. Add the tomato paste, turmeric, cumin, cinnamon, and cayenne (if using). Cook, stirring constantly, for 1‑2 minutes to toast the spices.  
4. Add the sweet potato cubes and chickpeas, tossing to coat them evenly with the spice mixture.  
5. Pour in the vegetable broth and bring the mixture to a gentle boil. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15‑20 minutes, or until the sweet potatoes are tender.  
6. Stir in the coconut milk, lime zest, and lime juice. Simmer uncovered for 5 minutes to allow the sauce to thicken slightly.  
7. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Adjust lime juice or a pinch of sugar if you prefer a brighter or sweeter balance.  
8. Remove from heat and garnish with chopped cilantro. Serve hot over couscous, quinoa, or warm flatbread. Enjoy!
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea & Sweet Potato Tagine

text:
Saffron‑Infused Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Chickpeas and Lime  

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed  
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth  
- ½ teaspoon saffron threads  
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed  
- 2 cloves garlic, minced  
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided  
- Zest of 1 lime  
- Juice of 1 lime  
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped  
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste  

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, combine the saffron threads with 2 Tbsp hot water; let steep for 5 minutes.  
2. Bring the quinoa and 2 cups broth (or water) to a boil in a saucepan. Stir in the saffron infusion, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and fluff with a fork.  
3. While the quinoa cooks, preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).  
4. Toss the chickpeas with 1 Tbsp olive oil, minced garlic, salt, and pepper. Spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until golden and crisp.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together lime zest, lime juice, the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, and a pinch of salt.  
6. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl; add the roasted chickpeas, cilantro, and the lime dressing. Toss gently to combine.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired.  
8. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with extra cilantro or lime wedges if desired.
title: Saffron‑Infused Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Chickpeas and Lime

text:
Saffron‑Infused Lentil and Roasted Tomato Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 cups cherry tomatoes, halved
- ½ teaspoon saffron threads
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 medium onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the halved cherry tomatoes with 1 tablespoon olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper; spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 15‑20 minutes, until they begin to caramelize.
2. While the tomatoes roast, place the saffron threads in a small bowl with 2 tablespoons hot water; let steep for 5 minutes.
3. In a medium saucepan, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 3‑4 minutes, until translucent.
4. Stir in the minced garlic and smoked paprika; cook for another 30 seconds until fragrant.
5. Add the rinsed lentils to the saucepan, pour in the vegetable broth, and stir in the saffron infusion (including the liquid). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender but still hold their shape. If needed, add a splash more broth or water.
6. Once the lentils are cooked, gently fold in the roasted tomatoes, reserving a few for garnish. Season the pilaf with salt and pepper to taste; let it sit off the heat for 2 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
7. Transfer the pilaf to a serving bowl, sprinkle with the reserved roasted tomatoes and chopped fresh parsley. Serve warm as a hearty main or a side dish.
title: Saffron‑Infused Lentil and Roasted Tomato Pilaf

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Roasted Broccoli and Chickpea Couscous

Ingredients:
- 1 cup couscous
- 1 ¼ cups vegetable broth
- 2 cups broccoli florets
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the broccoli florets and chickpeas with 1 tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread them on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway, until broccoli is tender‑crisp and chickpeas are lightly crisped.  
3. Meanwhile, bring the vegetable broth to a boil in a medium saucepan, stir in the couscous, cover, and remove from heat. Let sit for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.  
4. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, lemon juice, grated ginger, lemon zest, and a pinch of salt.  
5. Transfer the fluffed couscous to a large mixing bowl, add the roasted broccoli and chickpeas, and drizzle the lemon‑ginger dressing over everything. Toss gently to combine and adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed.  
6. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with chopped fresh parsley if desired. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Ginger Roasted Broccoli and Chickpea Couscous

text:
Sesame‑Crusted Miso‑Glazed Cod with Coconut Lime Rice

Ingredients:
- 4 cod fillets (about 6 oz each)
- 2  tbsp white miso paste
- 1  tbsp soy sauce
- 1  tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1  clove garlic, minced
- 1  tbsp honey
- 2  tbsp toasted sesame seeds (mixed black and white)
- 1  tbsp neutral oil (e.g., grapeseed)
- 1  cup jasmine rice
- 1  cup coconut milk
- 1  cup water
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2  tbsp fresh lime juice
- 2  tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Rinse the jasmine rice under cold water until the water runs clear. Combine rice, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 12‑15 minutes until tender. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork, stir in lime zest, lime juice, and cilantro; set aside.  
2. While the rice cooks, whisk together miso paste, soy sauce, grated ginger, minced garlic, and honey in a small bowl to form the glaze.  
3. Pat the cod fillets dry with paper towels; season lightly with salt and pepper. Brush each fillet generously with the miso‑ginger glaze.  
4. Spread the toasted sesame seeds on a shallow plate. Press the glazed side of each cod fillet into the seeds, coating evenly.  
5. Heat the neutral oil in a large non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. When the oil shimmers, add the cod fillets, sesame‑seed side down. Cook 3‑4 minutes without moving, until the seeds are golden and form a crust. Carefully flip and cook an additional 2‑3 minutes, or until the fish flakes easily with a fork.  
6. Transfer the cod to serving plates. Spoon a generous portion of coconut lime rice beside each fillet. Drizzle any remaining pan juices over the fish, garnish with extra cilantro and a lime wedge if desired. Serve immediately.
title: Sesame‑Crusted Miso‑Glazed Cod with Coconut Lime Rice

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Soup

Ingredients:
- 1 lb carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch pieces  
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed  
- 1 medium onion, diced  
- 2 cloves garlic, minced  
- 2 tbsp olive oil  
- 1 tbsp pure maple syrup  
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon  
- ½ tsp ground cumin  
- ¼ tsp smoked paprika  
- 4 cups vegetable broth  
- ½ cup coconut milk (optional, for creaminess)  
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste  
- Fresh cilantro or parsley, chopped (for garnish)  

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).  
2. Toss the carrot pieces with 1 tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, cumin, smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt. Spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway, until caramelized and tender.  
3. While the carrots roast, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 5 minutes until translucent. Add the garlic and cook another minute.  
4. Add the roasted carrots and chickpeas to the pot. Pour in the vegetable broth and bring to a gentle boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes to let the flavors meld.  
5. Using an immersion blender (or transfer to a countertop blender in batches), blend the soup until smooth but still slightly chunky.  
6. Stir in the coconut milk, if using, and season with salt and pepper to taste. Heat through for 2‑3 minutes.  
7. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with chopped cilantro or parsley, and serve hot.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Soup

text:
Maple‑Glazed Roasted Eggplant and Barley Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 1 cup pearl barley
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 3 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves (or ½ tsp dried)
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- ¼ cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped
- ¼ cup dried cranberries
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together 2 Tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, minced garlic, thyme, salt, and pepper. Add the eggplant cubes and toss to coat evenly.  
3. Spread the glazed eggplant in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until the pieces are tender and caramelized.  
4. While the eggplant roasts, rinse the barley under cold water. Place it in a saucepan with 3 cups water, bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cook uncovered for 30‑35 minutes, or until the grains are tender but still have a slight bite. Drain any excess water and set aside to cool slightly.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, lemon juice, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of pepper to make the dressing.  
6. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked barley, roasted eggplant, toasted walnuts, and dried cranberries. Drizzle the lemon‑olive oil dressing over the mixture and toss gently to distribute.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if desired.  
8. Transfer the salad to a serving platter or individual bowls. Sprinkle crumbled feta cheese on top (if using) and garnish with chopped fresh parsley.  
9. Serve warm, at room temperature, or chilled—perfect as a hearty side or a light main dish. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Roasted Eggplant and Barley Salad

text:
Maple‑Glazed Chickpea and Sweet Potato Gnocchi Bake

Ingredients:
- 1 lb sweet potato gnocchi (store‑bought or homemade)
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves (or ½ tsp dried)
- 1 cup fresh baby spinach
- ¼ cup grated Parmesan cheese (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and lightly grease a 9‑inch baking dish.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, olive oil, minced garlic, thyme, salt, and pepper.  
3. Add the gnocchi, chickpeas, and spinach to the bowl; toss until everything is evenly coated with the maple‑garlic mixture.  
4. Transfer the mixture to the prepared baking dish, spreading it out in an even layer.  
5. Sprinkle the grated Parmesan over the top, if using.  
6. Bake for 20‑25 minutes, or until the gnocchi are golden and slightly crisp on the edges and the spinach is wilted.  
7. Remove from the oven, let cool for a couple of minutes, then serve warm, drizzling any pan juices over the top.
title: Maple‑Glazed Chickpea and Sweet Potato Gnocchi Bake

text:
Maple‑Glazed Chickpea and Roasted Beet Salad with Citrus Vinaigrette

Ingredients:
- 1 cup cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)  
- 2 medium beets, peeled and cubed  
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup  
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided  
- 1 tsp smoked paprika  
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste  
- 4 cups mixed baby greens (arugula, spinach, and radicchio)  
- ¼ cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped  
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)  

Citrus Vinaigrette:
- 2 Tbsp fresh orange juice  
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice  
- 1 tsp Dijon mustard  
- 1 tsp honey or agave nectar  
- 3 Tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil  
- Pinch of salt  

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the beet cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, or until tender and caramelized, stirring halfway through.  
3. While the beets roast, place the chickpeas in a separate bowl. Drizzle with the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
