Transfer the chickpeas to the same baking sheet (or a second sheet) and roast for 15‑18 minutes, shaking the pan once, until they are lightly crisp and glossy.  
4. Meanwhile, whisk together all the citrus vinaigrette ingredients in a small jar or bowl until emulsified. Adjust seasoning with extra salt or honey if needed.  
5. In a large salad bowl, combine the mixed greens, roasted beets, and maple‑glazed chickpeas. Drizzle with the citrus vinaigrette and toss gently to coat.  
6. Sprinkle the toasted walnuts and crumbled feta (if using) over the top. Serve immediately as a hearty lunch or a vibrant side dish.
title: Maple‑Glazed Chickpea and Roasted Beet Salad with Citrus Vinaigrette

text:
Crispy Coconut‑Lime Shrimp with Mango Avocado Salsa

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- ½ cup coconut flakes
- ¼ cup panko breadcrumbs
- 1 tbsp lime zest
- 2 tbsp lime juice
- 1 egg, lightly beaten
- 1 ripe mango, diced
- 1 avocado, diced
- ¼ cup red onion, finely chopped
- 1 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Cooking oil for frying

Instructions:
1. In a shallow bowl, combine coconut flakes, panko, lime zest, salt, and pepper.
2. Place the beaten egg in a separate bowl.
3. Pat the shrimp dry, then dip each piece first in the egg, then coat thoroughly with the coconut‑panko mixture.
4. Heat a thin layer of oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Fry the shrimp in batches, turning once, until golden and crispy, about 2‑3 minutes per side. Transfer to a paper‑towel‑lined plate.
5. While the shrimp cook, toss mango, avocado, red onion, cilantro, lime juice, and a pinch of salt together in a bowl to make the salsa.
6. Serve the crispy shrimp immediately, topped with a generous spoonful of mango‑avocado salsa. Enjoy!
title: Crispy Coconut‑Lime Shrimp with Mango Avocado Salsa

text:
Spiced Coconut‑Lime Quinoa with Charred Broccoli and Toasted Almonds

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups coconut milk
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 Tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 Tbsp coconut oil
- 2 cups broccoli florets
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ cup sliced almonds, toasted
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine the rinsed quinoa and coconut milk. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is tender. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and stir in the lime zest, lime juice, and coconut oil. Season with salt and pepper; set aside.  
2. While the quinoa cooks, preheat a grill pan or large skillet over medium‑high heat. Toss the broccoli florets with olive oil, minced garlic, smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt. Spread in a single layer on the pan and cook, stirring occasionally, until the broccoli is deeply charred in spots and just tender, about 6‑8 minutes. Transfer to a bowl.  
3. In a small dry skillet over medium heat, toast the sliced almonds, stirring frequently, until golden and fragrant, about 2‑3 minutes. Remove from heat and set aside.  
4. To assemble, divide the coconut‑lime quinoa among serving bowls. Top each with a generous portion of charred broccoli, then sprinkle toasted almonds over the top. Garnish with chopped cilantro if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Spiced Coconut‑Lime Quinoa with Charred Broccoli and Toasted Almonds

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Parsnip and Chickpea Power Bowl

Ingredients:
- 2 large parsnips, peeled and cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup cooked farro (or quinoa)
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- Fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish
- Lemon wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the parsnip cubes and chickpeas with olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the parsnips are golden‑brown and tender and the chickpeas are crisp.  
4. While the vegetables roast, cook farro (or quinoa) according to package instructions; fluff with a fork and set aside.  
5. Divide the cooked farro among serving bowls. Top each with the roasted parsnip‑chickpea mixture.  
6. Sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds, crumbled feta (if using), and chopped parsley over each bowl.  
7. Finish with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice and an extra drizzle of maple syrup, if desired.  
8. Serve warm or at room temperature, enjoying the sweet‑spicy crunch of the parsnips and chickpeas.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Parsnip and Chickpea Power Bowl

text:
Sesame‑Crusted Tofu with Mango‑Chili Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 Tbsp sesame seeds (white or black)
- 1 Tbsp cornstarch
- 2 Tbsp soy sauce (or tamari for gluten‑free)
- 1 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp rice‑vinegar
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 small ripe mango, diced
- ½ red bell pepper, finely diced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 small red chili, thinly sliced (adjust heat to taste)
- 2 Tbsp lime juice
- 2 Tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine the quinoa and water (or broth). Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and set aside to cool slightly.  
2. While the quinoa cooks, prepare the tofu: In a shallow bowl whisk together soy sauce, maple syrup, rice‑vinegar, and grated ginger. Add the tofu cubes and toss gently to coat; let marinate for 5 minutes.  
3. In a separate shallow dish, spread the cornstarch. Remove tofu from the marinade (reserve the liquid) and roll each cube in cornstarch, shaking off excess.  
4. Heat 1 Tbsp olive oil in a large non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the tofu cubes in a single layer and cook 3‑4 minutes per side, or until golden and crisp. Transfer to a paper‑towel‑lined plate.  
5. In the same skillet, add the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil and the reserved marinade. Cook, stirring, for 1‑2 minutes until slightly thickened; drizzle this glaze over the cooked tofu.  
6. In a large mixing bowl combine the cooked quinoa, diced mango, red bell pepper, cilantro, sliced chili, and lime juice. Toss gently to distribute the flavors. Season with salt and pepper to taste.  
7. To serve, divide the mango‑chili quinoa salad among plates, top each portion with a handful of sesame‑crusted tofu, and sprinkle the sesame seeds over everything for extra crunch.  
8. Optional: garnish with additional cilantro leaves or a wedge of lime for extra brightness. Enjoy immediately while the tofu is still warm.
title: Sesame‑Crusted Tofu with Mango‑Chili Quinoa Salad

text:
Saffron‑Infused Coconut Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Pomegranate  

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup water
- 1/2 teaspoon saffron threads
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/4 cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 tablespoons toasted pistachios, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh mint leaves, for garnish  

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Toss the chickpeas with olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper; spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking halfway, until crisp and golden.  
2. While the chickpeas roast, combine the saffron threads with 2 tablespoons of hot water in a small bowl; let steep for 5 minutes.  
3. In a medium saucepan, bring the coconut milk, water, and saffron infusion to a gentle boil. Add the quinoa, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is tender. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
4. Season the cooked quinoa with salt and pepper, then transfer to a large serving bowl.  
5. Fold the roasted chickpeas, pomegranate seeds, and toasted pistachios into the quinoa, mixing gently to distribute evenly.  
6. Garnish with fresh mint leaves and an extra sprinkle of pistachios if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature as a vibrant side dish or light main course.
title: Saffron‑Infused Coconut Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Pomegranate

text:
Maple‑Glazed Carrot and Lentil Tacos

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and grated
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- 1 ½ tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp sea salt
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 8 small corn tortillas
- 1 lime, cut into wedges
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 avocado, sliced (optional)
- ¼ cup crumbled feta or cotija cheese (optional)

Instructions:
1. In a saucepan, combine the rinsed lentils and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer, uncovered, for 12‑15 minutes, or until lentils are tender but not mushy. Drain any excess liquid and set aside.  
2. While the lentils cook, heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the grated carrots, cumin, smoked paprika, and salt. Sauté for 5‑7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the carrots are softened and lightly caramelized.  
3. Stir the maple syrup into the carrots, cooking for another 2 minutes to create a glossy glaze. Remove the carrot mixture from the pan and set aside.  
4. Return the skillet to the heat, add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, and toss the cooked lentils in to warm them through, about 2 minutes.  
5. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet or directly over a low flame, 20‑30 seconds per side, until pliable.  
6. To assemble each taco, place a spoonful of glazed carrots on the tortilla, top with a generous scoop of lentils, a squeeze of lime juice, and a sprinkle of chopped cilantro. Add avocado slices and cheese, if using.  
7. Serve immediately, with extra lime wedges on the side. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Carrot and Lentil Tacos

text:
Herb‑Infused Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Lemon Asparagus

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 bunch asparagus, trimmed and cut into 2‑inch pieces
- 4 cloves garlic, peeled
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
- 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley
- 1 tablespoon chopped fresh thyme leaves
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the asparagus pieces and whole garlic cloves with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 12‑15 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized. Remove from the oven and set aside.
2. While the asparagus roasts, combine the quinoa and water (or broth) in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
3. Fluff the cooked quinoa with a fork and stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, chopped parsley, and thyme. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste.
4. Gently fold the roasted asparagus and garlic into the herb‑infused quinoa, distributing evenly.
5. Serve warm or at room temperature, optionally garnished with extra parsley or a drizzle of lemon‑infused olive oil. Enjoy!
title: Herb‑Infused Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Lemon Asparagus

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Shrimp with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined  
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed  
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk  
- ½ cup water  
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice  
- zest of 1 lemon  
- 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger  
- 2 cloves garlic, minced  
- 2 tbsp olive oil  
- ¼ tsp sea salt, plus more to taste  
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper  
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro  

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine the quinoa, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and transfer to a large bowl; set aside to cool slightly.  
2. While the quinoa cooks, whisk together the lime juice, lemon zest, grated ginger, minced garlic, olive oil, salt, and pepper in a small bowl to form a quick vinaigrette.  
3. Heat a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the shrimp in a single layer and sauté for 2 minutes per side, or until pink and opaque. Drizzle half of the vinaigrette over the shrimp while cooking, allowing it to glaze the surface. Remove the shrimp from the pan and set aside.  
4. Add the remaining vinaigrette to the warm quinoa, tossing gently to coat the grains evenly.  
5. Fold the cooked shrimp into the quinoa mixture, then sprinkle the chopped cilantro over the top. Adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired.  
6. Serve the salad warm or at room temperature, garnished with an extra sprinkle of cilantro or a thin lemon wedge for brightness. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Ginger Shrimp with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa Salad

text:
Coconut‑Lime Basil Shrimp Paella

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup short‑grain rice (such as Arborio)
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 small onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1 cup frozen peas, thawed
- 1 cup canned coconut milk
- 2 cups low‑sodium chicken broth
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice
- ¼ cup fresh basil leaves, torn
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Lemon wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large, deep skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 3 minutes.
2. Stir in the garlic, red bell pepper, and smoked paprika; cook for another 2 minutes until fragrant.
3. Add the rice, stirring to coat each grain with the oil and vegetables; toast lightly for 1 minute.
4. Pour in the chicken broth and coconut milk, then bring the mixture to a gentle boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the rice is tender and most of the liquid is absorbed.
5. Gently fold in the peas, lime zest, lime juice, and shrimp. Cover and cook for 4‑5 minutes, or until the shrimp turn pink and are cooked through.
6. Remove the pan from heat; stir in the fresh basil, and season with salt and pepper to taste.
7. Serve the paella hot, garnished with additional basil leaves and lemon wedges on the side.
title: Coconut‑Lime Basil Shrimp Paella

text:
Spiced Coconut‑Lime Shrimp and Pineapple Quinoa Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- ½ cup pineapple chunks (fresh or canned, drained)
- 1 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tbsp lime zest
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch piece ginger, grated
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat; add the quinoa and toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
2. Pour in the coconut milk, bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.
3. While the quinoa cooks, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the garlic, ginger, and diced red bell pepper; sauté for 2 minutes until fragrant.
4. Add the shrimp, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 3‑4 minutes until the shrimp turn pink and opaque.
5. Stir in the pineapple chunks, lime juice, and lime zest; cook for an additional minute to combine flavors.
6. Gently fold the cooked quinoa into the shrimp‑pineapple mixture, ensuring an even distribution. Adjust seasoning with more salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired.
7. Transfer to a serving bowl, garnish with chopped cilantro, and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Coconut‑Lime Shrimp and Pineapple Quinoa Pilaf

text:
Cinnamon‑Rosemary Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 3 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 tsp dried rosemary (or 1 Tbsp fresh, chopped)
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- Optional: ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes and chickpeas with olive oil, cinnamon, rosemary, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the sweet potatoes are tender and lightly caramelized and the chickpeas are crisp.  
5. Transfer the roasted vegetables to a serving bowl; drizzle with fresh lemon juice and toss gently to combine.  
6. Sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds (and feta, if using) over the top for added crunch and flavor.  
7. Serve warm or at room temperature as a hearty salad or side dish.
title: Cinnamon‑Rosemary Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Salad

text:
Sesame‑Ginger Miso Glazed Eggplant with Brown Rice

Ingredients:
- 2 medium eggplants, sliced into ½‑inch rounds
- 3 Tbsp white miso paste
- 2 Tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 Tbsp sesame oil
- 1 Tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 Tbsp honey or maple syrup
- 1 tsp freshly grated ginger
- 1 tsp minced garlic
- 1 Tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- 2 Tbsp chopped scallions (green parts only)
- 1 cup brown rice
- 2 cups water or low‑sodium vegetable broth
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Rinse the brown rice, combine with water or broth in a saucepan, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40‑45 minutes until tender; fluff with a fork and set aside.  
2. While the rice cooks, preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
3. In a small bowl, whisk together miso paste, soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, honey, grated ginger, and minced garlic until smooth.  
4. Brush both sides of each eggplant slice with olive oil, then season lightly with salt and pepper; place on the prepared baking sheet.  
5. Roast the eggplant for 12 minutes, flip the slices, and brush generously with the miso‑ginger glaze.  
6. Return to the oven and roast an additional 10‑12 minutes, or until the eggplant is tender and the glaze is caramelized.  
7. Transfer the cooked brown rice to serving bowls, top with the glazed eggplant slices, and drizzle any remaining glaze from the pan over the dish.  
8. Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds and chopped scallions over each bowl for crunch and freshness.  
9. Serve warm, optionally with a side of steamed greens or a simple cucumber salad.
title: Sesame‑Ginger Miso Glazed Eggplant with Brown Rice

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Black Bean Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 ½ cups cooked black beans (canned, drained and rinsed)
- 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- ¼ cup diced red onion
- 1 avocado, sliced
- Juice of 1 lime
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, cinnamon, smoked paprika, olive oil, salt, and pepper.  
3. Add the cubed sweet potatoes to the bowl and toss until evenly coated. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast the sweet potatoes for 20‑25 minutes, turning once halfway through, until tender and caramelized.  
5. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine the black beans, red onion, and cilantro in a medium bowl.  
6. When the sweet potatoes are done, let them cool slightly, then add them to the bean mixture.  
7. Drizzle the lime juice over the salad, gently toss to combine, and adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed.  
8. Serve the salad topped with sliced avocado; enjoy warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Black Bean Salad

text:
Citrus‑Herb Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Grilled Zucchini

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- Salt and black pepper, to taste
- 2 medium zucchini, sliced lengthwise into ½‑inch strips
- 1 tablespoon lemon zest
- 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
- 2 teaspoons chopped fresh thyme
- 2 teaspoons chopped fresh parsley
- 1 garlic clove, minced
- Optional: 1 tablespoon toasted pine nuts for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the chickpeas with olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper; spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking halfway, until crisp.
2. While the chickpeas roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together lemon zest, lemon juice, thyme, parsley, minced garlic, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of olive oil to create the citrus‑herb dressing.
4. Heat a grill pan or outdoor grill over medium‑high heat; brush zucchini strips with a little olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Grill 3‑4 minutes per side until tender and lightly charred; set aside.
5. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl; pour half of the citrus‑herb dressing over it and toss to combine. Gently fold in the roasted chickpeas and grilled zucchini strips.
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if needed. Serve warm or at room temperature, sprinkled with toasted pine nuts if desired. Enjoy!
title: Citrus‑Herb Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Grilled Zucchini

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Shrimp with Garlic‑Herb Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or low‑sodium vegetable broth
- 1 tbsp coconut oil
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 lime, zest and juice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- 1 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa and water (or broth); bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and fluff with a fork.
2. While the quinoa cooks, heat coconut oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add minced garlic and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
3. Sprinkle the shrimp with turmeric, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; add to the skillet. Cook 2‑3 minutes per side, until pink and opaque.
4. Add lime zest and juice to the skillet, stirring to coat the shrimp. Cook an additional minute, then remove the shrimp from the pan and set aside.
5. Return the skillet to medium heat, add the cooked quinoa, and toss to combine with any remaining pan juices. Stir in chopped parsley, cilantro, and a drizzle of extra lime juice if desired.
6. Plate the quinoa mixture, top with the turmeric shrimp, and garnish with additional fresh herbs and a wedge of lime. Serve immediately.
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Shrimp with Garlic‑Herb Quinoa

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Lentil and Spinach Stew with Herb Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 large onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- Zest of 1 lemon
- Juice of 1 lemon
- 2 cups fresh spinach, roughly chopped
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- 1 tbsp chopped fresh mint (optional)

Instructions:
1. In a medium pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
2. Stir in the minced garlic, grated ginger, and ground turmeric; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add the rinsed lentils and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender.
4. While the stew simmers, prepare the quinoa: combine rinsed quinoa and 2 cups water in a saucepan, bring to a boil, then cover and reduce to low heat. Cook for 15 minutes, or until the water is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.
5. Once the lentils are tender, stir in the chopped spinach, lemon zest, and lemon juice. Cook for an additional 2‑3 minutes, just until the spinach wilts. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
6. To serve, spoon a generous portion of quinoa onto each plate, top with the lentil‑spinach stew, and garnish with chopped parsley and mint if using. Enjoy warm.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Lentil and Spinach Stew with Herb Quinoa

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Couscous

Ingredients:
- 1 small head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 ½ cups cooked couscous
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp saffron threads
- 2 tbsp warm water
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp ground coriander
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup toasted slivered almonds
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 1 tbsp lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, combine the saffron threads with warm water; let steep for 5 minutes.  
3. Toss the cauliflower florets with 1 tbsp olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika, coriander, salt, and pepper. Spread on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender.  
4. While the cauliflower roasts, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the chickpeas and sauté for 4‑5 minutes until lightly crisped; season with a pinch of salt and pepper.  
5. Fluff the cooked couscous with a fork and stir in the saffron infusion, lemon zest, and lemon juice. Adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed.  
6. In a large mixing bowl, combine the roasted cauliflower, sautéed chickpeas, and saffron‑couscous. Toss gently to distribute evenly.  
7. Transfer the mixture to a serving platter, sprinkle with toasted slivered almonds and chopped parsley. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Couscous

text:
Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Beet and Chickpea Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 medium beets, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped
- 2 tbsp fresh orange juice
- 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar
- 1 tsp honey or maple syrup
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Toss the beet cubes and chickpeas with olive oil, cinnamon, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread them in a single layer on a baking sheet.
2. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway, until the beets are tender and slightly caramelized and the chickpeas are crisp.
3. While the vegetables roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside to cool slightly.
4. In a small bowl, whisk together orange juice, apple cider vinegar, honey (or maple syrup), and a pinch of salt to create the dressing.
5. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted beets, roasted chickpeas, toasted walnuts, and chopped parsley. Drizzle the dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat evenly.
6. Adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed. Serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Spiced Roasted Beet and Chickpea Quinoa Salad

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea & Spinach One‑Pot

Ingredients:
- 1 cup canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 cups fresh spinach leaves
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- ½ cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat; add the garlic and ginger, sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.  
2. Stir in the turmeric and toast for another 30 seconds, then add the quinoa, coating it with the spices.  
3. Pour in the vegetable broth and bring to a gentle boil; reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 12‑15 minutes, or until the quinoa is tender and the liquid is absorbed.  
4. Add the chickpeas and coconut milk, stirring to combine; simmer for 5 minutes to heat through.  
5. Fold in the fresh spinach and cook for 2‑3 minutes, just until wilted.  
6. Remove from heat, stir in the lime juice, and season with salt and pepper to taste.  
7. Serve hot, garnished with extra lime wedges or a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds if desired.
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea & Spinach One‑Pot

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Lentil Salad with Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, cubed
- 1 cup cooked green lentils (or ½ cup dry lentils)
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- ¼ red onion, thinly sliced (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together maple syrup, cinnamon, olive oil, salt, and pepper.  
3. Add the cubed sweet potatoes and toss to coat evenly; spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
4. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and caramelized.  
5. While the sweet potatoes roast, cook lentils if using dry: rinse, combine 1 cup lentils with 2½ cups water, bring to a boil, reduce heat, simmer 20‑25 minutes until tender; drain.  
6. In a large mixing bowl, combine roasted sweet potatoes, cooked lentils, red onion, lemon juice, and parsley; toss gently.  
7. Sprinkle pomegranate seeds over the salad just before serving for a burst of freshness.  
8. Serve warm or at room temperature as a hearty side or light main dish.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Lentil Salad with Pomegranate

text:
Maple‑Glazed Carrot and Chickpea Tagine with Apricot

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch rounds
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 ½ × 15‑oz cans, drained and rinsed)
- ½ cup dried apricots, chopped
- 1 medium onion, finely diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- ½ tsp ground cinnamon
- ¼ tsp ground turmeric
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- 1 tbsp toasted slivered almonds (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy‑bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes.  
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for another 30 seconds until fragrant.  
3. Add the cumin, coriander, cinnamon, and turmeric. Toast the spices for 1 minute, stirring constantly to prevent burning.  
4. Toss in the carrot rounds, coating them with the spiced onion mixture. Cook for 3–4 minutes, allowing the carrots to begin softening.  
5. Pour in the vegetable broth, bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer. Cover and let simmer for 15 minutes, or until the carrots are fork‑tender.  
6. Stir in the cooked chickpeas, chopped apricots, and maple syrup. Simmer uncovered for an additional 5 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken slightly.  
7. Taste and season with salt and pepper as needed. If the tagine looks too dry, add a splash more broth.  
8. Remove from heat and let stand for 2 minutes. Garnish with fresh cilantro leaves and toasted slivered almonds, if using.  
9. Serve hot over couscous, quinoa, or warm flatbread, and enjoy the sweet‑savory harmony of the maple‑glazed carrots and apricots.
title: Maple‑Glazed Carrot and Chickpea Tagine with Apricot

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Soup

Ingredients:
- 1 lb carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch pieces
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch piece fresh ginger, grated
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- ½ tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 3 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the carrot pieces with 1 tbsp olive oil, ½ tsp salt, and a pinch of black pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway, until caramelized and tender.  
2. While the carrots roast, heat a large pot over medium heat. Add the remaining ½ tbsp olive oil and sauté the onion until translucent, about 5 minutes.  
3. Add the garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Stir in the cumin, coriander, and cinnamon; toast the spices for 30 seconds.  
4. Add the roasted carrots, chickpeas, maple syrup, and vegetable broth to the pot. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes to let the flavors meld.  
5. Remove the pot from heat and blend the soup with an immersion blender (or transfer to a countertop blender in batches) until smooth and creamy.  
6. Return the soup to the pot, stir in the coconut milk, and season with additional salt and pepper to taste. Warm over low heat for 2‑3 minutes, being careful not to boil.  
7. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve hot. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Soup

text:
Herb‑Infused Barley with Roasted Sweet Peppers and Lemon Zest

Ingredients:
- 1 cup pearl barley
- 2 cups low‑sodium vegetable broth
- 1 red bell pepper, sliced into strips
- 1 yellow bell pepper, sliced into strips
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon dried oregano
- 1 teaspoon dried thyme
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
- ¼ cup chopped fresh parsley
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the sliced bell peppers with olive oil, dried oregano, dried thyme, salt, and pepper; spread them on a baking sheet.
2. Roast the peppers for 15‑20 minutes, turning once, until they are tender and lightly charred. Remove from the oven and set aside.
3. While the peppers roast, rinse the barley under cold water. In a medium saucepan, combine the barley and vegetable broth; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30‑35 minutes, or until the barley is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
4. Fluff the cooked barley with a fork and stir in the lemon zest, lemon juice, and chopped parsley. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste.
5. Gently fold the roasted sweet peppers into the barley mixture until evenly distributed.
6. Transfer the herb‑infused barley and peppers to a serving bowl. Drizzle with a little extra olive oil if desired and garnish with extra parsley or lemon zest.
7. Serve warm or at room temperature as a hearty side dish or a light main course. Enjoy!
title: Herb‑Infused Barley with Roasted Sweet Peppers and Lemon Zest

text:
Maple‑Glazed Carrot and Lentil Shepherd’s Pie

Ingredients:
- 2 lb carrots, peeled and diced
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 1 large onion, finely chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp salt, plus more to taste
- ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 2 lb potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- ¼ cup plant‑based milk (or dairy milk)
- Fresh parsley, chopped (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Lightly grease a 9‑inch deep dish casserole or a similar baking dish.  
2. Place the cubed potatoes in a pot of salted water. Bring to a boil and cook until fork‑tender, about 15 minutes. Drain and return to the pot.  
3. While the potatoes cook, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes.  
4. Stir in the garlic and cook for another 30 seconds until fragrant.  
5. Add the diced carrots and thyme to the skillet; sauté for 5 minutes, allowing the carrots to begin softening.  
6. Pour in the lentils and vegetable broth. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils and carrots are tender and most liquid is absorbed.  
7. Stir in the maple syrup, salt, and pepper. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Remove from heat and set aside.  
8. Return the cooked potatoes to the pot. Add butter, milk, and a pinch of salt. Mash until smooth and creamy; taste and adjust seasoning.  
9. Spoon the carrot‑lentil mixture into the prepared baking dish, spreading it evenly. Top with the mashed potatoes, smoothing the surface with a spatula.  
10. Bake in the preheated oven for 20‑25 minutes, or until the potato topping is golden brown and the filling is bubbling around the edges.  
11. Remove from the oven and let stand for 5 minutes. Garnish with chopped parsley, if desired, before serving. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Carrot and Lentil Shepherd’s Pie

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Pilaf with Pomegranate  

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch chunks  
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 ½ cups canned, drained and rinsed)  
- 1 cup basmati rice, rinsed  
- 2 cups vegetable broth  
- ½ teaspoon saffron threads, steeped in 2 Tbsp hot water  
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds  
- 2 Tbsp olive oil  
- 1 small red onion, finely diced  
- 1 clove garlic, minced  
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste  
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish  

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the carrot chunks with 1 Tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until caramelized and tender.  
2. Meanwhile, heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 3‑4 minutes until translucent; stir in the garlic and cook another 30 seconds.  
3. Add the rinsed basmati rice to the saucepan, stirring to coat the grains with the aromatics. Pour in the vegetable broth and the saffron infusion (including the threads). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the rice is cooked and the liquid absorbed.  
4. Gently fold the roasted carrots and chickpeas into the cooked rice. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste, and let the pilaf sit, covered, for 5 minutes to allow flavors to meld.  
5. Transfer the pilaf to a serving bowl, sprinkle pomegranate seeds and fresh cilantro over the top, and serve warm.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Pilaf with Pomegranate

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa & Roasted Beet Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 2 medium beets, peeled and cubed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika
- Salt and pepper, to taste
- 1/2 cup canned coconut milk
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice
- 1 tablespoon maple syrup
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the cubed beets with olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, until tender and caramelized.  
2. While the beets roast, combine quinoa and water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.  
3. In a small bowl, whisk together coconut milk, lime zest, lime juice, maple syrup, and a pinch of salt to create the dressing.  
4. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl; pour the dressing over the quinoa and toss to coat evenly.  
5. Add the roasted beets, chopped cilantro, and toasted pumpkin seeds to the quinoa; gently fold everything together.  
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature as a hearty salad or side dish.
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa & Roasted Beet Salad

text:
Harissa‑Spiced Lentil and Roasted Eggplant Stack

Ingredients:
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 medium eggplants, sliced into ½‑inch rounds
- 2 tbsp harissa paste
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 small red onion, thinly sliced
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ cup fresh parsley, chopped
- 1 lemon, zest and juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup crumbled feta (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the eggplant slices with 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1 tablespoon harissa paste, salt, and pepper; spread them in a single layer on the sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, flipping halfway, until tender and lightly charred.  
3. While the eggplant roasts, combine lentils, 2 cups water, a pinch of salt, and the cumin in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook 20‑25 minutes, or until lentils are tender but not mushy. Drain any excess
title: Harissa‑Spiced Lentil and Roasted Eggplant Stack

text:
Coconut‑Lime Chickpea Sweet Potato Tostada with Avocado Crema

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 medium sweet potato, peeled and diced
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 4 small corn tortillas
- ½ cup shredded red cabbage
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- 1 ripe avocado, sliced
- 2 Tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp coconut aminos (or soy sauce)
- ¼ cup vegan sour cream or Greek yogurt
- 1 tsp lime zest

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the diced sweet potato with ½ Tbsp olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika, cayenne, salt, and pepper; spread on the sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
3. While the sweet potato roasts, combine chickpeas, remaining ½ Tbsp olive oil, lime juice, maple syrup, coconut aminos, salt, and pepper in a bowl; spread on a separate part of the baking sheet and roast for 12‑15 minutes, shaking the pan once, until slightly crisp.  
4. Warm the corn tortillas: place them on a dry skillet over medium heat for 30 seconds per side, or wrap in foil and heat in the oven for 5 minutes.  
5. Assemble the avocado crema: mash the avocado with the sour cream (or yogurt), lime zest, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of lime juice until smooth.
title: Coconut‑Lime Chickpea Sweet Potato Tostada with Avocado Crema

text:
Sesame‑Miso Glazed Eggplant with Quinoa Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 2 medium eggplants, sliced into ½‑inch rounds
- 3 Tbsp white miso paste
- 2 Tbsp toasted sesame oil
- 1 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp rice‑vinegar
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- ½ cup frozen peas
- ¼ cup sliced scallions
- 1 Tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl whisk together miso, sesame oil, maple syrup, soy sauce, ginger, and rice‑vinegar until smooth.  
3. Brush both sides of each eggplant slice with the glaze, placing them on the prepared sheet. Season lightly with salt and pepper.  
4. Roast the eggplant for 20‑25 minutes, flipping halfway through, until caramelized and tender.  
5. While the eggplant roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.  
6. Remove the quinoa from heat, stir in frozen peas, cover, and let sit for 5 minutes until peas are warmed through. Fluff with a fork.  
7. Transfer the quinoa to a serving bowl, drizzle with a splash of sesame oil, and toss to combine.  
8. Arrange the glazed eggplant slices atop the quinoa pilaf. Garnish with sliced scallions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve warm.
title: Sesame‑Miso Glazed Eggplant with Quinoa Pilaf

text:
Coconut‑Lime Quinoa Stuffed Acorn Squash with Pomegranate  

Ingredients:
- 2 medium acorn squash, halved and seeded
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups coconut milk
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon lime zest
- 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice
- ½ teaspoon sea salt
- ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 tablespoons toasted pumpkin seeds

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Place the acorn squash halves cut‑side up on a baking sheet, brush with olive oil, and season with a pinch of salt and pepper. Roast for 35‑40 minutes, until the flesh is tender and lightly caramelized.  
2. While the squash roasts, combine quinoa and coconut milk in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes.  
3. Fluff the cooked quinoa with a fork and stir in lime zest, lime juice, salt, pepper, and chopped cilantro. Adjust seasoning to taste.  
4. Remove the roasted squash from the oven. Spoon the coconut‑lime quinoa mixture into each squash cavity, packing gently but evenly.  
5. Return the stuffed squash to the oven and bake for an additional 10 minutes to warm the filling.  
6. Remove from the oven and garnish each half with pomegranate seeds and toasted pumpkin seeds for a burst of color and crunch. Serve warm.
title: Coconut‑Lime Quinoa Stuffed Acorn Squash with Pomegranate

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Parsnip and Kale Salad

Ingredients:
- 4 large parsnips, peeled and cut into 1/2‑inch sticks
- 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- ½ teaspoon sea salt
- ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- 4 cups chopped kale, stems removed
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tablespoons crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- 1 tablespoon lemon juice
- 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, olive oil, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Add the parsnip sticks and toss to coat evenly.  
3. Spread the coated parsnips in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway through, until golden‑brown and tender.  
4. While the parsnips roast, place the chopped kale in a dry skillet over medium heat. Toast for 2‑3 minutes, stirring frequently, until the leaves wilt slightly and become fragrant. Transfer to a large mixing bowl.  
5. In a small jar, combine the lemon juice, Dijon mustard, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of olive oil; shake well to make the dressing.  
6. When the parsnips are done, let them cool for a few minutes, then add them to the bowl with the kale. Drizzle the dressing over the salad and toss gently to combine.  
7. Sprinkle the toasted pumpkin seeds and crumbled feta (if using) over the top. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Parsnip and Kale Salad

text:
Maple‑Glazed Carrot and Lentil Curry with Coconut Rice

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and diced
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 tablespoon coconut oil
- 1 medium onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 teaspoon ground coriander
- ½ teaspoon turmeric powder
- ¼ teaspoon cayenne pepper (optional)
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon maple syrup
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 1 cup jasmine rice
- 1 ½ cups water
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)
- Lime wedges (for serving)

Instructions:
1. Rinse the jasmine rice under cold water, then combine with 1 ½ cups water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.
2. While the rice cooks, heat coconut oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté for 4‑5 minutes until translucent.
3. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for another minute until fragrant.
4. Add the diced carrots, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and cayenne (if using). Stir to coat the vegetables with the spices and cook for 2 minutes.
5. Pour in the rinsed red lentils, coconut milk, and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to a simmer.
6. Cover the pot and let the curry simmer for 20‑25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the carrots are tender and the lentils have broken down, creating a thick sauce.
7. Stir in the maple syrup, then season with salt and black pepper to taste. Adjust the consistency with a splash of water or broth if the curry is too thick.
8. Serve the maple‑glazed carrot and lentil curry over a bed of coconut rice. Garnish with chopped cilantro and a squeeze of fresh lime juice. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Carrot and Lentil Curry with Coconut Rice

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea and Spinach Flatbread

Ingredients:
- 2 large whole‑wheat flatbreads or naan
- 1 cup canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 cups fresh baby spinach
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- ½ tsp ground turmeric
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- ¼ tsp red‑pepper flakes (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat a large skillet over medium heat and add the olive oil.
2. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger; sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
3. Stir in the chickpeas, turmeric, lemon zest, and red‑pepper flakes; cook 3–4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chickpeas are lightly browned.
4. Add the spinach and toss until wilted, about 2 minutes. Season with salt, pepper, and lemon juice; remove from heat.
5. Meanwhile, warm the flatbreads in a dry pan or under a broiler for 1–2 minutes until pliable.
6. Spread the chickpea‑spinach mixture evenly over each flatbread.
7. Sprinkle crumbled feta (if using) and garnish with fresh cilantro leaves.
8. Slice into wedges and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea and Spinach Flatbread

text:
Turmeric‑Honey Roasted Carrot and Lentil Salad with Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch sticks  
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed  
- 2 Tbsp honey  
- 1 tsp ground turmeric  
- 2 Tbsp olive oil  
- ½ tsp sea salt, plus more to taste  
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper  
- ½ cup pomegranate seeds  
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley  
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice  

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together honey, turmeric, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Add the carrot sticks and toss to coat evenly.  
3. Spread the carrots in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until caramelized and tender.  
4. While the carrots roast, place the rinsed lentils in a saucepan, cover with 2 cups water, bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cook 20‑25 minutes, or until lentils are just tender but still hold their shape. Drain any excess water and set aside.  
5. In a large mixing bowl combine the roasted carrots, cooked lentils, lemon juice, and chopped parsley. Toss gently to distribute the flavors.  
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed.  
7. Transfer the salad to a serving platter and sprinkle the pomegranate seeds over the top for a burst of sweetness and color.  
8. Serve warm or at room temperature as a hearty side or a light main dish. Enjoy!
title: Turmeric‑Honey Roasted Carrot and Lentil Salad with Pomegranate

text:
Honey‑Sriracha Glazed Tempeh with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 8 oz (225 g) tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- 2 Tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 2 Tbsp honey or maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp Sriracha sauce
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp lime zest
- 2 Tbsp lime juice
- 1 Tbsp sesame oil
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 cup shredded red cabbage, thinly sliced
- ½ cup edamame, shelled (optional)
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a shallow bowl, whisk together soy sauce, honey, Sriracha, grated ginger, lime zest, lime juice, sesame oil, and minced garlic to create the glaze.  
2. Place the tempeh strips in the glaze, toss to coat, and let marinate for at least 15 minutes while you prepare the quinoa.  
3. In a medium saucepan, combine the rinsed quinoa and coconut milk. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and fluff with a fork; season with a pinch of salt.  
4. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated tempeh strips (reserve any remaining glaze) and cook for 3‑4 minutes per side, until golden brown and caramelized.  
5. While the tempeh cooks, pour the reserved glaze into a small saucepan and simmer for 2‑3 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens slightly.  
6. Drizzle the thickened glaze over the cooked tempeh in the skillet, tossing to coat evenly. Remove from heat.  
7. Assemble the bowl: start with a base of coconut‑lime quinoa, top with glazed tempeh, shredded red cabbage, edamame (if using), and a sprinkle of fresh cilantro.  
8. Finish with an extra squeeze of lime juice, a drizzle of any remaining glaze, and season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve warm.
title: Honey‑Sriracha Glazed Tempeh with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa

text:
Ginger‑Lime Tempeh with Coconut‑Brown Rice and Roasted Broccolini

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 cup brown rice
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk (full‑fat)
- 1 ½ cups water
- 1 lb broccolini, trimmed
- 2 tbsp fresh ginger, minced
- 2 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tbsp lime zest
- 3 tbsp soy sauce (or tamari)
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tbsp sesame oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 green onions, sliced (for garnish)
- 2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, whisk together soy sauce, maple syrup, lime juice, lime zest, minced ginger, garlic, smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt and pepper.  
3. Add the tempeh cubes to the bowl, toss to coat, and let marinate while the oven heats (about 5 minutes).  
4. Meanwhile, combine the brown rice, coconut milk, and water in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 35‑40 minutes
title: Ginger‑Lime Tempeh with Coconut‑Brown Rice and Roasted Broccolini

text:
Saffron‑Infused Lentil and Roasted Eggplant Stack  

Ingredients:
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 large eggplants, sliced into ½‑inch rounds
- 1 ½ teaspoons saffron threads
- 2 ½ cups vegetable broth
- 1 medium onion, finely diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 ½ cups cherry tomatoes, halved
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 teaspoon ground coriander
- 2 tablespoons olive oil, plus more for brushing
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, chopped
- 1 tablespoon lemon juice
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, combine the saffron threads with 2 ¼ cups of hot vegetable broth; let steep for 10 minutes.  
3. Place the eggplant slices on the prepared sheet, brush both sides with olive oil, and season with salt, pepper, and smoked paprika. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and tender.  
4. While the eggplant roasts, heat 2 Tbsp olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in the minced garlic and cook another minute.  
5. Add the cumin and coriander; toast the spices for 30 seconds, then pour in the saffron‑infused broth (including the threads) and the remaining ¼ cup broth. Bring to a gentle boil.  
6. Add the rinsed lentils, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25‑30 minutes, or until lentils are tender but still hold their shape. Season with salt, pepper, and lemon juice.  
7. Remove the roasted eggplant from the oven. To assemble each stack, place one eggplant slice on a plate, spoon a generous layer of lentils over it, top with a handful of cherry tomato halves, and repeat the layers, ending with eggplant on top.  
8. Garnish each stack with chopped parsley and, if desired, crumbled feta. Serve warm, accompanied by a simple green salad or crusty bread.
title: Saffron‑Infused Lentil and Roasted Eggplant Stack

text:
Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Sweet Potato and Farro Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup farro, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth or water
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 1 tbsp fresh thyme leaves (or 1 tsp dried thyme)
- 1/2 tsp sea salt
- 1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 2 cups baby arugula
- 1/4 cup crumbled feta cheese
- 2 tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds
- Optional: 1 tbsp honey or maple syrup for a touch of sweetness

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the cubed sweet potato with 1 tablespoon olive oil, thyme, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
2. While the sweet potato roasts, bring the vegetable broth (or water) to a boil in a medium saucepan. Add the farro, reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook 20‑25 minutes until the grains are tender and the liquid is absorbed. Drain any excess liquid if needed.  
3. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, lemon juice, lemon zest, and a pinch of salt and pepper to create the dressing.  
4. Transfer the cooked farro to a large mixing bowl. Add the roasted sweet potato, baby arugula, and drizzle with the lemon‑thyme dressing. Toss gently to combine.  
5. Sprinkle the crumbled feta, toasted pumpkin seeds, and, if desired, a drizzle of honey or maple syrup over the salad.  
6. Serve warm or at room temperature as a hearty main dish or a vibrant side. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Sweet Potato and Farro Salad

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Tostada with Lime Crema

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 8 small corn tortillas
- 1 ripe avocado, sliced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped
- ¼ cup red onion, finely diced
- ¼ cup plain Greek yogurt (or vegan yogurt)
- Juice of 1 lime
- Zest of 1 lime
- Optional: hot sauce for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the diced sweet potatoes with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, cinnamon, maple syrup, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
3. Roast the sweet potatoes for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway through, until tender and caramelized.  
4. While the sweet potatoes roast, place the chickpeas on a separate portion of the baking sheet, drizzle with the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and roast for the last 15 minutes of the sweet potato cooking time.  
5. Meanwhile, prepare the lime crema: in a small bowl, whisk together the yogurt, lime juice, lime
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Tostada with Lime Crema

text:
Saffron‑Infused Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Chickpeas and Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups vegetable broth
- 1 ½ teaspoons saffron threads
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice
- ½ cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 Tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, combine the saffron threads with 2 Tbsp of hot vegetable broth; let steep for 5 minutes.  
2. Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the chickpeas with minced garlic, 1 Tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking halfway, until crisp and golden.  
3. In a medium saucepan, bring the remaining broth to a boil. Add the soaked saffron mixture and the rinsed quinoa; reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy.  
4. Remove the quinoa from heat and fluff with a fork. Stir in lemon juice, a drizzle of olive oil, and season with additional salt and pepper to taste.  
5. Transfer the quinoa to a serving bowl. Top with the roasted garlic chickpeas, sprinkle pomegranate seeds over the top, and garnish with chopped parsley.  
6. Serve warm or at room temperature as a vibrant side dish or a light main course.
title: Saffron‑Infused Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Chickpeas and Pomegranate

text:
Spiced Ginger Carrot and Chickpea Tagine

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch rounds
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 medium onion, thinly sliced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 in piece fresh ginger, grated (about 1 tbsp)
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- ½ tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tbsp tomato paste
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- 1 tbsp toasted almond slivers, for garnish
- Cooked couscous or quinoa, for serving

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy‑bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the sliced onion and sauté until softened, about 4 minutes.  
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for another minute until fragrant.  
3. Sprinkle the cumin, coriander, cinnamon, smoked paprika, and cayenne (if using) over the aromatics. Toast the spices for 30 seconds, stirring constantly to prevent burning.  
4. Add the carrot rounds to the pot, tossing to coat them in the spiced mixture. Cook for 2‑3 minutes, allowing the carrots to begin softening.  
5. Stir in the tomato paste, then pour in the vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.  
6. Add the chickpeas, season with salt and pepper, and continue to simmer uncovered for another 10‑12 minutes, or until the carrots are tender and the sauce has thickened slightly.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Remove from heat.  
8. Serve the tagine over a bed of fluffy couscous or quinoa. Garnish each portion with fresh cilantro leaves and toasted almond slivers for added texture and flavor.
title: Spiced Ginger Carrot and Chickpea Tagine

text:
Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Lentil Tacos with Avocado Crema  

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 cup dried brown lentils, rinsed
- 1 small red onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp chili powder
- ¼ tsp ground cinnamon
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 8 small corn tortillas
- 1 ripe avocado
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- Optional garnish: crumbled feta or cotija cheese  

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the diced sweet potatoes with 1 tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, cumin, smoked paprika, chili powder, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until caramelized and tender.  
3. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine the lentils with 2 cups water, a pinch of salt, and the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook for 20‑25 minutes, or until lentils are soft but not mushy. Drain any excess liquid.  
4. In a skillet over medium heat, sauté the onion until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add the garlic and cook another minute. Stir in the cooked lentils, season with additional salt and pepper, and heat through for 2‑3 minutes.  
5. Prepare the avocado crema: in a small bowl, mash the avocado with lime juice, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of maple syrup until smooth. Adjust seasoning to taste.  
6. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet or directly over a low flame, about 30 seconds per side, until pliable.  
7. Assemble each taco: place a spoonful of roasted sweet potatoes, top with lentil mixture, drizzle avocado crema, and sprinkle fresh cilantro. Add optional cheese if desired.  
8. Serve immediately, accompanied by extra lime wedges for squeezing. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Lentil Tacos with Avocado Crema

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Chickpea and Kale Pasta

Ingredients:
- 12 oz whole‑wheat spaghetti
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 4 cups chopped kale, stems removed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- zest of 1 lemon
- juice of 1 lemon
- ½ cup low‑sodium vegetable broth
- ¼ cup grated Parmesan cheese
- salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- pinch red‑pepper flakes (optional)

Instructions:
1. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti according to package directions until al dente; reserve ½ cup of the cooking water, then drain the pasta.  
2. While the pasta cooks, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger, sautéing for 30 seconds until fragrant.  
3. Stir in the chickpeas and cook, stirring occasionally, for 3–4 minutes until they begin to brown slightly.  
4. Add the chopped kale to the skillet and toss until it wilts, about 2 minutes.  
5. Pour in the vegetable broth, lemon zest, and lemon juice; bring the mixture to a gentle simmer and let it reduce by half, about 3 minutes.  
6. Add the cooked spaghetti to the skillet, tossing to combine. If the sauce seems dry, add a splash of the reserved pasta water until the desired consistency is reached.  
7. Remove the pan from heat and stir in the grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt, black pepper, and red‑pepper flakes, if using.  
8. Divide the pasta among serving bowls, garnish with extra Parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil if desired, and serve immediately.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Chickpea and Kale Pasta

text:
Spiced Cardamom Pumpkin and Chickpea Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 lb (450 g) fresh pumpkin, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 large onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch piece fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp ground cardamom
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 cups fresh spinach leaves
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional garnish: toasted pumpkin seeds and fresh cilantro

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Sprinkle the ground cardamom, cumin, and coriander over the aromatics; toast the spices for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
4. Add the cubed pumpkin and chickpeas to the pot, mixing to coat them with the spice mixture.
5. Pour in the vegetable broth, bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer. Cover and cook for 15‑20 minutes, or until the pumpkin is tender.
6. Stir in the coconut milk and let the stew simmer uncovered for an additional 5 minutes to thicken slightly.
7. Fold in the fresh spinach leaves and cook until wilted, about 2 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
8. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with toasted pumpkin seeds and chopped cilantro if desired, and serve hot.
title: Spiced Cardamom Pumpkin and Chickpea Stew

text:
Turmeric‑Honey Glazed Carrot and Lentil Salad with Pomegranate  

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and sliced into thin ribbons
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 Tbsp honey
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 Tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley  

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan, combine the lentils with 3 cups water; bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook until tender, about 20 minutes. Drain and set aside.  
2. While the lentils cook, whisk together honey, olive oil, turmeric, cumin, salt, pepper, and lemon juice in a large bowl to form the glaze.  
3. Add the carrot ribbons to the bowl and toss thoroughly, ensuring each piece is coated with the glaze.  
4. Heat a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the glazed carrots and sauté for 5‑7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they are just tender and lightly caramelized.  
5. Transfer the cooked carrots to a serving platter. Top with the cooked lentils, pomegranate seeds, toasted pumpkin seeds, and chopped parsley.  
6. Drizzle any remaining glaze over the salad, give a final gentle toss, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Turmeric‑Honey Glazed Carrot and Lentil Salad with Pomegranate

text:
Spiced Coconut‑Lime Chickpea & Sweet Potato Gnocchi

Ingredients:
- 1 lb sweet potato gnocchi (store‑bought or homemade)
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp coconut oil
- 1 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tsp lime zest
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional for heat)
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil; add the gnocchi and cook according to package directions, usually until they float to the surface (about 2‑3 minutes). Drain and set aside.  
2. While the gnocchi cooks, heat the coconut oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the chickpeas and sauté for 3‑4 minutes until lightly golden.  
3. Sprinkle the cumin, smoked paprika, cayenne (if using), salt, and pepper over the chickpeas; stir to coat and cook another minute.  
4. Add the cooked gnocchi to the skillet, tossing gently to combine with the spiced chickpeas. Cook for 2‑3 minutes, allowing the gnocchi to crisp on the edges.  
5. Stir in the lime juice, lime zest, and chopped cilantro; toss everything together until evenly distributed and heated through.  
6. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lime juice as desired.  
7. Serve immediately, garnished with extra cilantro and a squeeze of lime if desired. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Coconut‑Lime Chickpea & Sweet Potato Gnocchi

text:
Maple‑Glazed Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Power Salad with Citrus Vinaigrette

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- ¼ teaspoon ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 4 cups mixed baby greens (spinach, arugula, kale)
- ½ red bell pepper, thinly sliced
- ¼ red onion, thinly sliced
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tablespoons crumbled feta cheese (optional)

Citrus Vinaigrette:
- 3 tablespoons freshly squeezed orange juice
- 1 tablespoon lemon juice
- 1 teaspoon honey
- ¼ cup extra‑virgin olive oil
- Pinch of salt

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with maple syrup, olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the sweet potatoes in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and caramelized.  
4. While the sweet potatoes roast, whisk together orange juice, lemon juice, honey, olive oil, and a pinch of salt in a small jar; shake well to emulsify.  
5. In a large salad bowl combine the mixed greens, sliced red bell pepper, red onion, and toasted pumpkin seeds.  
6. Add the roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas to the bowl; toss gently to distribute.  
7. Drizzle the citrus vinaigrette over the salad and toss again until everything is lightly coated.  
8. Sprinkle crumbled feta on top, if using, and serve immediately. Enjoy your bright, maple‑sweet, and protein‑packed power salad!
title: Maple‑Glazed Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Power Salad with Citrus Vinaigrette

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Chickpea and Sweet Potato Curry with Coconut Rice  

Ingredients:
- 1 cup dried chickpeas (or 2 cups cooked chickpeas)
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 ½ cups jasmine rice
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- 1 ½ cups water
- 1 ½ tbsp fresh ginger, minced
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp curry powder
- 1 tbsp coconut oil
- ½ tsp ground turmeric
- ½ tsp sea salt (plus more to taste)
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)
- Optional: 1 small red chili, sliced for heat  

Instructions:
1. If using dried chickpeas, rinse them, place in a pot with water, bring to a boil, then simmer for 1 hour until tender. Drain and set aside. (Skip this step if using pre‑cooked chickpeas.)  
2. In a medium saucepan, combine the rice, 1 cup coconut milk, and 1 ½ cups water. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until the rice is fluffy. Remove from heat and let stand covered.  
3. While the rice cooks, heat the coconut oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and ginger; sauté 1 minute until fragrant.  
4. Stir in the curry powder, turmeric, and a pinch of salt;
title: Lemon‑Ginger Chickpea and Sweet Potato Curry with Coconut Rice

text:
Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Lentil Tostada with Chipotle Crema  

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 cup cooked brown lentils (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 8 small corn tortillas
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ½ cup chipotle mayo (mix ¼ cup mayo with 1 tsp chipotle in adobo, plus a squeeze of lime)
- 1 ripe avocado, sliced
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- 1 lime, cut into wedges  

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the diced sweet potatoes with olive oil, maple syrup, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until caramelized and tender.  
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 30 seconds per side, then place them on a baking sheet and bake for 5 minutes to crisp lightly.  
3. In a bowl, combine the roasted sweet potatoes with the cooked lentils, adjusting seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a drizzle of maple syrup if desired.  
4. Assemble each tostada: spread a generous spoonful of chipotle mayo on the tortilla, top with the sweet potato‑lentil mixture, add avocado slices, and sprinkle fresh cilantro.  
5. Serve immediately with lime wedges on the side for squeezing over the top. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Lentil Tostada with Chipotle Crema

text:
Maple‑Glazed Portobello Mushroom and Quinoa Stack

Ingredients:
- 4 large portobello mushroom caps, stems removed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 3 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves (or ½ tsp dried)
- 1 cup baby spinach leaves
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional garnish: toasted pumpkin seeds and a drizzle of extra maple syrup

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, olive oil, minced garlic, thyme, salt, and pepper.  
3. Brush both sides of each mushroom cap generously with the maple‑garlic mixture and place them on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast the mushrooms for 15‑18 minutes, flipping once, until they are tender and caramelized.  
5. While the mushrooms roast, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.  
6. Stir the baby spinach into the hot quinoa; the residual heat will wilt the leaves. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.  
7. To assemble the stack, place a spoonful of quinoa‑spinach mixture on a plate, top with a roasted mushroom cap, add another layer of quinoa, and finish with the remaining mushroom cap.  
8. Garnish with toasted pumpkin seeds and an extra drizzle of maple syrup if desired. Serve warm.
title: Maple‑Glazed Portobello Mushroom and Quinoa Stack

text:
Spicy Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Garlic Quinoa and Kale

Ingredients:
- 8 oz (225 g) tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp red‑pepper flakes
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 4 cups kale, stems removed and torn
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a shallow bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, smoked paprika, and red‑pepper flakes.
