3. Toss the tempeh strips in the glaze, ensuring each piece is coated, then spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast the tempeh for 15‑20 minutes, flipping halfway through, until the edges are caramelized and crisp.  
5. While the tempeh roasts, combine quinoa and water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until fluffy.  
6. In a small skillet, heat 1 Tbsp olive oil over medium heat; add half the minced garlic and sauté for 30 seconds, then stir in the cooked quinoa, season with salt and pepper, and keep warm.  
7. In a large skillet, heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil over medium‑high heat; add the remaining garlic and sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute.  
8. Add the kale to the skillet, tossing until wilted, about 3‑4 minutes; drizzle with lemon juice and season with salt and pepper.  
9. To serve, divide the garlic quinoa among plates, top with sautéed kale, and arrange the spicy maple‑glazed tempeh strips on top.  
10. Garnish with an extra pinch of red‑pepper flakes or a drizzle of maple syrup if desired, and enjoy immediately.
title: Spicy Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Garlic Quinoa and Kale

text:
Spiced Orange‑Ginger Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Kale

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 cups kale leaves, stems removed and torn
- 1 tbsp fresh orange zest
- 2 Tbsp fresh orange juice
- 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp soy sauce (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Toss the chickpeas with 1 Tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper; spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking the pan halfway, until crisp and golden.
2. While the chickpeas roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.
3. In a large skillet, heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil over medium heat. Add the kale and sauté 3‑4 minutes, until wilted but still bright green. Season lightly with salt and pepper, then set aside.
4. In a small bowl, whisk together orange zest, orange juice, grated ginger, maple syrup, and soy sauce (if using) to create a glaze.
5. Add the cooked quinoa to the skillet with the kale, pour the orange‑ginger glaze over, and toss to combine, cooking 1‑2 minutes until the mixture is evenly coated and heated through.
6. Transfer the quinoa‑kale mixture to a serving bowl, top with the roasted chickpeas, and finish with an extra drizzle of glaze or a squeeze of fresh orange juice if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Spiced Orange‑Ginger Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Kale

text:
Harissa‑Glazed Cauliflower Steaks with Pomegranate Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 large cauliflower, cut into 1‑inch thick “steaks”
- 2 tbsp harissa paste
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth or water
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds
- 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh mint
- 2 tbsp sliced toasted almonds

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together harissa paste, olive oil, salt, and pepper.  
3. Brush both sides of each cauliflower steak generously with the harissa mixture and place on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast the cauliflower for 20‑25 minutes, flipping halfway through, until tender and caramelized at the edges.  
5. While the cauliflower roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed.  
6. Remove the quinoa from heat and fluff with a fork; stir in lemon juice, chopped mint, and half of the pomegranate seeds.  
7. To serve, divide the quinoa among plates, top each with a harissa‑glazed cauliflower steak, and garnish with the remaining pomegranate seeds and toasted almonds. Enjoy while hot!
title: Harissa‑Glazed Cauliflower Steaks with Pomegranate Quinoa

text:
Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Carrot and Barley Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 cup pearl barley
- 3 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4‑inch dice
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 teaspoon lemon zest
- 2 teaspoons fresh thyme leaves (or 1 tsp dried thyme)
- 1/2 cup vegetable broth
- 1/4 cup toasted slivered almonds
- 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the diced carrots with olive oil, lemon zest, thyme, salt, and pepper; spread them in a single layer and roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway, until caramelized and tender.  
3. While the carrots roast, rinse the barley under cold water, then combine it with 2 cups water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook 30‑35 minutes until the grains are tender and the liquid is absorbed; fluff with a fork.  
4. Transfer the cooked barley to a large bowl, add the roasted carrots, toasted almonds, lemon juice, and a drizzle of olive oil if desired.  
5. Gently toss everything together, adjusting seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice to taste.  
6. Serve warm as a hearty side dish or a light main course, garnished with a few extra thyme leaves for color.
title: Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Carrot and Barley Pilaf

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Parsnip and Chickpea Salad with Pomegranate Vinaigrette

Ingredients:
- 2 large parsnips, peeled and cut into ½‑inch sticks
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- ¼ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 Tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds
- 3 Tbsp pomegranate vinaigrette (store‑bought or homemade)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together maple syrup, cinnamon, olive oil, salt, and pepper.  
3. Add the parsnip sticks to the bowl and toss until evenly coated.  
4. Spread the parsnips in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender.  
5. While the parsnips roast, place the chickpeas on a separate half‑sheet, drizzle with a little olive oil, and roast for the last 12‑15 minutes until slightly crisp.  
6. In a large serving bowl, combine the roasted parsnips, chickpeas, pomegranate seeds, and toasted pumpkin seeds.  
7. Drizzle the salad with pomegranate vinaigrette and toss gently to coat all ingredients.  
8. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with an extra sprinkle of pumpkin seeds and a few pomegranate arils for color.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Parsnip and Chickpea Salad with Pomegranate Vinaigrette

text:
Lemon‑Basil Orzo with Roasted Eggplant and Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 1 cup orzo pasta
- 1 medium eggplant, cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- ¼ cup fresh basil leaves, finely chopped
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Toss the eggplant cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper, then spread on a baking sheet.
2. Roast the eggplant for 20‑25 minutes, stirring once, until golden and tender. Remove from the oven and set aside to cool slightly.
3. While the eggplant roasts, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the orzo and cook according to package directions (usually 8‑10 minutes) until al dente. Drain, reserving ¼ cup of the cooking water.
4. In a large bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, minced garlic, lemon zest, lemon juice, chopped basil, and the reserved cooking water. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
5. Add the cooked orzo and roasted eggplant to the bowl with the dressing. Toss gently to combine and coat evenly.
6. Transfer the mixture to a serving platter or individual bowls. Sprinkle pomegranate seeds and crumbled feta (if using) over the top.
7. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with a few extra basil leaves if desired. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Basil Orzo with Roasted Eggplant and Pomegranate

text:
Spiced Cardamom Sweet Potato and Lentil Shepherd’s Pie

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 2 carrots, diced
- 2 celery stalks, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp ground cardamom
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp tomato paste
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Place the sweet potato cubes on a baking sheet, drizzle with a little olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and roast for 20‑25 minutes until tender.
2. While the potatoes roast, heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots, and celery; sauté for 5‑7 minutes until softened.
3. Stir in the garlic, ground cardamom, smoked paprika, and cumin; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Add the rinsed lentils, tomato paste, and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and most liquid is absorbed. Season with salt and pepper.
5. Mash the roasted sweet potatoes with a fork or potato masher; stir in a pinch of salt, pepper, and a drizzle of olive oil for extra richness.
6. Transfer the lentil mixture to a 9‑inch baking dish, spreading it evenly. Top with the mashed sweet potatoes, smoothing the surface with a spatula.
7. Bake the assembled shepherd’s pie for 15‑20 minutes, or until the top is lightly golden and the filling is bubbling.
8. Remove from the oven, let cool for a few minutes, then garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Cardamom Sweet Potato and Lentil Shepherd’s Pie

text:
Spiced Cardamom Sweet Potato and Black Bean Chili

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 medium onion, finely chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon ground cardamom
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper (optional, for heat)
- 1 (14‑oz) can diced tomatoes
- 1 (15‑oz) can black beans, drained and rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon tomato paste
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)
- Lime wedges (for serving)

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.  
2. Stir in the garlic and cook for another 30 seconds until fragrant.  
3. Sprinkle the ground cardamom, smoked paprika, cumin, and cayenne (if using) over the aromatics; toast the spices for 1 minute, stirring constantly.  
4. Add the diced sweet potatoes to the pot and toss to coat them with the spiced mixture.  
5. Stir in the tomato paste, then pour in the diced tomatoes, black beans, and vegetable broth.  
6. Bring the chili to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25‑30 minutes, or until the sweet potatoes are tender.  
7. Season with salt and pepper to taste. If the chili is too thick, add a splash more broth or water.  
8. Ladle the chili into bowls, garnish with chopped cilantro, and serve with lime wedges on the side. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Cardamom Sweet Potato and Black Bean Chili

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 ½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Pinch of saffron threads
- ¼ cup warm water
- 1 cup cooked quinoa
- 1 cup baby spinach leaves
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tbsp tahini
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tsp maple syrup
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Toss the sweet potato cubes and chickpeas with olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread them in a single layer on a baking sheet.
2. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until the sweet potatoes are tender and lightly caramelized and the chickpeas are crisp.
3. While the vegetables roast, place the saffron threads in the warm water and let steep for 5 minutes to release color and flavor.
4. In a small bowl, whisk together the saffron‑infused water, tahini, lemon juice, maple syrup, and a pinch of salt to create a smooth dressing. Adjust seasoning with additional lemon juice or maple syrup if desired.
5. Divide the cooked quinoa among four bowls. Top each with a handful of baby spinach, a portion of the roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas, and a sprinkle of toasted pumpkin seeds.
6. Drizzle the saffron‑tahini dressing over each bowl, finish with a final grind of black pepper, and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy a vibrant, nutrient‑dense Buddha bowl bursting with earthy saffron notes.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Parsnip and Quinoa Salad with Pomegranate Vinaigrette

Ingredients:
- 2 large parsnips, peeled and cut into ½‑inch dice
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- ½ cup pomegranate seeds
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh mint
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley

For the vinaigrette:
- 3 Tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil
- 2 Tbsp pomegranate juice
- 1 Tbsp apple cider vinegar
- 1 tsp Dijon mustard
- 1 tsp honey
- Pinch of salt

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the diced parsnips with olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the parsnips in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden‑brown and tender.  
4. While the parsnips roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.  
5. Prepare the vinaigrette: whisk together olive oil, pomegranate juice, apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, honey, and a pinch of salt in a small bowl until emulsified.  
6. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted parsnips, pomegranate seeds, toasted pumpkin seeds, mint, and parsley. Drizzle the vinaigrette over the salad and toss gently to distribute.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt or a splash of pomegranate juice if desired.  
8. Serve the salad warm or at room temperature, garnished with a few extra pomegranate seeds and pumpkin seeds for crunch. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Parsnip and Quinoa Salad with Pomegranate Vinaigrette

text:
Cinnamon‑Lime Roasted Cauliflower and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 large head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- Zest of 1 lime
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1/4 cup red onion, thinly sliced
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1/4 cup pumpkin seeds, toasted
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a large bowl, toss cauliflower florets with 1 tbsp olive oil, cinnamon, lime zest, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.
3. While the cauliflower roasts, combine quinoa and 2 cups water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside to cool slightly.
4. In a small skillet over medium heat, add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and the chickpeas. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5‑7 minutes until lightly crisp. Season with a pinch of salt.
5. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted cauliflower, crisp chickpeas, red onion, and cilantro.
6. Drizzle the lime juice over the salad, toss gently to coat, and adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed.
7. Transfer the salad to a serving platter and sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds on top for crunch. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Lime Roasted Cauliflower and Quinoa Salad

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Shrimp with Coconut‑Lime Rice and Roasted Asparagus

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup jasmine rice
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- ½ cup water
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 lb asparagus, trimmed and cut into 2‑inch pieces
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional garnish: chopped cilantro and lime wedges

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the asparagus with ½ tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper, spread on a baking sheet, and roast for 12‑15 minutes, until tender‑crisp.
2. While the asparagus roasts, rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear. Combine rice, coconut milk, water, turmeric, and a pinch of salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes.
3. In a large skillet, heat the remaining ½ tbsp olive oil over medium‑high heat. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger; sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
4. Add the shrimp to the skillet, drizzle with lime juice and lemon juice, and season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, for
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Shrimp with Coconut‑Lime Rice and Roasted Asparagus

text:
Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Edamame

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- zest of 1 lime
- juice of 1 lime
- 1 tablespoon coconut oil
- 1 cup frozen edamame, thawed
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine the rinsed quinoa and coconut milk; bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is tender.
2. While the quinoa cooks, preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Toss the thawed edamame with coconut oil, minced garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread in a single layer on a baking sheet.
3. Roast the seasoned edamame for 12‑15 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until lightly crisp and golden.
4. Fluff the cooked quinoa with a fork and stir in the lime zest, lime juice, and chopped cilantro; season with additional salt and pepper to taste.
5. Transfer the quinoa to a serving bowl, top with the roasted garlic edamame, and garnish with extra cilantro or a lime wedge if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Spiced Coconut Lime Quinoa with Roasted Garlic Edamame

text:
Sesame‑Crusted Tofu with Lemon‑Basil Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 2 tbsp sesame seeds (mixed black and white)
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- ¼ cup fresh basil leaves, chopped
- ¼ cup cherry tomatoes, halved
- 2 tbsp toasted pine nuts
- 1 tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil (for dressing)
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. Toss the tofu cubes with olive oil, salt, and pepper, then roll them in the sesame seeds until evenly coated. Arrange on the prepared baking sheet.
3. Roast the tofu for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until the crust is golden and the tofu is crisp.
4. While the tofu roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.
5. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large bowl. Stir in lemon juice, lemon zest, chopped basil, cherry tomatoes, toasted pine nuts, and extra‑virgin olive oil. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
6. Divide the quinoa salad among serving plates, top each with a generous portion of sesame‑crusted tofu, and garnish with additional basil leaves if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Sesame‑Crusted Tofu with Lemon‑Basil Quinoa Salad

text:
Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato & Black Bean Breakfast Burrito

Ingredients:
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and diced
- 1 tablespoon maple syrup
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 cup canned black beans, drained and rinsed
- 4 large eggs
- 1/4 cup milk (or plant‑based alternative)
- 1/2 cup shredded cheddar cheese
- 4 large flour tortillas
- 1 avocado, sliced
- 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Hot sauce (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the diced sweet potato with olive oil, maple syrup, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Spread evenly on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway, until tender and caramelized.  
3. While the sweet potatoes roast, heat a skillet over medium heat and add the black beans. Cook for 3‑4 minutes, stirring, until warmed through; set aside.  
4. In a separate bowl, whisk together the eggs, milk, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Pour into the same skillet and scramble until just set, then remove from heat.  
5. Warm the flour tortillas in a dry pan or microwave for about 20 seconds to make them pliable.  
6. Assemble each burrito: place a quarter of the roasted sweet potatoes, a quarter of the black beans, scrambled eggs, shredded cheddar, avocado slices, and a sprinkle of cilantro onto the center of a tortilla. Drizzle with hot sauce if desired.  
7. Fold the sides of the tortilla over the filling, then roll tightly from the bottom up to enclose the contents.  
8. Optional: Return the assembled burritos to the skillet, seam side down, and cook for 1‑2 minutes per side to crisp the exterior.  
9. Serve immediately, garnished with extra cilantro and a side of salsa if liked.
title: Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato & Black Bean Breakfast Burrito

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea and Spinach Stir‑Fry

Ingredients:
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 3 cups fresh baby spinach
- 1 medium yellow onion, thinly sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1 tablespoon soy sauce (or tamari for gluten‑free)
- 1 tablespoon lemon juice
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- ½ teaspoon red‑pepper flakes (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Cooked brown rice or quinoa, for serving

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the sliced onion and sauté for 3‑4 minutes until softened.
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
3. Sprinkle the turmeric over the aromatics, stirring to coat, then add the chickpeas. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 4‑5 minutes until the chickpeas are heated through and lightly browned.
4. Add the soy sauce, lemon juice, and red‑pepper flakes; mix well and let the flavors meld for another minute.
5. Toss in the fresh spinach and cook, stirring, until just wilted, about 2 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
6. Serve the stir‑fry over warm brown rice or quinoa, drizzling any remaining pan sauce on top. Enjoy immediately.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea and Spinach Stir‑Fry

text:
Spiced Orange‑Maple Tempeh with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa and Roasted Broccoli

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 2 Tbsp orange marmalade
- 1 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- 1 Tbsp coconut oil, divided
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- 1 Tbsp lime juice
- 1 lb broccoli florets
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro, chopped (optional garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the broccoli florets with olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread on the sheet and roast for 15‑20 minutes, until crisp‑tender and lightly browned.  
3. While the broccoli roasts, whisk together orange marmalade, maple syrup, smoked paprika, cumin, and ½ Tbsp coconut oil in a bowl. Add the tempeh cubes and coat evenly; let marinate for 5 minutes.  
4. Heat the remaining ½ Tbsp coconut oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated tempeh and sauté for 6‑8 minutes, turning occasionally, until the glaze caramelizes and the tempeh is golden.  
5. In a medium saucepan, combine rinsed quinoa and coconut milk; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy.  
6. Remove the quinoa from heat and stir in lime juice, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of olive oil for extra shine.  
7. To serve, spoon a bed of coconut‑lime quinoa onto plates, top with the spiced orange‑maple tempeh, and arrange roasted broccoli around the edges.  
8. Garnish with chopped cilantro, if desired, and enjoy the sweet‑savory‑tangy flavor combo.
title: Spiced Orange‑Maple Tempeh with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa and Roasted Broccoli

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Shrimp with Garlic‑Herb Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 lb (450 g) large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 tbsp coconut oil
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- Zest of 1 lime
- Juice of 1 lime
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups low‑sodium vegetable broth
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- 1 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 tbsp toasted coconut flakes (optional)

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, toss the shrimp with turmeric, smoked paprika, salt, pepper, half the minced garlic, lime zest, and lime juice. Let marinate for 10 minutes.  
2. While the shrimp marinates, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and fluff with a fork.  
3. Heat coconut oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the shrimp in a single layer and cook 2‑3 minutes per side, until pink and opaque. Transfer shrimp to a plate.  
4. In the same skillet, add olive oil and the remaining garlic; sauté 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the cooked quinoa, stirring to coat with the garlic‑oil mixture; heat for 2 minutes.  
5. Stir in the chopped parsley, cilantro, and toasted coconut flakes (if using). Season with additional salt and pepper to taste.  
6. Plate the garlic‑herb quinoa and top with the turmeric shrimp. Garnish with extra lime zest and a drizzle of olive oil if desired. Enjoy warm!
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Shrimp with Garlic‑Herb Quinoa

text:
Maple‑Saffron Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Carrot Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 8 oz (225 g) tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp saffron threads, steeped in 2 tbsp warm water
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 2 large carrots, peeled and cut into ¼‑inch dice
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups vegetable broth
- 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Chopped fresh cilantro, for garnish

Instructions:
1. In a shallow bowl combine maple syrup, saffron‑infused water, soy sauce, smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt; whisk until smooth. Add the tempeh strips, toss to coat, and let marinate while you prepare the vegetables (about 10 minutes).  
2. Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Spread the diced carrots on a parchment‑lined baking sheet, drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until caramelized and tender.  
3. While the carrots roast, heat a skillet over medium‑high heat. Remove tempeh from the marinade (reserve the liquid) and sear the strips for 3‑4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crisp. Transfer to a plate.  
4. In the same skillet, add the reserved glaze and simmer for 2‑3 minutes until slightly thickened. Return the tempeh to the pan, toss to coat, and keep warm.  
5. Meanwhile, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and cook 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork, stir in lemon juice, and season with salt and pepper.  
6. To serve, spoon quinoa onto plates, top with roasted carrots and glazed tempeh strips, and garnish with chopped cilantro. Enjoy warm!
title: Maple‑Saffron Glazed Tempeh with Roasted Carrot Quinoa

text:
Spiced Lemongrass Tofu with Coconut Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups coconut milk
- 1 cup water
- 2 stalks lemongrass, white part only, finely minced
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp turmeric powder
- 1 tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 2 tbsp vegetable oil
- 1 red bell pepper, sliced
- 1 cup snap peas
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Juice of 1 lime
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15‑18 minutes until liquid
title: Spiced Lemongrass Tofu with Coconut Quinoa

text:
Crispy Sesame‑Ginger Tofu with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- 1 ½ cups water
- 2 tbsp sesame oil
- 2 tbsp soy sauce (or tamari for gluten‑free)
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tbsp freshly grated ginger
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
title: Crispy Sesame‑Ginger Tofu with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa

text:
Maple‑Glazed Chickpea and Roasted Sweet Pepper Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 large red bell peppers, sliced into strips
- 2 large yellow bell peppers, sliced into strips
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup cooked quinoa, cooled
- ¼ cup toasted sliced almonds
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a large bowl, toss the sliced red and yellow peppers with ½ tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 15‑20 minutes, turning once, until the edges are lightly charred. Remove from the oven and set aside to cool slightly.
3. While the peppers roast, combine the chickpeas, remaining ½ tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, maple syrup, and a pinch of salt and pepper in a separate bowl. Toss until the chickpeas are evenly coated.
4. Transfer the chickpea mixture to a second baking sheet (or the same sheet after the peppers are removed) and roast for 12‑15 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until the chickpeas are golden and slightly crisp.
5. In a large serving bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted sweet peppers, and maple‑glazed chickpeas. Drizzle with fresh lemon juice and gently toss to distribute the flavors.
6. Sprinkle the toasted sliced almonds and chopped parsley over the top. Adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if desired.
7. Serve warm or at room temperature as a hearty salad or light main dish. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Chickpea and Roasted Sweet Pepper Salad

text:
Sesame‑Ginger Roasted Cauliflower with Turmeric Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 large head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 2 tbsp sesame oil
- 1 tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp freshly grated ginger
- 1 garlic clove, minced
- 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups water or vegetable broth
- ½ tsp ground turmeric
- ¼ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- Salt to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl whisk together sesame oil, soy sauce, maple syrup, grated ginger, and minced garlic.  
3. Toss cauliflower florets in the sauce until evenly coated; spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
4. Roast cauliflower 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway, until golden‑brown and tender.  
5. While the cauliflower roasts, combine quinoa, water (or broth), turmeric, cumin, and a pinch of salt in a saucepan; bring to a boil.  
6. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until quinoa is fluffy and liquid is absorbed; remove from heat and let sit 5 minutes.  
7. Fluff quinoa with a fork and stir in lime juice and half of the chopped cilantro; adjust salt and pepper to taste.  
8. Transfer roasted cauliflower to a serving platter, drizzle any pan juices over the top, and sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds and the remaining cilantro.  
9. Serve the sesame‑ginger cauliflower alongside the turmeric quinoa for a balanced, aromatic meal.
title: Sesame‑Ginger Roasted Cauliflower with Turmeric Quinoa

text:
Maple‑Miso Glazed Eggplant with Coconut Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 2 medium eggplants, sliced into ½‑inch rounds
- 3 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp white miso paste
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 Tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tsp freshly grated ginger
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 Tbsp sesame oil
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk (full‑fat)
- ½ cup water
- 1 lime, zest and juice
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- 1 Tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl whisk together maple syrup, miso paste, soy sauce, rice vinegar, ginger, garlic, sesame oil, lime zest, and a pinch of salt and pepper.  
3. Brush both sides of each eggplant slice generously with the maple‑miso glaze, placing them on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast the eggplant for 20‑25 minutes, flipping halfway through, until the edges are caramelized and the flesh is tender.  
5. While the eggplant roasts, combine quinoa, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15‑18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy.  
6. Remove the quinoa from heat and stir in lime juice and half of the chopped cilantro. Fluff with a fork.  
7. Transfer the roasted eggplant to a serving platter. Spoon a bed of coconut quinoa underneath the slices. Drizzle any remaining glaze from the baking sheet over the top.  
8. Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and the remaining cilantro. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Maple‑Miso Glazed Eggplant with Coconut Quinoa

text:
Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa and Roasted Brussels Sprouts

Ingredients:
- 8 oz (225 g) tempeh, sliced into ½‑inch strips
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 Tbsp lime juice
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 12 oz (340 g) Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional garnish: chopped fresh cilantro and lime zest

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, soy sauce, smoked paprika, and grated ginger.  
3. Toss the tempeh strips in the glaze, ensuring each piece is well‑coated; set aside.  
4. In a separate bowl, toss the halved Brussels sprouts with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread them cut‑side‑down on the prepared baking sheet.  
5. Roast the Brussels sprouts for 15 minutes, then flip them over and continue roasting another 10 minutes, until crisp‑tender and caramelized.  
6. While the sprouts roast, combine the rinsed quinoa and coconut milk in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed.  
7. Remove the quinoa from heat, stir in lime juice, and fluff with a fork. Season with a pinch of salt.  
8. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the glazed tempeh strips and cook 3‑4 minutes per side, until the edges are caramelized and the glaze is sticky.  
9. To serve, divide the coconut‑lime quinoa among plates, top with roasted Brussels sprouts, and arrange the maple‑glazed tempeh on top.  
10. Garnish with chopped cilantro and a sprinkle of lime zest
title: Maple‑Glazed Tempeh with Coconut‑Lime Quinoa and Roasted Brussels Sprouts

text:
Saffron‑Infused Coconut‑Lime Lentil and Spinach Stew

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 can (13.5 oz) full‑fat coconut milk
- 3 cups vegetable broth
- 2 cups fresh spinach, roughly chopped
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- ½ tsp saffron threads
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tsp lime zest
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, combine the saffron threads with 2 tablespoons of hot vegetable broth; let steep for 5 minutes.  
2. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes.  
3. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for another 1 minute until fragrant.  
4. Add the rinsed red lentils, cumin, and the saffron‑infused broth to the pot; stir to combine.  
5. Pour in the remaining vegetable broth and the coconut milk. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer, uncovered, for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and the stew has thickened.  
6. Season with salt and pepper, then stir in the lime juice, lime zest, and chopped spinach. Cook for 2‑3 minutes, just until the spinach wilts.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning, adding more lime juice or salt if desired.  
8. Ladle the stew into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, and serve hot.
title: Saffron‑Infused Coconut‑Lime Lentil and Spinach Stew

text:
Spiced Cardamom Sweet Potato and Chickpea Soup

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 1 medium onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh grated ginger
- 1 tsp ground cardamom
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp smoked paprika
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- A squeeze of lime juice (optional)

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 4‑5 minutes.  
2. Stir in the garlic, ginger, ground cardamom, cumin, and smoked paprika; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
3. Add the diced sweet potatoes and chickpeas, tossing to coat them with the spice mixture.  
4. Pour in the vegetable broth, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until the sweet potatoes are very tender, about 15‑20 minutes.  
5. Using an immersion blender (or transferring in batches to a countertop
title: Spiced Cardamom Sweet Potato and Chickpea Soup

text:
Lemon‑Basil Orzo with Roasted Cauliflower and Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 1 cup orzo pasta
- 1 medium head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- ¼ cup fresh basil leaves, chopped
- ½ cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss cauliflower florets with 1 Tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until golden and tender.
2. While the cauliflower roasts, bring the vegetable broth to a boil in a medium saucepan. Add the orzo and cook according to package directions (usually 8‑10 minutes) until al dente; drain any excess liquid.
3. In a large skillet, heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
4. Stir the cooked orzo into the skillet, then add lemon zest, lemon juice, and chopped basil. Toss to combine and season with salt and pepper to taste.
5. Transfer the roasted cauliflower to the skillet and gently fold it into the orzo mixture.
6. Remove from heat, sprinkle pomegranate seeds over the top, and serve warm. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Basil Orzo with Roasted Cauliflower and Pomegranate

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea and Kale Stir‑Fry

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 4 cups kale, stems removed and torn into bite‑size pieces
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, minced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 2 tablespoons soy sauce (or tamari for gluten‑free)
- 1 tablespoon sesame oil
- 1 teaspoon honey or maple syrup
- ½ teaspoon red‑pepper flakes (optional, for heat)
- 2 green onions, sliced
- 1 lime, juiced
- Cooked rice or quinoa, for serving (optional)

Instructions:
1. Heat the sesame oil in a large skillet or wok over medium‑high heat until shimmering.  
2. Add the minced garlic and ginger; sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.  
3. Sprinkle the turmeric over the aromatics and stir to combine, cooking for another 15 seconds.  
4. Add the chickpeas to the pan, tossing them in the spice mixture. Cook for 3–4 minutes, allowing the chickpeas to brown slightly.  
5. Pour in the soy sauce and honey, stirring to coat the chickpeas evenly.  
6. Add the kale and red‑pepper flakes; toss everything together and cook, stirring frequently, until the kale wilts but retains a bright green color, about 4–5 minutes.  
7. Remove the pan from heat and stir in the lime juice and sliced green onions. Adjust seasoning with extra soy sauce or a pinch more salt if needed.  
8. Serve the stir‑fry hot over cooked rice or quinoa, garnished with additional green onion or a drizzle of sesame oil if desired.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea and Kale Stir‑Fry

text:
Spiced Cardamom Pear and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 2 ripe pears, cored and thinly sliced
- 1/3 cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped
- 1/4 cup dried cranberries
- 2 cups baby arugula
- 1/4 cup crumbled feta cheese
- 3 tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tsp honey
- 1/2 tsp ground cardamom
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine the quinoa and water; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and allow to cool slightly.
2. While the quinoa cooks, toast the walnuts in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, stirring frequently, until fragrant and lightly browned. Transfer to a small bowl to cool.
3. In a small jar or bowl, whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, honey, ground cardamom, salt, and pepper to create the dressing.
4. In a large mixing bowl combine the cooked quinoa, sliced pears, toasted walnuts, dried cranberries, and baby arugula. Drizzle the dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly.
5. Sprinkle the crumbled feta cheese on top, give the salad one final light toss, and serve immediately or chill for up to 30 minutes for a cooler presentation.
title: Spiced Cardamom Pear and Quinoa Salad

text:
Saffron‑Infused Carrot and Lentil Pilaf with Toasted Almonds

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 2 large carrots, peeled and diced
- 1 small onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/4 teaspoon saffron threads
- 2 ½ cups vegetable broth
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- ¼ cup sliced almonds, toasted
- 1 tablespoon fresh parsley, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, combine the saffron threads with 2 tablespoons of hot vegetable broth; let steep for 5 minutes.
2. Heat the olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent, about 3 minutes.
3. Stir in the garlic and diced carrots; cook for another 2 minutes, stirring frequently.
4. Add the rinsed red lentils to the pan, then pour in the saffron‑infused broth followed by the remaining vegetable broth.
5. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and the carrots are soft. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
6. Season the pilaf with salt and pepper to taste. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
7. Fluff the pilaf with a fork, then stir in the toasted almonds and chopped parsley.
8. Serve warm as a side dish or a light main course. Enjoy!
title: Saffron‑Infused Carrot and Lentil Pilaf with Toasted Almonds

text:
Harissa‑Roasted Cauliflower and Lentil Salad with Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 1 medium cauliflower head, cut into florets
- 1 cup dried green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 Tbsp harissa paste
- 3 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice
- ½ cup fresh pomegranate seeds
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh mint
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Toss the cauliflower florets with 2 Tbsp olive oil, harissa paste, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet.
2. Roast the cauliflower for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until tender and caramelized.
3. While the cauliflower roasts, place the lentils in a saucepan, cover with water, bring to a boil, then simmer 20‑25 minutes until tender but firm. Drain and set aside.
4. In a large bowl combine the roasted cauliflower, cooked lentils, lemon juice, remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Toss gently to coat.
5. Fold in the pomegranate seeds and chopped mint just before serving.
6. Serve the salad warm or at room temperature, optionally garnished with extra mint or a drizzle of harissa‑infused olive oil.
title: Harissa‑Roasted Cauliflower and Lentil Salad with Pomegranate

text:
Lemon‑Basil Farro with Roasted Sweet Potato and Goat Cheese

Ingredients:
- 1 cup farro, rinsed
- 2 cups low‑sodium vegetable broth
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and cubed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp sea salt
- ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp lemon zest
- ¼ cup fresh basil leaves, chopped
- ½ cup crumbled goat cheese
- Optional: 1 tbsp toasted pine nuts for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, ½ tsp salt, and ¼ tsp pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine the farro and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the farro is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
3. In a small skillet, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant; do not let it brown.  
4. Transfer the cooked farro to a large mixing bowl. Add the sautéed garlic, lemon juice, lemon zest, and the chopped basil. Toss gently to combine.  
5. Fold the roasted sweet potato cubes into the farro mixture. Adjust seasoning with the remaining salt and pepper, if needed.  
6. Plate the farro salad, sprinkle the crumbled goat cheese over the top, and garnish with toasted pine nuts (if using). Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Basil Farro with Roasted Sweet Potato and Goat Cheese

title: Lemon‑Garlic Herb Quinoa with Roasted Broccoli

text:
Crispy Coconut‑Lime Chickpea & Avocado Wrap

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 ½ tbsp coconut oil, melted
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tsp lime zest
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 1 ripe avocado, sliced
- ¼ cup red cabbage, thinly shredded
- ¼ cup carrot, julienned
- 2 large whole‑wheat tortillas
- 2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 tbsp plain Greek yogurt (optional, for drizzle)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the chickpeas with melted coconut oil, lime juice, lime zest, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the seasoned chickpeas on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until crisp and golden.  
4. While the chickpeas roast, prepare the wrap fillings: slice the avocado, shred the cabbage, julienne the carrot, and chop the cilantro.  
5. Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet for 30 seconds per side, then layer each with roasted chickpeas, avocado slices, cabbage, carrot, and cilantro. Drizzle with Greek yogurt if desired.  
6. Fold the sides of the tortilla inward and roll tightly. Slice in half and serve immediately, or wrap in foil for a portable lunch.
title: Crispy Coconut‑Lime Chickpea & Avocado Wrap

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Power Bowl with Lime Yogurt Drizzle

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 cups kale, stems removed and torn into bite‑size pieces
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- ½ cup Greek yogurt
- 1 Tbsp lime juice
- 1 tsp honey
- Lime wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes and chickpeas with olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the sweet potatoes are tender and caramelized.  
4. While the vegetables roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
5. In a skillet over medium heat, add a splash of olive oil and sauté the kale for 3‑4 minutes, just until wilted. Season lightly with salt.  
6. Prepare the lime yogurt drizzle: whisk together Greek yogurt, lime juice, honey, and a pinch of salt in a small bowl until smooth. Adjust acidity with extra lime juice if desired.  
7. To assemble each bowl, start with a base of quinoa, top with roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas, then add sautéed kale. Sprinkle chopped cilantro over the top.  
8. Drizzle the lime yogurt sauce generously over the bowl, and serve with extra lime wedges on the side. Enjoy warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Power Bowl with Lime Yogurt Drizzle

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Glazed Pumpkin and Quinoa Salad with Pomegranate Vinaigrette

Ingredients:
- 1 small sugar pumpkin (about 2 lb), peeled, seeded, and cubed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp ground nutmeg
- ¼ tsp salt
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- ½ cup pomegranate seeds
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 cups baby arugula
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)

For the vinaigrette:
- 3 Tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil
- 2 Tbsp pomegranate juice
- 1 Tbsp apple cider vinegar
- 1 tsp honey
- Pinch of salt and black pepper

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the pumpkin cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, nutmeg, and ¼ tsp salt until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the pumpkin in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and caramelized.  
4. While the pumpkin roasts, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside to cool slightly.  
5. Prepare the vinaigrette: whisk together olive oil, pomegranate juice, apple cider vinegar, honey, salt, and pepper in a small bowl. Adjust seasoning to taste.  
6. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted pumpkin, arugula, pomegranate seeds, and toasted pumpkin seeds. Drizzle with the vinaigrette and toss gently to coat.  
7. Transfer the salad to a serving platter or individual bowls. Sprinkle crumbled feta on top, if using, and serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Glazed Pumpkin and Quinoa Salad with Pomegranate Vinaigrette

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Acorn Squash and Lentil Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 medium acorn squash, halved and seeded
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 small red onion, finely diced
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; brush the mixture over the cut sides of the acorn squash.
2. Place the squash halves cut‑side down on a parchment‑lined baking sheet and roast for 35‑40 minutes, until the flesh is tender and caramelized.
3. While the squash roasts, combine lentils and vegetable broth in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook for 20‑25 minutes, or until lentils are tender but not mushy. Drain any excess liquid.
4. In a skillet over medium heat, add a drizzle of olive oil and sauté the diced red onion until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
5. Stir the cooked lentils into the skillet with the onions, season with additional salt and pepper if needed, and heat through for 2‑3 minutes. Remove from heat.
6. To serve, fluff the lentil mixture onto plates, top each with a roasted acorn squash half, sprinkle with toasted pumpkin seeds and chopped parsley, and enjoy the sweet‑spicy harmony.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Acorn Squash and Lentil Pilaf

- 1 tablespoon lime zest
- 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed

text:
Coconut‑Lime Baked Tofu with Turmeric Quinoa and Roasted Brussels Sprouts

Ingredients:
- 1 block (14 oz) extra‑firm tofu, pressed and cut into 1‑inch cubes
- 2 Tbsp coconut milk
- 1 Tbsp lime juice
- 1 tsp lime zest
- 1 tsp maple syrup
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups water
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- ¼ tsp cumin
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- 12 oz Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)
- Lime wedges (for serving)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, whisk together coconut milk, lime juice, lime zest, maple syrup, salt, and pepper. Add the tofu cubes, toss to coat, and let marinate while you prepare the quinoa.  
3. In a saucepan, combine quinoa, water, turmeric, and cumin. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
4. On the prepared baking sheet, spread the halved Brussels sprouts. Drizzle with olive oil, sprinkle garlic, smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt. Toss to coat evenly.  
5. Arrange the marinated tofu cubes on the same sheet, leaving space between pieces.  
6. Roast the Brussels sprouts and tofu for 20‑25 minutes, turning the tofu halfway through, until the sprouts are caramelized and the tofu is golden and crisp.  
7. Serve the baked tofu over a bed of turmeric quinoa, top with the roasted Brussels sprouts, and garnish with chopped cilantro and lime wedges. Enjoy!
title: Coconut‑Lime Baked Tofu with Turmeric Quinoa and Roasted Brussels Sprouts

Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Shrimp & Mango Quinoa Bowl

- 12 oz large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp turmeric powder
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Shrimp & Mango Quinoa Bowl

text:
Maple‑Glazed Roasted Eggplant and Quinoa Salad with Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 cups arugula, loosely packed
- ½ cup crumbled feta cheese
- ¼ cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 Tbsp toasted pine nuts
- 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the eggplant cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, maple syrup, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the eggplant in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until caramelized and tender.  
4. While the eggplant roasts, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.  
5. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted eggplant, arugula, feta, pomegranate seeds, and pine nuts.  
6. Drizzle the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil and lemon juice over the salad; toss gently to distribute flavors.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if desired.  
8. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with a few extra pomegranate seeds and pine nuts.
title: Maple‑Glazed Roasted Eggplant and Quinoa Salad with Pomegranate

text:
Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Chickpea Breakfast Bowl

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 cups fresh baby spinach
- 1 ripe avocado, sliced
- 2 Tbsp pumpkin seeds, toasted
- Optional: a drizzle of hot sauce or sriracha

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, 1 Tbsp maple syrup, ½ tsp smoked paprika, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
3. In the same bowl, combine the chickpeas with the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, 1 Tbsp maple syrup, the remaining smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Arrange the chickpeas on the same baking sheet, keeping them separate from the sweet potatoes.  
4. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the sweet potatoes are tender and lightly caramelized and the chickpeas are crisp.  
5. While the vegetables roast, toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2‑3 minutes, shaking the pan frequently; set aside.  
6. To assemble, divide the fresh spinach between two bowls. Top each with the roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas, then add avocado slices.  
7. Drizzle any remaining maple‑glaze from the pan over the bowls, sprinkle with toasted pumpkin seeds, and add a splash of hot sauce if desired.  
8. Serve immediately and enjoy a warm, sweet‑savory breakfast bowl.
title: Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato and Chickpea Breakfast Bowl

text:
Sesame‑Ginger Tempeh with Coconut‑Lime Rice and Charred Broccoli

Ingredients:
- 8 oz (225 g) tempeh, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 2 Tbsp soy sauce (or tamari for gluten‑free)
- 1 Tbsp sesame oil
- 1 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp freshly grated ginger
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 Tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 cup jasmine rice
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- 1 Tbsp lime juice
- Zest of 1 lime
- 1 large head broccoli, cut into florets
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 Tbsp toasted sesame seeds (optional)
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (optional)

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, whisk together soy sauce, sesame oil, maple syrup, grated ginger, minced garlic, and rice vinegar. Add the tempeh cubes, toss to coat, and let marinate while you prepare the rice (about 10 minutes).
2. Rinse the jasmine rice under cold water until the water runs clear. In a saucepan, combine the rice, coconut milk, and ½ cup water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Remove from heat, stir in lime juice and lime zest, then keep covered.
3. Preheat a large skillet or grill pan over medium‑high heat. Drizzle the broccoli florets with olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and spread in a single layer. Cook, stirring occasionally, until charred edges appear and the stems are just tender, about 6‑8 minutes. Transfer to a plate and keep warm.
4. While the broccoli cooks, heat a non‑stick skillet over medium heat. Add the marinated tempeh (including any excess sauce) and sauté for 5‑7 minutes, turning occasionally, until the tempeh is golden brown and the sauce has thickened.
5. To serve, fluff the coconut‑lime rice with a fork and divide it among bowls. Top each portion with charred broccoli and the sesame‑ginger tempeh. Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds and chopped cilantro, if using. Enjoy warm!
title: Sesame‑Ginger Tempeh with Coconut‑Lime Rice and Charred Broccoli

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 small head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 ½ cups cooked quinoa
- 1 cup canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp saffron threads, steeped in 2 tbsp warm water
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- ¼ cup toasted almond slivers
- 2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cauliflower florets with 1 tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
3. Roast the cauliflower for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden‑brown and tender.  
4. While the cauliflower roasts, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the chickpeas and sauté for 5‑6 minutes until lightly crisped.  
5. Drizzle the saffron‑infused water over the roasted cauliflower, toss gently to coat, and return to the oven for an additional 2 minutes to absorb the flavor.  
6. In a serving bowl, place a base of cooked quinoa. Top with the saffron‑roasted cauliflower, sautéed chickpeas, a squeeze of lemon juice, and a sprinkle of toasted almond slivers.  
7. Garnish with fresh cilantro and adjust seasoning with extra salt, pepper, or lemon juice if desired.  
8. Serve warm or at room temperature, enjoying the vibrant colors and aromatic saffron notes.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

text:
Lemon‑Thyme Baked Cod with Herb‑Infused Couscous

Ingredients:
- 4 cod fillets (about 6 oz each)
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 lemon, thinly sliced
- 1 Tbsp fresh thyme leaves (plus extra for garnish)
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup couscous
- 1 ¼ cup vegetable broth
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley
- ½ cup cherry tomatoes, halved
- ¼ cup cucumber, diced
- ¼ cup red onion, finely chopped
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- Zest of 1 lemon

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Place the cod fillets on the prepared sheet, drizzle with olive oil, and season with salt, pepper, minced garlic, and fresh thyme. Top each fillet with a lemon slice.  
3. Bake the cod for 12‑15 minutes, or until the fish flakes easily with a fork.  
4. While the cod cooks, bring the vegetable broth to a boil in a saucepan. Stir in the couscous, cover, and remove from heat; let stand for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.  
5. Transfer the fluffed couscous to a large bowl and stir in chopped parsley, lemon zest, and a drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper to taste.  
6. Add the cherry tomatoes, cucumber, and red onion to the couscous, mixing gently to combine.  
7. Plate each baked cod fillet atop a generous serving of the herb‑infused couscous. Sprinkle with extra thyme leaves and crumbled feta, if using.  
8. Serve immediately with an extra lemon wedge on the side for squeezing.
title: Lemon‑Thyme Baked Cod with Herb‑Infused Couscous

text:
Spiced Orange‑Ginger Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Kale

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon orange zest
- 1 tablespoon fresh orange juice
- 1 tablespoon grated fresh ginger
- 2 cups kale, stems removed and torn into bite‑size pieces
- ¼ cup toasted sliced almonds
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the chickpeas with olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, orange zest, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking halfway, until crisp.
2. While the chickpeas roast, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
3. In a large skillet over medium heat, add a drizzle of olive oil and sauté the kale with a pinch of salt until wilted, about 3‑4 minutes. Remove from heat.
4. In a small bowl whisk together orange juice, grated ginger, a splash of olive oil, and a pinch of salt to make the dressing.
5. In a serving bowl, layer the cooked quinoa, roasted chickpeas, and sautéed kale. Drizzle the orange‑ginger dressing over the top, toss gently to combine, and sprinkle with toasted almonds.
6. Adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed, then serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Spiced Orange‑Ginger Quinoa with Roasted Chickpeas and Kale

text:
Saffron‑Infused Coconut Lentil & Spinach Stew with Lemon Zest

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 large onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon ground coriander
- ¼ teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon saffron threads, steeped in 2 tablespoons hot water
- 1 can (14 oz) coconut milk
- 3 cups vegetable broth
- 2 cups fresh spinach, roughly chopped
- Z
title: Saffron‑Infused Coconut Lentil & Spinach Stew with Lemon Zest

text:
Sage‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Lentil Soup with Coconut Milk

Ingredients:
- 2 lb carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch pieces
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 large onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh sage leaves, finely chopped
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk (full‑fat)
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional garnish: toasted pumpkin seeds and a drizzle of coconut cream

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the carrot pieces with olive oil, half the chopped sage, salt, and pepper, then spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring once, until caramelized and tender.
2. While the carrots roast, heat a large pot over medium heat. Add a splash of olive oil, then sauté the diced onion until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add the minced garlic and the remaining sage, cooking for another minute until fragrant.
3. Stir in the rinsed red lentils, then pour in the vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes.
4. Add the roasted carrots to the pot and continue simmering for another 10 minutes, or until the lentils are fully cooked and the carrots are very soft.
5. Using an immersion blender (or working in batches with a countertop blender), puree the soup until smooth and creamy. Return to the pot if needed.
6. Stir in the coconut milk and lemon juice, heating gently just until the soup is warmed through. Adjust seasoning with additional salt
title: Sage‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Lentil Soup with Coconut Milk

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa Stuffed Sweet Potatoes with Roasted Chickpeas

Ingredients:
- 4 medium sweet potatoes
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1 lemon, zest and juice
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 cup baby spinach, roughly chopped
- ½ cup feta cheese, crumbled
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional garnish: chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. Pierce each sweet potato several times with a fork, place them on the prepared baking sheet, and roast for 45‑50 minutes, or until tender.
3. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
4. Toss the chickpeas with 1 tablespoon olive oil, minced ginger, cumin, salt, and pepper. Spread them on the same baking sheet (or a separate one) and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until golden and slightly crisp.
5. In a large bowl, mix the cooked quinoa, roasted chickpeas, lemon zest, lemon juice, remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, chopped spinach, and feta. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste.
6. When the sweet potatoes are done, let them cool for a few minutes, then slice each lengthwise open, gently fluff the interior with a fork, and spoon the quinoa‑chickpea mixture into the cavities.
7. Garnish with chopped parsley and serve warm. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Ginger Quinoa Stuffed Sweet Potatoes with Roasted Chickpeas

text:
Garlic‑Lime Roasted Eggplant and Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 large eggplant, cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 3 tbsp olive oil
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 1 small red bell pepper, diced
- 1 small cucumber, diced

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the eggplant cubes with 2 tbsp olive oil, minced garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
3. Roast the eggplant for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.  
4. While the eggplant roasts, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside to cool slightly.  
5. In a small jar, whisk together the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, lime juice, a pinch of salt, and a splash of pepper to make the dressing.  
6. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, roasted eggplant, diced red bell pepper, cucumber, and cilantro. Drizzle the lime dressing over the mixture and toss gently to coat.  
7. Sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds on top for crunch. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Garlic‑Lime Roasted Eggplant and Quinoa Salad

text:
Saffron‑Infused Coconut Chickpea and Quinoa Salad with Lime Vinaigrette

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 cup canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup coconut milk
- ½ teaspoon saffron threads
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- ½ cup frozen corn, thawed
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 2 tablespoons extra‑virgin olive oil
- Juice of 1 lime
- 1 teaspoon honey or agave syrup
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a small saucepan, combine the coconut milk, saffron threads, and a pinch of salt; bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then remove from heat and let steep for 5 minutes.
2. Meanwhile, cook the quinoa: place quinoa in a pot with 2 cups water, bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook 15 minutes until water is absorbed; fluff with a fork.
3. In a large bowl, whisk together the olive oil, lime juice, honey, and a pinch of black pepper to create the vinaigrette.
4. Add the cooked quinoa, chickpeas, diced red bell pepper, corn, and chopped cilantro to the bowl; pour the saffron‑infused coconut milk over the mixture and toss gently to combine.
5. Drizzle the lime vinaigrette over the salad, season with additional salt and pepper to taste, and give one final toss to coat everything evenly.
6. Serve the salad at room temperature or chilled, garnished with extra cilantro leaves if desired. Enjoy!
title: Saffron‑Infused Coconut Chickpea and Quinoa Salad with Lime Vinaigrette

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Chickpea & Sweet Corn Salad with Avocado

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup fresh or frozen sweet corn kernels
- 1 ripe avocado, diced
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1 small red onion, finely chopped
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice

- 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar
- 1 tsp honey or maple syrup
- 1/4 tsp sea salt
- 1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- Optional: 1 jalapeño, seeded and minced for heat

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan, bring water to a boil, add the corn kernels and cook for 3‑4 minutes until tender; drain and set aside to cool.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Chickpea & Sweet Corn Salad with Avocado

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Garlic Chickpea and Kale Soup

Ingredients:
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 large onion, diced
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 carrot, peeled and diced
- 1 celery stalk, diced
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 2 cups chopped kale, stems removed
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Juice of ½ lemon (optional, for serving)

Instructions:
1. Preheat a large pot over medium heat and add the olive oil.  
2. Add the diced onion, carrot, and celery; sauté for 5‑7 minutes, until the vegetables are softened.  
3. Stir in the minced garlic, ground cinnamon, and maple syrup; cook for 1 minute, allowing the garlic to become fragrant.  
4. Add the chickpeas and vegetable broth; bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes.  
5. Stir in the chopped kale and continue to simmer for another 5 minutes, or until the kale is wilted but still bright green.  
6. Season the soup with salt and pepper to taste. If desired, finish with a squeeze of lemon juice for brightness.  
7. Ladle the soup into bowls and serve hot, optionally garnished with a drizzle of extra maple syrup or a sprinkle of toasted pumpkin seeds.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Garlic Chickpea and Kale Soup

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Chickpea & Sweet Potato Skillet with Cashew Crunch

Ingredients:
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and diced
- 1 ½ cups cooked chickpeas (or 1 can, drained and rinsed)
- 1 ½ tablespoons olive oil
- 1 inch fresh ginger, minced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon lemon zest
- 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- ¼ teaspoon cayenne pepper (optional)
- ¼ cup unsalted cashews, roughly chopped
- 2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 2 green onions, sliced (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat a large skillet over medium heat and add the olive oil.  
2. Add the diced sweet potato and sauté for 5‑7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it begins to soften and turn golden.  
3. Stir in the minced ginger and garlic; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.  
4. Sprinkle the cumin, smoked paprika, cayenne (if using), salt, and pepper over the vegetables; toss to coat.  
5. Add the chickpeas to the skillet and continue cooking, stirring, for 3‑4 minutes until the chickpeas are warmed through and the sweet potatoes are fork‑tender.  
6. Drizzle the lemon juice over the mixture, sprinkle the lemon zest, and give everything a quick stir to combine the flavors.  
7. While the skillet finishes cooking, toast the chopped cashews in a dry pan over low‑medium heat for 2‑3 minutes, shaking the pan frequently, until they are lightly browned and aromatic.  
8. Remove the skillet from heat; fold the toasted cashews and fresh cilantro into the dish.  
9. Transfer to serving plates, garnish with sliced green onions, and serve immediately. Enjoy the bright, spicy, and crunchy flavors!
title: Lemon‑Ginger Chickpea & Sweet Potato Skillet with Cashew Crunch

text:
Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato & Black Bean Breakfast Tacos

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 tablespoon maple syrup
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/4 teaspoon salt
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 (15‑oz) can black beans, drained and rinsed
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro
- 1/4 cup diced red onion
- 4 small corn tortillas
- 2 large eggs
- 1 avocado, sliced
- 1 lime, cut into wedges
- Hot sauce (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the diced sweet potatoes with olive oil, maple syrup, smoked paprika, cumin, and salt until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the sweet potatoes on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway, until tender and caramelized.  
4. While the sweet potatoes roast, heat a skillet over medium heat and add the black beans; cook for 3‑4 minutes until warmed through, then stir in the cilantro and red onion.  
5. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet for about 30 seconds per side or wrap them in foil and heat in the oven for the last 5 minutes of the sweet potato roasting.  
6. In the same skillet, scramble the eggs to your desired doneness.  
7. Assemble each taco: place a spoonful of roasted sweet potatoes, a scoop of black bean mixture, scrambled eggs, and avocado slices on a tortilla.  
8. Squeeze fresh lime juice over the tacos and drizzle with hot sauce if desired. Serve immediately.
title: Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato & Black Bean Breakfast Tacos
