Rosemary‑Lemon Farro with Pan‑Seared Scallops and Charred Asparagus

Ingredients:
- 1 cup
title: Rosemary‑Lemon Farro with Pan‑Seared Scallops and Charred Asparagus

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Tagine with Apricot  

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch sticks  
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed  
- 1 cup dried apricots, halved  
- 1 ½ teaspoons saffron threads, steeped in 2 Tbsp hot water  
- 1 medium onion, thinly sliced  
- 3 cloves garlic, minced  
- 1 inch piece fresh ginger, grated  
- 1 tsp ground cumin  
- 1 tsp ground coriander  
- ½ tsp ground cinnamon  
- 2 Tbsp olive oil  
- 2 cups vegetable broth  
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste  
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)  

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the carrot sticks with 1 Tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and half the cumin; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
2. While the carrots roast, heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil in a large, oven‑safe skillet or tagine over medium heat. Add the sliced onion and sauté for 5 minutes until softened.  
3. Stir in the garlic, ginger, remaining cumin, coriander, and cinnamon; cook 1‑2 minutes until fragrant.  
4. Add the chickpeas, apricot halves, and the saffron‑infused water (including the threads) to the skillet; stir to combine.  
5. Pour in the vegetable broth, bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce heat and let simmer for 5 minutes.  
6. Remove the skillet from the stovetop; add the roasted carrots, mixing them into the tagine.  
7. Cover the skillet or tagine with a lid or foil and transfer to the oven. Bake for 15‑20 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken slightly.  
8. Remove from the oven, season with salt and pepper to taste, and sprinkle chopped cilantro over the top. Serve hot with crusty bread or over couscous.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Tagine with Apricot

text:
Spiced Ginger‑Lime Tofu with Coconut Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- ½ cup water
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp grated fresh lime zest
- 1 tsp sesame oil
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- ½ cup shredded carrots
- ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a saucepan combine quinoa, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed; fluff with a fork and set aside.  
2. While the quinoa cooks, whisk together soy sauce, lime juice, maple syrup, grated ginger, lime zest, and sesame oil in a shallow bowl.  
3. Toss the tofu cubes in the sauce, ensuring each piece is well‑coated. Let marinate for 5 minutes.  
4. Heat olive oil in a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated tofu and sauté 6‑8 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden and crisp on the edges.  
5. Remove the tofu from the skillet and set aside. In the same skillet, add shredded carrots and sauté 2 minutes until just softened.  
6. Return the tofu to the skillet, add the cooked quinoa, and gently stir‑fold everything together. Cook 2 minutes to let flavors meld.  
7. Season with additional salt and pepper if needed, then transfer to serving bowls.  
8. Garnish each bowl with chopped cilantro and an extra drizzle of lime juice for brightness. Enjoy warm or at room temperature.
title: Spiced Ginger‑Lime Tofu with Coconut Quinoa

text:
Garlic‑Herb Quinoa Stuffed Portobello with Pomegranate Vinaigrette

Ingredients:
- 4 large portobello mushroom caps, stems removed and gills scraped
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon dried thyme
- 1 teaspoon dried rosemary
- 1/2 cup crumbled feta cheese
- 1/4 cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 1/3 cup pomegranate arils
- 2 tablespoons balsamic vinegar
- 1 tablespoon honey
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. Place the mushroom caps gill‑side up on the sheet, brush each with 1 tablespoon olive oil, and season with salt and pepper. Roast for 12‑15 minutes until tender.
3. While the mushrooms roast, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes or until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
4. In a small skillet, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add minced garlic and sauté 1 minute until fragrant. Stir in the cooked quinoa, thyme, rosemary, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Cook 2‑3 minutes, mixing well.
5. Remove the skillet from heat and fold in the crumbled feta, toasted pumpkin seeds, and half of the pomegranate arils.
6. In a small bowl, whisk together balsamic vinegar, honey, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of olive oil to create the vinaigrette.
7. Spoon the quinoa mixture into each roasted portobello cap, dividing evenly.
8. Drizzle the pomegranate vinaigrette over the stuffed mushrooms and garnish with the remaining pomegranate arils.
title: Garlic‑Herb Quinoa Stuffed Portobello with Pomegranate Vinaigrette

text:
Herb‑Crusted Tofu with Lemon‑Garlic Quinoa and Roasted Asparagus

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and sliced into ½‑inch slabs
- 2  tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1  tsp dried thyme
- 1  tsp dried oregano
- ½  tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1  cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2  cups vegetable broth
- 2  cloves garlic, minced
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2  tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1  bunch asparagus, trimmed and cut into 2‑inch pieces
- 1  tbsp grated Parmesan cheese (optional, for serving)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a shallow dish, combine 1  tbsp olive oil, thyme, oregano, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Brush both sides of each tofu slab with the herb mixture and place on the prepared baking sheet.  
3. Toss the asparagus pieces with the remaining 1  tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper; spread them on the same sheet beside the tofu.  
4. Roast the tofu and asparagus for 20‑25 minutes, turning the tofu halfway through, until the tofu is golden and the asparagus is tender‑crisp.  
5. While the tofu roasts, bring the vegetable broth to a boil in a medium saucepan. Add the rinsed quinoa, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes.  
6. Fluff the quinoa with a fork, then stir in the minced garlic, lemon zest, and lemon juice. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste.  
7. To serve, divide the lemon‑garlic quinoa among plates, top with slices of herb‑crusted tofu, and arrange the roasted asparagus alongside. Sprinkle with grated Parmesan, if using, and enjoy immediately.
title: Herb‑Crusted Tofu with Lemon‑Garlic Quinoa and Roasted Asparagus

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Power Bowl with Avocado Lime Dressing

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 cup cooked quinoa
- 1 avocado, sliced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 lime, juiced
- 1 tbsp honey
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, cinnamon, smoked paprika, maple syrup, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
3. Roast the sweet potatoes for 20 minutes, then flip them over.  
4. While the sweet potatoes roast, toss the chickpeas with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of maple syrup; add them to the baking sheet and roast for an additional 15 minutes, until crisp.  
5. Meanwhile, prepare the dressing: whisk together lime juice, honey, a pinch of salt, and a splash of water to reach a drizzle consistency. Set aside.  
6. In a serving bowl, place a base of cooked quinoa. Top with the roasted sweet potatoes, crispy chickpeas, sliced avocado, and chopped cilantro.  
7. Drizzle the lime‑honey dressing over the bowl, garnish with extra cilantro if desired, and serve
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Power Bowl with Avocado Lime Dressing

text:
Ginger‑Lime Tempeh with Coconut‑Basil Quinoa  

Ingredients:
- 8 oz tempeh, cut into ½‑inch cubes  
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed  
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk  
- ½ cup water  
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice  
- 1 tbsp lime zest  
- 2 tbsp soy sauce or tamari  
- 1 tbsp maple syrup  
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger  
- 2 cloves garlic, minced  
- ¼ cup fresh basil leaves, chopped  
- 1 tbsp sesame oil  
- 1 tbsp olive oil  
- Salt and pepper to taste  
- Optional garnish: sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds  

Instructions:
1. In a shallow bowl, whisk together soy sauce, maple syrup, lime juice, lime zest, grated ginger, minced garlic, and a pinch of salt. Add the tempeh cubes, toss to coat, and let marinate for 10 minutes.  
2. While the tempeh marinates, combine the rinsed quinoa, coconut milk, and water in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and stir in the chopped basil; season with salt and pepper.  
3. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated tempeh (reserve any excess liquid) and sauté for 4‑5 minutes, turning until golden brown on all sides.  
4. Add the reserved marinade to the skillet, drizzle with sesame oil, and cook for an additional 2 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken and coat the tempeh. Remove from heat.  
5. To serve, spoon a bed of coconut‑basil quinoa onto each plate, top with the ginger‑lime tempeh, and drizzle any remaining pan sauce over the top.  
6. Garnish with sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds if desired. Enjoy warm!
title: Ginger‑Lime Tempeh with Coconut‑Basil Quinoa

text:
Spiced Orange‑Ginger Lentil and Quinoa Soup

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- ½ cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 large carrot, diced
- 1 celery stalk, diced
- 1 small onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- Zest of 1 orange
- 2 tbsp orange juice
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp ground coriander
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Toasted pumpkin seeds, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, and celery; sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
2. Stir in the garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander, and cayenne pepper; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add the lentils, quinoa, orange zest, orange juice, and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer.
4. Cover and simmer for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils and quinoa are tender. Stir occasionally.
5. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. If the soup is too thick, add a splash of water or broth to reach desired consistency.
6. Ladle the soup into bowls and garnish with fresh cilantro leaves and toasted pumpkin seeds. Serve hot.
title: Spiced Orange‑Ginger Lentil and Quinoa Soup

text:
Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato & Chickpea Breakfast Hash

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, diced
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 small red onion, finely chopped
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the diced sweet potatoes, chickpeas, red onion, and bell pepper with olive oil, maple syrup, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the mixture in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the sweet potatoes are tender and lightly caramelized.  
4. While the hash is roasting, heat a small skillet over medium heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. Sauté any remaining liquid from the pan for 1‑2 minutes to create a glossy finish.  
5. Remove the hash from the oven, transfer to a serving dish, and drizzle the pan‑collected glaze over the top.  
6. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and serve hot, optionally with a fried or poached egg on top.
title: Maple‑Glazed Sweet Potato & Chickpea Breakfast Hash

text:
Maple‑Glazed Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch sticks
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 cups kale, stems removed and torn into bite‑size pieces
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice
- 2 Tbsp toasted
title: Maple‑Glazed Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Buddha Bowl

text:
Garlic‑Lime Grilled Halloumi with Herb Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 8 oz halloumi cheese, sliced ½‑inch thick
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water
- 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- ¼ cup fresh parsley, chopped
- ¼ cup fresh mint, chopped
- ¼ cup toasted pine nuts
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa and water; bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
2. While the quinoa cooks, whisk together 1 tbsp olive oil, lime juice, minced garlic, salt, and pepper in a shallow dish; add the halloumi slices and coat evenly. Let marinate for 5 minutes.
3. Heat a grill pan or outdoor grill over medium‑high heat; brush with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil. Grill the halloumi 2‑3 minutes per side, until golden brown grill marks appear; set aside on a plate.
4. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large bowl; stir in chopped parsley, mint, toasted pine nuts, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Drizzle with any remaining lime‑garlic dressing and toss to combine.
5. Slice the grilled halloumi into bite‑size wedges and arrange atop the herb quinoa salad.
6. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with an extra squeeze of lime if desired. Enjoy!
title: Garlic‑Lime Grilled Halloumi with Herb Quinoa Salad

text:
Turmeric‑Honey Glazed Cauliflower Steaks with Lemon‑Garlic Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 large cauliflower head
- 2 Tbsp honey
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Slice the cauliflower into ¾‑inch thick “steaks” by cutting from top to bottom; you should get 2–3 usable steaks.  
3. In a small bowl whisk together honey, turmeric, 1 Tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper.  
4. Brush both sides of each cauliflower steak generously with the turmeric‑honey mixture and place on the prepared baking sheet.  
5. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, flipping halfway through, until the edges are caramelized and the center is tender.  
6. While the cauliflower cooks, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a medium saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook 15‑18 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.  
7. Remove the quinoa from heat and fluff with a fork. Stir in the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, minced garlic, lemon zest, and lemon juice; season with a pinch of salt if needed.  
8. To serve, plate a cauliflower steak atop a mound of lemon‑garlic quinoa, drizzle any pan‑drippings over the top, and garnish with chopped parsley. Enjoy while hot!
title: Turmeric‑Honey Glazed Cauliflower Steaks with Lemon‑Garlic Quinoa

text:
Cinnamon‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Lentil Buddha Bowl

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and sliced into thin rounds
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- ¼ teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1 small red onion, thinly sliced
- 2 cups baby spinach leaves
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tablespoons tahini
- 1 tablespoon lemon juice
- 1 tablespoon maple syrup
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves for garnish (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the carrot rounds with olive oil, cinnamon, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
3. While the carrots roast, combine lentils with 2 cups water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer uncovered for 20‑25 minutes, or until lentils are tender but not mushy. Drain any excess water and set aside.  
4. In a small skillet over medium heat, add a drizzle of olive oil and sauté the red onion for 3‑4 minutes until softened and slightly golden. Season with a pinch of salt.  
5. Prepare the dressing by whisking together tahini, lemon juice, maple syrup, a splash of water (to thin), and a pinch of salt until smooth and creamy. Adjust consistency with more water if needed.  
6. To assemble the Buddha bowl, divide the spinach leaves between two serving bowls. Top each with a portion of lentils, roasted carrots, sautéed red onion, and a handful of toasted pumpkin seeds.  
7. Drizzle the tahini‑lemon dressing over the bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro if desired, and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Cinnamon‑Infused Roasted Carrot and Lentil Buddha Bowl

text:
Coconut‑Lime Shrimp with Mango‑Avocado Salsa

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 2 Tbsp coconut oil
- 1 tsp lime zest
- 3 Tbsp fresh lime juice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 1 ripe mango, diced
- 1 ripe avocado, diced
- ¼ cup red onion, finely chopped
- 1 Tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 Tbsp honey
- 1 tsp chili flakes (optional)

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, combine lime zest, lime juice, garlic, ginger, salt, pepper, and chili flakes; whisk to create a quick marinade.
2. Add the shrimp to the bowl, toss to coat, and let sit for 5 minutes while you prepare the salsa.
3. Meanwhile, in a separate bowl, gently mix mango, avocado, red onion, cilantro, and honey; set aside.
4. Heat coconut oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat until shimmering.
5. Add the marinated shrimp in a single layer and cook for 2‑3 minutes per side, until pink and opaque.
6. Remove the shrimp from the skillet and transfer to a serving platter.
7. Spoon the mango‑avocado salsa over the hot shrimp, allowing the heat to slightly soften the fruit.
8. Serve immediately, garnished with extra cilantro and a wedge of lime if desired. Enjoy!
title: Coconut‑Lime Shrimp with Mango‑Avocado Salsa

text:
Ginger‑Lime Coconut Shrimp with Quinoa Pilaf

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 1 tbsp lime zest
- 2 tbsp fresh ginger, minced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp red pepper flakes (optional)
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 small red bell pepper, diced (optional for color)

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine the quinoa, vegetable broth, and coconut milk. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the
title: Ginger‑Lime Coconut Shrimp with Quinoa Pilaf

text:
Crispy Coconut‑Lime Shrimp with Pineapple Salsa

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 tbsp lime zest
- 2 tbsp lime juice
- ½ cup panko breadcrumbs
- ¼ cup shredded unsweetened coconut
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- 1 cup fresh pineapple, diced
- ¼ cup red bell pepper, finely diced
- 2 tbsp red onion, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 tbsp honey
- 1 tsp rice vinegar
- 1 tsp sriracha (optional)

Instructions:
1. In a shallow bowl, combine coconut milk, lime zest, lime juice, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; stir to blend.
2. Add the shrimp to the coconut‑lime mixture, tossing to coat evenly; let marinate for 5 minutes.
3. In a separate bowl, mix panko breadcrumbs with shredded coconut.
4. Remove shrimp from the liquid, letting excess drip off, then dredge each piece in the breadcrumb‑coconut mixture, pressing gently to adhere.
5. Heat a large skillet over medium‑high heat and add 2 tbsp oil (vegetable or avocado). When shimmering, add the coated shrimp in a single layer; cook 2‑3 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through. Transfer to a paper‑towel‑lined plate.
6. While the shrimp cooks, prepare the pineapple salsa: combine diced pineapple, red bell pepper, red onion, cilantro, honey, rice vinegar, and sriracha (if using) in a bowl; toss gently and let sit for 5 minutes to meld flavors.
7. Serve the crispy shrimp atop a mound of pineapple salsa, garnished with extra cilantro and a lime wedge for squeezing. Enjoy warm!
title: Crispy Coconut‑Lime Shrimp with Pineapple Salsa

text:
Lemon‑Basil Orzo with Grilled Eggplant and Pine Nuts

Ingredients:
- 1 cup orzo pasta
- 2 medium eggplants, sliced into ½‑inch rounds
- 3 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- ¼ cup fresh basil leaves, chopped
- ¼ cup pine nuts, toasted
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat a grill or grill pan over medium‑high heat. Brush both sides of the eggplant slices with 2 Tbsp olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Grill the eggplant until tender and grill‑marks appear, about 4 minutes per side. Transfer to a cutting board and chop into bite‑size pieces.  
2. Meanwhile, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the orzo and cook according to package directions until al dente, about 8‑10 minutes. Drain, reserving ¼ cup of the cooking liquid.  
3. In a small skillet over low heat, toast the pine nuts in the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, stirring frequently, until golden and fragrant, 2‑3 minutes. Remove from heat and set aside.  
4. In a large bowl, combine the cooked orzo, grilled eggplant, minced garlic, lemon zest, lemon juice, and chopped basil. Toss gently, adding a splash of the reserved cooking liquid if the mixture seems dry.  
5. Fold in the toasted pine nuts, then season the salad with additional salt and pepper to taste. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Basil Orzo with Grilled Eggplant and Pine Nuts

text:
Maple‑Miso Glazed Tofu with Roasted Garlic Broccoli and Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 block (14 oz) firm tofu, pressed and cut into ½‑inch cubes
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp white miso paste
- 1 Tbsp low‑sodium soy sauce
- 1 tsp sesame oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced (plus 2 whole cloves for roasting)
- 1 lb broccoli florets
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional garnish: sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the broccoli florets with 1 Tbsp olive oil, the two whole garlic cloves, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until crisp‑tender and lightly browned.  
3. While the broccoli roasts, combine the maple syrup, miso paste, soy sauce, sesame oil, and minced garlic in a small bowl; whisk until smooth.  
4. Place the tofu cubes on a separate baking sheet lined with parchment. Drizzle the glaze over the tofu, tossing gently to coat each piece evenly.  
5. Roast the glazed tofu in the same oven for 15‑18 minutes, flipping halfway through, until the edges are caramelized and the tofu is heated through.  
6. Meanwhile, bring the quinoa and water (or broth) to a boil in a saucepan. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the grains are fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; then fluff with a fork.  
7. Remove the whole garlic cloves from the roasted broccoli, discard the skins, and stir the softened garlic into the broccoli for extra flavor.  
8. To serve, divide the quinoa among bowls, top with roasted broccoli and maple‑miso tofu. Sprinkle with sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds, if using. Enjoy warm!
title: Maple‑Miso Glazed Tofu with Roasted Garlic Broccoli and Quinoa

text:
Citrus‑Maple Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Grain Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp orange zest
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 2 Tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 Tbsp lime juice
- Optional: ½ avocado, sliced for topping

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together olive oil, maple syrup, smoked paprika, orange zest, salt, and pepper.  
3. Add the cubed sweet potatoes and chickpeas to the bowl, toss to coat evenly, and spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast for 25‑30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the sweet potatoes are tender and the chickpeas are crisp and golden.  
5. While the vegetables roast, bring 2 cups water to a boil, add the quinoa, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes or until the water is absorbed; fluff with a fork.  
6. Divide the cooked quinoa among serving bowls, top with the roasted chickpeas and sweet potatoes, and garnish with chopped cilantro, a drizzle of lime juice, and avocado slices if using.  
7. Serve warm or at room temperature, enjoying the sweet‑tart citrus notes balanced by the smoky, maple‑glazed crunch.
title: Citrus‑Maple Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Grain Bowl

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea and Sweet Potato Curry with Coconut Rice

Ingredients:
- 1 cup dried chickpeas (or 2 cups cooked chickpeas)
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 can (13.5 oz) coconut milk
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, minced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 cup jasmine rice
- 1 cup water
- ½ cup coconut milk (for the rice)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. If using dried chickpeas, rinse them, place in a pot with water, bring to a boil, then simmer for 1 hour until tender. Drain and set aside. (If using canned chickpeas, rinse and drain.)  
2. In a medium saucepan, combine the jasmine rice, 1 cup water, and ½ cup coconut milk. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the rice is fluffy and the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and keep covered.  
3. While the rice cooks, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the minced ginger and garlic; sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.  
4. Stir in the ground turmeric and cumin; cook for another 30 seconds, allowing the spices to release their aroma.
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Chickpea and Sweet Potato Curry with Coconut Rice

text:
Crispy Coconut‑Lime Chickpea and Mango Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 ripe mango, peeled and diced
- 1 red bell pepper, thinly sliced
- ½ cup red cabbage, shredded
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 2 tbsp coconut oil, melted
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tsp lime zest
- 1 tsp honey or agave syrup
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- ¼ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- ¼ cup toasted coconut flakes (optional, for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the chickpeas with melted coconut oil, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the chickpeas in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until golden and crisp.  
4. While the chickpeas roast, combine the diced mango, sliced red bell pepper, shredded cabbage, and chopped cilantro in a large mixing bowl.  
5. In a small cup, whisk together lime juice, lime zest, and honey (or agave) to create the dressing.  
6. When the chickpeas are done, let them cool for 5 minutes, then add them to the mango‑vegetable mixture. Drizzle the lime‑honey dressing over the salad and toss gently to combine.  
7. Transfer the salad to serving bowls, sprinkle toasted coconut flakes on top for extra crunch (if using), and serve immediately or chill for up to 30 minutes for a cooler bite.
title: Crispy Coconut‑Lime Chickpea and Mango Salad

text:
Sage‑Infused Quinoa with Roasted Butternut Squash and Pomegranate

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 small butternut squash, peeled and cubed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp fresh sage, finely chopped (plus extra for garnish)
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/4 tsp black pepper
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1/3 cup pomegranate seeds
- 2 tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the cubed butternut squash with 1 tbsp olive oil, half the sage, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.
2. While the squash roasts, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.
3. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, lemon juice, a pinch of salt, and the remaining chopped sage.
4. Transfer the cooked quinoa to a large mixing bowl; drizzle with the sage‑lemon dressing and toss to combine.
5. Add the roasted butternut squash, pomegranate seeds, and toasted pumpkin seeds to the quinoa; gently fold everything together.
6. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with extra sage leaves if desired. Enjoy!
title: Sage‑Infused Quinoa with Roasted Butternut Squash and Pomegranate

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Lentil Tacos  

Ingredients:
- 1 small head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 1 cup green or brown lentils, rinsed
- 1 cup quinoa
- 1½ teaspoons saffron threads
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- ½ teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon sea salt
- ¼ teaspoon black pepper
- 8 small corn tortillas
- ½ cup plain Greek yogurt
- 1 tablespoon lemon juice
- 1 teaspoon honey
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 small red onion, thinly sliced
- 1 avocado, sliced
- 1 lime, cut into wedges

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, combine the saffron threads with 2 tablespoons hot water; let steep for 5 minutes.  
2. Rinse the quinoa, then place it in a saucepan with the saffron infusion, 1 ½ cups vegetable broth, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until fluffy. Set aside.  
3. While the quinoa cooks, add the lentils to a pot with ½ cup vegetable broth, a pinch of salt, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer 20‑25 minutes until tender but not mushy. Drain any excess liquid.  
4. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss cauliflower florets with olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet and roast 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and caramelized.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together Greek yogurt, lemon juice, honey, and a pinch of salt to make the lime‑cilantro crema. Stir in half of the chopped cilantro.  
6. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 30 seconds per side, or wrap in foil and heat in the oven for 5 minutes.  
7. Assemble each taco: place a spoonful of saffron‑infused quinoa on the tortilla, top with roasted cauliflower, lentils, red onion slices, avocado, and a drizzle of the crema. Garnish with remaining cilantro and a squeeze of lime.  
8. Serve immediately and enjoy!
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Cauliflower and Lentil Tacos

text:
Miso‑Glazed Eggplant with Sesame‑Lime Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 2 medium Japanese eggplants (or regular eggplant), sliced into ½‑inch rounds
- 3 Tbsp white miso paste
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 Tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 tsp sesame oil
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 Tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- 1 lime, zest and juice
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- 1 Tbsp olive oil
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together miso paste, maple syrup, soy sauce, rice vinegar, grated ginger, and sesame oil to form the glaze.  
3. Brush both sides of the eggplant slices with olive oil, season lightly with salt and pepper, and place them on the prepared baking sheet.  
4. Roast the eggplant for 15 minutes, flip, brush generously with the miso glaze, and roast an additional 10‑12 minutes until tender and caramelized.  
5. While the eggplant cooks, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes.  
6. Fluff the quinoa with a fork, then stir in lime zest, lime juice, toasted sesame seeds, and chopped cilantro. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if needed.  
7. To serve, spoon a bed of sesame‑lime quinoa onto plates, top with the miso‑glazed eggplant rounds, and garnish with extra cilantro, sesame seeds, and a drizzle of any remaining glaze. Enjoy warm or at room temperature.
title: Miso‑Glazed Eggplant with Sesame‑Lime Quinoa

text:
Maple‑Glazed Chickpea and Roasted Sweet Pepper Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 large red bell peppers, seeded and cut into 1‑inch strips
- 1 large orange bell pepper, seeded and cut into 1‑inch strips
- 1 ½ tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tbsp olive oil, plus extra for roasting
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp kosher salt
- Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 cups mixed baby greens (arugula, spinach, and kale)
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- 2 tbsp crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tsp Dijon mustard

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the bell‑pepper strips with 1 tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and a dash of black pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.  
3. Roast the peppers for 15‑18 minutes, turning once, until the edges are lightly charred and the peppers are tender. Remove from the oven and set aside to cool.  
4. While the peppers roast, combine the chickpeas, maple syrup, smoked paprika, cumin, ½ tsp salt, and a drizzle of olive oil in a separate bowl. Toss until the chickpeas are evenly coated.  
5. Transfer the glazed chickpeas to the same baking sheet (or a second sheet) and roast for 12‑15 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until the chickpeas are golden and slightly crisp.  
6. In a small bowl, whisk together the lemon juice, Dijon mustard, and a pinch of salt to create the dressing.  
7. In a large serving bowl, place the mixed baby greens, roasted sweet peppers, and warm maple‑glazed chickpeas. Drizzle the lemon‑mustard dressing over the salad and toss gently to combine.  
8. Sprinkle toasted pumpkin seeds and crumbled feta (if using) on top for added texture and flavor. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Maple‑Glazed Chickpea and Roasted Sweet Pepper Salad

text:
Maple‑Miso Glazed Cod with Roasted Brussels Sprouts and Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 4 cod fillets (about 6 oz each)
- 2 Tbsp maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp white miso paste
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp freshly grated ginger
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 lb Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Juice of ½ lemon

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, miso paste, soy sauce, grated ginger, and minced garlic until smooth.  
3. Place the cod fillets on the prepared baking sheet, brush each side generously with the maple‑miso glaze, and set aside.  
4. Toss the halved Brussels sprouts with 1 Tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread them on the same baking sheet around the fish, keeping the fillets skin‑side up.  
5. Roast for 12‑15 minutes, or until the cod flakes easily with a fork and the Brussels sprouts are caramelized and tender.  
6. While the fish and sprouts roast, combine the rinsed quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and stir in the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and the lemon juice.  
7. Remove the cod and Brussels sprouts from the oven. Plate a scoop of quinoa, top with a cod fillet, and arrange the roasted Brussels sprouts alongside. Drizzle any remaining glaze from the pan over the fish for extra flavor.  
8. Serve immediately, garnished with a sprinkle of fresh herbs (such as parsley or chives) if desired.
title: Maple‑Miso Glazed Cod with Roasted Brussels Sprouts and Quinoa

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Shrimp and Avocado Quinoa Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or low‑sodium chicken broth
- 1 ripe avocado, diced
- 1 lemon, zest and juice
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- ¼ tsp red‑pepper flakes (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 Tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa and water (or broth); bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
2. While the quinoa cooks, whisk together lemon zest, lemon juice, grated ginger, minced garlic, olive oil, red‑pepper flakes, salt, and pepper in a shallow bowl to create a marinating sauce.
3. Add the shrimp to the sauce, toss to coat, and let marinate for 5 minutes.
4. Heat a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the shrimp and cook 2‑3 minutes per side, until pink and opaque. Remove from heat.
5. Assemble the bowls: divide the cooked quinoa among four serving bowls, top with the cooked shrimp, diced avocado, and a sprinkle of chopped cilantro.
6. Drizzle any remaining lemon‑ginger sauce over each bowl, adjust seasoning with extra salt or pepper if
title: Lemon‑Ginger Shrimp and Avocado Quinoa Bowl

text:
Coconut Lime Shrimp with Mango Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups water
- 1 ripe mango, diced
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1 avocado, cubed
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 2 tbsp coconut milk
- 2 tbsp lime juice (about 1 lime)
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- ½ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp black pepper
- ¼ tsp red‑pepper flakes (optional)

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa and water; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and transfer to a large bowl to cool slightly.  
2. While the quinoa cooks, whisk together coconut milk, lime juice, olive oil, salt, pepper, and red‑pepper flakes in a small bowl; set the dressing aside.  
3. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the shrimp and sauté 2‑3 minutes per side, or until pink and opaque. Remove from heat and toss the shrimp with half of the dressing.  
4. To the bowl of quinoa add diced mango, red bell pepper, avocado, and cilantro. Drizzle the remaining dressing over the mixture and gently toss to combine.  
5. Fold the cooked shrimp into the quinoa salad, ensuring everything is evenly coated. Adjust seasoning with extra salt, pepper, or lime juice if desired.  
6. Serve the salad chilled or at room temperature, garnished with additional cilantro and a lime wedge on the side. Enjoy!
title: Coconut Lime Shrimp with Mango Quinoa Salad

text:
Sage‑Infused Roasted Beet and Barley Salad with Citrus Vinaigrette

Ingredients:
- 1 cup pearl barley
- 3 medium beets, peeled and cubed
- 2 tbsp fresh sage leaves, finely chopped
- 1/4 cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped
- 1/4 cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
- 2 tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil
- 1 tbsp orange juice
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tsp honey or maple syrup
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the beet cubes with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper; spread them on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, until tender and caramelized.  
2. While the beets roast, rinse the barley and place it in a saucepan with 2 cups water. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 25‑30 minutes, or until the grains are tender and the water is absorbed. Drain any excess liquid and fluff with a fork.  
3. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining olive oil, orange juice, lemon juice, honey, chopped sage, and a pinch of salt and pepper to create the citrus vinaigrette.  
4. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked barley, roasted beets, toasted walnuts, and feta (if using). Drizzle the vinaigrette over the salad and toss gently to coat evenly.  
5. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or a splash of citrus juice if needed. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with a few extra sage leaves.
title: Sage‑Infused Roasted Beet and Barley Salad with Citrus Vinaigrette

text:
Spiced Orange‑Ginger Chickpea and Quinoa Skillet

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ¾ cups vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 small onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, grated
- zest of 1 orange
- ¼ cup fresh orange juice
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1½ cups canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 cup baby spinach leaves
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 green onions, sliced (for garnish)
- Optional: toasted sesame seeds for garnish

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan, combine the quinoa and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy. Remove from heat and set aside.
2. While the quinoa cooks, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 3‑4 minutes, until translucent.
3. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for another 30 seconds until fragrant.
4. Add the orange zest, orange juice, cumin, and smoked paprika to the skillet. Stir to combine and let the mixture simmer for 2 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.
5. Fold in the chickpeas and cooked quinoa, tossing everything together. Cook for 3‑4 minutes, allowing the chickpeas to heat through and absorb the orange‑ginger sauce.
6. Add the baby spinach leaves and stir until wilted, about 1 minute. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
7. Transfer the skillet contents to serving plates, garnish with sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds if desired, and serve warm.
title: Spiced Orange‑Ginger Chickpea and Quinoa Skillet

text:
Cardamom‑Spiced Pumpkin and Lentil Soup

Ingredients:
- 1 lb (450 g) red lentils, rinsed
- 2 cups (500 ml) pumpkin puree (canned or roasted)
- 1 large onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1 tsp ground cardamom
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- ¼ tsp smoked paprika
- 4 cups (1 L) vegetable broth
- 1 cup (240 ml) coconut milk
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- 1 tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Sprinkle the ground cardamom, cumin, and smoked paprika over the aromatics; toast the spices for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
4. Add the pumpkin puree and rinsed red lentils to the pot, mixing to combine.
5. Pour in the vegetable broth, bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook for 20‑25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender.
6. Stir in the coconut milk, season with salt and pepper, and simmer for an additional 5 minutes to meld the flavors.
7. Using an immersion blender, blend the soup until smooth (or blend in batches in a countertop blender). Adjust seasoning if needed.
8. Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro leaves and toasted pumpkin seeds, and serve hot.
title: Cardamom‑Spiced Pumpkin and Lentil Soup

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Black Bean Quinoa Bowl

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 (15‑oz) can black beans, drained and rinsed
- 1/4 cup red onion, finely diced
- 1 tablespoon lime juice
- 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 avocado, sliced (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the cubed sweet potatoes with olive oil, cinnamon, maple syrup, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.  
3. Spread the sweet potatoes in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway through, until tender and caramelized.  
4. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes or until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.  
5. In a medium bowl, mix the cooked quinoa, black beans, red onion, lime juice, and cilantro. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.  
6. To assemble the bowl, place a generous scoop of the quinoa‑bean mixture in the bottom of each serving bowl, top with roasted sweet potatoes, and add avocado slices if using.  
7. Drizzle any remaining maple‑cinnamon glaze from the baking sheet over the bowl, garnish with extra cilantro, and serve warm.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Sweet Potato and Black Bean Quinoa Bowl

text:
Cocoa‑Spiced Sweet Potato and Black Bean Chili

Ingredients:
- 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 medium onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon unsweetened cocoa powder
- 1 tablespoon chili powder
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1 (15‑oz) can black beans, drained and rinsed
- 1 (14‑oz) can diced tomatoes
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)
- Lime wedges (for serving)

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté for 4–5 minutes, until softened.
2. Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another 30 seconds until fragrant.
3. Sprinkle the cocoa powder, chili powder, cumin, and smoked paprika over the onions. Stir constantly for 1 minute to toast the spices.
4. Add the diced sweet potatoes to the pot
title: Cocoa‑Spiced Sweet Potato and Black Bean Chili

text:
Maple‑Glazed Carrot and Lentil Curry with Coconut Rice

Ingredients:
- 2 large carrots, peeled and diced
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 tablespoon maple syrup
- 1 tablespoon coconut oil
- 1 onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 teaspoon ground coriander
- ½ teaspoon turmeric powder
- ¼ teaspoon cayenne pepper (optional)
- 1 can (14 oz) coconut milk
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup jasmine rice
- 1 cup water
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)
- Lime wedges (for serving)

Instructions:
1. Rinse the jasmine rice, then combine it with 1 cup water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until fluffy. Remove from heat and set aside.
2. While the rice cooks, heat coconut oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté for 4‑5 minutes until translucent.
3. Stir in the garlic and ginger; cook for another minute until fragrant.
4. Add the diced carrots, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and cayenne (if using). Stir to coat the vegetables with the spices.
5. Pour in the coconut milk and vegetable broth, then bring the mixture to a gentle boil.
6. Add the rinsed red lentils, reduce heat to a simmer, and cook for 20‑25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the carrots are tender and the lentils have broken down, creating a thick sauce.
7. Drizzle the maple syrup over the curry, season with salt and black pepper, and stir to combine. Adjust seasoning to taste.
8. Spoon the coconut rice onto serving bowls, ladle the maple‑glazed carrot and lentil curry over the rice, and garnish with fresh cilantro and a squeeze of lime. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Carrot and Lentil Curry with Coconut Rice

text:
Miso‑Maple Glazed Sweet Potato and Chickpea Bowl

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp white miso paste
- 2 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 Tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 2 cups baby spinach leaves
- ¼ cup toasted pumpkin seeds
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional: sliced avocado and lime wedges for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20 minutes, turning halfway through.  
3. While the sweet potatoes roast, whisk together the miso paste, maple syrup, soy sauce, and the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil in a small bowl to form the glaze.  
4. After the sweet potatoes have roasted for 20 minutes, add the chickpeas to the baking sheet, drizzle the miso‑maple glaze over both the sweet potatoes and chickpeas, and toss gently to coat. Return to the oven and roast for an additional 15 minutes, or until the sweet potatoes are tender and the chickpeas are slightly caramelized.  
5. Remove the sheet from the oven and let the mixture cool for a couple of minutes.  
6. Assemble the bowls: divide the baby spinach between two serving bowls, top with the roasted sweet potatoes and glazed chickpeas, and sprinkle with toasted pumpkin seeds.  
7. If desired, add sliced avocado and a squeeze of fresh lime juice for extra creaminess and brightness.  
8. Serve warm and enjoy!
title: Miso‑Maple Glazed Sweet Potato and Chickpea Bowl

text:
Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Shrimp with Coconut‑Lime Rice

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup jasmine rice
- 1 ½ cups coconut milk
- ½ cup water
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, minced
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tbsp lime zest
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Rinse the jasmine rice under cold water until the water runs clear.  
2. In a saucepan combine the rice, coconut milk, water, half the lime zest, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and stir in lime juice and the remaining lime zest. Set aside.  
3. While the rice cooks, pat the shrimp dry with paper towels and season with salt, pepper, and the ground turmeric.  
4. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the minced garlic and ginger; sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.  
5. Add the seasoned shrimp to the skillet in a single layer. Cook 2‑3 minutes per side, or until the shrimp turn pink and opaque. Remove shrimp from the pan and set aside.  
6. Return the skillet to the stove, add a splash of water if needed, and deglaze the pan, scraping up any browned bits. Return the shrimp to the pan, toss to coat in the ginger‑turmeric aromatics, and heat through for another minute.  
7. Serve the shrimp over the coconut‑lime rice, garnish with chopped cilantro, and finish with an extra drizzle of lime juice if desired. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Ginger Turmeric Shrimp with Coconut‑Lime Rice

text:
Roasted Garlic‑Tahini Quinoa Stuffed Portobello Mushrooms

Ingredients:
- 4 large portobello mushroom caps, stems removed
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 cup fresh spinach, chopped
- ½ cup cherry tomatoes, halved
- ¼ cup tahini
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- ¼ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a saucepan, combine quinoa and vegetable broth; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
3. While the quinoa cooks, brush the mushroom caps on both sides with 1 tablespoon of olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Place them gill‑side up on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 12‑15 minutes, until tender.
4. In a skillet over medium heat, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil and sauté the minced garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the chopped spinach and cook until wilted, about 2 minutes. Remove from heat.
5. In a small bowl, whisk together tahini, lemon juice, maple syrup, smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt. Thin the sauce with 2‑3 tablespoons of warm water until it reaches a drizzling consistency.
6. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, sautéed spinach, cherry tomatoes, and half of the tahini‑lemon sauce. Toss gently and adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.
7. Spoon the quinoa mixture into the roasted mushroom caps, dividing it evenly among the four mushrooms. Drizzle the remaining tahini‑lemon sauce over the tops.
8. Return the stuffed mushrooms to the oven and bake for an additional 8‑10 minutes, allowing the filling to heat through and the edges to crisp slightly.
9. Remove from the oven, garnish with chopped fresh parsley, and serve warm. Enjoy as a hearty main dish or a satisfying lunch.
title: Roasted Garlic‑Tahini Quinoa Stuffed Portobello Mushrooms

text:
Herb‑Infused Quinoa with Roasted Fennel, Lemon Zest, and Toasted Pistachios

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 large fennel bulb, thinly sliced
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp sea salt, divided
- ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- Zest of 1 lemon
- ¼ cup pistachios, roughly chopped
- 2 Tbsp fresh parsley, finely chopped
- Optional: pinch of red‑pepper flakes for heat

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the sliced fennel with 1 Tbsp olive oil, ½ tsp salt, and black pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning once, until caramelized and tender. Remove and set aside.
2. While the fennel roasts, combine quinoa and water (or broth) in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the grains are fluffy. Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes.
3. Fluff the quinoa with a fork and stir in the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, the lemon zest, and the remaining ½ tsp salt. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
4. In a small skillet over medium heat, toast the chopped pistachios for 2‑3 minutes, stirring frequently, until fragrant and lightly golden. Transfer to a bowl.
5. Fold the roasted fennel into the quinoa, then sprinkle the toasted pistachios and fresh parsley over the top. Add a pinch of red‑pepper flakes if desired.
6. Serve warm or at room temperature as a side dish or light main course. Enjoy!
title: Herb‑Infused Quinoa with Roasted Fennel, Lemon Zest, and Toasted Pistachios

text:
Lemon‑Basil Farro with Roasted Sweet Potato and Goat Cheese

Ingredients:
- 1 cup farro, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 large sweet potato, peeled and cubed
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp sea salt
- ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- 1 tsp dried basil (or 1 tbsp fresh basil, chopped)
- ¼ cup crumbled goat cheese
- 1 tbsp toasted pine nuts (optional)
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tsp lemon zest

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until tender
title: Lemon‑Basil Farro with Roasted Sweet Potato and Goat Cheese

text:
Harissa‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Carrot and Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 14 oz (400 g) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 tbsp harissa paste
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 lb (450 g) carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch sticks
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tbsp honey or maple syrup
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Lemon wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Toss the carrot sticks with ½ tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread them in a single layer and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until caramelized and tender.  
2. While the carrots roast, whisk together harissa paste, honey (or maple syrup), and the remaining ½ tbsp olive oil in a bowl. Add the tofu cubes, toss to coat evenly, and let sit for 5 minutes.  
3. Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the harissa‑coated tofu and sear for 2‑3 minutes per side, until the edges are crisp and the glaze is glossy. Transfer the tofu to a plate.  
4. In a saucepan, combine rinsed quinoa and vegetable broth; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the quinoa is fluffy and the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and season with a pinch of salt.  
5. To assemble, divide the quinoa among serving bowls. Top with roasted carrots and harissa‑glazed tofu. Drizzle any remaining glaze from the skillet over the dish.  
6. Garnish with fresh cilantro leaves and serve with lemon wedges for a bright finish. Enjoy!
title: Harissa‑Glazed Tofu with Roasted Carrot and Quinoa

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Tacos with Lime Crema  

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced 1‑inch
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 ½  teaspoons saffron threads
- 2  tablespoons hot water
- 1  tablespoon olive oil (plus extra for roasting)
- 1  teaspoon ground cumin
- 1  teaspoon smoked paprika
- 2  garlic cloves, minced
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 8 small corn tortillas
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped (plus extra for garnish)
- ½ cup raw cashews
- 2  tablespoons lime juice (plus extra wedges for serving)
- ¼ cup water (for crema)
- 1  teaspoon maple syrup (optional, for a hint of sweetness)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a small bowl, combine the saffron threads with 2  tablespoons hot water; let steep for 5 minutes.  
3. In a large mixing bowl, toss the diced sweet potatoes with 1  tablespoon olive oil, half the cumin, half the smoked paprika, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20 minutes, turning once.  
4. While the sweet potatoes roast, whisk together the remaining cumin, smoked paprika, minced garlic, salt, pepper, and the saffron‑infused water. Add the chickpeas and toss to coat. After the sweet potatoes have roasted 20 minutes, add the chickpeas to the sheet and roast together for an additional 12‑15 minutes, until both are golden and tender.  
5. Meanwhile, make the lime crema: blend the cashews, lime juice, ¼ cup water, and maple syrup in a high‑speed blender until smooth and creamy. Season with a pinch of salt and set aside.  
6. Warm the corn tortillas on a dry skillet over medium heat for about 30 seconds per side, or wrap them in foil and heat in the oven for 5 minutes.  
7. Assemble each taco by placing a generous spoonful of the roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas onto a tortilla, sprinkling with chopped cilantro, and drizzling with lime crema. Serve with extra lime wedges. Enjoy!
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Chickpea and Sweet Potato Tacos with Lime Crema

text:
Saffron‑Infused Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Pilaf with Lime Yogurt

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 ½ cups quinoa, rinsed
- ¼ tsp saffron threads
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 small onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Zest of 1 lime
- ¼ cup Greek yogurt
- 1 Tbsp lime juice

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, salt, pepper, and half the cumin; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25‑30 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and caramelized.  
2. While the sweet potatoes roast, place the saffron threads in a small bowl with 2 Tbsp hot water; let steep for 5 minutes.  
3. In a medium saucepan, heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 4 minutes. Stir in the garlic and the remaining cumin and smoked paprika; cook 1 minute more.  
4. Add the rinsed quinoa to the saucepan, toast lightly for 2 minutes, then pour in the vegetable broth and the saffron infusion (including the threads). Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15‑18 minutes, or until the quinoa is fluffy and the liquid is absorbed.  
5. In a large mixing bowl, combine the roasted sweet potatoes, chickpeas, and cooked quinoa. Gently fold together, adjusting seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.  
6. For the lime yogurt sauce, whisk together Greek yogurt, lime juice, lime zest, and a pinch of salt until smooth.  
7. Serve the pilaf in bowls, drizzled with the lime yogurt sauce and sprinkled with fresh cilantro. Enjoy warm or at room temperature.
title: Saffron‑Infused Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Pilaf with Lime Yogurt

text:
Harissa‑Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Flatbread

Ingredients:
- 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp harissa paste
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 4 large flatbreads or naan rounds
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese
- 2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- Optional: ¼ cup thinly sliced red onion

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a bowl, toss the sweet potato cubes with 1 Tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet and roast for 20 minutes, turning once.  
3. While the sweet potatoes roast, combine the chickpeas, harissa paste, remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and a squeeze of lemon juice in a separate bowl.  
4. After the sweet potatoes have roasted, add the harissa‑coated chickpeas to the baking sheet, stir to combine, and roast for an additional 10‑12 minutes until the chickpeas are slightly crisp.  
5. Remove the vegetables from the oven and let cool for 5 minutes.  
6. Warm the flatbreads on a dry skillet over medium heat for 1‑2 minutes per side, or until lightly toasted.  
7. Assemble each flatbread by spreading a generous layer of the sweet potato‑chickpea mixture, sprinkling feta cheese, red onion (if using), and a drizzle of fresh lemon juice.  
8. Garnish with chopped cilantro, slice the flatbreads in half, and serve immediately.
title: Harissa‑Roasted Sweet Potato and Chickpea Flatbread
