title: Herb‑Infused Farro with Lemon‑Garlic Roasted Brussels Sprouts and Toast

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea & Spinach One‑Pot

Ingredients:
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 large onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 4 cups fresh spinach leaves
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Lime wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 4–5 minutes, until softened and translucent.  
2. Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly to avoid burning.  
3. Sprinkle the turmeric and cumin over the aromatics, stirring to coat; cook for another 30 seconds to release the spices’ fragrance.  
4. Add the chickpeas, coconut milk, and vegetable broth to the pot. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.  
5. Stir in the fresh lime juice, then add the spinach leaves. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the spinach wilts, about 2 minutes.  
6. Season the stew with salt and pepper to taste. Adjust the lime juice if a brighter acidity is desired.  
7. Ladle the one‑pot stew into bowls, garnish with chopped cilantro, and serve with lime wedges on the side. Enjoy warm!
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea & Spinach One‑Pot

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Shrimp with Garlic‑Herb Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 tbsp coconut oil
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups low‑sodium vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
- 1 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, toss the shrimp with turmeric, smoked paprika, lime juice, minced garlic, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of coconut oil; let marinate for 10 minutes.
2. While the shrimp marinates, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and fluff with a fork.
3. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the marinated shrimp and cook 2‑3 minutes per side, until pink and opaque. Transfer shrimp to a plate and set aside.
4. In the same skillet, add a little more olive oil if needed and sauté the remaining garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant.
5. Stir the cooked quinoa into the skillet, mixing with the garlic; season with salt and pepper, and heat through for 2 minutes.
6. Fold the cooked shrimp back into the quinoa mixture, then remove from heat.
7. Sprinkle chopped parsley and cilantro over the dish, give a final gentle toss, and serve immediately with extra lime wedges if desired.
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Shrimp with Garlic‑Herb Quinoa

text:
Citrus‑Infused Coconut Quinoa with Charred Sweet Peppers and Toasted Almonds

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup water
- zest of 1 orange
- juice of 1 orange
- 2 large red bell peppers, sliced into strips
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1/4 cup sliced almonds, toasted
- 2 green onions, thinly sliced
- 1 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 tsp sea salt
- 1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the bell‑pepper strips with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 15‑20 minutes, turning once, until charred and tender. Set aside.
2. In a medium saucepan combine the rinsed quinoa, coconut milk, water, orange zest, and orange juice. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy.
3. While the quinoa cooks, toast the sliced almonds in a dry skillet over medium heat, stirring frequently, until golden and fragrant, about 3‑4 minutes. Transfer to a small bowl.
4. Fluff the cooked quinoa with a fork and season with sea salt and black pepper to taste. Stir in the roasted bell‑pepper strips, toasted almonds, and green onions.
5. Transfer the quinoa mixture to a serving bowl, garnish with chopped cilantro, and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Citrus‑Infused Coconut Quinoa with Charred Sweet Peppers and Toasted Almonds

text:
Maple‑Glazed Coconut Curry with Roasted Cauliflower and Quinoa

Ingredients:
- 1 large head cauliflower, cut into florets
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 teaspoon sea salt
- ½ teaspoon black pepper
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 can (13.5 oz) coconut milk
- 2 tablespoons maple syrup
- 1 tablespoon red curry paste
- 1 inch fresh ginger, grated
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 red bell pepper, sliced
- 1 cup snap peas
- 1 tablespoon lime juice
- Fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Lime wedges, for serving

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss cauliflower florets with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender.  
2. While the cauliflower roasts, combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside.  
3. In a large skillet, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add garlic and ginger; sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.  
4. Stir in red curry paste, cooking for another 30 seconds. Pour in coconut milk and maple syrup, whisking to combine. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.  
5. Add sliced red bell pepper and snap peas to the sauce; cook for 4‑5 minutes until vegetables are just tender.  
6. Stir in lime juice, then season the curry with additional salt or pepper to taste.  
7. Fold the roasted cauliflower into the curry, allowing it to heat through for 2 minutes.  
8. To serve, spoon a bed of quinoa onto each plate, top with the maple‑glazed coconut curry, and garnish with fresh cilantro and lime wedges. Enjoy!
title: Maple‑Glazed Coconut Curry with Roasted Cauliflower and Quinoa

text:
Harissa‑Spiced Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Tagine

Ingredients:
- 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1‑inch chunks
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp harissa paste
- 1 medium onion, thinly sliced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 cup diced canned tomatoes (or fresh tomatoes)
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- ½ cup dried apricots, halved
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- ½ tsp ground coriander
- ¼ tsp ground cinnamon
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 2 Tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 Tbsp lemon juice
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Toss the carrot chunks with 1 Tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20‑25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.  
2. While the carrots roast, heat the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil in a large oven‑safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the sliced onion and sauté for 5 minutes, until softened.  
3. Stir in the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more, being careful not to brown it.  
4. Add the harissa paste, cumin, coriander, and cinnamon; stir to coat the onions and garlic, cooking for another minute to release the spices’ aromas.  
5. Pour in the diced tomatoes and vegetable broth, scraping any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.  
6. Add the roasted carrots, chickpeas, and dried apricot halves to the skillet. Stir to combine, then season with additional salt and pepper to taste.  
7. Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven and bake, uncovered, for 15‑20 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken slightly.  
8. Remove from the oven and stir in the lemon juice and chopped cilantro. Adjust seasoning if needed.  
9. Serve the tagine hot, over couscous, quinoa, or warm flatbread, and garnish with extra cilantro and a drizzle of olive oil if desired.
title: Harissa‑Spiced Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Tagine

text:
Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Tabbouleh

Ingredients:
- 1 medium cauliflower head, cut into florets
- 1 (15‑oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp lemon zest
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- ½ tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup fine‑bulgur wheat
- 1 ½ cups boiling water
- ½ cup fresh parsley, finely chopped
- ¼ cup fresh mint leaves, finely chopped
- ¼ cup red onion, finely diced
- ¼ cup cucumber, diced
- 3 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 2 Tbsp extra‑virgin olive oil
- 1 clove garlic, minced

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, toss cauliflower florets and chickpeas with olive oil, lemon zest, thyme, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread evenly on the prepared sheet.  
3. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, turning halfway through, until cauliflower is golden‑brown and chickpeas are crisp. Remove and let cool slightly.  
4. Meanwhile, place bulgur in a heat‑proof bowl; pour boiling water over it, cover, and let sit 10‑12 minutes until fluffy. Drain any excess water and fluff with a fork.  
5. In a small bowl, whisk together lemon juice, extra‑virgin olive oil, minced garlic, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of pepper to make the dressing.  
6. In a large mixing bowl combine the cooked bulgur, roasted cauliflower‑chickpea mixture, parsley, mint, red onion, and cucumber.  
7. Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently until everything is evenly coated. Adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if desired.  
8. Serve at room temperature or chilled, garnished with a sprinkle of fresh parsley and a lemon wedge. Enjoy!
title: Lemon‑Thyme Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Tabbouleh

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea & Quinoa Salad

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup water
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1/2 cucumber, diced
- 1/4 red onion, finely chopped
- 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan combine quinoa, coconut milk, water, and turmeric; bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
2. While the quinoa cooks, preheat a skillet over medium heat. Toss chickpeas with olive oil, lime juice, salt, and pepper; sauté 5‑7 minutes until lightly browned and fragrant. Set aside.
3. In a large bowl combine the cooked quinoa, sautéed chickpeas, diced red bell pepper, cucumber, and red onion.
4. Drizzle the mixture with an additional splash of lime juice, season with salt and pepper, and toss gently to combine.
5. Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy!
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea & Quinoa Salad

text:
Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea & Quinoa Power Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 1 ½ cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 (15 oz) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 1 tablespoon coconut oil
- 1 teaspoon ground turmeric
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1 tablespoon fresh lime juice
- 1 tablespoon coconut milk
- 1 cup red cabbage, thinly sliced
- 1 carrot, julienned
- ½ cup shelled edamame
- 2 green onions, sliced
- 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- Optional: toasted coconut flakes for garnish

Instructions:
1. Rinse the quinoa under cold water. In a saucepan combine quinoa with water (or broth), bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat and fluff with a fork. Set aside.
2. While the quinoa cooks, heat coconut oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the chickpeas, turmeric, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Sauté 5‑7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chickpeas are lightly browned and aromatic.
3. Stir in lime juice and coconut milk, coating the chickpeas evenly. Cook an additional 2 minutes, then remove the skillet from the heat.
4. In a large mixing bowl combine the cooked quinoa, spiced chickpeas, sliced red cabbage, julienned carrot, edamame, and green
title: Coconut‑Lime Turmeric Chickpea & Quinoa Power Bowl

text:
Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Chickpea and Kale Tabbouleh  

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 cups kale leaves, stems removed and torn into bite‑size pieces
- 1 cup cooked quinoa, cooled
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 1 Tbsp pure maple syrup
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- ½ tsp ground cumin
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- Juice of 1 lemon
- Zest of 1 lemon
- ¼ tsp sea salt
- ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- ¼ cup toasted sliced almonds (optional)
- 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, whisk together olive oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, cumin, minced garlic, salt, and pepper.  
3. Add the drained chickpeas to the bowl and toss until they are evenly coated with the maple‑cinnamon mixture.  
4. Spread the chickpeas in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20‑25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until golden and slightly crisp.  
5. While the chickpeas roast, massage the kale: place the torn kale leaves in a separate bowl, drizzle with a little olive oil and a pinch of salt, and massage for 2‑3 minutes until the leaves soften and darken.  
6. In a large mixing bowl combine the cooked quinoa, roasted chickpeas, massaged kale, lemon juice, and lemon zest. Toss gently to distribute all ingredients evenly.  
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or lemon juice if desired.  
8. Transfer the tabbouleh to a serving platter, sprinkle toasted almonds and chopped parsley on top for extra crunch and freshness.  
9. Serve warm, at room temperature, or chilled—perfect as a hearty side dish or a light main course.
title: Cinnamon‑Maple Roasted Chickpea and Kale Tabbouleh

text:
Lemon‑Thyme Quinoa with Roasted Sweet Peppers and Feta

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed
- 2 cups low‑sodium vegetable broth
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon fresh thyme leaves (or ½ teaspoon dried)
- Zest of 1 lemon
- 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice
- 2 large red or orange bell peppers, sliced into strips
- ½ teaspoon smoked paprika
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
- ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese
- Optional garnish: chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  
2. Toss the sliced bell peppers with olive oil, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; spread them in a single layer on the prepared sheet.  
3. Roast the peppers for 15‑20 minutes, turning once, until the edges are caramelized and the peppers are tender. Remove from the oven and set aside.  
4. While the peppers roast, combine the quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is fluffy.  
5. Remove the saucepan from heat; fluff the quinoa with a fork and stir in the lemon zest, lemon juice, thyme, and a pinch of salt and pepper.  
6. Gently fold the roasted sweet peppers into the quinoa mixture.  
7. Transfer the quinoa to a serving bowl, sprinkle the crumbled feta over the top, and garnish with chopped parsley if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.
title: Lemon‑Thyme Quinoa with Roasted Sweet Peppers and Feta
